title: sinexd startup reconciler: populate derivation.product_declarations from AutomatonSpec::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS
description:
## Problem
`derivation.enforce_event_product_declaration()` trigger (sinex-0vx.4, merged #2506) rejects any derived event write (source_event_ids set) whose product_class/source/event_type isn't matched by a row in `derivation.product_declarations`. Verified 2026-07-31 (during sinex-egyf review): grep across the whole crate confirms NO production code path ever inserts into this table — only test files (`crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/*_test.rs`, `crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence_test.rs`, `crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry_test.rs`, and 4 more from the egyf sweep) seed rows, always scoped to that single test's transaction.

Meanwhile `crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry.rs` already statically declares `OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS` for all 14 registered automata (TerminalCommandCanonicalizer, Analytics, AttentionStream, IntervalLift, HealthAggregator, SessionDetector, HourlySummarizer, DailySummarizer, EntityExtractor, EntityResolver, RelationExtractor, EntityEnricher, TagApplier, EmbeddingProducer, DocumentParser, InstructionExpectationReconciler) via `DeclaresOutputs::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS`. Nothing reconciles this static source of truth into the DB table the trigger actually checks.

**Blast radius: every automaton in the system is currently unable to persist a single derived event against any schema with the 0vx.4 trigger applied (i.e. current master/dev schema, and prod once rebuilt).** This is not automaton-specific breakage (that would self-heal); it's a structural gap that makes the entire derived-event plane a hard no-op in any fresh deployment. Directly blocks the fresh-rebuild campaign (sinex-poma): post-wipe, sinexd would boot and every automaton would immediately start failing all writes with sqlstate 23514.

Originally homed as item 2 of sinex-0vx.5's design ("STARTUP DECLARATION RECONCILE... sinexd startup reconciles static AutomatonSpec.outputs... into derivation.product_declarations and REFUSES TO START if a registered automaton can emit an undeclared source/type/class"), bundled with an unrelated actor-kind curation-policy concern. Splitting out because this is urgent/blocking and self-contained; sinex-0vx.5 keeps the actor-kind/finalizer-registry half.

## Scope
- Reconciler runs at sinexd startup (supervisor bootstrap, alongside other startup reconcilers), reads `AutomatonSpec::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS` for every registered automaton, upserts matching rows into `derivation.product_declarations`.
- Fail-closed per sinex-0vx.5's original design intent: if a registered automaton's static declaration conflicts with an existing DB row (same declaration_id, different product_class/source/event_type), refuse to start rather than silently drift.
- Out of scope: curation's own declarations (sinex-q46n, non-automaton derived events) — separate registration path, curation proposals aren't automaton output.
- Out of scope: actor-kind/finalizer-registry policy (stays on sinex-0vx.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- sinexd startup populates derivation.product_declarations for all 14 current automata without manual intervention.
- A test proves at least one automaton's real output insert succeeds end-to-end against a schema-applied (not manually-seeded) database.
- Static-vs-DB declaration mismatch causes startup failure with a clear error, not silent drift or silent write rejection later.
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(product_declaration_startup_diff)' passes (name from 0vx.5's original VERIFY line, reuse or rename as fits the actual implementation).
notes:
DISPATCH-READY IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (prep done 2026-07-31, host under memory pressure — not yet dispatched):

Data shapes already exist and map 1:1 to the DB row:
- crate/sinex-primitives/src/derivation.rs:447 DerivationOutputDeclaration { declaration_id, owner, product_class, write_surface, output_source, output_event_type, projection_kind, artifact_kind, proposal_kind, semantics_version, input_eligibility, default_support, verification_command }
- crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry.rs: AUTOMATA: &[AutomatonSpec] — each entry has `outputs: &'static [DerivationOutputDeclaration]` via `<Runtime as DeclaresOutputs>::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS`. 14 entries currently (lines ~64-175ish, canonicalizer/analytics/attention_stream/interval_lift/health_aggregator/session_detector/hourly_summarizer/daily_summarizer/entity_extractor/entity_resolver/relation_extractor/entity_enricher/tag_applier/embedding_producer/document_parser/instruction_expectation_reconciler).
- DB target table: derivation.product_declarations (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/derivation.rs, columns match the struct almost exactly: declaration_id, owner, product_class, write_surface, output_source, output_event_type, semantics_version, input_eligibility, default_claim_support, verification_command).

Insertion point: crate/sinexd/src/supervisor/mod.rs::Supervisor::run — after event_engine is confirmed ready (event_engine_ready_rx awaited, ~line 108) and BEFORE `start_automata(shutdown_rx.clone())` is called (~line 168). This is the correct fail-closed point: DB pool is up, automata haven't spawned yet, so a startup failure here prevents any automaton from ever attempting an undeclared write.

No DB pool is currently threaded into Supervisor::run — only EventEngineConfig.database_url (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/config.rs:33) and pool_size. The reconciler needs its own short-lived pool/connection (or thread the event_engine's pool out if start_event_engine already exposes one — check event_engine/config.rs and jetstream_consumer/service.rs return shape first, may already have a reusable DbPool handle from ServiceContainer worth reusing instead of opening a second pool).

Implementation shape:
1. New fn (e.g. `reconcile_product_declarations(pool: &DbPool, automata: &[AutomatonSpec]) -> Result<()>`), likely in crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry.rs or a new crate/sinexd/src/runtime/product_declarations.rs.
2. For each automaton, for each declaration in `.outputs`: UPSERT into derivation.product_declarations keyed on declaration_id. On upsert, if an existing row's (product_class, output_source, output_event_type, ...) differs from what's being written for the same declaration_id -> hard startup failure (SinexError::configuration or similar), not silent overwrite — this is the "fail-closed on static-vs-DB mismatch" requirement from the original 0vx.5 design.
3. Call from Supervisor::run per the insertion point above; propagate errors as a startup failure (same pattern as the event_engine-ready failure block just above it — escalate_tx, teardown, return Err).
4. Curation/non-automaton declarations (sinex-q46n) are explicitly OUT of scope for this reconciler — automata only.

Test target: a test that runs schema-apply (not manual row seeding) then calls the reconciler, then proves a real automaton's build_output_event()-shaped insert succeeds. Consider whether crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry_test.rs (already validates outputs non-empty and tuple-unique) is the right home, or a new integration test under tests/api or tests/runtime.

Also worth checking whether `xtask doctor` / dev bootstrap already has an equivalent gap for local dev (would explain why this hasn't been noticed yet in daily dev-loop usage) — if dev workflows never restart sinexd from a truly fresh schema, this could have been silently masked.
Implemented and PR opened: https://github.com/Sinity/sinex/pull/2528 (branch feature/fix/sinexd-startup-product-declaration-reconciler).

Scope delivered: ProductDeclarationRepository (sinex-db), reconcile_product_declarations (sinexd::automata::product_declarations) wired into Supervisor::run after event-engine-ready and before start_automata, using a short-lived pool from EventEngineConfig::create_db_pool(). Fail-closed on any field mismatch for an existing declaration_id row. DerivationWriteSurface::as_str()/InputEligibility::as_str() added to sinex-primitives for DB-string conversion.

AC status:
- sinexd startup populates derivation.product_declarations for all 16 current automata (registry census is actually 16 now, not the bead's stated 14 -- verified against registry_test.rs::automata_derivation_declarations_cover_registry) without manual intervention: SATISFIED.
- Test proves a real automaton's output insert succeeds end-to-end against a schema-applied (not manually seeded) DB: SATISFIED (reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert).
- Static-vs-DB mismatch causes startup failure with a clear error: SATISFIED (reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row).
- Named test 'product_declaration_startup_diff' from 0vx.5's original VERIFY line: renamed to reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert / reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row (AC text explicitly allowed a rename to fit the actual implementation).

Verification run in worktree devshell: xtask check -p sinexd clean; xtask check -p sinex-db -p sinex-primitives clean; both new tests pass; all 4 pre-existing registry_test.rs tests pass unchanged; pre-push drift guard (xtask check --changed-strict origin/master) passed for sinex-db/sinex-primitives/sinexd.

Still open: CodeRabbit automated review pending on the PR at time of this note; will triage before merge.
CLOSED. Merged via PR #2528 (squash-merge a2e3df5, merged 2026-07-31T21:37:36Z).

Closure Evidence Manifest:
- AC "sinexd startup populates derivation.product_declarations for all
  automata without manual intervention": SATISFIED. Reconciler wired into
  Supervisor::run (crate/sinexd/src/supervisor/mod.rs, right after
  await_event_engine_ready and before start_automata). Registry census is
  16 automata (not the bead's stated 14 -- verified live against
  registry_test.rs::automata_derivation_declarations_cover_registry, which
  asserts AUTOMATA.len() == 16). Applies to the default/production path
  (SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_ENABLED=true, the default); the split-process dev mode
  where SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_ENABLED=false relies on a sibling process (the one
  actually running the event engine against the same DB) to have reconciled
  -- documented in the guard comment, not a gap in the covered scope.
- AC "test proves at least one automaton's real output insert succeeds
  end-to-end against a schema-applied (not manually-seeded) database":
  SATISFIED. crate/sinexd/src/automata/product_declarations_test.rs::
  reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert runs against the sandbox
  template DB (built by real xtask schema apply, never manual row seeding),
  calls the reconciler, then inserts a canonicalizer-shaped derived event via
  EventRepository::insert and asserts it round-trips. Anti-vacuity: deleting
  the reconcile_product_declarations call (or breaking its INSERT) turns this
  red with derivation.enforce_event_product_declaration()'s "undeclared
  product write" check_violation -- the exact production trigger this bead
  exists to satisfy.
- AC "static-vs-DB mismatch causes startup failure with a clear error, not
  silent drift or silent write rejection later": SATISFIED.
  reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row seeds a conflicting
  product_class for a real declaration_id then asserts reconcile_
  product_declarations returns Err naming both the declaration_id and the
  disagreeing field.
- AC "xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(product_declaration_startup_diff)'
  passes (name ... reuse or rename as fits the actual implementation)":
  DEFERRED/RENAMED per the AC's own allowance -- implemented as
  reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert +
  reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row (more accurately describes what
  each test actually proves than a single combined test would).

Verification commands run (worktree devshell, live sandbox DB):
- xtask check -p sinexd -> clean
- xtask check -p sinex-db -p sinex-primitives -> clean
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert)' -> pass
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row)' -> pass
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(automata_derivation_declarations_cover_registry) + test(automata_declared_event_types_match_runtime_output) + test(registered_automata_have_unique_names) + test(registered_automata_are_bridge_repairable)' -> all 4 pass unchanged
- Pre-push drift guard (xtask check --changed-strict origin/master) -> passed for sinex-db/sinex-primitives/sinexd

Automated review triage: CodeRabbit and the Codex GitHub connector both hit
usage/rate limits on this PR and posted zero substantive findings (0 inline
comments, 0 formal reviews) -- classified as tool failure, not an unresolved
actionable finding; requested a manual @coderabbitai re-review which also
produced no findings. GitGuardian passed. No hosted PR-blocking CI in this
repo; local gate is the gate.

Out of scope (unchanged): curation/non-automaton declarations (sinex-q46n),
actor-kind/finalizer-registry policy (remains on sinex-0vx.5).
close_reason:
Merged #2528. Closes the systemic gap where no production code path populated derivation.product_declarations, meaning every automaton in the system was structurally unable to persist a single derived event against a freshly-applied schema.

Implementation: crate/sinexd/src/automata/product_declarations.rs (new) — reconcile_product_declarations(pool, automata), fail-closed on any static-vs-DB mismatch (named-field error, never silent overwrite/drift). Repository layer: crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/derivation.rs (new, narrow find-by-id + insert-if-absent). Wired into crate/sinexd/src/supervisor/mod.rs::Supervisor::run right after event-engine-ready and before any automaton spawns — the correct fail-closed point.

Verification (independently re-run in review, not just trusted): xtask check -p sinexd -p sinex-db -p sinex-primitives clean. xtask test -E 'reconcile_allows_real_canonicalizer_output_insert or reconcile_rejects_conflicting_existing_row or registry_test' — 14/14 passed. The core test proves end-to-end, against a database that only ever went through real xtask schema apply (zero manual row seeding), that the reconciler is the ONLY thing that makes a real automaton output insert succeed through the actual production write path (EventRepository::insert) — explicitly documents the anti-vacuity condition (deleting the reconciler call turns it red with the trigger's check_violation).

AC disposition: all satisfied. Curation/non-automaton declarations (sinex-q46n) correctly deferred as out of scope — unblocking that bead now.

title: Fresh-rebuild campaign: full remaining scope (2026-07-12 checkpoint)
description:
# Fresh-rebuild campaign: full remaining scope

> Standalone durable snapshot, written 2026-07-12 as the `sinex-0vx` derivation-control-plane
> wave 1 checkpoint (PRs #2502-#2509, all merged). Supersedes reliance on the local Claude Code
> plan file `~/.claude/plans/maybe-1877-could-be-snug-salamander.md` (DRAFT-status, not repo-durable,
> not visible to other agents/sessions) as the single source of truth for what's left. Read this
> bead before resuming the campaign in any future session — it replaces re-deriving scope from
> `bd list`/`bd show` scattered across dozens of beads.

## Where this campaign came from (context, not action)

The operator chose a **fresh-start rebuild** over sinex's normal fix-forward-via-replay doctrine,
because the current dataset is heavily polluted (journald flood, self-capture loop, pre-ecy/pre-x9i
derived-plane pollution) and replaying it in place is wasteful. The plan: land every "bake-in" fix
first so the rebuilt dataset is clean from row zero, then do one clean wipe + re-import. This is a
deliberate, operator-ratified override of the "state is durable, never wipe" doctrine (memory:
`feedback_state_is_durable`) — survivable because a full state snapshot precedes the wipe, not because
it's doctrinally clean. Full original rationale, decisions D1-D3, and backup/wipe mechanics live in
the plan file above; this bead does not repeat that context, only the **remaining execution scope**.

## Status snapshot as of 2026-07-12 (verify against `bd show` before trusting — this decays)

### Done today (session 2026-07-12, PRs #2502-#2509, all merged to master)
- `sinex-8cr.1` — derivation-control-plane primitives (`DerivedProductClass`, `ClaimSupport`,
  `DerivationScope`, `DerivationOutputDeclaration`) in `sinex-primitives`.
- `sinex-0vx.1` — every one of the 16 registered automata statically declares its output(s) via
  `Automaton::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS`, threaded through the whole trait hierarchy, bridged to the
  registry via `DeclaresOutputs`.
- `sinex-0vx.2` — `DerivedOutput<T>` carries `declaration_id`/`product_class`/`claim_support`/
  `derivation_epoch_id`/`derivation_lane_id`; `AutomatonRuntime::validate_output_declaration()`
  enforces the claim at emission time (undeclared-id, class/source/type mismatch, adjudicated-
  without-judgment-id all rejected).
- `sinex-0vx.3` — all 24 real `DerivedOutput` construction call sites across the 16 automata now
  claim their declaration for real, activating 0vx.2's gate live.
- `sinex-0vx.4` — new `derivation`/`authority` Postgres schemas (8 tables total), additive columns
  + enforcement trigger on `core.events`/`reflection.events`, plus the required mechanical
  `EventRecord`/COPY-contract follow-through in `sinex-db` (not optional — sqlx `query_as!`
  requires exact column parity, so this HAD to bundle into the same PR).
- `sinex-8cr.2` — the six new columns (`product_class`, `claim_support`, `derivation_declaration_id`,
  `derivation_epoch_id`, `derivation_lane_id`, `adjudication_event_id`) are now actually persisted
  through every write path (single insert, QueryBuilder batch, stream batch, COPY/staging,
  `EventRecord` conversion) instead of being validated then discarded. `derivation_epoch_id`/
  `derivation_lane_id`/`adjudication_event_id` deliberately stay `None` everywhere — no producer
  exists yet (that's 0vx.5/0vx.6/0vx.7/0vx.9's job).

Also merged today (housekeeping, not campaign scope): `sinex-ijz6`'s automaton-portfolio profile
gates (#2501, landed just before this wave started).

### The chain is now real end-to-end for `product_class`/`claim_support`
Declared (0vx.1) → validated at emission (0vx.2) → actually claimed by all 16 automata (0vx.3) →
DB columns + trigger exist (0vx.4) → persisted for real (8cr.2). What's NOT yet real: nothing reads
`derivation.product_declarations` at startup to cross-check the static declarations against the DB
(that's 0vx.5's "startup declaration reconcile" AC), and nothing mints a non-canonical epoch/lane id
yet (0vx.5/0vx.6/0vx.7/0vx.9).

## Remaining scope, part 1: the `sinex-0vx` derivation-control-plane sub-campaign

Waves 2-4 below are **ready to resume immediately** — no external blocker, just execution capacity.
Two lanes are parallel-dispatchable right now (`0vx.5` and `68c.1`, disjoint footprints).

| Wave | Bead | What | Footprint | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `sinex-0vx.5` | DB-backed `authority.finalizer_registry`, curation-bypass rejection, sinexd startup declaration-reconcile (refuse to start if a registered automaton can emit an undeclared source/type/class), Agent-actor-kind promotion-sufficiency policy (Agent Accept is non-sufficient by default per the 0vx design pass decision (a)) | `sinex-db` (new authority repo) + `sinexd` (api curation handlers, startup reconcile) | `sinex-0vx.4` done, `sinex-8cr.2` done — **ready now** |
| 2 | `sinex-68c.1` | Generic projection repo (new) + sinexd context handler wiring | `sinex-db` (new file) + `sinexd` | `sinex-0vx.4` done — **ready now**, disjoint from 0vx.5 |
| 3 | `sinex-0vx.6` | Generic `DerivationRepository` + port entity/relation lane onto `derivation.lane_outputs` (drop `semantic.*` tables in 0vx.8, not here) + generic `LaneDiffReport`/`LaneOutputKind` trait in primitives (entity/relation is the first `impl`) | `sinex-db` (new repo) + `sinex-primitives` (`LaneDiffReport`) | `sinex-0vx.4` done — **ready now**, but `0vx.5`'s finalizer registry is a natural pairing (promotion path) |
| 3 | `sinex-68c.2/.3/.4` | Projection read surfaces + replay/staleness propagation, `ProjectionInvalidationRepository::mark_stale_for_event_scope` | `sinexd` read handlers | `68c.1` |
| 4 | `sinex-0vx.7` | Sessionization shadow lane — 2nd generality proof, `event_set` batch scope, canonical product class | needs `0vx.5`+`0vx.6` | wave 3 |
| 4 | `sinex-0vx.9` | Entity-chain shadow lane, `stream_checkpoint` scope — pq5-B re-entry, the FIRST real client of `DerivationScope::StreamCheckpoint`; this is the sole re-entry path for the entity chain (default-off per `ijz6`/pq5 ratification) | needs `0vx.5`+`0vx.6` | wave 3, parallel to `0vx.7` |
| close-out | `sinex-0vx.8` | Strict cleanup: forbidden-pattern gate, DROP `semantic.*` tables, ban anonymous `DerivedOutput`/scalar `EvidenceTier` vocabulary anywhere in the codebase | gated on `0vx.3`+`68c.4`+`8cr.2` (all satisfied except `68c.4`) | wave 3 done |

**Still unhomed on the `sinex-8cr` parent bead** (not covered by any child above): *"No read surface
renders `semantic_candidate` or `analysis_claim` rows without support-vector caveats; UI badges
derive from the vector, never stored instead of it."* This is a consumer-facing (sinexctl/API/MCP
read-surface) requirement — likely belongs inside `68c.2`/`68c.3` (projection read surfaces) or needs
its own child bead. Flag this when picking up wave 3.

**Design reference for all of the above**: `.agent/scratch/027-0vx-derivation-control-plane-design.md`
(the three settled decisions: Agent actor-kind, `StreamCheckpoint` scope, `derivation.*`-vs-`semantic.*`
port-not-wrap) plus `.agent/scratch/new-gpt-pro/04-interpretation-plane-blueprint.report.md` (original
DDL/type sketches — verified accurate against master as of 2026-07-12, two tautological CHECK bugs
and one nonexistent SQL function already corrected during 0vx.4's implementation, do not re-introduce
them if consulting the blueprint directly).

## Remaining scope, part 2: the rest of Phase B (bake-in fixes, non-0vx)

These are **not gated on the 0vx sub-campaign** — they can run in parallel with it.

- `sinex-08z` (P2, open) — Dedup observability / import-idempotence report: "N new / M suppressed /
  K superseded" reporting so the eventual re-import (Phase C) is auditable. Depends on `sinex-908`
  (closed) only.
- `sinex-0eam` (P2, open) — Cross-provider observation fusion: one canonical composite from multiple
  witnesses of the same occurrence. Depends on `sinex-0vx` (parent, still open via its children),
  `sinex-908`/`sinex-n9a` (both closed), `sinex-rkv.6` (blocks, check status), `sinex-a4w.3.6`.
- `sinex-ijz6` (in-progress) — **only remaining AC is a post-deploy verification note**: actually run
  `nix develop --command switch` from `/realm/project/sinnix` to deploy the ratified 7-automaton
  default-enabled set to `sinnix-prime`, then confirm via `sinexctl runtime automata` that the running
  set matches. This is a real deploy action, not more code — do it once the operator wants a live
  verification checkpoint, or fold it into the Phase C deploy step (Phase C deploys anyway, so this
  AC could be satisfied for free as part of that single deploy instead of a separate one now).
- `sinex-x9i` (in-progress) — Telemetry lane separation. Per its own notes, table+routing already
  landed (#2363/#2364/#2365/#2474); remaining scope is verification-only.
- `sinex-h3g` — **reclassified OUT of the Phase-B bake-in set** (2026-07-11 note): the AW
  settling-window bug only affects LIVE rows still growing; the rebuild imports a STATIC AW SQLite
  snapshot where durations are already final, so this does not affect the rebuilt historical data.
  Not a wipe blocker — do post-rebuild alongside `sinex-r6d.4`.

## Remaining scope, part 3: Phase A (decide + backup) — not started

- `sinex-sn6s` (P2, open) — Declare per-source criticality tiers, confirming the wipe premise
  (personal sources reconstructable, chatter non-critical). Should land before Phase C as the last
  sanity check on the whole rebuild rationale.
- **A2, the actual backup**: `sinexctl ops state snapshot --auto-stop --compression 15 --output
  /realm/inbox/sinex-snapshots/$(date +%F).tar.zst` → `sinexctl ops state inspect`. On-machine only
  (no off-machine target per operator). Needs ≥1.5× state free (~292G live → ~450G free) — check disk
  headroom before running. **Not yet executed** as of this snapshot.
- **A1, doctrine-override record**: a `bd remember` / `sinexctl ops` log entry citing
  `feedback_state_is_durable` as the explicit, operator-authorized exception. Cheap, do it right
  before the snapshot.

## Remaining scope, part 4: Category C beads (fold into re-import, execute DURING Phase C)

These are not pre-wipe blockers — they ARE the historical-import legs the rebuild's Phase C step 7
("re-run source historical scans") executes:

- `sinex-rkv.15` (open) — Google Takeout product family raw-archive import.
- `sinex-rkv.16` (open) — Web-history backfill from raw artifacts (Takeout Chrome JSON + historical
  browser exports).
- `sinex-2bk` (open) — Verify deployed static imports (git + raindrop) after next Sinnix
  switch/restart.
- `sinex-k4c` source-layer children (not individually re-verified in this snapshot — re-check `bd show
  sinex-k4c` before Phase C).

## Remaining scope, part 5: Phase C — the wipe + rebuild itself (entirely un-started)

**Gated on all of Phase B landing.** One-shot, operator-gated, do not execute without explicit
go-ahead even under standing autonomy (this is the plan's own "destructive operation, state intent

title: Choose canonical CAS architecture before lossless wipe import
description:
## Rationale
The current custom exact-byte BLAKE3 CAS plus legacy git-annex compatibility is not yet an explicit canonical architecture decision. Wipe-scale ingestion must not begin while backup, metadata, corruption recovery, replay-after-source-removal, and large-object semantics depend on an implicit choice.

## Alternatives Considered
- Retain and harden the custom CAS: evaluate its existing exact-byte, manifest, lease, quarantine, fsck, and restore properties and close their proof gaps.
- Adopt a third-party content-addressable/object store: evaluate viable stores for metadata preservation, immutable manifests, corruption detection, backup/restore, range reads, pack/chunk/repack semantics, and migration cost.
- Keep legacy git-annex as canonical: currently rejected as insufficiently specified for the full metadata/restore/control contract; may remain compatibility backend.

## Decision Requirement
Record a reviewed selection and proof plan before wipe-scale ingestion. Preserve exact encoded bytes and manifests regardless of the choice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A reviewed decision record selects the canonical CAS architecture.
- Viable third-party options are evaluated or explicitly ruled out.
- Migration/restore and metadata-preservation proofs are named.
- No source is ingested under an ambiguous authority model.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed decision record selects the canonical CAS architecture; viable third-party options are evaluated or explicitly ruled out; migration/restore and metadata-preservation proofs are named; no source is ingested under an ambiguous authority model.
notes:
2026-08-13 primary-doc research: casync official README describes content-defined variable chunking, compressed hash-named chunks, chunk indexes, random-access directory-tree serialization, shared chunk stores, and GC; it explicitly lists some verify/diff operations as not implemented (https://github.com/systemd/casync). Perkeep provides immutable content-addressed blobs, metadata/schema blobs, signed claims/permanodes, no-delete semantics, indexing and replication, but its current docs describe a broad personal-storage system rather than a drop-in replay CAS (https://perkeep.org/doc/overview, https://perkeep.org/doc/terms). git-annex provides content keys plus arbitrary metadata stored in its git-annex branch, but its model is filename/git tracking plus distributed key/value content, not the required manifest/replay contract (https://git-annex.branchable.com/metadata/, https://git-annex.branchable.com/how_it_works/). IPFS provides chunked DAG/CID addressing and range-friendly structures, but CIDs depend on chunking/DAG/codec parameters and are not direct file hashes for multi-block files, requiring a separate exact-byte digest authority (https://docs.ipfs.tech/concepts/content-addressing/). This is evidence only; canonical selection and proof plan remain undecided.
2026-08-13 Luna audit: canonical decision is not ready for closure. Existing evidence supports Sinex-owned MaterialManifestV1 plus exact encoded-byte BLAKE3 CAS as the reference authority. Third-party casync/Perkeep/git-annex/IPFS are not proven against replay, metadata, portability, or operational requirements and should be secondary adapters only, never replacements for Sinex provenance/manifests/exact-byte identity. Remaining blockers: route-level source-removal replay proof (y0o3.12.2/.3), manifest-root purge semantics (r6d.16), CAS-inclusive backup/restore and Beads/Dolt/topology proof (w98), portable export/import, logical source-part reconstruction, and explicit metadata fidelity when logical digest/size are unknown. Proposed exclusions: no canonical chunk/CID identity, no inferred missing legacy metadata, no unproven pack/defrag/compression semantics. Keep open pending ratification and proofs.

title: Preserve manifest-backed source material as a tombstone retention root
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ingest/finalize a source material with a MaterialManifestV1 and encoded-byte CAS object.
2. Archive/tombstone its only event so the material has no live/archived event references.
3. Run the ordinary orphan-material deletion path and CAS GC/fsck.
4. Observe that  can remove the registry row despite manifest metadata, after which CAS authority can be classified as orphaned and source-removal replay loses its root.

## Problem
Manifest-backed source material is treated as a retention root by CAS GC but not by tombstone/material deletion.

## Expected
Ordinary cleanup retains manifest-backed material and its exact encoded bytes; only an explicit reviewed purge can remove that replay authority.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A manifest-backed source-material row cannot be deleted by ordinary orphan/tombstone cleanup.
- Manifest and encoded-byte authority remain discoverable and replayable after source removal.
- Explicit purge has an authority/review boundary.
- Focused tests prove retention and intentional purge semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest-backed source-material row cannot be deleted by ordinary orphan/tombstone cleanup; its manifest and encoded-byte authority remain discoverable and replayable after source removal; explicit purge has an authority/review boundary; focused tests prove both retention and intentional purge semantics.
notes:
Correction: the reproduction names delete_material_if_orphan as the affected repository method; the previous shell invocation stripped inline backticks from the description only.
2026-08-13 implementation ecab6b5e9: periodic stale-registry GC now excludes rows whose metadata carries material_manifest in both candidate selection and final DELETE predicate; regression test periodic_gc_retains_stale_material_with_manifest_replay_authority passed in xtask invocation 2007349. Remaining AC: delete_material_if_orphan/tombstone path still needs the same retention boundary; explicit reviewed purge semantics and production source-removal replay proof remain open.
2026-08-13 follow-up eb815cb88: delete_material_if_orphan now also refuses ordinary deletion when metadata contains material_manifest; repository regression delete_material_preserves_manifest_replay_root passed in xtask invocation 2007350. Periodic GC proof remains 2007349. Explicit reviewed purge and production source-removal replay remain unresolved.

title: Expose canonical runtime liveness in system health
description: Implement the first executable migration of the canonical runtime_liveness evaluator: system.health, /health, and sinexctl runtime health must receive unfiltered runtime evidence and expose failed/stale sources or automata instead of relying only on DB/NATS transport probes. Preserve /ready as infrastructure readiness unless current contract requires otherwise. Keep source temporal coverage, DLQ pressure, and worker progress as separate planes; do not claim the parent closed until all named consumers and children are handled.
acceptance_criteria: An unfiltered runtime evidence snapshot reaches a typed aggregate evaluated by sinex-primitives; system.health and /health expose runtime degradation/failure; sinexctl runtime health renders the aggregate; tests seed otherwise-healthy infrastructure plus a failed or stale runtime and fail against the old all-clear behavior; disabled/profile-gated/historical stopped membership semantics are explicit.

title: Bound replay scope collection and preview materialization
description: Implement the high-relevance remainder of sinex-p61n: replay previews and execution must not materialize every scope-root UUID and full StoredEvent set in one public/in-memory handoff at large reimport scale. Preserve complete processing semantics while using bounded samples/counts for preview and paged/streamed execution. Reconcile current keyset paging and cascade chunking before editing. Do not close the parent until every p61n hazard has an explicit disposition.
acceptance_criteria: At 10,001+ matching roots, preview exposes bounded sample/count rather than all root IDs; execution processes every root without one unbounded public root UUID array or full-scope Vec<StoredEvent>; focused tests exercise the real replay preview/execution route and prove complete cardinality and bounded response/memory handoff; current smaller-scope behavior remains correct.

title: Delay top-level sinexd readiness until hosted workers warm
description: The worker-level source readiness and restart jitter controls exist, but supervisor startup still emits top-level systemd READY immediately after spawning hosted workers. During cold start this reports healthy before snapshots/gap-fill and automaton durable consumers are warmed. Implement a lifecycle-safe readiness barrier or distinct process-started versus fully-warmed signal, preserving cancellation/failure propagation and avoiding deadlock when no workers are enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level readiness is not emitted before required hosted workers reach their startup barrier; worker startup failure prevents or degrades readiness explicitly; zero-worker/development modes remain correct; focused lifecycle tests prove the ordering and failure behavior.
notes:
2026-08-13 verification: landed implementation d0786419f adds supervisor HostedReadiness barrier and tests zero-worker, shutdown cancellation, and multi-worker warm ordering. xtask invocation 2007352 passed both hosted_readiness tests. AC still needs independent production startup failure/degradation evidence and review of process-global readiness lifecycle before closure.
2026-08-13 evidence: route-level manifest replay test commit 85945fdce could not reach capture because the fs source host failed to emit READY=1 within the 60s startup barrier (xtask/src/sandbox/orchestrator.rs:306). This is an independent production-path startup/readiness gap; do not treat the focused HostedReadiness tests as sufficient closure evidence.
2026-08-13 Luna audit: d0786419f proves only happy-path HostedReadiness ordering. Remaining AC is production-route lifecycle: readiness currently configures after worker spawn, uses process-global OnceLock state, lacks worker identity/failure outcome, waits through pre-ready failures that are indefinitely restarted, and has no post-ready revocation/degradation. Existing tests manually mutate barrier state and do not exercise Supervisor::run. Follow-up sinex-x9jz.1 is claimed for a supervisor-owned failure-aware barrier; the 85945fdce fs-source timeout is not itself proof of this defect.

title: Align production CAS Borg backup with deployed content-store path

Preserve the existing repository and timer policy.

title: Bridge WorkController to durable source scans and replay/import control
description:
The audit of sinex-0r01.1.1 found that a generic pause/resume/rate/concurrency wrapper is not safe to wire in yet. The existing authorities are distinct: WorkController keeps one caller-owned WorkProgress cursor; ScanPacer owns token-bucket rate state, backlog hysteresis, and transient KV progress; normal historical source scans advance the adapter cursor only through CommitFrontier after durable emission receipts; CAS material replay has no resumable checkpoint and returns Checkpoint::None; replay control persists only processed_events and the source cancel path drops the worker scan future.

Implement the bridge as one coherent operation-control slice. Preserve unlimited completion-oriented defaults. Explicit budgets must be operator selected, resumable, and checked before any destructive boundary. Do not replace source cursors, replay state, projection registry state, or backfill state with a generic item counter.

Exact integration points:
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/work_control.rs: extend or adapt the cancellation/control contract for cooperative pause, resume, and cancel while retaining bounded WorkBudget, WorkAdmission, latest-cursor progress, and explicit outcomes.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/pacing.rs: make ScanPacer use the shared cancellation/control path for rate waits and BacklogGate waits, without duplicating token accounting or applying a hidden default refusal.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/command_listener.rs:352-410 and :485-531: create and route one operation-scoped control handle for SourceScanCommand and SourceScanCancel. Add pause/resume protocol only if it has an explicit durable operation identity and terminal/partial reporting.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/dispatch.rs:73-87: pass control into the worker, distinguish cooperative cancellation from worker failure, and preserve cleanup and receipt semantics.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:707-928: add a real material-replay cursor or explicitly keep the route non-resumable and reject bounded pause/partial completion before archive compensation can be proven. Do not claim WorkProgress alone makes this route resumable.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:1448-1995 and :2318-2390: adapt normal historical/import scans around the existing adapter cursor, CommitFrontier, durable-emission receipt, and ScanPacer. WorkProgress is metadata only until the source cursor and parser checkpoint are durably persisted together.
- crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:303-313, :702-726, and :743-755 plus crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/mod.rs:372-397 and :560-616: persist operation identity, source cursor or occurrence position, budget, pause/cancel/partial outcome, and checkpoint atomically enough to resume without replaying archived scope blindly.
- Projection rebuild/invalidation remains separately gated by sinex-lk67 and its recompute-state correctness companion. Use projection_registry and scope invalidation authorities, not WorkProgress as a replacement.
- Schema apply remains atomic. Schema backfill remains on crate/sinex-schema/src/backfill.rs:136-255 and xtask/src/commands/schema.rs:140-198 until its failure-state, quiescence, preview, and database-side checkpoint work is complete.
- Material/CAS GC remains partially migrated through CAS fsck. Finish its lease/deletion receipt lifecycle with sinex-r6d.14 and sinex-cgcs before sharing destructive control.

Dependencies and related open work: sinex-w4i, sinex-vxu, sinex-tjy, sinex-r6d.14, sinex-cgcs, sinex-lk67, sinex-audit-2n9-unlimited-negctrl-cap, sinex-b8xr, and sinex-racu.
design: Use one adapter around the existing authorities. WorkCancellation should become a sticky operation control with separate pause and cancel state; pause wakes on resume and cancel, while cancel remains terminal. ScanPacer should consume the adapter instead of maintaining a second cancellation or rate-accounting implementation. The source route must commit WorkProgress only after the same durable-emission receipt that unlocks the adapter cursor. Replay checkpoint persistence must carry an opaque source progress envelope or a deliberate non-resumable state, because processed_events alone cannot resume a replay safely after archive compensation. Keep projection invalidation and schema/backfill as explicit exclusions until their own durable state machines are ready.
acceptance_criteria:
- A single operation-scoped control contract supports pause, resume, cancel, explicit item/byte/runtime/rate budgets, bounded concurrency, pressure/backlog waits, latest durable progress, and explicit completed/partial/cancelled/failed outcomes.
- The normal historical source/import route uses the shared control path only after its adapter cursor, parser checkpoint, durable-emission receipt, and operation progress can be persisted and resumed together.
- CAS material replay either gains a real durable occurrence cursor and resumable partial outcome or remains explicitly unbounded/non-resumable with a fail-closed reason; no false resumability claim is allowed.
- SourceScanCancel and any pause/resume commands are cooperative at rate/backlog waits and report terminal state through the existing progress protocol; cleanup and compensation remain correct.
- Focused real-route tests prove cancellation during rate and backlog waits, pause/resume without cursor loss, budget exhaustion before mutation, bounded admission, resume from a persisted source cursor, and replay compensation after partial/cancelled work.
- WorkController::default remains unlimited and no arbitrary runtime or throughput refusal is introduced.
- Update crate/sinexd/docs/work-control.md and the parent bead with migrated/excluded dispositions and exact verification commands.
notes:
Audit evidence gathered 2026-08-13 on current HEAD 7e4e23420. Parent remains open because the existing WorkController contract is proven only on CAS fsck. Do not implement a generic wrapper that treats ScanProgressSnapshot, replay processed_events, or a source cursor as interchangeable.
2026-08-13: CAS-owned portion advanced in commit 56701231f. Shared WorkFileAdmission now serializes destructive CAS work across processes; fsck holds it through reconciliation; drop/quarantine/finalize/restore have ownership-preserving internal variants to avoid recursive lock acquisition. Verification: xtask check -p sinexd --skip-tests passed; admission focused tests passed invocation 2007342; CAS fsck regression tests passed after moving pre-cancel handling ahead of walker construction (invocation 2007345). The bridge remains open: historical imports/replay still require durable source/occurrence cursors and coordinated cancellation/resume; no generic WorkProgress claim made.

title: Persist canonical manifests through owned CAS staging and transaction leases
description:
The canonical manifest is intentionally staged in the assembler state directory, outside the configured CAS root, but finalize.rs currently calls the external-path store_file API. That rejects the path as escaping the CAS root, so production finalization can fail before the manifest-backed replay authority is recorded. Use the owned-temp CAS path for internal manifest staging, retain its durable lease through the same source-material metadata transaction as the material bytes, and release or recover both leases at every commit outcome.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the normal material assembler finalization route with a configured CAS root and a separate assembler state directory.
2. Allow material bytes to publish and then persist the canonical manifest.
3. Observe the manifest staging path is rejected as outside the CAS root before the database finalization transaction.

## Acceptance Criteria
A real material finalization route stages and publishes both material bytes and MaterialManifestV1 from outside the CAS root without containment errors. Both CAS write leases survive until the metadata commit is confirmed, are released on landed success or reconciled landed outcomes, and remain recoverable on pre-commit failure. The post-commit-response fault test proves manifest authority, exact replay bytes, one material/blob authority, and retry convergence.
acceptance_criteria: A real material finalization route stages and publishes both material bytes and MaterialManifestV1 from outside the CAS root without containment errors. Both CAS write leases survive until the metadata commit is confirmed, are released on landed success or reconciled landed outcomes, and remain recoverable on pre-commit failure. The post-commit-response fault test proves manifest authority, exact replay bytes, one material/blob authority, and retry convergence.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: canonical MaterialManifestV1 staging now uses the owned-temp CAS API rather than the external source-path API, so assembler state-directory staging is accepted without escaping-root failure. Manifest and material write leases are carried through the same finalization request and released on confirmed landed or reconciled outcomes; pre-commit cleanup remains recoverable. The real-route post-commit recovery test proves manifest authority, exact CAS bytes, one material/blob authority, and retry convergence. Verification: nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd --impact-mode=off --lib -E focused-finalization-three-tests; result 3 passed, 0 failed. Also passed nix develop --command xtask check -p sinexd --skip-tests. No deferred ACs.

title: Inject and prove database commit landed then returned error for CAS recovery
description:
The CAS lifecycle parent requires deterministic evidence for the failure window where CAS publish succeeds, the database transaction commit actually lands, but the caller receives an error or loses the response. The current fault-injection surface has no database-commit fault point, so the parent criterion cannot be honestly closed. Add a narrowly scoped injectable commit seam or test-double boundary that can distinguish pre-commit failure from post-commit response failure, then exercise the real CAS recovery/reconciliation path without deleting the published object or duplicating material state. Preserve the production transaction contract and keep the fault mode test-only or explicitly operator-disabled.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Publish a CAS object and execute the material persistence transaction.
2. Inject an error after the database commit has landed but before the caller observes success.
3. Run the normal reconciliation/recovery path.
4. Verify the object and material authority converge without data loss or duplicate live authority.

## Acceptance Criteria
A deterministic test proves CAS publish plus database commit landing followed by an injected post-commit error; recovery/reconciliation converges without data loss or duplicate authority. The fault point is isolated, documented, and cannot activate in normal production configuration. The test uses the real CAS lifecycle route rather than only asserting a mock callback. xtask check and focused CAS tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test proves CAS publish plus database commit landing followed by an injected post-commit error; recovery/reconciliation converges without data loss or duplicate authority. The fault point is isolated, documented, and cannot activate in normal production configuration. The test uses the real CAS lifecycle route rather than only asserting a mock callback. xtask check and focused CAS tests pass.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: deterministic post-commit response-loss seam implemented as test-only FaultPoint::MaterialCommitPostCommitResponse. The real material finalization route commits PostgreSQL, releases the material and manifest CAS leases, then injects an unknown-outcome response error. Recovery test proves the committed material remains Completed, both CAS leases are gone, the published bytes remain readable, the manifest authority is preserved, retry converges without replacing authority, and raw material/blob counts remain one each. Verification: nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd --impact-mode=off --lib -E focused-finalization-three-tests; result 3 passed, 0 failed. Also passed nix develop --command xtask check -p sinexd --skip-tests. No deferred ACs.

title: Generalize work control across replay, imports, rebuilds, and maintenance
description: The shared WorkController is proven on CAS fsck, but the integration map still leaves historical replay/import, projection rebuilds, schema/backfill, material maintenance, snapshot/restore, and other expensive operations on separate pacing/cancellation paths. Audit each caller, select the correct operation identity/cursor/outcome contract, and migrate or explicitly classify it. Preserve unlimited completion-oriented behavior by default; explicit limits must be operator-selected, resumable, and fail closed before destructive mutation. This is a pre-wipe dependency because replay/import and restore must be governable at large scale without unbounded bursts, silent partial completion, or cancellation loss.
design: Use one lane for tightly coupled caller clusters, but keep write scopes disjoint where practical. Start with replay/import and projection/material maintenance; schema convergence remains atomic and needs its own database-side checkpoint design. Bridge existing NATS cancellation and ScanPacer semantics instead of replacing them blindly. Record exclusions and follow-up bead IDs in crate/sinexd/docs/work-control.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every caller in the integration map is classified with evidence as migrated, intentionally unlimited, or separately excluded with a linked bead; replay/import and at least one rebuild/maintenance route use the shared controller where their durable cursor permits; cancellation, partial, resume, rate/concurrency, progress, and destructive-boundary behavior have real-route tests; no default arbitrary runtime/throughput refusal is introduced; the wipe gate has an explicit dependency on this disposition.

title: General bounded-work controller for maintenance and rebuild operations
description:
Define and implement a reusable control plane for expensive or destructive work across Sinex. The controller must support cooperative cancellation, bounded concurrency, item and byte budgets, optional sustained byte/item rate limits, backlog or pressure gates, progress and resumability, and an explicit destructive-boundary recheck. Apply it first to CAS fsck/orphan reconciliation and then identify the same integration point for replay/import, projection rebuilds, schema/backfill work, and other maintenance loops. Preserve operation identity, distinguish paused/cancelled/partial/failed/completed outcomes, avoid starvation between live and maintenance work, and never treat a wall-clock timeout or mtime grace period as proof of safety.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A typed controller contract exists with explicit cancellation, item/byte accounting, rate/concurrency limits, pressure gating, resumable progress, and terminal outcome states.
- Unit tests prove cancellation, budget exhaustion, fairness, and no unbounded memory accumulation.
- CAS fsck or orphan reconciliation uses the controller on a real production route and has anti-vacuity tests.
- The integration note names replay/import, projection rebuild, schema/backfill, GC, and other maintenance callers, with each classified as migrated, intentionally excluded, or tracked separately.
- Destructive operations recheck authority at the mutation boundary and do not infer safety from elapsed time alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typed controller contract covers cancellation, item/byte accounting, rate/concurrency limits, pressure gating, resumable progress, and terminal outcomes.
- Unit tests prove cancellation, budget exhaustion, fairness, and no unbounded memory accumulation.
- CAS fsck or orphan reconciliation uses the controller on a real route with anti-vacuity tests.
- Integration documentation classifies replay/import, projection rebuilds, schema/backfill, GC, and other maintenance callers.
- Destructive operations recheck authority at the mutation boundary and do not infer safety from elapsed time alone.
close_reason:
Completed the shared work-control contract and its CAS integration in commits d19706c6f, 0f5237d4a, 7d37ef4d8, and a53ffadf5.

| AC-3 | runtime | CAS fsck/orphan reconciliation route | CAS fsck uses the controller for cancellation, explicit runtime/byte/entry limits, resumable cursors, streamed reporting, and fail-closed apply boundaries; anti-vacuity tests cover cancellation, partial apply refusal, in-flight staging, and configured paths. | `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(default_fsck_options_do_not_impose_arbitrary_limits) or test(cancelled_fsck_reports_incomplete_without_scanning) or test(apply_fsck_refuses_to_delete_after_a_partial_budgeted_pass) or test(in_flight_cas_staging_file_survives_apply_fsck) or test(missing_cas_report_uses_configured_hash_path)' --impact-mode=off` | Satisfied |

title: CAS commit/delete lifecycle: leases, fsync, quarantine, reconciliation, and safe sweep
description: The CAS audit found orphan windows, ACK-before-fsync exposure, direct irreversible deletion during PostgreSQL transactions, and a scheduled orphan sweep that can delete in-flight objects. Define one recoverable lifecycle for CAS objects: ingest intent and lease, bounded streaming write/hash, fsync of object and parent directories, atomic publish, DB commit state, reconciliation/quarantine for interrupted writes, pending-delete state, reference recheck, quarantine grace period, and crash-resumable deletion. The sweep must be dry-run by default until the lifecycle is proven.
acceptance_criteria: A fault-injection or VM test proves ACKed material survives power loss or is redelivered; an in-flight object survives sweep; DB commit failure after CAS publish remains recoverable; delete failure after quarantine is resumable; orphan ratios and object age/lease rules are enforced; t3qc/cgcs/j44k dispositions are updated with real-route evidence.

title: EventBuilder's canonical .from_material().build() construction path has NO mechanism to set equivalence_key -- any handler using this documented-as-correct pattern instead of the MaterialParser pipeline is permanently un-deduplicable, including on replay
description:
The canonical event-construction pattern this project's own CLAUDE.md documents as the right way to build events -- EventPayload::from_material(material_id).build() -- has NO WAY to set equivalence_key at all. Any handler using this pattern (rather than going through the MaterialParser -> ParsedEventIntent -> adapter_source.rs pipeline) produces events that are permanently un-deduplicable.

Root cause: crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/builder.rs:228-306 -- EventBuilder<T, HasProvenance>::build() unconditionally sets equivalence_key: None at line 305, and there is NO builder method on this type to set it (confirmed: grep -n "fn equivalence_key\|\.equivalence_key(" crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/builder.rs -> nothing). A DIFFERENT builder, AutomatonOutput (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/output.rs:227, .with_equivalence_key(...)), does have this capability, but it's only used by derived-event automata (attention.rs:97, session.rs:293) -- not reachable from EventBuilder at all.

The occurrence-key-to-equivalence-key conversion that DOES exist (maybe_occurrence_key_string, crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:2648) is only reachable through the MaterialParser pipeline. Any handler that constructs an Event directly via the documented canonical pattern cannot ever carry a key, no matter what any EventContract declares for it.

Consequence: at admission, resolve_equivalence (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:633-635) short-circuits to EquivalenceOutcome::Fresh whenever event.equivalence_key is None -- so EVERY event from an affected handler is admitted fresh and un-deduplicated, forever, including on replay of the underlying material (the same gap fires again since replay re-runs through the same builder path).

Two confirmed production instances hitting this exact gap (filed separately, both relating to this bead): browser.rs's webextension-live handlers (navigation.observed/tab.activated/download.observed) and ops.rs's email.capture_runtime.observed emitter. Both have real, feasible occurrence-identity fields available in their payloads (profile_id/tab_id/url/observed_at, provider/account_binding_ref/mode_id/observed_at respectively) -- the key COULD be built, it's just structurally impossible with the builder API these handlers use.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) systematically cross-checking every source contract's declared occurrence-identity against its actual parser/handler implementation (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/builder.rs:228-306 -- confirm build() hardcodes equivalence_key: None with no setter method anywhere on EventBuilder<T, HasProvenance>.

title: tombstone-approve's 3rd (completion) write can fail after irreversible deletion already committed -- self-corrupts into a false 'Expired before approval' status via the expiry-reconciliation path, with no retry/cancel recovery
description:
handle_tombstone_approve's completion write can leave irreversibly-deleted events permanently reported as an operation that "expired before approval" -- a factually false status on the single most destructive path in the system.

crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/lifecycle.rs:886-1276 (handle_tombstone_approve):
1. Line 990-1002: update_tombstone_operation(..., "Executing", ...) -- separate write.
2. Line 1030-1034: execute_cascade_tombstone(...) -- the actual irreversible deletion, ONE atomic SQL function call (confirmed via crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence.rs:1936-1951), fine in isolation.
3. Line 1246-1266: update_tombstone_operation(..., "Completed", ...) -- a THIRD, separate DB write, made AFTER the irreversible deletion in step 2 has already committed.

If step 3 fails (network blip, pool exhaustion, crash between steps 2 and 3), the events are PERMANENTLY GONE (step 2 already committed, not rolled back), but the tombstone_operations row is stuck at "Executing" from step 1. TombstoneOperationState::can_approve()/is_cancellable() (crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/lifecycle.rs:296-305) only return true for Previewed/Pending -- "Executing" supports NEITHER retry NOR cancellation. No operator-facing recovery path exists.

Worse: reconcile_tombstone_expiry (lifecycle.rs:661-700), which fires on every status check, has guard !operation.state.is_terminal() && now > expires_at. Executing.is_terminal() is false, and expires_at is a fixed 1-hour TTL set once at preview time (TOMBSTONE_OPERATION_TTL_SECS=3600), never refreshed or cleared on approval. Once that TTL elapses, the NEXT status check silently flips the stuck-Executing row to "Expired" with error_details: "Expired before approval" -- FALSE, since approval and the permanent deletion both already happened. An operator checking status on this path would be told the operation never went through, when irreversible deletion already occurred.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for non-atomic multi-step DB writes across the workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger handle_tombstone_approve for an operation, and inject a failure (connection drop/pool exhaustion) specifically on the third write (update_tombstone_operation to Completed, lifecycle.rs:1246-1266) after execute_cascade_tombstone (step 2) has already committed.
2. Observe the tombstone_operations row is stuck at Executing.
3. Wait past the 1-hour TOMBSTONE_OPERATION_TTL_SECS and check status again -- observe reconcile_tombstone_expiry flips it to Expired with error_details 'Expired before approval', despite the deletion having actually succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: The completion write (step 3) either happens atomically with the deletion (step 2), or a stuck-Executing-past-TTL operation is reconciled to reflect that the deletion DID occur (not silently mislabeled Expired), with an operator-visible signal distinguishing 'deletion happened, completion write failed' from 'deletion never started'.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 63bf8310b, which makes the irreversible tombstone boundary durable and recoverable when the post-delete completion write is lost.

## Closure Evidence Manifest

| AC | Evidence kind | Surface | Evidence | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | runtime | tombstone cascade and lifecycle status reconciliation | The cascade serializes on the operation row, records an authoritative deletion receipt before transaction commit, and status reconciliation recovers committed deletion instead of reporting `Expired before approval`. The regression also proves the persisted receipt remains authoritative on retry. | `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(tombstone_completion_failure_is_recoverable_after_deletion_boundary) or test(tombstone_cascade_reuses_committed_receipt)' --impact-mode=off` | Satisfied |

title: distributed_rate_limit.rs: unbounded local-bucket growth (never reclaimed if non-zero) + window-seconds inconsistency between limit-math and KV-retention (enforcement bypass); curation.rs: proposal/judgment and finalize/lane-promotion are both non-atomic two-step writes; browser.rs batch insert is non-transactional
description:
Findings from wave128-040 (five findings, one file cluster):

1. HIGH -- distributed_rate_limit.rs's local buckets are never reclaimed if non-zero (distributed_rate_limit.rs:369,377,475). A one-off token with even a single request leaves a bucket at to_reserve-1 (typically 49); eviction only removes zero-value buckets. Long-lived/varied tokens grow the DashMap without bound -- memory leak.
2. HIGH -- distributed_rate_limit.rs's "window seconds" validation is inconsistent between the computed-limit path and the KV-retention path (distributed_rate_limit.rs:59,70,147). rpc_rate_limit_window_secs=0 gets .max(1) for RPM computation but raw 0 for KV max_age -- counters expire immediately while limits are computed as if 1s, an unintended enforcement bypass.
3. HIGH -- curation.rs's duplicate-judgment batch can create a permanently orphaned proposal (curation.rs:544,556,593,599). Proposal event is inserted, then judgment event inserted separately; if judgment insertion fails (transient DB error), the proposal remains persisted with no judgment, and retries create repeated orphaned proposals -- not wrapped in one transaction.
4. HIGH -- curation.rs's finalize writes the finalized claim BEFORE the lane-promotion side effect (curation.rs:701,708,710,719). If set_lane_status fails after the finalize event is already persisted, the caller sees an error but curation.finalized is durably recorded with no matching lane state change -- a retry can emit a second contradictory finalization event.
5. MEDIUM -- browser.rs's batch observation persistence is non-transactional (browser.rs:67,125,220). One insert per observation in a loop; any single failure leaves 0..N-1 persisted with no compensation, and client retry can produce partial duplicate captures.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Send single one-off-token requests repeatedly with varied tokens -- observe local_buckets grows unboundedly since non-zero buckets are never evicted.
2. Set rpc_rate_limit_window_secs=0 -- observe the computed RPM uses 1s but KV retention uses 0s, producing mismatched enforcement.
3. Trigger a judgment-event insert failure right after a proposal-event insert succeeds -- observe a permanently orphaned proposal with no judgment.
4. Trigger set_lane_status to fail right after a curation.finalized event is persisted -- observe the finalization looks failed to the caller but is durably recorded, and a retry creates a contradictory duplicate.
5. Trigger a mid-batch insert failure in browser.rs's observation loop -- observe partial persistence with no compensation.
acceptance_criteria: Rate-limit local buckets are reclaimed on a TTL/idle basis regardless of remaining credit, not just at zero. window_seconds is validated consistently across both the limit-math and KV-retention paths. curation.rs's proposal+judgment and finalize+lane-promotion sequences each run inside one transaction (or gain an explicit compensation/reconciliation path). browser.rs's batch insert either wraps in one transaction or gains idempotent retry semantics.

title: content_store: max_blob_size unenforced, path traversal via unrooted relative/absolute inputs (HIGH security), async command lock not actually held around subprocess execution; regression detector uses cumulative not windowed throughput; dlq_retry retry-count can wrap around
description:
Five findings, wave128-060:

1. ContentStoreConfig.max_blob_size is defined/documented as a limit but never enforced (content_store/mod.rs:228-243,550-551,1002-1007) -- store_file/lookup_content_key never compare file_size against it, and compute_blake3_hash always reads the full file into memory regardless of size.
2. HIGH, security -- Path traversal via unrooted relative/absolute inputs in content-store path resolution (content_store/mod.rs:534-538,710-715,752-760). Relative paths are joined with root_path with no canonical-prefix check; an input like ../etc/passwd or /etc/shadow can become a candidate outside the store root.
3. Async command serialization lock isn't actually held around subprocess execution (content_store/mod.rs:181-189). run_command_async acquires the mutex only inside a short inner scope to increment counters, then drops it before awaiting cmd.output() -- concurrent invocations can overlap process execution against the same content store, contradicting the locking/counting intent.
4. Throughput regression detector uses a cumulative-time denominator, not window-scoped (diagnostics/regression.rs:32,82-83,269-290,288). successes / self.start_time.elapsed() decays naturally over long-lived detector instances even when recent throughput is stable -- false regressions.
5. Potential retry-count wraparound in DLQ requeue header (dlq_retry.rs:447-450,491-493). retry_count + 1 with unchecked arithmetic; a corrupted/legacy u32::MAX value wraps, effectively lowering the observed count and bypassing max-retry gating.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ingest a file well above the intended max_blob_size -- observe it's fully processed with no rejection.
2. Construct a content-store path argument like ../etc/passwd relative to root_path -- observe it resolves outside the store root.
3. Run two concurrent async content-store commands -- observe they can overlap execution despite the locking/counting intent.
4. Run a long-lived regression detector and observe throughput naturally decay over elapsed time even with stable recent activity.
5. Simulate a corrupted Retry-Count header at u32::MAX -- observe the +1 wraps instead of erroring/capping.
acceptance_criteria: max_blob_size is enforced before/during ingestion. Content-store path resolution canonicalizes and verifies containment within root_path before any file operation. The async command lock is held across the actual subprocess execution, not just the counter increment. Regression detection uses a sliding/windowed throughput measure. retry_count uses checked/saturating arithmetic.

title: PrivacyEngine::apply_literal can panic on non-ASCII case-insensitive matching (byte-length mismatch between original and lowercased); contains_encrypted_token over-broadly bypasses redaction for any string containing the envelope prefix anywhere
description:
Four findings in crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy, wave128-016:

1. HIGH -- PrivacyEngine::apply_literal can panic or corrupt slice boundaries on Unicode case-insensitive matching (engine.rs:551-568). `input_lower = input.to_lowercase()` can have a different byte length than `input` for non-ASCII text (case mappings that change byte width); byte indices found in input_lower are then reused to slice `input` directly, risking out-of-range/mid-codepoint panics. A matching case-insensitive literal rule can crash privacy processing for that event.

2. HIGH -- contains_encrypted_token short-circuit is over-broad, letting mixed strings bypass redaction entirely (engine.rs:241-244). Any string containing the envelope prefix `⌜enc:v1:` anywhere -- even as plaintext/stale data, not a real encrypted token -- is treated as fully processed and skipped, even if it ALSO contains fresh unredacted sensitive content (e.g. a credit card number alongside stray envelope-prefix-looking text). Real redaction bypass.

3. MEDIUM -- Strategy::Redact's documented capture-group interpolation ($1/$2) is never implemented (mod.rs:138-141 doc vs engine.rs:453-457,579-580). The engine always uses a literal replacement string; config expecting dynamic capture-based labels silently gets the literal "TOKEN-$1" text instead of the matched capture.

4. MEDIUM (doc/contract mismatch) -- Documented SINEX_PRIVACY_BUILTIN default is "all" but the runtime default is CategorySet::None (config.rs:51-53 vs 336-338) -- a clean config/env path silently disables all built-in detection until the operator discovers the mismatch.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11). Directly relevant to the privacy-catalog work this session already flagged (sinex-t5sr).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a case-insensitive literal privacy rule and feed it text containing non-ASCII characters whose lowercase form has a different UTF-8 byte length -- observe a potential panic or corrupted slice.
2. Feed the engine a string containing both the literal envelope prefix text ⌜enc:v1: (not a real token) and separately a genuinely sensitive value like a credit card number -- observe contains_encrypted_token causes the WHOLE string to be skipped, leaking the sensitive value.
3. Configure a Strategy::Redact rule with a label containing  -- observe the literal text 'TOKEN-' in output instead of the matched capture group.
4. Check SINEX_PRIVACY_BUILTIN's actual default in config.rs vs its documented default.
acceptance_criteria: apply_literal computes byte offsets safely across the lowercase transform (or avoids the byte-length-mismatch class entirely). contains_encrypted_token's short-circuit only skips the specific matched token span, not the whole string. Redact's capture-group interpolation is implemented to match its documented contract, or the doc is corrected. SINEX_PRIVACY_BUILTIN's doc and runtime default agree.

title: xtask macros: proc-macro attribute parsing panics on malformed input instead of compile-erroring, rstest context rewriting hardcodes 'ctx'/Sandbox-only; release_readiness.rs shell-injects --base-ref unescaped (HIGH, security)
description:
Three findings across xtask macros/build tooling:

1. wave128-079: #[sinex_proptest]/#[sinex_test] proc-macro attribute parsing panics on malformed input instead of emitting a compile error (xtask/macros/src/lib.rs:837-850, `attr.parse_args().unwrap()` for #[cases]/#[timeout]/etc). A malformed test attribute aborts compilation with a raw panic trace instead of a normal diagnostic.

2. wave128-079: rstest-context rewriting hardcodes the context identifier as "ctx" and only special-cases the Sandbox type by name (xtask/macros/src/lib.rs:1025-1033,1050-1057,970-979), while the broader context-detection helper (is_context_type) also accepts TestContext. Any rstest-enabled sinex_test whose context isn't literally typed/named to match can produce a broken generated function.

3. wave128-089: HIGH, security -- release_readiness.rs interpolates --base-ref directly into a shell command string with no escaping (release_readiness.rs:220,372: `format!("xtask check --changed-strict {base_ref}")` then `ProcessBuilder::new("sh").args(["-lc", check.command.as_str()])`). A base-ref containing shell metacharacters (e.g. `foo; touch /tmp/x`) achieves arbitrary shell execution under the xtask user during the release gate.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Write a malformed #[cases] or #[timeout] attribute on a sinex_proptest/sinex_test function -- observe a raw panic trace at macro-expansion time instead of a compile error.
2. Write an rstest-enabled sinex_test whose context parameter isn't literally named ctx or typed Sandbox -- observe generated-code mismatch/compile failure.
3. Run xtask release-readiness with a --base-ref value containing shell metacharacters (e.g. 'main; touch /tmp/pwned') -- observe arbitrary shell execution.
acceptance_criteria: Proc-macro attribute parse failures emit a proper compile_error! diagnostic, not a panic. rstest context rewriting handles both Sandbox and TestContext consistently with is_context_type, without assuming a hardcoded 'ctx' identifier. release_readiness.rs passes base_ref as a properly-escaped/quoted argument (or validates it against an allowlist pattern) rather than raw string interpolation into a shell command.

title: events/persistence.rs insert_batch: reflection events silently written to core.events + chunk-local parent checks reject valid in-batch parent references
description:
Three findings in crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence.rs, wave128-003:

1. HIGH -- Reflection lane silently ignored in multi-event insert_batch path. insert_batch_unnest_in_tx (persistence.rs:1144,1153) hardcodes target table core.events and liveness lane EventStorageLane::Activity regardless of actual event source. A batch containing 2+ reflection events (source like sinex.*) gets written to core.events instead of reflection.events, and parent liveness is validated against Activity semantics even for reflection parents.

2. HIGH -- Derived parent checks are chunk-local in insert_batch, so valid in-batch parent references can be rejected. After global split into fixed chunks of 50 (persistence.rs:944,1016,1141,1152), each chunk computes its parent-allowed set from only that chunk's IDs, but ensure_no_intra_batch_synthesis_cycles runs across the FULL input. A batch of 51 derived events where event_1 (chunk 1) references event_51 (chunk 2) fails as "missing parent" despite the parent being in the same overall batch -- non-deterministic failures depending on event ordering/chunk boundaries.

3. MEDIUM -- get_cascade_ids (persistence.rs:2120, non-Tx) omits validate_cascade_table_name that the Tx sibling (persistence.rs:2901) enforces -- inconsistent defense-in-depth for the same logical operation.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call insert_batch with 2+ reflection-source events (source matching sinex.*) in one batch -- observe they land in core.events, not reflection.events.
2. Call insert_batch with 51 derived events where an early-chunk event references a late-chunk parent -- observe a spurious 'missing parent' rejection.
acceptance_criteria: insert_batch_unnest_in_tx routes by actual source_role per event, not a hardcoded Activity/core.events default. Chunk-local parent-liveness checks are computed against the full batch's ID set, not per-chunk. get_cascade_ids validates table_name in both Tx and non-Tx variants.

title: staged-source replay's error/cancel path skips the same compensation block sinex-2vve's deadlock path also never reaches -- no cascade restore, no replacement linking, on ANY early exit from dispatch_staged_source_replay; visibility-timeout probe masks real DB errors as a synthetic -1
description:
Two findings related to (but distinct from) the already-tracked sinex-2vve staged-source-replay deadlock, found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-046):

1. HIGH -- staged-source replay bypasses the non-staged replay's completion/failure compensation path entirely. In replay_events, staged scopes return DIRECTLY from dispatch_staged_source_replay (replay_writer.rs:435-446) before ever reaching the shared restore/replacement/invalidation compensation block that runs after completion for the non-staged path (replay_writer.rs:754-831). Failure scenario: a staged replay begins, the SourceScan archive/invalidation is already published, the parse command succeeds, then the source operation fails or is cancelled -- the function returns Err directly to the caller and the archived cascade is NEVER restored, replaced events are never linked, and staged-path post-processing (wait_for_replay_outputs_visible + record_event_replacements) never runs. This leaves stale archived rows and missing event lineage/visibility reconciliation, distinct from sinex-2vve's deadlock-on-success-path finding -- this is what happens when the staged path errors or is cancelled BEFORE hitting the deadlock, i.e. an even earlier failure mode in the same function.

2. MEDIUM -- collect.rs:331-335 wait_for_replay_outputs_visible's timeout path collapses genuine DB failures into a synthetic -1 via unwrap_or(-1), discarding the real error. A transient DB error occurring exactly when the visibility-probe timeout is reached returns "not visible" with visible=-1 instead of surfacing the actual database failure that caused the probe to fail -- weaker diagnostics, misclassifying a persistence/availability issue as mere timeout lag.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/{replay_writer,collect}.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch). Relates to sinex-2vve (same function, staged-source replay).

## Steps to Reproduce
1.
