title: xtask verify --dry-run reports success even when closure contracts fail; command-filtering can capture and execute prose as commands; perf-verification stages can be left phantom-in-progress on early error
description:
xtask's own closure-verification command (xtask verify, the tool used all session to check whether a Bead's closure evidence is real) can report success in dry-run mode even when the underlying closure contract is actually broken.

xtask/src/commands/verify.rs:1327:
```rust
let mut result = if overall_passed || dry_run { /* success */ } else { /* failure */ };
```
A bead with invalid evidence (non-empty matrix_errors/manifest_errors) combined with `--dry-run` returns SUCCESS regardless of overall_passed. Automation that intentionally uses --dry-run as a safe preflight-validation mode (checking contract shape before doing anything destructive) will not learn about real contract violations -- exactly backwards from what a "check without side effects" mode should do.

This is a meaningful finding given this session's own repeated theme of "verification tooling that looks load-bearing but isn't" -- xtask verify is the literal mechanism this session used to validate its own bead-closure claims.

Second finding, same file -- command-filtering inconsistency (verify.rs:1518,1522,2072,2100): `$ ...` lines in a verify section are captured as runnable commands using only self-command exclusion (no stricter `looks_like_runnable_command` filter that DOES exist and is applied elsewhere in the file), and inline-backtick extraction likewise uses the looser `looks_like_shell_command` check. Prose/example text like `` `rg this branch` `` or `$ git push (pre-push drift guard)` can be captured and executed as if it were an actual verification command.

Third finding: verify.rs:624,625,628,629,693 -- performance-verification stages (`ctx.start_stage("bench")` / `"verify"`) are not guaranteed to reach `finish_stage` on an early error return (bench::run/load_contracts/load_latest_run_rows failing before finish_stage runs), leaving stage-accounting history in an inconsistent "phantom in-progress" state.

Found via a second, narrate-through audit pass of xtask/src/commands/verify.rs (2026-08-11, gpt-5.3-codex-spark) -- this file's closure-evidence extraction logic (~lines 1466-2300) was explicitly deprioritized by the earlier audit-xtask-gates review this session for time reasons.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct a bead-closure evidence set with matrix_errors/manifest_errors present (invalid), then run xtask verify closure <id> --dry-run -- observe it reports success.
2. Add prose text like `$ git push (see pre-push drift guard)` inside a verify-section markdown block -- observe the coarse shell-prefix filter can capture and attempt to execute it.
3. Inject a failure in bench::run or load_contracts before finish_stage is called -- observe the stage remains recorded as in-progress.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above; this is the tool used this session to validate bead-closure claims, so its own vacuity holes deserve the same priority as the ones it was built to catch elsewhere.

title: core.events has zero full-text-search index -- every text-search query does a full per-row tsvector-build sequential scan, which will not return on a freshly reimported multi-million-row DB
description:
Full-text search over core.events has NO INDEX AT ALL -- every text search on a freshly reimported multi-million-row DB will be a full sequential scan of the hypertable with a per-row tsvector build. This is a mechanical, no-judgment-call reimport-scale correctness/performance risk.

to_tsvector('simple', payload::text) is computed PER-ROW at query time in: composable_query.rs:835 (PayloadFilter::TextSearch), :1114-1133 (relevance + ts_headline), embeddings.rs:344-347 (hybrid_search FTS branch), and the core.hybrid_search DB function (apply.rs:2701-2723). Checked every index declaration in defs/events.rs:535-681: ix_events_payload_gin is jsonb_path_ops (does NOT serve the @@ full-text operator) and there is no to_tsvector expression index anywhere on core.events.

Contrast: document_search.rs's FTS IS correctly backed by ix_document_chunks_text_fts -- proving the project knows how to build this index, it just wasn't applied to core.events.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read defs/events.rs:535-681's full index list for core.events -- confirm ix_events_payload_gin is jsonb_path_ops (doesn't serve @@) and no to_tsvector expression index exists.
2. Run EXPLAIN on any query using PayloadFilter::TextSearch (composable_query.rs:835), the relevance/ts_headline path (:1114-1133), or hybrid_search's FTS branch (embeddings.rs:344-347, or the core.hybrid_search DB function) against a multi-million-row core.events -- observe a full sequential scan.
3. Compare against document_search.rs's ix_document_chunks_text_fts, proving the project already knows the correct pattern for a sibling table.
acceptance_criteria: core.events gains a to_tsvector expression GIN index (matching ix_document_chunks_text_fts's pattern) covering whatever text-search surface PayloadFilter::TextSearch/hybrid_search actually query, verified via EXPLAIN showing an index scan instead of a sequential scan on a representative reimport-scale row count.

Fix: FTS index verified used by the production query shape -- crate/sinex-db/tests/schema/schema_tests_index_tests.rs's test_events_text_search_index_is_used_by_production_query_shape corrected to insert 201 real rows (via ctx.create_source_material) and ANALYZE core.events before EXPLAIN, since an empty never-analyzed table made enable_seqscan=off insufficient to force the planner's hand (seq scan cost near-zero at low row counts) -- the test was vacuously passing for the wrong reason. title: sinex-db's write chokepoint is unenforced (only runtime sqlx::query forbidden, not the query!/query_as! macro forms) and is already breached in 3 live production sites -- one writes a reserved metadata key directly, one leaves dangling tagged_items on TTL delete, one permanently stalls materials at status=sensing
description:
The DbPoolExt write chokepoint ("never raw sqlx::query!/query_as! on a pool outside repositories") is convention-only, NOT enforced -- and it's already breached in 3 concrete live production sites.

xtask/src/commands/lint_forbidden.rs:188-196 forbids only RUNTIME sqlx::query(/sqlx::query_as(. The compile-checked macro forms sqlx::query!/query_as! are entirely unpoliced -- ladder level 6 (convention only) for a doctrine CLAUDE.md states as a hard rule.

1a. HIGH, reimport-relevant -- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:1053-1062:
    sqlx::query!("UPDATE raw.source_material_registry SET metadata = $1 WHERE id = $2", ...)
SourceMaterialRepository::update_metadata_with_executor (source_materials.rs:733-783) exists precisely to prevent this: strip RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS, deep-merge via core.jsonb_merge_deep, re-apply existing system values on top. RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS (source_materials/helpers.rs:616-626) includes source_material_contract, blake3, total_bytes, staged_by, staged_on_host. The handler does read-modify-write on a snapshot + whole-object SET, writing the RESERVED source_material_contract key directly, and is a lost-update vs any concurrent assembler write.

1b. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/api/lifecycle_ttl.rs:317:
    sqlx::query!("DELETE FROM core.events WHERE id = ANY($1)", cascade_ids)
Annotations/embeddings ARE safe (core.fn_archive_before_delete trigger, sinex-schema/src/defs/events.rs:1090-1150, archives them idempotently). core.tagged_items is NOT handled by the trigger -- only by execute_cascade_archive_in_tx (persistence.rs:2414-2437), whose own comment states "tagged_items has no FK to events, so the DELETE below will not cascade -- we must remove dangling references explicitly." The TTL path leaves dangling tagged_items rows and writes no audit.archived_tagged_items copy, which core.execute_cascade_restore (apply.rs:2455-2468) reads on restore. Also missing the archived_count != requested_count assertion (persistence.rs:2449).

1c. MED-LOW -- sources.rs:245, api/handlers/ops.rs:1951, api/handlers/ops/media.rs:392: "UPDATE raw.source_material_registry SET total_bytes = $1" bypasses finalize_in_flight_as/update_material_state (source_materials.rs:213-256): sets the column but not metadata.source_material_contract.statistics.total_bytes, status, or end_time. Material stays status='sensing' forever, permanently listed by list_stale_sensing (source_materials.rs:437).

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. grep -n 'sqlx::query!' crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:1053-1062 -- confirm a raw UPDATE on raw.source_material_registry.metadata that bypasses update_metadata_with_executor's RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS stripping and deep-merge.
2. Trigger a TTL-driven event delete (lifecycle_ttl.rs:317) on an event with tagged_items -- confirm the rows are left dangling with no archived_tagged_items copy for restore.
3. Call the total_bytes-only UPDATE path (sources.rs:245 / ops.rs:1951 / media.rs:392) -- confirm the material's status stays 'sensing' forever and is permanently flagged by list_stale_sensing.
acceptance_criteria: xtask/src/commands/lint_forbidden.rs's forbidden-pattern check is extended to also catch bare sqlx::query!/query_as! on core/raw schema tables outside crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (or an equivalent stronger-than-convention enforcement per the type-enforcement ladder). All 3 concrete breach sites are migrated to their existing repository methods (update_metadata_with_executor, the tagged_items-aware cascade archive path, finalize_in_flight_as/update_material_state).
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: 3 named sqlx::query!/query_as! sites that were bypassing the repository chokepoint routed through it, plus a lint extension added to catch the pattern class going forward. Verified via xtask check --lint + xtask test -p sinex-db on the merged commit.

title: a material stuck in AssemblyPhase::Finalizing (e.g. a panicked detached finalize worker) has no stale-sweep, no re-drive, no redelivery, and no telemetry -- only a full sinexd restart recovers it
description:
A material stuck in AssemblyPhase::Finalizing is invisible to BOTH recovery mechanisms, permanently -- no stale sweep, no re-drive, no redelivery, no telemetry. Only a full process restart (WAL replay) recovers it.

maintenance.rs:265-266 -- find_stale_materials unconditionally skips Finalizing with NO age bound:
    if state.phase == state::AssemblyPhase::Finalizing { continue; }
maintenance.rs:317 -- redrive_pending_finalizes likewise excludes Finalizing.

dispatch_finalize (finalize.rs:538-573) spawns a DETACHED tokio::spawn, not tracked in the JoinSet that run_with_shutdown_signal_and_ready (mod.rs:879-914) awaits. A worker that panics has its panic swallowed into a dropped JoinHandle (InFlightGuard decrements the counter, but nothing reverts the phase); a worker aborted at shutdown after the phase was set leaves the same state. The END frame was already ACKed off the WorkQueue at pipeline.rs:398-405, so JetStream will not redeliver either.

Net: a material wedged in Finalizing has no stale sweep, no re-drive, no redelivery, no telemetry -- every event referencing that material defers until its delivery budget expires (interacting with the max_deliver bypass finding, sinex-w2sg), then DLQs. Only a process restart (WAL replay) recovers it.

WAL ordering itself IS correct (verified, no finding there): io.rs:881 sets force_sync for Begin/End, and mark_ready is post-commit at both sites (state.rs:440, finalize.rs:1033).

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a panic in dispatch_finalize's detached worker (finalize.rs:538-573) mid-finalization, or crash sinexd exactly during that window.
2. Observe the material's phase stays Finalizing indefinitely -- find_stale_materials (maintenance.rs:265-266) and redrive_pending_finalizes (maintenance.rs:317) both unconditionally skip that phase with no age bound, and JetStream won't redeliver since the END frame was already ACKed (pipeline.rs:398-405).
3. Confirm no telemetry surfaces the stuck material -- only a full process restart (via WAL replay) recovers it.
acceptance_criteria: find_stale_materials (or a new sweep) applies an age bound to Finalizing materials too, so a genuinely-stuck one is eventually detected and either redriven or DLQ'd with a visible record -- not silently invisible until an operator happens to restart sinexd. dispatch_finalize's detached spawn is either tracked in the JoinSet so a panic is observable, or an explicit panic-recovery path reverts the phase so the stale sweep (once fixed) can catch it.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: SATISFIED. Finalizing materials now have an age-bounded stale sweep and re-drive path; detached finalization panics restore retry state and publish visible termination evidence. Verified: nix develop --command xtask check -p sinexd; nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E "test(finalize_worker_termination_reverts_phase_and_emits_dlq)". No deferred AC.

title: max_deliver=32 safety margin over app-level DLQ thresholds is convention-only (no assertion), AND persist.rs's retryable-DB-error short-circuit bypasses the terminal-DLQ threshold entirely -- silent loss with zero alert on a WorkQueue stream under DB contention
description:
The max_deliver margin protecting against silent redelivery-exhaustion data loss is convention-only (no compile-time or runtime assertion), AND several real paths bypass the app-level DLQ thresholds entirely, burning all 32 deliveries with no app-level DLQ escape on a WorkQueue stream that never redelivers past that point.

settings.rs:22-24 states the invariant as a comment: "max_deliver ... Must be >= the highest application-side terminal threshold below so app-level DLQ routing fires before NATS silently stops redelivery." MAIN_CONSUMER_JETSTREAM_MAX_DELIVER=32, SOURCE_MATERIAL_READY_DLQ_THRESHOLD=30, MAIN_CONSUMER_TERMINAL_DLQ_THRESHOLD=10.

(a) Convention-only enforcement: no const _: () = assert!(...), no test -- grepped every reference (only run_loop.rs:35, persist.rs:711/715/850, three test uses of the terminal threshold). A 2-delivery margin on a silent-data-loss boundary, at the bottom rung of the project's own type-enforcement ladder.

(b) Several paths bypass the thresholds entirely. persist.rs:845-847:
    if sinex_db::query_helpers::is_retryable_db_error(err) { return Ok(false); }
short-circuits BEFORE the `delivered >= MAIN_CONSUMER_TERMINAL_DLQ_THRESHOLD` check at :850, and the caller then issues ChildOutcome::Retry(None) -- no delay (persist.rs:515-518). A DB down or lock-blocked for a few seconds burns all 32 deliveries almost immediately. SINEX_RAW_EVENTS is retention="work" (nixos/modules/nats.nix:190), so a message past max_deliver is never redelivered and never DLQ'd -- it sits unacked until maxAge=72h drops it. There is NO $JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES consumer anywhere in the repo (grepped *.rs and *.nix: zero hits) -- so this silent loss produces no alert of any kind.

Same shape for the confirmation-durability-gap path (children deliberately left unsettled, persist.rs:206-218) and route_validation_failure's DLQ-publish-failure retry (prepare.rs:304-306).

Amplification: RawEnvelopeSettlement NAKs the whole envelope if ANY child needs retry, so delivery count is per-message not per-event. A 100-event intent where one material lags burns the budget for all 100.

Stale doc: settings.rs:38-40 says "counts toward max_deliver (10) ... (= 50s with 5s delay)" while the adjacent SOURCE_MATERIAL_READY_DLQ_THRESHOLD doc correctly says ~150s -- the "(10)" predates the bump to 32.

Directly relevant to the imminent reimport: a DB contention window (plausible under reimport-scale write load) can silently drop messages past max_deliver with zero DLQ trace and zero alert, on the exact stream that carries reimport data.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Induce a retryable DB error (e.g. a brief connection contention window) during batch persistence.
2. Observe persist.rs:845-847 short-circuits before the terminal-DLQ threshold check, returning ChildOutcome::Retry(None) with no delay -- repeatedly, burning through MAIN_CONSUMER_JETSTREAM_MAX_DELIVER=32 deliveries quickly.
3. Observe the message then sits unacked on SINEX_RAW_EVENTS (retention=work) with no redelivery, no DLQ entry, and no advisory consumer anywhere in the repo to alert on it -- until maxAge=72h silently drops it.
acceptance_criteria: persist.rs's retryable-DB-error path respects the terminal-DLQ threshold (routes to DLQ after MAIN_CONSUMER_TERMINAL_DLQ_THRESHOLD deliveries rather than looping indefinitely with no delay) or applies real backoff so it doesn't burn the delivery budget in seconds. Add a compile-time or startup assertion that MAIN_CONSUMER_JETSTREAM_MAX_DELIVER exceeds every app-level terminal threshold, per the type-enforcement-ladder doctrine, so this invariant can't silently drift. Consider wiring a $JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES consumer so silent redelivery-exhaustion loss is at least alertable. Fix settings.rs:38-40's stale '(10)' comment.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest

AC disposition: SATISFIED.

Evidence:
- crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/settings.rs uses a compile-time assert that MAIN_CONSUMER_JETSTREAM_MAX_DELIVER strictly exceeds both application terminal thresholds.
- persist.rs routes persistence failures by actual JetStream delivery attempt, including retryable DB errors, and persists durable failure evidence before terminal DLQ settlement; below-threshold failures remain delayed retries.
- The route is exercised by the production JetStreamConsumer path, not a test-only helper.

Verification:
- nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(nats_delivery_ceiling_exceeds_every_application_terminal_threshold) | test(persistence_failure_routing_terminally_dlqs_retryable_db_errors)' --impact-mode=off (both passed in invocation 2006645)
- Companion material DLQ retryability test passed in the same invocation; one separate durable-evidence test was blocked by transient NATS 503 no responders.

No destructive operation or wipe performed.

title: content_hash is computed AFTER redact_batch mutates the payload in the only production path -- defeats sinex-w1w7's fix, currently masked by the empty privacy catalog (sinex-t5sr), arms the moment any redaction rule is enabled
description:
content_hash is computed AFTER redaction in the only production path, defeating sinex-w1w7's fix -- currently masked only because the privacy catalog is confirmed empty (sinex-t5sr), and arms the moment any privacy rule is enabled.

admission.rs:1465-1474 asserts the invariant in a comment: "sinex-w1w7: hash the candidate payload exactly as it arrived at admission, BEFORE strip_postgres_jsonb_nul_chars (below) or the downstream redact_batch chokepoint can mutate it." postgres_copy.rs:735-743 repeats the claim.

Actual production ordering is the REVERSE -- persist.rs:603-669:
- :631 `let admitted_batch = self.policy_engine.redact_batch(admitted_batch).await;` -- mutates admitted.event.payload IN PLACE (policy.rs:752-765 -> apply_policy_to_event)
- :647 plan_persistence_batch_refs(&admitted_refs) on the REDACTED batch
- :661 persist_plan(&plan) -> admission.rs:1248 admitted_to_stream_rows -> :1474 hashes the already-redacted payload

Stored content_hash = hash(redacted). classify_live_match (admission.rs:134-151) compares payload_content_hash(&candidate.payload) on the PRE-redaction candidate (admission runs in prepare_events, before persist_batch_optimized). For any SupersedeOnChange type touched by a privacy rule, an UNCHANGED re-emit never hash-matches -> Supersede -> archive + re-insert on every re-emit, indefinitely -- verbatim the churn loop sinex-w1w7 exists to prevent.

Only the NUL-stripping half of the fix is real (stripping happens inside admitted_to_stream_rows, AFTER the hash). Masked today ONLY because the dev privacy catalog is empty; arms the moment any rule is enabled -- directly relevant to this session's earlier privacy-catalog-filling discussion (sinex-4kbm, sinex-t5sr) since fixing the catalog emptiness would simultaneously ARM this bug for every SupersedeOnChange type a new rule touches.

The regression test is vacuous on this exact point: admission_test.rs:37-60 hand-constructs a LiveEquivalenceRow{content_hash: Some(original_hash.to_vec()), ..} and asserts classify_live_match prefers the stored hash -- it never exercises persist_batch_optimized, so it cannot observe that production stores a POST-redaction hash, despite its own doc comment (admission_test.rs:22-24) naming redact_batch as a mutation the fix handles.

Also: three independent content_hash computation sites (admission.rs:1474, postgres_copy.rs:631, persistence.rs:1102), each with a comment explaining why ITS recompute is self-consistent -- same-value-independently-re-resolved pattern, with a live divergence this time.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a privacy policy rule that redacts a field on a SupersedeOnChange event type.
2. Re-emit an unchanged event of that type through the live production path (persist.rs:603-669) -- observe redact_batch (:631) mutates the payload before admission.rs:1474 computes content_hash, so the stored hash is hash(redacted).
3. Compare against classify_live_match (admission.rs:134-151), which hashes the PRE-redaction candidate -- observe the hashes never match, causing an unnecessary archive+re-insert (Supersede) on every re-emit.
4. Read admission_test.rs:37-60's test -- confirm it hand-constructs the stored hash rather than exercising persist_batch_optimized, so it cannot catch this divergence.
acceptance_criteria: content_hash is computed once, consistently, on the SAME payload state (pre-redaction, per the existing comment's stated intent) on both the write side (admission.rs:1474/postgres_copy.rs/persistence.rs -- unify the three independent computation sites into one) and the read side (classify_live_match). A new test exercises persist_batch_optimized end-to-end with an active redaction rule and confirms an unchanged re-emit does NOT trigger Supersede. Given this session's privacy-catalog-filling work (sinex-4kbm) is expected to arm real rules, sequence this fix before or alongside that work, not after.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: privacy admission path now captures content_hash before redaction (pre-redaction), closing the gap where hash-based dedup/verification could be defeated by redaction. crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission_test.rs carries the regression test. Verified via xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(admission)' on the merged commit.

title: Id::<T>::timestamp() silently returns Timestamp::now() for a non-v7/v6/v1 UUID, fabricating a wall-clock ts_coided -- violates the project's 'never falsify provenance clocks' doctrine at the type level
description:
Id::<T>::timestamp() silently fabricates a wall-clock timestamp when the UUID isn't v7/v6/v1 -- a type-level violation of this project's hard doctrine tripwire "never falsify provenance clocks."

crate/sinex-primitives/src/ids.rs:114-127 returns Timestamp::now() when the UUID is not v7/v6/v1 (and again if extracted seconds are out of range). Callers treat the result as ts_coided:
  crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/context.rs:100,123,149 -- ts_coided: trigger_event_id.timestamp()
  crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/invalidate.rs:196 -- same
  crate/sinex-primitives/src/views/events.rs:112 -- presented as `ingested`

Id::from_uuid and FromStr are both unrestricted, so an externally-supplied non-v7 UUID (e.g. from a malformed wire payload, or a future integration accepting external ids) yields a wall-clock "interpretation time" unrelated to the actual interpretation moment -- silently, with no error, no warning. This sits one layer below every consumer that assumes the type-enforcement ladder holds for ts_coided.

Smaller version of the same hazard: Id::<T>::default() (ids.rs:131-135) minting a fresh UUIDv7 is a smaller instance for any #[derive(Default)] struct containing an Id -- a default-constructed id looks freshly-minted-now even when that's not semantically intended.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct an Id<T> from a non-v7 UUID (e.g. via Id::from_uuid or FromStr with a v4 UUID).
2. Call .timestamp() on it -- observe it returns Timestamp::now() rather than an error/None, silently.
3. Trace a consumer (context.rs:100,123,149 or invalidate.rs:196) treating this result as ts_coided -- confirm no validation catches the fabricated value before it's presented as real provenance timing.
acceptance_criteria: Id::<T>::timestamp() returns a fallible type (Option/Result) instead of silently fabricating Timestamp::now() for non-v7/v6/v1 UUIDs, and every caller (context.rs, invalidate.rs, views/events.rs) is updated to handle the failure case explicitly (propagate an error, or explicitly document+justify a deliberate fallback if one is still needed) rather than silently treating a fabricated clock as real.

title: canonicalizer/entity_extractor/tag_applier/embedding_producer/document_parser never stamp equivalence_key (the sole occurrence-dedup mechanism) or semantics_version on their emitted events -- structurally un-dedupable, mints duplicates on any restart-during-catchup
description:
semantics_version and equivalence_key are convention-only on the emission path; five registered automata set neither, and equivalence_key is the SOLE occurrence-dedup mechanism.

build_output_event (adapter/output.rs:439-478) hard-enforces declaration_id, product_class, claim_support (rejects missing at output.rs:281-330) and always stamps automaton_model (output.rs:465) -- but semantics_version (output.rs:462) and equivalence_key (output.rs:463) pass straight through from DerivedOutput, where both default to None in every constructor (automaton/output.rs:132-138, :157-165, :181-190, :207-215). Level 6 on the type-enforcement ladder for two fields CLAUDE.md explicitly lists as "set them".

Never stamped on any emission site: canonicalizer.rs, entity_extractor.rs, tag_applier.rs, embedding_producer.rs, document_parser.rs. health.rs stamps equivalence_key only on the alert path (health.rs:372), not on its main output. All of these DECLARE a semantics_version in their static DerivationOutputDeclaration (canonicalizer.rs:44, entity_extractor.rs:58, document_parser.rs:79/98, embedding_producer.rs:32, tag_applier.rs:53), so the registry-vs-runtime cross-check in registry_test.rs:86-242 passes while the persisted rows carry NULL.

equivalence_key is the SOLE occurrence-dedup mechanism -- admission.rs:633 returns early on None, so those events are structurally un-dedupable. Combined with sinex-vxu's finding (c) that mandatory catch-up scan runs on every restart, any input reprocessed after a lagging checkpoint mints permanent duplicate derived events for exactly these five automata, while their siblings are deduped. NULL semantics_version likewise makes semantics-bump-driven recompute undecidable for them.

Directly relevant to the reimport: catch-up/replay of historical material for canonicalizer/entity_extractor/tag_applier/embedding_producer/document_parser outputs will mint duplicates on any restart-during-reimport, silently, with no dedup safety net.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/ + crate/sinexd/src/automata/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a restart during a catch-up historical scan for any of canonicalizer/entity_extractor/tag_applier/embedding_producer/document_parser (mandatory per automaton_runtime.rs:260-279 on every start).
2. Observe the same input gets reprocessed and re-emitted with a fresh event id -- since equivalence_key is None (admission.rs:633 returns early on None), no dedup catches the duplicate.
3. grep -n 'equivalence_key\|semantics_version' for each of the 5 automata's output-construction call sites -- confirm none set either field despite output.rs:462-463 accepting them and CLAUDE.md documenting 'automaton_model, semantics_version, equivalence_key -- set them' as a hard requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 named automata stamps a real equivalence_key (and semantics_version, matching their already-declared DerivationOutputDeclaration value) on every emitted event, not just health.rs's alert-path partial coverage. Consider hard-enforcing this at build_output_event (output.rs:439-478) alongside the existing declaration_id/product_class/claim_support checks, matching this session's recurring theme that convention-only enforcement of a hard requirement eventually gets missed.

title: Scope-invalidation consumer is entirely unreachable in production (F1), AND the default recompute logic that would run if naively wired would clobber whole-automaton global state instead of just the invalidated scope (F2) -- must be fixed together
description:
The entire scope-invalidation consumer is unreachable in production -- every invalidation the replay cascade publishes is consumed by nobody. AND the default recompute logic that WOULD run if this were fixed naively would clobber whole-automaton state instead of just the invalidated scope. These two findings must land together: fixing F1 alone (wiring the consumer) would immediately activate F2 (the state-destroyer) for most automata.

=== F1: invalidation consumer unreachable ===
AutomatonRuntime declares manages_own_continuous_loop: false at crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/mod.rs:586. The runner branches on exactly that bit (stream/runner/automaton_runtime.rs:46-57): if capabilities.manages_own_continuous_loop { self.module.scan(...) } else { self.run_automaton_event_bridge(...) }. AutomatonRuntime::scan is the only route to run_continuous (adapter/mod.rs:539); run_continuous (adapter/run.rs:32-283) is the only caller of handle_invalidation_message, which is the only caller of prepare_invalidation/apply_prepared_invalidation. The other public entry, process_invalidation (adapter/invalidate.rs:379), has ZERO non-test callers.

Not a might-happen: crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry_test.rs:272-276 asserts !contract.manages_own_continuous_loop for EVERY registered automaton, so the dead branch is structurally guaranteed for all 16 currently-registered automata.

Meanwhile the replay cascade DOES publish invalidations, with real scope keys, on every archive: crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/collect.rs:642-700. The durable "debt" recorded alongside it (record_scope_invalidations_pending_with_tx at collect.rs:530, cleared by record_scope_invalidations_published at execution/replay_writer.rs:416) tracks only that the PUBLISH happened -- nothing tracks consumption, and nothing consumes.

Consequences: after any replay/archive/backfill, Windowed and ScopeReconciler derived outputs are never recomputed; stale outputs never archived; audit.event_replacements gets no rows from this path; projection_registry().mark_stale_by_scope_key (invalidate.rs:312) never fires. ~660 lines of invalidate.rs + run.rs's invalidation loop + invalidation.rs are dead weight that reads as live machinery, and this makes r6d.7's own "REMAINING: crash during recompute" carve-out moot in production.

Module docs assert the opposite in two places and should NOT be trusted: adapter/mod.rs:6-9 ("replay/archive therefore also records pending scope invalidations durably and drains them through operation/debt recovery" -- there is no drain) and traits.rs:196-201.

=== F2: default recompute clobbers whole-automaton state (latent behind F1) ===
Both Windowed::recompute_window (traits.rs:295-307) and ScopeReconciler::recompute_scope (traits.rs:400-410) build fresh state from ONE scope's working set, then overwrite EVERYTHING: `let mut rebuilt_state = Self::State::default(); ...; *state = rebuilt_state;`. No automaton overrides either (rg 'fn recompute_scope|fn recompute_window' crate/sinexd/src/automata/ -> zero hits).

The states overwritten are GLOBAL, not per-scope: EnricherState.entities (HashMap, cap 20000, entity_enricher.rs:49-58), HealthState.component_health (health.rs:170-174), RelationExtractorState.window (relation_extractor.rs:64-79), AnalyticsState open activity window (analytics.rs:112-131), InstructionExpectationState.pending_hyprland_workspace (instruction_reconciler.rs:36-39).

Trigger would be routine once F1 is fixed: prepare_invalidation calls process_invalidation_derived for ANY model (invalidate.rs:213-226), gated only by matches_input(self.automaton.input_event_type(), ...) -- and analytics, entity-extractor, document-parser, interval-lift, instruction-reconciler ALL return "*" from the singular input_event_type(); matches_input short-circuits on "*" (invalidation.rs:145). The scope working-set query filters on the invalidated scope_key, which for a FOREIGN scope returns empty, so rebuilt_state is default() and the live accumulator is wiped -- then persisted at invalidate.rs:520-524.

WindowedWrapper IMPLEMENTS process_invalidation_derived (traits.rs:754) rather than returning empty, directly contradicting the Windowed doc's "out of scope for scope-based invalidation recompute". Smaller trap in the same wrapper: ScopeReconcilerWrapper::process_invalidation_derived hardcodes event_type: None at traits.rs:936, silently discarding a per-output with_event_type(..) set by recompute_scope, while the live path (traits.rs:887, via serialize_outputs) preserves it.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/ + crate/sinexd/src/automata/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. F1: read stream/runner/automaton_runtime.rs:46-57's branch on manages_own_continuous_loop, and registry_test.rs:272-276 asserting it's false for every registered automaton -- confirm run_continuous (the only path to invalidation handling) is structurally unreachable for all 16 automata.
2. F1: trigger a replay/archive operation and confirm via collect.rs:642-700 that invalidations ARE published, then confirm via journalctl (or code tracing) that nothing ever logs consuming/draining them.
3. F2: hypothetically wire F1's consumer, then trigger an invalidation for a foreign scope against e.g. the analytics or entity-extractor automaton (both declare input_event_type()=="*") -- trace process_invalidation_derived's scope-filtered query returning empty, rebuilt_state defaulting, and the live global accumulator (EnricherState.entities, AnalyticsState's open window, etc.) being wiped and persisted.
acceptance_criteria: F1: the invalidation consumer is actually wired into the live runtime path for all automata (not gated behind manages_own_continuous_loop, which registry_test.rs guarantees is always false). F2: recompute_window/recompute_scope's default implementations are changed to merge/patch the invalidated scope's contribution into existing state rather than wholesale-replacing global accumulator state, OR each automaton with a genuinely-global (not per-scope) state override recompute_scope/recompute_window to no-op / explicitly opt out of scope-based recompute. Both halves ship together -- do not land F1 without F2, per the reporting audit's explicit warning that doing so activates a state-destroying bug for the majority of automata (any declaring input_event_type()=="*").

title: DurableDebt-unlocked events have their only evidence trace on a 72h-max_age NATS stream with zero Postgres backing (sinex_schemas.dlq_events table exists but nothing writes to it) -- reimport DLQ evidence self-deletes after 3 days
description:
DurableDebt unlocks the source cursor permanently, but the debt record it's supposed to represent evaporates in 72 hours with zero Postgres backing -- directly relevant to the wipe decision.

durable_emission.rs:258-261 defines DurableDebt as "durably persisted to an operator-visible debt/DLQ/quarantine record before progress advances"; is_progress_unlocking() (:301) includes it; adapter_source.rs:1694 advances the cursor past it for good.

The record is a NATS message on a stream with max_age = 72h (bootstrap.rs:89 -> :200-205). sinex_schemas.dlq_events EXISTS in schema (sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:1784) but has ZERO writers/readers in crate/sinex-db or crate/sinexd outside tests (rg dlq_events crate/sinex-db/src crate/sinexd/src -> nothing). The raw-ingest DLQ has no Postgres backing.

So the cursor advances permanently past an event whose only trace self-deletes in three days, with no row in core.events and no operator-visible residue after that window.

Directly relevant to the wipe decision: post-wipe re-import will DLQ a nonzero fraction of records (schema drift, malformed historical data, etc. -- entirely expected at reimport scale), and the evidence of exactly which records were dropped has a 72h fuse. If the reimport takes longer than 72h to complete and be reviewed (plausible for a large historical corpus), or if the operator doesn't audit the DLQ within that window, there will be no way to know what was silently skipped.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a DurableDebt-unlocking event (a record that resolves via a durable DLQ write rather than a real settlement).
2. Confirm the DLQ record exists only as a NATS message (bootstrap.rs:89, max_age=72h) with no corresponding row in sinex_schemas.dlq_events.
3. grep -rn 'dlq_events' crate/sinex-db/src crate/sinexd/src -- confirm zero writers/readers despite the table existing in schema (sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:1784).
acceptance_criteria: sinex_schemas.dlq_events (or an equivalent durable table) actually gets written whenever a DurableDebt resolution occurs, so DLQ evidence survives past the NATS stream's 72h max_age. Given this session's fresh-rebuild campaign, treat this as a precondition for trusting reimport completeness signals -- flag explicitly if the reimport is expected to run longer than 72h without this fix landing first.

title: one deterministically-rejected event (bad clock, schema-invalid payload) permanently wedges its whole source's cursor -- livelock introduced by the r6d.11 durable-emission integration
description:
A rejected event permanently wedges its source's cursor -- a livelock introduced by the r6d.11 integration. One deterministically-rejectable record (bad source clock, schema-invalid payload) takes the whole source permanently offline.

prepare.rs:144-148 forwards only rejection.reason to route_validation_failure and DROPS rejection.event_id at the call site -> no settlement_registry.resolve() ever fires (the code's own TODO at prepare.rs:284 admits this).

The TODO's justification ("no trustworthy key even in principle") does NOT hold. Root cause is upstream: AdmissionRejection::with_event_id (admission.rs:337) is called in exactly TWO places (admission.rs:683, :1138), both Suppressed/demotion. Every AdmissionDecision::Rejected is built via AdmissionRejection::new(...) -> event_id: None -- INCLUDING cases where the id is in hand and logged one line above: admission.rs:723-729 PastTimestamp, :745-751 FutureTimestamp, :768-772 NegativeAnchor, :776-781 SchemaValidation (all log event_id = ?event.id).

Consequence for one deterministically-rejectable record:
 1. emit_batch_durable waits the full 30s (ADAPTER_DURABLE_EMISSION_PER_ITEM_TIMEOUT, adapter_source.rs:154) -> FailedTransient.
 2. adapter_source.rs:1706-1719 treats it as a hole -> cursor not advanced, parser rolled back.
 3. CommitFrontier head-of-line blocking (sinex-primitives/src/commit_frontier.rs:5-9) blocks every LATER record too.
 4. Next drain re-reads it, mints fresh ids, re-fails. Forever, ~30s/cycle, one new DLQ entry per cycle.

Pre-r6d.11 it DLQ'd and the cursor moved on. Fix is small: thread the AdmissionRejection (not just .reason) into route_validation_failure and populate with_event_id at the four sites where the id is known, resolving to DurableDebt after a successful DLQ write.

Directly relevant to the imminent fresh reimport: any historical import containing even one record that deterministically fails admission (bad clock, malformed payload -- both plausible in bulk historical data) will permanently stall that source's entire import, not just skip the bad record.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11), cross-referencing event_engine/jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs and event_engine/admission.rs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed a source a record that will deterministically fail admission (e.g. a far-future timestamp, or a schema-invalid payload).
2. Observe: emit_batch_durable times out after 30s (FailedTransient) since route_validation_failure never resolves the settlement registry; the cursor doesn't advance; the parser rolls back; the source re-reads and re-fails the same record every ~30s indefinitely, generating a fresh DLQ entry each cycle.
3. Read prepare.rs:284's TODO admitting event_id is never threaded through, and admission.rs:723-781's four Rejected-construction sites, each logging event.id one line above building AdmissionRejection::new(...) with no .with_event_id() call.
acceptance_criteria: route_validation_failure receives the full AdmissionRejection (not just .reason), and the four sites in admission.rs (PastTimestamp/FutureTimestamp/NegativeAnchor/SchemaValidation, :723-781) call .with_event_id() with the id already in hand. The settlement registry resolves to DurableDebt after a successful DLQ write for these paths, unlocking the source cursor exactly as it did pre-r6d.11. A test reproduces the reproduction steps above and confirms the source cursor advances past the deterministically-rejected record after one DLQ write, not forever.

Already fixed on master via PR #2615 (this session's admission/DLQ fix-fork cluster), discovered stale during TDD-audit-v2. AdmissionRejection::with_event_id() is now wired at all 5 rejection sites this bead named (MissingTimestamp/PastTimestamp/FutureTimestamp/NegativeAnchor/SchemaValidation), and prepare.rs::route_validation_failure (doc comment explicitly cites sinex-iq4f) resolves settlement_registry to DurableDebt on a successful DLQ write, unlocking the source cursor instead of livelocking.

Closure Evidence Manifest:
- AC: rejected event's cursor must advance past it (DLQ + settlement resolution), not livelock.
- Evidence: crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs:296-309 (route_validation_failure resolves DurableDebt when event_id is Some); crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:719,745,770,793,806 (.with_event_id() wired at all 5 named rejection sites).
- Verification: crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/jetstream_consumer_test.rs:2467 settlement_registry_resolves_durable_debt_for_an_admission_rejected_event -- real, non-ignored, already passing regression test (publishes a deterministically-future-timestamped event over real NATS, asserts DurableDebt resolution and non-persistence).

title: source-side durable-emission receipt timeout (30s) is 5x shorter than the event engine's own FK-deferral budget (150s) it's meant to wait out -- causes duplicate live interpretations under normal assembler lag
description:
The 30s durable-emission receipt timeout contradicts the event engine's own 150s FK-deferral budget, causing duplicate live interpretations under any assembler lag in the 30-150s regime -- the EXACT regime the engine is deliberately tuned for.

settings.rs:24-48 documents the cross-stream material race as load-bearing and budgets FK_VIOLATION_RETRY_DELAY (5s) x SOURCE_MATERIAL_READY_DLQ_THRESHOLD (30) ~= 150s, deliberately raised from a shorter 50s window because that shorter window "DLQ'd every fresh self-observation material's first events." persist.rs:804-816 correctly refuses to resolve during deferral.

But the source-side waiter gives up at 30s (adapter_source.rs:154; automaton side identical, automaton/adapter/mod.rs:46), and await_batch then CANCELS the registration (durable_emission.rs:428-436), so the eventual real settlement resolves against nothing.

Under any assembler lag between 30s and 150s -- the exact regime the engine is tuned for -- the source concludes "not settled," re-emits with FRESH event ids, while the originals persist normally on redelivery. Two live interpretations of one occurrence. Occurrence dedup saves you only if the parser supplied an occurrence key (adapter_source.rs:2647 sets equivalence_key from intent.occurrence_key, which is Option and per-parser -- not universal, see the separate finding on 5 automata never setting equivalence_key).

Two constants in one pipeline disagreeing 5x is the actionable core: the 30s source-side timeout should be raised to exceed the 150s engine-side deferral budget (or the engine-side budget lowered, if 150s is no longer actually needed), so the two halves of the same pipeline agree on how long "still settling" means.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11), cross-referencing event_engine/settings.rs and event_engine/jetstream_consumer/persist.rs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger assembler lag between 30s and 150s for a fresh material (e.g. self-observation material under load, the exact scenario settings.rs:24-48 documents as needing the 150s budget).
2. Observe the source-side receipt waiter (ADAPTER_DURABLE_EMISSION_PER_ITEM_TIMEOUT=30s, adapter_source.rs:154) times out and cancels its registration BEFORE the engine's real settlement (which can legitimately take up to 150s per FK_VIOLATION_RETRY_DELAY x SOURCE_MATERIAL_READY_DLQ_THRESHOLD).
3. Observe the source re-emits with a fresh event id while the original persists normally on redelivery -- two live rows for one occurrence, deduped only if the parser happens to set equivalence_key.
acceptance_criteria: ADAPTER_DURABLE_EMISSION_PER_ITEM_TIMEOUT (and its automaton-side twin at automaton/adapter/mod.rs:46) is raised to safely exceed the 150s FK-deferral budget, or the two constants are unified into one shared source-of-truth value so they can never disagree again -- add a compile-time or startup assertion (per the type-enforcement-ladder doctrine) that the source-side timeout always exceeds the engine-side deferral budget, so this can't silently drift apart again.

title: FileDrop replay computes anchor_byte via a path-hash while original capture uses a real append-stream offset -- the two value spaces never coincide, so every fs-watch replay duplicates history instead of superseding it
description:
FileDrop replay mints a DIFFERENT anchor_byte than the original capture, for every non-content-materialized fs event (Modified/Deleted/Moved, or Created without content staging) -- breaking the "occurrence identity stable across replay" invariant and silently duplicating fs-watch history on every replay.

- Capture: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/file_drop.rs:947-1008 emits these as MaterialAnchor::DirectoryEntry{path, content_hash:None} with a nil placeholder material_id. Because material_id is nil, adapter_source.rs:1006-1032 (materialize_adapter_record) routes it through AppendStreamAcquirer::append_with_anchor, and the PERSISTED event's anchor_byte = anchor.offset_start -- a real, monotonically-growing byte offset in the shared append-stream material (confirmed via acquisition_manager_test.rs sequences: 0,4,8,9...).
- Replay: adapter_source.rs:689-742 (replay_file_drop_materials, dispatched from scan_historical:2090-2094 whenever A::KIND==InputShapeKind::FileDrop with a replay context -- this IS the live scope-invalidation replay path, not dead code) reconstructs the same DirectoryEntry{path, content_hash:None} anchor via file_drop_replay_anchor (line 2571), then computes anchor_byte via anchor_offsets_for_materialized_record (line 787-788) whose DirectoryEntry arm (2529-2536) does hash_anchor_key_to_i64(blake3(path)) -- a PATH HASH, structurally unrelated to an append-stream offset.
- These two value spaces cannot coincide except by coincidence. So replaying a FileDrop/fs source produces a different (source_material_id, anchor_byte) than the original capture, breaking the "occurrence identity stable across replay" invariant and the archive-then-supersede lookup that depends on it -- replay silently mints an apparent NEW occurrence instead of superseding the original, duplicating fs-watch history on every replay.
- The regression test can't catch this: adapter_source_test.rs:2117-2176 (file_drop_replay_reconstructs_distinguishable_anchors_for_multiple_events). Its own docstring (2110-2113) claims it verifies the replay path "reproduce[s] the exact anchor_byte captured live," but the test body only checks the replay-reconstructed value is non-zero and differs between two paths -- it never compares against a value obtained from the actual capture code path. Classic test-mirrors-implementation false-positive-green.

This directly threatens reimport/replay correctness for every fs-watch source (a substantial fraction of sinex's capture surface) -- any replay operation touching FileDrop-shaped material will duplicate history rather than superseding it.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Capture a FileDrop-shaped fs event (e.g. a Modified event without content staging) live -- note its persisted anchor_byte (an append-stream offset, per acquisition_manager_test.rs's sequence pattern).
2. Trigger a replay operation covering that material (via the scope-invalidation replay path, adapter_source.rs:689-742).
3. Compare the replayed event's anchor_byte (computed via hash_anchor_key_to_i64(blake3(path)), adapter_source.rs:2529-2536) against the original -- observe they differ, since one is a stream offset and the other a path hash.
4. Read adapter_source_test.rs:2117-2176's docstring claiming exact-reproduction, then its body -- confirm it never compares against a real capture-path value.
acceptance_criteria: The replay path reconstructs the SAME anchor_byte value space the original capture used (the append-stream offset), not a path hash -- likely requires threading the original offset through replay context rather than recomputing from path alone. adapter_source_test.rs's test is corrected to actually assert replay-reconstructed anchor_byte equals a value obtained from the real capture code path, not just 'non-zero and distinguishable between two paths'.

title: email mailbox-export privacy redaction is structurally broken for exports with >1 message -- field-path rules only ever protect one message but the export still claims redacted:true
description:
Email mailbox-export privacy redaction is structurally broken for any export containing more than one message -- it silently protects at most one message per export call while reporting "redacted": true for the whole export.

- execute_email_mailbox_export (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/email.rs:231-340) builds an aggregate export_manifest ({..., "messages": [...], "material_exports": [...]}) and runs the WHOLE aggregate through PolicyEngine::disclose_json_value_for_event(..., "email", "email.message.received") (email.rs:273-282).
- Field-scoped privacy rules are pure JSON Pointer resolved against the ROOT of whatever value is passed (event_engine/policy.rs:1301-1327, 1026-1040) -- no wildcard/array-broadcast anywhere in the module.
- A rule naturally configured for email.message.received uses paths like /subject (as used everywhere else this event type is redacted, i.e. per single-event admission) -- those don't exist at export_manifest's root, so the rule silently no-ops. The only way to hit at all is to hardcode an absolute index, e.g. /messages/0/subject, protecting at most one message per export call.
- Confirmed by the existing test itself: ops_start_email_mailbox_export_applies_disclosure_policy (crate/sinexd/tests/api/ops_handlers_test.rs:1647-1795) hardcodes rule paths at /messages/0/... and seeds exactly ONE projected message -- never exercises message_count > 1, so it "proves" redaction while only covering the one shape where the broken mechanism happens to work. Classic test-mirrors-implementation.
- Impact: any export with >1 tracked message leaks unredacted subject/from/to/source_file/raw_material_id for every message past whichever index a rule targets, and with include_material:true leaks up to 512 chars of literal raw email body (material_exports[i].raw_message_preview, built email.rs:731-747) for all but one message -- while the operation still records "redacted": true and lists the rule's policy_ref in caveats, i.e. it looks protected.
- Global (field_path:None, whole-document regex) rules DO generalize correctly (second test at ops_handlers_test.rs:1797-1877 confirms this working case) -- only structural field-path rules are affected.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/{ops,email,media,package}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a field-scoped privacy policy rule for email.message.received targeting /subject (the normal per-single-event path).
2. Run ops.start email.mailbox-export with a mailbox containing 2+ messages and include_material:true.
3. Observe the export report claims redacted:true and lists the rule in caveats, but only messages[0]/material_exports[0] are actually redacted -- subject/from/to/raw_message_preview for every other message leak unredacted.
4. Compare to ops_handlers_test.rs:1647-1795, which only ever seeds one message and hardcodes the rule path to /messages/0/..., so it cannot catch this.
acceptance_criteria: disclose_json_value_for_event (or the export handler) applies field-path rules per-message (iterating the messages/material_exports arrays) rather than once against the aggregate manifest root, OR the policy engine gains real array-broadcast JSON-Pointer support and callers use it. A new test seeds >=3 messages with a field-path rule and asserts every message is redacted, not just index 0.

title: media on-demand capture actions (ops.start .capture-region/.record-video/.run-ocr/.run-model) bypass the private-mode/session privacy gate entirely
description:
Media on-demand capture actions (run_model/run_ocr/retry/rebuild_artifact/capture_region/record_video, dispatched via ops.start) bypass the private-mode/session gate entirely -- engaging global private mode does NOT stop these captures.

- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs:285-300 (execute_media_operation) routes all of these to execute_worker_output (media.rs:302-484), which spawns/consumes a worker command and unconditionally registers material + admits events. It never touches core.source_session_state or the privacy gate.
- The real gate exists: crate/sinexd/src/sources/session_gate.rs:106-143 (evaluate_capture_gate) composes global private mode (fail-closed) with per-session private_mode_blocked + lifecycle pause/disable (fail-open). Its only callers are media_screen_capture_driver.rs and media_audio_capture_driver.rs (verified via grep -rln "session_gate::") -- the continuous/live drivers ONLY.
- execute_session_control's own doc comment (media.rs:144-148) scopes the guarantee explicitly to "the live capture driver" -- not this file's worker-output path.
- Net effect: engaging global private mode does not stop capture if anything (automation, cron, another Write-role caller) invokes ops.start with media.screen-ocr.capture-region/.record-video/.run-ocr/media.audio-transcript.run-model etc. Reachable by any RpcRole::Write token (ops.start's role per sinex-primitives/src/rpc/ops.rs:29-35), not just Admin.

This is a real privacy-boundary gap: the one mechanism whose entire job is "stop capture when the operator says stop capture" is bypassable via the on-demand worker-output path, silently.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/{ops,email,media,package}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable global private mode (sinexctl privacy enable, or equivalent).
2. Call ops.start with media.screen-ocr.capture-region (or .record-video, .run-ocr, media.audio-transcript.run-model) using any Write-role token.
3. Observe the capture executes and events are admitted, despite private mode being active -- execute_worker_output never calls evaluate_capture_gate.
acceptance_criteria: execute_worker_output (or execute_media_operation before dispatching to it) calls evaluate_capture_gate (or an equivalent private-mode/session check) before spawning any worker command, matching the guarantee already enforced for the continuous live capture drivers. A test confirms ops.start for each of the 4 on-demand media actions is rejected/blocked while private mode is active.

title: media capture (audio-transcript + screen-ocr) drivers are fully implemented and Nix-wired but undeployable -- their source_contracts/media.rs bindings are the sole ones missing required criticality(), so flipping either Nix enable option hard-fails sinexd startup entirely
description:
Both media-capture SourceDrivers (audio-transcript and screen-ocr) are fully implemented, registered, and wired into NixOS operator-facing options -- but enabling either one hard-fails sinexd startup entirely, for the whole daemon, not just that source.

Evidence chain:
1. crate/sinexd/src/sources/media_audio_capture_driver.rs:542-545 and media_screen_capture_driver.rs:494-497 register real, fully-implemented SourceDrivers via register_source!(source_id: "media.audio-transcript"/"media.screen-ocr", driver: ...) -- real ffmpeg/grim process spawning, WAV/PNG parsing, session-gate integration, drain-safe continuous loops, with their own passing unit tests.
2. crate/sinexd/src/sources/bindings.rs:161-213 (validate_bindings) enforces sinex-sn6s: every non-proposed SourceRuntimeBinding sharing an enabled binding's source_id must declare .criticality(...) or startup hard-fails (error built at bindings.rs:194-202) -- and this is a whole-daemon boot failure, not a skip-this-source degradation ("empty match set is itself a hard error" is the documented behavior).
3. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs declares 4 non-proposed bindings for media.audio-transcript and 5 for media.screen-ocr (only on-demand-video is proposed=true). grep -n "criticality" .../source_contracts/media.rs -> ZERO matches -- none declare it.
4. Every other source_contracts/*.rs file appearing in `grep -rl "criticality" crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/` (window_manager, activitywatch, git, bookmark, system/monitor, journald, terminal/monitor, dbus, fs/parser, atuin_history, udev, browser/history, systemd) DOES declare it -- media.rs is the sole outlier.
5. nixos/modules/sources.nix:1793-1832 (mkMediaGlue) + default.nix:2649-2663 wire real operator-facing Nix options services.sinex.sources.media.screen.enable / media.audio.enable (disabled by default, default.nix:1667,1727) that, when flipped true, emit exactly one manifest binding keyed by bare source_id -- SourceBinding has no per-subject/mode selector (bindings.rs:66-100).

Consequence: flipping either Nix option causes validate_bindings to find every matching non-proposed binding missing criticality and refuse to start sinexd entirely. The two concrete media drivers are currently undeployable via their own documented enable path.

Why uncaught: bindings_test.rs:65-66 (enabling_binding_without_criticality_fails_loudly) tests the mechanism against a synthetic fixture, not the real compiled inventory -- grep -n "media" bindings_test.rs finds nothing. No test asserts "every binding reachable through a documented Nix enable-path passes validate_bindings."

Secondary note: bindings.rs:150-160's own docstring claims "none of the 12 sources currently deployed are multi-mode" as justification for coarse per-source_id (not per-subject) criticality matching -- that's stale/wrong for the compiled inventory: media.audio-transcript and media.screen-ocr are each genuinely multi-mode (staged-parser bindings + live-capture bindings sharing one source_id), exactly the over-blocking scenario the docstring flags as a known limitation it assumes doesn't yet exist.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/sources/ (outside source_contracts/) (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set services.sinex.sources.media.screen.enable = true (or media.audio.enable) in the sinnix NixOS config and rebuild/restart sinexd.
2. Observe sinexd fails to start entirely -- validate_bindings rejects every non-proposed media.rs binding for missing criticality().
3. grep -n "criticality" crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs -- confirm zero matches, versus every other source_contracts file having it.
4. grep -n "media" crate/sinexd/src/sources/bindings_test.rs -- confirm no test exercises the real compiled media binding inventory against validate_bindings.
acceptance_criteria:
- source_contracts/media.rs's non-proposed bindings declare .criticality(...) matching the pattern used by every other source contract.
- A test constructs the REAL compiled binding inventory (not a synthetic fixture) and runs validate_bindings against it, so a future new source with the same gap is caught before it reaches this state again.
- bindings.rs:150-160's docstring is corrected to acknowledge media sources are genuinely multi-mode, or the per-subject/mode selector gap it flags is addressed if that's the actual root fix.
- Manual verification: flipping services.sinex.sources.media.screen.enable / media.audio.enable in a test deployment no longer prevents sinexd from starting.

Given this session's fresh-rebuild campaign context (project memory: 'maximal bake-in (capture/interval/civil-time/schema)' was the stated goal before the one-shot rebuild), flag for operator decision whether media capture is in scope for the upcoming rebuild -- if so, this should be fixed before or as part of that work, not left for later.

title: core.events vs reflection.events routing is a runtime string-prefix convention, not compile-time-enforced -- already caused one silent pollution incident (sinex-4k4b)
description:
The "self-observation must not pollute activity surfaces" doctrine (core.events vs reflection.events routing) is enforced purely by a runtime string-prefix match, not a compile-time typestate -- and it already caused one silent-data-loss incident.

- crate/sinex-primitives/src/sources/mod.rs:197-203 -- `source_role(source: &str)`: `if source == "sinex" || source.starts_with("sinex.") || source.starts_with("sinexd.")` -> Reflection, else Activity.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/self_observation.rs:190,210,228,279,318,346,376,394,412,432,459,510,531-533,579-580,632-633 -- every self-observation payload's `#[event_payload(source = "sinex...")]` macro attribute is a plain string literal.
- crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence.rs:283-286 -- at persistence time, `source_role(event.source.as_str())` decides core.events vs reflection.events. The comment there cites a PRIOR incident (sinex-4k4b) where this silently broke sinex_telemetry.current_health.

Nothing prevents (a) a future self-observation payload's `source =` literal omitting the sinex./sinexd. prefix (typo -> silently lands in core.events, polluting activity surfaces), or (b) a future activity source-contract choosing a namespace that happens to start with sinex./sinexd. (no guard exists anywhere in the source-contract registration path against this collision). This is a real, currently-live structural gap that has already fired once, not a hypothetical.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/ lifecycle/health files (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read sources/mod.rs:197-203's source_role() -- confirm the Reflection/Activity split is a plain string prefix check.
2. Read persistence.rs:283-286's comment citing the prior sinex-4k4b incident where a naming mismatch silently broke sinex_telemetry.current_health.
3. Confirm no compile-time mechanism (a typed SourceRole marker on EventPayload, a macro-level assertion, a registration-time lint) prevents a future payload's source string from typo'ing the prefix, or a future activity source choosing a colliding namespace.
acceptance_criteria: Some structural guard is added beyond the runtime string match -- e.g. a compile-time or registration-time check that a payload's declared source_role() matches its macro-declared source string, or a typed marker that makes SourceRole part of the EventPayload trait contract rather than derived post-hoc from a string. At minimum, a lint/test enumerates every registered source's resolved SourceRole and fails CI if it doesn't match the intended activity/reflection split, rather than relying on this only being caught in production telemetry (as sinex-4k4b was).

title: staged-source replay operations deadlock forever: poll loop waits for a state transition structurally gated behind its own function returning
description:
Any replay operation that takes the staged-source branch (`ReplayScope.is_staged_source_scope()` true — source_id/source_material_id/source_version set, the "staged-source replay #1060" path) deadlocks forever and cannot terminate without a full sinexd restart.

Root cause: `dispatch_staged_source_replay` (crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:941-983) polls the operation's DB state every 250ms in an UNBOUNDED loop with no `tokio::time::timeout` — contrast with the main scan-replay path in the same file, which wraps its equivalent loop in `tokio::time::timeout(self.scan_completion_timeout, ...)` at line 599. The loop waits for `ReplayState` to reach `Completed`/`Failed`/`Cancelled`.

Every code path that could set those three terminal states is gated behind `replay_events` (the function containing this very poll loop) *returning first*:
- `Completed`: set only by `finalize_operation()` (execution/mod.rs), called by `run_operation`/`run_submitted_operation` AFTER `replay_events(...)` returns.
- `Failed`: set only by `mark_failed()`, called only from `handle_execution_finish()`, likewise invoked only after `replay_events` returns. (The one exception, `commit_recovery()` in state_machine.rs, marks stale-Executing operations Failed — but only via the once-at-startup `recover_stale_replay_operations` sweep with a 10-minute staleness threshold, not periodically.)
- `Cancelled`: set only by `finish_cancellation()`, also only reachable via `handle_execution_finish()` — same gate.

`sources/parse_listener.rs` confirms the parse side is a single synchronous request/reply (accept the parse command, ack `{accepted, error, event_count}`) with no follow-up progress/completion message published anywhere — no analogue to `SourceScanProgress`/`final_report` exists for this path.

Net effect: `dispatch_staged_source_replay`'s task blocks forever polling for a state transition that structurally cannot happen until the function it's blocking inside of returns — a genuine circular deadlock. The operation sits `Executing` until sinexd restarts, at which point the 10-minute-stale sweep force-fails it and correctly restores the archived cascade (so no permanent data loss), but every staged-source replay effectively requires a service restart to terminate, burning a live tokio task + an execution lock + an archived-but-unrestorable-until-restart cascade for its whole hung lifetime.

Also: operator-initiated Cancel doesn't help — `Cancelling` falls into the loop's `_` match arm, so it never transitions to `Cancelled` without `replay_events` returning first (the exact thing that's blocked). The operator-cancel propagation fix already applied to the main scan path (sinex-audit-replay-cancel-orphan: publish_scan_cancel + Cancelling-aware match arm at replay_writer.rs:690-713) was never extended to this path.

Confirmed zero test coverage: grepped tests/{abort,bookkeeping,execution_failures,execution_outcome}.rs and replay_control_test.rs/validation_test.rs for staged_source/is_staged_source/dispatch_staged — zero matches.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/ (2026-08-11). Same audit confirmed the sinex-60r root_event_ids leak class (Preview-only fix, Status/List leaking) is now structurally fixed at a single chokepoint (ReplayControlResponse::success()) with no sibling-endpoint gap — no action needed there.
acceptance_criteria:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a replay operation with a staged-source scope (source_id/source_material_id/source_version set) via `ReplayControlRequest::Plan`/`Execute`.
2. Observe `dispatch_staged_source_replay` polls indefinitely — the operation never leaves `Executing` state.
3. Issue an operator Cancel against the same operation — observe it also never completes (Cancelling state falls through the loop's catch-all arm).
4. Confirm via `git grep -n "staged_source\|is_staged_source\|dispatch_staged"` across the test files listed above that no test exercises this path.

## Acceptance
- `dispatch_staged_source_replay`'s poll loop is wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout` (matching the main scan path's pattern) with timeout treated as failure+cascade-restore, OR `parse_listener.rs` is given an async completion/progress signal (mirroring `SourceScanProgress`) so state transitions aren't structurally gated behind the very function that's blocked polling for them — whichever direction is chosen should also fix operator-Cancel propagation for this path (extend the Cancelling-aware handling already present in the main scan path).
- A new test exercises a staged-source replay operation reaching a terminal state without requiring a sinexd restart.
- A new test confirms operator Cancel against a staged-source-scoped operation actually reaches Cancelled.

title: preflight verification subsystem is fully dead code (~4.2K lines, zero callers) AND its NixOS systemd wiring points at a Cargo binary that has never existed
description:

Only #[test]-level unit coverage exists (no integration test drives them through a real entry point, so CI can't catch the missing caller).

Level 2 — NixOS wiring points at a binary that doesn't exist, and defaults to hard-failing deployment:
- `nixos/modules/preflight-verification.nix:110` builds `preflightCommand` around `"${cfg.package}/bin/sinex-preflight" "verify" ...`; line 220-247 makes sinexd AND every generated source/automaton unit `after`+`requires` a `sinex-preflight.service` whose ExecStart is the same nonexistent path.
- No `[[bin]]` anywhere in the workspace (checked every member Cargo.toml) defines `sinex-preflight`. `crate/sinexd` has `sinexd` and `spool_rename_crash_harness`; `crate/sinexctl` has `sinexctl` and `sinex-mcp-server`. The path will not exist in the built derivation.
- `nixos/modules/default.nix:2313` — `services.sinex.lifecycle.preflight.enable` defaults to `true`; `default.nix:2331` — `failureAction` defaults to `"abort"`. A from-scratch deployment of this module on its OWN default settings would fail to start sinexd entirely (missing ExecStart path → sinex-preflight.service fails → requires= cascades the failure to every guarded unit).
- The only reason sinnix-prime doesn't hit this: the SEPARATE sinnix repo explicitly overrides it — `/realm/project/sinnix/modules/services/sinex/bridge.nix:158,365` sets `preflight.enable = lib.mkDefault false`. That rescue lives outside this repository; nothing here protects a third-party consumer of this module.
- Docs actively describe the illusion as real: `nixos/modules/deployment-topology.md:21,47,57,107` ("gates sinexd", "seven read-only phases"); `nixos/README.md:733` instructs operators to run `sudo -u sinex /run/current-system/sw/bin/sinex-preflight verify` — a command that cannot exist.

Interpretation: reads as a `crate/sinexd/src/bin/sinex-preflight.rs` binary that was planned or removed, while the library code, NixOS unit wiring, and docs were all left in place describing it as live. Currently harmless only because sinnix's private override disables it; if that override were ever removed (or a third party deployed this NixOS module directly), the result is either total deployment failure (enable=true default) or, if disabled, zero actual startup verification of schema presence, NATS streams, or the systemd notify contract — exactly the failure modes verification.rs/services.rs/database.rs/resources.rs were built to catch, currently unchecked at startup on every real deployment.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/ and crate/sinexd/src/runtime/preflight/ (2026-08-11). stream/ itself was reviewed in full and found solid — no new correctness bugs (backpressure, DLQ fallback, and confirmed-event-bridge ack-before-process semantics all match documented doctrine).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `grep -rn "verify_service_dependencies\|verify_end_to_end_integration\|verify_performance_baseline" crate/` — confirm no caller outside the preflight module itself.
2. `grep -rn '"sinex-preflight"' -- crate/*/Cargo.toml` (or check every member's [[bin]] list) — confirm no crate defines this binary.
3. Read nixos/modules/default.nix:2313,2331 — confirm preflight.enable defaults true and failureAction defaults abort.
4. Read /realm/project/sinnix/modules/services/sinex/bridge.nix:158,365 — confirm the only reason prod doesn't hard-fail is an external override outside this repo.

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded: either (a) build and ship the missing sinex-preflight binary wired to the existing verify_* functions, restoring the subsystem to actually gate startup as designed, or (b) remove the dead Rust module, the NixOS preflight-verification.nix wiring, and the docs describing it, since 'unfinished is not obsolete' but this has been unreferenced across 2+ major refactors with no sign of active completion intent.
- If (a): a real integration test drives sinexd startup through the preflight binary and confirms a deliberately-broken precondition (e.g. missing NATS stream) actually blocks startup.
- If (b): nixos/modules/deployment-topology.md and nixos/README.md are updated to remove the now-false operator instructions, and the sinnix bridge.nix override (now moot) is cleaned up as a followup in that repo.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above (decision + implementation + doc/rescue-override cleanup).

title: sinexctl tasks import is lossy (drops tags/due_at) and non-idempotent (never populates external_refs, so the server's own dup-reject guard never fires)
description:
`sinexctl tasks import` (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/tasks.rs:75-127, Taskwarrior JSON import) is both lossy and non-idempotent.

Lossy: the built `TaskCreateRequest` hardcodes `tags: vec![]` and `due_at: None` even though `TaskCreateRequest` supports both fields (crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/tasks.rs:77-92) and real Taskwarrior exports routinely carry both. Import silently drops them.

Non-idempotent (the more important half): `external_refs: vec![]` is never populated with the Taskwarrior UUID, even though the code already reads that UUID at tasks.rs:90 (just to gate an empty-skip). The server has a purpose-built dedup guard for exactly this case — `reject_duplicate_external_refs` in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/tasks.rs:597-629 — but it no-ops when `external_refs.is_empty()` (:602-604). Because the CLI never sends refs, running `sinexctl tasks import <file>` a second time silently duplicates every task, with no detection, no dry-run warning, and no title-based fallback dedup.

This is the session's recurring "enforcement mechanism exists but the caller never wires the field it depends on" shape: `reject_duplicate_external_refs` is real, tested-shaped guard logic sitting inert because its one intended caller doesn't populate the field it keys on.

Directly relevant to the imminent fresh reimport (sinex-kn14): if Taskwarrior import is used as part of reimport and run more than once (retry after partial failure, re-run after a fix), every prior task gets silently duplicated with no operator-visible warning.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{sources,runtime,runtime_presence,lifecycle,tasks,source_status,automata,instructions,curation,semantic,demo,config,state,gateway}.rs (2026-08-11).
acceptance_criteria:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Export a Taskwarrior task with tags and a due date to JSON.
2. Run `sinexctl tasks import <file>` — observe the created task has no tags and no due date (data loss).
3. Run `sinexctl tasks import <file>` again on the same file — observe a second, duplicate task is created with no warning or rejection, despite `reject_duplicate_external_refs` existing server-side specifically to prevent this.

## Acceptance
- `sinexctl tasks import`'s built `TaskCreateRequest` populates `tags` and `due_at` from the Taskwarrior record.
- `external_refs` is populated with the Taskwarrior UUID so `reject_duplicate_external_refs` (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/tasks.rs:597-629) actually activates on re-import.
- Re-running the reproduction above a second time either rejects/skips the duplicate with a clear message, or the CLI surfaces the server's rejection instead of silently succeeding.
