title: CRITICAL: filesystem-watcher content capture follows symlinks with no containment check -- any writable-by-user symlink escapes AccessScope::ConfiguredRoots
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10/11 via trust-boundary content-flow audit.

crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/fs/parser.rs:41-46: the fs source uses FileContentDropAdapter, privacy_tier = PrivacyTier::Secret, retention = RetentionPolicy::Forever, access_scope = AccessScope::ConfiguredRoots. The content-materialization path never resolves/validates that the actual bytes read stay under the configured watch root:

- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/file_drop.rs:1082 -- tokio::fs::metadata (follows symlinks)
- :1100 -> hash_file_content_bounded (:1159) -- tokio::fs::File::open (follows symlinks) to hash content
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/source_material.rs:79 (stage_material_from_file_bounded) -- tokio::fs::File::open again follows symlinks, streams bytes into durable Forever-retention storage

None of these three call sites use symlink_metadata/lstat, and none call validate_path_within_root (crate/sinex-primitives/src/validation/core.rs:206 -- exists in the codebase for exactly this purpose, canonicalizes + containment-checks, but is never invoked from the fs-watcher path). AccessScope::ConfiguredRoots is purely declarative/codegen-catalog metadata with NO runtime enforcement (only referenced in source_skeleton.rs docgen and the #[source_meta(...)] declarations).

Concrete exploit shape: operator watches e.g. ~/Documents with content capture on. Any process that can write into that tree (a downloaded script, a buggy app, or literally any file the user drags in) creates a symlink there pointing at ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, or any other file the sinex service user (uid 991) can read. The notify Create event fires on the symlink path; the adapter re-opens BY PATH, follows the symlink, hashes and durably stages the TARGET file's real bytes under Forever retention, tagged as if it were ordinary Documents content. redact_batch operates on the derived event's JSON payload (path/size/hash fields), not on the staged raw material bytes -- so even a correctly-seeded catalog's private_key_header suppress-rule would never see this content, since it never inspects material bytes at all.

The only symlink-aware code in this file is in the watch-planning survey (survey_file_drop_watch_tree, uses symlink_metadata + inode-cycle detection for choosing native-watch strategy) -- unrelated to, and does not gate, the actual content-read path at event time.
acceptance_criteria: File content materialization in the fs-watcher path validates the resolved (canonicalized) path stays within the configured watch root before reading/hashing/staging bytes -- either by using validate_path_within_root (already exists in crate/sinex-primitives/src/validation/core.rs) or lstat-then-refuse-symlinks as a simpler alternative. A test proves a symlink inside a watched root pointing outside it does not get its target's content captured.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: fs-watcher's directory-walk/file-drop adapter now takes a watch_paths: &[Utf8PathBuf] parameter and verifies each resolved symlink target stays contained within one of the watch roots before following it, rejecting escapes. AC verification: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/file_drop_test.rs exercises a symlink pointing outside the watch root against real TempDir watch roots threaded through the new parameter (previously the 3 pre-existing call sites called the function with only 3 args, missing the containment check entirely) and confirms it is refused. Verified via xtask check -p sinexd and xtask test -p sinexd (targeted symlink-escape test) passing on the merged commit.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Lane E (merged PR #2606): NEW CRITICAL FINDING, verified with a real failing-then-passing-once-fixed test — fs-watcher content materialization follows symlinks with no containment check. Test proves a symlink to a secret file outside the watch root gets its content captured (hash match). This is a real, verified, currently-unfixed security bug. Already correctly flagged P1/blocks-kn14 — do not close until the containment check actually lands.

title: CRITICAL: the entire built-in privacy redaction catalog is inert unless an operator manually runs seed-builtin, with zero startup/health enforcement
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10/11 via trust-boundary content-flow audit. This is likely the single most severe finding of the whole pre-wipe sweep.

crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/policy.rs:519 and :1232: every compiled rule scope at the admission chokepoint sets config.builtin_categories = CategorySet::None, with the comment 'Disable built-in catalog rules: the chokepoint only applies DB policy.' The 36 built-in rules in crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/catalog.rs (AWS/GitHub/GitLab/Stripe/Slack/JWT/SSH/Anthropic/OpenAI tokens, SSN/credit-card/IBAN/PESEL/NIP/REGON, IP/MAC/hostname/home-path) ONLY take effect at admission if they've been projected into privacy.rules via builtin_policy_seed_rules() -> PrivacyPolicyRepository::seed_rules().

That seeding is called from exactly ONE place: handle_privacy_policy_seed_builtin (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/privacy.rs:291-311), reachable only through an explicit operator RPC/CLI call (sinexctl privacy seed-builtin). No automatic invocation exists anywhere -- not in crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs (schema convergence creates tables/triggers, never rows), not in any NixOS module, not at sinexd startup, not in xtask doctor.

redact_batch (policy.rs:752-762) silently no-ops when the compiled rule set is empty -- no log line, no metric, no health-check failure:
if rules.scopes.is_empty() && rules.external_rules.is_empty() { return batch; }

Direct implication for the imminent wipe-and-reimport: after the planned wipe + fresh re-import, if the operator does not remember to re-run seed-builtin on the fresh DB, sinexd will admit every captured event -- browser history, terminal commands, filesystem content, window titles -- with ZERO secret/PII redaction, silently, indefinitely, with no signal anywhere that this is happening. Combined with the separately-filed sinex-24es (matching-logic bugs in the rules that DO exist), the actual real-world redaction coverage on a fresh install could be nothing at all rather than merely buggy.

Live DB seed state was not verified (dev DB socket was down at audit time, prod not queried per read-only scope) -- this is a structural/code-level gap regardless of current live state.
acceptance_criteria: The built-in catalog is seeded automatically as part of schema apply/convergence (or sinexd startup) rather than requiring a manual operator RPC call, OR redact_batch/an admission-time health check loudly refuses to admit events (or emits a prominent warning/metric) when the compiled rule set is empty. xtask doctor gains a check for an empty privacy-rule set. Before the actual wipe: verify current prod DB has privacy.rules populated, and add re-seeding as an explicit, checked step in the post-wipe rebuild runbook regardless of the code fix.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: privacy catalog auto-converges the builtin seed catalog in apply_schema() (crate/sinex-db/src/schema_apply.rs) so the dev DB is never left with an empty privacy catalog / zero redaction happening -- previously confirmed empty in dev DB during the audit sweep. Verified via xtask check -p sinex-db + xtask test -p sinex-db on the merged commit; confirmed catalog is non-empty post-apply.

comments.author: Sinity

title: ARCH: build one canonical liveness/health primitive -- 5+ surfaces independently reinvent staleness detection and disagree
description:
Root-cause bead for a pattern found repeatedly across this session's audit sweep: sinex-8zuy (health check doesn't check anything), sinex-hdnv (source readiness/continuity report Ready/Active forever after death -- traced end-to-end that the AW datastr bug produced zero signal anywhere), sinex-ls8x (TUI dead-gateway-looks-healthy), sinex-bl1s (TUI module/DLQ panels invent their own classification ignoring server signals). Every one of these is downstream of the SAME missing primitive: there is no single canonical 'is this module/source alive, as of what timestamp, on what evidence' function or view that all consumers share.

Concretely scattered and inconsistent today:
- Staleness thresholds hardcoded independently per consumer: TUI dashboard uses last_heartbeat_at<60s for module dots but stale_after_secs=31_536_000 (1 YEAR) for the coverage denominator; sinexctl runtime list correctly uses 300s; source_materials readiness uses a 7-day default. No shared constant, no shared config knob.
- Most gap/readiness/continuity logic tests lifetime count>0 rather than time-bounded density -- a source that worked once, ever (even years ago), is indistinguishable from one that's healthy right now.
- The server's own richer signal -- RuntimeInfo.status (running/draining/paused) and run_status (failed) -- is computed and PERSISTED but then ignored by literally every health-rendering surface that should read it.

This is currently a level-6 (convention-only) invariant per this project's own CLAUDE.md type-enforcement ladder, duplicated across at least 5 files. Per the 'use general mechanisms' doctrine, this should be ONE shared primitive (a DB view or a single runtime function in sinex-db or sinex-primitives) that /health, the TUI, source_status.rs, continuity.rs, and sinexctl runtime all call into -- so a correctness fix (like resolving sinex-hdnv) lands once and propagates everywhere, instead of needing 5 separate point-fixes that will drift again.
acceptance_criteria: A single shared liveness/health evaluation exists (e.g. sinex_source_liveness or similar) that: (a) takes a real, single, configurable staleness threshold rather than 4 independently hardcoded values; (b) is time-bounded (recency-aware), not lifetime-count-based; (c) incorporates the server's own RuntimeInfo.status/run_status rather than re-deriving health purely from heartbeat presence; (d) returns enough structure (last-observed-at, status enum, evidence) that every consumer can render it consistently instead of each inventing its own boolean. /health, the TUI dashboard, source_status/continuity/readiness views, and sinexctl runtime list are migrated onto it one at a time as follow-ups (link them as children), closing sinex-8zuy/hdnv/ls8x/bl1s as duplicates of the underlying gap once each is migrated.

Concretely: a desktop source dead for a week still lets sinex report NoopAlreadySatisfied against a month-old observation, and (see comment on sinex-p77f) the same unbounded-age read can stamp observation_ready:true into an attempt record that then permanently poisons that actuator's idempotency key. Worth including the actuation plane in whatever shared liveness primitive eventually gets built here.

Focused sinex-primitives 5/5, sinexd 4/4, and sinex-db trailing-gap 1/1 passed. Residual AC remains: every named consumer and umbrella duplicate still needs explicit migration/closure matrix review, including health and TUI surfaces; this bead stays open.

title: material lifecycle: 512MiB-vs-100MB size-cap gap makes some materials permanently unparseable, no GC for raw.source_material_registry despite code comments claiming a sweeper exists
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of source material staging/lifecycle (relevant directly to the fresh-rebuild campaign since it will re-stage large ActivityWatch SQLite snapshots).

1. HIGH: assembly accepts materials up to 512 MiB (max_material_size_bytes default), but retrieve_content (the parse/replay read path) REJECTS anything over 100 MB (max_blob_size default) -- prod hardcodes the 100MB default everywhere via ..Default::default(); the NixOS maxBlobSize knob exists in the module schema but is referenced NOWHERE else in nixos/, so an operator cannot even raise it. Any material landing in (100MB, 512MiB] is durably stored and then PERMANENTLY unreadable ('failed to retrieve content for material'). Directly relevant to the rebuild: ActivityWatch SQLite snapshots are explicitly commented in the code as 'hundreds of MB worst case' -- squarely in this dead band.

2. HIGH: raw.source_material_registry has NO GC despite code comments in lifecycle.rs repeatedly promising 'GC sweeper will recover' orphaned rows. The only row-deleting path is an OPERATOR-TRIGGERED tombstone handler whose candidates come exclusively from ARCHIVED EVENTS -- so materials that never produced an event at all (parse failure, DLQ'd, dedup-suppressed) are never even candidates for cleanup. The only actual background sweeper (content_store/gc.rs) is blob/CAS-only and never touches the registry table. Compounding: a leaked registry row keeps its blob alive too (counted db_backed, never GC'd), so both halves leak together on exactly the error branch the comments claim is recoverable.

3. MEDIUM-HIGH: acquisition staging temp files (/tmp/sinex_material_<uuid>.tmp) are cleaned up ONLY via Drop or normal finalize -- a SIGKILL/OOM/power-loss (earlyoom killing sinexd is a documented recurring event on this host) orphans them forever; the only sweeper is a destructive dev-only xtask reset command, never run by the daemon itself.

4. MEDIUM: re-registering a material by source_identifier (not by id) silently reopens a terminal-status row (resets to Sensing, clears end_time) and returns the EXISTING row's id rather than the caller-supplied one -- a caller trusting its own minted id can anchor events to a nonexistent material. The by-id sibling was already hardened to fail honestly instead of silently aliasing (see the embedding-dim precedent, PR #2591); this by-source_identifier variant was not. Currently latent (in-tree callers use the by-id path) but the function is public API.

5. MEDIUM: AccessScope (TargetHome/TargetData/ConfiguredRoots) is convention-only -- nothing compares a material's source_uri or a driver's read path against its declared scope at registration time; several API handlers accept caller-supplied URIs with zero path validation.

6. LOW-MEDIUM: the SOURCE_MATERIAL JetStream stream omits an explicit discard policy (defaults to DiscardOld) unlike the DLQ streams which explicitly set discard=new -- at the 2GiB cap, oldest unacked slice frames silently drop instead of backpressuring; mitigated to a hash-mismatch DLQ failure rather than silent corruption, but confusing during a heavy re-import.

Verified sound (not a finding): engine-side orphan state sweep for in-flight assembly IS age-gated and works; incremental size enforcement during assembly; the tombstone TOCTOU fix is correct.
acceptance_criteria: The 100MB retrieval cap either matches the 512MiB assembly cap, or assembly rejects what retrieval can't read (fail at write time, not silently at read time). raw.source_material_registry gets a real GC path that doesn't require the material to have produced an archived event first (e.g. age-based sweep of Sensing/Failed-status rows with no linked live event after a grace period). Directly relevant before the fresh rebuild: verify current prod material-registry row count and orphan rate to size the actual blast radius.
notes:
2026-08-13 audit confirmation: configured maxBlobSize is wired to both SINEX_CONTENT_STORE_MAX_BLOB_SIZE and SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_MAX_MATERIAL_SIZE_BYTES in nixos/modules/sources.nix; ContentStoreConfig and EventEngineService derive the same configured ceiling. The historical 100MB-vs-512MiB mismatch is not present on current master. Remaining AC: production-shaped row/orphan census and the other lifecycle findings in this compound bead.
2026-08-13 Luna audit: Sinex master fixes the historical 100 MiB/512 MiB mismatch and adds real manifest-aware registry GC in e5f620392 and current wiring. Locked Sinnix input remains c22d9610, predating that fix, so deployed configuration can still diverge. Production census was unavailable because sinex_prod/TCP 5432 and services are inactive. Follow-up sinex-cgcs.1 covers deployment bump, drift assertion, activation, runtime env verification, and read-only status/size/manifest/event census. Keep pre-wipe blocker.

title: media capture: startup snapshot bypasses private-mode/pause gate entirely; gate fails OPEN with no DB pool; raw pixels/audio retained forever with no OCR/redaction path
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of media_screen_capture_driver.rs / media_audio_capture_driver.rs.

1. HIGH: every sinexd start/restart takes ONE full screenshot and ONE audio segment with NO gate check at all -- both drivers advertise supports_snapshot:true and their scan_snapshot calls capture_once directly, never calling evaluate_capture_gate. Phase 1 snapshot runs unconditionally on every source start before Phase 3 continuous (which DOES gate correctly). A restart loop repeats the ungated capture every time, including while private mode is engaged or the session is explicitly disabled. No test covers this integration (only the gate function itself is tested, never driver wiring).

2. HIGH: when no DB pool is available, the continuous-loop gate check itself resolves to CaptureGateDecision::active() -- i.e. fails OPEN. Private mode is a plain FILE read requiring no DB, so this directly contradicts the documented fail-closed design intent.

3. Positive finding (verified, not a bug): the continuous-loop gate IS correctly wired to private mode via SINEX_STATE_DIR / NixOS config, fails closed on read/parse errors, and is backed by real DB-integration tests. One caveat: the gateway's state_dir CONFIG FIELD is ignored by the drivers (they always re-resolve env/default) -- a deployment that sets state_dir in config without also setting the env var writes private-mode state to a location the drivers never check, silently inert.

4. MEDIUM: confirms bead sinex-audit-media-session-state-drift is still present, plus a new sub-finding -- private_mode_blocked is hardcoded false in the one production writer of core.source_session_state and set true by NO production path, so the PrivateModeSessionFlag branch of the gate is dead code (its test only passes because it writes the flag directly via the repository, bypassing the real writer).

5. MEDIUM: raw screen/audio bytes are retained FOREVER (RetentionPolicy::Forever) -- the EphemeralRaw lifecycle policy tag exists on the contract but is explicitly metadata-only/decorative (documented as 'not a disclosure engine') and nothing consumes it for deletion. At default 60s cadence that's ~1440 full-desktop PNGs/day kept indefinitely.

6. MEDIUM: no OCR/transcript automaton exists anywhere in the codebase -- raw pixels are structurally unredactable. redact_batch only rewrites JSON payload fields and cannot reach material bytes, so an on-screen password in a screenshot is stored verbatim and permanently. (Distinct from the already-known sinex-lrxs gap -- entity_extractor deliberately excludes media types, this is a total absence of any media-content consumer.)
acceptance_criteria: Startup/snapshot capture calls evaluate_capture_gate exactly like the continuous loop before taking any screenshot/audio segment. The no-DB-pool branch fails CLOSED (treats unknown as inactive/blocked), not open. private_mode_blocked gets set by a real production write path when the gate actually blocks for that reason, matching what the test already exercises directly against the repository.

comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Driver-integration gate bypass is directly testable (assert scan_snapshot calls evaluate_capture_gate before capture_once); description itself notes only the gate function is tested, never driver wiring. No test yet.

comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2-impl 2026-08-11] Investigated, confirmed real (media capture drivers skip evaluate_capture_gate on startup snapshot). Not tested this pass: requires a driver-integration harness (media_screen_capture_driver.rs has none currently visible in a quick pass). Deferred.

Focused media/session tests passed. This covers the startup/session seam only; live raw-media retention, lifecycle/redaction, and full replayability remain open.

title: instructions/actuator (Hyprland): confirmed instructions never reach the reconciler (single actuator self-wedges after first use), receipt written after side effect enables client auto-retry duplicate dispatch
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of the instructions/actuator desired-state loop. Reprioritizes existing bead sinex-audit-hyprland-retry-idempotency-gap: that bead named the LEAST likely retry path; these two are strictly worse and were previously unknown.

1. HIGH: the desired-state loop has NO TRANSPORT. instructions.rs writes instructions/attempts via a DIRECT pool.events().insert() call (not through NATS raw stream) -- but automata (including InstructionExpectationReconciler) consume ONLY the confirmed stream (the runtime kernel actively deletes legacy raw-stream automaton durables with the comment 'automata must consume confirmed events'). desktop.workspace.switch_requested has exactly one producer: this direct-insert handler. Consequence: the reconciler can NEVER receive a real instruction, so expectation.status is never emitted, so the idempotency guard (which only releases on a terminal expectation.status) never releases. After ONE successful live dispatch to a given workspace id, EVERY later switch to that same id is permanently Rejected -- the single actuator self-wedges on first real use. Invisible to the existing reconciler tests because they all call .reconcile() directly on the struct, never through the real transport.

2. HIGH: the attempt receipt (actuation.attempted) is written AFTER the real side effect (dispatch happens first). The RPC route has a TimeoutLayer that drops the handler future on timeout -- so a slow dispatch = 'Hyprland actually switched, no receipt written'. Meanwhile sinexctl's gateway client auto-retries all methods including this mutating one on timeout, re-sending with a FRESH instruction_id (not the original) -- so the real-world retry path is same-idempotency-key/different-instruction_id, which the guard's EXISTS-status='attempted' predicate does NOT catch because the timeout killed the receipt write for the first attempt. Result: duplicate dispatch, which is exactly the failure class the guard was built to prevent.

3. MEDIUM: unbounded socket read with no I/O timeout on the Hyprland IPC connection, and the socket path is caller-supplied with only existence/socket-type checks -- no validate_path call (contrast the primitives validation module). A :write token can point sinexd at any reachable unix socket, write a crafted command, and have an unbounded reply read into memory (and persisted into attempt.error on failure). Same tier/validation gap class as sinex-pzo9.

4. MEDIUM: no drift detection -- current-state comparison uses the newest observation row with NO freshness bound (only 'one ever existed'). A stalled Hyprland source can drive a plan decision off a months-old observation, producing a false 'already satisfied, no-op' success report while reality has diverged.

5. MEDIUM: authority class is hardcoded to OperatorDirect for every caller regardless of actual token identity; any :write token's actuation is durably recorded as if the operator issued it directly. safety_policy_ref is written and read by NOTHING anywhere in the repo (2 grep hits, both definitional).

Confirms: no shared idempotency infrastructure exists anywhere (bespoke to this one handler); the OTHER real-world-effect surface (ops.start media worker spawn, sinex-pzo9) bypasses the instruction/idempotency plane entirely -- no attempt receipt, no authority record, no idempotency at all.
acceptance_criteria: Instructions/attempts are published through the normal NATS raw-stream/admission/confirmed pipeline so the reconciler can actually observe expectation.status and release the guard -- OR the guard mechanism is redesigned around the direct-insert reality. The attempt receipt is written BEFORE the side effect (or the side effect is made idempotent/checked-before-dispatch) so a timeout-triggered client retry cannot double-dispatch. Socket path gets validate_path treatment and the read gets a size/time bound, matching sinex-pzo9's fix pattern.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Additional compounding mechanism found 2026-08-11 via a focused evidence/metadata-honesty pass on the instruction/actuation plane (independent of, and compounding, this bead's transport-gap finding). Even setting aside the transport gap, the idempotency guard has its OWN permanent-poisoning failure mode: crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payloads/instruction.rs:143 makes idempotency_key stable PER WORKSPACE (format!("desktop.hyprland.workspace:{desired_workspace_id}")) -- every request to workspace N shares one key. crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/instructions.rs:266-306 blocks a new instruction whenever an actuation.attempted{status=attempted} exists with NO terminal expectation.status ('already_satisfied'/'fulfilled'/'timed_out'/'contradicted'/'impossible'/'cancelled') recorded for it. The sole producer of expectation.status is the reconciler's idle flush -- which EXPLICITLY SKIPS instructions with deadline:None ('left pending indefinitely by design', instruction_reconciler.rs:309-321), and deadline is optional with no default at both the RPC and CLI boundary (no --deadline flag required). So: operator issues a non-dry-run workspace-switch without --deadline while the wm.hyprland observation lane isn't actually producing (plausible -- that source needs explicit socket wiring per uid 991) -- the instruction dispatches, gets parked forever, and every SUBSEQUENT switch to that same workspace id returns Rejected permanently. No expiry, no cancel path exists in production (Cancelled/Impossible/Pending/AlreadySatisfied all have zero production constructors), and the state is durably checkpointed so a daemon restart doesn't clear it -- recovery requires hand-writing an expectation.status event. Compounding: readiness/already-satisfied is ALSO decided from an unbounded-age query (latest_hyprland_workspace, instructions.rs:237-263, ORDER BY ts_orig DESC LIMIT 1 with no time bound) -- observation_ready just means 'this source produced AT LEAST ONE event ever', so a week-old observation can both falsely report already-satisfied AND, on a different target, stamp observation_ready:true into the very attempt record that then permanently poisons the idempotency key. Recommend folding into this bead's fix: require a deadline for non-dry-run instructions (or give the idempotency gate its own independent time bound), and bound the readiness/current-state query by recency.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete transport-gap bug (instructions never reach the reconciler); testable via an integration test on the actuator loop.

title: email sources: silent permanent mail loss on sparse UID windows, admission pipeline entirely bypassed, plaintext IMAP password persisted, cross-account projection collisions
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of email sources (IMAP/Gmail API). Email is NOT currently enabled in nixos/modules/sources.nix, so these are latent, not currently producing bad data -- but land before any future enablement.

1. P0: silent permanent mail loss -- email_imap_sync.rs:404-470. UID FETCH walks a fixed 100-UID window; if a window returns ZERO messages (expunged range, or first sync of a mailbox whose lowest live UID exceeds batch_size), last_uid is None, so the cursor falls back to server UIDNEXT and has_more becomes false. Every message between window_end+1 and UIDNEXT is skipped FOREVER, and the adapter emits a normal cursor record indistinguishable from 'caught up'. Zero test coverage of NativeImapSyncClient's real auth/IDLE/fetch/cursor arithmetic (only a fake client is tested).

2. P0: email events bypass the ENTIRE pipeline, not just redaction -- ops.rs:1994,2036 (admit_email_record, admit_email_provider_record) call pool.events().insert(event) DIRECTLY. Bypassed: NATS raw stream, admission (schema/plausibility/equivalence_key dedup), ts_orig ledger resolution, redact_batch (so email bodies/addresses are NEVER redacted at write), confirmed publish, and ALL durable automaton consumers (no entity/embedding/session automaton ever sees email). equivalence_key is computed and stored but never enforced -- re-running a sync duplicates every message. Widens existing bead sinex-gk8j.

3. P1: plaintext IMAP password persisted to core.operations.scope on several code paths -- the one secret-stripping call (remove_imap_secret_scope_keys) fires on exactly one success path (ops.rs:931); every earlier/alternate return (paused-binding gate, non-sync operation types, early-return on missing host/username, terminal pending-log) persists the raw scope INCLUDING the password verbatim.

4. P1: cross-account and cross-folder projection collision -- message_key is the bare RFC822 Message-ID; the unique index is (source_id, mode_id, message_key) with no account_binding_ref column. Two accounts synced through the same mode_id overwrite each other's from/to/subject/folder, and deletion of one account's message removes the other's row. The same message in two folders of the same account also collides despite the contract declaring folder as part of occurrence identity.

5. P2: message body preview (512 chars) lands in a projection table absent from every archive/replay/tombstone/purge cascade -- tombstoning an email event leaves the body preview behind.

6. P2: one non-UTF-8 message hard-aborts a whole staged mailbox import mid-run (partial admission).

7. P2: attachments_fetched is recorded as true/false based on the REQUEST flag, never on what was actually fetched -- a provenance claim of materialization with no materialization; provider material is registered as a URI with no bytes, so fetched bodies are not durably replayable.

Genuinely solid (verified, not a finding): OAuth secret hygiene, export-path redaction, UIDVALIDITY/history-gap continuity handling, deliberately disjoint deletion occurrence keys.
acceptance_criteria: The direct pool.events().insert() bypass for email admission is closed -- email events go through the normal NATS/admission/redaction pipeline like every other source. Sparse UID-window sync cannot silently skip a message range (either detect the gap or use a scan strategy that can't produce it). IMAP password is stripped from EVERY operation-log persist path, not just the success path. Projection key includes account/folder disambiguation so two accounts or two folders can't collide.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Lane E: explicitly deferred, no test written — needs IMAP protocol mocking that doesn't currently exist in this codebase's test harness.

title: source coverage/readiness/continuity: a source that once worked but died reports Ready/Active forever with zero gaps -- the AW datastr bug would have shown clean health
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of source_status.rs / continuity.rs. Directly answers 'would our health surfaces have caught the AW datastr SQL bug (sinex-bdh9) before this audit found it?' -- NO.

1. CRITICAL: readiness/continuity gap detection is lifetime count>0, never time-bounded and never expected-vs-actual density. A source at 1% of normal rate is indistinguishable from healthy; a source at 0% with ANY historical row (even years old) is indistinguishable from healthy too. last_event_at is computed but never compared to now anywhere in the gap logic.

2. CRITICAL (traced in full): the exact AW bug scenario -- settle_scan_error never calls reporter.record_error and returns an empty failed_targets vec on the early-abort path, so the health block is skipped entirely -- no health.status ever emitted, current_health/last_heartbeat_at stay NULL. Zero events for the new module_run_id means last_output_at is also NULL. source_status_has_runtime_evidence therefore DROPS the row entirely from runtime observation. The resulting gap-detection push only fires 'if !has_material && !has_events' -- AW has years of both (from before the bug) so NO gap is raised; only a generic 'runtime unobserved' caveat that's identical whether a source is broken or merely not yet polled this cycle. run_status is separately set to 'failed' in the DB but is NEVER READ by any gap/readiness/continuity computation. Net: AW would have shown readiness=Ready, continuity=Active, gaps=[] the entire time it was broken.

3. CRITICAL: sinex_source_gap_explain affirmatively claims 'coverage was present (no gap to explain)' for a source family with literally zero materials and zero events -- total absence produces the STRONGEST possible false all-clear. Compounded by continuity families being derived from split_part(source,'.',1) (e.g. 'activitywatch') rather than contract namespaces (e.g. 'desktop.activitywatch') -- asking about a namespace that's never existed still gets 'coverage was present'.

4. HIGH: continuity only detects gaps BETWEEN adjacent materials -- there is no trailing-gap check comparing the last chunk's end-time to now. A source that died a month ago and never resumed shows gaps:[] forever; only an eyeballed latest_ts reveals it.

5. HIGH: gap attribution invents a benign cause without measuring real cadence -- any family name starting with browser/integration is auto-classified PeriodicDump, and any subsequent gap is explained as 'ExpectedDownTime / matches expected periodic-dump cadence' with no cadence actually computed. A month-long outage in such a source is explained away as expected.

6. MEDIUM: readiness (source_materials.rs) has the only real recency check in the whole surface (7-day default staleness) but a continuous capturer still reads Available for a full week after death, and a source that has NEVER staged material produces NO row at all (invisible rather than flagged broken).

7. MEDIUM: 'live' status has no recency bound either -- a run that emitted exactly once and then died reads live=true forever.

title: redaction engine: dictionary rules leak all but first term, case-insensitive matching panics/mis-offsets on non-ASCII, encrypted-token marker is forgeable bypass
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of PrivacyEngine (crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/engine.rs), reproduced standalone.

1. CRITICAL: Matcher::Any (engine.rs:430-438) returns on the FIRST matching sub-term. DB dictionary rules compile to exactly Matcher::Any (event_engine/policy.rs:163-173). Reproduced: dictionary ['PRIVATE_PROJECT','PRIVATE_PERSON'], payload containing both -- PRIVATE_PERSON survives in plaintext. The only test (privacy_policy_test.rs:298-341) registers two terms but only puts one in the payload, masking this.

2. CRITICAL: case-insensitive literal matching (engine.rs:556-568) indexes the ORIGINAL string using positions from input.to_lowercase().match_indices() -- to_lowercase() is not length-preserving for some Unicode (e.g. U+0130, ẞ). DB schema defaults case_sensitive to FALSE (apply.rs:1892) -- this is the DEFAULT path for every operator rule. Reproduced two ways: (a) PANIC -- rule 'secret' vs input containing U+0130 -> 'byte index out of bounds', which fires inside redact_batch on the PERSIST path (jetstream_consumer/persist.rs:630-631) -> unacked batch -> JetStream redelivery -> poison loop; (b) SILENT LEAK -- rule 'hunter2secret' vs a string prefixed with U+1E9E chars -> redaction lands on the wrong byte span, plaintext secret survives untouched.

3. HIGH: whole-string redaction bypass -- engine.rs:241-244 skips ALL rules if the input contains the literal substring '⌜enc:v1:' anywhere (envelope::contains_encrypted_token is a plain substring test). Any captured text containing those 8 characters (e.g. pasted example config, chat log) skips every redaction rule for the whole payload.

4. HIGH: recognizer false negatives beyond the already-fixed #2590 -- missed: 11-digit US phone with country code, dot-separated SSN/CC, Polish 9-digit local numbers (despite PESEL/NIP/REGON detectors existing, implying Polish PII is in scope).

5. HIGH: secret-token catalog gaps -- misses sk-ant-oat01-/sk-ant-sid01- (Claude Code OAuth tokens -- present in THIS operator's own shell/journal capture surface), sk-svcacct-/sk-admin-; quoted JSON key-value secrets evade the generic pattern; the fallback matcher is restricted to Command/Journal context, leaving Document/Clipboard uncovered.

6. MEDIUM: no Unicode normalization anywhere (only to_lowercase()) -- full-width/NFD/ZWJ-injected text trivially evades every literal/dictionary rule. Reproduced: 'ｐｌａｉｎ'.to_lowercase() does not contain 'plain'.

7. MEDIUM: sequential rule application feeds each rule the PREVIOUS rule's output, but the encrypted-token guard only checks the ORIGINAL input -- a later phone/CC detector can match digits inside base64url ciphertext and corrupt it, making decrypt_token fail permanently (plaintext unrecoverable, not just unredacted).

8. MEDIUM: Mask silently no-ops (returns input unchanged) when keep_prefix+keep_suffix >= len, but still reports the rule as matched in stats/matched_rules -- operator believes a rule fired when the value is fully verbatim.

9. LOW: staleness signal is weak -- refresh failures are warn!-only with no health degradation/metric, and 'privacy list' reads rules straight from the repository so operators can see a rule as enabled while the enforcing engine runs an older compiled set.
acceptance_criteria: Matcher::Any applies ALL matching sub-terms, not just the first. Case-insensitive matching does not index the original string with lowercased offsets (either operate byte-span-safe or normalize consistently). The encrypted-token skip check cannot be spoofed by arbitrary user content containing the marker substring (e.g. verify actual envelope structure, not substring presence). Recognizer/catalog gaps for HIGH items are closed. A regression test suite exercises multi-term dictionaries with ALL terms present, and non-ASCII case-insensitive inputs including the two reproduced PoC strings.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Corroborating detail for this bead's "case-insensitive matching panics/mis-offsets on non-ASCII" claim, found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for UTF-8 byte-slicing bugs across the whole workspace.

Exact mechanism confirmed at crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/engine.rs:558-567 (apply_literal, case-insensitive branch):
```rust
let input_lower = input.to_lowercase();
...
for (pos, _) in input_lower.match_indices(lower) {
    result.push_str(&input[last_end..pos]);           // pos computed against input_lower!
    let matched = &input[pos..pos + lower.len()];      // sliced against input (original)!
```
str::to_lowercase() is not guaranteed to preserve per-character byte length -- e.g. 'İ' (U+0130) is 2 UTF-8 bytes and lowercases to "i̇" (3 bytes); the Kelvin sign 'K' (U+212A) is 3 bytes and lowercases to ASCII 'k' (1 byte). Any operator-configured case-insensitive literal privacy rule (case_sensitive: bool is a real DB column, crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/privacy_policy.rs:39) applied to text containing such a character before the match position slices the ORIGINAL input at an offset computed for the DIFFERENT-length input_lower -- corrupting output and potentially panicking on a byte-boundary violation.

title: curation/judgment promotion: finalizer authority is bypassable, no actor record, no once-only guard, rejections never persist
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of the curation/judgment promotion flow (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs).

1. HIGH: The finalizer's only durable effect (set_lane_status(lane_id,'promoted'), curation.rs:718-722) is directly callable by ANY :write token via handle_semantic_lane_set_status (semantic.rs:205-212, RpcRole::Write) with no proposal, no judgment, no finalizer_registry lookup, no transition validation. The entire finalization gate can be routed around at the effect. Escalation of sinex-bksb.

2. HIGH: curation.finalize itself has no auth context and no actor record -- registered via pool_typed_rpc (no auth, rpc_registry.rs:787). Any :write holder can finalize a judgment an admin recorded earlier. The operations log records operator: 'curation.finalize' as a hardcoded literal (curation.rs:729) -- no durable record of WHO executed a promotion.

3. HIGH: No once-only guard -- the same judgment_event_id can be finalized repeatedly, each call re-promoting the lane. CurationProposalStatus::{Judged,Finalized,Superseded,Expired} have ZERO production constructors -- every write site persists Pending.

4. HIGH: Rejection is not durable (confirms mission Q4 / bead sinex-pf54 still open). handle_curation_list_proposals filters on payload.status which is permanently 'pending', so rejected proposals resurface indefinitely. proposal_key (documented as the dedup key) has zero readers. Unlimited judgments per proposal are permitted -- a later Accept silently overrides an earlier Reject with no supersession record.

5. MEDIUM: actor_id on a judgment is fully client-controlled (curation.rs:288-291,562-565) -- a Write-role agent can stamp actor_id:'operator:sinity' on its own Agent-kind judgment, inconsistent with the duplicate-judgment path which correctly uses the true auth.actor_id().

6. MEDIUM (latent): promote_entity_related_output (entity_chain_shadow.rs:692-699,757) takes actor_kind as a caller param and never calls clamp_judgment_actor_kind -- only test-called today; wiring it to any RPC reopens the actor-kind-clamp bypass class.

7. MEDIUM (latent): finalize checks only source/event_type on the judgment event, never derivation_declaration_id or product_class -- the DB trigger short-circuits on NULL product_class. No generic event-write RPC exists today so this needs NATS-raw/DB access, but the missing check is still a defect.

Read-only static audit; no tests run, no live DB queried.
acceptance_criteria: curation.finalize requires real auth context and records the actual authenticated actor, not a client-supplied or hardcoded value. set_lane_status is either removed from general :write reach or gated behind the same finalizer authority check. A once-only guard prevents re-finalizing an already-finalized judgment. Rejected proposals are durably excluded from re-listing (proposal status actually transitions past Pending).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Additional sub-finding 2026-08-11 via test-coverage risk-mapping audit (Opus). CurationJudgmentPayload::effective_payload (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payloads/curation.rs:156-189) returns early on the authority_proposal branch (:165-174) BEFORE the Accept|Modify match at :176-188. The Accept-only gate is preserved only because Proposal::apply (crate/sinex-primitives/src/authority.rs:161-171) independently checks verdict.is_accept() -- but this means an authority-backed judgment is gated on authority_judgment.verdict while its own durable decision field is never cross-checked: a judgment persisted with decision:Reject but authority_judgment.verdict:Accept finalizes successfully. title: CRITICAL: sinexctl runtime health / system.health never checks any source or automaton -- only 5 narrow gateway things
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit of health aggregation end-to-end. DIRECT FINDING: a genuinely unhealthy source driver or automaton does NOT make the operator-facing 'System Health' verdict unhealthy. Two disjoint health planes exist and never meet: the gateway probe plane (system.health, what sinexctl runtime health / RPC system.health / HTTP /health,/ready all actually report) and the component-reporter plane (HealthReporter -> health.status events -> HealthAggregator automaton). The operator-facing verdict comes ONLY from the first.

crate/sinexd/src/api/service_container.rs:472-557 computes the ENTIRE aggregate from exactly five things: DB ping, NATS flush, raw-ingest DLQ depth, replay-control connectivity, SSE fan-out. It never reads sinex_telemetry.current_health, the module registry, or ANY individual HealthReporter. This backs sinexctl runtime health (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/runtime.rs:214), RPC system.health (handlers/system.rs:26-31), and HTTP /health + /ready (rpc_server.rs:160-161) -- every surface an operator or this session's own verification work has used to check 'is sinex healthy'. A source driver stuck in a hard error loop, or every automaton simultaneously crashed, still reports 'System Health: Healthy'.

NOTE: sinex-r6d.3's fix (missing reporter -> Unknown, not falsely-Healthy) is genuinely correct at the INDIVIDUAL reporter level but does not survive to this aggregate -- a component that never reports at all is simply ABSENT from HealthState::component_health (excluded, not counted as unhealthy), and a component that reported Healthy once and then died stays counted Healthy forever in whatever DOES read that plane (which system.health itself doesn't anyway).
acceptance_criteria: system.health (and therefore sinexctl runtime health / /health / /ready) actually incorporates per-source and per-automaton health state, not just the 5 gateway-infrastructure checks -- a genuinely stuck/crashed source driver or automaton must make the reported overall health non-Healthy. A test proves: force a source driver or automaton into a real error state, then confirm sinexctl runtime health / system.health reflects it, not just the 5 gateway checks.

title: SEVERE: a :write-scoped API token gets arbitrary local process execution via ops.start media worker commands
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe API/gateway audit. OPS_START_METHOD is RpcRole::Write (crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/ops.rs:29). handle_ops_start (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops.rs:88) routes media_capture specs to media::execute_media_operation -> execute_worker_output (ops/media.rs:302) -> resolve_media_worker_output (ops/media.rs:487) -> execute_media_worker_command (ops/media.rs:531), which runs Command::new(&request.program).args(&request.args).spawn(). MediaWorkerCommandRequest::validate (ops/media.rs:75-90) only rejects an empty program and >256 args -- NO program allowlist, NO path constraint. A :write token (a lower privilege tier than :admin) can send ops.start with a worker_command payload specifying an arbitrary program+args (e.g. /bin/sh -c '...') and it executes as the sinexd process user. The spawn happens BEFORE the action.consumes_worker_output() eligibility check (ops/media.rs:322), so even actions that shouldn't trigger a worker command still execute it. Separately, read_media_worker_output (ops/media.rs:757-777) does tokio::fs::read(path) on a caller-supplied worker_output_path with NO validate_path call (contrast runtime/config.rs:482's existing path-validation pattern), then admits the bytes as events readable by a mere :readonly token -- arbitrary local file read via the same tier gap. Meanwhile ops.cancel, sources.archive, and all lifecycle.* methods correctly require Admin -- the authorization tiering here is inverted relative to the rest of the API surface.
acceptance_criteria: ops.start's media worker command path either requires Admin scope (matching the tier of every other consequential mutation on this surface), or is restricted to an explicit allowlist of known-safe worker programs/paths (matching how other subprocess-spawning paths in this codebase are gated). read_media_worker_output validates worker_output_path through the existing validate_path mechanism before reading. A test proves: a :write token cannot spawn an arbitrary program via ops.start, and a caller-supplied worker_output_path outside the expected directory is rejected.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: ops.start media worker command/output execution path now requires Admin scope instead of being reachable by a :write-scoped token. Verified via xtask check + targeted scope-enforcement test on the merged commit.

title: system.systemd source: ~50x false-event amplification -- nearly every journal line becomes a fabricated unit.started event
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep, verified against 4000 real journal records on this host via a Python simulation of the actual Rust dispatch logic. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/system/systemd.rs:123 gates only on the _SYSTEMD_UNIT field, but journald sets that field on EVERY message logged by any process running inside a unit -- not just genuine manager lifecycle transitions (those carry UNIT/USER_UNIT specifically). The dispatch chain's unconditional else-branch at systemd.rs:239 emits unit.started for anything that doesn't match a more specific case. Measured: 3996/4000 real records carry _SYSTEMD_UNIT; only 111 carry UNIT/USER_UNIT. Simulating the exact dispatch produces 3965 fabricated unit.started + 31 unit.stopped events, of which at most 80 are genuine lifecycle transitions -- roughly a 50x false-positive amplification that ALSO duplicates the entire journald lane's content under a different event type. Every fabricated event carries hardcoded active_state:'inactive', sub_state:'dead' defaults (systemd.rs:165-176) and unit_name = the LOGGING unit, not any actually-transitioning unit -- structurally wrong data, not just excess volume. This is exactly the class of pollution bug that would immediately re-flood a freshly-wiped dataset if unfixed before Phase C.

SAME FILE, two regressions the already-merged journald MESSAGE/timestamp fix (sinex-gr7d, PR #2599) never got propagated to: (a) systemd.rs:147 still reads MESSAGE via .as_str() instead of the now-shared decode_journald_field helper -- measured 1578/4000 real records carry array-valued MESSAGE, so those fall through to empty string then the unit.started else-branch, compounding the amplification; (b) systemd.rs:141 still truncates timestamp_us to whole seconds via from_unix_timestamp instead of from_unix_timestamp_nanos, while still labeling the result TimingEvidence::Intrinsic (claiming full precision it doesn't have).
acceptance_criteria: system.systemd only emits unit.started/unit.stopped for genuine manager lifecycle messages (gate on UNIT/USER_UNIT presence, or an equivalent real signal, not just _SYSTEMD_UNIT presence). The else-branch either drops non-lifecycle journal lines for this source entirely (journald already captures them) or classifies them honestly as something other than a fabricated lifecycle transition. Reuse decode_journald_field and from_unix_timestamp_nanos from the journald fix rather than duplicating the now-fixed bug. A test proves: a real journal slice with N genuine unit transitions and M non-lifecycle messages from units produces exactly N lifecycle events, not N+M.
notes:
2026-08-13 implementation commits 0b0b977a1 and 3fe921c2a: SystemdParser now gates lifecycle events on UNIT/USER_UNIT, drops ordinary _SYSTEMD_UNIT logs, decodes journald byte-array fields, and preserves microsecond timestamp precision. Added anti-vacuity unit fixture with two genuine transitions plus two ordinary logs; updated production-path and required-key fixtures to the new manager-field contract. Worker invocation 2007384 compiled but its two production-path tests failed under severe host pressure; coordinator retry then hit checkout-local xtask rebuild termination before test execution. Must rerun focused tests under lower contention before closure.
Correction 2026-08-13: production-path fixture update is 3fe921c2a; formatting follow-up is 40e8a861a. Focused parser invocation 2007385 passed 3, and production-path systemd::tests invocation 2007387 passed 6. Bead was closed with this evidence.

title: CAS orphan sweep can delete in-flight/mismatched blob content, and its own dry-run always shows zero keys before --apply deletes them
description:
Combined finding from 3 independent audit lanes converging on the same root cause (2026-08-10 pre-wipe sweep):

1. DRY-RUN LIES (CLI audit, CRITICAL): crate/sinexd/src/runtime/content_store/gc.rs:77-82 -- 'let unused_entries: Vec<UnusedContentEntry> = cas_report.orphaned.checked_div(1).map(|_| Vec::new()).unwrap_or_default();' -- always returns an EMPTY vec regardless of what was actually found orphaned. ContentStoreConfig::default().legacy_annex_enabled==false (content_store/mod.rs:242), and crate/sinexctl/src/commands/blob.rs:84-105 constructs the store with ..Default::default(), so this CAS branch is ALWAYS taken. sinexctl blob sweep-orphans's dry-run preview shows orphaned_entries:N (nonzero count) but orphaned_keys:[] (empty identity list) -- the formatter (blob.rs:159) then silently prints nothing when the key list is empty. Operator sees a count with no identities in the dry-run preview, then --apply deletes the real files with no way to have inspected what would be deleted first.

2. SILENT DATA LOSS (blob/CAS audit, HIGH): check_cas classifies ANY on-disk file with no core.blobs row as orphaned and removes it with NO age/grace/mtime guard (content_store/cas_fsck.rs:139-152). Two real windows: (a) staging temp files are written INSIDE the CAS tree itself (mod.rs:568, '{hash}.tmp-{uuid}') and walk_cas takes the filename verbatim as the hash (mod.rs:1063) -- a .tmp- file mid-copy is by construction not yet in the DB and gets deleted; (b) write-then-commit gap: content lands on disk (material_assembler/io.rs:1731) before the blob row commits in the finalization transaction (finalize.rs:936->962) -- no post-commit existence re-check closes this window.

3. A DATABASE_URL/SINEX_CONTENT_STORE_PATH mismatch (both independent env vars, blob.rs:58,86) makes EVERY file in the content store look orphaned relative to that DB connection, and --apply would wipe the entire content store in one command.

Deployment note: sinex-blob-cas-sweep.timer defaults enabled+apply=true, weekly (nixos/modules/default.nix:618-641, blob-storage.nix:85-92) -- this runs automatically, unattended, on a schedule.
acceptance_criteria: The dry-run preview actually lists the real orphaned keys it found (fix the discarded-vector bug in gc.rs), so an operator can inspect before --apply. title: CRITICAL: snapshot restore drill has zero real test coverage; sinexctl ops demo has no confirmation and can write 10000 synthetic events into any DATABASE_URL
description:
Two related CRITICAL findings from the 2026-08-10 backup/CLI audit sweep, both about unverified/unguarded write paths near the wipe:

1. Postgres dump/restore round-trip has ZERO real coverage: crate/sinexctl/tests/admin_snapshot_test.rs:954 mocks pg_restore as '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0' and psql as a canned-output script; the 'dump' is the literal bytes 'custom pg dump fixture' (line 151). Every assertion about row counts and timescaledb_pre_restore()/post_restore() reads the MOCK's own log, not real Postgres behavior. The file header explicitly states tests deliberately pass an invalid DATABASE_URL so pg_dump only ever FAILS. No VM/e2e coverage exists anywhere. The central claim this whole backup mechanism rests on -- that a pg_dump -Fc of the real TimescaleDB+pgvector prod DB actually restores -- is unverified by anything in the test suite.

2. Separately, execute_postgres_restore_drill (snapshot.rs:868-918) performs ZERO emptiness/identity check on the target database despite docs (crate/sinexctl/docs/state_snapshot.md:140-147) explicitly claiming it 'refuses to run unless pointing at an empty drill database'. It runs timescaledb_pre_restore() then pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges (no --clean) against whatever SINEX_RESTORE_DATABASE_URL resolves to -- env-sourced, so a stale env var could point the 'drill' at PROD and merge dump rows into live tables. This is the exact command that would be used to VERIFY the backup works before trusting it for the wipe.

3. Separately, bare 'sinexctl ops demo' (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/demo.rs:41-52,66-76) connects directly to postgresql:///sinex_dev?host=/var/cache/sinex/sinity/566e9bf8d5e8/dev-state/run, bypassing the gateway and admission pipeline entirely, and bulk-inserts 10,000 default synthetic rows into core.events -- no --confirm flag, no prod check, no dry-run. This is precisely the class of accidental contamination that motivates the whole fresh-rebuild campaign in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real (not mocked) pg_dump/pg_restore round-trip test exists, exercised against a real Postgres instance, proving the actual backup format restores real data correctly. 2. execute_postgres_restore_drill actually verifies the target database is empty/a genuine drill target before running, matching what the docs already claim it does. 3. sinexctl ops demo requires an explicit --confirm flag and/or refuses to run against a URL that doesn't look like an obvious throwaway/dev database.
notes: Correction to closure evidence: the shell-rendered close reason lost inline code formatting, but the underlying evidence is exact. Real archive: /realm/tmp/work/sinex-dev-live-rehearsal.tar.zst. Real restore command: nix develop --command sinexctl ops state restore --archive /realm/tmp/work/sinex-dev-live-rehearsal.tar.zst --target-dir /realm/tmp/work/sinex-restore-drill --restore-database-url postgresql:///sinex_restore_drill_20260813?host=/var/cache/sinex/sinity/566e9bf8d5e8/dev-state/run --confirm-restore --format json. Result: checks_passed=true, all 52 PostgreSQL table row counts matched, all component hashes matched, and the target database was newly created as sinex_restore_drill_20260813. sinexctl ops demo --help independently confirms --confirm is required. No existing database was dropped or overwritten.
close_reason:
Resolved and verified. Closure Evidence Manifest: the current restore code validates disposable target identity and emptiness before pg_restore; Seed deterministic demo events directly into the database

Options:

          Acknowledge that this command writes synthetic events directly to the database

      --rpc-url <RPC_URL>
          Gateway RPC URL

          RNG seed for deterministic event generation. Same seed + same count always produces identical events
          
          [default: 0]

      --count <COUNT>

      --client-cert <CLIENT_CERT>

      --client-key <CLIENT_KEY>
          Client private key path (for mTLS)

      --insecure
          Accept invalid certificates (dev only!)

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Request timeout in seconds
          
          [default: 30]

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format (can be overridden per command)

          Possible values:
          - table:  Human-readable table (default)
          - json:   JSON output — the entire response serialized as one finite pretty-printed document
          - ndjson: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — one JSON object per line, for streaming/bulk use
          - yaml:   YAML output
          - dot:    Graphviz DOT language (for provenance graphs)
          
          [default: table]

      --runtime-target <RUNTIME_TARGET>
          Runtime target descriptor to load for gateway/auth/TLS settings
          
          [env: SINEX_RUNTIME_TARGET_CONFIG=]

      --list-formats
          Print the format-support matrix for all commands and exit

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

EXAMPLES:
    # Seed 10 000 events with default seed (explicitly confirmed)
    sinexctl ops demo --confirm

    # Deterministic seed — same args always produce same events
    sinexctl ops demo --seed 42 --confirm

    # Smaller run
    sinexctl ops demo --count 5000 --confirm

    # Wipe previous demo data first, then seed
    sinexctl ops demo --count 5000 --clear --confirm confirms explicit --confirm is required for direct synthetic writes. title: CRITICAL: Phase A backup (ops state snapshot) never captures NATS JetStream state, and every check reports green
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit of the ops lifecycle/backup mechanism -- verified LIVE against the deployed system. crate/sinexctl/src/admin/snapshot.rs:424 captures state_dir.join('nats/jetstream'). The live NATS store dir is /var/lib/nats/jetstream (confirmed via systemctl cat nats -> validate-nats-conf: "store_dir": "/var/lib/nats/jetstream"). Neither /var/lib/sinex/nats/jetstream (CLI default) nor /var/lib/sinex/state/nats/jetstream (deployed SINEX_STATE_DIR) exists -- so JetStream state is NEVER actually captured by any realistic invocation. capture_dir_component (snapshot.rs:599) then records bytes=0, blake3="absent" with NO ERROR. inspect_snapshot_archive filters component.bytes>0 before computing missing_component_paths, so 'ops state inspect' prints 'Manifest paths: ok' anyway. The restore drill's nats_member_paths_match compares empty-to-empty -> passes. Snapshot, inspect, AND drill are all green with zero JetStream state in the archive. This is the exact backup the operator's fresh-rebuild plan (sinex-poma Phase A) is relying on as the safety net for an otherwise-irreversible prod DB wipe.
acceptance_criteria: The snapshot captures the ACTUAL live NATS JetStream store_dir (read from the real nats config or a discovered runtime value, not a hardcoded assumed path), OR the component-absent case is loudly flagged as a FAILURE (not silently reported as bytes=0/absent with a passing inspect). A test proves: run a real snapshot against a live NATS instance with actual JetStream data, and confirm the snapshot archive actually contains that data and inspect would fail if it didn't.

title: CRITICAL: ops state snapshot --auto-stop cannot actually stop sinexd/nats; quiesce guard is vacuous or breaks Postgres
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit of the backup mechanism, verified LIVE. crate/sinexctl/src/admin/exec.rs:386,417 match services via the glob 'sinex-*'. The real daemon unit is sinexd.service and the broker is nats.service -- NEITHER matches this glob (verified: systemctl list-units --all 'sinex-*' returns nothing on this host). When the operator starts sinexd directly (sudo systemctl start sinexd, exactly as CLAUDE.md itself documents), sinex-runtime.target stays inactive, active_sinex_services() returns [], the pre-snapshot quiesce check passes SILENTLY, and the manifest records mode:'quiesce' for what is actually a FULLY LIVE, actively-writing capture daemon. Quiesce mode then uses the non-tolerant cp_tree, so a concurrently-mutated tree either hard-fails or gets copied torn and mislabeled consistent.

SEPARATE failure mode, same code: if sinex-runtime.target IS active, the glob DOES match it, but PartOf propagation ALSO stops PostgreSQL (verified live: systemctl show postgresql -p PartOf -> 'postgresql.target sinex-runtime.target'), breaking the subsequent pg_dump. Also: systemctl stop <target> does not wait for PartOf-propagated stop jobs (no ordering edge), so even the 'working' path gives no guarantee sinexd finished flushing before pg_dump/cp start.
acceptance_criteria: The quiesce check matches the ACTUAL deployed unit names (sinexd.service, nats.service, or whatever the real units are called), not a glob that happens to miss them. Stopping services for a quiesced snapshot does not inadvertently also stop PostgreSQL (the thing being dumped) via unintended PartOf propagation. A test proves: with sinexd genuinely running (real unit, real writes), --auto-stop actually stops it before capture and the manifest's mode:quiesce claim is true.

title: MCP/gateway per-event-card privacy_state is a hardcoded raw_visible() literal regardless of actual redaction
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via the same MCP audit as the envelope-level finding (sinex-<envelope-bead-id>). crate/sinex-primitives/src/views/events.rs:161 sets privacy_state: PrivacyStateView::raw_visible() as a literal constant for every event card, regardless of what the persist-time redact_batch chokepoint actually did to that event's payload. This is shared code -- affects the gateway/TUI surfaces too, not just MCP. Combined with the envelope-level finding: an MCP client can receive an envelope claiming Redacted while every card inside it claims raw_visible -- two contradictory hardcoded constants, neither of which reflects reality, and no real signal exists anywhere in the read path for whether a given piece of data was actually redacted.
acceptance_criteria: Event card privacy_state reflects the actual redaction outcome recorded at persist time (e.g. whether the payload differs from its pre-redaction form, or a stored flag/marker from the redact_batch chokepoint), not a hardcoded literal. Coordinate with the envelope-level fix (sinex-<envelope-bead-id>) since they're the same underlying gap at two layers.

title: MCP envelopes falsely claim privacy_state: redacted on tools where zero redaction ran
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep of the MCP server surface (crate/sinexctl/src/mcp.rs). mcp_view_envelope_with_caveats (mcp.rs:2972-2994) UNCONDITIONALLY appends caveat 'mcp.raw_samples_redacted' ('MCP read tools redact raw payload samples and snippets by default') and sets privacy_state = Redacted{reason: 'gateway_default raw sample redaction'} on EVERY envelope. Actual redaction only runs on 4 call sites: mcp.rs:1967 (trace_lineage), :2489 (llm_prompts), :2548 (curation_proposals), :2602 (source_material), plus document-specific passes at :2183/:2197. sinex_search_events (:1949-1954), sinex_context_pack (:3216-3231), sinex_tasks_list, sinex_source_materials, sinex_relation_evidence, and most other tools pass the gateway response through completely untouched while stamping the redaction claim onto it anyway. Each event card carries payload_preview (up to 8 top-level keys, 240 chars per string, sinex-primitives/src/views/events.rs:768-798) that is NOT redacted despite the envelope's explicit claim that it was. This is the machine-readable trust signal an AI agent (or any downstream automation deciding whether a response is safe to persist/log/paste elsewhere) reads to decide how to handle the data -- and it is wrong, in the dangerous direction (claims MORE protection than actually happened, not less).
acceptance_criteria: privacy_state accurately reflects whether redaction actually ran for that specific envelope -- either wire up real redaction for the tools currently claiming it falsely, or stop claiming redaction ran when it didn't (report the true, unredacted state). A test proves: for a tool that does NOT currently redact (e.g. sinex_search_events), the envelope's privacy_state does not claim Redacted unless redaction genuinely ran.

title: Replay output-validation gate is trivially satisfiable -- archiving 30000 events and re-emitting 1 passes
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/collect.rs:224 sets minimum_visible_count = logical_source_identifiers.len() (normally just 1), and the verification query at :269-296 counts DISTINCT logical_source_identifier -- not row/event counts. A replay that archives 30,000 events and successfully re-emits just ONE satisfies this gate. Nothing in validation.rs or ReplayScope::validate (state_machine.rs:147-158) checks that the source material backing the scope is still actually READABLE -- only that registry rows exist (collect.rs:348-384). A replay of a scope whose backing file was truncated, rotated, or deleted between archive and re-scan is an operator-invisible DELETION disguised as a successful replay.
acceptance_criteria: The output-validation gate checks something proportional to what was actually archived (a row-count-based sanity bound, not just distinct-source-identifier presence), and/or explicitly verifies source material readability before declaring a replay successful. A test proves: a replay where the backing source material becomes unreadable between archive and re-scan is detected and surfaced as a failure, not silently reported as a successful (near-)no-op replay.

title: Replay cancel restores derived descendants while material parents stay archived -- stale derivation permanently wins over fresh recomputation
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep of replay execution logic (separate from the already-audited crash-consistency windows). crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:711 sets restore_archived_cascade: true unconditionally on operator cancel; restore_cascade calls core.execute_cascade_restore, whose occurrence-safety guard (crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:2417-2425) only skips rows with source_material_id IS NOT NULL -- it has no equivalent guard for DERIVED rows.

Concrete scenario: material root m1 archived, source re-emits m2 at the same (material_id, anchor_byte) before the cancel completes, derived child d1 (source_event_ids=[m1]) was archived in the same cascade. On cancel: m1 correctly stays archived (occurrence-safety guard works for materials), but d1 -- a LIVE derived event whose parent now only exists in audit.archived_events -- gets restored anyway, since the guard doesn't cover derived rows. Worse: d1 still carries its original equivalence_key, so the automaton's fresh recomputation from m2 gets rejected at admission as OccurrenceDuplicate (event_engine/admission.rs:633-682) for SuppressDuplicate-policy payloads -- the STALE derivation wins permanently over the correct fresh one, with no operator-visible signal that this happened. The existing code comment at replay_writer.rs:787-795 only reasons about the material half of this restore, missing the derived-event case entirely.
acceptance_criteria: core.execute_cascade_restore's occurrence-safety guard (or an equivalent check before restoring on cancel) also covers derived rows -- a derived event whose parent(s) are NOT being restored alongside it should not be restored either, or restoring it should not permanently block a fresh recomputation via equivalence-key collision. A test proves: archive a material+derived pair, re-emit the material before cancel, cancel the replay, and confirm the derived event's fresh recomputation is NOT silently suppressed by a stale restored duplicate.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix (with correction, see prior comment): core.execute_cascade_restore now performs a post-restore liveness recheck pass instead of gating liveness inside the restoring INSERT's own snapshot, so a derived row restored alongside its material parent in the same call no longer sees the parent as not-yet-live. AC: test proves archiving a material+derived pair, re-emitting the material before cancel, and cancelling correctly does not let the stale derived restore permanently block the fresh recomputation via equivalence-key collision. Verified via xtask test -p sinex-schema -E 'test(cascade_restore)' passing on the merged commit (previously returned 1 restored row instead of 2, now correct).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [PR #2615 2026-08-11] Correction to the fix: the initial parent-liveness guard checked each row's parent-liveness against the SAME self-referential INSERT...SELECT's pre-statement snapshot, so two rows restored together in one call (e.g. a material and its derived child) incorrectly saw each other as not-yet-live -- execute_cascade_restore under-restored (returned 1 instead of 2 in the regression test). Fixed by splitting into two passes: the main INSERT restores all requested rows first (guard removed from its WHERE clause), then a separate subsequent statement block builds a _parent_dead_ids temp table by checking core.events (now correctly seeing same-batch siblings that already landed), pre-deletes the stale audit.archived_events row for those ids (required because fn_archive_before_delete's raw INSERT has no ON CONFLICT and would collide), then deletes the now-confirmed-dead rows from core.events and _restored_ids. Also fixed an unrelated Rust string-literal syntax error introduced along the way (a literal " inside a SQL comment broke the enclosing non-raw Rust string).

title: Scoped replay archives a subset but re-scans the WHOLE source -- can create duplicate live interpretations for out-of-scope occurrences
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:2090-2092 is the ONLY consumer of args.replay across the whole scan-dispatch path; scan_historical otherwise drains from the persisted cursor (adapter_source.rs:2132-2136), and crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/dispatch.rs:141-147 gives the replay worker a FRESH CheckpointManager namespace (replay-<opid>), meaning the cursor starts at zero regardless of the replay's intended scope. A replay scope narrowed by --since/--event-type/--material therefore correctly archives only the narrow subset, but re-reads and re-derives events across the ENTIRE source from position zero -- affecting AppendOnlyFile, SqliteQuery, ApiCursor, IncrementalDump, and Archive adapter kinds (only FileDrop actually consults the scope). Out-of-scope occurrences that the parser emits without an occurrence_key (adapter_source.rs:2647 leaves equivalence_key=None in that case) get a SECOND live interpretation alongside their still-live original -- a direct violation of the one-live-interpretation-per-occurrence invariant, for events that were never even supposed to be touched by the replay.
acceptance_criteria: Either the replay worker's checkpoint/cursor is seeded to skip re-scanning out-of-scope material, or every affected adapter kind (not just FileDrop) actually consults args.replay to bound its scan to the intended scope. A test proves: a scoped replay against a source containing both in-scope and out-of-scope occurrences results in exactly one live interpretation per out-of-scope occurrence (no duplicate), for at least one of the affected adapter kinds.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Independently re-derived via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs (2026-08-11), before discovering this bead already covers it -- strong corroboration. Widen this bead's scope/AC: adapter_source.rs:2082-2094 scan_historical only consults args.replay (MaterialReplayContext) when A::KIND == InputShapeKind::FileDrop. For every OTHER kind (AppendOnlyFile incl. weechat/terminal history, SqliteRow, DbusStream, JournalctlStream, ApiCursor, ImapSync, GmailApi, EmailMboxFile, ClipboardPolling, UnixSocketStream, StaticFile, DirectoryWalk, Chained, IncrementalDump), the replay context is silently dropped and execution falls to the normal historical branch (:2131-2136, drain_adapter(cursor: state.cursor.clone(), ...)) -- i.e. just resumes live ingestion from the persisted cursor. api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:456-506 dispatches MaterialReplayContext via SourceScanCommand unconditionally, no adapter-kind check before sending. Net effect for non-FileDrop sources (the large majority): replay is either a silent no-op (cursor already caught up -- 'succeeds' having replayed nothing) or ingests unrelated new live content mislabeled under the replay operation_id. This is a STRONGER/more common failure mode than the bead's current title suggests ('duplicate interpretations') -- recommend widening the AC to state replay is a no-op/wrong-content-substitution for all non-FileDrop kinds, not just a duplication risk.

title: Replay failure paths (non-cancel) orphan archived cascade rows with no recovery sweep -- silent permanent delete
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:750 (scan-completion timeout) and :722/:732 set restore_archived_cascade: false, and wait_for_replay_outputs_visible at :759 propagates with ? after a SUCCESSFUL scan report without restoring. All these paths route to mark_failed, which only writes operation metadata -- it does not restore the archived cascade. The #2194 cascade-journal restore mechanism (crate/sinex-db/src/replay/state_machine.rs:1239-1270, the SAME durable-journal mechanism this session's sinex-afd crash-consistency audit examined) only runs from the stale-Executing recovery sweep at process startup. An operation that reaches Failed cleanly (no crash involved -- an ordinary timeout or output-validation error) is NEVER repaired: the archived cascade for that scope is a silent, permanent delete with no operator-visible trace, distinct from the crash-window case already tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Every non-cancel failure path that has already archived a cascade either restores it (matching cancel's own restore behavior, once sinex-<F1-bead-id>'s derived-row gap is also fixed) or explicitly and visibly marks the operation as requiring manual recovery (not silently mark_failed with no trace). A test proves: force a replay to fail via the output-validation-timeout path after archiving, and confirm the archived data is either restored or the failure is operator-visible as requiring recovery, not silently dropped.

title: The entire structural/plausibility event validation suite is dead code in production -- IngestEventValidator::validate_event has one caller, a test
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. AdmissionService::validate_event (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:1347-1353) calls only guard.validate_payload_for(...) -- schema validation only. The wrapper that actually runs the structural checks, IngestEventValidator::validate_event (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/validator.rs:254), has EXACTLY ONE caller in the entire repo: crate/sinexd/tests/.../validator_test.rs:17 (verified via rg across crate, tests, xtask).

Consequence: none of EventValidator::validate (crate/sinex-db/src/validation.rs:313-337) runs on real ingest -- validate_envelope (empty source / NUL bytes, :517+), check_payload_size (:582, per-event size bound), ensure_object_payload (:594), validate_domain_specific_rules (fs path/size, terminal command required-field checks, :483-547), validate_temporal_bounds (:422), validate_id_timestamp (5-min ID drift check, :409), validate_provenance (duplicate parent-id check, :438) -- ALL of it is unreachable dead code from production's perspective. Every event that reaches admission today skips this entire layer.

Corroborating rot found in the same sweep: crate/sinex-primitives/tests/event_validation_property_test.rs:196-201 is commented 'Production validation wrapper for events (avoid mock-only checks)' and calls exactly the path production never reaches -- that comment is now false, and the property-test suite it's attached to protects dead code, giving false confidence that these checks are exercised.
acceptance_criteria: AdmissionService::validate_event actually calls IngestEventValidator::validate_event (or the structural checks get folded directly into the admission path some other way) so the whole validation layer -- envelope sanity, per-event payload size, domain-specific field requirements, temporal bounds, ID-timestamp drift, provenance duplicate-parent detection -- actually runs on real ingest. A test proves at least one of these checks (e.g. the NUL-byte/empty-source envelope check) actually rejects a malformed real event through the production admission path, not just through the currently-dead direct-call test.
