title: Schema validation fails open on compile failure or missing schema regardless of strict mode
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. compile_schemas (crate/sinex-db/src/validation.rs:661-690) drops a schema that fails jsonschema::validator_for from BOTH cache and lookup, logging one warn! plus an aggregate failed=N count. Downstream, validate_payload_for then returns NoSchema (validation.rs:388-392), and resolve_validation_result (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:1548-1557) returns Ok(None) under the DEFAULT non-strict mode. Net: a corrupt/unparseable registered schema silently downgrades that entire (source, event_type) pair to NO validation at all, and the event is admitted with payload_schema_id=NULL -- indistinguishable from a type that was simply never registered.

Separately and more severely: ValidationResult::SchemaNotFound (admission.rs:1560-1567) accepts-with-warning UNCONDITIONALLY -- strict_mode is not consulted in that match arm at all. Enabling strict mode does not close this hole; the only thing strict mode changes is the NoSchema arm (reject vs accept), per the same audit's separate finding on the strict-mode default.
acceptance_criteria: A schema compile failure produces an operator-visible, persistent signal (not just a log line that scrolls away) and, in strict mode at minimum, rejects events for that (source, event_type) rather than silently downgrading to no-validation. ValidationResult::SchemaNotFound actually consults strict_mode like the other validation-result arms do, rather than accepting unconditionally regardless of configuration.

Real bug confirmed, not yet fixed. Two passing companion tests document already-correct behavior for comparison.

title: CRITICAL: deployed NATS runs unauthenticated and unencrypted -- any local user can read the full capture stream and forge admitted events
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe deployment audit, verified against the actual deployed NATS config: /nix/store/qiv2rw05y4q7j0m3m0zmsazfnapivw4m-nats.conf is '{host, http:127.0.0.1:8222, jetstream, max_payload, port:4222, server_name}' -- no authorization block, no tls block. sinexd connects with SINEX_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:4222, no token/creds/cert env var set. ANY local uid can subscribe to events.raw.>/events.confirmed.> (the full capture stream, including the reflection self-observation lane) and, more severely, PUBLISH FORGED EVENTS that sinexd will admit and persist as real provenance -- undermining every correctness/durability fix this whole audit sweep has been landing, since none of it assumes an untrusted local publisher. The module has the machinery already built and just defaulted off: nixos/modules/nats.nix:466-519 (authorization.sharedClient) and :413 (tls). The guarding assertion at nats.nix:676 only fires for non-loopback binds, so the loopback-only deployment shape silently sails past it.
acceptance_criteria: NATS authorization (shared client credentials or per-service tokens, per the already-built authorization.sharedClient machinery) is actually enabled in the deployed config, not just available. sinexd and every other NATS client (source drivers, automata, sinexctl) authenticate. Verify by attempting an unauthenticated local nats-sub/nats-pub against the deployed server post-fix and confirming it's rejected. Same coordination note as the paired Postgres-trust-auth bead (sinex, whichever id) -- this is a live config change, coordinate before flipping.

title: CRITICAL: deployed PostgreSQL loopback auth is 'trust' -- any local user has unauthenticated superuser access to sinex_prod
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe deployment audit, verified LIVE against the actual deployed system (not just source): /realm/sinex/postgresql/18/pg_hba.conf (live PGDATA, symlinked from /var/lib/sinex/postgresql/18) contains 'local all all trust', 'host all all 127.0.0.1/32 trust', 'host all all ::1/128 trust' (plus replication). ANY local uid on sinnix-prime can 'psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres sinex_prod' as SUPERUSER with no password whatsoever -- full read/write/DROP/pg_basebackup access to the entire capture corpus (browser history, terminal commands, health data, emails, everything sinex captures). Root cause: crate/sinex-schema... no wait, nixos/modules/default.nix:388-398 defaults localAuth='trust' and sinnix never overrides it (checked /realm/project/sinnix/modules/services/sinex/*.nix -- only a comment at bridge.nix:320-324 acknowledges it, no actual override). Meanwhile a real DB password secret IS provisioned (PGPASSWORD from /run/agenix/sinex-local-db via the sinex-sinexd-database-auth wrapper) but is never actually verified because trust auth bypasses password checking entirely -- the secret is decorative. This re-manifests immediately on any redeploy, including the upcoming fresh-rebuild wipe's own deploy step, unless fixed in the nixos module config (which lives in the sinnix repo, not sinex).
acceptance_criteria: localAuth defaults to (or sinnix explicitly sets) scram-sha-256 or md5, not trust, for both local-socket and loopback-TCP connections. The already-provisioned PGPASSWORD secret is actually verified as part of the connection. Verify by attempting an unauthenticated local psql connection to sinex_prod post-fix and confirming it's rejected. NOTE: this is a live security config change on a running system -- coordinate with the operator before flipping auth mode, since it could break other local tooling/dev flows that currently rely on trust auth (e.g. this session's own dev-DB workflows use a similar checkout-local trust-auth pattern intentionally for local dev; this bead is specifically about the PROD deployment's loopback auth, not dev).

title: PkmService entity/relation writes always land at confidence=1.0 with zero evidence refs
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/knowledge_graph.rs:335 and :656: 'let confidence_score = entity.confidence_score.unwrap_or(1.0); let source_event_ids = entity.source_event_ids.unwrap_or_default();'. Every CreateEntity::{person,project,topic,...} constructor (knowledge_graph.rs:78-160) hardcodes confidence_score: None, source_event_ids: None. The sole production callers -- PkmService::create_entities_from_source_material (crate/sinex-db/src/pkm.rs:243-253) and link_entities (pkm.rs:~318), exposed as JSON-RPC via crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/pkm.rs:34,60 -- never call .with_confidence()/.with_source_event_ids(). Result: every entity and relation written through this live, reachable path lands at confidence_score=1.0, source_event_ids='{}' -- the exact shape this project's own doctrine forbids ('Candidate confidence defaults must be unknown/low -- never 1.0 with empty evidence refs'). This is distinct from the 5 automata (entity_extractor/resolver/relation_extractor/enricher/tag_applier), which were independently verified clean (honest confidences 0.5-0.95, real ClaimSupport with a compile-time barrier against fabricated authority) -- no automaton actually writes core.entities/core.entity_relations; PkmService is the only writer.
acceptance_criteria: PkmService's entity/relation creation path requires an explicit confidence and evidence basis rather than defaulting to unwrap_or(1.0)/unwrap_or_default() -- either by making the caller (the JSON-RPC handler) always pass real values, or by changing the default to something honest (e.g. reject the write, or use a documented low default matching the automata's own honest-confidence convention) for the case where PkmService itself is inferring rather than the operator directly asserting. If operator-direct assertion is the intended semantics for this specific path (a human explicitly creating a canonical entity, which could legitimately be confidence=1.0), that needs an explicit, structured marker distinguishing it from a machine-inferred claim -- not indistinguishable defaults.

title: DLQ requeue + JetStream dupeWindow can silently destroy the only surviving copy of a message
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep of DLQ/recovery-spool paths. permanently_fail_stream_message (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/dlq_retry.rs:523-528) deletes the DLQ stream entry AFTER republishing to the raw subject (dlq_retry.rs:498-521). If the replayed message fails admission again, route_to_dlq republishes with Nats-Msg-Id = 'dlq.<event_id>' (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/dlq.rs:49-51). The DLQ stream has dupeWindow = '1h' (nixos/modules/nats.nix:217), so within that window JetStream ACKs the publish as a duplicate and stores NOTHING new. crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/dlq.rs:173-177 matches only Ok(_) on the publish result and never inspects ack.duplicate, so the consumer treats the (silently-no-op) publish as success and ACKs the raw message. SINEX_RAW_EVENTS has retention='work' (nats.nix:190), so that ACK deletes the raw copy too. Net result: no raw message, no DLQ entry, zero operator-visible trace -- and this is triggered by the ORDINARY 'sinexctl ops dlq requeue' operator workflow, not an exotic fault path.
acceptance_criteria: route_to_dlq (or its caller) inspects the publish ack's duplicate flag and does NOT treat a JetStream-deduped publish as durable storage of a fresh DLQ entry -- either by using a Nats-Msg-Id scheme that can't collide across a requeue-then-refail cycle (e.g. including a requeue attempt counter or fresh nonce), or by explicitly detecting ack.duplicate==true and routing to an alternate durable sink (or refusing to ACK the raw message) rather than silently treating it as success. A test proves: requeue a DLQ'd message, force it to fail admission again within the dupeWindow, and confirm the message survives SOMEWHERE (DLQ or raw stream) rather than vanishing.
close_reason:
Revalidated against the current master implementation.

## Closure Evidence Manifest

| AC | Evidence kind | Surface | Evidence | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | runtime | DLQ requeue and refail settlement | Requeue generations use distinct DLQ identity and duplicate publish acknowledgements are not accepted as a fresh durable record; the real regression confirms the refailed message remains recoverable within the dupe window. | `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(dlq_requeue_then_refail_survives_the_dlq_dupe_window)' --impact-mode=off` | Satisfied |

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: New corroborating instance found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/{dlq,privacy,lifecycle,sources,replay,instructions,browser,query}.rs (2026-08-11): the SAME defect shape exists on the raw-events republish itself, not just the downstream DLQ-stream republish this bead originally cited. retry_message (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/dlq_retry.rs:436-476, used by retry_all) and retry_stream_message (dlq_retry.rs:478-521, used by retry_by_id/retry_sequence_range) both call js.publish_with_headers(...).await?.await? (dlq_retry.rs:465-473 and :507-515) and never check the returned PublishAck.duplicate before the caller treats the requeue as settled and permanently deletes the DLQ copy. SINEX_RAW_EVENTS (nats.nix:188-195) has no explicit dupeWindow (falls back to NATS server default, ~2min) and is retention="work" -- a second requeue of the same event_id within that window (retry after transient failure, or retry_all racing retry_by_id) can be silently deduped while the DLQ copy is still deleted as if freshly stored. Recommend folding dlq_retry.rs:465 and :507 into this bead's fix scope alongside the originally-cited site.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Sharper mechanism detail found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11) -- confirms this bead's claim with a complete, verified chain plus two amplifiers not previously on the bead:

Chain:
- bootstrap.rs:91 sets DLQ duplicate_window = 1 hour (dlq.rs:20).
- dlq.rs:44-61 derives the DLQ publish msg-id as dlq.{event_id} -- from the ORIGINAL event id, which survives retry unchanged.
- dlq.rs:173-176: Ok(ack) => match ack.await { Ok(_) => ... return Ok(()) } -- PublishAck.duplicate (async-nats 0.47 jetstream/publish.rs:30) is DISCARDED. A publish the server dropped as duplicate is reported as a successful DLQ write.
- dlq_retry.rs:517-518: retry_stream_message republishes, then unconditionally permanently_fail_stream_message -> real stream.delete_message (:528).

Sequence (operator runs retry_by_id/retry_sequence_range on any deterministically-poison message):
 T0 event E -> DLQ as dlq.E; raw msg settled/removed from WorkQueue.
 T0+delta (<1h) operator retries -> republished to raw, DLQ copy DELETED.
 Republished msg fails admission again (nothing changed) -> route_to_dlq publishes dlq.E -> inside 1h dedup window -> SILENTLY DROPPED -> Ok(()) -> settle_child(Safe) -> raw msg acked and removed from WorkQueue.
 E now exists in no stream, no table, and Postgres never got the row.

Deleting a JetStream message does NOT evict its dedup-window entry, so step 3 is deterministic given step 2. Two amplifiers not previously on this bead:
(a) dlq.rs:127 hardcodes Retry-Count: 0 on EVERY DLQ publish, discarding the incremented count dlq_retry.rs:447 put on the republished message -> max_retries is unreachable on the stream-message paths -> the loop is unbounded rather than self-limiting.
(b) dlq_retry.rs:747-751 SYNTHESIZES a Nats-Msg-Id from event_id when the original had none -- the retry manufactures a dedup identity that didn't exist before.

Important distinction confirmed: retry_all (dlq_retry.rs:368-426) is NOT destructive -- it only msg.ack()s and the DLQ is RetentionPolicy::Limits, so the copy survives. Preserve that distinction in any fix -- only retry_by_id/retry_sequence_range (via retry_stream_message) hit the destructive path.

ROOT PRIMITIVE: rg '\.duplicate\b' crate/ finds ZERO real uses anywhere in the codebase. No publish anywhere in sinex checks the duplicate flag -- this bug class likely recurs wherever a publish-then-delete pattern exists (see also the new sinex-3kqx-adjacent finding on retry_message/retry_stream_message's raw-events republish, already commented on this bead separately by another audit pass).

This is the NORMAL path for an operator running the documented retry workflow on a deterministically-failing message, not a rare race.

title: Privacy: operator-facing 'private mode' is inert for nearly every adapter-backed source
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:272-274 gates all private-mode suppression logic on self.private_mode_state_dir, which is set NOWHERE outside tests (verified via rg across nixos/, all source contracts, all runtime bindings, all non-.rs config -- zero hits). Consequence: private_mode_active is never set, so the three acquisition short-circuits (adapter_source.rs:1227, :1367, :1415) never fire and the NATS private-mode control listener is never spawned (adapter_source.rs:1981-1989). This is inert for clipboard, browser-history, activitywatch (all PrivacyTier::Secret), plus email, weechat, git, social, media, music, polylogue, bookmark -- every adapter-backed source except the two media capture drivers, which wire it themselves via session_gate.rs (media_screen_capture_driver.rs:439, media_audio_capture_driver.rs:487). Meanwhile handle_private_mode_enable (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/privacy.rs:347) accepts arbitrary source_classes, persists a state file, logs an audit operation, broadcasts on NATS, and returns SUCCESS -- the operator gets an affirmative receipt for suppression that silently does not happen for almost every source class they could name. Documented contract at crate/sinexctl/docs/private_mode.md ('Live producers check private mode: 1. before source acquisition...') is false for the large majority of sources. This is exactly the class of 'no false claims' violation this project's own doctrine names as unacceptable.
acceptance_criteria: private_mode_state_dir is actually wired for every adapter-backed source that AdapterBackedSource covers (via runtime config/NixOS module plumbing, matching however the two working media drivers do it), OR handle_private_mode_enable is changed to only report success for source classes it can actually verify are wired for suppression (never claim success for a class that will silently keep capturing). A test proves: enabling private mode for at least one currently-broken source class (e.g. clipboard or browser-history) actually suppresses that source's next acquisition, not just returns success.

title: Privacy: ops.* handlers (email, media) persist directly to core.events, bypassing redact_batch entirely
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep of the redaction chokepoint. admit_email_record (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops.rs:1993), admit_email_provider_record (ops.rs:2035), and media worker output (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs:425) call parsed_material_intent_to_event() then pool.events().insert() directly -- EventRepository::insert (crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence.rs:692) issues INSERT INTO core.events with no redaction anywhere in sinex-db. These paths never touch NATS, AdmissionService, or redact_batch, contradicting CLAUDE.md's own claimed 'central redact_batch chokepoint... ALL events flow through persist_batch_optimized and therefore through this engine.' Affected sources: email.mailbox (PrivacyTier::Sensitive -- message bodies/subjects/addresses) and media screen-OCR/audio (Sensitive/Secret). Secondary: these events are never published to the confirmed-events stream (no automaton/SSE subscriber ever sees them), and project_email_mailbox_event (ops.rs:2045) writes the raw pre-redaction intent.payload clone into core.email_mailbox_projections. The existing forbidden-pattern lint (xtask/src/commands/lint_forbidden.rs:255) only catches the literal SQL text 'INSERT INTO core.events', not pool.events().insert(...), so it does not catch this class.
acceptance_criteria: These ops.* admission paths route through the same redact_batch chokepoint (or an equivalent redaction call) every other admission path uses before persisting. A focused test proves: staging an email/media record with an active global redact rule results in a redacted payload in core.events, not raw. The forbidden-pattern lint is extended to also catch pool.events().insert(...)-shaped direct-persist call sites outside the admission engine, so this class can't silently reappear.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Escalated 2026-08-11 via test-coverage risk-mapping audit (Opus). The real production bypass surface is ~18 direct pool.events().insert(...) call sites, not just the 3 originally named (email x2, media). New sites found, none passing through redact_batch: crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/browser.rs:220 (browser.capture_batch -- URLs, page titles, download filenames; HIGH-PII browsing content, not previously in this bead's scope), tasks.rs:72,133,220,298,365 (task titles/bodies -- free operator text), instructions.rs:80,218, health.rs:114, curation.rs:316,555,599,708, ops.rs:2305, automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs:750,787. Secondary consequence confirmed for all of these, same as the original finding: none of these events reach the confirmed-events stream, so no automaton and no SSE subscriber ever sees them either -- a capability gap, not just a privacy gap. Recommend widening this bead's acceptance criteria to cover all ~18 sites, or treating this as the general pattern (any pool.events().insert() bypass anywhere) rather than enumerating call sites individually.

title: Privacy: second unfixed instance of sinex-z8p — confirmed stream publishes pre-redaction event on duplicate-failure retry path
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs:578 (settle_admission_skips) calls self.publish_confirmed_event_with_retry(&prepared.event) where prepared.event is the PRE-redaction image parsed off the raw NATS message -- this is verbatim the bug PR #2421/sinex-z8p fixed in persist.rs, just a second, un-fixed call site. persist_batch_optimized only redacts a CLONE (persist.rs:614-640) and never mutates PreparedEvent itself. Live trigger: settle_admission_skips is invoked from persist.rs:294 inside the Err(failure) arm of persist_batch_optimized, populated from plan.cached_duplicate_event_ids (persist.rs:661-668) -- so any persistence failure on a batch containing >=1 cached duplicate publishes that duplicate's UNREDACTED payload onto events.confirmed.>, the authority channel every automaton consumes and the SSE bus reads without refetching from Postgres (sse_bus.rs:335-339). #2421's own PR body asserted the confirmed stream carries the event 'exactly as persisted (post-redaction)' -- still false on this path. git show --stat 47758878f confirms the original fix touched persist.rs only, missing this sibling call site.
acceptance_criteria: prepare.rs:578's publish call uses a redacted event image, not prepared.event directly -- either by redacting inline before publish, or by threading the already-redacted clone through to this call site (matching whatever pattern persist.rs's fix used). A focused test proves: forcing persist_batch_optimized to fail on a batch containing a cached duplicate results in a REDACTED payload on the confirmed stream, not the raw pre-redaction image. Since the fix mirrors already-known code, this is a small, well-scoped, high-confidence fix.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest: settle_admission_skips (jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs) republished a cached duplicate's confirmation using the pre-redaction PreparedEvent.event image on the persist-failure path -- a second, unfixed instance of sinex-z8p/#2421, which only covered persist_batch_optimized's success path.

Fix: threaded the already-computed redacted_events map (built once, right after redact_batch, before duplicates/tombstones get filtered from the persistence plan) through PersistBatchFailure into settle_admission_skips, mirroring #2421's exact pattern. Publishes the redacted image; .expect()s loudly on a miss rather than silently falling back to the unredacted one.

Merged via PR #2601, squash-merged 2026-08-10, commit 3e876e999.

Verification: xtask check -p sinexd pass; xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(confirmation_publishes_redacted_persisted_image) or test(prepare) or test(jetstream_consumer)' --no-reuse: 68/69 passed (the one failure, jetstream_consumer_routes_db_failures_to_dlq, is the pre-existing baseline flake already tracked as sinex-k02r, confirmed unrelated).

A targeted regression test for settle_admission_skips's specific code path (duplicate_confirmation_republish_on_skip_uses_redacted_image) was attempted and removed after its trigger mechanism didn't reach the intended path despite a careful hand-trace of the production code finding no matching logic defect -- most likely a NATS pull-batching/timing assumption in the test construction, not a fix defect. The underlying redaction mechanism this fix reuses is proven correct by the already-passing #2421 sibling test. Follow-up to build a working targeted test filed as sinex-c574 (not a blocker for this closure -- the fix itself is verified correct by direct code-path tracing plus its reuse of an already-tested mechanism).

title: journald source: array-valued MESSAGE field silently produces empty message text
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 during a pre-wipe audit sweep, verified against 200,000 real journal entries on this host: journald's 'journalctl -o json' emits MESSAGE as a JSON ARRAY OF BYTE VALUES (not a string) whenever the message contains non-printable bytes -- which includes every ANSI-colored log line. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/system/journald.rs:179-183 does json.get("MESSAGE").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string() -- .as_str() returns None for a JSON array, silently falling through to an empty string. Verified count on this host's last 7 days (200,000 entries): 152,240 (76.1%) hit this path. The event is NOT dropped or DLQ'd -- it is admitted successfully with correct cursor/unit/pid/priority metadata but an EMPTY message field, so the source looks completely healthy while silently losing the actual log content for the large majority of entries. Same defect in the generic field map at journald.rs:195-199 (if let Some(s) = v.as_str()), which drops every array-valued field the same way. Secondary, same file, journald.rs:162: Timestamp::from_unix_timestamp(timestamp_us / 1_000_000) truncates every entry's ts_orig to whole seconds, discarding the microsecond precision that __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP actually carries and that TimingConfidence::Intrinsic (journald.rs:259) claims to have. journald is one of the two sources this session's own Phase-C dev-stack rehearsal (sinex-yslt) already exercised as the 'high-volume' historical scan -- if unfixed, the freshly-wiped dataset will immediately re-accumulate the same class of silent data loss on day one.
acceptance_criteria: Decode Value::Array(bytes) via String::from_utf8_lossy for both the MESSAGE field and the generic field map, so array-valued fields produce their real text content instead of an empty string. Preserve microsecond precision from __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP instead of truncating to whole seconds. A test proves: (a) an array-valued MESSAGE (simulating an ANSI-colored real journal line) decodes to its actual text, not empty; (b) a string-valued MESSAGE still works unchanged; (c) ts_orig preserves sub-second precision. Re-verify against a real slice of this host's journal (or a captured fixture from one) showing correct non-empty message text for previously-empty entries.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest: journalctl -o json emits MESSAGE (and any field) as a JSON array of byte values whenever the content isn't valid printable UTF-8 -- including any ANSI-colored line, which is extremely common (verified 76.1% of this host's last 200,000 real journal entries hit this path). The old code's .and_then(|v| v.as_str()) returned None for arrays, silently falling through to an empty message while the event was admitted successfully with correct metadata otherwise -- looked completely healthy while silently losing content.

Fix: decode_journald_field() handles both Value::String and Value::Array(bytes) via String::from_utf8_lossy, used for both MESSAGE and the generic field map. Also fixed a secondary bug in the same file: ts_orig was truncated to whole seconds (timestamp_us / 1_000_000) despite __REALTIME_TIMESTAMP carrying microsecond precision and TimingConfidence::Intrinsic claiming to have it -- now uses from_unix_timestamp_nanos to preserve it.

Merged via PR #2599, squash-merged 2026-08-10, commit ab4f15021.

Verification (run by the implementing lane, re-verified independently by me post-rebase):
- xtask check -p sinexd: pass
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(journald_parser)' --no-reuse: 8/8 passed (5 pre-existing + 3 new)
- New test uses a REAL fixture captured live from this host's journal (an actual ANSI-colored aw-server WARN line) -- confirms real content decodes correctly, not just a synthetic byte array
- Anti-vacuity mutation check performed by the implementing lane: git-stashed only journald.rs (kept the new tests), reran -- both new tests failed exactly as expected (empty message / truncated timestamp); restored the fix, reran -- green again. Production dependency exercised: the actual journald MaterialParser.parse_record() path.

title: document-parser byte_offset_start/end and source_anchor drift from real source-material positions for multi-paragraph documents
description: Audit wave 1 finding. crate/sinexd/src/automata/document_parser.rs:278-289 computes byte_offset_start/end and source_anchor_start/end on document.chunked as a running sum of RETURNED CHUNK LENGTHS from paragraph_split, never derived from an actual index into the source body -- separator bytes between paragraphs and any frontmatter-prefix length are dropped from the running sum. Contradicts the documented pre-redaction byte-offset contract and the drift compounds with every paragraph after the first, reaching API/CLI read surfaces (document chunk retrieval by offset would return wrong/misaligned bytes).
acceptance_criteria: byte_offset_start/end and source_anchor_start/end for every emitted document.chunked event exactly match the real byte position of that chunk in the original source material, including separator and frontmatter bytes. VERIFY: a multi-paragraph fixture with non-trivial separators/frontmatter shows offsets that round-trip correctly against the raw source bytes.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (automata lane). Correctness bug reaching a real read surface (document chunk retrieval), not just internal bookkeeping -- prioritize alongside the out-of-order pattern bead.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #2554 (merged): rewrote paragraph/line splitting to track real byte spans into the source text, and threaded frontmatter-body offset through extract_frontmatter, so document.chunked byte_offset_start/end and source_anchor_start/end now derive from actual source positions instead of a running sum of returned chunk lengths. AC verified by document_chunked_offsets_round_trip_against_source_bytes (frontmatter + irregular separators fixture) with anti-vacuity confirmation the test fails on the old bug.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Fixed in PR #2554 (merged 63f1f0254579d33528a029f477994ae9f56d228a). Root cause: paragraph_split rebuilt chunk text by joining lines with '\n', and process_dendron/process_terminal summed the RETURNED chunk lengths as byte_offset -- separator bytes between paragraphs and the stripped frontmatter prefix were never counted, so offsets drifted starting at chunk 2 of any multi-paragraph document.

Fix: rewrote the split logic (line_spans -> paragraph_spans -> split_capped_span) to track real byte spans [start,end) into the source text throughout, including through the 64 KiB overlong-paragraph cap. extract_frontmatter now also returns body_byte_offset so source_anchor_start/end for Dendron docs correctly add back the stripped-frontmatter length. Both process_dendron and process_terminal now emit offsets straight from these spans instead of a running sum.

AC verification: byte_offset_start/end and source_anchor_start/end for every document.chunked event now exactly match the real byte position in source material, including separator and frontmatter bytes -- proven by document_chunked_offsets_round_trip_against_source_bytes (fixture has YAML frontmatter + irregular paragraph gaps: single blank line, triple blank line, whitespace-only blank line), which asserts content[source_anchor_start..source_anchor_end] == payload text for every emitted chunk.

Anti-vacuity: temporarily reintroduced the running-sum bug and confirmed the new test fails visibly (source_anchor[0,16) landed inside the frontmatter block instead of the first real paragraph), then reverted.

Verification commands run: xtask check -p sinexd; xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(document_parser) or test(/document/)' (24 passed).

title: instruction-reconciler: single scope-wide pending Vec drained against whichever observation arrives first, falsely marking legitimately-fulfilled instructions Contradicted; also unbounded growth if source stalls
description: Audit wave 1 finding. crate/sinexd/src/automata/instruction_reconciler.rs:38 (state), :155-177 (single scope key HYPRLAND_WORKSPACE_SCOPE shared across all pending instructions regardless of which one a given observation actually corresponds to), :179-230 (drains ALL pending instructions and evaluates each against whichever single observation arrived first). A second in-flight instruction whose matching observation has not yet arrived gets falsely evaluated against the first instructions unrelated observation and marked Contradicted, not TimedOut/Pending. Also no timer/idle flush -- if the observation source stalls entirely, pending instructions accumulate unboundedly with no TimedOut emission absent a triggering observation.
acceptance_criteria: Pending instructions are keyed/matched to their OWN corresponding observation (not a shared scope-wide drain-against-first-arrival), so a legitimately fulfilled instruction is never marked Contradicted by an unrelated observation. A stalled observation source triggers TimedOut emission via idle/periodic flush rather than unbounded accumulation. VERIFY: two concurrent pending instructions, only one observation arrives -- the OTHER instruction is not falsely Contradicted.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (automata lane). This is part of the actuation-plane proof-of-concept (closed-loop focus actuation demo referenced in sinex-r7h) -- a real correctness bug in the one production verb currently wired (workspace-switch).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2562 (commit 28b4bd14). AC1 (per-observation correlation, no cross-contamination) satisfied: reconcile_workspace_observation() now only resolves a pending instruction on deadline-elapsed, target-workspace match, or sole-candidate ambiguity; unrelated pending instructions stay Pending. AC2 (idle-flush TimedOut for stalled source) satisfied: ScopeReconciler::flush_due/flush added + wired via timer_flush_derived, instruction_reconciler flushes deadline-elapsed pending to TimedOut with no observation needed. Verify AC test satisfied: concurrent_pending_instructions_are_not_cross_contaminated (two concurrent pending, only one observation arrives, other instruction not falsely Contradicted) + anti-vacuity confirmed reverting the fix fails that test. Verification commands: xtask check -p sinexd; xtask test -p sinexd -E "test(instruction_reconciler)".

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Fixed and merged in PR #2562 (commit 28b4bd14). Root cause: reconcile_workspace_observation() drained ALL pending Hyprland workspace-switch instructions and evaluated every one against whichever single observation arrived first -- the observation payload carries no dispatch-correlation id back to the instruction, only desired_workspace_id vs to_workspace_id. Fix: a pending instruction is now only resolved against an arriving observation when its deadline has elapsed, its desired_workspace_id matches the observed workspace, or it is the sole pending candidate (unambiguous N=1 case, preserving prior Contradicted semantics there); otherwise it stays pending untouched instead of being drained. Added ScopeReconciler::flush_due()/flush() (mirroring Windowed::flush_due) plus ScopeReconcilerWrapper::timer_flush_derived(), reusing the existing periodic-timer infra; instruction_reconciler now flushes deadline-elapsed pending instructions to TimedOut via idle flush even if no observation ever arrives. Verification: xtask check -p sinexd; xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(instruction_reconciler)' (6 tests, 2 new: concurrent_pending_instructions_are_not_cross_contaminated, idle_flush_times_out_pending_instruction_with_no_observation). Anti-vacuity: reverting the per-candidate correlation guard to 'false' reproduces the bug and fails the new cross-contamination test (left: 2, right: 1). xtask check -p sinexd --lint has one pre-existing unrelated failure in crate/sinex-primitives/src/commit_frontier.rs (clippy::expect-used, last touched 2026-07-09) -- not part of this change, zero findings in touched files.

title: Systemic: 6 automata unconditionally overwrite last-seen timestamp state with no monotonic guard, corrupting gap/window arithmetic on out-of-order arrival
description: Audit wave 1 finding (automata lane). health.rs:307-315 (status_changed/current_status/status_since from arrival order, no ts_orig comparison -- an out-of-order health.status event silently REVERTS current status to a stale healthier value, suppressing a real outage). hourly.rs:174-184 and daily.rs:177-187 (bucket-transition check is current_bucket != bucket_start only, never checks direction -- late input reopens an already-emitted bucket, truncating the currently-open one, duplicate/partial rollups with no error signal). relation_extractor.rs:196,214 (state.last_seen = Some(now) unconditional overwrite, no monotonic guard -- unlike the ADJACENT entity_enricher.rs which guards correctly; drain_and_emit_pairs picks last-pushed not max-arrived_at). session.rs:161-168,229-230 (last_window_end overwritten unconditionally, session_start fixed to first-arriving not earliest-by-time window, resulting negative duration silently .max(0)-clamped rather than flagged). analytics.rs:328-334 (last_event_time unconditional overwrite corrupts subsequent gap-close classification). This is the SAME bug class already fixed in interval_lift.rs (sinex-uzc/sinex-zs6) and correctly avoided in entity_enricher.rs -- six independent automata reimplemented the vulnerable pattern instead of adopting the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the six sites adopts a monotonic/tie-aware guard equivalent to entity_enrichers or the fixed interval_lift.rs pattern (deterministic tiebreak for equal ts, out-of-order routed to durable debt or explicitly handled, never silent overwrite/clamp). Tests cover each of the six automata with an out-of-order/late-arrival fixture proving the corrected behavior. VERIFY per-automaton test names to be defined by implementer, following the interval_lift regression-test shape.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (automata lane, which internally used 5 parallel sub-checks). RECOMMENDED as one coherent implementation slice covering the shared pattern (implementer suggests reusing/extending the sinex-pdq5 interval-property-suite harness) rather than 6 unrelated point fixes -- systemic pattern-adoption gap, not 6 independent bugs. health.rs status-revert (item 1) is the most operationally dangerous instance: it can suppress a REAL outage.
close_reason: Merged PR #2556 (cdefa24f3). All 6 sites fixed (health.rs highest priority, hourly.rs+daily.rs, relation_extractor.rs, session.rs, analytics.rs), each with dedicated regression tests following the interval_lift (sinex-uzc/sinex-zs6) fix shape: monotonic watermark guard, deterministic tie-break on equal ts, out-of-order routed to a tracing::warn (durable debt) rather than silent overwrite/clamp. Independently re-verified by coordinator: reviewed health.rs and relation_extractor.rs diffs directly (correct watermark-anchored window pruning, correct max-arrived_at ts_orig computation replacing last-pushed). Re-ran xtask test -p sinexd -E test(/health/)-or-test(/hourly/)-or-test(/daily/)-or-test(/relation_extractor/)-or-test(/session/)-or-test(/analytics/) myself: 116/117 passed; the 1 failure (test_service_health_monitoring, event_engine startup readiness) independently confirmed pre-existing on unmodified master (not touched by this PR), filed separately as sinex-audit-svc-health-flake.

title: Collapsed sinexd daemon has no hard memory ceiling (MemoryMax) by default -- rebuild-time OOM risk
description: Audit wave 1 finding. Post source-collapse, ALL source bindings + automata + API run in one sinexd.service unit (nixos/modules/sources.nix:568-575,939) governed by exactly one resource block: mkBaseServiceConfig coreCfg.api.resources. resourceModule defaults defaultMemory=8G/defaultCpu=75% (default.nix:836-840) but memoryMax defaults to null regardless (default.nix:108-113) -- only MemoryHigh=8G (soft throttle) applies, no hard kill unless an operator sets one explicitly. Confirmed unset in both nixos/examples/workstation.nix and the live sinnix services/sinex.nix. Contrast: per-automaton light/standard/heavy profiles DO pair memoryHigh with a hard memoryMax citing a 2026-05-15 forensic (automaton leaked to 4.5G RSS unbounded) -- that lesson is not applied to the live daemon's actual cgroup boundary (per-automaton profiles are dead post-collapse, tracked separately as sinex-om75).
acceptance_criteria: services.sinex.core.api.resources.memoryMax is set to an explicit hard cap (e.g. 12-16G on a 32G host) in the live sinnix deployment before the Phase C rebuild runs.
notes: HIGH priority specifically because bulk re-import of all sources through one process (the exact rebuild operation) is the highest-memory-pressure workload sinexd runs (MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 comment at sources.nix:278 re backlog-drain RSS pinning). Without a hard cap, a leak/backlog spike during rebuild competes with Postgres for host RAM until host-level OOM/earlyoom intervenes instead of a clean systemd-scoped restart -- risking a badly-timed kill mid-transaction on Postgres during the rebuild window.
close_reason: Wired services.sinex.core.api.resources.memoryMax=14G on sinnix-prime (sinnix abbe7c9, pushed to master). Verified in built sinexd.service unit: MemoryHigh=8G/MemoryMax=14G both present via nix build --no-link, no activation run. AC satisfied.

Verified in the built sinexd.service unit derivation: MemoryHigh=8G / MemoryMax=14G both present. nix build .#nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.config.system.build.toplevel succeeded; no switch/boot run, config-only change pending operator deploy.

title: No backup mechanism actually wired anywhere -- prod has zero recovery path outside a second full wipe+reimport
description: Audit wave 1 finding, coordinator-verified: grepped /realm/project/sinnix/modules/services/sinex.nix and hosts/sinnix-prime/ for pg_basebackup, sinex-basebackup, walArchiveCommand -- zero hits, confirmed. crate/sinex-db/docs/backup_restore.md:38-40 states outright the sinex module does not ship a pg_basebackup timer and the operator was supposed to add one to host config -- nobody did. nixos/modules/database.nix walArchiveCommand defaults to null (WAL archiving explicitly optional, unset). sinex-w98 (existing open bead for backup/restore drill) asserts in its own description that prod pg backup exists per backup_restore.md -- that premise is FALSE, the doc only documents a manual pattern nobody actually applied.
acceptance_criteria: A pg_basebackup timer (or equivalent) is actually wired into sinnix services.sinex host config, not just documented as something an operator should add. VERIFY: after wiring, a backup artifact exists on disk/off-machine and a restore drill (sinex-w98 scope) succeeds from it.

Recommend wiring this BEFORE declaring the rebuild campaign done, not after. sinex-w98's description should be corrected to remove the false premise.

title: Client-controlled actor_kind self-authorizes curation finalization
description: Audit wave 1 (sinex-audit-wave1) finding, verified by coordinator. CurationRecordJudgmentRequest.actor_kind (crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/curation.rs:88) is a plain client-supplied JSON field, copied verbatim into the persisted curation.judgment event by handle_curation_record_judgment (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs:295,566) with no derivation from RpcAuthContext. judgment_actor_sufficient_for_acceptance (crate/sinex-primitives/src/authority.rs:317-332) treats User/Operator/DeterministicPolicy/TestFixture as ALWAYS sufficient authority by themselves -- only Agent needs an explicit grant. handle_curation_finalize (crate/sinexd/src/authority.rs, crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs:677-684) calls authorize_finalization using the actor_kind read back from that client-set DB row. Both curation.judgments.record and curation.finalize are gated at RpcRole::Write, the same tier as ordinary event ingestion -- well below Admin. CurationJudgmentActorKind::TestFixture (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payloads/curation.rs:54) has a doc comment claiming test-only existence but carries NO #[cfg(test)] gate -- confirmed reachable via ordinary JSON deserialization in the production binary.
acceptance_criteria: A holder of a plain :write token cannot self-authorize curation finalization by claiming actor_kind=operator/user/test_fixture. Concretely: (1) actor_kind is derived/clamped server-side from the authenticated RpcAuthContext.role/actor_id rather than trusted verbatim from the request body -- e.g. a Role::Write token can only ever record a judgment as Agent-kind; only Role::Admin tokens may assert Operator/User. (2) CurationJudgmentActorKind::TestFixture is gated behind #[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))] so it cannot be constructed from production JSON at all. VERIFY: a new test proves a :write-scoped auth context cannot get a judgment finalized via a self-claimed Operator/TestFixture actor_kind -- the finalize call must fail closed.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1, coordinator-verified against source (actor_kind flow + TestFixture cfg-gate absence both confirmed directly). This is the sinex-0vx.5 authority gate's real threat model gap: that PRs review verified Agent-kind is never auto-sufficient by default, but did not verify that actor_kind itself is bound to authenticated identity rather than client-supplied. Should be prioritized for wave-2 implementation given exploitability with the weakest mutating token tier.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2553: actor_kind is now clamped server-side to the authenticated RpcAuthContext.role (Role::Admin passes through, everything below forced to Agent) instead of trusted verbatim from the client. CurationJudgmentActorKind::TestFixture gated behind cfg(any(test, feature="testing")). AC1 (server-side derivation/clamp) satisfied: crate/sinexd/src/authority.rs clamp_judgment_actor_kind, wired into both record-judgment handlers in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs. AC2 (TestFixture cfg-gated) satisfied: crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payloads/curation.rs. AC3 (test proving :write cannot self-authorize) satisfied: curation_record_judgment_clamps_self_claimed_operator_actor_kind in crate/sinexd/tests/api/curation_handlers_test.rs, plus clamp_judgment_actor_kind_forces_agent_below_admin unit test in crate/sinexd/src/authority_test.rs. Verification: xtask check -p sinex-primitives -p sinexd clean; all curation/authority/finalizer tests re-verified individually passing; pre-push schema-bundle drift guard passed.

title: 19 sinex-db tests fail on unmodified master (6% of suite) — pre-existing, discovered during sinex-w1w7
description:
Discovered 2026-08-01 while reverifying sinex-w1w7's admission-time content-hash fix: running the FULL sinex-db test suite surfaced 19/304 failures. Independently confirmed via a clean worktree checkout of origin/master (commit 04eb820e3, zero local changes) that ALL 19 fail identically there too — this is pre-existing baseline breakage, not caused by sinex-w1w7 or any other recent change.

## Steps to Reproduce
xtask test -p sinex-db --test '*' --impact-mode=off (against a real dev DB) on unmodified origin/master.

## Failing tests (19)
- composable_query_test: test_lineage_ancestors, test_lineage_descendants, test_lineage_max_depth
- database_test: test_concurrent_event_insertion
- lifecycle_restore_test: cascade_restore_preserves_synthetic_metadata_columns
- replay_state_machine_test: replay_preview_nulls_cascade_impact_when_metadata_queries_fail
- repositories_events: all_automaton_model_variants_roundtrip, all_temporal_policy_variants_roundtrip, events_repository_preserves_provenance, get_material_root_events_in_range_excludes_synthesis_rows, synthetic_metadata_roundtrips_through_insert, synthetic_metadata_survives_batch_insert, test_replacement_query_distinguishes_material_from_derived
- repositories_schema_management: concurrent_schema_bundle_sync_is_idempotent
- repositories_state: fresh_runtime_health_preserves_live_run_identity, health_events_attach_live_run_identity, runtime_presence_uses_latest_nonterminal_run_per_manifest
- temporal_facts_view_test: mixed_projection_no_cross_contamination, synthetic_event_projected_inline

Many share a shape: "assertion left == right failed" with left:0 right:1 (something that should have produced/found one row produced/found zero) — suggests a possible common root cause (a shared helper, fixture, or timing assumption broken for all of them at once), but this needs real investigation, not assumed from the shared shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Root-cause each failure (or the shared root cause if one exists across several).
- Either fix the underlying bug, or determine these are environment-specific (e.g. depend on DB extension/version not present in this dev setup) and document why with evidence.
- xtask test -p sinex-db --test '*' passes clean (or every remaining failure has its own tracked, justified exception).
notes:
## Root cause identified (2026-08-01, cross-session, sinex-xjx8 resurrection work)

Confirmed via isolated reproduction (xtask test -p sinex-db --test composable_query_test -t 2): all three composable_query_test lineage failures, and by identical error signature the repositories_events/repositories_state/temporal_facts_view_test/lifecycle_restore_test/replay_state_machine_test/database_test failures, share ONE root cause:

  Validation error: insert event (sqlstate: 23514, constraint: events_derived_requires_product_class, ...)

i.e. a derived-event insert (source_event_ids set) that omits product_class, which core.events has required since the sinex-0vx.4 / sinex-8cr.2 derivation-control-plane rollout (commit ae9b51221, PR #2508, 'persist product/support metadata through every event insert path'). That PR did not update every pre-existing test fixture that constructs a derived event -- these 18 tests (of your 19; repositories_schema_management/concurrent_schema_bundle_sync_is_idempotent is the one exception, likely a separate/environmental cause) all go through a shared derived-event construction path that predates product_class enforcement.

Likely fix shape: a shared test helper used by these fixtures (composable_query_test.rs / repositories_events.rs / repositories_state.rs / temporal_facts_view_test.rs / lifecycle_restore_test.rs / replay_state_machine_test.rs / database_test.rs) needs a product_class/claim_support/derivation.product_declarations default for derived-event construction -- same treatment sinex-xjx8 applied per-file to crate/sinex-db/tests/schema/*.rs (see that bead's closing notes for the exact pattern: ensure_product_declaration_for + product_class/claim_support columns on the insert).

## Related, separate finding from the same discovery pass

crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events_test.rs's no_extraneous_columns and column_count_matches_schema unit tests ALSO fail (not in your original 19 -- these are src/ unit tests, not tests/ integration tests, so xtask test -p sinex-db --test '*' with a --test filter wouldn't have picked them up unless run with --lib too). They assert a hardcoded EXPECTED_COLUMNS list of 26 columns against the live event_select_columns! macro output, now 32 columns -- again consistent with #2508 adding 6 derivation-control-plane columns (product_class, claim_support, derivation_declaration_id, derivation_epoch_id, derivation_lane_id, adjudication_event_id) that EXPECTED_COLUMNS was never updated for. Worth folding into this bead's AC.

(Filed independently as sinex-70gu before discovering this bead already existed -- closing 70gu as duplicate, this bead sinex-94mh is the canonical tracker.)
close_reason:
Merged #2540. Found and fixed FIVE distinct real bugs behind the shared "assertion left==right, left:0 right:1" shape (not one root cause, as the bead's own notes flagged as uncertain):

1. 14/19 failures: stale test fixtures predating the sinex-0vx.4/8cr.2 events_derived_requires_product_class CHECK constraint (fixture repair, mirrors PR #2539's pattern).
2. Real production bug: EventsRepository::insert() unconditionally ran REPEATABLE READ, causing deterministic sqlstate 40001 serialization failures on concurrent material inserts sharing one source_material_id — fixed by scoping REPEATABLE READ to derived-event inserts only.
3. Real, currently-live production bug: core.execute_cascade_restore() never carried 9 columns (product_class, claim_support, derivation_declaration_id, derivation_epoch_id, derivation_lane_id, adjudication_event_id, anchor_payload_hash, ts_quality, content_hash) through from audit.archived_events on restore — silent data loss (or hard failure post-CHECK-constraint) on the crash-recovery/replay-recovery path. Fixed by adding the 9 columns to both INSERT and SELECT lists.
4. Real production bug: insert_new_schema()'s ON CONFLICT (content_hash) only guarded one of two unique constraints on sinex_schemas.event_payload_schemas — a concurrent insert racing on the other (uk_schema_identity) still raised a raw 23505 instead of converging. Fixed by targeting the correct arbiter.
5. Real bug found during isolation, not in the original 19: repositories_state.rs's shared health-fixture helper inserted source="sinex" health events into core.events, but source_role("sinex")==Reflection and the health view only reads reflection.events (sinex-4k4b doctrine) — silently making health rows invisible to every reader. Fixed by routing into reflection.events.

Verification: agent's own full-suite run (xtask test -p sinex-db --impact-mode=off --no-reuse -t 2) reported 372/372 passed, 2 skipped. Independently spot-verified in a completely fresh throwaway worktree: 19/19 originally-failing tests pass cleanly (isolated run), xtask check -p sinex-db clean.

Also produced real operational value beyond the bead's own scope: discovered and cleaned up 5 orphaned dev-postgres instances (72 processes) accumulated from this session's worktree churn, filed as field evidence on sinex-grlv; discovered a real connection-pool budget issue under default test parallelism, filed as sinex-96fg.

title: Curation and instructions RPC handlers create derived events without product_class declaration
description:
Discovered 2026-07-31 while working sinex-egyf (test-fixture sweep for the
sinex-0vx.4 events_derived_requires_product_class / events_claim_support_requires_product_class
enforcement added in PR #2506).

Root cause is NOT a test fixture gap for these 12 tests -- it's a production
code gap. Unlike the automata output path (which sinex-4k4b's fix pattern
covers via seeding a matching derivation.product_declarations row in the
TEST), these RPC handlers build and insert their OWN derived events in
PRODUCTION code, and never set product_class/claim_support/derivation_declaration_id
on them at all:

- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs
  - handle_curation_record_judgment (line ~104-107): builds a judgment event
    via `.from_parents([parent])?.build()?` and inserts it with product_class
    left None.
  - handle_curation_record_duplicate_judgment (line ~337-381): builds BOTH a
    duplicate-resolution proposal event and a judgment event the same way.
  - handle_curation_finalize (line ~470-473): builds a finalization event the
    same way.
- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/instructions.rs
  - handle_hyprland_workspace_switch (line ~170-173): builds an "attempt"
    event via `.from_parents([pending.instruction_event_id])?` and inserts it
    with product_class left None.

Because these are derived events (source_event_ids set) inserted with
product_class NULL, master now rejects every one of them at the DB level
(events_derived_requires_product_class CHECK). No test-fixture change can
fix this -- the insert happens inside production handler code, not in test
setup, so sinex-egyf's mechanical "seed a declaration for the test's own
event" pattern does not apply. Confirmed by reproducing: after seeding
declarations for every failure that WAS test-fixture-fixable, these 12
tests still fail because the handler's insert is the one hitting the
constraint:
  - curation_handlers_test::curation_record_judgment_persists_synthesis_event
  - curation_handlers_test::curation_duplicate_judgment_records_proposal_over_candidate_set
  - curation_handlers_test::curation_duplicate_accept_finalizes_through_operation_record
  - curation_handlers_test::curation_duplicate_reject_does_not_create_finalization_operation
  - curation_handlers_test::curation_finalize_persists_lineage_to_original_proposal_and_judgment
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_dry_run_records_plan_without_dispatch
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_dispatches_typed_command_when_observation_ready
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_records_unavailable_without_observation
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_resolves_default_socket_from_runtime_env
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_rejects_duplicate_active_idempotency_key
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_records_failed_attempt_on_socket_rejection
  - instructions_handlers_test::hyprland_workspace_switch_noops_when_already_satisfied

Real fix needs product/design judgement, not a mechanical sweep: decide the
right DerivedProductClass for curation judgments/proposals/finalizations and
instruction-attempt events, register derivation.product_declarations rows
for them (likely via a startup path similar to what sinex-0vx.5's eventual
declaration-reconciler would provide for automata, or an explicit one-time
registration at handler-module init), and set product_class/claim_support/
derivation_declaration_id on the handler-built Event before insert -- same
shape as the fix already applied to automata output in sinex-4k4b, but for
RPC-driven derived-event handlers instead of automaton outputs.

Verification: xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(/api::curation_handlers_test::/ or /api::instructions_handlers_test::/)' should go green once these are declared.
notes: sinex-x79t merged (#2528). Unblocked — dispatch now. The reconciler mechanism this bead should hook into: crate/sinexd/src/automata/product_declarations.rs::reconcile_product_declarations() + crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/derivation.rs::ProductDeclarationRepository, wired from crate/sinexd/src/supervisor/mod.rs::Supervisor::run. Curation/instructions handlers need their own small static declaration list (shape: DerivationOutputDeclaration) fed through the same reconciler call (or a sibling call right after it) rather than automata_registry::AUTOMATA — these aren't automaton outputs. See original bead description for the 4 handler call sites needing product_class/claim_support/derivation_declaration_id set.
close_reason:
Merged #2530.

Root cause: 4 production handlers (handle_curation_record_judgment,
handle_curation_record_duplicate_judgment [2 events], handle_curation_finalize
in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs; handle_hyprland_workspace_switch's
attempt-event write in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/instructions.rs) build
and insert derived events directly, outside the automaton adapter, without
ever setting product_class/claim_support/derivation_declaration_id -- so
sinex-x79t's automaton-only startup reconciler couldn't cover them.

Fix: 4 static DerivationOutputDeclarations in curation.rs (curation.proposal
= SemanticCandidate/CurationWriter; curation.judgment = OperatorJudgment/
CurationWriter, shared by record_judgment + duplicate_judgment since both
emit the same source/event_type; curation.finalized = ReportArtifact/
ArtifactWriter) and 1 in instructions.rs (runtime.instruction/
actuation.attempted = ReportArtifact/ArtifactWriter) -- 5 declared outputs
across 4 distinct (source,event_type) pairs. Each handler now stamps
product_class/claim_support/derivation_declaration_id on its built Event
before insert. Extracted reconcile_declarations(pool, writer_name,
declarations) out of sinex-x79t's reconcile_product_declarations so
non-automaton writers reconcile through the same production primitive;
wired two more calls into Supervisor::run's existing startup reconciliation
point (same fail-closed guarantee).

Test-fixture note: could NOT satisfy the original bead text's "no test-fixture
change" framing literally -- the sinexd startup reconciler only runs from
Supervisor::run, which the api test sandbox never spawns (this constraint
was already documented on tests/api/common/mod.rs::seed_product_declaration
by sinex-egyf). Added seed_rpc_handler_product_declarations() to
common/mod.rs, which calls the REAL production reconcile_declarations()
(not a hand-rolled seed row) from each of the 12 target tests -- this
exercises the actual production declaration+insert path, so it is not
"seeding extra test data" in the sense the bead was trying to avoid.

Verification:
- xtask check -p sinexd: clean.
- xtask check --changed-strict origin/master: sinexd passed.
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(/curation_/) or test(/hyprland_workspace/) or test(/reconcile_/) or test(/automata_derivation_declarations_cover_registry/)':
  22 passed, 0 failed (was 12 failed / 10 passed pre-fix). All 4
  registry-derivation-declaration + reconciler fail-closed tests from
  sinex-x79t still pass unchanged, confirming the reconcile_declarations
  extraction didn't regress automaton reconciliation.

PR checks: CodeRabbit rate-limited (0 findings, tool failure not an
unresolved actionable finding); GitGuardian passed. No hosted PR-blocking
CI in this repo -- local gate is the gate.

description:

This is also where sinex-rkv.15 (Takeout import) and sinex-rkv.16 (web-history backfill) get their first real dry run.

- sinex-08z idempotence report produced and its counts reconcile with what was actually scanned
- sinexctl runtime health reports all-green with no default-true masking (cross-check against sinex-r6d.3)
- no admission-correctness bug from the Lane B sweep (7s0/f8v/w1w7/wv7/4pm) reproduces under this rehearsal, or if one does, it's caught HERE instead of during the real Phase C
- results (pass/fail per check, evidence) recorded on this bead and cited from sinex-poma before Phase A is scheduled

- Empty-DB -> sinex-schema apply, zero manual patching: PROVEN.
- 2+ real historical-scan sources (journald high-volume, git-commit-history low-volume, atuin bonus) against real host/repo data, not synthetic fixtures: PROVEN.

A DIFFERENT real bug was caught instead, exactly per this bead's purpose: desktop.activitywatch source adapter references a stale schema column on the real local aw-server-rust DB. Filed as sinex-bdh9.

CORE CAPSTONE CLAIM PROVEN: Phase C's actual composed procedure (empty DB -> sinex-schema apply -> deploy sinexd dev -> real historical source scans -> verify) works end-to-end on this codebase as of 2026-08-10. This is what unblocks scheduling Phase A/the fresh-rebuild wipe itself -- which still requires a fresh, explicit operator go-ahead per standing session policy, not granted by this rehearsal.

Rehearsal executed 2026-08-01 in worktree checkout (isolated dev cache ca12d922becb, port 4224/19202) — NEVER touched sinex_prod or the prod systemd service. Full command log + evidence below.

Ran `schema-apply-bootstrap` binary directly (`nix build .#schema-apply-bootstrap`) against the empty DB with only DATABASE_URL set -> exit 0, silent, created 6 schemas / 50 tables declaratively. `xtask schema strict-diff` immediately after: `drift_count: 0`. Re-ran strict-diff again after the full rehearsal (post-ingestion): still `drift_count: 0`.

2. **>=2 real historical-scan sources against real /realm/data archive subsets: PARTIAL PASS with one deviation.** Used `git-commit-history` (this worktree's own real git history, 1813 commits) and `raindrop-bookmarks` (real export, `/realm/data/exports/raindrop/processed/bookmarks.csv`, 34,483 real rows) via a `.agent/dev/dev-source-bindings.json`-style manifest + `SINEX_SOURCE_BINDINGS_PATH` + `xtask run all-sources --bg` (in-process source-binding supervisor, `scan-source-driver` subcommand). Deviation: did NOT use `system.journald`/systemd as the high-volume example the bead suggested, because `JournalctlStreamAdapter` (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/journalctl_stream.rs) is hardcoded to `journalctl -f`/live-system-journal only — there is no config field to point it at the archived `.journal` files under `/realm/data/captures/syslog/journal/`. That's a real gap if the operator ever wants sinex to re-ingest the ARCHIVED journal captures specifically (vs. the live host journal) — filing as a follow-up rather than fixing inline (out of rehearsal scope). raindrop-bookmarks (34k rows) served as the high-volume source instead.

3. **sinex-08z idempotence report: NOT IMPLEMENTED (confirmed gap, not a rehearsal failure).** `rg -in "idempotence" crate/` finds zero hits anywhere in the codebase. sinex-08z is OPEN, exactly as tracked. No import/scan CLI run prints any suppression/supersession/idempotence line. This AC cannot be satisfied until sinex-08z ships.

4. **sinexctl runtime health all-green, no default-true masking: PASS.** `sinexctl runtime health` reported Database/NATS/Raw-Ingest-DLQ/Replay-Control/SSE-Confirmations all healthy with real evidence (DB ping, NATS latency 0.00ms, DLQ-empty check, etc) — consistent with sinex-r6d.3's fix (already merged, CLOSED) that replaced default-Healthy with evidence-gated Unknown. Cross-checked against `sinexctl sources status`: the source-level view correctly showed `raindrop-bookmarks` as `missing-material`/`gapped`/events=0 even while the *source driver's own* checkpoint claimed success (see finding below) — so the operator-facing read models are NOT masking the real failure; only the source driver's internal bookkeeping is wrong.

5. **Lane B sweep (7s0/f8v/w1w7/wv7/4pm) reproduction: NONE OF THE FIVE REPRODUCED**, but the rehearsal surfaced a NEW, more severe bug in the same class. Detail:
   - sinex-w1w7 (SupersedeOnChange content-hash) and sinex-wv7 (>2700-row chunk boundary) are already CLOSED/merged on master; not applicable.
   - sinex-7s0 (material ts_orig plausibility gate), sinex-4pm (payload_schema_id FK strip-retry), and sinex-f8v (reflection-lane admission lane-blindness) are still OPEN but their specific trigger conditions (implausible registry timestamps / FK violation / reflection-lane events) were not naturally hit by this rehearsal's two sources — absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, for those three.

## NEW FINDING (the important one): silent, total, self-reported-success data loss on raindrop-bookmarks

git-commit-history worked perfectly end-to-end: 1813 real commits -> exactly 1813 rows in `core.events`, exactly 1813 messages through `DEV_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_CONFIRMED`, exactly 1813 in the `event-engine-dev` JetStream consumer's `events_processed` stat. Verified via 4 independent surfaces (DB, NATS stream, consumer stats, `sinexctl sources status`).

raindrop-bookmarks did NOT: the source driver (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs, `emit_batch_durable` path added by sinex-r6d.11) ran its Phase-2 gap-fill scan, parsed the real CSV (fingerprinted header matches the real file's 11 columns exactly — genuinely read the real file, not a stub), and its checkpoint — durably saved to NATS KV bucket `KV_dev_sinex_checkpoints`, key `source-driver-raindrop-bookmarks-1...` — records `"total_events_emitted":27452` with every event settled as progress-unlocking (no "did not fully unlock progress" warnings logged, unlike a genuine partial-failure case, e.g. git's log did show that warning once and self-corrected). But:
  - `core.events` has ZERO raindrop rows (only the 1813 git rows exist).
  - `sinex_schemas.dlq_events` has 0 rows.
  - `audit.archived_events` has 0 rows.
  - `DEV_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS` stream: only 155 total messages ever published+consumed across the whole session (git + reflection heartbeats) — nowhere near 27,452.
  - `event-engine-dev` JetStream consumer stats stayed frozen at `events_processed=1813` (git's exact count) for 7+ straight minutes after raindrop's checkpoint claimed 27,452 settled, with `events_failed=0`, `validation_failures=0`, `dlq_routed=0` — the consumer never saw them at all, successfully or otherwise.
  - `sinexctl sources status` independently reports raindrop-bookmarks as `missing-material`/`gapped`, `runs=0`, `events=0` — the operator-facing surface agrees with the DB, not with the source driver's own checkpoint.
  - The source then got stuck indefinitely (30s poll loop, 5+ repeats observed) logging `runtime.checkpoint_kv_behind_total` / "Checkpoint KV is ahead of this save; skipping without regressing or crashing" every cycle without ever finalizing or retrying the actual scan.

Net effect: the source's own durable-emission receipt / checkpoint bookkeeping believes a full successful historical import of the entire real bookmarks archive (27,452 rows) completed and is durably settled — while not one single row of that import exists anywhere in the persistence layer, and the checkpoint being durable means a future re-scan of the same file would likely skip re-emitting (since the cursor already advanced past the whole file), making this data **permanently unrecoverable without a manual checkpoint reset**. This is the doctrine's documented "Known open correctness seam" (`CLAUDE.md`: "Emission is an in-memory handoff end-to-end until NATS publish: source cursors and automaton checkpoints can durably advance before outputs are durable") manifesting concretely and reproducibly, NOT merely under a crash scenario as the doc implies, but during ordinary same-process operation for at least one source/volume profile — and worse than "a loss window on crash", because nothing crashed, nothing retried, and the checkpoint is durably wrong. `emit_batch_durable`'s own doc comment (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/durable_emission_backend.rs) still says "it does NOT wire it into any real caller... that caller integration is the next slice (sinex-vxu et al.)" — that comment is now STALE, since adapter_source.rs clearly does call it as a real caller; this rehearsal is likely the first real-volume exercise of that integration.

Given repo doctrine ("Do not 'fix' these ad-hoc in passing — they are sequenced campaign work with a shared primitive; check bd state first", r6d epic), I am NOT attempting a fix here. Filing this as a NEW P1 bug is blocked by the known `bd create`/DB-schema-mismatch issue (Error 1105, Field 'id' doesn't have a default value) already flagged for this environment — recording full evidence here instead so it can be filed properly once `bd` writes are fixed. Suggested title: "Adapter-source emit_batch_durable settlement lies: checkpoint reports AdmissionSettled with zero events actually persisted (raindrop-bookmarks repro, 27452 events)". Should probably land under epic r6d alongside r6d.4/vxu/r6d.7/w4i, or be a prerequisite blocking sinex-poma Phase C (a real re-import that hits this exact code path for a large source would silently lose the entire source with a durably-corrupted checkpoint that resists retry).

## Other observations

- `$HOME/.cache/sinex/<service_name>.checkpoint.json` is a per-user, NOT per-checkout-scoped, checkpoint cache (confirmed via directory listing: stale files from July 3 for git-commit-history/raindrop-bookmarks under an OLD naming scheme, unrelated to this run's `source-driver-*-1` naming). Did not cause a problem this time (different key names), but is a latent hazard for Phase C: wiping prod DB/NATS state does NOT reset this directory, so a real re-import must also account for or clear stale local checkpoint files for any source whose service_name collides with a prior run, or sources could silently resume from stale cursors instead of truly re-scanning from empty.
- `sources.stage` RPC (used for manual one-off material registration) explicitly rejects directory/repository-shaped material (`crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:165-173`) — it's a dead end for git-commit-history/knowledgebase-vault-style sources; the only way to run those is the source-bindings-manifest + `scan-source-driver` mechanism. Took real effort to discover this during the rehearsal; worth a command-guide note (`xtask/docs/command-guide.md`) since "how do I run one specific historical-scan source against an arbitrary path in dev" isn't documented anywhere obvious.
- Civil-time (2ged), attention-window (60r), and occurrence-keying (ecy) checks were not exercisable: neither chosen source type produces intervals, attention windows, or is subject to the specific ecy identity concern; not a rehearsal gap, just orthogonal to git-commit-history/raindrop-bookmarks' event shapes.

## Verdict

Phase C is **NOT yet proven ready**. The schema-apply-from-empty step is solid (AC1 clean pass) and one full source (git-commit-history) round-tripped perfectly. But this rehearsal's whole purpose — proving the composed procedure works end-to-end for real historical-scan sources — surfaced a serious, reproducible, self-masking data-loss bug on the very next source tried (raindrop-bookmarks), of a more severe character than any of the five named Lane-B beads (it isn't a partial-correctness bug or a rare edge case; it's a full-source-loss-with-a-lying-durable-checkpoint). Recommend: block sinex-poma Phase A scheduling until this new finding is filed as a tracked bead and fixed or explicitly triaged/accepted by the operator, and re-run this exact rehearsal afterward before touching prod.

Commands used (worktree-scoped throughout, `direnv exec .` used repeatedly to force per-worktree env after discovering the shared shell had stale main-checkout devshell vars): `xtask infra stop`, `rm -rf $SINEX_DEV_CACHE_ROOT/dev-state/data`, `xtask infra start`, `nix build .#schema-apply-bootstrap` + direct invocation against empty DB, `xtask schema strict-diff`, `xtask run core --bg`, custom `SINEX_SOURCE_BINDINGS_PATH` manifest + `xtask run all-sources --bg` (git-commit-history + raindrop-bookmarks), `sinexctl runtime health`, `sinexctl sources status`, `sinexctl sources stage` (for the directory-rejection finding), direct `psql`/`nats kv get`/`nats stream info` queries for evidence.

title: attention-stream and interval-lift have zero NixOS deployment config — never run in prod
description:
CRITICAL rebuild-blocking finding (2026-07-12, discovered while implementing ijz6's corrected 8-set).

registry.rs (crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry.rs) catalogs 16 automata including attention-stream and interval-lift. But nixos/modules/lib/automata.nix's `specs` list has only 14 entries — attention-stream and interval-lift are ABSENT. SINEX_AUTOMATA_ENABLED is built purely from `map (spec: spec.automaton) (filter (spec: automataCfg.${spec.optionName}.enable) automataLib.specs)` (sources.nix:1740-1743) — there is no other path that adds names to this list, no "all" literal, no override anywhere in nixos/modules/*.nix or the sinnix flake (verified via rg, zero hits for "attention"/"interval-lift"/"intervalLift" across both repos).

Consequence: in the deployed (module-driven) sinexd, attention-stream and interval-lift can NEVER be started, regardless of any config setting — they are permanently absent from SINEX_AUTOMATA_ENABLED. This has presumably been true since these automata were added (interval-lift is the automaton just hardened in the fresh-rebuild campaign's Tier-2 work: sinex-ecy/uzc/zs6/5s6/pdq5 — PR #2484/#2485). If the fresh-rebuild wipe+reimport (Phase C) proceeds without fixing this, the rebuilt dataset will have ZERO state.interval and ZERO attention-stream derived events — a correctness regression far larger than anything the wipe was meant to fix.

Fix: add `attentionStream`/`intervalLift` mkSpec entries to nixos/modules/lib/automata.nix (matching the existing 14-entry pattern), add corresponding `cfg.automata.attentionStream`/`cfg.automata.intervalLift` option submodules to nixos/modules/default.nix (same enable/profile/env submodule shape as the other 14), and verify SINEX_AUTOMATA_ENABLED includes both names after `nix develop --command switch` (or `nix eval` against the module). Default enable = true for both (per ijz6's corrected 8-set, both are KEEP-7 pipeline-core automata).

MUST land and deploy BEFORE Phase C (the wipe). Blocks/gates the fresh-rebuild campaign's Phase C.

title: Land the generalized recorded-effect envelope contract
description: Land the independently reusable typed contract and persistence boundary for recorded effects before any embedding or analysis runner constructs keys. This child owns canonical RequestKey, ResultRecord, EligibilityRecord, ReplayPolicy, encoding/versioning, and the identity/eligibility explainer. Parent sinex-k4c.1 owns the recorded-analysis application; sinex-5v6 owns the embedding worker.
design:
CONTRACT AUTHORITY:
- RequestKey contains only pre-execution facts that can affect result bytes: operation kind; executor/provider/tool identity and revision; code/prompt/template hash; canonical input material/event refs and digest; canonicalization/preprocessing; computation parameters; input/output schema identities; deterministic/nondeterministic settings.
- ResultRecord contains output hash/digest, result/artifact refs, dimensions/shape, timestamps, cost/usage, producer, and emitted derived-event refs. Output hash never participates in request lookup.
- EligibilityRecord contains privacy/access authorization, policy version, redaction/invalidation scope, retention/deletion state, and replay decision. Eligibility gates reuse but is not computational identity.
- ReplayPolicy distinguishes exact reuse, revalidation, reuse forbidden after invalidation, and nondeterministic sample-only behavior.

Provide one canonical encoding/version, typed construction API, persistence/repository boundary, and dry-run explainer. Checked-in fixtures exercise at least a model-effect/embedding caller and a recorded-analysis caller. Operation-specific fields extend this envelope; they cannot define another key type. This slice deliberately excludes the full recorded-analysis runner and the real embedding worker.
acceptance_criteria: The typed envelope and persistence path land independently of either runner. A shared fixture canonicalizes to one RequestKey from model-effect/embedding and recorded-analysis caller adapters. Changing any computational input, tool, schema, or parameter changes the key; changing output bytes changes ResultRecord output_hash only; changing privacy authorization changes EligibilityRecord only. Dry-run explains both identity and eligibility. Invalidation prevents reuse without corrupting historical request/result records. A mutation test that moves output_hash or policy into RequestKey fails. No full analysis runner or embedding worker is required to close this contract child.
