title: curation finalize's set_lane_status write (708-722) can fail after the finalized-claim event already committed, leaving a permanent finalization with no matching lane promotion
description:
Distinct from the already-tracked sinex-j0hl (which covers extract_lane_id's parse-failure-after-insert ordering bug): even when extract_lane_id succeeds, handle_curation_finalize's set_lane_status write is a genuinely separate DB call from the finalized-claim event insert, with no transaction spanning both.

crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs:609-753:
- Line 708: pool.events().insert(event) -- the finalized-claim event, durably persisted.
- Line 718-722: if let Some(lane_id) = extract_lane_id(...)? { pool.derivation_lanes().set_lane_status(lane_id, "promoted", ...).await?; } -- a SECOND, separate DB call.

If set_lane_status fails (DB error, lane_id referencing a row that's concurrently gone) AFTER the event insert already committed, the result is a permanent finalization event asserting the lane was promoted, while the derivation.lanes row's actual status never changed.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for non-atomic multi-step DB writes across the workspace (2026-08-11), which also re-verified sinex-j0hl's claim holds and confirmed this is a genuinely distinct write-failure scenario, not the same bug.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger handle_curation_finalize with a proposal whose candidate_payload resolves a real lane_id via extract_lane_id.
2. Inject a failure into pool.derivation_lanes().set_lane_status specifically (curation.rs:720) after the event insert (708) has already committed.
3. Observe a permanent curation.finalized event exists claiming promotion, while the lane's actual status is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Both writes happen atomically (one transaction), or a failed set_lane_status after a committed finalization is detectable/retryable rather than silently permanent.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete race (set_lane_status write can fail after finalized-claim event already emitted); testable via a fault-injected DB-call-failure test.

title: xtask bench history persistence is non-atomic + trend/baseline ignore mode/profile + DB-pool scenarios drop thread dimension; replay state_machine allows silent metadata mutation after terminal states; pkm.rs silently downgrades unrecognized material_type to blob
description:
Findings from wave128-080 (xtask bench, lower stakes) and wave128-000 (sinex-db, directly relevant):

wave128-080:
1. xtask bench history.rs's run+results persistence is non-atomic across sqlite inserts (history.rs:90,106) -- a write error on the Nth result insert leaves a runs row with partial/no results, corrupting later trend/baseline computation.
2. Trend/baseline queries ignore benchmark mode/profile when selecting historical points (history.rs:130,165) -- comparing release vs debug runs mixes incomparable conditions into one trend.
3. DB-pool benchmark scenarios drop the thread dimension at execution time (runner.rs:256,341,397) -- multiple thread-count scenarios with db_pool_size set all run the identical command with no thread control, overstating matrix coverage.

wave128-000 (crate/sinex-db):
4. MEDIUM -- replay/state_machine.rs's update_preview/update_checkpoint don't enforce a state gate after terminal states (state_machine.rs:610-630,944-959) -- any caller can silently mutate replay metadata (preview/checkpoint) on a Completed/Failed/Cancelled operation, misleading monitoring/audit tooling that treats terminal artifacts as historically fixed.
5. MEDIUM -- pkm.rs's register_source_material silently downgrades unrecognized material_type values to SourceMaterial::blob() instead of rejecting (pkm.rs:418-430) -- a typo'd or deprecated material type is silently accepted as blob, bypassing type-specific validation paths (e.g. required_source_uri) used for file/stream-shaped types.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Inject a write failure on a non-first result insert in xtask bench's history persistence -- observe a runs row with incomplete results.
2. Compare bench history across --profile release and --profile debug runs -- observe trend/baseline mixes them.
3. Call update_preview or update_checkpoint on a replay operation already in Completed/Failed/Cancelled state -- observe it silently succeeds and mutates the terminal record.
4. Call register_source_material with a typo'd material_type (e.g. 'fil') -- observe it's silently accepted as SourceMaterial::blob() instead of erroring.
acceptance_criteria: Bench history run+results insert wraps in one transaction. Trend/baseline queries filter by mode/profile. update_preview/update_checkpoint reject mutation attempts once an operation reaches a terminal state. register_source_material rejects unrecognized material_type values instead of silently coercing to blob.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Multiple concrete, independently testable claims (non-atomic sqlite persistence, trend/baseline ignoring mode/profile) in xtask/src/history -- no tests found for any of them. All AC-shaped and directly testable.

title: supervised_watcher restart off-by-one (max_restarts=1 never actually restarts); drain.rs active_work can underflow; dispatch.rs defaults missing material_id to a colliding synthetic ID; bindings validation stops at first error; SSE dropped-delivery + DLQ-unknown never surface as unhealthy
description:
Findings from wave128-072 and wave128-048 (bundled, both runtime/api reliability signal gaps):

wave128-072:
1. HIGH -- supervised_watcher.rs restart-count off-by-one drops the first configured restart attempt (supervised_watcher.rs:243). `restarts += 1; if restarts >= max_restarts { return }` -- with max_restarts=1, the first failure immediately hits the limit and no restart happens at all.
2. drain.rs's active_work counter can underflow on a mismatched exit_work call (drain.rs:166-168, unsigned fetch_sub with no zero guard) -- wraps to a huge value, poisoning wait_for_active_work so drains report phantom in-flight work.
3. dispatch.rs silently replaces a missing material_id with a synthetic default typed ID (dispatch.rs:183-186, unwrap_or_default()) instead of failing fast -- inputs without a material id can collide on the same default source_material_id identity.
4. bindings.rs's validation stops on the FIRST malformed source_id despite claiming full aggregation (bindings.rs:130-173) -- operators must re-run repeatedly to discover each subsequent fault one at a time.

wave128-048:
5. sse_bus.rs's dropped-delivery accounting is never wired into the health signal it's supposed to feed (sse_bus.rs:224-229 increments a per-slot gap counter; the bus-level dropped_confirmations_total atomic that service_container.rs's health check reads is never incremented anywhere) -- confirmation fan-out reports healthy even when clients are actively receiving gaps.
6. service_container.rs treats DLQ-stream-lookup failures as "Unknown" and composite health still reports Healthy for that condition (service_container.rs:385,395-433,527-531) -- a broken DLQ observability probe doesn't produce a hard health signal.
7. rpc_server/protocol.rs's JSON-RPC validator doesn't constrain the id field's shape (protocol.rs:12-24) -- non-spec ids pass validation and get echoed back, risking client correlation/parsing failures.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure max_restarts=1 and trigger a transient watcher failure -- observe zero restarts happen.
2. Call exit_work() one extra time relative to enter_work() -- observe active_work wraps to a huge value.
3. Dispatch a parser call with material_id=None -- observe it gets a synthetic default ID shared by other None-material_id calls.
4. Provide 2+ malformed source_id bindings -- observe validate_bindings reports only the first.
5. Cause SSE delivery drops via a slow client -- observe dropped_confirmations_total stays 0 and health reports fine.
6. Make the raw-ingest DLQ stream lookup fail -- observe composite health still reports Healthy.
acceptance_criteria: Restart-count comparison allows the configured number of restarts (off-by-one fixed). active_work uses checked/saturating arithmetic or panics loudly on underflow rather than wrapping silently. dispatch.rs fails fast on missing material_id rather than defaulting. bindings validation aggregates ALL malformed entries, not just the first. SSE per-slot gap counts roll up into the bus-level dropped_confirmations_total health signal. DLQ-unknown status is treated as degraded, not silently healthy.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Lane G: self-selected as a candidate for TDD coverage in this campaign but not reached this pass (turn budget spent on depth over breadth for the 4 beads above). Still open, no test written.

title: knowledgebase.rs CRLF front-matter offset drift corrupts parsed body; finance.rs declared vs emitted occurrence-key field mismatch; media.rs misroutes plain '-->' text into timed-subtitle parser; directory_walk.rs unbounded symlink-cycle recursion; dbus malformed rules match everything; paginated-source cursors don't checkpoint page_index
description:
Findings across several source parsers, wave128-076 and wave128-064:

wave128-076:
1. HIGH -- knowledgebase.rs's split_front_matter miscomputes byte offsets on CRLF files (knowledgebase.rs:79-99). `s.lines()` strips \r but the running offset only adds +1 (LF width) per line -- on CRLF files this drifts by one byte per line, so body_start ends up inside the closing --- fence, contaminating parsed body content, tag/wikilink extraction, and causing unstable/double-publishing.
2. finance.rs's declared occurrence identity (date, description, first_explicit_posting_amount) doesn't match the actual emitted key field name ("first_amount" -- finance.rs:70,387-390) -- a real declared-vs-emitted contract mismatch.
3. media.rs's audio-transcript parser misroutes plain text containing "-->" into the timed-subtitle parser (media.rs:571-573), which then fails on non-timing content -- an ordinary transcript line like "A --> B" rejects the whole material batch.

wave128-064:
4. HIGH -- directory_walk.rs has no visited-node guard for symlink cycles when follow_symlinks=true (directory_walk.rs:162) -- a cyclic symlink tree causes unbounded recursion/stack overflow, stalling the source.
5. dbus_stream.rs's malformed D-Bus match rules silently become "match everything" (dbus_stream.rs:559,237) -- parse errors are filter_map'd away; an empty parsed-rules list is treated as "no filter" rather than "no valid filter," leaking broad traffic despite a restrictive operator config.
6. api_cursor.rs/email_gmail_api.rs's page-index position isn't checkpointed in their StreamFrame cursor anchors (api_cursor.rs:443,459; email_gmail_api.rs:577,760) -- every cursor resume restarts page numbering at 0, destabilizing anchor identity for paginated sources across restarts.
7. api_cursor.rs's retry jitter can exceed the configured max_delay bound (api_cursor.rs:157) -- capping happens before jitter multiplication, so effective sleep can exceed the documented upper bound.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Parse a CRLF-line-ended markdown file with --- front-matter fences via knowledgebase.rs -- observe body content includes part of the closing fence.
2. Compare finance.rs's declared occurrence-identity fields against its actual emitted occurrence-key field names.
3. Parse an audio transcript containing the literal text '-->' in an ordinary (non-timed) line -- observe the whole batch rejected.
4. Point directory_walk.rs at a symlink cycle with follow_symlinks=true -- observe unbounded recursion.
5. Configure dbus_stream.rs with malformed match rules that all fail to parse -- observe it falls back to matching everything instead of matching nothing.
6. Resume a paginated cursor (api_cursor.rs or email_gmail_api.rs) from page N>0 -- observe emitted records get material_offset starting from 0 again.
acceptance_criteria: Front-matter byte-offset computation is CRLF-safe. finance.rs's declared and emitted occurrence-identity fields agree. Timed-subtitle routing requires real timing-line structure, not just the substring '-->'. directory_walk.rs tracks visited inodes/paths to break symlink cycles. dbus_stream.rs treats zero successfully-parsed rules as 'match nothing', not 'match everything'. Paginated cursors persist page_index (or an equivalent) so resume doesn't restart page numbering at 0.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: AC1 CRLF-safe front-matter offsets: SATISFIED; verified by test split_front_matter_handles_crlf_without_body_contamination. AC2 finance declared/emitted occurrence identity agreement: SATISFIED; verified by test occurrence_key_field_name_matches_declared_contract. AC3 transcript routing requires real timing structure: SATISFIED; verified by test transcript_plain_text_emits_one_segment_per_nonempty_line. AC4 symlink-cycle traversal terminates: SATISFIED; verified by test test_symlink_cycle_does_not_over_collect_the_same_file. AC5 malformed D-Bus rules match nothing: SATISFIED; verified by test test_dbus_all_malformed_rules_match_nothing_not_everything. AC6 paginated checkpoint preserves page position semantics: SATISFIED; verified by tests page_zero_mid_page_checkpoint_refetches_page_zero, runtime_checkpoint_overrides_config_initial_cursor, and terminal_checkpoint_does_not_reimport. AC7 retry jitter remains within max_delay: SATISFIED; implementation clamps after jitter and verified by retry_policy_delay_caps_at_max. Verification command: nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd --impact-mode=off --lib -E source-correctness-target-filter; result 8 passed, 0 failed. title: source-material total_bytes finalization split across 3 non-transactional raw-SQL call sites, bypassing update_material_state -- permanent Completed+NULL-total_bytes state on write failure with no reconciliation sweep
description:
Source-material total_bytes finalization is split across 3 independent, non-transactional call sites, all bypassing the repository layer with raw sqlx::query! UPDATEs instead of the existing update_material_state (which already accepts total_bytes and composes into a transaction via a generic E: sqlx::Executor).

The registry INSERT path (insert_material_with_id, crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/source_materials.rs:260-346) never accepts total_bytes -- the column is always NULL at insert and the row is immediately status='completed' (default from SourceMaterial::new). Every caller that already knows the byte size does a SEPARATE, non-transactional raw UPDATE afterward:

- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs:385-402 (execute_worker_output)
- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:232-256 (handle_sources_stage) -- comment at line 242 literally says "Persist file size if we have it (registration doesn't set total_bytes)."
- crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops.rs:1905-1963 (register_email_staged_material -> update_material_total_bytes), called from a PER-FILE LOOP during staged mbox/maildir email sync -- exposure compounds across a batch.

Consequence: if the UPDATE fails after the INSERT succeeded, the material row is permanently status='completed', total_bytes=NULL. Per crate/sinex-primitives/src/sources/continuity.rs:391-428 (ContinuityScorecard::from_material_facts), total_bytes.is_some() IS the anchor_stability signal, and the doc comment states total_bytes IS NULL is supposed to mean "material still in sensing" -- so a genuinely complete material gets permanently mis-scored as anchor-unstable in replay/continuity reports (sinexctl replay preview), with no correcting signal. Confirmed no backfill/reconciliation sweep exists for this gap (reconcile_orphaned_sensing_materials in material_assembler/maintenance.rs:403 only handles the streaming-capture sensing lifecycle, not these handler-level Completed-with-NULL-total_bytes writers).

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for non-atomic multi-step DB writes across the workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a material registration + total_bytes UPDATE sequence via any of the 3 sites (media.rs worker output, sources.rs staging, ops.rs staged email sync) where the UPDATE fails after the INSERT succeeds (connection drop, pool exhaustion).
2. Observe the material row is stuck at status='completed', total_bytes=NULL permanently.
3. Run sinexctl replay preview or a continuity report against that material -- observe it's mis-scored as anchor-unstable with no signal explaining why.
acceptance_criteria: All 3 call sites route through update_material_state (or an equivalent transactional repository method) instead of raw sqlx::query!, so the INSERT and total_bytes UPDATE either both land or the failure is visible/retryable rather than silently permanent.

title: ARCH: 21 independently-defined, semantically-divergent UTF-8 truncation helpers (not one unreachable one) -- root cause of 9+ byte-slicing panics; corrected plan: promote existing sinex-primitives helper + narrow clippy::string_slice warn
description:
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS + CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (2026-08-11, from a dedicated Opus design investigation).

The original framing ("the one correct helper is stranded in a leaf CLI crate") is HALF WRONG. A correct, char-boundary-safe helper with exactly the max_chars signature most callers want ALREADY EXISTS in crate/sinex-primitives/src/views/common.rs:330 (truncate_chars) -- it's pub(crate), one keyword from being reachable, and sinex-primitives::views is not feature-gated, so sinexd/sinex-db/sinexctl/xtask can all already reach it (xtask's Cargo.toml already depends on sinex-primitives). The real diagnosis is 21 INDEPENDENTLY-DEFINED truncation helpers with divergent semantics, not one correct helper nobody can reach -- three of six "independent" copies are byte-for-byte identical (views/common.rs, shortcuts.rs, tui.rs; two of those in the SAME crate with zero layering barrier -- plain copy-paste, not a dependency problem). Two variants have actively diverged: context.rs:2108 gates on byte length but cuts at a char index (spurious "..." on untruncated CJK text); query_units.rs:548 uses a different ellipsis char and different semantics entirely.

DECISIVE finding against the newtype (DisplayText) alternative also proposed in this thread: this codebase already has a MAXIMALLY restrictive string newtype, Id<T> (crate/sinex-primitives/src/ids.rs:27) -- no Deref, no AsRef<str>, no as_str(), only Display. The exact byte-slicing bug shape is STILL committed through it 7+ times across the workspace (trace.rs:209-211,250-251,270-271; table.rs:58-60; views/events.rs:813-817; automata.rs:156-158; ops/debt.rs:413-414) via the unavoidable Display -> to_string() -> String -> slice escape. A DisplayText newtype cannot be stricter than Id<T> and would leak the identical way. Do NOT build a newtype for this.

Lint investigation: ast-grep (this repo's existing forbidden-pattern mechanism) is DOUBLY disqualified -- empirically confirmed type-blind (matches &v[..n] on Vec<u8> identically to &s[..n] on &str) AND macro-blind (tree-sitter treats format!/debug! args as opaque token trees, invisible to ast-grep -- and the MAJORITY of real bug instances are inside format!/tracing::debug! calls). clippy::string_slice (an allow-by-default restriction lint already available in this toolchain) is the right mechanism -- sees into macros, respects Deref-transparency, correctly ignores Vec/slice -- but firing it as `deny` would produce ~150-165 findings at ~90% false-positive rate (measured: ~135 string-typed range-index sites total across the workspace, only ~15-20 are real bugs; the rest are correct .find()/regex-offset-derived slicing in parsers like privacy/detector.rs, zsh_history.rs, finance.rs). Use `warn`, not `deny` -- an allowlist of ~140 exceptions is exactly the fossilized-diff antipattern this project's own doctrine forbids.

CONCRETE PLAN (supersedes this bead's original acceptance criteria):
1. Promote truncate_chars to pub, move to a new crate/sinex-primitives/src/text.rs module (sibling to units.rs), re-export from views/common.rs for compat, delete the 3 byte-identical clones (shortcuts.rs, tui.rs, and the third copy).
2. Add sibling functions in the same module: truncate_bytes (absorbs sinexctl's truncate_str_boundary_safe, no ellipsis, for log/wire size caps), truncate_cols (delegates to the ALREADY-a-workspace-dependency console::truncate_str for CJK/emoji display-width correctness -- this is also sinex-8dus's fix, same call sites, don't fix width-counting twice), prefix_chars (replaces the 7 &x[..8.min(x.len())] id-prefix sites).
3. Add clippy::string_slice as workspace-level `warn` (not deny), matching the existing posture of unwrap_used/expect_used=deny, panic=warn in Cargo.toml:35-42 -- string_slice is the missing sibling of that family.
4. First 5 retrofits (max blast-radius-per-diff, in this order): (a) bench/environment.rs + reset.rs's /proc/pid/cmdline truncation (the only sites triggerable by ANY host process, not just sinex data) -> truncate_cols; (b) rate_limit.rs + rpc_server.rs's 4 token-prefix sites -> prefix_chars, AND correct sinex-lsmu's severity in the same pass (see that bead's own correction); (c) motd.rs's branch-name/commit-message sites -> truncate_cols (already uses console::measure_text_width nearby, natural first full-width-aware consumer); (d) delete the 4 sinexctl duplicate helpers (shortcuts.rs/tui.rs/context.rs/query_units.rs), import shared one -- fixes context.rs's live byte/char mismatch bug as a side effect; (e) the pub-and-move from step 1, listed last since 1-4 depend on it structurally but it's the enabling change not a bug fix.

Explicitly OUT of scope for this fix (different root cause, file separately): document_parser.rs:578-581 (needs floor_char_boundary on a chunking cursor, not truncation) and completion_endpoint.rs's 7 sites (need --cursor clamped to a char boundary once at the CLI parse boundary, not routed through a text helper).

Investigation used clippy::string_slice tested empirically against synthesized fixture files (not the real workspace, since bare cargo/clippy invocation is hook-blocked for a read-only investigation) -- confirmed macro-visibility, Deref-transparency, and slice-non-matching behavior on isolated test cases; expect the ~150-165/~90%-false-positive estimate to be directionally correct within roughly +/-20%.
acceptance_criteria: See the concrete 5-step plan in the description (promote+consolidate truncate_chars/truncate_bytes/truncate_cols/prefix_chars into sinex-primitives::text, add clippy::string_slice as workspace warn not deny, retrofit bench/environment.rs+reset.rs+rate_limit.rs+rpc_server.rs+motd.rs+the 4 sinexctl duplicate helpers first). Do NOT build a DisplayText-style newtype -- empirically disproven against this codebase's own Id<T> precedent.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11), together with sinex-lsmu. Fix: string-truncation helpers consolidated onto crate::text canonical implementations (sinex_primitives::views::truncate_chars and sinexctl's context.rs truncate now both delegate to crate::text::truncate_chars after strip_unsafe_display_chars), removing duplicate ad-hoc truncation logic. Verified via xtask check on the merged commit.

title: sinexctl _complete has 5 unguarded byte-index slices on the shell-supplied --cursor argument, very plausibly triggered since many shells report cursor as a char count not byte offset
description:
crate/sinexctl/src/commands/completion_endpoint.rs has 5 call sites (active_token:159-160, query_unit_candidates:349, ops_dlq_subcommand:634-636 x2, command_context:754-756 x2) that all clamp a --cursor argument's UPPER bound (cursor.min(line.len())) before slicing, but never check char-boundary alignment.

--cursor is documented (line 24) as "Cursor byte offset in the command line buffer" but is a raw untrusted usize from an external CLI/shell-integration caller. Many shells report cursor position as a CHARACTER count, not a byte offset, making this a very plausible real-world trigger, not just a theoretical one.

Failure scenario: `sinexctl _complete --line 'sinexctl query --tag héllo' --cursor 2` (or any cursor value landing inside a multi-byte character) panics the completion process, breaking shell tab-completion.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for UTF-8 byte-slicing bugs across the whole workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run sinexctl _complete --line 'sinexctl query --tag héllo' --cursor 2 (or any --cursor value landing inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character in --line).
2. Observe the process panics instead of returning completion candidates.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 sites clamp --cursor to the nearest valid char boundary before slicing, not just the upper bound. A test with a multi-byte-straddling cursor value confirms no panic.

title: document_parser.rs's chunk-boundary slicing (pos + MAX_CHUNK_BYTES) has no UTF-8 char-boundary check, on the live document-ingestion automaton path
description:
crate/sinexd/src/automata/document_parser.rs:578-581 slices raw byte arithmetic (pos + MAX_CHUNK_BYTES, MAX_CHUNK_BYTES=64*1024) with no char-boundary awareness, unlike every other offset in this file (all .find()-derived).

```rust
let want_end = (pos + MAX_CHUNK_BYTES).min(end);   // line 578
...
let search_slice = &text[search_start..want_end];  // line 581
```

Reached from paragraph_chunks (line 608-615), called at line 220 by the live document-parser automaton -- this is on the production document-ingestion path, not a diagnostic/error branch.

Failure scenario: any ingested document (knowledgebase note, markdown file, etc.) containing a single paragraph >64 KiB with no blank-line break, where a multi-byte UTF-8 character (accented text, CJK, emoji, curly quotes) straddles the pos+65536 cut point, panics the automaton.

2. Observe paragraph_chunks/document_parser panics on the byte-boundary violation.

title: token.rs's role-aware auth path doesn't trim the token (non-role path does) -- non-deterministic auth failure on trailing-newline tokens; snapshot.rs silently loses row-count integrity signal on transient DB error; verify baseline's --strict flag is a complete no-op
description:
Findings from wave128-028 and wave128-036 (gateway.rs SSE malformed-JSON silent drop from wave128-028 is already tracked as sinex-dah7, not repeated):

1. HIGH -- token.rs's role-aware token path preserves raw bytes (including trailing newline) while the non-role path trims (token.rs:58-62). A token file/env value with a trailing newline (common) makes role-based auth non-deterministically fail while the same source works fine without a role flag.
2. MEDIUM -- admin/snapshot.rs's row-count integrity signal can be silently lost (snapshot.rs:579, `exec::pg_row_counts(database_url).unwrap_or_default()`). A transient DB error during capture produces an empty row-count map with no error surfaced; later restore/dry-run can no longer detect row-count drift because expected counts are empty.
3. MEDIUM -- admin/snapshot.rs has inconsistent vanished-file handling between dirs and files in --mode live (snapshot.rs:664-703): directory copy tolerates disappearing entries, single-file copy aborts on the same condition.
4. sinexctl ops verify baseline's --strict flag is documented ("include advisory checks") but never branched on anywhere (verify/baseline.rs:27-35,192-201,258 -- check_closure_health takes `_strict` and ignores it). Operators cannot actually request the stricter verification mode.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Provide a gateway token with a trailing newline via env/file -- observe role-based access fails while non-role access with the same source succeeds.
2. Inject a transient DB error during pg_row_counts in a snapshot capture -- observe the manifest still records success with an empty row-count map.
3. Run --mode live snapshot and remove a top-level file mid-scan -- observe it aborts, while the same removal of a file inside a directory is tolerated.
4. Run sinexctl ops verify baseline --strict -- observe identical output to omitting the flag.
acceptance_criteria: Role-aware token application trims the token identically to the non-role path. pg_row_counts errors are surfaced (not silently defaulted) so restore/dry-run can still detect drift. Live-mode vanished-file handling is consistent between files and directories. --strict actually changes baseline's check set/behavior, or is removed if genuinely not planned.

title: initialize_with_transport leaks the schema listener + checkpoint-cleanup task on failed module init; replay scan workers spawned from command dispatch are fully detached from runner shutdown
description:
Two findings, wave128-071:

1. HIGH -- initialize_with_transport can return with background tasks running after a failed module init (initialize.rs:72). Schema listener + checkpoint-cleanup task are started, then if module.initialize(...) fails, the function returns early WITHOUT shutting either down -- Shutdown cleanup is never invoked on this path, and dropping the JoinHandle values doesn't cancel detached tokio tasks. A malformed module config or init panic leaves stale NATS subscriptions/KV cleanup loops running indefinitely.

2. HIGH -- Replay scan workers spawned from command dispatch are entirely detached from runner shutdown (command_listener.rs:358). `tokio::spawn(async move { execute_dispatched_scan(...) })` with no handle tracked; shutdown.rs:47 only closes command_listener/parse listener/consumer/batcher handles. Starting a long historical replay then triggering service shutdown leaves the replay task scanning/emitting after the command listener has stopped -- post-shutdown background activity, potential duplicate/late emissions.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger module.initialize(...) to fail after the schema listener and checkpoint-cleanup task have already started -- observe neither is shut down on the early-return error path.
2. Start a long historical SourceScanCommand, then trigger service shutdown while it's running -- observe the scan task keeps running/emitting after the command listener has stopped and shutdown has begun.
acceptance_criteria: initialize_with_transport shuts down the schema listener and checkpoint-cleanup task on any error path after they've started, not just the success path. Replay scan worker tasks are tracked and included in the runner's shutdown wait set.

title: event_engine heartbeat task has no shutdown gate (false-failure on every clean stop); BufferedAppendStreamWriter masks dropped-task send failures as Ok(()); IngestEventValidator's strict_mode is tracked but never actually enforced
description:
Three findings, wave128-056:

1. HIGH -- event_engine/service.rs's heartbeat task has no shutdown gate (service.rs:553). run_event_engine_heartbeat loops `interval.tick() -> emit_heartbeat` forever with no shutdown-signal check. On normal shutdown, this task is only killed by abort-on-timeout, so wait_for_tasks returns a background_task_timeout error even though every service-critical component shut down cleanly -- operator-visible false failure on every clean stop.

2. MEDIUM -- acquisition_manager.rs's BufferedAppendStreamWriter masks dropped-task failures as success (acquisition_manager.rs:1600 area). prime/finalize/flush all `return Ok(())` if writer_tx.send(...) fails (writer task already ended, channel closed) -- callers get false-positive success and proceed as if the control action executed, causing material-lifecycle state to diverge from reality.

3. MEDIUM -- event_engine/validator.rs's strict_mode is tracked but never branched on. IngestEventValidator::new_strict sets strict_mode: true, but validate_payload_for/validate_event never read it; should_accept still treats NoSchema/SchemaNotFound as acceptable regardless. The periodic schema-reload path (service.rs:1245) doesn't even thread strictness through load_fresh_schemas_with_options. "Strict" validation can become non-enforcing depending on call path.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start sinexd, then issue a normal clean shutdown -- observe the shutdown path reports a background_task_timeout error from the heartbeat task despite nothing being actually wrong.
2. Trigger the BufferedAppendStreamWriter's writer task to end (channel closed), then call prime/finalize/flush -- observe Ok(()) returned despite the control action never executing.
3. Construct an IngestEventValidator via new_strict(true) and validate a schema-missing payload -- observe should_accept still returns true (NoSchema is always acceptable) regardless of strict_mode.
acceptance_criteria: run_event_engine_heartbeat selects on a shutdown signal and exits cleanly rather than relying on abort-on-timeout. prime/finalize/flush propagate a real error (not Ok(())) when the writer channel is closed. strict_mode actually changes should_accept's behavior for NoSchema/SchemaNotFound outcomes, and the schema-reload path preserves strictness.

title: stage_as_you_go.rs loses an acquisition handle permanently if a preflight step fails between remove and the only reinsert path; automaton_runtime.rs drain exits on a transient empty-channel read, can lose late events
description:
Two findings, wave128-070:

1. HIGH -- stage_as_you_go.rs removes an acquisition handle from the shared map before an early-return preflight error path, permanently losing it (stage_as_you_go.rs:539). Handle is `.remove(&id)`'d, then resumed_prefix_len/skip_stream_prefix run; if either fails (UnexpectedEof, inconsistent resume state), the function returns BEFORE the only reinsertion path (which lives inside the finalize_result error branch). acquisition_handles loses the handle for that material while registry state may remain -- future finalization retries can't locate the handle ("Missing acquisition handle"), producing a permanently stuck in-flight material.

2. MEDIUM -- automaton_runtime.rs's drain mode exits on an empty non-blocking channel read even if the producer may still be alive (automaton_runtime.rs:336). `try_recv().ok()` returning None during a transient empty-channel gap is treated as "no more events," breaking the drain loop -- abort_runtime_work() is only called in a narrow pre-live-loop case, not when drain flips true later. Real event loss during shutdown if the confirmed-event producer resumes sending after a transient gap.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger resumed_prefix_len or skip_stream_prefix to fail (e.g. inconsistent resume state, truncated reader) after the acquisition handle has been removed from the map -- observe the handle is never reinserted and 'Missing acquisition handle' occurs on subsequent finalization attempts.
2. Trigger drain mode while the confirmed-event channel is transiently empty but the producer will resume sending shortly after -- observe the drain loop exits early on the first empty try_recv.
acceptance_criteria: stage_as_you_go.rs reinserts the acquisition handle (or otherwise handles cleanup) on EVERY early-return error path after removal, not just the finalize_result branch. automaton_runtime.rs's drain loop distinguishes a genuinely-closed channel from a transiently-empty one before exiting.

title: 3 D-Bus notification parsers (notifications/notification_closed/notification_action) always fabricate ts_orig and falsely tag it Intrinsic, unlike sibling parsers udev.rs/dbus.rs in the same directory which correctly use Atemporal for the same situation
description:
Three D-Bus notification parsers (notifications.rs, notification_closed.rs, notification_action.rs) tag a Timestamp::now() value as TimingEvidence::Intrinsic even though there is NO genuine intrinsic timestamp field in the D-Bus signal data at all -- the "timestamp" value is injected by the parser itself, not read from the source. This is worse than the missing-field case in journald/systemd/activitywatch: it's not a fallback for a sometimes-missing field, it's ALWAYS fabricated and ALWAYS mistagged.

crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/system/notifications.rs:72,109-115 (and the same shape in notification_closed.rs:81,100-105, notification_action.rs:72,86-90):
```rust
let ts_orig = Timestamp::now();
...
.ts_orig(ts_orig)
.timing(TimingEvidence::Intrinsic { field: "timestamp".into(), confidence: TimingConfidence::Intrinsic })
```

Contrast with two directly comparable sibling D-Bus parsers in the SAME directory that face the identical "no real intrinsic time available" situation and correctly tag it Atemporal instead: udev.rs:142,250-251 and dbus.rs:180,358-359. This asymmetry within the same directory is strong evidence the three notification parsers are simply wrong, not intentionally different.

Failure scenario: on replay, the parser re-runs against the persisted material and calls Timestamp::now() again at replay wall-clock time -- the persisted ts_orig silently becomes "when replay ran," not "when the notification actually fired," with the Intrinsic tag actively preventing admission's raw.temporal_ledger resolution from ever correcting it.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) of this session's confirmed activitywatch.rs finding, found by cross-referencing sibling D-Bus parsers for the same TimingEvidence-tagging convention rather than a literal unwrap_or_else grep (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Capture any D-Bus notification (sent/closed/action) event.
2. Observe ts_orig is always Timestamp::now() at parse time, tagged TimingEvidence::Intrinsic with field="timestamp" -- a field that doesn't actually exist as an intrinsic source value, it's synthesized by the parser.
3. Compare to udev.rs:142,250-251 and dbus.rs:180,358-359 in the same directory, which correctly tag the equivalent synthesized-now() value as Atemporal.
acceptance_criteria: All three notification parsers tag their synthesized ts_orig as TimingEvidence::Atemporal, matching the sibling udev.rs/dbus.rs convention, so admission's raw.temporal_ledger resolution isn't permanently bypassed on replay.

title: same-batch parent IDs bypass UUIDv7 validation entirely in ensure_source_event_ids_are_live; find_batch_violations flags cross-source clock skew as false regressions (no PARTITION BY source) and has one dead branch
description:
Two findings, wave128-004:

1. events/persistence/validation.rs's same-batch parent-ID bypass skips UUIDv7 validation entirely. validation.rs:119-131: source_uuids filters OUT ids present in batch_event_ids BEFORE the is_uuid_v7/DB-existence checks run -- the checks then only run on the remainder. A caller supplying an explicit non-UUIDv7 event ID that also happens to appear in the same batch gets it silently accepted as a valid parent reference with no version validation, weakening the UUIDv7-derived ts_coided/ordering invariant used elsewhere in provenance checks.

2. queries.rs's find_batch_violations has a cross-source false-positive and one dead branch. queries.rs:491-510: the LAG() window function has no PARTITION BY source, so ts_orig/id regressions are detected against the immediately-preceding GLOBAL row rather than the same source's prior row -- cross-source clock skew in multi-source ingestion produces spurious "regression" flags even when each source is internally consistent. Separately, `id < prev_event_id` is dead logic given ORDER BY id ascending (the prior row in that ordering is always <= current by construction).

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit a batch with event A (id = a UUIDv4, not v7) and event B with source_event_ids=[A] in the same batch -- observe the parent-liveness check accepts A with no UUIDv7 version validation, since A is in batch_event_ids.
2. Ingest events from two sources with slightly different clock skew, interleaved by id -- observe find_batch_violations flags a spurious regression on a cross-source boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The same-batch bypass in ensure_source_event_ids_are_live still validates UUIDv7 shape for in-batch parent IDs (only skip DB-existence lookup, not version validation). find_batch_violations partitions its LAG window by source, and the dead id-regression branch is either fixed to catch something real or removed.

title: content_store manager.rs leaks temp upload files on store_file/verify_post_write failure; cas_fsck.rs's missing-CAS report emits a literal 'XX/YY' placeholder instead of the real path
description:
Two findings in crate/sinexd/src/runtime/content_store, wave128-059 (the gc.rs empty-detailed-list finding from this same report is already tracked as sinex-zx3s, not repeated):

1. HIGH -- Temporary-file leak on ingest_from_bytes error path (manager.rs:405-419,425-429). Temp file is created and written; store_file(...) and verify_post_write(...) are awaited BEFORE cleanup; remove_file only runs after both succeed. If either fails, the temp upload file is left on disk indefinitely -- retry loops produce orphaned temp files, potentially exhausting disk under sustained load/failures.

2. MEDIUM -- cas_fsck.rs's missing-CAS report uses a literal placeholder path, not a real resolvable one (cas_fsck.rs:189-194): `format!("{LOCAL_BLAKE3_CAS_DIR}/XX/YY/{hash}")` -- the "XX/YY" is never substituted with the real hash-derived subdirectory. Diagnostics/remediation based on this report mislead operators about the actual missing file's location.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a store_file or verify_post_write failure during ingest_from_bytes (e.g. inject a write error) -- observe the temp file created earlier is never cleaned up.
2. Run a CAS fsck against a DB row whose blob is missing on disk -- observe the reported path literally contains 'XX/YY' instead of the hash-derived subdirectory.
acceptance_criteria: ingest_from_bytes's temp file is cleaned up on every error path (e.g. via a scope guard/RAII), not just the success path. cas_fsck.rs's missing-file report substitutes the real hash-derived subdirectory into the reported path.

title: browser history parser can emit events with no occurrence key (visit_id absent) or a shared visit_id='0' (row_id absent, malformed rows collapse together); ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length is dead
description:
Two occurrence-identity gaps in browser/history.rs (wave128-074) plus one dead-config finding (activitywatch's own ts_orig-fabrication from this report is already filed as sinex-dmz9):

1. HIGH -- Browser history parser can emit events without the declared occurrence identity. browser/history.rs:337,575: `visit_id` is optional in fallback parser paths; if omitted, `maybe_occurrence_key` emits NO occurrence key even though the contract requires identity derived from (source, browser_profile, visit_id). Records from secondary-leg exports or malformed rows lose occurrence identity entirely -- replay/repair can create unintended duplicates instead of stable dedup/revision behavior.

2. HIGH -- Missing row_id can collapse all malformed rows to one shared visit identity. browser/history.rs:358,360: for SQLite row parsing, missing/invalid rowid becomes 0 via unwrap_or(0), which is then used AS visit_id. Multiple rows with a shape mismatch (adapter query drift) all get visit_id="0" and share occurrence semantics -- incorrect replacement/collision, loses row-level distinction.

3. MEDIUM -- ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length is dead configuration (desktop/clipboard.rs:36,131) -- declared/documented but parse_record hardcodes raw_text.chars().take(100) regardless of the configured value.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed the browser history parser a record missing visitId -- observe no occurrence_key is set on the resulting intent, despite the contract requiring one.
2. Feed a SQLite row with a missing/invalid rowid -- observe visit_id becomes the literal string '0', and a second such malformed row gets the SAME visit_id, colliding with the first.
3. Set a non-default ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length -- observe clipboard.rs still truncates previews to exactly 100 chars.
acceptance_criteria: Browser history parser either derives a fallback occurrence key from other stable fields when visit_id is absent, or explicitly marks the record as occurrence-identity-less rather than silently omitting the key. Missing row_id fails the record or uses a genuinely unique fallback instead of the literal constant 0. ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length is read by parse_record.

title: email.rs parser hard-rejects entire message on any non-UTF8 byte instead of best-effort parsing; document/staging.rs silently drops non-UTF8 paths with no error
description:
Two non-UTF8-handling findings, wave128-075:

1. HIGH -- email.rs's parser rejects the ENTIRE record on any non-UTF8 byte in an RFC822 body/headers (email.rs:1605, `std::str::from_utf8(&record.bytes).map_err(...)?`). Real-world legacy-encoded or partially-binary email bodies fail hard for the whole message, producing zero email.message.* events, rather than a best-effort parse (MessageParser already provides fallback metadata paths that this hard-fails past).

2. MEDIUM -- document/staging.rs silently drops non-UTF8 record paths with no error surfaced (staging.rs:125, `Err(_) => { return Ok(vec![]); }`). A staged record with an undecoded path is treated as "nothing to ingest" -- silent data loss from staging/replay, not a parse failure the caller can see.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed email.rs a staged message with non-UTF8 bytes in the body/headers (legacy encoding, partial binary) -- observe the whole record fails to parse with zero output events.
2. Feed document/staging.rs a SourceRecord whose path bytes aren't valid UTF-8 -- observe it silently returns an empty intent list with no error.
acceptance_criteria: email.rs falls back to lossy/best-effort text extraction (or explicit partial-parse with a caveat) instead of hard-failing the whole message on non-UTF8 bytes. document/staging.rs surfaces an explicit error/warning for undecoded paths instead of silently returning empty.

title: hourly.rs's pending_window overwrite drops boundary-crossing events on flush lag (real data loss); health.rs's unhealthy_threshold_minutes is dead config; hourly.rs doc claims UTC but buckets by civil hour
description:
Three findings in crate/sinexd/src/automata, wave128-050 (entity_extractor/entity_resolver ts_orig-fabrication and interval_lift out-of-order-restart from this same report are NOT filed here -- ts_orig fabrication in these two is the sanctioned Derived-provenance default per the sinex-g0ve correction, and interval_lift is already tracked as sinex-e5fl):

1. MEDIUM -- hourly.rs's pending_window is a single slot overwritten on each next-hour event before emission (hourly.rs:194-203). If multiple next-hour events arrive before the old bucket flushes (flush lag/stall), only the LAST survives into the next hour's accumulation -- prior boundary-crossing events are silently discarded. Real data loss by construction, not a hypothetical.

2. MEDIUM -- health.rs's unhealthy_threshold_minutes is parsed from env (health.rs:42-44,91-97, SINEX_HEALTH_AGGREGATOR_UNHEALTHY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES) but no reconciliation/evidence logic in the file reads it -- dead config knob, same class as several other findings this session.

3. LOW -- hourly.rs's doc comment claims UTC-hour summaries (lines 3-4) but actual bucketing uses floor_to_civil_hour (lines 25-28) -- doc/runtime mismatch, consumers expecting UTC boundaries will misinterpret report boundaries across timezone/DST.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger flush lag such that 2+ next-hour events arrive before the current hour's bucket flushes -- observe only the last such event survives into the next hour's summary.
2. Set SINEX_HEALTH_AGGREGATOR_UNHEALTHY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES and observe no behavioral change in health.rs's reconciliation logic.
acceptance_criteria: hourly.rs's pending-window mechanism accumulates (or forces an intermediate flush for) all boundary-crossing events rather than overwriting a single slot. health.rs's threshold config is either wired into real reconciliation logic or removed. hourly.rs's doc comment is corrected to describe civil-hour bucketing.

title: admission.rs drops event_id on 5 rejection branches (missing/past/future timestamp, negative anchor, schema validation) despite the ID being known and logged at each site
description:
crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs's AdmissionService::admit_event_with_metadata rejects several parse-valid cases without attaching event_id, even when the ID is already known (wave128-051). Missing-timestamp branch (admission.rs:701), past/future-timestamp branches (724,745), negative-anchor and schema-validation branches (768,777) all construct AdmissionRejection::new(...) with no .with_event_id(...), even though event.id is available and logged one line above at each site.

with_event_id() exists and IS used in other paths (suppressed duplicates, admission.rs:682,337). The rejection docs explicitly state event_id is the candidate ID except when parsing hasn't reached that point (admission.rs:311,317) -- these branches ARE past that point.

Failure scenario: a malformed-but-parsable event with a known ID gets rejected; settlement/checkpoint unwind paths that rely on rejection carrying event_id can't anchor the exact candidate deterministically, mis-handling frontier/cursor unlock semantics on repeated bad events from durable streams.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit an event with a valid ID but a missing/past/future ts_orig, a negative anchor, or a schema-invalid payload.
2. Inspect the resulting AdmissionRejection -- observe event_id is None despite event.id being known and logged one line earlier at each rejection site.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 rejection branches call .with_event_id(event.id) (or equivalent) since the ID is genuinely known at that point, matching the pattern already used for suppressed-duplicate rejections.

title: event_engine/policy.rs redact_batch never refreshes the compiled rule set (only ensure_fresh/disclose_* do) -- write-path redaction can run on stale policy indefinitely
description:
crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/policy.rs's redact_batch snapshots the compiled privacy rule set without calling ensure_fresh, so admission-time redaction can run on stale policy (wave128-055, policy.rs:752-766):

```rust
let rules = self.rules.read().await.clone();
if rules.scopes.is_empty() && rules.external_rules.is_empty() { return batch; }
```

Refresh is only triggered by ensure_fresh plus the disclose_* APIs, none of which redact_batch calls. If a privacy rule is changed in the DB after process startup, ingested batches continue through redact_batch using the stale rule snapshot until some unrelated caller happens to invoke ensure_fresh or a disclosure path. Sensitive content can be persisted unredacted even though policy was already changed to catch it.

Directly relevant to the privacy-catalog work this session already flagged (sinex-t5sr: catalog confirmed empty in dev) -- once the catalog is populated, this staleness gap means rule updates don't take effect on the write path promptly.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start sinexd, let a batch flow through redact_batch once.
2. Change a privacy rule in the DB (add/modify a redaction rule).
3. Push another batch through redact_batch without any intervening call to ensure_fresh/disclose_* -- observe it still uses the pre-change rule snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: redact_batch either calls ensure_fresh itself (with an appropriate staleness/rate-limit policy) or is otherwise guaranteed to observe rule changes within a bounded, documented window.
close_reason: Duplicate of sinex-3l9n's redact_batch/ensure_fresh staleness finding (same code path, event_engine/policy.rs:752-766, same root cause). sinex-3l9n kept open (has an independent second finding: config from_args/default() asymmetry) and its AC narrowed accordingly. No fix landed for either; the underlying bug tracking continues under sinex-3l9n.

title: composable_query.rs lineage traversal (ancestors/descendants) ignores reflection.events entirely; knn_search silently narrows i64 limit to i32; email attachment metadata coercion masks malformed input
description:
Three findings in crate/sinex-db/src/repositories, wave128-002 (register_model race already tracked as sinex-dkkz, not repeated here):

1. HIGH -- Lineage traversal ignores reflection.events entirely. composable_query.rs:563,595 (fetch_ancestors/fetch_descendants) hardcode `WITH RECURSIVE ... FROM core.events e` for both directions. For reflection-lane events (or reflection-projected relationships), lineage can be silently missing even when related nodes exist in reflection.events -- UI/ops see incomplete provenance graphs.

2. MEDIUM -- embeddings.rs knn_search silently narrows limit from i64 to i32 (embeddings.rs:269, `.bind(limit as i32)` after validate_positive_limit). Callers passing limit > i32::MAX wrap to unexpected/negative values.

3. MEDIUM -- email_mailbox_projection.rs coerces malformed attachment metadata to 0 instead of erroring (lines 487, 532: `integer_value(...).and_then(|v| i32::try_from(v).ok()).unwrap_or(0)`), then attachment_observed_count = attachment_index + 1 -- projection state can silently become inconsistent.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call lineage() with a root event in reflection.events with related nodes also in reflection.events -- observe the recursive CTE only ever queries core.events.
2. Call knn_search with limit > i32::MAX -- observe silent truncation/wraparound instead of an error.
acceptance_criteria: fetch_ancestors/fetch_descendants query both core.events and reflection.events (or route by the root's actual lane). knn_search validates limit fits i32 before casting, erroring otherwise. Attachment metadata coercion failures are surfaced rather than defaulted to 0.

title: occurrence_filter.rs's bounded key fallback still unboundedly prepends SourceId, can still exceed DB column limit; Timestamp::from_postgres_timestamp silently masks invalid sub_nanos as unchanged
description:
Two findings in crate/sinex-primitives, wave128-015:

1. HIGH -- occurrence_filter.rs's bounded_occurrence_key_string doesn't actually guarantee its own DB-safety contract (occurrence_filter.rs:78-89). When the exact key exceeds MAX_EQUIVALENCE_KEY_BYTES, the hash fallback still prepends the full, currently-unbounded SourceId: `format!("{}|occurrence_hash={}", key.source_id.as_str(), blake3::hash(...).to_hex())`. A very long SourceId with a short payload key can produce a "bounded" key that still exceeds the 512-byte DB column limit.

2. MEDIUM -- Timestamp::from_postgres_timestamp doesn't validate sub_nanos is in the expected 0..999 range before recombining (primitives/timestamp.rs:74-82). Out-of-range sub_nanos makes replace_nanosecond fail and silently falls back to the un-adjusted base timestamp -- reconstructed time appears valid but is wrong, with no error.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct an OccurrenceKey with a very long SourceId (currently unbounded by validator) and a short remaining key -- observe bounded_occurrence_key_string can still exceed 512 bytes despite its bound contract.
2. Feed Timestamp::from_postgres_timestamp a sub_nanos value outside 0..999 -- observe replace_nanosecond fails silently and the timestamp reconstructs without the fractional adjustment, with no error surfaced.
acceptance_criteria: bounded_occurrence_key_string's fallback path enforces the actual byte bound including the source_id prefix (truncate/hash the source_id too if needed). from_postgres_timestamp validates sub_nanos range and errors (or logs) rather than silently falling back to base on out-of-range input.

title: sinex-schema: events_source_event_ids_no_nulls CHECK constraint doesn't reject NULL via array_position quirk; authority finalizer allowlist excludes operator_judgment
description:
Three findings in crate/sinex-schema, wave128-025:

1. HIGH -- events_source_event_ids_no_nulls CHECK constraint doesn't actually prevent NULLs. crate/sinex-schema/src/converge.rs:759: `source_event_ids IS NULL OR array_position(source_event_ids, NULL) IS NULL`. Inserting source_event_ids = ARRAY[NULL::uuid] satisfies array_position(..., NULL) as NULL (not false), making the whole predicate true. The constraint allows NULL parent references despite the column's purpose (concrete parent IDs), weakening provenance integrity.

2. MEDIUM -- authority.rs's finalizer output_product_class allowlist excludes operator_judgment despite the file's own doctrine describing authority as the mechanism for operator judgment emissions (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/authority.rs:91): `output_product_class IN ('canonical_derived_event', 'analysis_claim', 'semantic_candidate', 'report_artifact')`. Registering a finalizer intended to emit operator_judgment fails at insert time.

3. LOW -- schema-strict-diff.rs's documented exit-code contract (2=operator error) doesn't match actual behavior (all Result-error paths use process default, typically 1; only drift explicitly exits 1).

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Insert a derived event with source_event_ids = ARRAY[NULL::uuid] -- observe the CHECK constraint passes when it should reject.
2. Attempt to register a finalizer with output_product_class = 'operator_judgment' -- observe a CHECK violation despite the doctrine describing this as a legitimate authority output.
acceptance_criteria: The NULL-parent CHECK actually rejects arrays containing a NULL element (e.g. via NOT (NULL = ANY(source_event_ids)) or a proper unnest-based check). The finalizer allowlist either includes operator_judgment or the doctrine/schema mismatch is resolved with an explicit decision recorded.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Lane C (merged PR #2605): finding 1 (events_source_event_ids_no_nulls NULL-element check) is a FALSE POSITIVE from the original wave128 audit — Postgres's array_position is NULL-aware (array_position(ARRAY[1,2,NULL,3], NULL) finds the NULL), so the CHECK constraint already works correctly. Test doc comment corrected to document this. Finding 2 (operator_judgment excluded from the finalizer allowlist) is a real, still-open doctrine/schema mismatch — added a characterization test that deliberately does not presuppose the resolution.

title: ActivityWatch parser fabricates ts_orig at parse time instead of leaving it None for temporal-ledger resolution (material-provenance events only)
description:
crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/desktop/activitywatch.rs:224-227 fabricates ts_orig at parse time and passes it explicitly to the event builder, bypassing the Material-provenance "leave ts_orig=None, resolve later from raw.temporal_ledger" path that EventBuilder::build() is specifically designed to support (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/builder.rs:275-287, "#1570 Prong B").

```rust
let ts_orig = row
    .get("started_at")
    .and_then(parse_aw_timestamp)
    .unwrap_or_else(Timestamp::now);
...
.ts_orig(ts_orig)   // explicit setter, line 311 -- never leaves it None
```

Unlike derived-event automata (where wall-clock fallback is the correct, documented default -- see the now-closed sinex-g0ve, filed against the wrong files), this IS a real gap: ActivityWatch rows are MATERIAL provenance. A row with a missing/unparseable `started_at` should leave ts_orig unset so the event_engine admission stage can resolve it from the source material's own timing tier (the mechanism that exists specifically for this case), not get silently wall-clock-stamped at parse time.

Failure scenario: an AW export row with a malformed/missing started_at field (schema drift, corrupted export, edge-case device clock) gets ts_orig = "whenever sinexd happened to parse this row" instead of a real event-time or a deferred None. On replay/backfill this produces a different (wrong) ts_orig every run, corrupting temporal ordering and any logic keying off event-time.

Found via a narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark) as part of this session's wave128 fanout; re-verified directly against source and the EventBuilder's documented policy (2026-08-11) after an earlier related bead (sinex-g0ve) was found to conflate this with a different, non-bug pattern in derived-event automata.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed an ActivityWatch export row with a missing or unparseable started_at field to activitywatch.rs's row parser.
2. Observe ts_orig gets Timestamp::now() at parse time and is passed explicitly to the builder via .ts_orig(...), rather than being left unset for raw.temporal_ledger resolution at admission time.
acceptance_criteria: activitywatch.rs's row parser leaves ts_orig unset (routes through the builder's Material-without-explicit-timestamp path) when started_at is missing/unparseable, instead of fabricating wall-clock time. A test with a malformed started_at field confirms the resulting event has ts_orig=None pre-admission, matching the documented Material-provenance contract.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [PR #2615 2026-08-11] Fixed and merged: ActivityWatch ts_orig Atemporal handling corrected, with real tests added covering the fix. Note: leaving this bead OPEN per the original triage list rather than closing -- if the fix fully satisfies this bead's acceptance criteria with no remaining scope, it can be closed directly; flagging here rather than unilaterally closing since the AC wasn't independently re-verified in this bookkeeping pass.

title: RuntimeTargetGatewayTokenRole::apply_to_token silently ignores the requested role whenever the token already has ANY recognized role suffix, even a mismatched one
description:
crate/sinex-primitives/src/runtime_target.rs:103 RuntimeTargetGatewayTokenRole::apply_to_token does not enforce the requested role when a recognized suffix is already present on the token: `if let Some((_base, suffix)) = trimmed.rsplit_once(':') && Self::from_suffix(suffix).is_some() { return trimmed.to_string(); }` -- this short-circuits and returns the token UNCHANGED whenever ANY recognized suffix exists, even if it mismatches the requested token_role.

Failure scenario: a token file contains "...:readonly" or "...:admin" and a runtime descriptor requests a DIFFERENT token_role. apply_to_token() returns the token unchanged, silently ignoring the requested role -- a binding may run with lower or higher privilege than intended, causing authorization failures or unexpected operation capability mismatch depending on the token's actual encoded role versus what was requested.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/runtime_target.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Supply a token file ending in ":readonly".
2. Request apply_to_token with token_role = Admin (or any role other than the token's actual suffix).
3. Observe the function returns the token unchanged with the readonly suffix still attached, silently ignoring the Admin request -- no error, no warning.
acceptance_criteria: apply_to_token either reconciles a mismatched suffix (strips and re-applies the requested role) or errors loudly when the token's existing role doesn't match what was requested, rather than silently returning the token as-is.

title: journalctl_stream.rs blank-line handling corrupts cumulative byte-offset anchors (and the test-fixture helper computes frame indices differently from the runtime); parser fixture harness's FieldPresent/FieldAbsent null-handling is inverted relative to its own documented contract
description:
Three bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-066):

1. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/journalctl_stream.rs:155-157 blank journal lines corrupt cumulative byte-offset accounting: `if line.is_empty() { continue; }` skips before `bytes_read += len + 1` executes for that line's newline -- the offset isn't incremented for the skipped empty line, even though its newline byte was consumed from the stream. A journal stream containing blank lines produces incorrect material_offset for all subsequent non-empty records (offsets too small), corrupting occurrence-identity assumptions for anything relying on byte-offset anchors.

2. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/fixture.rs:744-751,754-761 the FieldPresent/FieldAbsent fixture assertions contradict their own documented contract on null handling: FieldPresent is documented "present (non-null)" but a JSON null value passes the check (only actual absence fails); FieldAbsent's comment says "absent or null" but a `Some(Null)` value is treated as a failure. The two assertions have inverted null-handling relative to their own doc comments, making the parser-fixture test harness itself internally inconsistent -- a parser producing null where it should have omitted the field (or vice versa) is masked rather than caught.

3. LOW -- journalctl_stream.rs:471-483 the test-fixture helper's frame-index computation diverges from the runtime path: the runtime skips empty lines via `continue` without yielding a record (no frame-index increment), but the test helper computes frame index from `enumerate()` over ALL input lines including blanks -- fixtures built with this helper produce anchor expectations that don't match runtime behavior whenever blank lines exist, causing spurious test failures.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/journalctl_stream.rs and crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/fixture.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed a journalctl stream containing blank lines followed by real entries -- observe material_offset on the post-blank-line entries is smaller than the true byte position.
2. Author a parser fixture asserting FieldPresent on a field the parser sets to JSON null -- observe the assertion passes despite the doc comment saying 'present (non-null)'. Author one asserting FieldAbsent on a field set to null -- observe it fails despite the doc comment saying 'absent or null' should pass.
3. Compare the test helper's frame-index computation (journalctl_stream.rs:471-483) against the runtime path's for a stream containing blank lines -- observe they diverge.
acceptance_criteria: bytes_read is incremented for skipped blank lines too, matching the real newline byte consumed from the stream. FieldPresent actually rejects JSON null (matching its 'non-null' doc); FieldAbsent actually accepts JSON null (matching its 'absent or null' doc) -- or the doc comments are corrected to match the actual, intentional behavior if that's the real contract. The test-fixture helper's frame-index computation matches the runtime path exactly, including blank-line handling.

title: privacy.rs add_dictionary skips projection-staleness invalidation; runtime_registry.rs swallows finalize failure leaving ops stuck Running; query.rs relation-evidence candidate query can become an unbounded scan on empty seed set

title: interval_lift.rs silently replaces open interval state on out-of-order older systemd starts (overstates duration); hourly.rs single-slot pending_window drops earlier next-hour events on flush lag; hourly.rs doc claims UTC but buckets by civil time; health.rs threshold config parsed but never read
description:
Three bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-050):

1. HIGH -- crate/sinexd/src/automata/interval_lift.rs:1009-1015,1034 out-of-order older systemd start events silently replace open interval state instead of being rejected: `let restart_close = state.active_subject_states.get(&subject_id).filter(|previous| observation.ts_orig > previous.ts_orig).map(...)` only computes a close when the new observation is NEWER; but the code then unconditionally does `state.active_subject_states.insert(subject_id, observation)` regardless. A delayed/replayed start at t=5 for a unit with an already-open interval from t=10 silently replaces the open state -- a later stop at t=20 then yields [5,20] instead of the correct [10,20], overstating duration. Contrasts with adjacent transition branches in the same module that explicitly guard against old transitions.

2. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/automata/hourly.rs:194-203 the hourly summarizer's single-slot pending_window is overwritten by each subsequent next-hour event before flush, silently dropping earlier next-hour events: with no intermediate emit before a second next-hour event arrives (flush lag/stall), only the LAST such event survives into the next hour's accumulation -- real data loss by construction for boundary-crossing bursts.

3. LOW -- crate/sinexd/src/automata/hourly.rs:3-4 vs :25-28 doc/code mismatch: header comment claims UTC-hour summaries, but bucketing actually uses floor_to_civil_hour (local civil time) -- consumers expecting UTC buckets will misinterpret report boundaries across timezone/DST transitions. Also health.rs:42-44,91-97: unhealthy_threshold_minutes is parsed from SINEX_HEALTH_AGGREGATOR_UNHEALTHY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES and defaulted, but no reconciliation/evidence logic in the file reads it -- operators setting this env var observe no behavioral change.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/automata/{interval_lift,hourly,health}.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Emit a unit.started at t=10 (opening an interval), then a delayed/replayed unit.started at t=5 for the same unit, then a stop at t=20 -- observe the resulting interval is [5,20] instead of [10,20].
2. Cause a flush stall in hourly.rs and emit two next-hour events before the stall clears -- observe only the second event's data survives into the summary.
3. Set SINEX_HEALTH_AGGREGATOR_UNHEALTHY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES and observe no change in health reconciliation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Relate to sinex-2ged for the civil-time doc/code mismatch.

title: xtask status --summary panics on non-ASCII git branch/commit-message truncation (byte-slice not char-boundary-safe); xtask snapshot --scope passes a bare arch string to cargo metadata --filter-platform instead of a full target triple
description:
Two bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-090):

1. MEDIUM -- xtask/src/commands/status/motd.rs:95,634 non-ASCII UTF-8 panic via byte-range slicing in MOTD truncation: `format!("{}...", &branch_raw[..max_branch - 1])` and the equivalent for commit messages slice by raw byte index without checking char boundaries. A Git branch name or commit message containing multi-byte UTF-8 (e.g. a branch like "feature/тест") longer than the truncation threshold panics `xtask status --summary` instead of rendering a summary -- external/user-provided git metadata, not sanitized before the slice.

2. LOW-MEDIUM -- xtask/src/commands/snapshot.rs:626 `cargo metadata --filter-platform` is invoked with just `std::env::consts::ARCH` (e.g. "x86_64") rather than a full target triple, in collect_crate_scope for a `--scope <crate>` invocation. --filter-platform expects a target selector (triple), and feeding only an architecture string can reject or misresolve target selection depending on Cargo's parser behavior, causing `xtask snapshot --scope <crate>` to error even for a valid crate request.

Found via narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{status/motd,snapshot}.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Check out a git branch with a multi-byte UTF-8 name longer than the truncation threshold, run xtask status --summary -- observe a panic.
2. Run xtask snapshot --scope <a-valid-crate-name> -- observe cargo metadata --filter-platform receiving a bare architecture string and check whether it errors/misresolves versus a full target triple.
acceptance_criteria: motd.rs's truncation uses a char-boundary-safe truncation helper (matching the pattern already fixed elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. truncate_str_boundary_safe used in sinexctl). snapshot.rs's --filter-platform argument uses a full target triple (matching rustc's target-list format) instead of a bare architecture string.

title: run_loop.rs catch-up throttle can stay engaged forever when observer is disabled; material_assembler finalize.rs swallows durable-failure-marking errors; policy.rs redact_batch doesn't refresh the rule snapshot (privacy rule changes not consistently applied to the write path)
description:
Three bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-053/055):

1. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/run_loop.rs:152-258 catch-up completion is gated on observer presence: `catching_up` can only transition to false inside `if self.observer.is_some() { ... if catching_up && info.num_pending == 0 { catching_up = false; } }`. With the observer disabled, the loop never observes num_pending==0, so catching_up stays true forever -- with a non-unlimited restart_drain_budget, the consumer remains in long-term throttled mode indefinitely instead of exiting startup-catch-up-only throttling once the backlog actually drains.

2. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/material_assembler/finalize.rs:248-258,424-443 route_material_error_then_finalize_failed's "unclaimed" cleanup path always returns Ok even when durable failure finalization itself failed (e.g. DB unavailable while marking a material failed): finalize_failed_material only warn!()s on error, never propagates. Caller sees success while the material was never durably marked failed/superseded -- silent loss of control-flow visibility, risking a material treated as handled with no durable terminal-failure state written.

3. MEDIUM-HIGH -- crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/policy.rs:752-766 redact_batch reads the compiled privacy-rule snapshot directly (`self.rules.read().await.clone()`) without calling ensure_fresh, unlike the disclosure APIs (disclose_event_payload/disclose_event_text/disclose_json_value*). A privacy rule changed in the DB after process startup is not applied to admission-time redaction in this path until some other caller happens to invoke ensure_fresh -- rule changes are inconsistently enforced on the write path, so sensitive content can be persisted unredacted even though the policy already changed.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/{run_loop,material_assembler/finalize,policy}.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run sinexd with the observer disabled and a non-unlimited restart_drain_budget, through a large-startup replay -- observe catching_up never clears even after the backlog fully drains.
2. Inject a DB failure specifically during finalize_failed_material's durable write, after route_material_error succeeded -- observe the caller sees Ok(()) with no durable failed-state row written.
3. Change a privacy rule in the DB after sinexd startup, then admit a new event through redact_batch without any other caller having invoked ensure_fresh -- observe the new event is redacted per the STALE rule snapshot, not the updated one.
acceptance_criteria: Given the redact_batch finding directly concerns privacy enforcement, relate to sinex-t5sr.

title: FilesystemSourceConfig's max_files/extension-filter/follow_symlinks/scan-targets fields are entirely dead (scan ignores all of them); file_tailer.rs's poll_utf8_lines re-reads the whole unread segment on every poll when a line lacks a trailing newline
description:
Two bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-061):

1. HIGH -- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/examples/filesystem_source.rs: FilesystemSourceConfig's fields are entirely dead. max_files, include_extensions, exclude_extensions, and follow_symlinks (declared :29-35) are never read anywhere in the scan flow (:121-187, :311-378) -- scan always iterates every self.watch_paths unconditionally, ignoring ScanArgs.targets too (:311,321-338,347-352,374-378). An operator configuring these knobs gets identical behavior regardless -- silent config-contract drift and unbounded over-scan versus intended behavior.

2. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/file_tailer.rs:174-176,189-197,219-222 poll_utf8_lines repeatedly re-reads an unfinished tail segment indefinitely: offset_bytes is only advanced for complete lines (ending in \n); a very long line without a trailing newline (or one appended slowly) means each poll re-reads and re-parses the entire unread segment from scratch. Under a long partial-line workload with a growing file, this is an O(n^2)-shaped re-read pattern -- real CPU/IO throughput regression, not just a correctness nit.

Found via narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{examples/filesystem_source,file_tailer}.rs (2026-08-11, wave128 batch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure FilesystemSourceConfig with a restrictive max_files, extension filter, or follow_symlinks=false -- observe scan behavior is unchanged in all cases (every file under every watch path is still processed, symlinks still followed).
2. Have a producer write a very long line without a trailing newline to a tailed file, growing it slowly -- observe poll_utf8_lines re-reads and re-parses the entire unread segment on every poll instead of advancing incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: Given the file lives under runtime/examples/, verify whether this is production-reachable or a template before treating the config-drift finding as user-facing -- adjust priority down if it's example-only, matching the earlier-session finding that some runtime/examples/ content is dead scaffolding.
