title: MAC-address detector misses uppercase hex; IPv6 detector's docstring claims IPv4-mapped-notation coverage it doesn't actually have
description:
Two structural PII/sensitive-data detectors in crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/detector.rs miss common real-world format variants of exactly what they claim to detect:

1. MAC address detector (detector.rs:314) only matches lowercase hex:
```
[0-9a-f]{2}(?::[0-9a-f]{2}){5}
[0-9a-f]{2}(?:-[0-9a-f]{2}){5}
[0-9a-f]{4}\.[0-9a-f]{4}\.[0-9a-f]{4}
```
`AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF` (uppercase, a very common format in logs/configs/OS output) is not matched -- sensitive MACs pass undetected.

2. IPv6 detector (detector.rs:246) has a docstring claiming it "covers full, compressed (::  notation), and mixed IPv4/IPv6 notation" but the regex's alternates only accept hex groups, with no IPv4 dotted-decimal tail:
```rust
/// Covers full, compressed (`::` notation), and mixed IPv4/IPv6 notation.
static IPV6_RE: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"(?xi)
    ...
        ::(?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}:){0,5}[0-9a-f]{1,4}
        |
        ::
```
Addresses like `::ffff:192.168.1.1` (the common IPv4-mapped/compat form) are missed despite the doc's explicit claim.

Both are real detection-coverage gaps in the mechanism this session already flagged as critical (the privacy catalog exists but is empty/inert in dev, sinex-t5sr) -- when the catalog IS populated, these gaps mean common real-world formats of two sensitive-data categories still leak through undetected.

Found via a targeted audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/detector.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11), verified against the quoted code.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run find_mac_addresses on the string "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF" -- observe no match (only lowercase [0-9a-f] is in the character class).
2. Run the IPv6 detector on "::ffff:192.168.1.1" -- observe no match despite the docstring's explicit claim of mixed-notation coverage.
acceptance_criteria: MAC detector's character classes are case-insensitive (or the regex uses (?i)). IPv6 detector either gains an IPv4-mapped alternate matching the dotted-decimal tail form, or the docstring is corrected to state the actual coverage. A test for each covers the previously-missed format.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Trivially testable -- Steps to Reproduce give exact literal inputs (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, ::ffff:192.168.1.1) that should match and currently do not. No test yet.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Compiled and ran real tests against master (worktree tdd-audit-v2-privacy): MAC-uppercase claim is FALSE -- MAC_RE is compiled with the (?xi) flag (detector.rs), so [0-9a-f] already matches uppercase hex; AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF matches fine. Kept as a real (non-ignored) regression test, not a red one. IPv6 finding (::ffff:192.168.1.1 IPv4-mapped notation) is REAL but narrower than described: the regex has no dotted-decimal tail in its alternatives, so it matches a truncated hex-only prefix (::ffff:192) rather than the documented full mixed-notation address -- tightened the red test to assert the exact match span, not just a match count. Narrowing this bead's scope to the IPv6 finding only.

title: EventRepository's read methods (get_by_id, count_all, get_recent, lineage CTEs, etc.) only query core.events, silently returning empty/None for reflection-lane events -- and find_orphan_materials's orphan check has the same blind spot, causing an FK-violation error rather than a correct verdict
description:
EventRepository's core read methods only ever query core.events, silently returning None/empty for any reflection-lane event id -- a read-side lane-blindness gap, distinct from insert()'s already-correct write-side routing.

EventRepository::get_by_id (queries.rs:20-34) reads ONLY core.events -- as do count_all, get_recent, get_by_source, get_by_event_type, get_by_time_range, get_by_ids_chunk (:631), and the lineage CTEs fetch_ancestors/fetch_descendants (composable_query.rs:570-623). Since insert() correctly routes reflection events INTO reflection.events (persistence.rs:283-286), any reflection event id passed to get_by_id (or the others) returns None/empty with no error -- looks identical to "id doesn't exist".

find_live_by_equivalence_key and filter_tombstoned in the same file carry careful lane-rationale comments explaining why they're core.events-only -- get_by_id and its siblings have no such rationale, suggesting an oversight rather than a deliberate scoping decision.

Same class, different repository: find_orphan_materials / delete_material_if_orphan (source_materials.rs:1627-1712) check only core.events + audit.archived_events for referencing rows, but reflection.events has a real FK to the source_material_registry (apply.rs:2776-2780) -- so the "orphan" verdict is WRONG when only a reflection event references the material, and the subsequent DELETE raises a 23503 FK violation rather than silently corrupting anything (fail-safe by accident, but confusing).

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Insert a reflection-source event (confirm it correctly lands in reflection.events via persistence.rs:283-286).
2. Call get_by_id (or count_all/get_recent/get_by_source/get_by_event_type/get_by_time_range/get_by_ids_chunk/fetch_ancestors/fetch_descendants) with that event's id -- observe it returns None/empty, identical to a nonexistent id, despite the event existing in reflection.events.
3. Call find_orphan_materials/delete_material_if_orphan on a source material only referenced by a reflection event -- observe it's misclassified as orphaned (since only core.events + audit.archived_events are checked) and the subsequent delete raises a 23503 FK violation.
acceptance_criteria: EventRepository's core read methods either check both lanes (core.events UNION reflection.events, matching find_live_by_equivalence_key/filter_tombstoned's existing lane-aware pattern) or explicitly document why they're intentionally activity-only, with callers updated accordingly. find_orphan_materials checks reflection.events as well as core.events + audit.archived_events before declaring a material orphaned.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Independently re-confirmed via gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through audit (wave128-002): composable_query.rs's lineage() ancestors/descendants recursive CTEs (fetch_ancestors/fetch_descendants, lines 563/595) are hardcoded to core.events only, same lane-blindness class as this bead's finding for get_by_id/count_all/get_recent.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete lane-blindness bug (EventRepository reads never see reflection-lane events); testable via a reflection-lane read test.

title: 5 more reimport-scale query hazards: unbounded scope-root-id collection, LIMIT-after-window-function timestamp-regression scan, unindexed per-blob associated_blob_ids full scan, per-row round-trips in batch APIs, deep-offset pagination
description:
Five more reimport-scale hazards in the read/write path, all mechanical (no unbounded query, missing index, or N+1 pattern needs judgment to confirm):

4b. replay.rs:355-364 collect_scope_root_ids has NO LIMIT -- materializes every root id into a Vec, then binds the whole array. The session record already documents a 555k-event scope having hit this path.

4c. queries.rs:437-461 find_timestamp_regressions runs LAG() OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY id) over the ENTIRE table, LIMIT applied only AFTER the window (find_batch_violations at :484 correctly bounds inside the CTE, proving the right pattern is known). find_invalid_timestamps (:560) and find_invalid_payloads (:393) are likewise unindexed full scans.

4d. blobs.rs:335-359 is_referenced_excluding_material does `$1 = ANY(associated_blob_ids)` on core.events AND audit.archived_events -- no GIN index on associated_blob_ids exists anywhere. Double full scan PER BLOB on delete-on-tombstone -- multiplies badly at reimport scale with many blobs.

4e. Per-row round-trips inside batch APIs: embeddings.rs:167-175 and :527-531 call validate_embedding_for_model per row (1000 extra SELECTs for a 1000-row batch); privacy_policy.rs:187-203 does one get_recognizer_backend per rule on the chokepoint cache refresh; knowledge_graph.rs:900-928 find_paths does one query per path over an unbounded recursive-CTE result (lower priority given knowledge_graph has zero production callers per sinex-6t5h).

4f. Deep-offset pagination: queries.rs:82/108/217, events_extensions.rs:895/927 -- OFFSET-based pagination degrades badly at reimport-scale row counts for any deep page.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a large-scope replay (replay.rs:355-364) -- confirm collect_scope_root_ids has no LIMIT and materializes the full id set (already documented as hit at 555k events).
2. Run find_timestamp_regressions (queries.rs:437-461) against a large core.events -- observe the LAG() window function runs over the whole table before LIMIT is applied, unlike its sibling find_batch_violations which correctly bounds inside the CTE.
3. Delete-on-tombstone a blob and observe is_referenced_excluding_material (blobs.rs:335-359) does an unindexed array-containment full scan on both core.events and audit.archived_events.
4. Run a batch embedding validation (embeddings.rs:167-175/:527-531) and count the per-row validate_embedding_for_model SELECTs.

title: 6 multi-statement DB operations across the repository layer lack transaction wrapping, leaving partial/ambiguous state on mid-sequence failure -- one instance is on the destructive tombstone-cancel path
description:
Six non-atomic multi-statement operations across the repository layer, all sharing the same root-cause shape: missing transaction wrapping around a sequence of dependent writes, so a mid-sequence failure leaves partial/ambiguous state.

1. derivation.rs:524-570 write_lane_outputs -- one INSERT per row on the pool, NO transaction; mid-loop failure leaves a half-written lane. seed_entity_relation_outputs_from_event_scope (:933,:971) calls it per-event = N+1 inside N+1 (compounding the exposure).

2. privacy_policy.rs:689-731 add_dictionary -- dictionary INSERT then N term INSERTs, no transaction; term failure returns Err with the dictionary already committed and the caller holding no id to clean up or retry against.

3. projection_registry.rs:1344-1388 insert_row -- stale_superseded_semantics then INSERT, no transaction; a crash between leaves the exact ambiguous state the comment at :1349-1356 says must never be observable.

4. state/tombstone.rs:195-261 cancel_tombstone_operation -- get -> parse scope -> update across 3 pool round-trips, no FOR UPDATE, and update_tombstone_operation (:165-181) does `scope = $3` (FULL overwrite from the stale snapshot). Concurrent workflow advance silently lost, on the destructive tombstone path.

5. events/persistence/replacements.rs:538-568 record_replacements -- executes on self.pool, not the replay transaction, so the audit.event_replacements trail is NOT atomic with the archive+insert it's supposed to record.

6. state.rs:876-930 cancel_operation -- TOCTOU between the status check and the UPDATE.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
For each of the 6 instances: interrupt (or induce a failure) between the first and a later statement in the sequence, and observe the partial state left behind is exactly the ambiguous/inconsistent state the surrounding code comments (where present) say must not occur:
1. derivation.rs:524-570 write_lane_outputs -- kill mid-loop, observe a half-written lane.
2. privacy_policy.rs:689-731 add_dictionary -- fail a term insert, observe the dictionary row committed with no cleanup path.
3. projection_registry.rs:1344-1388 insert_row -- crash between stale_superseded_semantics and the INSERT.
4. state/tombstone.rs:195-261 cancel_tombstone_operation -- race two concurrent calls, observe the full scope=$3 overwrite silently drops a concurrent update.
5. replacements.rs:538-568 record_replacements -- fail after the archive+insert but before this pool call, observe the audit trail is missing despite the archive succeeding.
6. state.rs:876-930 cancel_operation -- race the status check against a concurrent status change.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 sequences is wrapped in a real database transaction (or, for #1/#2's N+1 loop shape, batched into a single multi-row statement) so a mid-sequence failure cannot leave the documented-as-forbidden ambiguous state. #4 additionally gains a FOR UPDATE lock or equivalent instead of a stale-snapshot full overwrite.

title: insert_batch's multi-element path hardcodes core.events regardless of source_role, while the single-element path correctly routes by role -- a size-dependent lane-routing bug matching the sinex-4k4b reflection-pollution class
description:
insert_batch's lane routing is size-dependent -- a single-element batch routes correctly by source_role, but the multi-element path hardcodes core.events regardless of role, risking the exact sinex-4k4b class of silent reflection-lane pollution.

But :1010-1014 delegates a SINGLE-element batch to insert_with_tx, which DOES route by source_role (:645-648). A reflection-source event that happens to land in a multi-element batch goes to core.events alone, while a reflection-source event alone in a single-element batch correctly goes to reflection.events -- the exact sinex-4k4b class (silent activity-surface pollution) the comments in this file explicitly say must not happen.

Only test callers exercise the multi-element batch path today (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/tests/processing_replay.rs:505,593,814), so tests can pass with wrong-lane placement -- if a production caller ever batches multiple events including a reflection-source one, this fires silently.

1. Call insert_batch with a single reflection-source event -- observe it correctly routes to reflection.events via insert_with_tx's source_role check (:645-648, reached via the single-element delegation at :1010-1014).

title: EventValidator::validate (7 real checks incl. provenance validation) is never called at ingest -- but DO NOT wire it wholesale, since its id-timestamp-drift check would reject every historical reimport by design
description:
A real 7-check event validator exists (EventValidator::validate, crate/sinex-db/src/validation.rs:313-327 -- envelope, payload-size limit, object-payload check, domain-specific rules, temporal bounds, ID-drift, provenance) but the ingest path never calls it. Its only wrapper, EventEngineValidator::validate_event (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/validator.rs:254, doc-commented "used in tests and pipelines"), has ZERO non-test callers. Production admission calls only validate_payload_for (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:1348-1355) -- payload schema alone.

Two of the unwired checks cut in OPPOSITE directions -- read this carefully before acting:

1. validate_provenance is a real invariant NOT enforced at ingest today. Wiring it would add real protection.

2. validate_id_timestamp (validation.rs:408-419, MAX_ID_DRIFT_SECS = 300) would REJECT EVERY HISTORICAL IMPORT if wired as-is, since it requires |ts_coided - ts_orig| <= 5min -- directly CONTRADICTING the three-clock provenance model where that difference being large for historical imports is the entire point (ts_coided = when sinex minted the interpretation, ts_orig = when it happened in the world; for a historical import these are deliberately far apart).

DO NOT "fix" this finding by wiring EventValidator::validate() wholesale into the ingest path -- that would immediately break the imminent fresh reimport, which is entirely composed of historical data where this exact drift is expected and correct. Any fix must either wire validate_provenance alone, or make validate_id_timestamp's check conditional on provenance kind (skip/relax it for Material-provenance historical imports), before any wholesale wiring is considered.

This finding sits at the boundary between sinex-db (validation.rs) and sinexd (event_engine); flagged here as the call-site verification for the sibling Id::timestamp() finding (sinex-ja51), but the validator itself may be in another audit lane's region -- treat this as a pointer, not a full audit of validation.rs.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11), cross-referencing crate/sinex-db/src/validation.rs and crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/validator.rs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. grep -rn 'EventEngineValidator::validate_event\|EventValidator::validate' crate/ -- confirm zero non-test production callers.
2. Read validation.rs:408-419's validate_id_timestamp -- confirm MAX_ID_DRIFT_SECS=300 would reject any event where ts_coided and ts_orig differ by more than 5 minutes, which is EXPECTED and CORRECT for every historically-imported event.
acceptance_criteria: IMPORTANT: do not close this by wiring EventValidator::validate() as-is into the ingest path -- verify first that validate_id_timestamp either doesn't fire for the reimport's provenance shape, or is made conditional on provenance kind. Decision recorded on whether validate_provenance specifically (not the id-timestamp check) is worth wiring for the real protection it would add, independent of the id-timestamp landmine.

title: Sequence relation evaluates seeds, not candidates -- directly contradicting its own doc comment; a live RPC path runs a MAX_LIMIT candidate query and silently discards the result, and reports it as used
description:
The Sequence relation evaluates the WRONG event set, directly contradicting its own doc comment -- and a live RPC path unconditionally resolves and executes a MAX_LIMIT candidate-query whose result is then silently discarded.

crate/sinex-primitives/src/relations.rs:288 documents: "The candidates themselves form a time-ordered chain spanning <= within_secs. (Seeds are ignored for this relation.)" relations.rs:490 does the OPPOSITE: `return self.evaluate_sequence(*within_secs, seeds, seed_refs, trace);` -- candidates is never touched for Sequence; the chain is built from seeds instead.

Live impact: crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/query.rs:255-263 unconditionally resolves a candidate query (defaulting one via default_candidate_query, limit = Pagination::MAX_LIMIT), executes it against the DB, passes it to evaluate() -- and the result is discarded (per the code above, evaluate_sequence never reads candidates). query_echo (query.rs:266-271) reports "candidate_query"/"candidate_query_defaulted" as if used, misleading the caller into thinking their candidate filter mattered. CLI: sinexctl events relations sequence (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/relations.rs:160-176) accepts candidate_query_json and it is silently ignored.

Why tests miss it: crate/sinex-primitives/src/relations_test.rs:248,254,263 -- every Sequence test calls .evaluate(&[a,b,c], &[]), passing the chain as SEEDS with an empty candidate slice. The suite encodes the implementation, not the contract, and passes under either reading.

This is a needs-a-decision bug, not a fix-it-either-way bug: it's not clear which of the doc or the implementation reflects the intended semantics of a "Sequence" relation. What IS clear is the current state is defensible under neither reading -- a MAX_LIMIT DB query whose result is silently dropped is wasted work and misleading API feedback regardless of which direction the fix goes.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read relations.rs:288's doc comment ('candidates form the chain, seeds are ignored') vs relations.rs:490's implementation (evaluate_sequence(within_secs, seeds, seed_refs, trace) -- candidates unused).
2. Call sinexctl events relations sequence with a candidate_query_json filter -- observe query.rs:255-263 resolves and runs the query (MAX_LIMIT), the response's query_echo claims candidate_query_defaulted/candidate_query as if applied, but the actual chain is built entirely from seeds.
3. Read relations_test.rs:248,254,263 -- confirm every Sequence test passes the chain as seeds with empty candidates, so the suite can't distinguish the two readings.
acceptance_criteria: Operator decision recorded on which of doc vs implementation is the intended Sequence semantics. Whichever is chosen: (a) the other is corrected to match, (b) if candidates should be evaluated, query.rs's already-resolved candidate query is actually passed through and used, (c) if seeds is correct, the doc comment is fixed and query.rs stops resolving/running a MAX_LIMIT query it will discard, and query_echo stops claiming a candidate_query was applied when it wasn't. A relations_test.rs case is added that distinguishes the two readings (non-empty candidates AND non-empty seeds, asserting which one drove the result).

title: settlement.rs's real retry/backoff/park policy machinery is completely unread by all three production call sites -- FailureContext is a hardcoded constant, backoff is never applied, ParkReason/EffectKind are unconstructible
description:
settlement.rs's retry/backoff policy is built correctly and completely, then read by nobody -- a clean instance of this session's central meta-pattern: real logic built, never wired to its call site.

DefaultFailurePolicy::settle (settlement.rs:170-215) constructs Settlement::Retry { backoff: Exponential{200ms..30s}, budget: RetryBudget{ max_attempts:10, max_elapsed:5min, backoff, terminal: HaltModule{EscalateOperator} } }. All three production consumers match Settlement::Retry { .. } and discard BOTH fields:
  crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/run.rs:440
  crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/process.rs:370
  crate/sinexd/src/runtime/source_driver.rs:321
Each just halts the batch / propagates. No backoff is ever applied, no budget is ever counted, RetryBudget.terminal is unreachable.

Zero files outside settlement.rs reference: RetryBudget, ProgressProposal, ProcessingFailureIntent, ParkReason, HaltReason, EffectKind (verified rg -l across crate/, xtask/, tests/).

FailureContext is a CONSTANT at all three call sites -- all hardcode attempts:0, input_scope:None, effect_kind:None, delivery_count:None, operation:ProcessBatch, phase:ProcessInput (run.rs:402-410, process.rs:333-341, source_driver.rs:291-299). Because attempts is always 0, `ctx.attempts >= 10` (settlement.rs:178) is STATICALLY UNREACHABLE -> Settlement::Park and the whole ParkReason enum are unconstructible in production.

Unconstructed variants confirmed workspace-wide: RuntimeOperation::{HandleInvalidation,HistoricalReplay,OutputEmission,CheckpointSave,DlqRouting,JournalIngestion} (6 of 7); RuntimePhase::{EmitEffect,PersistProgress,Drain,Recovery} (4 of 5); all of ParkReason and EffectKind; InputScope (which also name-collides with an unrelated InputScope in derivations.rs, same crate).

settle() reads only err.error_class() and ctx.attempts -- never operation/phase/input_scope/effect_kind/delivery_count. Six-field context struct, one load-bearing field, pinned to a constant.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read DefaultFailurePolicy::settle (settlement.rs:170-215) -- confirm it constructs a real Retry{backoff, budget} settlement.
2. Read the three production call sites (run.rs:440, process.rs:370, source_driver.rs:321) -- confirm each matches Settlement::Retry {..} and discards both fields, just halting/propagating.
3. grep -rn 'FailureContext {' crate/sinexd/src/runtime/ -- confirm all three construction sites hardcode attempts:0 and the other fields to fixed values, making settle()'s attempts>=10 branch statically unreachable.

title: invalidation recompute can emit duplicate replacement events on crash-during-recompute redelivery (r6d.7's own named-but-unfiled carve-out) -- currently masked by sinex-lk67, becomes live once that's fixed
description:
Confirms sinex-r6d.7's own named-but-never-filed carve-out: a duplicate-output window in invalidation recompute, currently masked only by sinex-lk67 (the invalidation consumer being entirely unreachable).

handle_invalidation_message emits replacements through the non-durable mpsc path (invalidate.rs:467-494) and only afterwards archives the stale originals (invalidate.rs:495-519). The doc at invalidate.rs:373-375 claims this ordering means "channel/transport failures cannot create an empty scope" -- but mpsc acceptance is not durability, so the claim overstates what's actually guaranteed.

Because the invalidation stream uses Limits retention with a fresh ephemeral consumer per start (per r6d.7's own closure evidence), the LOSS side of a crash-during-recompute self-heals via redelivery (r6d.7 correctly closed that half) -- but the DUPLICATE side does not: if a crash happens after replacement events are emitted but before the stale originals are archived, redelivery re-runs the recompute and emits a SECOND set of replacement events, since the archive-marking that would prevent redelivery from re-emitting never landed.

r6d.7's own close reason explicitly names this exact window: "REMAINING, explicitly out of scope and NOT closed by this bead: a separate window where a crash during recompute (after invalidate.rs emits replacement events but before archiving stale originals) can let redelivery r[e-emit]..." (close reason text, truncated in the CLI's own display but confirmed present). It was never filed as a follow-up bead.

Currently masked entirely by sinex-lk67 (the invalidation consumer is unreachable in production for all 16 automata) -- this bead becomes live the moment lk67 is fixed, so should land as part of the same effort or immediately after.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/ + crate/sinexd/src/automata/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. (Requires sinex-lk67 fixed first, since the invalidation consumer is currently unreachable.) Trigger an invalidation recompute, and crash sinexd after invalidate.rs:467-494 emits replacement events but before invalidate.rs:495-519 archives the stale originals.
2. Restart -- the ephemeral consumer's fresh ack floor causes JetStream to redeliver the invalidation message, re-running recompute and emitting a SECOND set of replacement events for the same scope, since nothing marks 'replacements already emitted, don't redo.'
3. Read sinex-r6d.7's close_reason text -- confirm it explicitly names this exact window as out of scope and not yet filed.
acceptance_criteria: The archive-marking (or an equivalent idempotency marker) happens BEFORE or atomically with replacement emission, so a crash-and-redeliver doesn't produce duplicate replacement events -- matching the durability discipline already applied to the loss-side window r6d.7 closed. Relates to sinex-r6d.7 (names this carve-out) and sinex-lk67 (currently masks it).

title: derived events minted during ordinary startup catch-up (not real replay) inherit a foreign operation_id from their input's provenance, and replay-abort collects/acts on them as if it produced them
description:
Derived outputs inherit a foreign replay operation_id during ordinary catch-up (not actual replay), and the abort/rollback path treats that attribution as ownership -- aborting a replay operation would collect and act on derived events it never produced.

AutomatonContext::live (context.rs:103-105) and ::historical (context.rs:152-156) both fall back to the INPUT event's created_by_operation_id; build_output_event then stamps it onto the derived event (output.rs:433-437, :464). The startup catch-up scan passes operation_id = None (run.rs:322-323, since args.replay is None at automaton_runtime.rs:277), so it takes the fallback: derived events minted during ORDINARY CATCH-UP are attributed to whatever replay operation created their inputs.

That attribution is load-bearing: collect_operation_output_events selects FROM core.events WHERE created_by_operation_id = $1::uuid (collect.rs:113-140), and count_visible_replay_outputs does the same (collect.rs:270-285) -- so aborting or rolling back that replay operation will collect and act on derived events it never actually produced.

Worth confirming intent: cascade attribution may be deliberate for the LIVE path (a derived event genuinely produced as a direct consequence of a replay operation's inputs), but the catch-up case is clearly not a replay -- and the ProcessingMode::Replay / TriggerKind::ReplayRecompute labelling of ordinary startup catch-up (context.rs:150-151) compounds the mislabelling by making catch-up look like replay at the type level too.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/ + crate/sinexd/src/automata/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger an ordinary sinexd restart with a mandatory catch-up scan (automaton_runtime.rs:260-279), where the input events being processed were themselves produced by an earlier replay operation.
2. Observe context.rs:103-105/152-156 falls back to the input's created_by_operation_id for the derived output's own operation_id, since run.rs:322-323 passes operation_id=None for catch-up.
3. Later, abort/rollback the earlier replay operation and observe collect_operation_output_events (collect.rs:113-140) collects the catch-up-produced derived events too, since they carry the same operation_id by coincidence of provenance rather than genuine causation.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: either (a) ordinary catch-up mints derived events with operation_id=None (or a distinct catch-up marker) rather than inheriting the input's operation_id, so replay-abort/rollback can't accidentally collect them, or (b) if cascade attribution is deliberate even for catch-up, document why and confirm abort/rollback semantics are actually correct under that model.

title: PacingController's lifetime-average rate calculation allows an unbounded burst after any pause, contradicting its own stated purpose of preventing instantaneous-burst boot flaps
description:
PacingController allows an unbounded burst after any BacklogGate pause, defeating the module's own stated purpose.

pacing.rs:114-134 computes sleep from LIFETIME averages. After a BacklogGate pause (:205-238) elapsed grows while events_total doesn't, so required_sleep returns zero until the average catches up. Worked example against the module's stated purpose (pacing.rs:5-13, the 1.24M-event journald backlog that flapped the daemon on boot): budget 100 ev/s, 600s elapsed, 1000 events emitted -> ~59,000 events at full speed with zero throttle before any sleep engages. BacklogGate re-engages only BETWEEN batches, not within one unthrottled run.

Documented as "average rate since start" so this isn't hidden behavior, but the incident it exists to prevent (pacing.rs's own docstring) is instantaneous-burst-driven, not average-rate-driven -- a token bucket or windowed rate would actually match the stated intent. No silent dropping anywhere in pacing.rs -- pure sleep backpressure, correctly implemented for what it computes, just computing the wrong thing for the stated goal.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a BacklogGate pause (pacing.rs:205-238) that lasts several minutes with events_total unchanged.
2. Resume processing -- observe required_sleep (pacing.rs:114-134) computes zero throttle for a large burst of events, since the lifetime average hasn't caught up to the elapsed idle time.
3. Compare against pacing.rs's own docstring (:5-13) describing the 1.24M-event journald backlog boot-flap incident this module exists to prevent -- confirm that incident was burst-driven, not average-rate-driven.
acceptance_criteria: PacingController is changed to a token-bucket or windowed-rate model (bounding instantaneous burst size directly) rather than a lifetime-average model, matching the actual failure mode it was built to prevent.
close_reason:
Implemented bounded one-second token buckets and cooperative cancellation for pacing in commit 728d65fc3. Closure Evidence Manifest: AC token-bucket/windowed enforcement satisfied by crate/sinexd/src/runtime/pacing.rs; focused command ALTER ROLE

title: save_checkpoint returns Ok for a CAS-conflict write it silently skipped -- one caller (state_io.rs) treats that as real persistence and deletes the hot-reload file, the other durability copy of the state
description:
save_checkpoint reports success for a write it silently skipped, and two callers treat "skipped" as "persisted" -- one of them deletes the other durability copy of the state as a result.

checkpoint.rs:679-701: on CAS conflict, when checkpoint_conflict_would_regress is true, it logs and returns Ok(state.revision) WITHOUT writing. Callers can't distinguish this from a real write:
- adapter_source.rs:1831-1834 sets checkpoint_revision AND last_stream_checkpoint_persist = now -- the 5s throttle starts as if persisted.
- automaton/adapter/state_io.rs:305-307 goes further: on Ok it calls finalize_restored_hot_reload_file, which DELETES the hot-reload file (state_io.rs:59) -- the other copy of the restored state.

The predicate (checkpoint.rs:97-103) compares only processed_count, so equal-count-with-advanced-cursor is misclassified as a regression and dropped. Reachable: adapter_source.rs:1690 marks event_count==0 records unlocked and advances the frontier while processed_count = total_events_emitted (:1810) doesn't move -- a heavily-filtering source (journald w/ filter, fs-watcher skipping temp files) advances its cursor without incrementing the count.

Mitigating: state_io.rs:136 rebases last_revision onto the live KV revision on restore, removing the common stale-revision trigger; remaining trigger is a genuine concurrent writer (leader/standby overlap, peer adoption). Also note data embeds last_checkpoint: Timestamp::now() (state_io.rs:264-268), so checkpoint_states_match is essentially always false under conflict, leaving processed_count as the sole discriminator.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a heavily-filtering source (e.g. a fs-watcher skipping temp files) so it advances its cursor on event_count==0 records without incrementing processed_count.
2. Trigger a CAS conflict on checkpoint save under this condition -- observe checkpoint_conflict_would_regress misclassifies it as a regression (comparing only processed_count) and save_checkpoint silently skips the write while returning Ok.
3. Observe automaton/adapter/state_io.rs:305-307 treats the Ok as successful persistence and deletes the hot-reload file via finalize_restored_hot_reload_file -- losing the other durability copy of state that was never actually re-persisted.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a CheckpointSaveOutcome enum (Written vs Skipped) so save_checkpoint's return type lets callers distinguish real persistence from a silent skip -- state_io.rs must not delete the hot-reload file on a Skipped outcome. checkpoint_conflict_would_regress's predicate should also account for cursor advancement, not just processed_count, to reduce false-positive 'regression' classifications.

title: AppendOnlyFileAdapter under-counts byte_offset by 1 per line on CRLF-terminated files, corrupting the occurrence-identity anchor
description:
AppendOnlyFileAdapter's byte-offset tracking drifts on CRLF line endings, corrupting the occurrence-identity anchor for any CRLF-terminated file source.

crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/append_only_file.rs:124-169: std::fs::read_to_string + content.lines(). Rust's str::lines() strips a trailing \r in addition to \n, but byte_offset += line_len + 1 only ever accounts for one \n byte. For CRLF files this cumulatively under-counts the true on-disk offset by 1 per line, so MaterialAnchor::Line{byte_start,..} -- part of the occurrence-identity tuple -- no longer matches the file's real byte position. Zero CRLF test coverage (grep for \r in append_only_file_test.rs: no hits).

Secondary smell: read_to_string hard-fails open() entirely on any invalid-UTF-8 byte rather than degrading gracefully -- plausible for arbitrary app/terminal logs.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed append_only_file.rs a CRLF-terminated (Windows-style) log file.
2. Compare the computed MaterialAnchor::Line{byte_start} against the file's real on-disk byte offset for lines past the first -- observe cumulative 1-byte-per-line drift.
3. grep append_only_file_test.rs for \r -- confirm zero CRLF coverage.
acceptance_criteria: byte_offset accounting accounts for the actual line-terminator length (1 for LF, 2 for CRLF) rather than assuming LF unconditionally. A test with a CRLF-terminated fixture confirms byte_start matches the real on-disk offset. Separately consider (lower priority, same finding) whether read_to_string's hard-fail on invalid UTF-8 should degrade instead of erroring the whole adapter.

title: events.query returns raw unredacted events while sibling events.cards/events.lineage on the same rows both apply privacy disclosure -- needs a design confirmation, not necessarily a bug
description:
handle_events_query (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/query.rs:26-28) returns raw events via pool.events().query(...) with ZERO privacy-policy disclosure applied -- no PolicyEngine call at all -- unlike its two siblings on the same event data: handle_events_cards (query.rs:111-131) and handle_events_lineage (query.rs:30-36), which both correctly wrap through the disclosure pipeline.

This may be intentional per project doctrine ("redaction is presentation, not a security boundary" -- CLAUDE.md), but it means events.query (which backs sinexctl query/show) is unconditionally unredacted regardless of privacy-catalog state, while events.cards/events.lineage on the SAME underlying rows are not. This asymmetry needs an explicit design confirmation so no future caller assumes events.query inherits events.cards' redaction posture, or accidentally exposes a redaction bypass by preferring the raw query endpoint.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/{dlq,privacy,lifecycle,sources,replay,instructions,browser,query}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a privacy rule that redacts a field on some event type.
2. Call events.cards or events.lineage for that event -- observe the field is redacted.
3. Call events.query for the same underlying event -- observe the field is NOT redacted.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: either events.query is documented as the intentional raw/unredacted escape hatch (with a doc comment explaining why, and confirmation that sinexctl query/show callers are meant to see raw data), or it's brought in line with events.cards/events.lineage's disclosure wrapping for consistency.

title: xtask doctor's Postgres Extensions check lists installed extensions but never validates pgvector/timescaledb are actually present
description:
xtask doctor's "Postgres Extensions" check never validates required extensions -- it's a display-only listing, not a pass/fail check, despite being wired into the overall all_ok verdict.

xtask/src/commands/doctor.rs:312-372, wired at 1318-1331. probe_postgres_extensions runs `SELECT extname FROM pg_extension` and only sets all_ok=false on a psql EXECUTION error (e.g. connection failure). The returned extension list is printed for humans but never diffed against an expected set. pgvector and timescaledb are both load-bearing per project CLAUDE.md ("PostgreSQL (TimescaleDB + pgvector)"). A dev DB entirely missing pgvector/timescaledb still reports "Postgres Extensions: [OK]" implicitly and all_ok=true. Confirmed via grep -- zero references to pgvector/timescaledb/vector anywhere in doctor.rs.

Same vacuity-hole class as the TlsCheck finding in this same audit (sinex-doctor-tls) -- a check that queries real state and displays it, but never actually gates on the thing it's ostensibly checking.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of xtask/src/commands/{verify,check,ci,doctor,doctor_build_cache_policy_tests,proof_obligations,release_readiness}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask doctor against a Postgres instance missing pgvector and/or timescaledb.
2. Observe the Postgres Extensions section lists whatever extensions ARE present but doctor's overall verdict is unaffected -- no failure is raised for the missing required extensions.
acceptance_criteria: probe_postgres_extensions (or its caller) diffs the queried extension list against the required set (pgvector, timescaledb) and sets all_ok=false with a clear message when either is missing, not just on a psql execution error.

title: xtask doctor's TlsCheck::is_healthy() vacuously passes when certs are entirely absent or key_matches was never computed
description:
xtask doctor's TLS health check vacuously passes when certs are entirely absent, or when a server cert exists with no matching key file.

xtask/src/commands/doctor.rs:223-229:
```rust
impl TlsCheck {
    fn is_healthy(&self) -> bool {
        self.error.is_none()
            && !self.server_expired.unwrap_or(false)
            && self.key_matches.unwrap_or(true)
    }
}
```
Never inspects ca_exists/server_cert_exists/client_cert_exists. In detect_tls_check() (doctor.rs:242-290), if the TLS dir exists but is empty, every optional field is None -> is_healthy() evaluates true (error.is_none()=true; server_expired.unwrap_or(false)=false negated=true; key_matches.unwrap_or(true)=true). Same result if a server cert exists with no matching key file -- check_tls_config (xtask/src/tls/verify.rs:103-109) only sets key_matches = Some(...) inside `if let Some(key_file) = key_path`, else it stays None (struct default, verify.rs:47).

Caller doctor.rs:1334-1337:
```rust
if tls_check.as_ref().is_some_and(|check| !check.is_healthy()) { all_ok = false; }
```
xtask doctor prints "All checks passed" for a TLS dir with zero certs on disk, or a cert with no matching key. The three *_exists booleans are collected and displayed but never wired into the pass/fail decision -- this is exactly the "verification tooling that looks load-bearing but isn't" pattern flagged repeatedly this session.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of xtask/src/commands/{verify,check,ci,doctor,doctor_build_cache_policy_tests,proof_obligations,release_readiness}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point xtask doctor at an empty (or nonexistent-cert) TLS directory.
2. Run xtask doctor -- observe it reports the TLS check as healthy/passed despite zero certs present.
3. Read doctor.rs:223-229's is_healthy() -- confirm it never checks ca_exists/server_cert_exists/client_cert_exists, only error/server_expired/key_matches, all of which default to a passing value when unset.
acceptance_criteria: TlsCheck::is_healthy() requires the expected certs to actually exist (ca_exists/server_cert_exists/client_cert_exists as appropriate for the configured mode) before reporting healthy, and requires key_matches to have actually been computed (Some(true)), not just defaulted true when absent. A test with an empty TLS dir confirms xtask doctor now reports the TLS check as failed, not passed.

title: DesktopContextView family is a shared-crate 'view' type with zero server RPC surface -- entirely client-assembled, computing new interpretive confidence scores that only sinexctl's context.rs can reproduce
description:
The DesktopContextView family (crate/sinex-primitives/src/views/desktop.rs: DesktopContextView, DesktopContextCandidateView, DesktopNotificationPressureView, DesktopFocusSessionListView, DesktopProjectContextListView) is declared in the shared sinex-primitives crate exactly like every other server-response view (JsonSchema, doc comments, registered in output_kind.rs) -- but has ZERO server RPC surface. It is entirely assembled client-side, computing new interpretive content that no other consumer can reproduce.

- No RPC method exists: `rg "desktop.context" rpc/methods.rs` -> no match.
- `rg -l "DesktopContextView"` workspace-wide -> only views_test.rs, views/desktop.rs, output_kind.rs, and crate/sinexctl/src/commands/context.rs. No sinexd handler anywhere.
- Entirely assembled in sinexctl/src/commands/context.rs:1374-1477 from raw EventCardViews. The "confidence" field is a CLI-only heuristic with no relation to evidence quality/adjudication:
```rust
// context.rs:1479
fn evidence_ref_confidence(evidence_ref_count: usize, max_evidence_refs: usize) -> f32 {
    if max_evidence_refs == 0 { return 0.0; }
    (evidence_ref_count.min(max_evidence_refs) as f32) / max_evidence_refs as f32
}
```

Mitigating factor: output_kind.rs:140-154 does honestly label these "rebuildable ... computed from admitted observations" (the correct disclaimer pattern, matching package_completeness.rs's existing good practice). But placement in the shared sinex-primitives::views module makes the type signature indistinguishable from a server-authoritative view, and the confidence/candidate-ranking logic exists in exactly ONE place (a sinexctl command function) -- any other consumer (an MCP tool, a future UI) would have to reimplement this exact heuristic to get consistent results, or would get a different "confidence" for the same underlying data depending which client computed it.

This is presentation code computing NEW interpretive content rather than just rendering server-provided data -- closer to violating the "presentation/context packs are consumers, never authorities" doctrine (project CLAUDE.md storage/authority-split section) than the sinex-89mx unconstructed-variant findings, which are about incomplete coverage of an existing authoritative type rather than a client inventing a new derived type.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/ + views/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. rg "desktop.context" crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/methods.rs -- confirm no RPC method exists for this view family.
2. rg -l "DesktopContextView" -- confirm the only non-test/non-declaration usage is crate/sinexctl/src/commands/context.rs.
3. Read context.rs:1374-1479's evidence_ref_confidence -- confirm the 'confidence' score is a CLI-local heuristic, not server-provided or adjudicated.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: either (a) give DesktopContextView a real server RPC method so the confidence/candidate-ranking computation happens once, authoritatively, and any consumer gets consistent results (matching how other views work), or (b) move the type declaration out of the shared sinex-primitives::views module into sinexctl itself, so its type signature no longer implies server authority it doesn't have.

title: sinexctl _complete panics on multi-byte UTF-8 input at a non-char-boundary --cursor offset (same bug class already fixed elsewhere in this file's sibling shortcuts.rs)
description:
sinexctl _complete panics on non-ASCII input at a non-char-boundary cursor offset.

crate/sinexctl/src/commands/completion_endpoint.rs takes a raw --cursor <usize> byte offset from shell/picker frontends and slices line[..cursor] unguarded in 4 places: active_token (line 160), query_unit_candidates (347-349), ops_dlq_subcommand (636-649), command_context (756-770) -- none check is_char_boundary. Any completion request over a buffer with multi-byte UTF-8 (a unicode window title, path, or search string in the shell command line being completed) at a cursor offset landing mid-codepoint panics the process.

completion_endpoint_test.rs (254 lines) has zero unicode/boundary coverage. Notably this is the SAME bug class already fixed elsewhere in this exact region -- shortcuts_status_tests.rs:250-269 explicitly tests format_watch_summary's UTF-8-safe truncation (truncate_str_boundary_safe, used in shortcuts.rs and baseline.rs) with a comment describing this exact failure mode -- but completion_endpoint.rs's cursor slicing never got the equivalent treatment, despite a numeric user-supplied offset being an even easier trigger than a string-length threshold.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{tui,verify/mod,verify/baseline,shortcuts,shortcuts_status_tests,telemetry,completion_endpoint,metrics,audit,mod,common}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct a shell completion request with a command-line buffer containing multi-byte UTF-8 (e.g. an emoji or accented character in a search string) and a --cursor offset landing mid-codepoint.
2. Call any of active_token/query_unit_candidates/ops_dlq_subcommand/command_context with that input -- observe a panic on the unguarded line[..cursor] slice.
3. Compare to shortcuts_status_tests.rs:250-269's existing coverage of truncate_str_boundary_safe in the same crate, proving the project already has and tests a fix for this exact class elsewhere.

title: sinexctl TUI's raw-payload toggle and event/payload-JSON copy actions are permanently dead since the #1923 privacy-disclosure refactor removed their raw-row data source without replacement
description:
The TUI's copy-menu "event JSON"/"payload JSON" items and the raw/pretty payload toggle are permanently dead for every event, every session -- confirmed as a regression via git log, not a design dead-end.

crate/sinexctl/src/commands/tui.rs:103 declares `recent_event_rows: Vec<QueryResultEvent>`, populated empty at init (line 135) and thereafter only ever `.clear()`'d (lines 405, 413) -- never filled. `selected_event_row()` (line 229) always returns None, so:
- `payload_lines()` (line 1853) always falls back to the truncated `card.payload_preview` -- the `p` (raw/pretty payload toggle) keybind never shows real raw JSON.
- `event_copy_actions()` (line 1928) always takes the else branch (1977-1986), permanently disabling the "event JSON" and "payload JSON" copy-menu items with reason "raw query event is unavailable" -- for every event, every session.

`git log -p --follow` on tui.rs proves this is a regression: commit acf553d9d ("feat(privacy): disclose event cards through policy (#1923)", 2026-06-18) switched the refresh call from `client.query_events(query)` (which set `self.recent_event_rows = events;`) to `client.event_cards(query)` (privacy-disclosed EventCardListView, no raw rows) and replaced the assignment with `.clear()`, apparently as an unfinished stopgap. Both `query_events` (gateway.rs:1009) and `event_cards` (gateway.rs:1014) still exist client-side, so this is a straightforward wiring gap, not a design dead-end -- the privacy-disclosure refactor removed the raw-row source without replacing the two features that depended on it.

Not caught by tests: tui_test.rs:150 constructs App with `recent_event_rows: Vec::new()` directly and never exercises the Some(row) branch -- no test would catch a re-regression even after a fix.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{tui,verify/mod,verify/baseline,shortcuts,shortcuts_status_tests,telemetry,completion_endpoint,metrics,audit,mod,common}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open sinexctl tui, select any event row, press 'p' to toggle raw/pretty payload -- observe it always shows the truncated card.payload_preview, never real raw JSON.
2. Open the copy menu on any event -- observe 'event JSON'/'payload JSON' are always disabled with reason 'raw query event is unavailable'.
3. git log -p --follow crate/sinexctl/src/commands/tui.rs -- find commit acf553d9d switching query_events -> event_cards and replacing the row assignment with .clear().
acceptance_criteria: recent_event_rows (or an equivalent privacy-safe raw-row fetch) is populated so selected_event_row() can return Some, restoring the raw-payload toggle and the two copy-menu actions -- routed through whatever privacy-disclosure gate #1923 introduced so the fix doesn't regress that feature's original purpose. A test exercises the Some(row) branch of event_copy_actions()/payload_lines() so a re-regression is caught.

title: TimeRange is always-inclusive on both ends: causes day-boundary double-counting in report/calendar AND silently collapses strict < / > to <= / >= in the query DSL
description:
`sinexctl report`/`report calendar` day-bucketing double-counts any event with `ts_orig` exactly at a UTC-midnight boundary, and the same always-inclusive-range root cause independently causes `sinexctl query`'s DSL to silently collapse strict (`<`/`>`) time comparisons to non-strict (`<=`/`>=`).

**Day-boundary double count**: report.rs builds each day as `TimeRange::new(day_start, day_end)` where day_end of day N == day_start of day N+1 (lines 592-595, 719-723). TimeRange is inclusive on both ends -- confirmed via `TimeRange::contains()` in crate/sinex-primitives/src/query.rs:127-140, and via the DB layer crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/composable_query.rs:777-783 which emits `ts_orig >= start AND ts_orig <= end`. Any event with ts_orig exactly at a UTC-midnight boundary is counted in BOTH adjacent days. Reachable in practice: `--at YYYY-MM-DD` date-only inputs parse to exact midnight (crate/sinexctl/src/validation.rs:29-37), used on `sinexctl record health intake/effect --at` and `sinexctl record task --due` (record.rs:101-103,153-155,212-214).

**Query DSL strict/non-strict collapse**: crate/sinex-primitives/src/query_units.rs:552-568 (`apply_time_bound`, invoked from `event_query_from_sinex_query`, query_units.rs:81, which `sinexctl query 'events where ...'` calls) collapses `>`/`>=` to the same inclusive start bound and `<`/`<=` to the same inclusive end bound -- `ts_orig < X` silently behaves as `<= X`.

Both are the same always-inclusive-TimeRange root cause and land squarely in the civil-time/boundary risk area this project already tracks (sinex-2ged: hourly/daily buckets are UTC-bucketed, calendar-shaped products misaligned with the civil day/DST).

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{query,query_units,show,events,documents,trace,timeline,relations,record,annotate,throughput,explain,context,report,llm}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an event with ts_orig exactly at a UTC-midnight boundary (e.g. via sinexctl record task --due 2026-08-11, which parses to exact midnight per validation.rs:29-37).
2. Run sinexctl report calendar spanning that boundary -- observe the event counted in both adjacent days.
3. Run sinexctl query 'events where ts_orig < <midnight-timestamp>' -- observe the boundary event is included despite the strict operator, per query_units.rs:552-568's collapse of < / <= and > / >=.
acceptance_criteria: TimeRange (or its consumers) support genuinely half-open or operator-aware bounds so day-bucketing doesn't double-count boundary events and the query DSL's < / <=, > / >= operators produce actually distinct behavior. Relate to sinex-2ged rather than duplicate its broader civil-time-bucketing scope -- this bead is specifically about the inclusive-range mechanism, 2ged is about UTC-vs-civil-day bucket alignment.

(matching the total/session_count pattern in the same file) or attach the existing report_coverage_caveat (or equivalent) when a section's query fails, so a report operator can distinguish 'no data' from 'query failed'.

title: HeartbeatEmitter (real production health surface) has no emit-stall/liveness-of-work detection, unlike HealthReporter -- a wedged module reports Healthy forever, and systemd's watchdog thread can't catch it either
description:
`HeartbeatEmitter` (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/heartbeat.rs) can report Healthy indefinitely while a module is genuinely wedged, and it's real production wiring (used in crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/service.rs, runtime/stream/runtime_state.rs, crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/service.rs), not a test-only path.

Two parallel health-status mechanisms exist with very different rigor:
- `health_reporter.rs`'s `HealthReporter::calculate_status` (lines 546-575) is evidence-gated (has_evidence(), Unknown until real evidence) AND has emit-stall detection (`emit_stalled()`, lines 510-529) that demotes Healthy->Degraded when a module stops actually emitting despite ticking.
- `heartbeat.rs`'s `HeartbeatEmitter::determine_status` (lines 234-246) has NO such check -- status is derived solely from the 5-minute sliding error-count window (recent_error_count). A module that hangs/deadlocks without ever calling record_error (e.g. blocked on a channel/lock, or an await that never resolves) reports Healthy in every heartbeat, forever.

Compounding factor: `systemd_notify.rs:92-130` runs the WATCHDOG=1 pinger on a dedicated std::thread specifically so tokio-runtime starvation from big COPY batches doesn't false-positive-SIGTERM (deliberate design). Side effect: a genuinely wedged (not just busy -- actually deadlocked) tokio runtime still gets WATCHDOG=1 pings from the unaffected OS thread, so systemd never auto-restarts it. Combined with HeartbeatEmitter's gap above, there is no independent "the async runtime is actually making progress" signal feeding either the systemd watchdog or the heartbeat/health surface for modules using HeartbeatEmitter instead of HealthReporter.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/ lifecycle/health files (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Compare heartbeat.rs:234-246 (determine_status, error-count-only) against health_reporter.rs:510-529,546-575 (emit_stalled + evidence-gated calculate_status) -- confirm the two mechanisms have materially different rigor for the same conceptual purpose.
2. Confirm HeartbeatEmitter's production call sites (stream/runner/service.rs, stream/runtime_state.rs, event_engine/service.rs) are real, not test-only.
3. Read systemd_notify.rs:92-130 -- confirm the watchdog pinger runs on a separate OS thread that stays alive even if the tokio runtime deadlocks.
acceptance_criteria: HeartbeatEmitter gains an equivalent to HealthReporter's emit-stall detection (ticking without genuine emission progress demotes status), OR the modules currently using HeartbeatEmitter are migrated to HealthReporter if the two mechanisms don't need to coexist. Decision recorded on whether unifying to one health-reporting mechanism is preferable to maintaining two with different guarantees.

title: checkpoint-path default resolution bypasses environment() namespacing that its two sibling work-dir resolvers apply (dev/prod checkpoint collision risk); ShutdownConfig.grace_period_secs is also dead
description:
`default_checkpoint_path` (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/shutdown.rs:74-88) resolves the runtime dir via SINEX_RUNTIME_DIR -> SINEX_WORK_DIR -> raw dirs::cache_dir().join("sinex") -> /tmp/sinex, with NO environment().work_directory(...) namespacing and no per-service SINEX_<SERVICE>_WORK_DIR lookup.

Contrast with two sibling resolvers in the same region that both correctly namespace:
- config.rs:477-494 (default_work_dir, backing RuntimeConfig.work_dir) -- uses environment().work_directory(get_cache_dir_or_fallback().join("sinex")).
- runtime_cli.rs:960-974 (resolve_work_dir) -- uses environment().work_directory("/tmp/sinex/runtime").

environment().work_directory() (crate/sinex-primitives/src/environment.rs:509-524) appends the deployment-environment suffix (dev/staging/prod) specifically to prevent cross-environment path collisions.

Blast radius: if SINEX_RUNTIME_DIR/SINEX_WORK_DIR aren't explicitly set (true for any non-NixOS run -- dev boxes, ad-hoc xtask run, etc.), a dev and a prod sinexd/automaton-adapter instance on the same host would both resolve checkpoints to the SAME unnamespaced ~/.cache/sinex/<module>.checkpoint.json, silently cross-contaminating replay/hot-reload state. In the actual NixOS deployment (nixos/modules/sources.nix:297) SINEX_RUNTIME_DIR is set explicitly per service, masking this in prod -- but the code-level default is inconsistent with its two siblings and exposed whenever that env var isn't provided.

This is the same "same conceptual value independently re-resolved" class already found repeatedly this session (sinex-racu, sinex-c5fz, sinex-67t6) -- and it's not isolated to shutdown.rs: acquisition_manager.rs:393 and preflight/resources.rs:46 also each independently read SINEX_WORK_DIR directly rather than consuming RuntimeConfig.work_dir.

Also found in the same file: ShutdownConfig.grace_period_secs (shutdown.rs:100, default 30) is dead -- grepped every call site, set in Default and tests but never read anywhere. Actual shutdown grace periods are unrelated hardcoded constants elsewhere (watcher_handle.rs 250ms, stream/runner/shutdown.rs 250ms, stream/listener.rs 2s). An operator who sets this field expecting it to control shutdown timing is silently ignored.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/ lifecycle/health files (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Compare shutdown.rs:74-88 (default_checkpoint_path, raw dirs::cache_dir, no environment() namespacing) against config.rs:477-494 and runtime_cli.rs:960-974 (both use environment().work_directory(...)).
2. Run sinexd (or an automaton adapter) locally without SINEX_RUNTIME_DIR/SINEX_WORK_DIR set, in both a dev-labeled and prod-labeled environment config -- confirm both resolve to the identical checkpoint path.
3. grep every call site of ShutdownConfig.grace_period_secs -- confirm it's set but never read.
acceptance_criteria: default_checkpoint_path is namespaced via environment().work_directory(...) matching its two siblings. acquisition_manager.rs:393 and preflight/resources.rs:46 are migrated to consume RuntimeConfig.work_dir instead of independently reading SINEX_WORK_DIR. ShutdownConfig.grace_period_secs is either wired to the real shutdown-timing constants it should control, or removed if genuinely superseded by the hardcoded per-component timeouts.

title: MaterialParser::Config is never threaded to parse_record -- any parser config with real fields silently no-ops (2 confirmed instances: clipboard max_preview_length, hyprland require_hyprland)
description:
`MaterialParser::Config` is structurally dead across the entire crate: `MaterialParser::parse_record(&mut self, record, ctx)` (crate/sinex-primitives/src/parser/mod.rs:764-769) never receives `Self::Config`. The runtime that drives all `AdapterBackedSource`-based sources constructs the parser unconditionally via `Default::default()`, never threading the deserialized config through:

- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:418-436 -- `AdapterBackedSource<A, P>`'s `config: Option<A::Config>` field only stores the ADAPTER's config; the struct comment on the `parser` field literally reads "The parser instance. Constructed in `Default`." (no config).
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:542-543 -- `parser: P::default()` in `new()`, no config threading at all.
- crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/fixture.rs:407,787 -- even the test-fixture harness takes `_parser_config: &P::Config` as an explicitly unused (underscore-prefixed) parameter.

Consequence: any `*ParserConfig` struct with real fields is dead on arrival -- deserializable from Nix binding config, but nothing ever reads the deserialized value. Two concrete casualties found in the source_contracts region (most other ParserConfigs are empty unit structs, so this root cause currently has limited blast radius, but the mechanism is crate-wide and any future parser with real config fields would silently no-op):

- crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/desktop/clipboard.rs:34-38 -- `ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length` (documented "Maximum preview length to include in the payload"). `parse_record` (line 131) hardcodes `raw_text.chars().take(100)` literally instead of reading it -- and structurally can't read it anyway since `ClipboardParser` is a unit struct with no field to hold the config.
- crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/desktop/window_manager.rs:40-44 -- `HyprlandParserConfig.require_hyprland` ("Whether to degrade gracefully when Hyprland is absent") is declared, documented with intended behavior, and referenced nowhere else in the file.

Neither key is currently set anywhere in the sinnix Nix config (grep confirmed empty), so no operator override is silently being dropped today -- but both configs look live and would silently no-op if someone tried to use them.

Contrast: document/runtime.rs's `DocumentIngestorConfig` (mime types, max size, allowed roots) IS correctly wired -- but that's a `SourceDriver`, a different trait whose `initialize()` genuinely stores `self.config`, not a `MaterialParser`.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/ (2026-08-11), cross-referenced against the shared MaterialParser trait and AdapterBackedSource runtime.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read crate/sinex-primitives/src/parser/mod.rs:764-769 -- MaterialParser::parse_record's signature has no Config parameter.
2. Read crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:542-543 -- parser: P::default(), config never threaded.
3. Set ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length or HyprlandParserConfig.require_hyprland to a non-default value in a test/local config and confirm parse_record's behavior is unaffected (hardcoded take(100) for clipboard; no reference at all to require_hyprland).
acceptance_criteria:
- MaterialParser::parse_record (or an equivalent construction path) actually receives and can read Self::Config, matching how SourceDriver's initialize() genuinely stores config.
- ClipboardParserConfig.max_preview_length is read instead of the hardcoded take(100).
- HyprlandParserConfig.require_hyprland is read and actually gates graceful-degradation behavior when Hyprland is absent.
- A grep-based or compile-time check confirms no other MaterialParser impl in the workspace has declared-but-unread config fields after this fix.

title: Event/Provenance fields are all pub, making EventBuilder's typestate invariants convention-only rather than compile-time-enforced; one production bypass site already exists
description:
`Event<T>`'s fields are all `pub`, including `provenance: Provenance`, and `Provenance`'s enum variant fields are also `pub` — by explicit, documented design (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/builder.rs:326-332's own doc comment flags this: "raw struct construction bypasses the EventBuilder typestate guarantees... earlier surface area is preferable" but does not prevent it). This means any crate in the workspace can construct a fully valid-looking `Event` via a plain struct literal, skipping `.build()` — which is where several real invariants live: the offset-triplet check (builder.rs:238-260), the `ts_orig` Material-vs-Derived derivation rule (#1570 Prong B, builder.rs:283-287), and the `anchor_payload_hash`-dropped-for-Derived rule (builder.rs:266-273).

One production (non-test) call site already does this: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/output.rs:439 constructs `Event { .. }` directly rather than via `EventBuilder::build()`. Traced by hand — it currently reimplements the invariants correctly for its Derived-only use case (always sets ts_orig, drops anchor_payload_hash, canonicalizes source_event_ids via Provenance::from_derived), so it is NOT currently producing invalid events. But it establishes precedent, and demonstrates the typestate is convention-enforced (enforcement ladder rung 6) rather than compile-time-enforced (rung 1) as CLAUDE.md's type-enforcement-ladder doctrine implies for this exact type — the DB layer only re-checks the material/derived XOR and the ts_orig<=ts_coided+1s ordering (defs/events.rs:318,348), NOT offset-triplet consistency or ts_orig-derivation correctness. A future direct-literal Event construction with an unbalanced offset triplet or a provenance-mismatched ts_orig compiles fine and is invisible until/unless some downstream consumer happens to notice.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/output.rs:439 — confirm it constructs `Event { .. }` directly rather than through `EventBuilder::build()`.
2. Read builder.rs:238-287 — confirm the offset-triplet check, ts_orig derivation rule, and anchor_payload_hash-drop rule live ONLY in `.build()`, with no DB-level backstop for them (only the material/derived XOR and ts_orig ordering are DB-checked, per defs/events.rs:318,348).
3. Confirm nothing prevents a hypothetical future direct `Event { .. }` literal from violating any of the three build()-only invariants — it would compile and pass the DB CHECK.

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded: either (a) narrow `Event`'s and `Provenance`'s field visibility to `pub(crate)` (or a dedicated visibility scope) so production code outside the events module must go through `EventBuilder`, with output.rs:439 migrated to use the builder as part of the same change, or (b) if full field-privacy is out of scope pre-wipe, at minimum output.rs:439 is migrated to use `EventBuilder` now that a second manual-construction site would otherwise establish real precedent.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above.

The remaining gap (EventBuilder's OTHER invariants -- consistent anchor_payload_hash, ts_orig presence rules, automaton stamping requirements) has no validate() function to assert against; nothing panics or returns Err for a 'wrong' raw construction because there's no runtime check to bypass, only a documented convention. This is a compile-time/architecture gap (needs private fields + a builder-only construction path), not something a runtime #[ignore]'d test can meaningfully prove failing today.

title: DynamicPayload::into_event() silently stamps wall-clock ts_orig regardless of provenance kind, violating #1570 Prong B (currently dormant, zero production callers)
description:
`DynamicPayload::into_event()` (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payload.rs:207-211) bypasses the builder differently than `EventPayload::into_event()` does, and would produce invariant-violating events if ever called with Material provenance.

`EventPayload::into_event` (payload.rs:77-82, typed payloads) correctly routes through `Event::builder(self).with_provenance(provenance).build()`. But `DynamicPayload::into_event` (same method name, different type, JSON/dynamic payloads) calls `Event::new_json(...)` (mod.rs:315-350) directly instead — and `new_json` unconditionally sets `ts_orig: Some(Timestamp::now())` regardless of provenance kind (mod.rs:329), directly violating the "#1570 Prong B" contract: Material-provenance events without an explicit timestamp must leave `ts_orig = None` as the "derive me at persistence" signal for the event_engine admission stage to resolve it from the source-material temporal ledger. If ever called with `Provenance::Material{..}`, this silently stamps a wall-clock timestamp instead of deferring to temporal-ledger resolution — a ts_orig quality regression invisible at compile time, uncaught by any existing test.

Currently dormant, not exploited: the only caller in the entire workspace is a test, crate/sinex-primitives/tests/provenance_wire_test.rs:188. But it's a live public API with a name identical to the safe path (`into_event`), inviting a future caller to reach for it by mistake.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read payload.rs:207-211 (`DynamicPayload::into_event`) vs payload.rs:77-82 (`EventPayload::into_event`) — confirm they route through different construction paths despite the identical method name.
2. Read mod.rs:315-350 (`Event::new_json`) — confirm ts_orig is unconditionally `Some(Timestamp::now())` at line 329, with no check of provenance kind.
3. Confirm via grep that the only caller of `DynamicPayload::into_event` in the workspace is crate/sinex-primitives/tests/provenance_wire_test.rs:188.

## Acceptance
- `DynamicPayload::into_event()` either routes through the same builder path as `EventPayload::into_event()` (via `.into_builder().with_provenance(provenance).build()`), or is deleted since it has no production callers and its only use is a landmine waiting for a future caller.
- If kept, a test confirms calling it with Material provenance and no explicit timestamp leaves ts_orig = None.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above.

title: sinexctl replay commands never disclose replay's non-idempotent-by-design semantics
description:
None of the replay-command caveat/table-formatting code in crate/sinexctl/src/commands/replay.rs — `replay_preview_caveats` (:748-802), `replay_operation_caveats` (:804-833), or any `format_replay_*_table` function, or the `after_help` text for `plan/preview/approve/execute/submit/run` — discloses that replay is non-idempotent by design: every execution mints a new event `id` and a new `ts_coided`, even for an identical scope re-run. This is explicit, load-bearing doctrine in this repo's CLAUDE.md ("Replay is not idempotent by design... New id, new ts_coided, same occurrence coordinates").

Matters most for two paths that have no comparable gate:
1. `execute_run`'s dry-run-less convenience path (:591-682) — no disclosure before minting new interpretations.
2. Re-running `replay execute` after a `Failed` state — the existing caveat at :807-813 only says "source interpretations may remain stale... until failure is resolved," which reads as if a re-run would resume/complete the prior attempt. It does not warn that re-running instead mints an entirely new set of interpretations rather than continuing the failed one.

Other replay risks (anchor churn, cascade depth, schema mismatch) already have dedicated caveats/gates in this file — non-idempotency has none, despite being the more fundamental property.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{privacy,dlq,replay,blob,ops,ops/*}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `sinexctl replay preview` or `sinexctl replay execute` for any scope.
2. Read the printed caveats and `after_help` text.
3. Observe no caveat states that a second run over the same scope mints new event ids/ts_coided rather than being a no-op or resuming a prior attempt — contrast with anchor-churn/cascade-depth/schema-mismatch, which do have dedicated caveats in the same file.
acceptance_criteria:
- `replay_preview_caveats` and/or `replay_operation_caveats` includes an explicit caveat stating that replay execution is non-idempotent (new id/ts_coided minted every run), at the same visibility level as the existing anchor-churn/cascade-depth/schema-mismatch caveats.
- The `Failed`-state re-execute caveat is corrected to state plainly that re-running mints new interpretations rather than resuming the prior attempt.
- `after_help` text for `execute`/`run` mentions non-idempotency for operators who skip preview.

title: ops catchup status has no signal for automaton checkpoint-outran-emission lag (reports caught_up in exactly the scenario it exists to catch)
description:
`sinexctl ops catchup status` (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/ops/catchup.rs:70-207, `build_catchup_readiness`) folds DLQ backlog, source-material completion counts, runtime-module heartbeats (active_count/inactive_count), optional stream-pressure telemetry, and optional shadow-consumer backlog into its "caught_up" verdict. None of these signals measure per-automaton checkpoint position against actual durable-emission progress.

This is a direct blind spot for the tracked open seam (CLAUDE.md "Known open correctness seam", r6d epic): an adapter automaton's checkpoint can durably advance before its outputs are actually emitted, and once that happens catch-up cannot repair it. An automaton stuck in exactly this state still heartbeats normally (`runtime_signal.active_count` reads healthy) while its derived-event output is silently behind. `catchup status` would report `verdict: "caught_up"` in precisely the scenario the command exists to catch.

This is a design gap, not a simple wiring bug: fixing it needs a new runtime read-surface (per-automaton checkpoint-vs-emission-lag) that doesn't currently exist, not just calling an existing function from a new call site like the other findings in this audit batch.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexctl/src/commands/{privacy,dlq,replay,blob,ops,ops/*}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Put an adapter automaton into the known checkpoint-outran-emission state (per the r6d/vxu tracked seam: checkpoint advances durably before output emission completes).
2. Run `sinexctl ops catchup status`.
3. Observe `runtime_signal.active_count` reads healthy (automaton is heartbeating) and the overall verdict reports `caught_up`, despite derived-event output being silently behind — no signal in `build_catchup_readiness`'s inputs measures per-automaton checkpoint-vs-emission lag.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision recorded on whether this is in scope for the current r6d/vxu emission-ordering campaign or a separate follow-on: if r6d/vxu's existing work items already plan a per-automaton lag read-surface, this bead should be relate-linked (not duplicated) and closed as covered; if not, it should be added as a new r6d child.
- Once the read-surface exists (wherever it lands), `catchup status` consumes it and `build_catchup_readiness` can no longer report "caught_up" while a known-lagging automaton is stuck in the checkpoint-outran-emission state.
