Corroborating comment confirms VectorSearchParams has zero real constructions anywhere -- strengthens the case this is untested, not just undertested.

title: core.hybrid_search RRF fusion: UUID sort-order tiebreak injects more rank spread than the entire text-relevance signal, GREATEST() silently collapses FTS scoring to trigram-only, and two disagreeing 'hybrid search' implementations exist in the same repo
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (Opus), with a worked numerical example. Dormant (embedding lane is currently 0 models/0 vectors) but load-bearing for whenever it activates -- sharpens/extends sinex-bksb.

1. crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:2690-2726: the text_results CTE unconditionally includes every VECTOR hit even with zero text similarity (WHERE e.id IN (SELECT event_id FROM vector_results) OR <text match>), then assigns every row -- including the zero-similarity ones -- a dense rank via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY GREATEST(...) DESC, e.id ASC). RRF is rank-based, so zero-text-similarity events still receive text-channel score, and their rank among the zero-similarity tie group is decided purely by e.id (UUIDv7 = ts_coided order, i.e. interpretation-mint-time). WORKED EXAMPLE with defaults (limit=20, fetch_limit=100, rrf_k=60, weights 0.7/0.3), 3 genuine text matches: an event with vector-rank-1/no-text-match sorting 90th among zero-similarity ties scores 0.013436; the SAME vector-rank-2 event but sorting 1st among ties scores 0.015978 -- the pure-UUID-tiebreak spread (0.0047->0.0020) EXCEEDS the spread of the genuine text signal across ranks 1-3 (0.00492->0.00476). The ranking is dominated by interpretation-mint-time ordering, not relevance.

2. GREATEST(word_similarity(...), ts_rank_cd(...)) (apply.rs:2694-2704) mixes incomparable scales -- word_similarity typically returns ~0.7-1.0 for a present query (measured 0.70 in the sibling documents.search finding), ts_rank_cd typically returns 0.02-0.2, so GREATEST reduces to word_similarity in essentially every case -- the FTS/ts_rank channel is silently overridden, not fused, DESPITE the candidate-selection predicate being @@ websearch_to_tsquery (a DIFFERENT relevance notion than word_similarity) -- selection and scoring use two different notions of relevance.

3. LIMIT v_fetch_limit (apply.rs:2725) has no ORDER BY at that query level -- the window function is computed over the full match set, then an arbitrary 100 rows survive whatever plan Postgres picks. Today the WindowAgg happens to emit in window order; a parallel plan would not guarantee it. Latent nondeterminism that could silently drop a genuine rank-1 match.

4. TWO DISAGREEING hybrid-search implementations exist in this repo: the SQL function above (which knn_search actually calls, embeddings.rs:283) does the buggy fusion described here; the parallel Rust implementation at crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/embeddings.rs:306-395 does CLASSIC, CORRECT RRF (COALESCE(1.0/(k+rank), 0.0) per channel, missing->0) -- but it's not the one wired to knn_search's live call path. Its own tie-break (ORDER BY vector_rrf+fts_rrf DESC, no deterministic secondary sort) has the same tie-order-nondeterminism issue as #3 above, at exactly-equal 1/(k+i) ties.
acceptance_criteria: Fix core.hybrid_search (the one actually called by knn_search): zero-text-similarity events should not receive a rank in the text channel at all (missing -> 0 contribution, matching the correct Rust implementation's pattern); replace GREATEST(word_similarity, ts_rank_cd) with a properly normalized/weighted combination of the two, or pick one consistently for both selection and scoring; add ORDER BY before LIMIT v_fetch_limit; add a deterministic secondary sort key (not e.id/UUID order) to any RRF tie. Consider consolidating on ONE hybrid-search implementation (the correct Rust one, or a fixed SQL one) rather than maintaining two that disagree.

title: semantics_version is a write-only stamp with zero readers anywhere -- version bumps silently duplicate data via changed equivalence_key rather than being detected or migrated
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via residual-risk-ledger follow-up. Exhaustive grep of every semantics_version occurrence in the workspace: producers (~8 automata) stamp it via with_semantics_version(), storage code persists/archives/restores the column, and converge.rs enforces only a length<=64 CHECK constraint. The SINGLE conditional read anywhere in the codebase (admission.rs:587-597) only cross-checks a candidate's own parser_semantics_version metadata against its OWN semantics_version field -- no consumer anywhere compares a STORED event's version against the reader's own version, gates behavior on it, or migrates across a version boundary. It is purely decorative from a machine-enforcement standpoint.

Demonstrated real consequence, not hypothetical: commit d37085976 ('feat(automata): operator-local civil-time bucketing for hourly/daily (2ged) (#2482)') bumped hourly and daily automata from semantics_version 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 while changing bucketing from UTC to DST-aware operator-local civil time (automata/civil.rs:48-89). The daily summarizer's occurrence key is day_id = format!('activity-day-{}', day_start.unix_timestamp()) (daily.rs:260) where day_start is now computed via the new civil-time function -- so PRE-bump rows keyed on UTC midnight and POST-bump rows keyed on local midnight are DIFFERENT equivalence_key values. The old 1.0.0 daily rows are never superseded by the new 2.0.0 rows and stay live alongside them -- any consumer of activity.summary.daily double-counts across the version boundary. The bump's own PR body concedes the mitigation is 'Under the fresh rebuild, no historical replay is needed' -- i.e. the operator's imminent wipe is the ONLY thing that saves this specific instance; there is no actual mechanism preventing recurrence. (Hourly happens to escape this specific incident only because Europe/Warsaw's UTC offset is a whole number of hours, an accident of the operator's timezone, not a design property.)

The NEXT semantics_version bump, without a wipe to paper over it, will silently mix regimes again with no detection.
acceptance_criteria: Either give semantics_version a real enforcement mechanism (a migration path, a version-gated equivalence_key derivation so old and new versions collide/supersede correctly, or at minimum a startup check that flags mixed-version live data for an operator to review) or accept and document that semantics_version bumps require an explicit data migration/backfill step every time, since today nothing detects or prevents silent duplication across a bump.

title: reflection-lane event supersession is structurally impossible and fails CLOSED -- apply_supersession's archive step is hardcoded to core.events regardless of which lane resolved the collision
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via residual-risk-ledger follow-up, alongside the reflection-lane equivalence-key-collision confirmation (see comment on sinex-txt4). apply_supersession (event_engine/jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs:473-483) calls execute_cascade_archive with NO lane parameter, and that function is hardcoded to the activity lane at the SQL level: crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence.rs:2298 (SELECT count(*) FROM core.events WHERE id=ANY(...)) and :2442 (DELETE FROM core.events WHERE id=ANY(...)).

A reflection-lane event resolving as Superseded therefore hits the pre-validate existence-count mismatch (0 rows found in core.events for an id that's actually live in reflection.events), returns Err, apply_supersession returns false, and the revision is silently suppressed while the stale reflection row stays live forever -- the documented safe-fallback behavior (keep existing live interpretation) fires for the WRONG reason (a lane mismatch, not a genuine absence) and produces a permanently-stuck stale reflection event with no error surfaced to the caller. crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/queries.rs:656-658 already documents 'no archive/tombstone pathway exists yet for reflection.events rows' as a known omission, but this specific fail-closed consequence on the supersession path was not previously traced or tracked.
acceptance_criteria: execute_cascade_archive (and apply_supersession's call into it) becomes lane-aware, targeting reflection.events when the resolving event is on the reflection lane, matching the pattern already used for the storage_lane-aware admission pre-pass. At minimum, if reflection archive/tombstone remains genuinely unbuilt, apply_supersession should detect the lane mismatch and surface a clear error/log distinct from a genuine archive-target-not-found case, rather than silently suppressing the revision.

title: dbus source: 6 of 8 event types build entirely stubbed payloads (hardcoded/wrong fields, not just missing) -- distinct bug layered under the already-tracked sinex-8xqo subscription/classification fix
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via per-source bespoke-logic audit. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/system/dbus.rs:217-301: body_json/args_value (the real D-Bus signal payload) is captured but only actually used for notification.sent and the generic signal.received/method.called fallback. For the other SIX typed variants, every semantically meaningful field is a compile-time constant, not derived from the signal:
- media.state_changed (217-241): status always Stopped, title/artist/album/position always None -- the entire now-playing/MPRIS data path is a non-functional stub.
- bluetooth.device_changed (252-264): connected:true and paired:false HARDCODED regardless of whether the signal was actually a connect or disconnect -- a SILENTLY WRONG value, not just missing. device_name/device_class/rssi always None.
- network.state_changed (266-275): state always Unknown; ssid/ip_address always None.
- mount.event (278-288): event_type always Mounted (never Unmounted), device and mount_point both set to the SAME path value (conflating two different concepts), filesystem always 'unknown'.
- device.connected (291-301): device_type always Other, vendor/model/serial always None, properties always an empty map (real D-Bus properties never captured).

dbus_test.rs only asserts on event_type/summary/body for the notification case -- nothing asserts on media/bluetooth/network/mount/device field contents, so this ships green. This is DISTINCT from and NOT fixed by the already-open sinex-8xqo (which only addresses match-rule subscription and event-type classification, e.g. PropertiesChanged misfiled as method.called) -- 8xqo's fix would make these branches fire MORE often, surfacing this stub-payload bug more, not less.

Compounding privacy gap in the SAME area: dbus.rs:255 sets device_address to the raw D-Bus object path, and BlueZ paths embed the device MAC as /org/bluez/hci0/dev_AA_BB_CC_DD_EE_FF (underscore-separated hex). The privacy catalog's mac_address regex (privacy/detector.rs:305-323) only matches colon/dash/dot-separated MACs, not underscore-separated -- so this leaks unredacted even though the rule's empty contexts:[] means it's meant to apply everywhere. Currently low-likelihood-triggered (bluetooth branch rarely fires per 8xqo's own subscription-gap finding) but becomes live the moment 8xqo's fix lands, landing simultaneously with the hardcoded connected/paired values above.

Also grep-confirmed (not fully read): udev.rs has the same hardcoded-None stub pattern for vendor/model/serial/properties -- related completeness gap, not independently verified beyond the grep.
acceptance_criteria: media.state_changed/bluetooth.device_changed/network.state_changed/mount.event/device.connected payload builders actually parse body_json/args_value into their declared fields instead of hardcoding stub values -- prioritize bluetooth.device_changed given it currently emits an ACTIVELY WRONG connected/paired value, not just a missing one. Add the underscore-separated MAC format to the mac_address privacy detector regex. Add field-content assertions to dbus_test.rs for the currently-unasserted event types so a future regression is caught. Sequence relative to sinex-8xqo: fixing 8xqo without this makes the bug more visible, not less -- consider fixing together or fixing this first.

title: git source: no force-push/rewrite detection (orphaned pre-rewrite commits accumulate forever with no signal), full history buffered twice per scan, non-UTF8 author/committer name fails the WHOLE repo's capture
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via per-source bespoke-logic audit. Three distinct robustness gaps in crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/git.rs:

1. No force-push/rewrite detection: occurrence identity is (commit_sha, repo_path) with no ref-history pinning against previously-seen state. StaticFileAdapter's cursor (adapters/static_file.rs:49-70) triggers a rescan when .git/HEAD's resolved OID changes -- exactly what happens on a force-push. On rescan, git log re-walks the NEW history from the new HEAD: rewritten commits get new SHAs -> new occurrence keys -> new commit.created events. The OLD commits already emitted for the pre-rewrite SHAs are never marked superseded/invalidated/archived (sinex never deletes, per doctrine) -- they remain in the event log forever with no field or companion event indicating a rewrite happened. A consumer reconstructing 'current' repo history from the commit.created stream cannot distinguish live-branch commits from orphaned pre-rewrite ones.

2. Fully-buffered, doubled history read: run_git_log (216-230) and run_git_log_stats (335-353) both use Command::...output().await, buffering the ENTIRE git log stdout in-process, TWICE (a second full-history --shortstat pass), with no batching/streaming. For a large tracked repo this is memory-proportional to full history size, doubled -- a real resource risk given this host's documented earlyoom SIGTERM-at-<15%-free behavior.

3. Non-UTF8 author/committer name/email fails the ENTIRE repo's capture, not just one commit: String::from_utf8(output.stdout) on the COMBINED multi-commit output (239-243). --encoding=UTF-8 (222) only re-encodes each commit's subject/body per its own encoding header -- it does NOT touch %aN/%aE/%cN/%cE (author/committer name/email), which git stores as raw header bytes with no encoding guarantee (old repos/tools sometimes wrote Latin-1 names). One such commit anywhere in history means total capture failure for that repo, with no per-commit isolation (unlike other CSV-shaped parsers in this codebase that report the specific failing row).
acceptance_criteria: Detect a force-push/rewrite (compare the new git log's earliest-divergence point against previously-recorded SHAs at the same ref) and emit some signal (a companion event, a superseded marker) rather than silently accumulating orphaned commits forever. Stream/batch git log output instead of buffering the full history twice per scan. Isolate per-commit UTF8 decode failures so one bad historical commit doesn't abort capture of the entire repo.

title: DirectoryWalkAdapter and StaticFileAdapter read entire files into memory with zero size ceiling before any downstream cap applies -- real OOM vector on the live knowledgebase-vault source
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via untrusted-file-parser-robustness audit. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/directory_walk.rs:316 (fs::read(...).await) and static_file.rs:97 (std::fs::read(...)) both read a whole file into a Vec<u8> with NO size check before or after. Downstream, adapter_source.rs:1401-1476 batches records with a 256KiB cap (ADAPTER_MATERIAL_BATCH_MAX_BYTES), but that cap is only enforced on the BATCH after the first record is already unconditionally admitted (pending_batch = vec![first_pending] precedes the size-check loop) -- a single large file has already been fully read into memory by the time any of this runs.

Concrete live-reachable scenario: the knowledgebase-vault source (KnowledgebaseVaultParser) uses DirectoryWalkAdapter to scan an Obsidian vault. A sync-tool corruption, a hardlink loop, or a user accidentally dropping a large binary file with a .md extension into the vault causes the adapter to allocate the whole file before any downstream logic (including the 256KiB batch cap) ever sees it. This is a distinct, earlier, unaudited call site from the already-filed sinex-cgcs (100MB/512MiB dead band at the acceptance/retrieval layer) and sinex-dpof (MaterialReadySet's unrelated O(n) TTL sweep) -- this is the adapter's own read boundary, which has no cap at all, not even the wrong one.
acceptance_criteria: DirectoryWalkAdapter and StaticFileAdapter enforce a size check (stat the file, compare against a configured max, reject/stream instead of read-whole-file) before reading file contents into memory, rather than relying entirely on downstream batch-size caps that only apply after the fact.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest

AC satisfied: StaticFileAdapter and DirectoryWalkAdapter stat before read, enforce the 64 MiB whole-file ceiling, re-check during bounded reads with a one-byte sentinel, and reject without truncating or emitting partial source bytes. Adapter stream errors now return contextual runtime errors without cursor advancement.

Changed: commit 3a29ff8c2.

Verification: xtask test invocation 2006670; 41 passed, 0 failed, 2253 skipped. Relevant passing tests include static_file_bounded_read_rejects_growth_without_partial_material, oversized_directory_file_is_rejected_as_a_visible_error, and adapter_stream_error_is_returned_without_advancing_cursor.

No wipe, deployment, or PR.

title: instruction_reconciler's expectation.status claim-support vector is fabricated: hardcoded instantiate(2,0,1,0) regardless of actual evidence, rendered verbatim as 'Direct/2 supporting/0 counterevidence' on every read surface
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via evidence/metadata-honesty audit (Opus). INSTRUCTION_RECONCILER_OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS declares SupportLevel::Direct (instruction_reconciler.rs:73-77), and both emission paths hardcode the SAME instantiation regardless of what actually happened: the observation-match path (:295, instantiate(2,0,1,0)) AND the idle-flush 'this instruction was never observed and timed out' path (:360, ALSO instantiate(2,0,1,0)) -- while that idle-flush output actually carries exactly ONE parent (:346, vec![candidate.instruction_event_id]) and an EMPTY matched_event_ids (:333). A 'no observation ever arrived' claim declares two supporting events. counterevidence_count is hardcoded 0 even for the Contradicted outcome (instruction.rs:263-267 produces Contradicted; the emitter at :295 still passes 0) -- the observation that DISPROVES the instruction is recorded as zero counterevidence. SupportLevel::Direct is also used identically for the genuine target-match case AND for the heuristic sole-pending-candidate inference the code's own doc comment describes as a correlation guess (instruction_reconciler.rs:206-230) -- the epistemic weakness lives only in a code comment, the machine-readable claim vector says Direct either way.

Why this is not cosmetic: AnalysisClaim is candidate-grade and every consumer (API events.cards, sinexctl query/show/timeline/context/tui, sinex_search_events MCP) renders the fabricated numbers verbatim to the operator (views/events.rs:655-667): 'support=Direct, coverage=Partial, temporal_quality=DeclaredEffective, adjudication=unreviewed (2 supporting event(s), 0 counterevidence)'. Nothing validates these values at emission -- the shared output guard (automaton/adapter/output.rs:84-117) checks only parent-count limits, never that evidence_event_count <= source_event_ids.len(). Sibling automata (health.rs:358,378, entity_enricher.rs:266,275) derive the count from the actual id vector -- this is an outlier, not house style. No test asserts these values.
acceptance_criteria: instruction_reconciler's claim-support emission derives evidence_event_count/counterevidence_count from the actual matched_event_ids/parent vectors (matching health.rs/entity_enricher.rs's pattern) instead of a hardcoded instantiate(2,0,1,0), and distinguishes SupportLevel between a genuine target-match and the heuristic sole-candidate inference. Consider adding the missing evidence_event_count<=source_event_ids.len() check to the shared output guard (automaton/adapter/output.rs) so this class of fabrication is caught for any future automaton, not just this one.

title: two telemetry continuous aggregates group by unbounded raw strings (shell commands, filesystem paths) with zero retention policy anywhere in sinex_telemetry
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via surface/signal honesty re-audit (metrics cardinality sweep). crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs: sinex_telemetry.command_frequency_hourly (3024-3067) groups by time_bucket + LEFT(command_string, 500) -- every distinct shell command (up to 500 chars) creates a new row every hour it's seen; interactive shell commands are highly unique (embedded paths/timestamps/hashes/UUIDs/flag values), so this is functionally one row per unique command per hour, not a small fixed-cardinality dimension. sinex_telemetry.file_activity_summary (3196-3208) groups by time_bucket + raw filesystem directory path (regexp_replace to strip the filename) -- also unbounded domain (temp dirs, per-invocation cache/build dirs with random names). No retention policy exists for EITHER, or for any sinex_telemetry.* relation at all -- grep for add_retention_policy across apply.rs returns exactly one hit (reflection.events, 30 days); continuous aggregates are themselves TimescaleDB hypertables needing their own retention policy to bound growth, and none is declared for the telemetry schema anywhere. Net effect: two rollup tables driven directly off a busy interactive user's (or a misbehaving source's) unbounded-domain strings, with no cap on cardinality and no cap on retention -- distinct from sinex-07qk (wrong values, not unbounded growth) and sinex-audit-telemetry-cagg-mixed-clock (clock semantics).
acceptance_criteria: Add a retention policy to sinex_telemetry's continuous aggregates (matching the pattern already used for reflection.events), and reduce cardinality on command_frequency_hourly/file_activity_summary -- e.g. bucket/normalize the command string (strip arguments, hash long tails) and the path (fixed depth) rather than grouping on raw unbounded text.

title: semantic/derivation lane lifecycle (create/set-status/discard) has zero actor attribution and zero durable audit record -- neither operations_log nor auth context reaches these handlers
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via surface/signal honesty re-audit (audit-trail completeness sweep). Related to but distinct from sinex-scrl (which flags handle_semantic_lane_set_status as an AUTHORIZATION bypass -- no transition validation); this finding is that even after the fact, there is no audit RECORD of who did it.

crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/semantic.rs: handle_semantic_lane_create (154-189), handle_semantic_lane_set_status (205-216), handle_semantic_lane_discard (218-230) take NO auth: &RpcAuthContext parameter at all -- the handler literally never learns who called it. All three register via pool_typed_rpc (not pool_auth_typed_rpc) -- no auth threading exists at the registration boundary either. The backing table derivation.lanes (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/derivation.rs:341-357) has no actor/operator column; operation_id is nullable and CLIENT-SUPPLIED verbatim (req.operation_id at semantic.rs:181), not generated/verified server-side against a real core.operations_log row. None of the three handlers call log_operation/log_operation_with_executor. The sibling handle_semantic_epoch_create (semantic.rs:96-140) in the SAME FILE DOES take auth and DOES populate created_by (derivation.epochs has that column) -- proving the pattern is known and used elsewhere in this exact module, just not carried to lanes, which are the more frequently-mutated object (every status transition -- running->completed->discarded/promoted -- is unattributed). An operator asking 'who created/discarded lane X, and when, and why' has nothing to consult beyond the row's own created_at/completed_at.

Verified solid for contrast: PKM entity/relation creation (pkm.rs:249-273,326-349) correctly calls log_operation_with_executor in the same transaction as the write. Tasks/instructions handlers don't write operations_log either, but that's architecturally fine -- they route through the normal EventBuilder->core.events pipeline instead, which is a legitimate alternate audit trail. Semantic lanes use NEITHER mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: handle_semantic_lane_create/set_status/discard take auth like their sibling handle_semantic_epoch_create, and either add an actor column to derivation.lanes (matching epochs) or call log_operation_with_executor so lane lifecycle mutations are attributable after the fact.

title: raw shell command text logged at INFO level in canonicalizer.rs, bypassing all DB-side privacy machinery permanently -- own contract declares this data Sensitive
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via surface/signal honesty re-audit (log-leakage sweep). crate/sinexd/src/automata/canonicalizer.rs:108: info!("Canonicalizing command: {}", payload.command) fires in TerminalCommandCanonicalizer::process() for every command.executed event from shell.kitty/shell.atuin/bash/zsh/fish sources. payload.command is the full, unmodified shell command string. Default-on: crate/sinexd/src/main.rs:51 sets RUST_LOG default_value='info', so this executes in production by default. The same file's own register_source_contract! block (canonicalizer.rs:313-328) declares privacy_tier: ContractPrivacyTier::Sensitive for this exact automaton's output -- the code knows this data class is sensitive, but the log call is a separate, independent write path straight to stdout/journald that redact_batch (policy.rs:752, the one documented redaction chokepoint) never touches -- nothing downstream (tombstone, purge, privacy-policy rule changes, retroactive redaction) can ever reach or retract it. Redaction wouldn't have caught it anyway: existing PII/secret detection is pattern-based and known-incomplete (sinex-24es), and shell commands routinely carry credentials verbatim (export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=..., psql 'postgresql://user:pw@host/db', curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...', git clone https://token@github.com/...) -- these land in journald in cleartext even if the DB copy is later redacted or the source event tombstoned. Minor secondary instance, same shape: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/content_store/manager.rs:387 logs raw filenames (can carry PII) outside redact_batch too. Verified CLEAN for contrast: DB URL/bearer-token logging at preflight/database.rs:657-659, services.rs:705-714, configuration.rs:139 all correctly route through redact_url_password_for_diagnostics before interpolation, and privacy_coverage.rs:263-271 explicitly and honestly documents that guarantee's scope ('arbitrary tracing payloads remain outside this guarantee') -- which is exactly the gap this finding demonstrates in practice.
acceptance_criteria: Remove or redact the raw command interpolation from canonicalizer.rs's info! call (e.g. log only a hash/length, or gate full-command logging behind an explicit debug-only opt-in that's clearly documented as bypassing all privacy controls). Sweep for and fix the content_store/manager.rs filename-logging instance too.

title: cold start has zero stagger across ~25 runtime tasks and crash-restart backoff has zero jitter -- synchronized thundering herd on every restart, worsened by systemd readiness firing before the snapshot phase
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via lifecycle/crash-consistency audit. Extends/sharpens what a sibling perturbation-robustness audit flagged more generally as cold-start thundering herd risk -- this finding traces the exact mechanism.

crate/sinexd/src/supervisor/mod.rs: start_automata (546-551) and start_source_bindings (639-645) are tight for loops calling tokio::spawn with NO delay, NO concurrency cap, NO jitter -- all ~25 runtime tasks (15 source bindings + 10 automata on this deployment) begin at the same instant. Each source then immediately runs Phase 1: Snapshot in run_source_startup_sequence (source_startup.rs:35-51) -- the function's own comment notes adapter-backed sources 'load their full event table into memory' here, so ~15 full snapshot loads start concurrently.

Compounding: restart backoff (spawn_automaton lines 567-608, spawn_source_binding 654-695) uses an IDENTICAL, DETERMINISTIC 1s -> 2s -> ... -> 30s ladder with NO randomization. Tasks that fail from a shared cause (DB connection exhaustion per sinex-mi2y, NATS unavailable, disk pressure) fail together and therefore retry together, permanently phase-aligned, hammering the shared resource every 30s in lockstep -- this directly compounds sinex-mi2y's connection-budget overrun into a recurring, synchronized failure storm rather than a one-time spike. STABLE_THRESHOLD=60s resets backoff to 1s, so a resource degrading on a ~60s cadence converts the ladder into a hot loop.

Also: systemd_notify::notify_ready fires at source_startup.rs:33 BEFORE the snapshot phase -- systemd reports the unit healthy while all 15 snapshots are still thundering, so any healthcheck/monitoring gating on systemd readiness gets a false-positive during exactly the highest-load window.
acceptance_criteria: Stagger initial task spawn (even a small random delay per task) and add jitter to the crash-restart backoff ladder so a shared-cause failure doesn't produce a permanently phase-aligned retry storm. Consider deferring systemd readiness notification until past the snapshot phase, or add a separate 'fully warmed up' signal distinct from 'process started'.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: startup staggering, retry jitter, and readiness timing are fixed. Commit 10a94544f applies a shared 0-2 second runtime startup stagger to automata and source bindings, replaces deterministic retry delays with bounded jittered backoff capped at 30 seconds, and moves source READY notification after snapshot and gap-fill. Verification: supervisor tests runtime_startup_stagger_is_bounded_and_seeded and runtime_retry_backoff_has_bounded_jitter passed in the landed test update; source startup and top-level supervisor paths were reviewed at current HEAD 0476b5453. The related permanent cold-start delivery race is separately tracked by sinex-i41y and was fixed in 6e8e4c357, but its production-independent adversarial proof remains open there.

title: source control-plane addressing is not instance-unique -- multiple bindings sharing a source_id (e.g. 3 browser.history instances) share one NATS control subject, breaking replay dispatch and progress accounting
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via lifecycle/crash-consistency audit. Extends already-open sinex-nbag (whole-source-rescan on non-FileDrop adapters) with a distinct, more severe half: instance-level control-plane collision.

crate/sinexd/src/sources/bindings.rs:329-338 sets control_identity to the bare source_id (only checkpoint_identity gets the disambiguated service_name). command_listener.rs:59,72,88 subscribes plainly (no queue group -- verified no queue_subscribe exists anywhere in crate/sinexd/src) to sinex.control.sources.{module_name}.* keyed on that non-unique control_identity.

Live deployment has THREE browser.history bindings (Chrome Default/History, qutebrowser history.sqlite, qutebrowser webengine History), all with distinct service_name but the SAME source_id -- so all three subscribe to the IDENTICAL control subject. Replay dispatch (replay_writer.rs:526-534) is a single core-NATS request(scan_subject, payload), which: (1) delivers the SourceScanCommand to ALL THREE instances, (2) reads exactly ONE SourceScanAck -- from whichever responded first, possibly an off-target instance, (3) leaves all three publishing progress on the same sinex.control.replay.progress.<operation_id> subject, so replay progress accounting is summed across three unrelated scans. Same fan-out affects .drain/.resume/.set-horizon/.cancel.

Compounding with sinex-nbag: since scan_historical ignores args.replay entirely for non-FileDrop adapters, each of the three instances runs a FULL Checkpoint::None historical rescan of its own browser DB whenever ANY of the three is targeted. The two off-target scans are saved from producing visible duplicates only INCIDENTALLY, via browser.history's equivalence-key admission suppression -- which is fail-open dedup, the exact mechanism sinex-ecy already flags as collision-prone. So today's apparent safety is luck, not design.
acceptance_criteria: control_identity is instance-unique (matching checkpoint_identity's disambiguation via service_name), so replay/drain/resume/set-horizon/cancel commands target exactly the intended binding instance, not every binding sharing the same source_id.

title: hardcoded uniform ack_wait=30s/max_deliver=10/batch_size=128 for all 16 automata's confirmed-event consumers -- no override mechanism, conditional double-processing race for LLM-backlog-heavy automata
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via cross-implementation consistency audit (NATS JetStream consumer config vs AutomatonSpec registry). crate/sinexd/src/automata/registry.rs's AutomatonSpec has no consumer-tuning fields at all (name/run/contract/outputs only). crate/sinexd/src/runtime/jetstream_consumer.rs:248-250 hardcodes max_deliver=10 and ack_wait=Duration::from_secs(30) identically for every automaton, with no field in JetStreamEventConsumerConfig to override either. batch_size is likewise hardcoded to 128 for all automata (automaton_runtime.rs:523-526), independent of per-automaton processing latency.

Traced blast radius: RunnerConfirmedEventHandler::handle_confirmed (stream/listener.rs:120-132) only forwards into a bounded 1024-capacity mpsc channel before acking -- the slow (LLM-bound) work happens downstream, decoupled from the ack loop, so 30s ack_wait is not a routine bottleneck under normal throughput. The real failure mode: consume_confirmed_events (jetstream_consumer.rs:277-313) processes up to 128 messages SEQUENTIALLY per batch, each awaiting the channel send; if the downstream automaton task stalls (LLM gateway outage/backlog) long enough to fill the 1024-slot channel, .send() blocks, and if that exceeds 30s for a message still mid-batch, NATS independently redelivers that message server-side (unaffected by client-side blocking) -- which can then be re-fetched and re-pushed a second time, a genuine double-processing/duplicate-derivation race bounded to max_deliver=10 attempts. LLM-calling automata (embedding-producer, potentially entity-extractor/relation-extractor/document-parser) are structurally the ones most likely to saturate the shared channel during backlog catch-up (which the re-import will produce), while the uniform ceiling was clearly tuned for the fast automata.
acceptance_criteria: Per-automaton ack_wait/max_deliver/batch_size become configurable (either via AutomatonSpec fields or a lookup keyed by automaton name), sized appropriately for LLM-calling automata specifically, so a downstream stall doesn't trigger server-side redelivery and duplicate derivation while the local channel is merely backed up rather than actually stuck.

title: hledger finance occurrence_key collides to a fixed sentinel when NO posting has an explicit amount -- distinct real transactions silently collapse as revisions of each other
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via cross-implementation consistency audit (equivalence_key/OccurrenceKey sweep across all source contracts). crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/finance.rs:374-386 derives first_amount via tx.postings.iter().find(|p| p.amount.is_some())...unwrap_or("0"). When NO posting in an hledger transaction has an explicit amount (a common hledger style: only implicit/auto-balanced amounts), first_amount collapses to the literal string '0' for every such transaction. Two distinct real transactions on the same date with the same description (e.g. two recurring 'Grocery run' entries, both auto-balanced) produce an identical OccurrenceKey{date, description, '0'} and collide -- the second is silently treated as a revision of the first under SupersedeOnChange/dedup rather than a new occurrence, meaning one of the two transactions is effectively lost from the live event set.
acceptance_criteria: finance.rs's occurrence key derivation does not collapse to a fixed sentinel when no posting has an explicit amount -- either include a real distinguishing field (posting count, account list, computed/inferred amount) or fall back to a different identity strategy for implicit-amount transactions so two distinct transactions with the same date+description don't alias.

title: admission ts_orig lower bound (default 2000-01-01) silently routes genuinely old historical imports into a documented-lossy DLQ path; duration_ms int4 overflows at 24.86 days for long-running operations
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via numeric/temporal envelope audit. Two findings, both relevant given this operator's real historical data spans years/decades and the imminent re-import is expected to carry genuinely old timestamps:

1. MEDIUM: crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/config.rs:172-173 (ts_orig_lower_bound_unix, default 946_684_800 = 2000-01-01) is enforced at admission.rs:708-726 -- any event with ts_orig before this bound is AdmissionRejectionKind::PastTimestamp, routed through route_validation_failure to the DLQ. No override exists in the live deployment (grepped sinnix + nixos/ for TS_ORIG_LOWER_BOUND -- zero hits), so this default is what's actually running. Given this operator's data can genuinely predate 2000 (documents, financial/hledger data, photo EXIF, old chat exports per the data-lake structure), such records don't just get quarantined for review -- they land in a DLQ path this project's own CLAUDE.md documents as LOSSY: DLQ requeue can silently destroy the only surviving copy of a message when it collides with the DLQ stream's dupeWindow (sinex-3kqx, open), and the material-assembler's own DLQ publish is unconfirmed core-NATS, not JetStream-acked (sinex-wb1, reopened). So pre-2000 historical data hitting this default risks actual permanent loss, not just quarantine.

2. LOW-MEDIUM: core.operations_log.duration_ms is declared plain .integer() (Postgres int4, max ~2.147B) in crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/operations.rs:642, computed via (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - uuid_extract_timestamp(p_operation_id))) * 1000)::integer in core.complete_operation/fail_operation (apply.rs:2048-2050, 2069-2071). This overflows at ~24.86 days of wall-clock elapsed between start and completion of a SINGLE operation (archive/restore/replay/purge/tombstone/projection-rebuild). Postgres raises a hard ERROR on the cast (fails loud, not silent corruption) -- but a legitimately long-running operation (e.g. a replay spanning a large multi-year cascade during the fresh-rebuild campaign, paused/resumed across weeks) would fail to close out with a DB error precisely at completion time.
acceptance_criteria: Before the actual wipe/re-import: verify whether any source's historical data plausibly predates 2000-01-01, and if so either raise/remove ts_orig_lower_bound_unix via config, or confirm the DLQ path is safe for that volume given the still-open sinex-3kqx/wb1 lossy-DLQ bugs. Separately, widen duration_ms to bigint (int8) to remove the 24.86-day ceiling on any single operation.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: implementation verified on current branch. Historical timestamp lower bound defaults to None in crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/config.rs, so pre-2000 source material is not silently routed to the lossy DLQ; the data-lake inventory identifies historical photos, finance, chat, journal, and Takeout exports, so this is the required policy for the wipe campaign. Existing admission test admission_service_preserves_pre_2000_historical_timestamp proves an old timestamp is accepted. Duration storage/completion was widened to BIGINT with bigint casts and i64 repository types. Verification: nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd --impact-mode=off --test event_engine -E "test(admission_service_preserves_pre_2000_historical_timestamp) or test(defaults_match_constants) or test(defaults_read_process_environment)"; nix develop --command xtask check -p sinexd --skip-tests. Remaining DLQ defects sinex-3kqx and sinex-wb1 remain explicit pre-wipe blockers.

title: DLQ dedupe identity derives from only the FIRST child of a multi-event intent -- two distinct intents sharing a leading event collapse into one DLQ entry and silently lose the second
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via test-coverage risk-mapping audit (Opus). New finding adjacent to (not the same as) the already-open sinex-3kqx (DLQ requeue + dupeWindow collision) and sinex-w4i (multi-intent partial-record re-emit duplication) -- this is the mechanism that produces the exact re-emitted-intents-sharing-a-leading-event scenario sinex-w4i describes.

dlq_publish_msg_id (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/dlq.rs:44-51) derives dedupe identity from events[0].id only (dlq_event_id, lines 30-41) -- the first child of a multi-event intent. Combined with the 1h dupeWindow and the ack-handling at lines 165-171 (match ack.await { Ok(_) => return Ok(()) }, which never inspects ack.duplicate), two distinct multi-child intents that happen to share a first child (as produced by sinex-w4i's re-emit mechanism) collapse into ONE DLQ entry, and the SECOND message is treated as successfully DLQ'd and ACKed off a retention=work stream -- meaning its other sibling events are gone with no trace. The Event-Id header used for requeue-by-id has the same first-child-only limitation, so requeue cannot recover the lost siblings either.

Realistic gap test: publish intent A = [X, Y] and intent B = [X, Z] (same leading event id, different siblings), both failing admission, inside one dupe window. Assert two distinct DLQ entries exist, or that Z's failure is recorded somewhere. Today: one entry, Z gone with no trace.
acceptance_criteria: DLQ dedupe identity for a multi-event intent incorporates all child event ids (or a hash of the full intent), not just the first, so two distinct intents sharing a leading event don't collapse into one DLQ entry. A test proves the scenario above (two intents sharing a first child, both failing) results in both being recoverable, not just one.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: SATISFIED. Multi-child DLQ identity hashes all ordered child identities/JSON rather than only the first child, and the production route test proves [X,Y] and [X,Z] sharing X produce two recoverable DLQ records. Verified: nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E "test(dlq_route_keeps_multi_child_intents_with_same_leading_event_recoverable)". No deferred AC.

title: gateway: SSE Last-Event-ID is accepted but never actually resumes (silent event loss on reconnect), unauthenticated /health leaks DB error text, SSE bypasses rate limiting
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 pre-wipe audit of the API/gateway surface (crate/sinexd/src/api/). Scope enforcement itself was verified genuinely solid (single chokepoint in RpcRegistry::dispatch, zero role/mutability inversions across 134 registrations, role not client-forgeable, no token leakage) -- these findings are narrower gaps beyond the confirmed-fixed sinex-pzo9 (ops.start RCE, filed same session).

1. MEDIUM-HIGH: SSE's Last-Event-ID header is parsed and validated but NEVER actually used to resume -- SubscriptionSlot::new uses resume_from only to seed a recent-delivered dedup set with that single id, no NATS/DB backfill exists. Events published while a client was disconnected are silently absent with no gap signal on reconnect (SseMessage::Gap only fires for live channel-full drops). Browser EventSource clients auto-send this header and correctly assume resume semantics -- they get silent data loss instead.

2. MEDIUM: /health and /ready are unauthenticated AND leak internal error text -- service_container.rs builds format!("Database ping failed: {error}") from raw sqlx Display and returns it in the unauthenticated response body, the exact 'Display may leak paths/SQL' tripwire this project's own CLAUDE.md warns about. /ready also runs a real DB query plus a NATS round-trip per unauthenticated request with no rate limiter (compounds existing open bead sinex-audit-auth-no-rate-limit).

3. MEDIUM: SSE subscriptions bypass rate limiting entirely (handle_sse_stream never calls state.rate_limiter) and the only cap is a single process-global MAX_ACTIVE_SUBSCRIPTIONS=512 counter with no per-token share -- one readonly token opening 512 connections locks out every other subscriber.

4. MEDIUM-LOW: the distributed rate limiter has no real window-reset primitive -- the 'window' is implemented solely via KV bucket max_age = window_seconds*2, so effective quota is roughly half the configured RPM and an exhausted token stays blocked until 2x the window after its last write, not on a rolling window. Up to 49 locally-reserved tokens can also survive global-key expiry unaccounted.

5. LOW: SSE gap frames reference from_seq/to_seq but event frames use the event UUID as the SSE id (falling back to seq only when id is None) and the payload struct omits seq entirely -- only the 'dropped' count in a gap frame is actionable, not which events were lost.

6. LOW (latent, currently unreachable): native_messaging's dispatch_method maps a missing extension_id to RpcAuthContext::system() = Admin -- currently dead because enforce_extension rejects a missing id first, but the default is inverted relative to the sibling resolve_extension_role's ReadOnly default; a future refactor could reopen this.
acceptance_criteria: SSE reconnect either does a real backfill from the last-seen event id (NATS replay or DB query) or explicitly tells the client via a Gap frame that events were missed across the disconnect window, rather than silently resuming with a hole. /health error responses do not leak raw error Display text (use PublicError's key-allowlisted context pattern like the rest of the API). SSE connections go through the same rate limiter as RPC calls, or get their own explicit per-token cap.

title: TUI: module/DLQ health panels invent their own classification that ignores/contradicts the server's real signals
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via the same TUI audit as the dead-gateway finding. Two related 'the server knows better but the TUI ignores it' bugs:

1. Module health (healthy_modules 670-677, dashboard icons 713-721, Modules tab 1131-1139) classifies SOLELY on last_heartbeat_at < 60s. RuntimeInfo.status (running/draining/paused) is NEVER READ -- a draining module shows a healthy green dot. The server's actual health status filter admits BOTH 'healthy' and 'degraded' (sinex-db/src/repositories/state.rs:1278-1280) but RuntimeInfo.status carries the RUN status instead, so a genuinely degraded module is indistinguishable from healthy in this view. Separately, this panel passes stale_after_secs=31_536_000 (1 YEAR) where sinexctl runtime list correctly uses 300 (commands/runtime.rs:172) -- the denominator absorbs a full year of historical modules, and because last_heartbeat_at falls back to MAX(ts_coided) of outputs when no heartbeat exists, a perfectly normal 5-minute-cadence source can render as a red 'unhealthy' circle.

2. DLQ panel (render_dlq, 2129-2160) uses only total_messages/total_bytes/sequence numbers, discarding DlqListResponse's actual pressure_level (can be 'critical'), resource_pressure, recommended_action, and action_reason fields -- and hardcodes 'requeue --all' advice (2141) even when the server's own recommendation (based on real pressure state) would be a paced batch instead. A CRITICAL-pressure DLQ can visually look like a 1-message DLQ. Worse: the dashboard's top-level 'DLQ Messages: 0 checkmark' (689-696) covers ONLY the NATS SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_DLQ stream -- the SEPARATE persistent sinex_schemas.dlq_events table (apply.rs:1784) is never consulted at all, so the green checkmark can be FALSE while real DLQ'd events sit in the other table.
acceptance_criteria: Module health incorporates the server's actual RuntimeInfo.status (draining/paused correctly rendered, not shown as healthy) and uses the same stale_after_secs value as sinexctl runtime list (300s, not 1 year) for consistency. DLQ panel surfaces the server's real pressure_level/recommended_action instead of a hardcoded suggestion, and the top-level DLQ indicator checks BOTH the NATS stream and the persistent dlq_events table before showing a green checkmark.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete: TUI module/DLQ health panels compute their own classification instead of using the server's. Testable via a TUI unit test feeding a server state the panel currently misclassifies; not written yet.

title: TUI: a dead gateway renders as a normal healthy dashboard (3 compounding bugs)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep of the sinexctl TUI (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/tui.rs). Three defects compose into a dashboard that looks perfectly fine while completely disconnected from a live backend:

1. refresh() (283-303) aborts on the FIRST version() failure and returns WITHOUT touching any panel data -- every panel keeps its last-good values from whenever the gateway was last actually reachable. There is no per-panel staleness marker and no 'data as of' timestamp anywhere in the UI.

2. app.feedback is NEVER reset to None (only ever assigned Some, at lines 254/261/273/474/529/535/542/550). The status bar checks feedback BEFORE error (637-646) and picks its style from feedback first (648-654). So after the operator presses ANY key that sets feedback even once (e.g. 'c' or 'p'), the red 'Error: ... | Press r to retry' line becomes PERMANENTLY UNREACHABLE -- a stale yellow informational message sits there instead, even while the gateway has been gone for the entire session.

3. Per-panel failures (306-311, 312-335, 339-380, 384-394) also leave previous data in place, and only the FIRST error across all panels is retained (if self.error.is_none() guards at 318/331/344/357/368/376/390/409) -- 5 simultaneously-failing RPCs surface as exactly 1 error message. The '... unavailable; see status footer' labels only fire when the underlying vec is EMPTY (never loaded), never on a refresh that failed after a prior success.

Net effect: an operator staring at this dashboard cannot distinguish 'everything is genuinely fine right now' from 'the gateway died N minutes ago and nothing has updated since.' No test covers this -- tui_test.rs builds App literals by hand and only snapshots renderers; refresh() itself is never exercised.
acceptance_criteria: Each panel tracks its own last-successful-refresh timestamp and visibly marks stale data (not just silently keeping old values). app.feedback is cleared appropriately (e.g. after N seconds, or superseded by a new error) so a genuine connection error is never permanently masked by an older informational message. Multiple simultaneous panel failures are all surfaced, not just the first. A test exercises refresh() itself (not just renderers) proving a gateway-down scenario visibly differs from a gateway-up one.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] 3 compounding TUI bugs (dead-gateway-looks-healthy) are directly testable against the TUI's refresh()/dashboard render with a simulated unreachable gateway. No test yet.

title: Health aggregation: unhealthy_threshold_minutes is dead config, aggregation isn't clock-driven, unhealthy verdicts surface nowhere
description:
Batch of related HIGH findings from the same 2026-08-10 health-aggregation audit as sinex-<system-health-bead>, on the OTHER health plane (the HealthReporter/HealthAggregator automaton pipeline itself, separate from the gateway's system.health which doesn't consult it at all):

1. HealthAggregatorConfig::unhealthy_threshold_minutes ('Threshold for marking component as unhealthy (in minutes)') is declared (crate/sinexd/src/automata/health.rs:43-44), defaulted (:65-67,78), and env-overridable (:94-97) -- but NEVER READ by any actual logic anywhere. Its only consumers are config-mirror assertions in tests that check the DEFAULT VALUE, not behavior. A component's last-reported status (even 'Healthy' from hours/days ago) is counted forever with no staleness demotion.

2. Health aggregation is not clock-driven at all: HealthAggregator::reconcile is the only entry point, ScopeReconciler has no flush_due/timer hook, and Automaton::timer_flush_derived defaults to empty for non-Windowed models (runtime/automaton/traits.rs:596-602) -- ScopeReconcilerWrapper does not override it. Total runtime silence from every reporting component therefore produces ZERO new aggregated reports; the last emitted aggregate just sits there unchanged forever.

3. Nothing surfaces an unhealthy verdict operationally even when correctly computed: health.rs:356-381 mints HealthAlertSeverity::Critical alerts, but the only non-test references to health.aggregated_report outside the automaton itself are a dev-tooling 'did the automaton emit anything' check (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/verify/mod.rs:122,124,996). No log line, no metric, no notification anywhere. Contrast HeartbeatEmitter::emit_status_alert_if_needed (runtime/heartbeat.rs:509-596), which DOES log WARN process.failed for a comparable case -- the pattern exists elsewhere in this codebase and just wasn't applied here.

4. Automaton HealthReporters are strictly event-driven with no liveness probe and no stall detection wired: automaton/adapter/mod.rs:501-505 constructs the reporter with no .with_liveness_probe(...) and never calls enable_emit_stall_detection() (only source_driver.rs:583 does this). check_and_emit() is only called inside per-event processing (adapter/process.rs:307) -- a wedged or input-starved automaton emits nothing, ages out of the 1-hour view window (sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:2938-2942), and simply vanishes from any view that DOES look at it.

5. Minor: record_warning counts warnings (health_reporter.rs:483-485) but calculate_status never reads metrics.warnings -- a dead signal. Probe-only evidence alone satisfies r6d.3's has_evidence() gate (health_reporter.rs:540-543) -- a source driver with zero processed events reports Healthy purely from a NATS-reachability probe; emit-stall only demotes to Degraded, and only after 600s.
acceptance_criteria: 1. unhealthy_threshold_minutes is actually consulted -- a component whose last report predates the threshold gets demoted (Unknown or Unhealthy), not counted at its stale last-known value forever. 2. Aggregation has a clock-driven path (periodic reconcile independent of new incoming events) so total silence gets detected, not just silently frozen. 3. An unhealthy aggregate verdict produces at minimum a log line (matching the existing heartbeat.rs precedent), ideally a metric an operator could alert on. 4. Automaton HealthReporters get liveness probes and stall detection matching source_driver.rs's existing pattern.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Dead-config/non-clock-driven health-aggregation findings are directly testable (assert unhealthy_threshold_minutes actually gates something, assert aggregation is clock-driven). None exist yet.

title: CLI safety findings: recall/context silent truncation, DLQ requeue/purge weak safety rails, replay run executes by default, blob backup path decoupled
description:
Batch of related CLI/ops safety findings from the 2026-08-10 audit sweep (tombstone two-step, lifecycle archive dry-run sharing, and events query pagination were independently verified SOLID -- do not re-litigate those):

1. sinexctl recall / events context (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/context.rs) silently truncates at --limit (default 200) and then presents the cap as if it were the complete window -- next_cursor is fetched but never surfaced (only a degraded stub at :360), the footer prints '{count} events across {n} sources in {window}' as if complete, and the JSON envelope's query echo reports limit:event_cards.count (the RETURNED count, not the requested limit) so even machine consumers can't distinguish '200 existed' from '200 was the ceiling'. Contrast: events query correctly surfaces next_cursor (query.rs:305-316).

2. ops dlq requeue --all silently discards messages past max_retries (acked and counted as permanently_failed server-side, dlq_retry.rs:375-390) but DlqRequeueResponse has no field for this and the CLI prints only an unqualified 'success: N messages requeued' (dlq.rs:207-211) -- messages then stay visible in dlq list while being unreachable by the retry consumer, inviting a follow-up purge that actually destroys them.

3. ops dlq purge --confirm destroys the ENTIRE DLQ from a single flag with no two-step/dry-run requirement (dlq.rs:213-260), unlike tombstone's verified two-step+TTL+drift-check pattern. Range purge also drops purged_count entirely on first failure (handlers/dlq.rs:698-729).

4. ops replay run executes by default -- --dry-run is opt-in (replay.rs:228-231), inverting the polarity of lifecycle archive/restore which correctly default to dry-run and require --confirm.

5. lifecycle archive --before 30d --confirm silently caps at 1000 rows with no signal that more rows matched the filter (lifecycle.rs:117-118) -- a 'success' can leave a tier essentially undrained. Contrast: the archive audit summary DOES flag its own sampling elsewhere (affected_event_ids_truncated, handlers/lifecycle.rs:97-98) -- this cap should follow that same honest-truncation pattern.

6. Blob CAS backup: sinnix hardcodes /realm/sinex/state/blob-repository (backup.nix:787) while sinex derives the path from stateRoot (nixos/modules/default.nix:504-509) -- a stateRoot change silently drops blob backup with no error. The borg integrity check is --repository-only, never verifying actual blob content, and no restore drill exists for it.

7. privacy export --output <path> does a bare std::fs::write with no existence check (privacy.rs:718) -- silent clobber of an existing file at that path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. recall/context surfaces next_cursor and reports truncation honestly when the result was capped, matching events query's existing correct pattern. 2. dlq requeue --all's response includes a permanently_failed count and the CLI prints it. 3. dlq purge gets a two-step confirmation or dry-run requirement matching tombstone's pattern; range purge preserves purged_count on partial failure. 4. replay run defaults to requiring --confirm or an explicit dry-run-first step, matching lifecycle's polarity. 5. lifecycle archive's cap-hit case is flagged the same way affected_event_ids_truncated already is. 6. Blob backup path is derived consistently (both sides read from the same source of truth) or the divergence is loudly asserted at build/deploy time. 7. privacy export refuses to silently overwrite an existing file without an explicit --force.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Additional finding 2026-08-11 via content-interpretation/rendering-safety audit, complementing this bead's existing recall/context/lifecycle-archive truncation-honesty findings: crate/sinexctl/src/commands/privacy.rs:753-766 builds the privacy-export query with ..Default::default(), and crate/sinex-primitives/src/query.rs:290-309 defaults lane:EventQueryLane::Activity -- so a privacy export SILENTLY EXCLUDES the entire reflection.events lane with no operator-visible indication. PrivacyExportScope (privacy.rs:853, populated at :783-796) records sources/event_types/since/until/text_search_used/limit but has NO lane field at all -- the export artifact's own recorded scope cannot even reproduce the query that produced it, let alone reveal the omission. Related, same file family: crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/email.rs:275-280 passes a hardcoded synthetic identity ('email','email.message.received') to disclose_json_value_for_event, but the manifest it covers also embeds material_exports derived from attachment-typed events -- operator privacy rules scoped to email.attachment.* never match and silently don't apply to that content. Lower severity than this bead's existing findings (LOW, not data loss, just an undisclosed scope gap) but worth folding into the same fix pass given the shared root cause (query defaults silently narrowing scope without recording that they did).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Bundled multi-finding bead (recall/context silent truncation, DLQ requeue/purge weak safety rails, replay risk disclosure, plus an appended rendering-safety finding) -- each sub-finding is individually testable, but this bead as a unit doesn't reduce to one AC; needs splitting or a table-driven test per sub-finding before it can be called fully executable.

title: Telemetry/CAGG findings: assembly_stats_1h sums cumulative counters (~60x inflated), current_device_state never refreshed, post-import CAGGs wrong-by-construction, freshness monitor itself broken
description:
Batch of findings from the 2026-08-10 telemetry/continuous-aggregate audit (schema convergence engine itself already separately audited; this covers runtime data correctness):

1. assembly_stats_1h (crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs:3032-3036) does SUM((payload->>'total_completed')::bigint) etc on fields that are LIFETIME cumulative atomics (material_assembler/mod.rs:103-113, snapshot()=plain load(), no reset, documented 'since service start'). The emitter fires every 60s, so an hour bucket sums ~60 copies of the running total -- the reported number rises even during an hour with zero actual completions. Contrast event_engine_batch_stats_1h (apply.rs:3105-3111) in the SAME file, which correctly uses MAX for cumulative fields -- the correct pattern is understood elsewhere and just wasn't applied here.

2. current_device_state (apply.rs:2947-2958) is a plain materialized view that is NEVER REFRESHED in production -- the only REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW in the whole tree is a test file. docs/architecture.md:494 claims it is 'refreshed explicitly' but no systemd timer/xtask/sinexctl command/cron does this anywhere. On the upcoming fresh rebuild, apply runs against an empty DB so the MV populates empty and STAYS empty forever -- the handler and MCP tool will silently return nothing.

3. current_device_state also repeats a stale-order bug already fixed for current_health (ORDER BY unit_name, ts_coided DESC instead of ts_orig DESC NULLS LAST, ts_coided DESC) -- post-import, ts_coided=import order, so 'current' state resolves to whichever row got the largest UUIDv7, not the actually-latest occurrence.

4. All 10 CAGGs bucket on time_bucket(..., id) i.e. ts_coided/interpretation-time. A wipe-and-reimport mints fresh UUIDv7s for everything, so YEARS of re-imported history will collapse into the import-hour's buckets -- not a gap, a false activity SPIKE. recent_activity_summary (WHERE bucket >= NOW() - 30min) will report decade-old activity as happening right now during the re-import.

5. The Grafana 'Continuous Aggregate Freshness' panel that would catch #4 queries sinex_telemetry.node_stats_1h, a relation that DOES NOT EXIST (the real CAGG is named source_stats_1h) -- the freshness monitor's own query errors, so it can never actually alert on staleness. docs/architecture.md carries the same wrong name.

6. Four telemetry contracts declare RetentionPolicy::Forever (sinex-metrics, sinexd-event-engine-telemetry, sinexd-api-telemetry, sinex-runtime-telemetry, metrics.rs:722,741,760,773) but land in reflection.events, which is hard-dropped at 30 days (apply.rs:1352) -- nothing reconciles the per-contract retention declaration against the actual table-level policy that silently overrides it.
acceptance_criteria: 1. assembly_stats_1h uses MAX for cumulative counter fields, matching the already-correct pattern in event_engine_batch_stats_1h. 2. current_device_state gets an actual refresh trigger (a timer, or refresh-on-write, or documented as needing manual xtask/sinexctl invocation with that command actually built) so it isn't silently empty forever post-rebuild. 3. current_device_state's ORDER BY matches current_health's already-fixed pattern. 4/5. Either CAGGs bucket on ts_orig where meaningful for 'recent activity' semantics, or the freshness monitor is fixed to use the real table name AND actually catches the false-spike case a mass re-import produces. 6. Reconcile per-contract Forever declarations against actual table retention, or document the override as an accepted, deliberate exception.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] 4 independently testable CAGG/telemetry findings (assembly_stats_1h double-counts a cumulative counter, current_device_state never refreshed, post-import CAGG correctness, broken freshness monitor) -- each has a clear before/after SQL assertion. None written.

Deferred writing tests this round -- these are CAGG/continuous-aggregate behaviors needing either real-time-based aggregation windows or manual refresh_continuous_aggregate() calls plus multi-emission-cycle fixtures, more setup than this pass's remaining budget allows. title: Provenance type-safety gaps: serde XOR untested through the real Event shape, Id<T> typing discarded on several Event fields, second hand-rolled encoder drops operation_id
description:
Batch of related type-safety findings from the 2026-08-10 core-invariant audit (the serde/Id<T> levels of CLAUDE.md's claimed 4-level provenance enforcement):

1. No test asserts the serde XOR rejection (builder.rs:465-530, correct in isolation) through the actual #[serde(flatten)] Event shape production ingest uses (admission.rs:903 deserializes Event<JsonValue>, Event.provenance is #[serde(flatten)] per events/mod.rs:90). crate/sinex-primitives/tests/provenance_wire_test.rs only tests bare Provenance, never through the flattened Event wire shape actually used on the hot path. Residual risk: whether serde's FlatMapDeserializer/Content buffering path actually propagates these rejection errors through the flatten boundary is UNPROVEN, not just untested.

2. A second, hand-rolled provenance encoder exists on the publish side: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/nats_publisher.rs:78-151 (ProvenanceFields/destructure_provenance/PublishEvent) duplicates ProvenanceWire instead of serializing Provenance directly. XOR survives (matches on the enum) but PublishEvent has no operation_id field, so Provenance::Derived::operation_id is silently dropped on this wire path (recoverable today only via a separately-carried created_by_operation_id field). Two encoders, one decoder, zero round-trip equality test between them.

3. Event (events/mod.rs:83,86,99,120,146,151,158) untypes several ids the type-enforcement ladder says must stay typed: module_run_id, payload_schema_id, associated_blob_ids, created_by_operation_id, derivation_epoch_id, derivation_lane_id, adjudication_event_id are all bare Uuid instead of Id<T>. created_by_operation_id is the SAME value Provenance::Derived holds as a properly-typed Id<OperationMarker> -- the phantom type is discarded at the copy into Event. adjudication_event_id is an event id stored as a raw Uuid. Combined with pub fn from_uuid (ids.rs:106) and a blanket impl<T> From<Uuid> for Id<T> (ids.rs:151), cross-type casts are a one-liner -- 416 from_uuid-family call sites exist in the crate, so Id<T> prevents ACCIDENTAL direct mixing but does not survive a round-trip through these specific fields.

4. The EventBuilder typestate is a softer gate than its name implies: build() exists only on HasProvenance (builder.rs:126,228), but Event's own fields are all pub (events/mod.rs:43-159), and Event::new_json (mod.rs:315) / DynamicPayload::into_event (payload.rs:209) are public construction bypasses that PRODUCTION code actually uses (automaton/adapter/output.rs:439). What actually holds the XOR guarantee at the Rust type level is that Provenance is a non-Option two-variant enum, not the typestate itself. A raw struct-literal Provenance::Material{offset_start:Some(_), offset_end:None,..} skips build()'s offset-pairing check (builder.rs:238-260), caught only by the DB CHECK at defs/events.rs:332 -- and xtask/src/commands/lint_forbidden.rs:936 forbids raw DerivedOutput literals but nothing forbids raw Event{}/Provenance::X{} literals, despite builder.rs:326-332 documenting them as undesirable.
acceptance_criteria: Item 1: a test exercises the serde XOR rejection through the actual flattened Event wire shape (not just bare Provenance), proving the guarantee survives the flatten boundary. Item 2: nats_publisher's hand-rolled encoder either gets a round-trip test against ProvenanceWire proving equivalence, or is replaced with the shared encoder to eliminate the duplication (and its operation_id gap) entirely. Item 3: the untyped Uuid fields on Event get proper Id<T> types where a natural target type exists (module_run_id -> Id<ModuleRun> or similar, adjudication_event_id -> Id<Event>, etc), closing the round-trip-discards-phantom-type gap. Item 4: a forbidden-pattern lint (matching the existing raw-DerivedOutput-literal precedent) forbids raw Event{}/Provenance::X{} struct literals outside the builder module itself.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Both findings (serde XOR untested through the real flattened Event wire shape; nats_publisher.rs's hand-rolled PublishEvent silently drops operation_id) are directly testable via wire round-trip assertions. None have tests yet.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2-impl 2026-08-11] Test added for finding 1 (crate/sinex-primitives/tests/provenance_wire_test.rs::event_wire_shape_rejects_neither_material_nor_derived_provenance_through_flatten) -- NOT #[ignore]'d, result pending verification run (may turn out to already pass, in which case this closes the residual-risk gap rather than proving a bug). Finding 2 (PublishEvent silently drops operation_id) investigated and found STALE: PublishEvent.created_by_operation_id IS populated from event.created_by_operation_id (nats_publisher.rs:839), which builder.rs:264 and mod.rs:322 both correctly derive from provenance.operation_uuid() at Event-construction time regardless of path. The claim does not reproduce on current master.
