comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2-impl 2026-08-11] Verification run complete: event_wire_shape_rejects_neither_material_nor_derived_provenance_through_flatten PASSED. Confirms the serde XOR provenance rejection DOES correctly propagate through the real #[serde(flatten)] Event wire shape -- the previously-cited residual risk ("UNPROVEN, not just untested") is resolved as NOT a bug; this is now a real regression test (not #[ignore]'d) guarding that guarantee going forward.

title: Provenance XOR invariant: DB CHECK excluded from schema convergence, and reflection.events/audit.archived_events inherit it only by accident
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit of the core provenance type-invariant enforcement (verifying CLAUDE.md's own claimed 'four enforcement levels' independently). Two related gaps in the DB-CHECK level specifically:

1. crate/sinex-schema/src/converge.rs:743-746 explicitly documents: 'Anonymous CREATE TABLE CHECKs (the XOR provenance invariant) are excluded here; they're set-and-forget at table creation.' The XOR expression itself (defs/events.rs:317-319) is correct, but on any database where it's absent or gets dropped, sinex-schema apply will NEVER restore it -- unlike the 19 other named constraints alongside it in the same table. This is the ONE thing convergence can't repair, and it's the load-bearing provenance invariant the whole 'no both-material-and-derived, no neither' guarantee rests on at the DB layer. Detection exists only via the opt-in xtask schema strict-diff, matching on constraintdef substrings, not semantics.

2. reflection.events and audit.archived_events are both created via LIKE core.events INCLUDING ALL (apply.rs:2754; defs/events.rs:1006-1012) -- a one-shot copy of whatever core.events had AT THAT INSTANT. DECLARED_INLINE_CHECKS (strict_diff.rs:681) only declares expectations for core.events. The reflection DO-block repairs FKs and newer named checks but never the XOR, and the checks it does add are NOT VALID (apply.rs:2857,2870,2882 -- constrain new rows only, not existing ones). The self-observation lane's provenance contract is therefore unverified end-to-end -- exactly the lane this session already found other pollution-class bugs in (sinex-x9i, sinex-f8v).
acceptance_criteria: The XOR CHECK constraint is given a real name and added to the convergence-tracked constraint set (matching the other 19 named constraints on the same table), so sinex-schema apply can actually detect and restore it if dropped. reflection.events and audit.archived_events get the same convergence coverage for this specific constraint as core.events, not just a one-shot LIKE-table copy.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Provenance XOR CHECK excluded from schema convergence -- directly testable via a strict-diff test that drops the CHECK and asserts apply restores it (same pattern as the 19 other named-CHECK convergence tests this bead's description implies already exist for other constraints).

title: MCP read-only enforcement is substring name-matching, not the typed RpcMutability data that already exists
description:
Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe MCP audit. assert_read_only_tool_names (mcp.rs:1662-1671, called at startup :1674) rejects tools whose NAME contains 'stage'/'publish'/'delete'/'archive'/'tombstone'/'finalize'/'actuate' -- a tool named e.g. sinex_ops_start or sinex_events_annotate would pass this check despite not being read-only. read_only:true is a hand-written literal on all ~55 catalog entries (mcp.rs:473,481,489,...), and mcp_test.rs:36 asserts that same literal back -- a test with zero behavioral value, since it mirrors the implementation rather than checking it against anything independent. The correct, already-existing carrier is unused: each catalog entry lists backing_rpc_methods, and every RpcMethod already carries a typed RpcMutability/RpcRole (sinex-primitives/src/rpc/mod.rs:92-99). Nothing checks backing_rpc_methods against RpcMutability::ReadOnly, and nothing verifies a handler only calls its declared methods.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT -- this is a fragility/enforcement-mechanism finding, NOT a currently-exploitable one: the audit independently cross-checked every backing_rpc_methods entry against real role declarations and found ALL of them are genuinely RpcRole::ReadOnly today, including the risky-looking ones (SHADOW_LIST vs SHADOW_CREATE/DELETE, LIFECYCLE_STATUS vs tombstone methods, OPS_LIST/GET, DLQ_PEEK). No read handler MCP reaches performs a DB write or emits events today. The gap is that nothing MECHANICALLY enforces this stays true as new tools get added -- it currently holds by manual discipline, not by a structural check.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only enforcement checks the typed RpcMutability/RpcRole data on backing_rpc_methods (matching this project's own type-enforcement-ladder doctrine: 'pick the strongest affordable level'), not tool-name substrings. mcp_test.rs's assertion is replaced with one that actually verifies something independent of the hand-written literal it currently mirrors.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Substring-name-matching vs typed RpcMutability is directly testable: register a tool whose name happens to contain 'stage'/'publish'/etc but whose typed mutability is read-only, assert it's wrongly rejected (or the inverse: a truly-mutating tool with a clean name wrongly allowed). No test yet.

title: SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_STRICT_VALIDATION defaults to false; sandbox tests set SINEX_VALIDATE_SCHEMAS=false globally
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. config.rs:361-362 defaults SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_STRICT_VALIDATION to false; nixos/modules/default.nix:775-781 also defaults it false -- an operator must opt INTO the safer validation posture rather than opt out of a lenient one. The practical delta of strict mode is exactly one match arm (NoSchema: reject vs accept-with-warning) -- it does NOT affect Invalid (always rejected either way) or the separate SchemaNotFound hole (accepted unconditionally regardless of strict mode, tracked separately). Compounding: xtask/src/sandbox/orchestrator.rs:1180 sets SINEX_VALIDATE_SCHEMAS=false for ALL sandbox test instances, meaning the schema-reject-to-DLQ route has essentially zero live-route sandbox test evidence across this whole test suite.
acceptance_criteria: Either the default flips to strict (safer default, matching the project's own 'no silent data loss, no false claims' doctrine), or the non-strict default is kept but justified explicitly with documented rationale for why permissive-by-default is the intended posture. Separately: at least one sandbox test exercises the actual schema-validation-rejects-to-DLQ route with SINEX_VALIDATE_SCHEMAS enabled, so this code path has real test coverage instead of none.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Current default-false state is trivially assertable; whether the safer default SHOULD be true is an operator policy decision, not a test.

title: Entity-graph medium findings from the 2026-08-10 audit: merge confidence ratchet, dead promotion markers, co-occurrence dedup, supervisor default
description:
Batch of 4 related findings from the 2026-08-10 pre-wipe entity-graph audit, each moderate on its own:

1. Merge ratchets confidence upward with no new evidence: knowledge_graph.rs:997 'let merged_confidence = target.confidence_score.max(source.confidence_score);'. Combined with sinex-jb7x (PkmService entities always land at 1.0), merging any operator-created duplicate promotes the survivor to certainty regardless of the other side's actual support.

2. core.entities.verified_at and external_ids columns are declared (entities.rs:78-79,139-145) but NO Rust code anywhere reads or writes them (EntityRecord itself, knowledge_graph.rs:46-60, omits both columns). 'Canonical vs candidate' status on the entity graph is therefore carried solely by confidence_score, which finding sinex-jb7x makes uninformative -- there is no actual structured promotion marker despite the schema having a column for one.

3. relation_extractor's co-occurrence equivalence_key has no time/window component (relation_extractor.rs:~250: format!("relation:{a}:{b}:co_occurs_with")), unlike the enricher's own time-scoped key. Admission-time equivalence-key dedup therefore permanently suppresses every re-observation of the same entity pair after the first one -- repeated co-occurrence, the actual signal this automaton is supposed to capture, is invisible after the first sighting. Also uses one global singleton scope (CO_OCCURRENCE_SCOPE), so unrelated sources within a 60s window get related at a flat 0.5 confidence regardless of actual relationship.

4. supervisor/mod.rs:29-30 documents 'unset/empty disables every automaton', but automata_enabled_arg (supervisor/mod.rs:554-560) maps None => Some("all") -- the OPPOSITE of the documented behavior. NixOS defaults the entity-chain automata off (nixos/modules/default.nix:2090,2102,2114,2126, 'pq5 dark-substrate') and xtask run core explicitly sets the env var empty (xtask/src/commands/run.rs:1014), so no CURRENT launch path trips this -- but any bare 'sinexd' invocation without going through those specific wrappers would silently re-enable the retired entity-chain automata (whose documented feedback-loop risk is in entity_extractor.rs:110-120), contradicting the code's own doc comment about what 'unset' means.
acceptance_criteria: Each item independently triaged: (1) merge confidence should combine evidence honestly (e.g. weighted by source count, not max-of), or explicitly document why max-of is the intended semantics if it is. (2) verified_at/external_ids either get wired up as the real promotion marker, or are removed if genuinely unused (per this project's own 'unfinished is not obsolete, complete it' doctrine -- check git history/design intent before deleting). (3) co-occurrence equivalence_key gets a time-window component so repeated co-occurrence is observable, matching the enricher's own pattern. (4) automata_enabled_arg's None-case is fixed to match its own documented 'unset disables everything' behavior, or the doc comment is fixed to match the code if the code's behavior is actually intended -- but the current contradiction between doc and code must be resolved one way or the other.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: LOW addendum: entity_enricher.rs:~247 -- when stats.source_event_ids was drained by a prior sweep, falls back to vec![trigger_uuid] and then reports evidence_event_count=1. The parent event is real but the count misrepresents a fallback trigger as genuine evidence. Low severity, fold into this batch's triage rather than a separate bead.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
CRITICAL sharpening 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (Opus): item 3's proposed fix (give the co_occurs_with equivalence_key a time-window component so repeated co-occurrence is observable) is INSUFFICIENT AS WRITTEN, because the relation extractor cannot observe co-occurrence AT ALL today -- there is no second event for that fix to act on.

Root cause: crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_resolver.rs:150-154 -- if let Some(existing) = state.known_entities.get_mut(&key) { existing.last_touched = touch_time; return Ok(()); } -- entity.resolved is emitted EXACTLY ONCE per (entity_type, canonical_name) for the lifetime of the checkpointed state. The relation extractor (relation_extractor.rs:127-129) and enricher (entity_enricher.rs:134-136) BOTH consume only entity.resolved. So the 'co-occurrence window' actually contains newly-DISCOVERED entities, not co-occurring ones -- concretely, two already-known entities appearing together in 1,000 subsequent documents produce ZERO relation events, while two unrelated entities first seen 30 seconds apart get a co_occurs_with edge. The automaton measures first-discovery adjacency and mislabels it co-occurrence. Item 3's equivalence-key fix cannot help until the resolver gate itself changes (emit on every observation, or add a distinct entity.observed event type feeding the extractor).

Second, distinct finding in the same automaton: relation_extractor.rs:177-179's should_close guard (window.len()>=2 required) means a one-entry window can never close on its own -- so the FIRST edge emitted after every quiescent period is a SPURIOUS pair spanning the entire gap (e.g. an entity from Monday paired with one from Friday, timestamped Friday) -- this fires after every quiescence, not as an edge case. Also drain_and_emit_pairs emits pairs by arrival-index only (for i, for j in i+1..), storing a SYMMETRIC predicate (co_occurs_with) as a direction-sensitive equivalence key -- find_paths(B,A) would return nothing where find_paths(A,B) succeeds for the same conceptual edge (though find_paths itself currently has zero callers, so this compounds a currently-latent issue).

Third: entity_enricher.rs:217-218 means occurrence_count is structurally CONSTANT AT 1 forever (one entity.resolved per entity, ever, per the root cause above) -- the module's own docstring promises 'temporal statistics (first/last seen, occurrence count, active-hours histogram)' and the product is a constant. Even after a hypothetical entity-resolver fix, the active_hours histogram would still have exactly one bucket per entity until the resolver-gate root cause is addressed.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Minor dormant finding 2026-08-11 via arbitrary-hardcoded-limits audit: crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/knowledge_graph.rs get_entity_relations/find_entities_by_name hardcode LIMIT 10000/LIMIT 1000 (lines 430,726,754,782,808) with NO pagination parameter at all -- unlike events.query (which correctly exposes next_cursor per sinex-g2dc), a caller cannot even ask for 'the next 10000'. Confirmed via grep that every current caller is a test -- zero production call sites anywhere in crate/sinexd/src, so this is dormant, consistent with the entity-graph-not-fully-wired status already documented across this bead/sinex-jb7x/sinex-nri2/sinex-z3a7. Flagging because the moment this repository method gets a real caller (an MCP/CLI entity-relations surface), a highly-connected personal-capture entity (a frequent project, a person referenced daily across years) could plausibly exceed 10,000 relations after a full historical import, and the cap would silently return a truncated set indistinguishable from complete. Add pagination before wiring any real caller to this method.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Mixed: hardcoded LIMIT 10000/1000 and dead promotion-marker findings are directly testable now. The equivalence_key time-window sizing for co_occurs_with needs a design choice (window size) before it's testable.

title: core.entities.canonical_name is globally unique across entity kinds, contradicting sibling index design and causing update drift
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/entities.rs:98-103 puts .unique_key() on canonical_name with no entity_type in the key; knowledge_graph.rs:325-327 derives it as name.to_lowercase().replace(' ', '_'). A Person 'Paris' and a Location 'Paris' both derive canonical_name='paris' -- hard 23505 constraint violation, not a silent merge (that part is safe), but with real consequences: (1) create_entities_from_source_material runs the whole batch in ONE transaction (pkm.rs:236,285), so a single cross-kind collision aborts every entity in the request; (2) the adjacent uk_entities_type_name index (entities.rs:203-212) is DELIBERATELY partial -- documented as letting 'a new entity reuse the (type, name) pair after the previous occupant was merged away' -- but canonical_name's UNIQUE is NOT partial, so a merged-away row permanently squats its canonical_name and the documented reuse behavior is actually impossible; (3) update_entity (knowledge_graph.rs:526-568) mutates name but never recomputes canonical_name, causing permanent name/canonical_name drift after any rename; (4) find_entities_by_name (knowledge_graph.rs:405-436) matches LOWER(canonical_name)= but canonical_name has spaces replaced with underscores, so a multi-word name search can never match.
acceptance_criteria: Either scope canonical_name uniqueness to (entity_type, canonical_name) matching the sibling partial-index design's intent, or make canonical_name computation and the unique constraint consistent with each other (partial index mirroring uk_entities_type_name's reuse-after-merge semantics). update_entity recomputes canonical_name whenever name changes. find_entities_by_name's lookup normalization matches canonical_name's actual derivation (both apply the same space-to-underscore transform, or neither does).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Globally-unique canonical_name contradicting per-kind sibling design is directly testable via a schema/constraint or repository-level test. None exists yet.

title: DLQ entries silently expire after 72h with no escalation or operator signal
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via a pre-wipe audit sweep. nixos/modules/nats.nix:215 sets maxAge = '72h' on SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_DLQ. A DLQ'd message not requeued within three days is silently deleted by JetStream's own retention policy -- no Postgres projection records the loss, no alert fires, no counter increments. This is a genuine, time-bounded silent-loss path for every DLQ'd event the operator doesn't act on within 72 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Either DLQ entries approaching expiry surface an operator-visible signal (health check, metric, or ops report) before they're silently dropped, or expiring entries get durably archived somewhere else before deletion (matching the project's own 'no silent data loss' doctrine), or the 72h window is deliberately widened with documented rationale if 72h is considered enough operator-response time by design -- but that decision needs to be explicit, not silent.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete: DLQ entries expire after 72h (nats.nix maxAge) with no escalation/operator signal. Testable by asserting the current absence of any escalation event/metric on approaching expiry (using JetStream's own maxAge, not a real 72h wait); not written yet.

title: Build a working regression test for sinex-z9vt's settle_admission_skips redaction path
description:
sinex-z9vt's production fix (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/{persist,prepare,persistence_support}.rs) is landed and verified correct by direct code-path tracing (mirrors the already-proven #2421/sinex-z8p pattern exactly: build a redacted_events map once, thread it to the settle_admission_skips confirmation republish, .expect() on a miss rather than silently falling back to the unredacted image). What's NOT landed: a passing targeted regression test for this specific code path.

An attempt was written (duplicate_confirmation_republish_on_skip_uses_redacted_image in crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/jetstream_consumer_test.rs, since removed) that tried to trigger settle_admission_skips specifically by: publishing a solo event, waiting for it to persist (making it a recognized cached duplicate), then resending it bundled with a genuinely-new sibling in one physical NATS message with a one-shot forced DB failure armed on the sibling's insert. The intent was for persist_plan's plan.events to contain only the new sibling (since the duplicate gets filtered into cached_duplicate_event_ids before persist_plan runs), so the forced failure would drive the whole batch through settle_admission_skips's Err(failure) arm.

This timed out waiting for the duplicate's confirmation republish. Traced the production code path by hand (persist_and_confirm_prepared_batch -> persist_batch_optimized -> admission.rs's filter_cached_batch/persist_plan/fail_once check -> settle_admission_skips) and did not find an obvious logic bug matching the test's premise -- the most likely explanation is a NATS pull-batching/timing assumption in the TEST that doesn't hold in practice (e.g. the two publishes not landing in the same persist_and_confirm_prepared_batch call the way the comment assumed), not a flaw in the fix itself. Did not have time to instrument with SINEX_LOG=debug and trace the actual runtime code path taken to confirm this hypothesis.
acceptance_criteria: A test proves settle_admission_skips's confirmation republish (the Err(failure) branch inside persist_and_confirm_prepared_batch, NOT the success-path duplicate handling which already has coverage) publishes the redacted image, not prepared.event's pre-redaction plaintext. Either fix the trigger mechanism in the removed test's approach (debug with SINEX_LOG=debug tracing to see which code path actually gets exercised), or find a more direct way to reach settle_admission_skips deterministically (e.g. a smaller-scoped unit test around persist_and_confirm_prepared_batch directly rather than going through the full NATS pull-consumer pipeline).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Bead IS a test-writing task: prior attempt (duplicate_confirmation_republish_on_skip_uses_redacted_image) was removed after a timing-assumption failure the bead documents precisely enough to fix and re-land. Not yet re-written.

title: Privacy: derived events (document_parser, entity_extractor) don't inherit parent redaction scope
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via audit sweep. document_parser.rs:181 does std::fs::read_to_string(&file_path) directly (re-reading the RAW file, not the already-redacted parent payload) then emits document.chunked with verbatim chunk text -- explicit comment at :213-216 admits 'Privacy policy is not applied here; the event engine owns admission/redaction decisions.' Chunks land in core.document_chunks via an AFTER INSERT trigger (sinex-schema/src/defs/documents.rs:324). Structural gap: compile_rules keys scopes by (event_source, event_type) (event_engine/policy.rs:502) and rules do not follow provenance -- a rule scoped to the originating source/field never applies to a derived event with a new source id. Same shape in entity_extractor.rs:207-256, which lifts URLs/emails/file paths verbatim into entity.extracted.raw_name under source 'entity-extractor'. Mitigating factor in the DEFAULT posture only: seeded builtin rules are unscoped/global (privacy/catalog.rs:24) -- an operator who writes a source-scoped rule hits this gap.
acceptance_criteria: Either derived events carry forward their parent's effective redaction scope (provenance-aware rule application), or document_parser/entity_extractor read the already-redacted parent payload instead of re-reading raw source material. Documented and tested: a source-scoped redact rule on a parent event's field is proven to also apply (or is explicitly, correctly decided not to apply, with rationale) to a derived chunk/entity event carrying the same sensitive substring.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Reproducing current non-inheritance (derived events dont carry parent redaction scope) is testable. But the correct target behavior (how privacy-rule scoping SHOULD extend across provenance) is an unresolved design question the bead itself does not answer.

title: Privacy: events.query RPC handler returns raw payloads with no disclosure pass
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 via audit sweep. crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/query.rs:26-28 is a bare pool.events().query(query) -- no disclose_* call. events.cards (:111), events.lineage (:30), SSE (sse_handler.rs:343), and DLQ preview (dlq.rs:225) all apply disclose_*; events.query does not. Redaction runs at ADMISSION time, so disclosure is the only mechanism that applies rules added AFTER an event was already stored -- events read via this method stay raw forever regardless of later rule changes. Exposed on the gateway to any :readonly token. Documented as deliberate at crate/sinexctl/src/client/gateway.rs:1006-1008, and sinexctl's own consumers are clean (use event_cards / sanitize on export) -- this is a gateway-surface gap specifically, reachable by any other MCP/API client that calls events.query directly rather than going through sinexctl.
acceptance_criteria: events.query applies the same disclose_* pass every other read surface uses, or the gap is explicitly documented as an accepted, permission-gated exception (e.g. requiring an elevated token scope) rather than silently available to :readonly.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Testable: configure a redaction rule, assert events.query is unredacted while events.cards/lineage on the same row are. No test yet. NOTE: likely duplicate of sinex-hfw8 (same code path/finding, hfw8 is the more hedged/design-question framing) -- flagged to coordinator.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Absorbing sinex-hfw8 (closed as duplicate): same code path (events.query, query.rs:26-28), same finding. hfw8's nuance worth preserving here: this asymmetry may be intentional per project doctrine ('redaction is presentation, not a security boundary') -- the actionable AC is an explicit design confirmation (should events.query disclose like its siblings, or is the current asymmetry deliberate and worth documenting), not necessarily a code fix.

title: atuin source: soft-deleted commands never re-read, deleted secrets stay captured forever
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 during a pre-wipe audit sweep: crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/terminal/atuin_history.rs:196-197 and nixos/modules/sources.nix:812-816 use query="history" with no WHERE deleted_at IS NULL filter. Atuin's real schema carries a deleted_at column (verified against the real local atuin history.db). When the operator runs 'atuin history delete' to purge a secret-bearing command from their own shell history, sinex has ALREADY captured and persisted it as an event before the deletion, and never re-reads the row to learn the deletion happened -- the deleted row is almost always outside the 32-row mutable_trailing_rows re-read window by the time it's deleted. This defeats the operator's own explicit intent to remove a secret from their history. Currently latent on this host (84,990 rows scanned, 0 currently deleted) but a real, live privacy-correctness gap that will persist into the freshly-wiped dataset unless fixed before re-import.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) the query filters WHERE deleted_at IS NULL so soft-deleted rows are never admitted in the first place, or (b) sinex detects a row transitioning to deleted_at != NULL and emits a tombstone/retraction for the already-captured event. Given sinex's own doctrine (privacy/redaction is presentation, not a security boundary; source access controls confidentiality) -- decide and document which of (a)/(b) matches operator intent (deleted commands were never meant to enter sinex at all, vs already-captured-then-deleted needs a tombstone), implement it, and add a test proving a soft-deleted atuin row does not end up as a live, undeleted sinex event.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest: atuin's history table carries a deleted_at column (set by 'atuin history delete'); the source query had no WHERE deleted_at IS NULL filter, so a command the operator explicitly deleted from Atuin (e.g. one that accidentally contained a secret) was still admissible into sinex.

Fix (option (a) of two considered, decided and documented in the module docs): filter WHERE deleted_at IS NULL at admission, in both the parser's baseline_adapter_config and the NixOS module's runtime binding -- a soft-deleted row is never admitted at all. Residual gap explicitly NOT closed and documented: a row already captured before the operator deletes it upstream stays live in sinex. Reasoned choice, not an oversight -- detecting the delete-after-capture transition needs new periodic full-table re-scan infrastructure, out of scope for this bead; sinex's own privacy doctrine ("presentation feature, not a security boundary") supports treating the already-captured case via the existing sinexctl ops tombstone operator workflow rather than inventing new automatic-retraction machinery.

Merged via PR #2598, squash-merged 2026-08-10, commit 36e158b81.

Verification: xtask check -p sinexd pass; xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(atuin)' --no-reuse: 12/12 passed (re-verified independently by me post-rebase onto latest master).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Reclassified task→bug: this describes a genuine correctness/privacy defect (verified during this session's audit), not a task. No behavioral change, metadata correction only.

title: desktop.activitywatch source adapter SQL references stale 'events.datastr' column
description: Discovered 2026-08-10 during the sinex-yslt fresh-rebuild rehearsal: starting the desktop.activitywatch source binding against the REAL local aw-server-rust sqlite DB (~/.local/share/activitywatch/aw-server-rust/sqlite.db) fails immediately with: 'no such column: events.datastr in SELECT rowid, * FROM (SELECT events.id AS rowid, buckets.name AS bucket_id, events.starttime AS started_at, ((events.endtime - events.starttime) / 1000000000.0) AS duration, events.datastr AS data FROM events JOIN buckets ON events.bucketrow = buckets.id ORDER BY events.id) ORDER BY rowid ASC LIMIT 10000 at offset 174'. The source binding crashes on its very first snapshot query (adapter_kind: sqlite_query), meaning the current activitywatch source contract's hardcoded SQL is written against an OLDER aw-server-rust schema than what is actually installed/running on sinnix-prime today -- a genuine schema-drift bug, not a fixture/test issue. This blocks ALL activitywatch ingestion on this host until fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Query the real local aw-server-rust sqlite.db schema (PRAGMA table_info(events)) to find the actual current column name/shape; update the activitywatch source contract's SQL to match; verify by starting the desktop.activitywatch source binding against the real DB and confirming it ingests without error (row counts sane vs the DB's actual event count).
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: events.datastr -> events.data, the one-token fix. Root cause exactly as filed -- the adapter's own doc comment already correctly described the schema, only the generated SQL and required_input_keys() lagged. Independently re-verified by a separate audit lane (direct sqlite query against a copy of the real local aw-server-rust DB, substituting events.data for events.datastr in the exact generated query through the full adapter wrapper, returns correct rows). Merged via PR #2597, squash-merged 2026-08-10. Verification: xtask check -p sinexd pass; xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(activitywatch)' --no-reuse 11/11 passed.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit 2026-08-11] Reclassified task→bug: this describes a genuine correctness/privacy defect (verified during this session's audit), not a task. No behavioral change, metadata correction only.

title: Pre-existing baseline failure: 4 jetstream_consumer DLQ/idempotency tests time out
description: Discovered while verifying sinex-ddy's restart-drain-pacing PR (#2596): jetstream_consumer_routes_db_failures_to_dlq, event_engine::jetstream_dlq_test::test_dlq_cases_table, event_engine::jetstream_idempotency_property_test::test_concurrent_duplicate_submission, and event_engine::jetstream_idempotency_property_test::test_duplicate_event_rejection_smoke all time out waiting on a DB condition (xtask/src/sandbox/timing.rs:522 wait_for_condition). Root cause not yet investigated; could be environmental (DB pool exhaustion under concurrent test load — the test output shows 'Reducing pool size to 12 (from 48) to respect Postgres max_connections budget' warnings) or a genuine logic regression from something that landed earlier this session (sinex-vxu #2593 or sinex-r6d.4 #2592 both touch adjacent admission/settlement code paths).

If a real bug: fixed, with the 4 tests passing deterministically across 3+ runs. If environmental: documented with the actual constraint (e.g. serialize these tests, don't run them under concurrent worktree/lane load) and either fixed or explicitly accepted with rationale.

title: Delete-on-tombstone blob reference check (is_referenced_excluding_material) is a TOCTOU race, not transactionally guarded
description: PR #2570 (fix/sinexd/cas-shared-blob-and-zombie-rows, merged 01963a7ff) fixed the deterministic shared-blob data-loss bug, but the new guard is itself racy. crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/lifecycle.rs handle_tombstone_approve, per orphan material: pool.blobs().is_referenced_excluding_material(...) (one round-trip) -> on Ok(false) -> content_store.drop_content(...) -> pool.blobs().delete_by_id(...) (two more round-trips). None of this is wrapped in a transaction, no row lock (no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on core.blobs), no advisory lock. Between the reference-count check returning false and delete_by_id actually removing the core.blobs row, a concurrent writer can create a brand-new reference to the exact same blob: (a) a concurrent sources.stage --with-bytes call whose ContentStoreManager::check_dedup finds the still-live core.blobs row (BLAKE3 match) and registers a NEW raw.source_material_registry row with optional_blob_id = this blob (this is the intended, designed dedup path -- see is_referenced_excluding_material doc comment on why dedup makes multi-reference legitimate), or (b) a concurrent event insert whose associated_blob_ids includes this blob. raw.source_material_registry.optional_blob_id has ON DELETE SET NULL to core.blobs.id (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/blobs.rs create_blob_foreign_key) -- so delete_by_id silently NULLs the freshly-created sibling materials blob reference with no error, while drop_content has already deleted the CAS bytes. Net effect: the new material (or event) believes it deduped successfully (blob.ingested{deduplicated:true} already published) but the content is permanently gone and the reference silently vanished. This is distinct from the already-tracked sinex-audit-tombstonerace (that bead is about the SAME material regaining a live event reference between orphan-check and delete_material -- a material-identity race); this finding is about a DIFFERENT, newly-created sibling material/event racing the blob-level reference count check that PR #2570 introduced.
acceptance_criteria: The check-then-delete sequence (is_referenced_excluding_material -> drop_content -> delete_by_id) is made atomic with respect to concurrent new references: either wrap the check+delete in a single transaction with a row lock on the core.blobs row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) so a concurrent INSERT referencing optional_blob_id cannot commit while the check-delete is in flight, or re-verify is_referenced_excluding_material immediately before delete_by_id inside the same transaction as the delete. VERIFY: a test that races a concurrent material registration (or event insert with associated_blob_ids) against delete-on-tombstone for the same blob shows the surviving new reference always has retrievable content -- never a live reference pointing at deleted CAS bytes with a silently-nulled blob_id.
notes: Found during independent adversarial review of PR #2570 (pre-wipe hardening pass, 2026-08-02). Narrow race window requiring a concurrent stage/ingest of identical content (or a concurrent event carrying associated_blob_ids for this blob) landing inside the same few-hundred-ms window as an operator-approved tombstone execution touching the last-known reference to that blob -- unlikely but not impossible on a system where replay/backfill and operator tombstone-approval can run concurrently. Silent failure mode (FK ON DELETE SET NULL swallows the dangling reference with no error) makes it worth tracking even though PR #2570 correctly fixed the deterministic (non-race) bug it targeted.

title: MaterialAnchor::StreamFrame/DirectoryEntry anchor_byte is hardcoded to 0, corrupting replay-lineage matching for fs/document.staging/system.systemd
description: Audit wave 3 finding (remaining source-adapters lane). anchor_offsets_for_materialized_record (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:2405-2428) converts MaterialAnchor to anchor_byte: StreamFrame{material_offset,..} uses material_offset (frame_index discarded); DirectoryEntry/GitObject -> anchor_byte=0 UNCONDITIONALLY. journalctl_stream.rs:152-155 sets material_offset:0 literally always (only frame_index, which is discarded, increments). system/systemd.rs declares OccurrenceIdentity::Anchor + CheckpointFamily::Journal (replayable=true) using this SAME adapter -- CONTRAST with system/journald.rs which correctly uses Uuid5From(source, journal_cursor), proof the two files sharing one adapter chose inconsistent identity strategies. file_drop.rs directory-scan records always carry DirectoryEntry{path, content_hash:None} -> anchor_byte=0 for EVERY event; system/udev.rs, fs/parser.rs (source fs), document/staging.rs all declare OccurrenceIdentity::Anchor and consume this adapter. Consequence verified in the consumer: record_event_replacements (replay_writer.rs:23-31,111-191) buckets old+new events by anchor_byte among other fields, then records a FULL CROSS-PRODUCT of old-new event ids per bucket as replacement relations. Non-replayable siblings (dbus/udev/clipboard, checkpoint_family=LiveObservation) have the same anchor degeneracy but its currently inert since replay is gated off for them.

HIGH severity for replayable sources (fs, document.staging, system.systemd) -- corrupts the replay-lineage/audit trail (not archived-event selection itself, which is FK/root-id driven elsewhere), a live reachable path. title: document_chunks projection trigger ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING silently defeats re-redaction on replay -- leaked text stays searchable forever
description: Audit wave 3 finding (document search/FTS lane), the standout finding of that lane. crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/documents.rs:311-335: document.parsed -> core.documents upsert uses ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE (self-heals on replay). But document.chunked -> core.document_chunks uses ON CONFLICT (document_id, chunk_index) DO NOTHING -- does NOT self-heal. document_id is a deterministic UUIDv5, chunk_index is stable, so a replayed document.chunked event for the same document always collides on the same PK and is silently dropped by the projection trigger. Scenario: operator tightens a privacy rule (adds a previously-missed SSN/API-key pattern) and replays affected source material. core.events correctly gets a new, properly-redacted document.chunked row (old archived, replay-not-idempotent doctrine). But the projection DO NOTHING means core.document_chunks.text -- the exact column FTS/trigram search indexes and returns verbatim -- keeps the ORIGINAL under-redacted text forever. Search continues to surface and highlight (ts_headline) the leaked text indefinitely with no staleness signal anywhere in the read path. No document-projection rebuild command exists anywhere in xtask.
acceptance_criteria: The document_chunks projection trigger self-heals on replay (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, matching the documents trigger pattern), or an explicit rebuild command exists and is documented/discoverable for recovering from this exact scenario.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 3 (document search/FTS lane). HIGH severity: silent, no error/staleness signal, defeats the explicit purpose of tightening a privacy rule and replaying to fix it -- the opposite of what the operator intended happens (leaked text stays searchable). Distinct from the closed sinex-audit-docparser-offsets (different bug, byte-offset arithmetic not redaction-persistence).

Since document_id is deterministic (UUIDv5) and chunk_index is stable, a replayed document.chunked event for the same chunk always collided on the composite PK and was silently dropped -- a re-redaction replay never overwrote core.document_chunks.text.

Fix: (1) documents.rs -- document.chunked upsert now DO UPDATE SET across text/byte_offset_start/byte_offset_end/source_anchor_start/source_anchor_end/chunked_event_id, matching the documents.parsed pattern. (3) strict_diff.rs -- fn_document_projection moved from non-goal into DECLARED_FUNCTION_BODIES with markers pinning the DO UPDATE clause, so a future regression back to DO NOTHING is caught.

title: core.blobs rows are never deleted anywhere -- re-ingesting previously-dropped content is silently swallowed by the dedup short-circuit, permanently believing missing content is present
description: Audit wave 3 finding (blob/CAS lane). crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/blobs.rs has NO delete/delete_by_id method at all (confirmed via full method-list read and grep -- zero DELETE FROM core.blobs in production code, only a schema test fixture). Delete-on-tombstone deletes the CAS FILE via drop_content but the core.blobs ROW survives forever -- a zombie row. cas_fsck::check_cas classifies this as status Missing (row present, file absent) on every future fsck run, but nothing consumes/repairs Missing entries -- no code path deletes a stale core.blobs row or reconciles it. WORSE: ContentStoreManager::check_dedup (manager.rs:215-248) runs BEFORE store_file() in both ingest_file and ingest_from_bytes. If the same content is re-ingested later (replay re-reading the same source, operator re-staging the same file), find_blob_by_blake3 finds the zombie row, treats it as a dedup hit, publishes blob.ingested{deduplicated:true}, returns existing (stale) metadata -- store_file is NEVER invoked, bytes are never rewritten to sinex-cas/. The system now believes the blob is present (dedup succeeded, event published) while the CAS file is permanently absent -- no error surfaces until the NEXT retrieve_content/replay attempt. The lifecycle.rs:1058-1063 comment claiming orphan blobs will get cleaned up by the GC sweeper is verified FALSE for this case -- gc::sweep_orphans/cas_fsck::check_cas only remove CAS files with zero matching core.blobs row (stray writes), never touch core.blobs rows that are logically dead or repair rows pointing at now-missing files.
acceptance_criteria: core.blobs gains a real deletion/repair primitive: either delete-on-tombstone also deletes the blob row (once confirmed zero remaining live references, per sinex-audit-cas-shared-blob-delete), or cas_fsck Missing entries get an actual repair/cleanup consumer. Re-ingestion of content whose blob row is a zombie (file absent) either re-writes the file (does not silently trust a stale row) or fails loudly rather than silently succeeding with deduplicated:true.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 3 (blob/CAS lane). HIGH severity: permanent DB-row leak COMBINED with a silent, non-obvious data-loss path on re-ingestion. Distinct root cause from sinex-audit-cas-shared-blob-delete (missing GC/repair primitive vs. missing reference-check-before-delete) but the two compound: fixing only the shared-blob-delete finding still leaves zombie rows from legitimately-fully-dereferenced blobs with no cleanup path.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #2570 (fix/sinexd/cas-shared-blob-and-zombie-rows). AC satisfied via both named mechanisms: (a) BlobRepository::delete_by_id + delete-on-tombstone deletes the core.blobs row in the same pass once is_referenced_excluding_material confirms zero remaining references (verified by tombstone_approve_deletes_blob_row_once_last_reference_is_gone); (b) ContentStoreManager::check_dedup verifies the local CAS file exists before trusting a dedup hit, self-healing zombie rows on re-ingestion via the existing ON CONFLICT (checksum_blake3) upsert instead of silently trusting a stale row (verified by ingest_repairs_zombie_blob_row_by_rewriting_missing_content, ARC also satisfied via re-write not loud-fail per the AC either/or). Verification commands: xtask check -p sinexd -p sinex-db; xtask test -p sinexd -E test(content_store) or test(blob) or test(tombstone) or test(cas).

title: Delete-on-tombstone drops CAS content shared by a still-live sibling material -- deterministic data loss, not a race
description: Audit wave 3 finding (blob/CAS lane). No UNIQUE constraint on raw.source_material_registry.optional_blob_id (FK is ON DELETE SET NULL) -- schema explicitly permits many materials to reference the same blob via content-addressed dedup (core.blobs UNIQUE on checksum_blake3). Every sources.stage --with-bytes call creates a NEW SourceMaterial row even when content_store.ingest_file dedups to an existing blob (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:178-198) -- so two different staged materials can legitimately share one optional_blob_id. Delete-on-tombstone (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/lifecycle.rs:1064-1139): for each orphaned material, reads THAT materials optional_blob_id, looks up the blob row, calls content_store.drop_content(force=true) UNCONDITIONALLY -- never checks whether any OTHER live source_material_registry row (or core.events) also points at the same blob. find_orphan_materials only checks whether the material_id itself is referenced, says nothing about the blob it points to being shared. Scenario: Material A and B staged from identical content (dedup collapses to one blob). A tombstoned/archived, becomes orphan (no live/archived events reference A) even though B is still fully alive pointing at the same blob. Tombstone execution drops the shared CAS file. Bs subsequent retrieve_content/replay now fails with local CAS content missing.
acceptance_criteria: Delete-on-tombstone checks for OTHER live material/event references to the same blob before calling drop_content -- a blob is only actually deleted from CAS when it has zero remaining live references, not just because the specific orphaned material happened to point at it.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 3 (blob/CAS lane). HIGH severity: this fires on ORDINARY SEQUENTIAL delete-on-tombstone whenever dedup has occurred (an expected, designed CAS behavior), not gated by a race window like sinex-audit-tombstonerace -- deterministic data loss, not probabilistic.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #2570 (fix/sinexd/cas-shared-blob-and-zombie-rows). AC satisfied: delete-on-tombstone now checks BlobRepository::is_referenced_excluding_material (other source_material_registry rows + core.events/audit.archived_events via associated_blob_ids) before calling drop_content, so a blob is only dropped when its reference count is genuinely zero. Verified: tombstone_approve_preserves_shared_blob_content_for_live_sibling_material (two materials share a blob; tombstoning one orphan leaves content+row intact and retrievable via the live sibling) and tombstone_approve_deletes_blob_row_once_last_reference_is_gone (unshared blob is genuinely dropped). Verification commands: xtask check -p sinexd -p sinex-db; xtask test -p sinexd -E test(content_store) or test(blob) or test(tombstone) or test(cas).

title: Curation duplicate-workbench: finalized judgments never remove events from core.events -- resolved clusters keep re-surfacing indefinitely
description: Audit wave 3 finding (curation duplicate-workbench lane). handle_curation_list_duplicate_candidates (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs:339-365) derives clusters purely by GROUP BY source,event_type,equivalence_key HAVING COUNT(*)>1 directly against core.events. handle_curation_finalize + CurationFinalizedPayload::from_judgment only ever INSERT a new curation.duplicate_resolution event carrying the decision -- no UPDATE core.events, no archive-cascade call, no status write-back, no automaton subscribed to curation.duplicate_resolution (confirmed zero hits workspace-wide outside curation handler/tests/payload files). The original candidate rows keep their original equivalence_key untouched. Result: the SAME GROUP BY query on the next list call returns the IDENTICAL cluster forever -- the workbench has no memory of adjudicated clusters. Compounds with partial-subset judgments (only event_ids.len()>=2 required, not full cluster membership) -- resolving all-but-one of a 3-way cluster still leaves the whole cluster re-listable. This is the intended downstream recovery surface for sinex-audit-equivrace/sinex-audit-intrabatchsuperseed duplicates -- admissions race creates extra live rows, the workbench is supposed to let an operator clean them up, but resolving via the workbench does not actually remove anything from core.events.

title: IMAP EXPUNGE/deletion is never observed -- ImapSyncRecordKind::Expunge is defined but never constructed
description: Audit wave 3 finding (email/OAuth lane). ImapSyncRecordKind::Expunge (email_imap_sync.rs:142) is defined but has zero producers anywhere in the codebase. NativeImapSyncClient::fetch_with_client (email_imap_sync.rs:315-456) only issues UID FETCH {start}:{end} and reads FetchStream items -- never registers for or drains untagged EXPUNGE/VANISHED(QRESYNC) responses, never re-fetches previously-consumed UIDs to detect deletion. Cursor only ever advances forward (uid_next=last_uid+1), previously-consumed UID ranges are never revisited. Combined with the Gmail finding (sinex-audit-gmail-delete-fabrication), BOTH email provider integrations are structurally incapable of reflecting message deletions.
acceptance_criteria: IMAP sync observes EXPUNGE/VANISHED signals (via IDLE or periodic UID-range re-check) and records deletions, so a message deleted+expunged on the server is not retained indefinitely in the mailbox projection.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 3 (email/OAuth lane). Note (not a bug, verified correct): UIDVALIDITY-reset handling is correct -- forces a full resync via a continuity-gap signal rather than silently reusing stale UIDs.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Disposition: partially deferred. Landed alongside the Gmail fix (sinex-audit-gmail-delete-fabrication) in PR (see that bead / PR link) but IMAP is NOT fixed end-to-end -- leaving this bead open.

What I verified while scoping this:

- `async_imap` 0.11.2 (the vendored version) exposes `Session.unsolicited_responses: channel::Receiver<UnsolicitedResponse>`, and `UnsolicitedResponse::Expunge(u32)` IS real and reachable -- so the "never constructed" gap is fixable in principle. But that variant only carries a bare IMAP sequence number, never a UID: this crate version has no QRESYNC `VANISHED` variant.
- Resolving seqno -> UID correctly needs: (1) a UID snapshot (e.g. `UID SEARCH 1:*`) taken immediately before each fetch cycle, (2) draining EXPUNGE events in arrival order and resolving each against a shrinking copy of that snapshot (RFC 3501 7.4.1's immediate-decrement rule). That's the standard correct algorithm, but this codebase has zero protocol-level test coverage of `NativeImapSyncClient::fetch_with_client` to validate it against (crate/sinexd/tests/runtime/email_imap_sync_adapter_test.rs only fakes the `ImapSyncClient` trait ABOVE the native client, never a raw IMAP transcript) -- building that harness from scratch is real, separate scope.
- Even with a correctly resolved UID, `core.email_mailbox_projection` has no UID-indexed lookup today. `message_key()` (crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/email_mailbox_projection.rs) resolves rows by `message_id` (the RFC822 header -- unavailable for an expunged message with no re-fetch) or `raw_material_id`+`source_file`+anchor (a random per-`SourceRecord` material id, NOT stable across a message's received-vs-expunged observations). So even a perfectly resolved UID deletion event can't reliably find the row to remove without a schema addition (a UID-indexed column/index on the projection, or an equivalent persisted uid<->message_key map).

Given the mission's explicit permission to land what's clean and defer the rest rather than force a rushed IMAP fix, I did not attempt a partial/unverified UID-resolution path here -- getting deletion semantics subtly wrong (deleting or failing to delete the wrong row) is worse than leaving the gap explicit. Filed as follow-up scope (attempted to open a dedicated tracking bead for it via `bd create`, but the write path is currently broken in this checkout -- `Error 1105: Field 'id' doesn't have a default value` on every create/comment-adjacent write; this comment itself is going through `bd comment` per the documented workaround). The follow-up scope, for whoever picks this up:

1. Build a protocol-level test harness (fake AsyncRead/AsyncWrite duplex IMAP transcript) for `NativeImapSyncClient::fetch_with_client`.
2. Implement the UID-snapshot + decrement-resolution algorithm for untagged EXPUNGE, construct real `ImapSyncRecordKind::Expunge` records with resolved UIDs.
3. Add a UID-indexed lookup path to `core.email_mailbox_projection` (new column(s) + index or equivalent) so an IMAP deletion event (wired through the same `email.message.deleted` payload/event type this PR adds for Gmail) can actually find and remove the right row.

Gmail side (sinex-audit-gmail-delete-fabrication) is fully fixed in the same PR: `parse_gmail_provider_record` now branches on `history_change_kind`, deleted history entries emit `email.message.deleted` instead of a fabricated `email.message.received`, and the mailbox projection has a real DELETE path (`EmailMailboxProjectionRepository::apply_deletion_event`) wired into the rebuild operation.

title: Gmail history message-deleted entries are fabricated into email.message.received events -- no deletion is ever recorded
description: Audit wave 3 finding (email/OAuth lane). fetch_history_page (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/email_gmail_api.rs:390-421) tags each history entry with history_change_kind (message-added/message-deleted/labels_added/labels_removed) via gmail_history_record. But parse_gmail_provider_record (crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/email.rs:281-309) only branches on provider_record.kind (Message|History) -- NEVER reads history_change_kind. Every History entry, added OR deleted, is emitted as email.message.received. No email.message.deleted event type exists anywhere (confirmed zero hits across payloads/email.rs, event_contracts/email.rs, schemas/v1/email/*.json). The mailbox projection upsert (email_mailbox_projection.rs:117-154) is accumulate-only (GREATEST/COALESCE/jsonb_agg DISTINCT) -- nothing can decrease. Even the rebuild-projection operator op replays stored core.events and cant repair this since the deletion fact was never captured as an event in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: A Gmail-deleted message is recorded as a real deletion signal (a distinct event type, or at minimum NOT fabricated as email.message.received) and the mailbox projection correctly reflects the deletion.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 3 (email/OAuth lane). Distinct from and upstream of sinex-new8 (tombstone/purge cascade, which assumes a ref exists to purge) -- here the providers own deletion signal is mismapped so no ref to purge ever gets created.

title: jetstream_dlq_test.rs leaks a spawned consumer task holding a DB pool connection past test teardown -- contributing cause of the recurring sinex_test_pool_N flake
description: Audit wave 2 finding (test-suite-quality lane), explains a pattern this session hit repeatedly (sandbox pool connection failures in PRs #2549/#2550/#2553/#2556/#2557). crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/jetstream_dlq_test.rs:190, test_dlq_cases_table: let _consumer_handle = tokio::spawn(async move { consumer.run().await }); -- consumer captures pool.clone() (the sandbox-issued ctx.pool). title: Replay cancel does not stop in-flight source scan -- orphaned events keep landing after cancellation is reported
description: Audit wave 2 finding. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/dispatch.rs:72-74 (execute_dispatched_scan) calls worker.scan(...) with no cancellation token/interrupt channel -- grep across the runtime/stream scan path finds zero cancel-message handling anywhere. crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:631-670 polls operation state every 250ms; on observing Cancelling/Cancelled it just returns a Cancelled error LOCALLY -- never signals the source runtime. The actual scan worker (a separately spawned tokio task) keeps running to completion on its own, continuing to emit real events tagged created_by_operation_id=<the cancelled op> into core.events. On this path, if emitted_count>0 at cancel-detection time, restore_archived_cascade is false (archived originals stay archived) while record_event_replacements (linking old->new) is only called on the Ok success branch -- never reached. Existing test coverage (replay_execution_returns_cancelled_operation_when_cancelled_midflight, tests/abort.rs) only exercises cancellation via a FAKE source that acks but never emits progress/events -- never tests cancellation while a real scan is actively mid-scan and emitting, so this gap has zero coverage in either direction.
acceptance_criteria: Cancel actually propagates to and stops the in-flight source-side scan (a cancellation token/channel threaded into worker.scan), not just flips operation state locally while the scan keeps running. A test exercises cancellation against a source that IS actively emitting events mid-scan (not the ack-only fake) and confirms no further events land with that operations created_by_operation_id after cancel is observed, and that archived originals are correctly restored if the cancelled operation never completed successfully.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 2 (replay control lane). HIGH severity, novel finding distinct from sinex-68c.4/sinex-audit-tombstonerace/sinex-q6js. Concrete impact: operator cancels a large historical replay expecting it to stop, but the scan silently keeps running and landing real events for its full original duration with no operator-visible signal that work is still in flight -- sinexctl replay status would show Cancelled while events keep landing.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2576: cancel now propagates via SourceScanCancel/watch-channel from ReplayExecutionEngine through RuntimeRunner into execute_dispatched_scan (tokio::select! against worker.scan), archived cascade restore is unconditional on genuine cancellation, and record_event_replacements now covers the cancelled-with-partial-emission path. New tests: runtime/stream/runner/tests/cancel.rs and replay_execution_cancel_midflight_stops_emission_and_restores_cascade. Anti-vacuity verified.

title: sinexctl panics on non-ASCII multi-byte truncation in tombstone list, watch, and xtask-stderr display paths
description: Audit wave 2 finding, coordinator-verified core claim. Three sites do unguarded byte-index string slicing for display truncation, which panics if the cut point falls mid-UTF8-codepoint: (1) crate/sinexctl/src/commands/lifecycle.rs:781-793 format_tombstone_list_table -- op.reason (unrestricted --reason free text, no length/charset validation anywhere) sliced at [..27], op.created_at sliced at [..19] with NO length guard at all. HIGH severity: this is the audit/list view for the permanent-deletion tombstone feature -- a single non-ASCII reason string (any operator using non-English text) crashes ops lifecycle tombstone list entirely, hiding the state of every tombstone operation until worked around out-of-band, undermining the documented no-silent-deletion control surface. (2) crate/sinexctl/src/commands/shortcuts.rs:988 (WatchCommand) -- live event summary text (window/browser titles, shell commands -- routinely non-ASCII) sliced at [..57], crashes the live watch session on any non-ASCII title over 60 bytes. (3) crate/sinexctl/src/commands/verify/baseline.rs:540 -- xtask subprocess stderr sliced at [..500], lower likelihood (stderr usually ASCII) but same defect class. Confirmed by cross-reference: replay.rs:1040 correctly guards the identical created_at field (if len()>19 { &s[..19] }) showing the author knew the hazard elsewhere but missed lifecycle.rs; several OTHER short-id helpers in the codebase (fmt/table.rs, trace.rs, sources.rs, ops/debt.rs) correctly use .min(len()) guards.
acceptance_criteria: All three sites use UTF-8-safe truncation (e.g. floor_char_boundary once stabilized, or a manual scan back from the byte limit to the nearest char boundary, matching the .min(len())-guarded pattern already used correctly elsewhere in this codebase). A test with a multi-byte-boundary-straddling non-ASCII string (e.g. Japanese/Cyrillic/emoji text) for each of the three fields (reason, live-event summary, stderr) proves no panic and produces a sensible truncated display.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 2 (sinexctl CLI lane). Coordinator spot-verified the lifecycle.rs:781-793 core claim directly against source. This is a real, easily-reproducible operator-facing crash on a data-deletion audit path -- worth prioritizing given any operator using non-English reason text would hit it immediately.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2561 (merged 4a19a13c). All 3 sites (lifecycle.rs tombstone reason/created_at, shortcuts.rs watch summary, baseline.rs xtask stderr) now use a shared truncate_str_boundary_safe() helper instead of raw byte-index slicing. 5 new tests with non-ASCII boundary-straddling fixtures prove no panic; anti-vacuity verified by reverting each site and observing the panic before restoring. title: DirectoryWalkAdapter::cursor_after persists modified_ms:0 sentinel, defeating its own dedup contract -- every file re-read and re-parsed on every poll forever
description: Audit wave 1 finding (source-adapters lane). crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/directory_walk.rs:372-394. open() correctly compares (size_bytes, modified_ms) against the stored cursor. But cursor_after() -- whose output becomes the PERSISTED checkpoint -- always writes modified_ms:0 (line 389), with a comment claiming the runtime merges cursors and uses the live FS value for comparison; no such correction exists anywhere else in the runtime (grep modified_ms finds only this one write site). merge_cursor_update/merge_cursor_json_update just recursively overlay JSON, never re-query the filesystem. Consequence: on the very next poll, every previously-processed files fingerprint is {size, modified_ms:0} vs the live {size, real_mtime_ms} -- never equal -- so EVERY file the adapter has ever seen is treated as changed and fully re-read/re-parsed on EVERY poll, forever, for any Continuous-shape source built on this adapter. directory_walk_test.rs test_cursor_based_dedup_skips_unchanged_files calls fingerprint() directly on live metadata, never cursor_after() -- the actual runtime path (open -> cursor_after -> persist -> open) is untested. Affected: terminal.asciinema (the only Continuous consumer; knowledgebase-vault/docs-library-index are OnDemand, wasteful-but-bounded not perpetual).
acceptance_criteria: cursor_after() persists the REAL mtime (re-stat, or thread the real value through SourceRecord/MaterializedAdapterRecord instead of discarding it), not a modified_ms:0 sentinel. A test exercises the actual runtime path (open -> cursor_after -> persist -> reopen) and shows an unchanged file is correctly skipped on the second poll, not re-read.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (source-adapters lane). Root-cause bug in a SHARED adapter (affects any future Continuous source built on DirectoryWalkAdapter, not just asciinema). Downstream corruption is likely masked by asciinema content-derived occurrence keys absorbing re-emission as duplicates at admission, but this is a standing, silent, unbounded resource drain scaling with total captured corpus size on every poll -- will get worse as the asciinema archive grows post-rebuild.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2558 (merged 500b5c6138658f136f45e6c6d11321c8dfa08591). cursor_after() now threads the real FileFingerprint (incl. modified_ms) through SourceRecord.metadata from open()s scan instead of persisting a modified_ms:0 sentinel. AC satisfied: (1) cursor_after persists real mtime -- verified via serde round-trip from metadata; (2) test exercises actual runtime path open->cursor_after->persist->reopen (test_persisted_cursor_after_skips_unchanged_files_on_reopen), anti-vacuity confirmed by reverting fix and observing test FAIL (2 re-emitted vs 0 expected). Verification: xtask check -p sinexd (pass), xtask test -p sinexd -E test(directory_walk) or test(asciinema) (12 passed 0 failed), pre-push drift guard passed.

title: Source continuity reports do 31+ sequential unindexed full-hypertable scans of core.events, reachable via a live API/MCP handler
description:
Audit wave 1 finding (performance lane). crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/continuity.rs:103-119 (observed_families) and :156-235 (build_report, two near-identical CTEs) all filter core.events on split_part(e.source, . ,1) = . EVENTS_REQUIRED_INDEXES has plain-column indexes on source (ix_events_source_ts_coided etc) but NONE is an expression index on split_part(source, ,1), so Postgres cannot use any of them for this predicate -- full chunk-by-chunk scan. observed_families has NO time bound at all on core.events (only sm.staged_at is filtered) -- genuinely unbounded. list_continuity_reports loops over every returned family and calls build_report, which re-runs the same split_part-filtered scan TWICE more per family (agg query + chunk_rows query). On a multi-million-row hypertable with ~15 observed source families: 1 + 15*2 = 31 sequential near-full-table scans per call. Reachable directly via the sources.continuity API handler (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:1868) and the sinex_source_continuity MCP tool -- operator/agent-triggered read path, not a rare background job.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/continuity.rs:103-119 (observed_families) -- filters core.events on split_part(e.source, '.', 1) with no expression index covering that predicate, and no time bound at all.
2. Read continuity.rs:156-235 (build_report) -- two near-identical CTEs re-run the same split_part-filtered scan per family.
3. Call the sources.continuity API handler (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/sources.rs:1868) or the sinex_source_continuity MCP tool against a multi-million-row core.events hypertable with ~15 observed source families.
4. Observe 1 + 15*2 = 31 sequential near-full-table scans triggered by one operator/agent-facing call.
acceptance_criteria: Either an expression index (CREATE INDEX ON core.events (split_part(source, ,1))) supports the predicate, or the family-list/per-family aggregation is computed from a smaller/precomputed source (e.g. raw.source_material_registry.source_identifier) instead of joining through the full events hypertable. A call against a populated multi-million-row events table completes without a full-table-scan query plan.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (performance lane). HIGH severity on a populated production DB -- this handler is exactly the kind of thing an operator or MCP-driven agent would call routinely post-rebuild to check source health, and it will get slower with every event ingested.
close_reason:
## Closure Evidence Manifest

| AC | Evidence kind | Surface | Evidence | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | runtime | `crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs` and `crate/sinex-db/tests/repositories_continuity_seams.rs` | The expression index `ix_events_source_family` is converged on `core.events`; missing physical chunk copies are repaired via `timescaledb_information.chunks`. The test seeds 201 events, applies convergence, pins planner settings and the EXPLAIN query to one connection, and asserts the JSON plan names the index. | `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinex-db -E 'test(source_family_filter_uses_an_index_not_a_seq_scan)' --impact-mode=off` | Satisfied |

### Verification commands

- `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinex-db -E 'test(source_family_filter_uses_an_index_not_a_seq_scan)' --impact-mode=off` — passed (1 test).

- AC: "Either an expression index... supports the predicate, or the family-list/per-family aggregation is computed from a smaller/precomputed source" -- SATISFIED via option (a). Added ix_events_source_family, an expression index on split_part(source, '.', 1), created in apply::configure_timescaledb and registered in EVENTS_REQUIRED_INDEXES (crate/sinex-schema/src/apply.rs).
- AC: "A call against a populated multi-million-row events table completes without a full-table-scan query plan" -- SATISFIED for the dominant repeated query (build_report's two split_part(source,'.',1) = $1 CTEs, called twice per family, i.e. 30 of the reported 31 scans per list_continuity_reports call). title: entity_resolver/entity_enricher hold unbounded in-memory checkpoint maps despite the exact OOM class being fixed nearby
description: Audit wave 1 finding. crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_resolver.rs:34-36 (known_entities: HashMap) and entity_enricher.rs:33-35 (entities: HashMap<String, EntityStats>) grow unboundedly -- every unique entity ever seen stays resident forever, no TTL/LRU/eviction. relation_extractor.rs in the same directory explicitly documents having been fixed for exactly this class (active_subject_states bounded to 1024, stalest eviction, per sinex-uzc closure note) -- the sibling automata never got the same treatment.

comments.text: Fixed via PR #2566 (merged, squash commit 1467a653096a258e4596bcc1d2eabd97d885b8ad). Root cause re-verified against master: the bead's citation of relation_extractor.rs as the precedent was stale/wrong -- relation_extractor.rs uses a bounded co-occurrence window (MAX_WINDOW_ENTITIES), not a stalest-eviction map. The actual precedent is interval_lift.rs's active_subject_states (sinex-uzc, capped 1024 with stalest eviction). Followed that pattern for both maps: entity_resolver.known_entities -> HashMap<String, KnownEntity{entity_id, last_touched}>, bounded 20_000, stalest-touch eviction, warn! debt marker; eviction is safe because a re-resolved entity recomputes the same deterministic UUIDv5 id/equivalence key, caught by admission-time equivalence-key dedup. entity_enricher.entities bounded 20_000, prefers evicting a non-dirty stalest entity (protects about-to-be-emitted snapshots), falls back to globally stalest if all dirty, same warn! shape. Bound is 20_000 not interval_lift's 1024 because these are cumulative all-time caches, not small concurrently-open sets. New tests: known_entities_map_is_bounded_under_high_cardinality, entities_map_is_bounded_under_high_cardinality (insert bound+500 distinct entities, assert map stays <= bound, stalest evicted, newest retained -- anti-vacuity: removing the eviction guard fails both). title: Intra-batch equivalence-key pre-pass is stale, silently dropping same-batch revisions
description: Audit wave 1 finding. admit_intent_bytes (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:963-1006) builds live_by_key from a single DB read ONCE before processing any event in the intent, then loops over intent.events comparing every event against that same static map -- never updated as earlier events in the same loop are decided. apply_supersession (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs:79-100,435-464) pre-validates the archive target still exists in core.events before archiving; if an earlier event in the SAME batch already archived it, the count mismatches, execute_cascade_archive returns Err, apply_supersession returns false, and the caller unconditionally suppresses the later candidate as an ordinary OccurrenceDuplicate (indistinguishable from a legitimate duplicate in telemetry). Net effect: only the FIRST event among same-equivalence-key competitors in one EventIntent/NATS message can ever apply under SupersedeOnChange; every subsequent same-key revision in that batch is silently dropped with no retry (ACKed via ChildOutcome::Safe).
acceptance_criteria: Multiple same-equivalence-key revisions within one batch (EventBatcher: 100 events/1s) under SupersedeOnChange all apply in order -- the live map used for equivalence classification is updated in-loop as each event is decided, not read once per intent. VERIFY: a test that emits 3 same-key revisions in one intent shows the FINAL revision live, not the first, and no silent OccurrenceDuplicate suppression of genuine later revisions.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (identity/provenance lane), interpretation-plane analogue of the r6d/vxu emission-durability gaps but at the admission/equivalence layer. Risk grows as more sources adopt SupersedeOnChange (currently AW window.active/browser.tab.active/afk.changed per sinex-h3g); the h3g fix (mutable_trailing_rows re-read) increases exactly the batching pattern that triggers this bug.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2584 (fix/sinexd/intrabatch-equivalence-key-supersession). admit_intent_bytes now updates live_by_key in-loop as each event in an intent is decided, and same-key runs within a batch collapse to a single winner (only the LAST revision applies, superseding the runs original pre-batch live row at most once); earlier same-batch siblings are demoted to a new AdmissionRejectionKind::SupersededWithinBatch, distinct from OccurrenceDuplicate, and never reach apply_supersession. Verification: xtask check -p sinexd passed; new test supersede_on_change_intrabatch_multiple_revisions_only_final_applies (crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/admission_test.rs) emits 3 same-key revisions in one EventIntent under SupersedeOnChange and shows decisions[0..1]=Suppressed(SupersededWithinBatch), decisions[2]=Superseded{target: original live row}; passed. Broader admission/supersede suite: 43 passed, 1 failed (scope_invalidation_outputs_preserve_payload_for_policy_admission, unrelated pre-existing gap in a different subsystem, reproduces identically in isolation, last touched by unrelated PR #2527, not fixed here).

title: h3g-class mutation-declared-but-never-reread pattern extends to browser history and atuin shell history
description: Audit wave 1 finding, extends closed sinex-h3g (PR #2541, AW-specific fix) to sibling sources. grep for CheckpointFamily::MutableSnapshot across crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts finds 5 sources: browser/history.rs, desktop/activitywatch.rs (fixed), terminal/asciinema.rs, terminal/atuin_history.rs, terminal/fish_history.rs. Only activitywatch.rs sets mutable_trailing_rows. browser/history.rs:170-172,241-247,394-409 reads Chromium visit_duration via plain ROWID cursor -- Chromium updates visits.visit_duration in place as a visit progresses, finalized only on navigate-away/tab-close; a row scanned mid-visit captures a low/zero duration and is never re-read. terminal/atuin_history.rs:87-96,145 reads via the same default ROWID cursor; Atuin inserts a history row on command START (duration/exit unset) and UPDATEs the same row on command FINISH -- a row scanned mid-command captures duration_ns=0/exit_code=0 and is never re-read once the command completes. fish_history.rs has no duration/mutable column (not affected); asciinema.rs uses directory backing-store (different mechanism, not assessed).
acceptance_criteria: browser.history and terminal.atuin_history either opt into mutable_trailing_rows (h3g mechanism) or an equivalent re-read/supersession strategy, so visit_duration/duration_ns/exit_code are not permanently frozen at scan-moment values for rows still mutating at scan time. VERIFY: fixture that grows a visit_duration/atuin duration after first scan shows the final stored event reflects the grown value exactly once (same fixture shape as h3g's AW test).
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (identity/provenance lane). Same construct-validity lens as h3g: captured duration = duration-at-scan-moment, not data loss or corruption, just systematically wrong for any row still mutating at scan time -- browser history and shell history are both extremely common capture-time states (an open tab, a running command).
