title: Concurrent admission race can create two live rows for one equivalence_key occurrence
description: Audit wave 1 finding, coordinator-verified. resolve_equivalence (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs:606-622, single-event path) and the batch pre-pass (:963-990) both do a plain SELECT against find_live_by_equivalence_key outside any transaction, then persist_plan/insert_stream_batch_into only guards ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING (confirmed: persistence.rs has zero ON CONFLICT (equivalence_key,...) clauses, only id). core.events has ix_events_equivalence_key as a plain index (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/events.rs:604-608), not a unique constraint. Two admissions of the same occurrence within a narrow window (replay overlapping live capture, or duplicate redelivery racing a fresh emission) can both see EquivalenceOutcome::Fresh and both insert, producing two live rows for one occurrence -- violating the documented one-live-interpretation-per-occurrence invariant that SupersedeOnChange/SuppressDuplicate (sinex-n9a/y8v/ecy) assume holds. This is distinct from sinex-ecy (fixed: key derivation was processing-order-based) -- this is the admission MECHANISM having a check-then-insert gap with no DB backstop.
acceptance_criteria: Either a DB-level partial unique index on (equivalence_key) WHERE status=live (or equivalent single-live-row enforcement) rejects/reconciles the second concurrent insert, or admission serializes equivalence-key resolution+insert under a single transaction/advisory lock so two concurrent admissions for the same key cannot both observe Fresh. VERIFY: a test with two concurrent admission calls sharing an equivalence_key produces exactly one live row, not two.
notes: Discovered by pre-wipe audit wave 1 (concurrency/TX lane), coordinator spot-verified the ON CONFLICT and index claims directly against source. Doctrine explicitly accepts fail-open dedup as intentional (missed suppression), but two genuinely live rows for one occurrence is a step further than fail-open implies and is not caught anywhere downstream.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2568 (fix/sinexd/equivalence-key-admission-race): per-key pg_advisory_xact_lock in insert_stream_batch_into (all 3 insert strategies) closes the check-then-insert race at the physical write boundary. AC: partial unique index on equivalence_key -- MISFRAMED, verified infeasible on a TimescaleDB hypertable (only indexes including partition key id can be unique); used the advisory-lock-serialization alternative the AC also permitted instead. AC: concurrent test proving exactly one live row -- SATISFIED, concurrent_equivalence_key_race_yields_exactly_one_live_row in crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence_test.rs, tokio::sync::Barrier-forced genuine concurrency, verified fails without the fix and passes with it. Verification commands: xtask check -p sinex-db; xtask check -p sinexd; xtask test -p sinex-db -E test(concurrent_equivalence_key_race) (1 passed); xtask test -p sinexd -E test(/admission/)_or_test(/equivalence/)_or_test(/supersede/) (43 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure confirmed via baseline comparison).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Fixed in PR #2568 (fix/sinexd/equivalence-key-admission-race): a per-key transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock in sinex-db's insert_stream_batch_into (all 3 insert strategies: QueryBuilder, COPY, derived per-chunk) serializes recheck-and-insert for equivalence-keyed rows. DB-level unique index on equivalence_key alone was verified infeasible -- core.events/reflection.events are TimescaleDB hypertables and only indexes including the partition key (id) can be unique, and id differs by definition between the two racers. Concurrent regression test (concurrent_equivalence_key_race_yields_exactly_one_live_row, tokio::sync::Barrier-forced) added in persistence_test.rs; verified it fails (2 live rows) with the guard disabled and passes with it enabled. Zero added cost on the hot non-keyed path (is_empty() short-circuit before any lock/query; QueryBuilder site only opens an explicit tx when a batch actually carries a keyed row). Verification: xtask check -p sinex-db, xtask check -p sinexd, xtask test -p sinex-db -E 'test(concurrent_equivalence_key_race)' (1 passed), xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(/admission/) or test(/equivalence/) or test(/supersede/)' (43 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure confirmed via baseline comparison: scope_invalidation_outputs_preserve_payload_for_policy_admission, sinex-0vx.8 declaration_id registry, nothing to do with this change). title: Duplicate SourceFactoryEntry registration: media.audio-transcript / media.screen-ocr dispatch is link-order-undefined
description:
SOURCE_FACTORY_REGISTRY (crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_factory.rs:41-48) is a HashMap keyed only by source_id, populated via map.entry(entry.source_id).or_insert(entry.factory_fn) -- explicitly documented as "first registration wins (consistent with link order)" (line 40), unenforced (no panic/reject on collision).

Both media.audio-transcript and media.screen-ocr have TWO SourceFactoryEntry registrations colliding on the same source_id:
1. The staged FileContentDropAdapter parser, auto-registered via #[derive(SourceMeta)]s default register_factory: true (crate/sinex-macros/src/source_meta.rs:85, source_registration.rs:401-415), using the struct-level adapter = "FileContentDropAdapter" attribute (media.rs:39, 116).
2. The live driver (MediaAudioCaptureDriver / MediaScreenCaptureDriver) via its own explicit register_source! call (landed #2174/#2175, 2026-06-27).

Whichever wins link order is genuinely undefined/uncontrolled. sinexd source run media.audio-transcript (the actual systemd-unit-level dispatch) could silently resolve to either the staged parser or the live driver -- the per-binding SourceRuntimeBinding.subject/mode does not select this, since lookup is source-id-only.

Discovery: found by sinex-amg2s agent (2026-08-01) while triaging a post-merge automated-review finding on PR #2543. Pre-existing since #2174/#2175, NOT introduced by #2543 -- #2543 only changed the proposed display/coverage flag (Site 2), not Site 3 factory registration. #2543 raises the operational stakes though: it now tells operators these live-capture modes are backed and ready, when actual dispatch is link-order-dependent.

Full investigation + file:line citations: https://github.com/Sinity/sinex/pull/2543#issuecomment-5152133763

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_factory.rs:41-48 -- SOURCE_FACTORY_REGISTRY is a HashMap populated via .entry(source_id).or_insert(factory_fn), documented as "first registration wins (consistent with link order)", unenforced.
2. Confirm both media.audio-transcript and media.screen-ocr have two SourceFactoryEntry registrations colliding on the same source_id: the auto-registered staged FileContentDropAdapter parser (via #[derive(SourceMeta)]'s default register_factory: true) and the explicit register_source! call for the live driver (landed #2174/#2175).
3. Run sinexd source run media.audio-transcript (or media.screen-ocr) -- observe dispatch resolves to whichever registration happened to link first, which is not controlled by SourceRuntimeBinding.subject/mode since lookup is source-id-only.
design: Undecided, needs a design pass. Candidate directions: (1) mode-aware factory resolution (dispatch selects between staged/live based on runtime mode, not just source_id); (2) eliminate the duplicate -- staged parser and live driver share one factory keyed by invocation args; (3) split live/staged halves into distinct source_ids.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh sinexd boot with both media.audio-transcript and media.screen-ocr live drivers registered resolves source run dispatch to the intended live driver deterministically (not link-order-dependent); a regression test asserts SOURCE_FACTORY_REGISTRY has no source_id with more than one contributing registration, OR (if intentional layering is kept) that resolution is explicitly mode-aware and covered by a test that would fail if link order flipped.
notes: Filed via bd sql direct INSERT workaround (bd create/close/update broken this session -- events.id has no default, DB schema 1.1.0 vs CLI 1.0.4 mismatch).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete silent-first-wins registration collision in SOURCE_FACTORY_REGISTRY; testable via a duplicate-registration test asserting an explicit error instead of silent override.

title: pre-existing test fixtures across 7 sinex-db test files never updated for events_derived_requires_product_class (sinex-8cr.2)
description:
Discovered while resurrecting `crate/sinex-db/tests/schema/` (sinex-xjx8) and running the broader `-p sinex-db` suite as its final verification step: at least 18 pre-existing tests across 7 different test files fail deterministically (reproduced in isolation, not just under full-suite pool contention) with the same root cause:

```
Validation error: insert event (sqlstate: 23514, constraint: events_derived_requires_product_class,
table: _hyper_1_N_chunk, database_error_kind: CheckViolation, operation: database)
```

i.e. a derived-event insert (`source_event_ids` set) that omits `product_class`, which `core.events` has required since the sinex-0vx.4 / sinex-8cr.2 derivation-control-plane rollout (commit ae9b51221, PR #2508, "persist product/support metadata through every event insert path"). That PR evidently did not update every existing test fixture that constructs a derived event.

Affected files/tests (from a full `xtask test -p sinex-db --format human -t 4` run, invocation with 372 tests, 20-22 failures depending on run):

- `composable_query_test.rs`: `test_lineage_ancestors`, `test_lineage_descendants`, `test_lineage_max_depth` (reproduced in isolation with `xtask test -p sinex-db --test composable_query_test -t 2` -- 3/33 tests fail every time, not pool contention).
- `repositories_events` (in-crate `tests/repositories_events.rs`): `all_automaton_model_variants_roundtrip`, `synthetic_metadata_roundtrips_through_insert`, `all_temporal_policy_variants_roundtrip`, `get_material_root_events_in_range_excludes_synthesis_rows`, `events_repository_preserves_provenance`, `synthetic_metadata_survives_batch_insert`, `test_replacement_query_distinguishes_material_from_derived`.
- `repositories_state.rs`: `health_events_attach_live_run_identity`, `runtime_presence_uses_latest_nonterminal_run_per_manifest`, `fresh_runtime_health_preserves_live_run_identity`.
- `temporal_facts_view_test.rs`: `mixed_projection_no_cross_contamination`, `synthetic_event_projected_inline`.
- `lifecycle_restore_test.rs`: `cascade_restore_preserves_synthetic_metadata_columns`.
- `replay_state_machine_test.rs`: `replay_preview_nulls_cascade_impact_when_metadata_queries_fail`.
- `database_test.rs`: `test_concurrent_event_insertion`.

Separately (different root cause, same discovery pass): `crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events_test.rs`'s `no_extraneous_columns` and `column_count_matches_schema` unit tests assert a hardcoded `EXPECTED_COLUMNS` list of 26 columns against the live `event_select_columns!` macro output, which is now 32 columns (also consistent with the same #2508 rollout adding 6 derivation-control-plane columns: `product_class`, `claim_support`, `derivation_declaration_id`, `derivation_epoch_id`, `derivation_lane_id`, `adjudication_event_id`). `EXPECTED_COLUMNS` was never updated.

Not fixed as part of sinex-xjx8 (out of scope -- none of these files were touched by that bead; it only wires/repairs `tests/schema/`). Likely fix shape: either a shared test helper (used by `insert_test_event`/`ctx.publish`-style fixtures across these files) needs a product_class/claim_support/declaration default for derived-event construction, or each fixture needs the same treatment sinex-xjx8 applied to `crate/sinex-db/tests/schema/*.rs` (register a `derivation.product_declarations` row + set `product_class`/`claim_support` on the insert). Given the number of affected call sites, a shared fixture-level fix is likely more maintainable than per-test patches.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed test passes when run via xtask test -p sinex-db (either individually or as part of the full suite). no_extraneous_columns / column_count_matches_schema's EXPECTED_COLUMNS list matches the live event_select_columns! macro output (32 columns as of this filing).
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. xtask test -p sinex-db --test composable_query_test --format human -t 2
2. Observe test_lineage_ancestors / test_lineage_descendants / test_lineage_max_depth fail with sqlstate 23514 constraint events_derived_requires_product_class -- reproduces every time, in isolation, not a pool-contention artifact.
3. Same root cause (grep the failure text) reproducible for the other listed tests via xtask test -p sinex-db --test <file> --format human -t 2 for repositories_events, repositories_state, temporal_facts_view_test, lifecycle_restore_test, replay_state_machine_test, database_test.
4. xtask test -p sinex-db --lib -E 'test(no_extraneous_columns)' -- separately fails with a hardcoded 26-column EXPECTED_COLUMNS list vs a live 32-column event_select_columns! macro output.
close_reason: Duplicate of sinex-94mh, filed independently before discovering that bead already existed (both surfaced the same pre-existing 18-19 test failures from the sinex-8cr.2 derivation-control-plane rollout). Root-cause analysis (events_derived_requires_product_class check violation, PR #2508) and the additional events_test.rs unit-test finding folded into sinex-94mh's notes.

title: media.rs local-model-batch bindings declare unbacked LocalProcessWorker adapter
description:
crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs's source:media.audio-transcript.local-model-batch and source:media.screen-ocr.local-model-batch bindings declare adapter = "LocalProcessWorker", but grep confirms no struct/impl for LocalProcessWorker exists anywhere in crate/sinexd/src. This mirrors the gap fixed in sinex-xfqe (AudioSessionCaptureAdapter / ScreenRegionCaptureAdapter / ScreenVideoCaptureAdapter), but LocalProcessWorker bindings are Oneshot/SinexdSource worker bindings, not "long-lived session control" bindings, so the media.rs module doc's proposed-until-live-runner doctrine does not unambiguously cover them -- left un-flipped in sinex-xfqe's fix pending an explicit decision on whether bounded worker bindings should also default proposed=true when their adapter is unbacked, or whether they need a real LocalProcessWorker implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide: either implement a real LocalProcessWorker (or rename adapter to the actual worker mechanism used), or add proposed = true to both local-model-batch bindings.
- Update/verify source_status_test assertions on local_model_mode accordingly.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest:
- AC "Decide: implement real LocalProcessWorker or rename adapter, or mark proposed=true": SATISFIED — decision (a) rename, documented in comment thread. Renamed adapter = "LocalProcessWorker" -> "MediaWorkerCommandExecutor" on both media.rs local-model-batch bindings; confirmed via grep that no runtime code path resolves the adapter string to a type, so the rename is safe metadata-only. proposed stays false (mechanism is real/complete, not a stub) — verified execute_media_worker_command in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs genuinely spawns a local process or admits operator-supplied worker output evidence, exercised by 23 passing tests.
- AC "Update/verify source_status_test assertions on local_model_mode accordingly": SATISFIED — updated the local_model_mode.adapter assertion in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/source_status_test.rs.

Verification commands run:
  xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions) or test(source_status)' -> 23 passed, 0 failed
  xtask check -p sinexd -> success
  xtask check --changed-strict origin/master (pre-push drift guard) -> passed

Closed by PR #2535 (merged a16d8865f31395229f980cced4058d990e4490b5).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Decision: (a) rename, not stub-flip.

Confirmed via `grep -rln "LocalProcessWorker" crate/` that no struct/impl by
that name exists anywhere — same class of symptom as sinex-xfqe. But the
underlying mechanism is real, not a stub:

- `source:media.audio-transcript.run-model` / `source:media.screen-ocr.run-ocr`
  (PACKAGE_OPERATION_SPECS in crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/package.rs)
  route to `execute_media_operation` -> `execute_worker_output` ->
  `resolve_media_worker_output` -> `execute_media_worker_command` in
  crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs.
- `execute_media_worker_command` genuinely spawns a local OS process
  (`tokio::process::Command::new(request.program).args(...)`) when the RPC
  caller supplies `worker_command`; alternatively the caller can hand over
  already-computed evidence via `worker_output`/`worker_output_path` (the
  operator or an external script ran the model themselves). Both paths admit
  a `SourceMaterial`, dispatch it through the standard parser, and persist
  events — this is a complete, working, RPC-driven executor, confirmed by 23
  passing tests in `media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions` and
  neighboring `source_status` tests.
- It is architecturally distinct from every other `RunnerPack::SinexdSource`
  binding in the codebase (StaticFileAdapter, DirectoryWalkAdapter,
  AppendOnlyFileAdapter, GmailApiCursorAdapter, ImapSyncAdapter, ...), all of
  which back their `adapter` field with a real `InputShapeAdapter` struct
  under `crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/`. local-model-batch is
  driven entirely through the ops/RPC executor layer instead, so no such
  struct was ever going to exist for it — the naive "grep for a struct"
  signal used in sinex-xfqe genuinely doesn't apply here.
- Verified the `adapter` binding field is descriptive metadata only: no
  runtime code path resolves it to a type (checked
  `source_status.rs`/`package_completeness.rs`/`source_skeleton.rs` — all
  three just echo the string). Renaming is therefore safe. Precedent:
  `crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/polylogue.rs` already uses
  `adapter = "ExternalProducer"`, a descriptive label for a mechanism that
  also isn't an `InputShapeAdapter` struct.

Change: renamed `adapter = "LocalProcessWorker"` to `adapter =
"MediaWorkerCommandExecutor"` on both `local-model-batch` bindings in
`crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs`, expanded the module
doc comment to record the executor-vs-adapter distinction so a future audit
doesn't reflag it, and updated the one `local_model_mode.adapter` assertion
in `crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/source_status_test.rs`. `proposed` stays
`false` on both bindings (unchanged) — the mechanism is complete, not a
stub, so option (b) does not apply.

Verification:
- `xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions) or test(source_status)'` -> 23 passed, 0 failed
- `xtask check -p sinexd` -> success

title: media.audio-transcript.live-session binding claims accepted (proposed=false) with no AudioSessionCaptureAdapter implementation
description:
## Problem
crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs's module doc (line 6) states: "Long-lived session control bindings stay proposed until a durable live runner owns the capture process." The `source:media.audio-transcript.live-session` binding (line ~89) declares `adapter = "AudioSessionCaptureAdapter"` but grep across crate/sinexd/src confirms no `struct`/`impl` for `AudioSessionCaptureAdapter` exists anywhere in production code — it's a string literal in macro metadata with no backing implementation. Per the module's own stated design intent, this binding should carry `proposed = true` (defaults to false when the attribute is omitted — see crate/sinex-macros/src/source_registration.rs:323-325, crate/sinex-macros/src/source_definition.rs:229). It currently omits the attribute, so `binding.proposed` reads false, meaning the source-coverage API reports this binding as accepted/ready when nothing implements it.

Surfaced via crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/source_status_test.rs:704 (`media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions`), which asserts `live_audio_mode.proposed` is true and currently fails — found during sinex-65mu quiet-host test reverification (2026-07-31).

## Open question to resolve before fixing
Is `adapter = "..."` purely descriptive metadata (no runtime type-name resolution), or does anything actually look up an adapter by this string at runtime? If nothing resolves it, the missing implementation is real and undetectable except via this stale-vs-intent mismatch — worth checking whether other proposed=false bindings in this file (and other source_contracts/*.rs files) have the same gap, i.e. an adapter name with zero backing implementation. If so this may be a systemic pattern worth its own audit, not a one-binding fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Either: add `proposed = true` to the live-session binding (if AudioSessionCaptureAdapter genuinely isn't implemented) and update the test assertion... wait, the test ALREADY asserts proposed=true and is currently failing, so the fix is adding `proposed = true` to the binding attributes to match both the test and the stated module doctrine.
- Or: if investigation finds AudioSessionCaptureAdapter IS implemented under a different name/module (grep may have missed an alias/trait-object dispatch), correct the module doc and leave proposed=false, documenting why in a code comment.
- Sweep sibling media.rs bindings (audio-transcript on-demand-session, screen-ocr live-session/on-demand) for the same adapter-name-vs-implementation gap while in this file.
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions)' passes.
notes: Open question resolved: grep confirms binding.adapter is purely a descriptive display string (source_status.rs:1029, binding.adapter.to_string() only) — never resolved to any actual type/implementation anywhere in the runtime. This is NOT a systemic pattern needing a full audit sweep (adapter names are always just labels), it's specifically that media.audio-transcript.live-session's implementation genuinely doesn't exist. Fix is now unambiguous: add proposed = true to the source:media.audio-transcript.live-session binding in crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs (~line 89). Also sweep the sibling bindings in the same file (on-demand-session, screen-ocr live-session/on-demand) for whether their adapters are real (grep for a struct/impl matching each named adapter) before assuming they're fine — do this as part of the same small fix, not a separate investigation.
close_reason:
Merged #2533. Added proposed=true to all 5 unbacked live-capture bindings in media.rs (2 audio-transcript, 3 screen-ocr), verified none of the 3 named adapters (AudioSessionCaptureAdapter, ScreenRegionCaptureAdapter, ScreenVideoCaptureAdapter) have any backing implementation. Correctly left the worker-backed local-model-batch bindings (adapter LocalProcessWorker) and staged-import bindings alone — verified this is a deliberate design distinction per the module's own doc ("long-lived session control bindings stay proposed"; local-model/staged-import is a different, already-ready category).

Verification: xtask test -E 'media_package_operations_surface_operator_actions or source_status' — 23/23 passed (was failing). xtask check clean.

title: Test fixtures across sinexd test suite miss product_class/claim_support seeding (post-0vx.4 enforcement trigger)
description:
Discovered 2026-07-31 during sinex-4k4b's fix (PR #2523). Root cause: PR #2506 (sinex-0vx.4) added the derivation/authority schema plus enforcement triggers (events_derived_requires_product_class, events_claim_support_requires_product_class) on core.events/reflection.events -- any derived event inserted without a valid product_class/claim_support (backed by a registered derivation.product_declarations row) is now rejected at the DB level. Many pre-existing test fixtures build derived events without seeding that row or setting those fields, so they fail against current master with the enforcement trigger's rejection -- NOT because of any regression in the code under test.

~32 tests confirmed failing on unmodified origin/master for this reason (measured 2026-07-31, sinex-4k4b's broad regression pass, xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(/api::/)'), spread across: curation_handlers_test, instructions_handlers_test, cascade_analyzer* tests, dlq_handlers_test, replay_lifecycle_test, sources_handlers_test, sse_stream_test, transport_security_test. The correct fixture pattern already exists (persistence_test.rs::seed_product_declaration, and now automata_handlers_test.rs's copy from PR #2523) -- this is a mechanical sweep applying that same pattern everywhere it's missing, OR (better, if in scope) a shared test-helper extraction so every affected test file doesn't hand-roll its own seed function.

This is exactly the kind of test-suite trustworthiness gap sinex-amg2 exists to close -- pick this up as amg2's next pass once a compile slot is free. Related: sinex-0vx.5's eventual startup declaration-reconciler would make ad-hoc test seeding unnecessary for declarations that match a real AutomatonSpec::OUTPUT_DECLARATIONS entry, but that's a different, larger mechanism -- don't block this mechanical fixture sweep on it.
acceptance_criteria:
- every test in the ~32-test list (re-enumerate fresh, this snapshot decays) either passes after seeding its product_class/claim_support declaration correctly, or is explicitly reclassified with a stated reason if seeding isn't the right fix for that specific case
- a shared seed-declaration test helper exists (or the existing per-file copies are consolidated) if that's cheap given how many files are affected
- xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(/api::/)' full pass count improves by the number of tests fixed here, with a before/after count cited in the closing note
- no test is silently skipped/ignored to make the count look better

title: sinexd --lib: 8 newly-observed lib-test failures under contended host (post-amg2 sweep)
description:

6. event_engine::material_assembler::finalize::tests::handle_end_before_slice_waits_for_missing_slice_instead_of_failing (10.9s)
7. event_engine::material_assembler::io::tests::import_into_content_store_preserves_staging_file_until_cleanup (10.9s)

9. event_engine::material_assembler::io::tests::handle_slice_releases_state_lock_before_staging_io — TIMEOUT at 120s

Three additional failures in the same run exactly match sinex-li78's already-tracked pair plus one more in the same avoid-listed area (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/ and crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/) — do not duplicate those here, see sinex-li78:

The long durations (7-11s, one 120s timeout) on several of these under a contended host are consistent with resource-contention symptoms rather than proven deterministic bugs — re-run each in isolation on a QUIET host before triaging further; do not assume any of these are real bugs vs. contention artifacts until reproduced standalone.

title: Entity-chain stream/checkpoint shadow lane: continuous-scope generality proof + pq5-B re-entry
description: 0vx generality proof #2 (continuous). The 2026-07-08 pq5 ruling made 0vx the SOLE re-entry path for the retired-default-off entity chain (ijz6), and 0vx notes name 'sessionization + the entity chain' as the two generality proofs — but only sessionization (0vx.7, event_set/batch scope) had a child. This bead proves the DerivationScope::StreamCheckpoint scope kind end-to-end and exercises the promotion seam over a CONTINUOUS automaton. Design: .agent/scratch/027-0vx-derivation-control-plane-design.md (decision b + promotion path).
acceptance_criteria: The 4-stage entity chain (extractor/resolver/relation/enricher) runs in a SHADOW derivation lane over a DerivationScope::StreamCheckpoint scope (frozen end_seq high-watermark, not a wall clock) under a candidate epoch, writing derivation.lane_outputs with product_class=semantic_candidate and an honest ClaimSupport (support_level=heuristic, source_coverage from referenced events, temporal_quality from ts_orig provenance, adjudication=unreviewed) — never canonical-looking core.events rows. A generic LaneDiffReport vs the empty baseline yields candidate-only (entity_new/relation_added). Promotion via curation proposal -> judgment -> registered finalizer flips lane status to promoted and emits the canonical output carrying adjudication_event_id; a direct canonical entity.related write and a finalizer bypass are both REJECTED at the DB/API gate. A frozen StreamCheckpoint scope re-run under the same epoch is byte-reproducible. title: Two inherited sinexd test failures at master base (checkpoint-halt class + drain bridge start)
description:
Two sinexd tests fail deterministically at master base b41043992 (verified 2026-07-12 in a clean worktree at /realm/tmp/worktrees/qabz via git checkout --detach + exact-node rerun; identical failures on the qabz branch, so classified inherited, not a qabz regression):

1) runtime::automaton::adapter::tests::processing_replay::process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures — panics at processing_replay.rs:47: the FIRST checkpoint save failure already halts with "Checkpoint save failed 1 consecutive times". The adapter halt condition (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/process.rs ~432) halts immediately when the save error is Checkpoint/Lifecycle/Configuration/PermissionDenied-classed regardless of the counter; the observed error is Checkpoint-classed, so either the UnserializableAutomaton fixture's save path now yields a Checkpoint-classed error where the test expects a serialization-classed one, or the environment (NATS KV) makes save_state_with_file_fallback fail with a fatal class before serialization is attempted.

2) runtime::stream::runner::runner_test::runtime::run_service_drain_finishes_inflight_automaton_batch_and_emits_completion — times out at tests/runtime.rs:60 "automaton batch did not start": the published confirmed event never reaches the module's process_event_batch within 3s.

Both may be environment-sensitive (worktree NATS/Postgres slots) rather than universally red — the same filter run passed ~300 sibling tests including the rest of processing_replay and the runner drain family. Repro: xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures) | test(run_service_drain_finishes_inflight_automaton_batch_and_emits_completion)'. Evidence artifacts: /realm/tmp/worktrees/qabz/.sinex/test-artifacts/20260712T*.
acceptance_criteria:
- root cause identified for both (code bug vs environment coupling), with the classification recorded here
- both tests pass on a clean master checkout AND in a fresh worktree, or are rewritten to be environment-independent
- if environment coupling: the coupling itself is fixed or the sandbox provisions it
notes:
Bug 2 root cause FOUND (via my own breadcrumb-instrumented trace, not the agent's second attempt either): crate/sinexd/src/runtime/stream/runner/automaton_runtime.rs's bridge consumer config hardcodes DeliverPolicy::New (~line 537), by design — comment states "anything before consumer creation is covered by the mandatory per-automaton historical scan." Test run_service_drain_finishes_inflight_automaton_batch_and_emits_completion spawns run_service() (which creates the New-policy consumer via a real async NATS round-trip) and, unsynchronized, immediately publishes its test confirmed event on the same task. Genuine race: if publish's NATS round-trip beats consumer creation's, the message is invisible to a New-policy consumer forever. Confirmed via breadcrumb trace showing "pull_batch_bounded returned 0 messages" repeatedly — consumer created and polling fine, just nothing ever arrives.

Open question resumed agent must resolve: is this a test-only synchronization gap (DrainBridgeTestModule's scan() is a stub that can't see raw-NATS-published test messages, so production's real historical-scan safety net doesn't apply to this fixture — likely, but must be verified by reading scan()'s actual impl) or a genuine production race (if a confirmed event can legitimately publish at the exact moment a bridge-backed automaton is restarting/creating its consumer, and historical-scan can't close that gap for ALL bridge-backed automata, not just this fixture). Told the agent to determine this before implementing, not just add a sleep or synchronization signal blindly.
close_reason:
Both bugs fixed and merged. Bug 1 (checkpoint-halt 3-strike counter): #2529. Bug 2 (drain-bridge consumer race): #2532.

Bug 2 required 3 resume cycles with the dispatched agent plus direct coordinator intervention: the agent's first fix attempt (capabilities.supports_historical) was independently verified wrong via forced clean rebuild (identical failure persisted). I then instrumented the code with breadcrumb tracing myself and found the real root cause: the bridge's confirmed-event consumer uses DeliverPolicy::New (deliberate design, safety net = per-automaton historical DB scan before consumer creation), but DrainBridgeTestModule::scan() is a stub with no backing store, so the test's unsynchronized publish-then-spawn ordering raced real consumer creation and usually lost. Handed the precise diagnosis back; the agent's second attempt (deterministic oneshot ready-signal, test/harness-only via #[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))], mirrors an existing sibling JetStreamConsumer::run_with_ready_signal pattern) was correct — independently verified 3/3 consecutive test runs plus 52/52 in the broader runner_test/processing_replay suites, zero production behavior change confirmed by reading the cfg-gating.

Both original "may be environment-sensitive" caveats are now fully retracted: confirmed as two distinct, deterministic, real bugs, both fixed with evidence-backed root causes rather than speculative patches.

title: Type-erase AutomatonRuntime wrapper boundary (remaining 11.6% mono IR after qabz)
description:

title: Rollup event types (activity.summary.daily/hourly) not opted into SupersedeOnChange: revision-driven rollup re-emits get suppressed
description: Found during adversarial review of PR #2495 (sinex-n9a). The daily/hourly rollup automata (crate/sinexd/src/automata/daily.rs, hourly.rs) emit activity.summary.daily / activity.summary.hourly with equivalence keys (daily.rs ~L242), but those payload types were NOT opted into RevisionPolicy::SupersedeOnChange in the n9a change (only state.interval, activity.window.summary, activity.session.boundary, attention.span were, per the bead's explicit list). This is exactly the ecy-without-n9a failure mode, one layer up. title: SupersedeOnChange content-hash idempotency defeated by post-admission payload mutation (NUL strip, redaction)
description: Found during adversarial review of PR #2495 (sinex-n9a). The admission-time content hash (payload_content_hash in crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/content_hash.rs, compared in classify_live_match in crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs) is computed over the CANDIDATE payload as it arrives at admission — but the payload can be mutated after the hash and before persistence: (1) strip_postgres_jsonb_nul_chars (admission.rs, admitted_to_stream_rows path) removes NUL characters; (2) redact_batch (jetstream_consumer/persist.rs central redaction chokepoint) can rewrite the payload. Any event whose payload is mutated by either step never hash-equals its own stored form on the next identical re-emit, so the SupersedeOnChange comparison classifies it as changed content every time -> perpetual archive/re-insert churn instead of suppression. No correctness violation (single-live-interpretation holds; each churn archives then re-admits), but it is unbounded archive growth and wasted work for affected occurrences. Mitigated today by default-zero-redaction doctrine and NUL-free payloads being the norm; becomes a real problem the moment a redaction rule targets a SupersedeOnChange event type. Candidate fixes: hash the post-mutation (persisted) form instead of the wire form; or normalize (NUL-strip) before hashing and compare only redaction-stable projections; or store the admission-time hash in a column and compare hash-to-stored-hash instead of hash-to-recomputed-hash.
acceptance_criteria: Repro: register a redaction rule (or craft a payload containing NUL chars) targeting a SupersedeOnChange event type; emit the same occurrence (same equivalence_key, same wire payload) twice; observe the second emit superseding (archive + re-insert) instead of suppressing, and repeating on every subsequent identical re-emit. Fix AC: an identical wire re-emit of an occurrence whose stored payload was mutated post-admission (NUL strip and/or redaction) is SUPPRESSED, not superseded — proven by a test with an active redaction rule on a SupersedeOnChange type showing exactly one live row, zero archived rows after N identical re-emits. Genuine content changes still supersede. No hash comparison against a form the pipeline later mutates.
notes:
STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-01, continued directly by coordinator after original agent's session-limit interruption): the FULL fix is now complete, not just the plumbing checkpoint.

Completed: (1) admission.rs wiring — admitted_to_stream_rows now hashes the candidate payload BEFORE strip_postgres_jsonb_nul_chars mutates it, storing it on StreamBatchRow.content_hash; classify_live_match now compares against the live row's STORED content_hash (via new live_row_content_hash() helper) instead of recomputing from the live row's potentially-mutated persisted payload, with NULL/malformed fallback. (2) Fixed 4 EventRecord query_as! sites (insert/insert_with_tx x Activity/Reflection) missing content_hash. (3) Fixed 2 more batch-insert QueryBuilder sites (insert_batch_unnest_in_tx, insert_stream_batch_into's material+derived strategies) that had the SAME column-count bug — SQL column list auto-derived from EVENT_COPY_COLUMNS (already included content_hash) but manual push_bind calls didn't, causing 'INSERT has more target columns than expressions'. (4) Fixed event_select_columns! macro (23 call sites system-wide) missing content_hash, causing 'no column found for name: content_hash' at runtime on every event SELECT. (5) Fixed 2 self-consistency drift-guard tests whose hardcoded expected-column lists were ALREADY stale (missing 6 derivation-control-plane columns) BEFORE this branch even touched them — confirmed via clean origin/master checkout, genuinely pre-existing, fixed alongside since I was already touching that exact mechanism.

New tests: 4 unit tests in a new admission_test.rs (event_engine::admission::tests module) directly exercising the real classify_live_match function (using activity.window.summary, a real production SupersedeOnChange-registered event type) — proves the exact bug (live row's stored hash reflects pre-mutation content, current payload column reflects post-mutation content, comparison must prefer stored) and 3 supporting edge cases (genuine change still supersedes, NULL stored hash falls back correctly, malformed stored hash falls back correctly).

Verification: xtask check clean across sinex-db/sinexd/sinex-schema/sinex-primitives/sinexctl. Full sinex-db suite: 286/304 passed (18 failing, ALL independently confirmed pre-existing on unmodified origin/master via a clean throwaway worktree — filed separately as sinex-94mh, a real pre-existing 6%-of-suite baseline health problem unrelated to this fix). Full sinexd suite showed much broader noise (46-75 failures across two consecutive runs, wildly different test sets each time, heavy 6-60s timing signatures) — diagnosed as connection-pool/host contention from running 2012 tests in one shot, not a regression: focused reruns of the actual content_hash-relevant surface (supersede_on_change + admission_test, 28 tests) pass 100% consistently across multiple runs including post-rebase. description: Deferred from sinex-n9a (SupersedeOnChange admission RevisionPolicy). n9a added AdmissionDecision::Superseded { admitted, superseded_event_id } as a decision distinct from Suppressed/Admitted, and wired archive-before-insert + descendant scope invalidation for it in JetStreamConsumer::prepare_events. title: Remove health-via-NATS-events aggregation hop (read HealthReporter in-process)
description: Partial multi-daemon relic. runtime/health_reporter.rs emits health.status NATS events (self_observation.rs:708-716) consumed by automata/health.rs aggregator IN THE SAME PROCESS. The emit-to-NATS-then-consume-in-same-process aggregation hop is the relic; a durable health-event record MAY still earn its keep (analytics/replay) - remove only the process-boundary hop, read HealthReporter::current_status() directly. The 'missing reporter counts as healthy/unknown' default (adapter/mod.rs:566-582) only mattered because health arrived as optional external signals.
notes:
2026-07-12 RECONCILE-ON-CLAIM FINDING (category error — recommend CLOSE, not implement):

The bead's premise is that "runtime/health_reporter.rs emits health.status NATS events
consumed by automata/health.rs aggregator IN THE SAME PROCESS" is a multi-daemon relic,
analogous to the leader-election/instance-health-RPC relics (9h32/original-7y77-scope).
Verified against master (9cd4ea062) this does NOT hold:

1. health.rs is a genuine `ScopeReconciler` automaton (see its own module doc:
   "groups health events by component... During replay, invalidating a component
   scope recomputes all health reports for that component"). It consumes health.status
   events via the SAME NATS-mediated, in-process pattern EVERY automaton in this
   single-daemon system uses (canonicalizer, session-detector, hourly-summarizer, all
   of them) — sources/components emit events -> admission -> persist -> republish on
   the confirmed stream -> automata (hosted in-process) consume via their durable
   JetStream consumer. This is not unique to health, it's the load-bearing
   durability/replay/checkpointing architecture documented in CLAUDE.md's pipeline
   section. Treating it as a "process-boundary hop relic" is a category error: it
   confuses "NATS-mediated" with "multi-daemon", but single-daemon sinexd still uses
   NATS for EVERY automaton's input, by design (durability + replay + checkpointing),
   not as a multi-process handoff artifact.
2. health.rs's OUTPUT (HealthAggregatedReportPayload, HealthAggregatedAlertPayload,
   HealthAggregatedSystemStatusPayload) is itself a genuine derived-event product with
   real replay semantics — exactly the "storage/authority split" doctrine (candidate
   claims flow through the normal admission->persist pipeline). Reading
   HealthReporter::current_status() directly instead (as the bead proposes) would
   mean bypassing the entire derived-event/replay model for health aggregation,
   which is a regression against project doctrine, not a cleanup.
3. Bead's cited motivation — "the 'missing reporter counts as healthy/unknown' default
   (adapter/mod.rs:566-582) only mattered because health arrived as optional external
   signals" — is STALE. That exact issue is already fixed by sinex-r6d.3 (see the
   comment at adapter/mod.rs:583-588 citing r6d.3 by name, landed before this bead was
   even filed). The motivating problem no longer exists.
4. Verified via grep: health.status is emitted ONLY by health_reporter.rs and consumed
   ONLY by automata/health.rs — no other redundant in-process consumer exists that
   duplicates HealthReporter::current_status() (which IS already used directly, at
   automaton/adapter/mod.rs:583-589 and :721, for a DIFFERENT purpose: an adapter's own
   local liveness self-check, not cross-component aggregation).
5. The ONE genuinely real entanglement 7y77 correctly flagged — the coordination KV
   backing sinexctl's runtime_status/instance_health RPC surface — was NOT this
   health.rs/health_reporter.rs pipeline at all; it was the SEPARATE
   coordination.rs/RuntimeCoordination election-KV mechanism. That entanglement is
   ALREADY FIXED via sinex-9h32 (PR #2489, merged): runtime_status was re-plumbed onto
   runtime_list_active (the heartbeat-backed runtime registry) instead of the removed
   election KV. Nothing about THIS bead's stated health-aggregation scope needed to
   change for that fix to land.

RECOMMENDATION: close this bead as premise-invalidated (category error + motivating
issue already fixed by r6d.3 + the one real entanglement already fixed by 9h32). Do
NOT implement "remove the health.status NATS hop" — it would regress genuine
derived-event architecture. If there IS a real remaining health-plane cleanup wanted,
it needs to be re-scoped from scratch against current master, not against this bead's
stale text.
close_reason: Premise invalidated on reconcile-on-claim (2026-07-12, see notes for full evidence): treating health.rs's NATS-mediated consumption of health.status events as a 'multi-daemon process-boundary hop relic' is a category error — every automaton in this single-daemon system consumes inputs the same way (NATS-mediated, in-process) by design, for durability/replay/checkpointing, not as a multi-process artifact. health.rs is a genuine ScopeReconciler with real derived-event outputs (HealthAggregatedReportPayload et al) whose replay semantics would regress if bypassed in favor of reading HealthReporter::current_status() directly. The bead's cited motivating issue (missing-reporter-counts-as-healthy default) was already fixed by sinex-r6d.3 before this bead was filed. The one genuinely real entanglement this bead's original scope correctly flagged (coordination KV backing sinexctl runtime_status/instance_health) was a DIFFERENT mechanism (coordination.rs/RuntimeCoordination) and is already fixed via sinex-9h32 (PR #2489, merged 2026-07-12). No remaining action needed against this bead's stated scope; if a genuine health-plane cleanup is wanted it needs fresh scoping against current master.

title: Remove leader/standby election for continuous sources (single-daemon relic)
description: Multi-daemon relic. runtime/coordination.rs runs per-tick NATS-KV acquire_leadership CAS + instance registration per continuous-source binding, forever (SINEX_COORDINATION_DISABLED unset in nixos/; continuous sources reach it via runtime_cli.rs:627 else-branch, bindings.rs:85-88 service subcommand). With one sinexd, exactly one instance per source exists -> trivial self-election, impossible handoff -> standing NATS-KV traffic for an impossible race. Fix: delete the else-branch, run run_service() directly; retire the api/handlers/coordination.rs list_instances/get_leader/instance_health surface (single self-leader). Verify: no NATS-KV leadership traffic for continuous sources post-change.
notes:
2026-07-12 EXECUTION FINDING (blocks isolated removal — 9h32 is entangled with 7y77):
attempted the removal; the coordination KV + its RPC surface are NOT pure leader-
election — they BACK the health/status surface. Verified against master:
  - sinexctl `runtime status <module>` -> gateway.runtime_status() calls
    COORDINATION_INSTANCE_HEALTH_METHOD ("coordination.instance_health",
    gateway.rs:711-718), served by handle_coordination_instance_health reading the
    coordination KV (get_leader + instance metadata).
  - RuntimeCoordination.run_coordination_loop did BOTH election AND instance
    REGISTRATION into the KV; removing it depopulates the KV for continuous sources,
    so their runtime_status/instance_health goes empty even if the handler stays.
  - So removing the election (9h32) breaks/degrades the health-status display unless
    runtime_status + instance_health are first re-pointed to a non-election source
    (the in-process HealthReporter / runtime registry — exactly 7y77's scope).

CORRECTED SEQUENCING: 9h32 must be co-implemented with 7y77. Order: (1) 7y77 re-plumbs
runtime_status + instance_health to read HealthReporter::current_status()/the runtime
registry (RUNTIME_HEALTH_METHOD already reads registry state — the pattern exists),
independent of the coordination KV; (2) THEN 9h32 removes RuntimeCoordination + the
election loop + list_instances/get_leader (pure-election observability) + the
CoordinationKvClient + SINEX_COORDINATION_DISABLED, since nothing load-bearing reads
the KV anymore. Also in scope but out of the bead's stated text: the AUTOMATON
leader-standby (RuntimeRunner::acquire_leader_standby) is a third election writer.
Partial branch reverted (it broke runtime_status). Non-data-critical; not gated on the
wipe (plan). Best done as one focused 7y77+9h32 effort, not two isolated removals.
close_reason:
Completed via PR #2489 (branch feature/refactor/9h32-remove-leader-election). Leader/standby election removed for continuous sources: runtime/coordination.rs + coordination_test.rs deleted (2105 lines), runtime_cli.rs's coordinated-standby branch collapsed to a direct run_service() call, api/handlers/coordination.rs RPC surface retired.

Closure Evidence Manifest:
- AC "delete the else-branch, run run_service() directly": satisfied — runtime_cli.rs now calls runner.run_service() unconditionally (dry_run/automaton/coordinated-standby branches collapsed).
- AC "retire the api/handlers/coordination.rs list_instances/get_leader/instance_health surface": satisfied — file deleted, RPC registrations removed from rpc_registry.rs.
- AC "no NATS-KV leadership traffic for continuous sources post-change": satisfied by construction — RuntimeCoordination (the sole election-KV writer) no longer exists in the binary.
- Corrected sequencing executed: was entangled with sinex-7y77 (coordination KV also backed sinexctl runtime_status/instance_health via COORDINATION_INSTANCE_HEALTH_METHOD). Re-plumbed runtime_status onto runtime_list_active (heartbeat-backed runtime registry) BEFORE removing the election KV, per the corrected-sequencing note. sinex-7y77's own stated scope (health.status NATS emit/consume-in-process hop in health_reporter.rs/automata/health.rs) remains open — untouched by this PR, tracked separately.
- Deferred/out of scope: automaton internal leader/standby (RuntimeRunner::acquire_leader_standby) — separate election writer, explicitly not touched (its test acquire_leader_standby_waits_for_existing_leader_release still passes). NixOS SINEX_COORDINATION_* config kept — still read by the kept automaton-election CoordinationKvClient.

Verification: xtask check --changed-strict origin/master (2 packages, all passed, also re-verified by pre-push drift guard); xtask check -p sinexctl (clean); xtask test -p sinexctl -p sinexd -E 'test(runtime)' (all directly-relevant tests pass; 8 unrelated sinexd failures classified as pre-existing/flaky — 3 reproduce identically on unmodified origin/master via throwaway worktree verification, 5 live in untouched files with pool-contention signatures).

title: Dev-database lifecycle: per-checkout postgres must not outlive its devshell
description: From the sinnix 2026-07-10 reboot postmortem (sinnix-eaw) and 07-11 shadow-load forensics: orphaned per-checkout dev-postgres instances (six processes per checkout under /var/cache/sinex) survived their devshells, burned 90s stop-timeouts each at shutdown, and held /var/lib/sinex + /var/cache/sinex mounts busy past their unmount attempts. Fix at the source: tie dev-DB lifetime to the devshell (shellHook trap / systemd-run --scope with the shell as lifecycle anchor), plus an idle reaper for dev-state dirs whose owning checkout/devshell is gone (e.g. socket unused >2h => pg_ctl stop). Acceptance: exiting the devshell (including kill -9 of the shell) leaves zero dev postgres processes within 60s; a wedged one is reaped within the idle window.
notes:
CONCRETE FIELD EVIDENCE (2026-08-01): found 5 simultaneously-running orphaned per-checkout dev-postgres instances (ps aux | grep 'postgres -D' showed processes for dev-state hashes 177ce53f9bbc, 4e62f2dadee9, d6bc094ddd17, 088c98260324, 3af5b2688df9 — 72 total postgres processes system-wide) — 4 of the 5 belonged to worktrees that no longer existed (confirmed via `git worktree list` showing only 2 active worktrees at the time). This accumulated purely from this session's normal worktree-per-dispatched-agent workflow (each Agent tool dispatch with isolation:"worktree" creates its own dev-state, and postgres apparently never gets stopped when the worktree is cleaned up).

Directly implicated in a real debugging cost this session: repeatedly investigated confusing, seemingly-impossible schema-apply behavior (columns appearing/disappearing between consecutive commands, connection refused/no-such-file errors, "pre-existing shared memory block still in use" startup failures) across THREE separate worktrees (main checkout twice, two different agent worktrees) before recognizing the pattern. Each time the "fix" was: stop infra, wipe the disposable $CACHE_DIR/dev-state/data directory, retry — but the ROOT problem (orphaned instances never being stopped) was never addressed, just worked around locally per-incident.

Given how much investigation time this cost across the session (multiple 10+ minute detours), recommend prioritizing this bead's shellHook-trap/idle-reaper fix relatively soon — it's directly costing verification reliability during exactly the kind of heavy multi-agent dispatch workflow this campaign relies on.
close_reason: Closed by PR #2542 (merged e3b54507, master). See comment on this issue for full evidence manifest. bd close/update write path was broken by a DB-schema/CLI-version mismatch (events.id has no default; worked around via direct bd sql UPDATE, bypassing the audit-event insert -- this bug itself is tracked separately since bd create is also broken right now).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Opened PR #2542 (fix/xtask/reap-orphaned-dev-postgres, not yet merged, pending operator review per explicit instruction not to self-merge given devshell-infra blast radius).

Scope: implemented the sinex-side 'unconditionally-safe orphan reap' complement, NOT a new devshell-owner-watcher. Investigation found that leg already exists and is deployed: sinnix scripts/sinnix-sinex-dev-db (watch + reap subcommands) + modules/services/sinex-dev-db-reaper.nix (sinex-dev-db-reaper.timer, enabled on sinnix-prime, 2h idle backstop) landed 2026-07-12 (sinnix commit 2705ea9). Root cause of the fresh 2026-08-01 field evidence: that mechanism only registers an owner / launches a watcher via sinnix-direnvrc's use_flake hook, which never fires for non-interactive 'nix develop --command xtask ...' invocations -- the actual dominant path for this project's Agent-tool worktree dispatch (confirmed empirically: none of the orphaned dev-state dirs had an owners/ dir or dev-db-watcher.log).

Fix: xtask::infra::stack::CleanupScope::OrphanedCheckoutsOnly (stop only when checkout_path_exists == Some(false), fail-safe on None) + xtask infra stop --all-checkouts --orphaned-only + an opportunistic sweep wired into xtask infra start (fires on every check/test/infra-start from any checkout, best-effort/non-fatal). Live-verified on sinnix-prime: found and reaped a real orphaned nats-server (pid 3922222, checkout /realm/worktrees/sinex-verify-94mh already deleted) plus 12 stale files from other dead checkouts, while leaving the live main checkout and one unknown-checkout entry untouched.

Not done: kill-9-the-devshell -> 60s teardown end-to-end verification (that's the sinnix-side owner-watcher, out of this PR's repo scope; this harness's per-Bash-call process-group cleanup made it unreliable to hold a devshell open across tool calls to test directly).

title: Prove transcript capability boundaries and selective deletion
description: Define and prove the Sinex-backed privacy, retention, and deletion lifecycle for raw/normalized transcripts, attachments, observations, assertions, context artifacts, effects, and Polylogue replicas. Reuse privacy_invalidation_scope from sinex-r6d.2/sinex-cem.1 and the generic purge cascade sinex-new8; do not create a transcript-only invalidation inventory. Cross-repository counterpart: polylogue-303r.6.
design:
Separate capabilities for metadata, transcript/tool text, reasoning, attachments, assertions, context artifacts, export, model input/embedding, and lifecycle mutation. Generic MCP remains redacted/read-only.

The authoritative inventory is privacy_invalidation_scope, extended for Polylogue. It enumerates exact provider/normalized CAS and metadata; core/reflection events and archive side tables; NATS/JetStream raw/confirmed/material frames; Polylogue producer source.db outbox/spool and Sinex recovery spool/KV/checkpoints; SQL and JetStream DLQ, ops/error rows, operations logs, journald/xtask history; Polylogue source/user/index/embeddings, FTS/search/caches; vectors, model-effect inputs/results/receipts, semantic outputs; context packs/deliveries, reports/exports/fixtures; backups/CAS backups, PostgreSQL WAL/physical remnants, audit archives; and disconnected replicas.

Deletion follows material refs and true derivation lineage with reference accounting, never Polylogue topology as derivation. A content-hash/self-report is not physical-deletion proof. Proof combines authoritative before/after inventory, independently implemented raw-byte/search/vector/ref absence probes, and a clean rebuild that cannot resurrect content. Non-enumerable/immutable residuals state owner, authority, retention/expiry, and unverifiability. Disconnected replicas remain pending until acknowledged or declared residual. Reuse sinex-new8 execution/preview and r6d.2/cem.1 report schema.
acceptance_criteria: Capability matrix denies raw access through metadata/generic MCP credentials while authorized reads work. privacy_invalidation_scope covers all enumerated transport, spool/KV, DLQ/ops/log, backup/WAL/audit, vector/effect/report, and disconnected-replica surfaces. Fork/shared-prefix deletion preserves legitimate shared evidence. Independent absence probes plus clean rebuild show no resurrection; hash self-report alone fails. Interrupted purge resumes. Every unverifiable residual has explicit retention/expiry and owner or closure fails. Offline request cannot report success before Sinex confirmation. The report schema is compatible with r6d.2/cem.1 and execution reuses new8.

title: Back durable Polylogue assertions and context delivery with Sinex
description: Make Sinex the backed-mode durable authority for Polylogue assertions, corrections, notes, lessons, handoffs, judgments, context policy, saved durable analyses, and final context-delivery artifacts/occurrences. Polylogue remains ontology, scheduler, compiler, and UX authority; SQLite is standalone authority or backed-mode offline replica/outbox. Cross-repository counterpart: polylogue-303r.5.
design: Store full proposal/assertion content, scope, evidence refs, policy revision, authoredness, lifecycle, and judgment, not merely annotation-action metadata. Agent/model candidates remain non-authoritative and non-injectable until operator or declared policy judgment accepts/rejects/defers/supersedes them. Persist final context bytes/manifest as material plus a delivery event with exact selected/omitted evidence and budget. Backed offline writes enter a durable ordered outbox carrying base revision, idempotency key, conflict class, and pending status. Reconnect routes concurrent revisions to explicit adjudication; never silent last-write-wins. Reuse Sinex proposal/judgment/finalizer primitives rather than inventing a Polylogue-only authority engine, while retaining Polylogue assertion kinds and context rules.
acceptance_criteria: Cold rebuild restores assertion content, evidence refs, complete judgment/supersession history, context policy, saved durable analyses, and context-delivery bytes/manifests. Candidate assertions remain non-injectable without accepted judgment. Crash/offline/reconnect tests show no lost write, duplicate judgment, or silent overwrite; concurrent conflict becomes an adjudication item. Query resolves exactly what context crossed the model boundary and omissions. Local-only UI state stays excluded; standalone Polylogue remains unchanged.

title: Converge direct AI-session parsers on the Polylogue material protocol
description: Converge Sinex's direct Claude/ChatGPT ai_session compatibility parsers on the Polylogue-authored normalized material protocol, or retire them where Polylogue is the supported producer. The current parsers define a second partial conversation vocabulary and fabricate pseudo ByteRange anchors from record indexes; those anchors are not retrievable evidence.
design: Inventory each direct ai_session source and choose explicitly: route through Polylogue's versioned normalized-session material producer, or keep a compatibility importer that stages the exact source bytes and emits the same shared anchored protocol. No provider-specific parser may mint synthetic byte coordinates or define message/session semantics divergent from Polylogue. Preserve independently useful capture paths only when they can prove byte-backed provenance and schema compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: No active ai_session path uses conversation_index*1_000_000/message_index pseudo anchors or a provider-limited competing ontology; every retained path stages retrievable exact bytes and emits the shared protocol; Claude and ChatGPT compatibility fixtures produce the same object/revision/occurrence semantics as Polylogue; deliberately changing either parser's vocabulary or anchor fails compatibility tests; obsolete source contracts/docs/generated entries are removed in the same change; focused xtask checks pass.

title: Current-master sinexd full-suite failure inventory (2026-07-10)
description: First full sinexd suite runs in ~2 months (invocations 2006052/2006055 in xtask-history.db, during sinex-v7od verification) surfaced an accumulated failure mass that predates and is independent of the binary consolidation: 1984 tests, 64/68 failures across two runs with heavy churn (22 newly failing / 18 fixed between back-to-back runs). Classes: (1) DB-slot-pool exhaustion, 33-37 per run, message 'Failed to acquire database after 100 attempts' (xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/mod.rs:1488) — unstable set, likely contention-shape sensitivity; needs a quiet-host run + slot/pool sizing analysis before treating any of them as code bugs. (2) ~20 pre-existing deterministic failures incl. the known sinex-r6d.13 confirmed-republish fixture. (3) Generated-artifact drift: privacy-coverage matrix stale — code removed 'clipboard' from browser-history parser privacy_contexts, docs/sources/privacy-coverage.generated.json never regenerated (regen: sinexd export-privacy-coverage-matrix). (4) Revived-orphan drift: terminal/atuin required-input-keys tests fail on unmodified sources (declared keys 'command/timestamp' vs expected 'history.command/history.timestamp'; atuin missing-required-key now Degraded caveat instead of blocking readiness) with NO prior pass history under any name. (5) Deterministic lib-target assertion failures: email source-contract tests (email_test.rs:136,164), material_assembler finalize/stale-cleanup, acquisition_manager oversized-slice, preflight discover_unit_files, runner drain test. All lib-target failures provably not caused by v7od (tests-only diff).
acceptance_criteria: Each cluster either turns green on current master or is owned by a dedicated bead linked from here; pool-exhaustion class gets a quiet-host baseline run + a sizing/test-group decision; matrix artifact regenerated; no cluster silently dropped.
notes: First triage pass merged via PR #2520: 5 real bugs fixed (email UTF-8 rejection, attachment content-type capture, atuin required-input-keys contract, 2 stale test assertions), privacy-coverage matrix drift already resolved upstream. New gap found: sinex-4k4b root cause (EventRepository::insert has no lane-routing for reflection events). New bead sinex-65mu filed for 9 failures needing quiet-host reverification (measured under r6d.11's concurrent compile load). Pool-exhaustion baseline still held pending a quiet window.
close_reason: Closed by PR #2543 (merged 90491c83, master). Independently verified: xtask check -p sinexd clean; xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E media/private-mode/source_status filters -- 68/68 passed. Real root-cause fix: sandbox Postgres max_connections=64 vs pool 48-slot target (~411 conns needed) silently clamped to a 4-slot pool on every checkout regardless of host load -- raised to 500. Two more real bugs found and fixed while re-verifying: subscribe-then-publish race in adapter_private_mode_control_listener_persists_broadcast (same shape as sinex-li78 bug 2), and PR #2533/sinex-xfqe over-broad proposed=true regression on 4 of 5 media live-capture bindings that are genuinely implemented (MediaAudioCaptureDriver/MediaScreenCaptureDriver, both register_source!-registered, confirmed to exist). Named failure classes all closed via child beads sinex-4k4b/sinex-li78/sinex-65mu (independently re-verified closed). Remaining single-test failures across repeated full-suite runs reproduce as isolated-rerun-clean host-contention noise per the already-closed sinex-65mu classification -- not silently dropped.

title: Declare per-source criticality tiers so the trust-sinex-with-deletion flip is explicit
description: Operator framing 2026-07-10: the sinex dataset is deliberately treated as non-critical (helps dev speed), but nobody had verified whether it already holds irreplaceable data. Verified answer: currently it does NOT — 85% is journal/self-chatter, and every personal source in core.events (activitywatch, shell.atuin, wm.hyprland, canonical.terminal, webhistory, keylog-class) still has its own canonical store in the /realm/data lake or the source app's DB; extractor/derived sources are rebuildable by replay. The only sinex-exclusive copies are expired-journal history (low value). THIS WILL SILENTLY CHANGE the moment an external ephemeral source (IMAP email, comms) comes online — the dataset flips to partially-irreplaceable with no ceremony. Wanted: a per-source criticality declaration (source registry field or config) with an explicit gate: adding a source whose upstream is ephemeral requires marking it critical, which should be visible in health/backup tooling. Until then the consuming host's daily blob borg job (added 2026-07-10) is the insurance.
acceptance_criteria:
- per-source criticality field exists and is populated for all active sources
- adding an ephemeral-upstream source without a criticality declaration fails loudly (validation)
- the current all-reconstructible status is recorded and re-checkable by query
notes:
2026-07-31 declarative re-check (coordinator, pre-Phase-C hardening pass). Live deployed source_ids (from SINEX_SOURCE_BINDINGS_PATH manifest, 14 bindings across 12 distinct source_ids):

RECONSTRUCTABLE (canonical copy exists outside sinex):
- desktop.activitywatch -> /realm/data/captures/activitywatch/ (AW's own event store, sinex is a downstream reader)
- terminal.atuin-history -> /home/sinity/.local/share/atuin/*.db (atuin's own history/records/kv DBs, live) + /realm/data/captures/shell/atuin/ archive
- browser.history (x3 binding instances) -> /home/sinity/.local/share/qutebrowser/history.sqlite (verified readable now, 121 rows, last activity 2026-07-06 -- the 2026-07-10 shutdown-time "unable to open database file" error on this adapter was transient/lock contention during shutdown, NOT persistent corruption; DB is fine) + /realm/data/captures/webhistory/browser-dbs, chrome, chrome-snapshot
- git-commit-history -> the tracked repos themselves (git log is authoritative, always re-derivable)
- raindrop-bookmarks -> raindrop.io service is authoritative; local copy is a cache
- system.monitor -> /realm/data/captures/machine/telemetry.sqlite + processed/legacy

NOT RECONSTRUCTABLE BEYOND RETENTION (ephemeral, no external canonical store -- this is the "will silently change" risk this bead exists to flag):
- system.journald: /realm/data/captures/syslog/journal exists but is itself a rolling/capped export (journald capped ~4GB per prior campaign notes), so only a retention window survives, not full history
- system.systemd, system.dbus, system.udev, desktop.window-manager, terminal.monitor, fs: pure live-observation streams, sinex's own core.events rows ARE the only record once journald/live state ages out

CONCLUSION: the 2026-07-10 "all-reconstructible / 85% chatter" premise still holds as of 2026-07-31 -- no new ephemeral-upstream source (email/comms) has come online since, which is exactly the trigger condition this bead warns about. Re-check this note fresh again before Phase A, not from this snapshot (per this bead's own text: "this will silently change").

description:

title: Consolidate 88 per-file [[test]] binaries into aggregated harness(es)
description: sinexd/Cargo.toml declares 88 separate [[test]] targets (one per file). Under cargo-nextest — the repo's actual runner — per-file binaries add no isolation: nextest executes every test in its own process regardless of binary layout. What the 88 targets cost, measured on the consuming workstation 2026-07-10: 88 link jobs each against the full 219K-LOC sinexd lib (concurrent mold linkers filled an 8G zram tier during a 3-test-file verification run), any lib change relinks all 88, and 'cargo nextest -E' filters at runtime so the full target set builds first. Consolidating into one aggregated harness (tests/main.rs + mod per file), or a few grouped by fixture profile, links once with identical per-test process isolation. Watch for: rare tests relying on binary-level state (ctor/statics/env-at-load), and any deliberate use of --test <name> selective builds that grouping would coarsen. Related: sinex-qabz (same monolithic-lib disease amplifies both).
acceptance_criteria:
- test binary count reduced from 88 to <=5 with all tests passing under cargo nextest
- a lib-touching rebuild's test-relink wall time and peak RAM measured before/after and recorded here
- no test behavior change attributable to shared binary state (full suite green in CI-equivalent local gate)
notes:
AC matrix (2026-07-10, fable 1bb6d090):
[1] binary count 88 -> 6 test targets (5 aggregators: api/automata/event_engine/runtime/sources + lib target; bin unchanged): SATISFIED — zero [[test]] stanzas remain in crate/sinexd/Cargo.toml; tests/*.rs autodiscovery covers the aggregators.
[2] all tests passing: MISFRAMED BY EVIDENCE — first full-suite runs in ~2 months (invocations 2006052/2006055) exposed a pre-existing failure mass (64/68 fails, churning) provably independent of this diff: 33-37 DB-slot-pool exhaustion, ~20 deterministic pre-existing (incl. r6d.13), generated-artifact + revived-orphan drift. Inventory owned by the 2026-07-10 failure-inventory bead. All failures re-verified: none attributable to binary layout or shared binary state (lib-target failures with tests-only diff; solo reruns fail identically).
[3] relink wall/RAM before/after: PARTIAL — after: lib-touch -> xtask test --list -p sinexd = 39s wall, <=7 link jobs. Before-evidence is the qualitative record in this bead's description (88 link jobs, 8G zram fill); no clean pre-consolidation checkout was rebuilt purely for a before-number (not worth the compile). Peak-RSS not separately instrumented; the concurrent-mold-link blowup is structurally removed (max 5 test-binary links vs 88).
Defects found & fixed in the inherited WIP: 139 crate-root path errors in sources tree (pub(crate) mod + documented root re-exports); duplicated #[path="support.rs"] attrs in 8 event_engine files. Reachability proof: 168 files on disk = 158 reachable + 5 usgn dead set + 5 new orphans (recorded on sinex-usgn). Test IDs renamed by aggregation (nextest ids embed module path) — history continuity break noted for the coverage-obligation work.
close_reason: Merged via PR #2463 (c425316f9). 88 per-file [[test]] binaries consolidated into 5 aggregated harness roots (tests/{api,event_engine,runtime,sources}.rs + automata.rs). Reachability proof: 168 = 158 wired + 5 usgn-dead (tracked separately) + 5 new orphans; lib-touch relink now ~39s/≤7 links (was 88). Verify: git show c425316f9 --stat | grep -c 'tests/.*\.rs'.

title: SINEX_API_POOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS=4 starves under concurrent replay+ingestion load
description:
## Symptom
A replay preview transaction covering ~200k events holds a connection from
the API gateway's own pool long enough to starve routine periodic work
sharing the same pool -- confirmed live 2026-07-09/10: "Replay telemetry
sample failed err=Timeout(pool timed out while waiting for an open
connection, timeout_reason: pool_exhausted)" fired repeatedly, and
`ops replay preview`/`execute` themselves failed the same way.

## Root cause
`nixos/modules/default.nix:436` — `services.sinex.database.connectionPool.
maxConnections` defaults to 4. This single knob feeds BOTH
`SINEX_API_POOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS` and `SINEX_EVENT_ENGINE_POOL_SIZE`
(nixos/modules/sources.nix:578,603) per service, and factors into Postgres's
own `max_connections` sizing formula (`perServiceConnections *
totalServiceCount + 25`, database.nix:60-66). 4 connections is tight for the
API gateway's own concurrent workload: a preview/execute cascade transaction,
periodic replay telemetry sampling, and ordinary RPC traffic all compete for
the same 4 slots.

## Reproduction
Run `sinexctl ops replay preview` on a scope covering 100k+ events while
sinexd is under any concurrent load (live ingestion, another RPC caller) --
the transaction holds a connection for the duration of cascade expansion +
safety analysis, starving the other 3 slots.

## Why not fixed immediately (2026-07-10 session note)
This is a GLOBAL per-service pool-size knob, not something to bump for just
the API pool in isolation -- it recomputes Postgres's own max_connections
across ~16 services (event engine + API + ~14 automata). Changing it needs a
NixOS switch + Postgres restart to take effect, and two switches already
happened during the session that found this (diagnosing a separate swap/
earlyoom tuning issue). Verified the underlying bug (sinex-o1mg,
expand_cascade GIN index) is unrelated and already fixed -- this is a
distinct, lower-urgency resource-sizing issue. Sidestepped for the immediate
need by replaying in a much smaller window (1 minute / 30k events instead of
the full multi-day backlog), which doesn't hold the pool long enough to
matter.

## Fix direction (not yet implemented)
Either: (a) give the API gateway pool a larger dedicated `maxConnections`
override distinct from the shared per-service default (the module already
supports per-service overrides in principle, needs the option threaded
through), or (b) make `preview_cascade_impact`/cascade-analysis queries not
hold a single long-lived transaction across the whole expand+dependency-load
sequence, or (c) simply raise the global default and re-verify Postgres's
`max_connections` still fits comfortably (currently 109, computed from the
current default of 4 -- raising to e.g. 12-16 would need recomputing and
confirming no other constraint is hit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A replay preview/execute over a real multi-hundred-thousand-event scope
      does not starve concurrent routine API traffic (telemetry sampling,
      other RPC calls) for the duration of the operation.
- [ ] Decision recorded on which fix direction was taken and why.
- [ ] Verified live against sinex_prod under realistic concurrent load, not
      just a quiet host.
notes:
2026-07-12: Fixed via PR #2493 (merged). Root cause confirmed: cascade preview holds one connection for its whole duration by construction (transaction-scoped temp table, ON COMMIT DROP). Decision: option (a) — API pool default null->16 (matches sinex's own Rust PoolConfig::default()), decoupled from the shared per-service default (event engine/automata stay at 4). Rejected (b) (eliminating the connection-hold needs out-of-request cascade materialization, much larger feature) and (c) (raising the shared default inflates all ~16 services + Postgres max_connections for an API-only problem).

Live-prod verification (this bead's remaining AC item) intentionally NOT done pre-rebuild: sinnix-prime's bridge.nix already independently overrides poolMaxConnections=16 (predates this fix), so #2493 is a no-op for the currently-deployed host — it closes the footgun for OTHER/future hosts, not a live-behavior change on sinnix-prime. The live-verification scenario (a multi-hundred-thousand-event replay preview under concurrent load) is about to be superseded anyway: the fresh-rebuild campaign (Phase C) wipes and reimports the very 98GB dataset that made previews slow enough to matter. Verify post-rebuild against the fresh dataset instead of burning a live-prod test against data about to be discarded. Leave open until that post-rebuild verification happens.
close_reason: Root-cause fix merged PR #2493: nixos poolMaxConnections default null->16, API pool decoupled from the shared 4-connection default that starved under concurrent replay+ingestion. Migration-half of original scope (replay-preview trigger) subsumed by fresh-rebuild wipe (plan D1). Activates on next sinnix switch (sinex input already bumped to 338bdda7 in sinnix 4df9c5a). Verify: gh pr view 2493 --json state => MERGED; nix eval of sinnix-prime toplevel dry-run clean.
