comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] NixOS config default change (poolMaxConnections null->16); verified via gh pr state + nix eval dry-run per its own close reason, not a Rust-testable code path

title: replay_event_sources() alias table doesn't know per-source dotted SourceContract ids, only 4 legacy umbrella names
description: Live incident 2026-07-09 (sinex-60r's AW replay attempt): ReplayScope::replay_event_sources() (crate/sinex-db/src/replay/state_machine.rs) maps a replay scope's source_name to the actual events.source value(s) it should match, via a hand-maintained match statement. It only has cases for 4 legacy umbrella names (filesystem-watcher, terminal-watcher, desktop-watcher, system-watcher) -- NOT the current per-source dotted SourceContract ids (desktop.activitywatch, desktop.clipboard, desktop.window-manager, terminal.atuin-history, etc, per crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/**) that are what operators actually pass to --source today and what sinexctl sources list/show surface as the canonical identifier. A replay scoped to any such id that has NO case in the match (the overwhelming majority -- grepped ~35 registered contract ids, only 1 legacy umbrella maps a subset) silently matches ZERO events: no error, no warning, preview just reports total_events=0 regardless of the time window, indistinguishable from 'this source genuinely has no data in this window'.
design: Two paths: (1) stopgap, already applied for desktop.activitywatch -> activitywatch as cases are discovered live (same pattern the existing 4-case table already uses) -- does not scale, will keep silently under-matching for every other untested contract id; (2) structural fix -- derive replay_event_sources() from the actual SourceContract registry (crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/**, the id/source_id declared per contract) instead of hand-maintaining a parallel list in sinex-db, which is a different crate with no current dependency on the runtime source registry. This is the SAME failure shape as sinex-dffy (sinnix's stream-topology mkForce override silently diverging from sinex's nats.nix defaults) -- a hand-maintained alias/list table drifting from its authoritative source. Consider whether both deserve the same general fix pattern (a canonical exported mapping both sides consume) rather than solving each one-off.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered SourceContract id resolves correctly via a replay scope's --source flag without needing a hand-added case; OR replay creation validates source_name against the registry and rejects/warns on an id that resolves to zero possible events.source matches, rather than silently previewing/executing an empty scope. A regression test proves at least one currently-broken contract id (before the desktop.activitywatch stopgap, or a different untested one) now resolves correctly.
notes: Discovered and stopgap-fixed live while attempting sinex-60r's ActivityWatch replay. Every sinexctl ops replay preview attempt against --source desktop.activitywatch returned Direct Events: 0 regardless of time window (tested 24h, 1-day, 1-week, 27-day windows, both before and after cancelling/replanning) until this was traced to the alias gap -- cost significant diagnostic time because the failure mode (silent zero-match) is indistinguishable from 'no data in this window'.
close_reason: SUBSUMED by fresh-rebuild campaign (2026-07-11). replay_event_sources() alias-table scoping is REPLAY tooling; the campaign re-imports raw materials rather than scoping replays by source id, so the bug has no live surface.

title: sinnix's mkForce stream-list override silently shadows sinex's own nats.nix defaults
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add or modify a stream declaration in sinex's nixos/modules/nats.nix bootstrapStreams.streams default list (e.g. sinex-bor's PR #2423 adding 5 reflection-lane streams).
2. Bump sinnix's flake.lock sinex input to a rev including that change.
3. nix develop --command switch on a host whose services.sinex config sets bootstrapStreams.streams via lib.mkForce (modules/services/sinex/bridge.nix).
4. Observe: sinex-nats-bootstrap.service runs and exits 0, but the new/changed streams are never created -- mkForce replaced the whole list, sinex's new defaults never entered the merge at all.
5. sinexd (if the runtime hard-gates on topology completeness, per sinex-bor) refuses to start; or (if it doesn't) silently runs against an incomplete topology.
design: Two paths sinex-bor's own close reason already named as deferred: (A) change bootstrapStreams.streams (or a sibling option) to support per-stream-name field overrides merged against sinex's own defaults, so a downstream flake only declares deltas (e.g. sinnix's maxBytes=null workaround for natscli's 32-bit limit on the raw/confirmed streams) instead of the whole topology; (B) sinex-bor's original larger-scope idea -- a Rust-exported canonical JSON stream-topology spec consumed by both nix and the runtime bootstrap, with downstream flakes only able to express recognized deltas against it, so an omitted stream is a build-time/eval-time error rather than a silent runtime refusal six days later. Either path should make 'sinex changed its stream defaults, sinnix wasn't updated' impossible to express, not just 'harder to get wrong'.
acceptance_criteria: A change to sinex's nixos/modules/nats.nix stream defaults (add/modify a stream) is either automatically inherited by sinnix's bootstrapStreams config, or produces a loud eval-time/build-time signal that sinnix needs updating -- never a silent runtime gap discovered only when sinexd refuses to serve. sinnix's bridge.nix no longer hand-copies stream definitions that are byte-identical to sinex's own defaults.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED — Path A (attrset delta-merge). 2026-07-12.

Chose Path A over Path B (Rust-exported canonical JSON spec): Path A is a
Nix-only refactor, zero Rust changes, no generated-surface plumbing, fully
verifiable by nix eval. Path B would duplicate the runtime's existing Rust-side
stream config across a JSON bridge for the same guarantee. Path A already makes
"sinex changed its defaults, sinnix wasn't updated" impossible to express:
downstream inherits by default.

Mechanism: services.sinex.nats.bootstrapStreams.streams is now attrsOf submodule
keyed by logical stream name (name sub-option dropped; key IS the name). Sinex
ships its canonical topology at config level as
`mapAttrs (_: mapAttrs (_: mkDefault)) defaultBootstrapStreams` — mkDefault on
EACH LEAF, not the whole attrset (a whole-attrset mkDefault is discarded the
moment a downstream defines any stream, since priority filtering precedes the
attrset merge — that would reintroduce the bug). namespacedStreams switched
map->mapAttrsToList. No consumer outside nats.nix reads .streams/.name (verified).

sinnix bridge.nix: mkForce whole-list (13 hand-copied entries) replaced by a
6-key delta attrset — SINEX_RAW_EVENTS {maxAge=168h,maxBytes=null},
SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_CONFIRMED.maxBytes=null, DLQ/PROCESSING_FAILURES maxAge=168h,
plus 2 host-local confirmation-lane streams (events.confirmations.>,
events.confirmation_retries.>; NOT in sinex canonical, unused by current Rust but
preserved as host additions). -104/+31 lines. Inheriting canonical also REPAIRS
prior drift the old list silently carried (RAW retention limits->work; DLQ/PF
gained discard=new/allowDirect=true/dupeWindow=1h).

VERIFIED (nix eval, evalModules over the real self.nixosModules.default):
- Downstream applying sinnix's EXACT deltas => 13 streams (11 canonical inherited
  + 2 host-added), field-level merge correct (deltas win, canonical inherited).
- Downstream declaring ZERO streams => all 11 canonical unchanged.
- xtask check --nix: all 5 nats-consuming VM host configs (sinex-basic-flow,
  sinex-chaos-*) evaluate to .drv; the only flake-check failure is a PRE-EXISTING
  `undefined variable 'sinexd'` in tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/
  failure-recovery.nix:10 (present on origin/master, untouched here, unrelated).

DEPLOY NOTE: JetStream retention is immutable post-creation. RAW retention
limits->work is harmless under the approved fresh-rebuild (streams recreate
fresh); against live streams it needs RAW recreation.

BRANCHES (NOT merged — left for coordinator):
- sinex PR #2494: https://github.com/Sinity/sinex/pull/2494
  branch feature/fix/nats-bootstrap-stream-deltas (commit c3d5efd0f)
- sinnix branch feature/fix/sinex-nats-stream-deltas (commit 77d085a) — HOLDING;
  land coupled with flake.lock bump to the merged sinex rev (old list-typed sinex
  input rejects the attrset). sinnix full-host eval currently also blocked by an
  unrelated uncommitted WIP (modules/services/sinex-dev-db-reaper.nix untracked +
  referenced by hosts/sinnix-prime) — not mine.
close_reason: Fixed both sides: sinex PR #2494 makes nats bootstrapStreams a delta-mergeable attrsOf submodule with per-leaf mkDefault (canonical 11-stream topology owned by sinex); sinnix 4df9c5a rewrites bridge.nix from a 13-entry whole-list mkForce to 6 host-specific deltas + bumps sinex input to 338bdda7 atomically. Topology changes on the sinex side now propagate instead of being silently shadowed. Verify: nix build .#nixosConfigurations.sinnix-prime.config.system.build.toplevel --dry-run evaluates clean; sinnix pushed (42f42e9..4df9c5a).

title: jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery deterministically fails: fail_confirmations(3) exhausts CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS
description: Discovered while adding sinex-r6d.12's missing multi-child settlement test coverage (PR #2440).
design:
crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/events_consumer_integration_test.rs::jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery
currently fails deterministically on master (verified 2026-07-09, isolated rerun, exit 101):

  Error: no message available in stream ..._CONFIRMED for subject ...confirm-retry...: no message found

Root cause: the test calls `TestHooks::builder().count_deliveries().fail_confirmations(3)`.
`fail_confirmations(3)` forces the counter-decrementing failure hook in
crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/confirmation.rs::publish_confirmed_event to
fail on every call while the counter is > 0. `publish_confirmed_event_with_retry` attempts
exactly CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 tries (confirmation.rs). With only ONE confirmable
event in the test and a forced-failure budget of exactly 3, ALL 3 in-process retries are
consumed and fail -- there is no successful attempt left. The batch then returns a
confirmation_durability_gap_error, which is_fatal_batch_processing_error() classifies as
fatal in run_loop.rs, so the consumer's run() returns Err and the task exits. The test then
waits (Timeouts::SHORT) for a confirmed-events stream message that will never appear, since
nothing is polling anymore, and fails on timeout.

The test's own name/intent ("republishes ... without raw redelivery") clearly wants: force
FEWER failures than the retry budget, so the LAST in-process attempt succeeds and the
confirmed event ships without needing JetStream to redeliver the raw message. That requires
`fail_confirmations(2)`, not `fail_confirmations(3)` -- off-by-one against
CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS.

Predates sinex-r6d.12: confirmation.rs's CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS and run_loop.rs's fatal
error handling were NOT touched by PR #2425 (r6d.12's RawEnvelopeSettlement landing) --
verified via `git show 4cf3a90bc --stat`. This is a pre-existing, orthogonal test bug, not a
regression from the settlement coordinator work.

Likely fix: change `.fail_confirmations(3)` to `.fail_confirmations(2)` in
events_consumer_integration_test.rs (single-line test fix), then re-verify the test actually
exercises in-process retry-then-succeed as its name claims.

Verification commands run:
  xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'
  (isolated run, single-threaded target) -> FAILED, exit code 101, as described above.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery passes in isolation
  and asserts genuine in-process retry-then-succeed (delivery count stays 1, confirmed event
  is published, idempotent persist count == 1).
- Root cause (off-by-one between fail_confirmations() budget and
  CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS) is fixed at the test call site, or CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS
  is deliberately reconsidered if the intended contract differs from "N < max forces recovery,
  N >= max forces a durability gap".
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. On current master (verified at commit 0ad01fcca / after PR #2425 sinex-r6d.12 landed):
   env DATABASE_URL=<live dev DB> nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd \
     -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'
2. Observe: FAILED, exit 101, "Error: no message available in stream ..._CONFIRMED for
   subject ...: no message found" (crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/support.rs:143).
3. Reproduces deterministically (not load/timing-dependent) because
   fail_confirmations(3) == CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) exactly -- see design notes.
2026-07-31 (sinex-amg2 test-suite-health pass): re-verified in isolation, quiet host — still fails identically. Same error signature: "no message available in stream ..._CONFIRMED for subject ...confirm-retry...: no message found" at crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/support.rs:143. `fail_confirmations(3)` is still the value at events_consumer_integration_test.rs:622. Not touched this pass (already tracked here with a clear diagnosis and fix — change to `fail_confirmations(2)` — out of amg2's scope, which only re-confirms it's unchanged, not something new).
close_reason:
Fixed: changed .fail_confirmations(3) to .fail_confirmations(2) in
crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/events_consumer_integration_test.rs
(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery),
as originally diagnosed, with an inline comment recording why.

## Closure Evidence Manifest

Acceptance criteria:
- "jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery
  passes in isolation and asserts genuine in-process retry-then-succeed
  (delivery count stays 1, confirmed event is published, idempotent persist
  count == 1)." -- SATISFIED. The test's existing assertions already checked
  all three (deliveries==1 wait, confirmed-event message on the CONFIRMED
  stream, count==1 idempotency query); only the fail_confirmations parameter
  was wrong. Verified passing in isolation twice:
    DATABASE_URL=<worktree dev DB> xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' \
      -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'
  -> "test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed" (both runs).
- "Root cause (off-by-one between fail_confirmations() budget and
  CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS) is fixed at the test call site" -- SATISFIED,
  fixed at the call site exactly as diagnosed. No production code changed.

## Reconciliation with sinex-5smc (closed as duplicate, pointing here)

sinex-5smc raised a legitimate deeper question: is the fatal
crash-on-durability-gap behavior (full exhaustion of
CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS -> confirmation_durability_gap_error ->
is_fatal_batch_processing_error -> JetStreamConsumer::run() returns Err,
killing a "critical task" in event_engine/service.rs) a real production gap,
or is fail_confirmations(2) merely dodging a boundary condition?

Investigated directly (confirmation.rs, run_loop.rs, service.rs, plus git
archaeology on `git show 2322eb0d2`, PR #196, 2026-03-27): the crash+restart
design IS intentional (CLAUDE.md: "confirmed publish GATES the ack
(durability gap = redelivery)" -- recovery is via systemd process restart +
JetStream redelivering the unacked raw message to a fresh consumer
instance). But this specific test was DELIBERATELY repurposed in PR #196
away from testing that scenario: its assertion changed from `deliveries >=
2` to `deliveries == 1` at the same time it was renamed from
jetstream_consumer_redelivers_when_confirmation_publish_fails to
jetstream_consumer_queues_durable_confirmation_retries_without_raw_redelivery
(current name after a later rename). The `fail_confirmations(3)` argument
was simply never updated to match -- a plain leftover off-by-one, not
evidence of a missing recovery mechanism. fail_confirmations(2) correctly
exercises real, already-existing production behavior: the in-process
backoff-retry loop inside publish_confirmed_event_with_retry recovering
within its budget, which is exactly what this test's current name and
assertions describe.

Anti-vacuity: this is a test-parameter-only fix, not a production-code fix.
What would make it fail again: reverting fail_confirmations() to 3 (or any
value >= CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS), or a regression in
publish_confirmed_event_with_retry's retry/backoff loop that stops it from
succeeding on the final attempt within budget.

The one real gap sinex-5smc surfaced -- the full-exhaustion
crash+restart+redelivery path itself has NO test coverage anywhere in the
suite, since the old test covering it was repurposed rather than duplicated
in PR #196 -- is tracked as a new follow-up, sinex-b0es.

## Verification commands run
- xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'
  -> passed, run twice in isolation.
- xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' -E 'test(jetstream_consumer)' --threads 2
  -> 34/35 passed; the 1 failure (jetstream_consumer_routes_db_failures_to_dlq)
  was confirmed pre-existing and unrelated: reproduced identically in
  isolation on the unmodified tree (stashed this fix, reran, same
  "Timeout: Test condition wait failed" failure), then restored the fix.
- xtask check -p sinexd -> "status": "success", cargo check passed.

title: confirmation durability-gap crashes consumer, contradicting jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery test premise
description:
Confirmation durability-gap crashes the whole consumer task with no non-redelivery recovery
path, contradicting the premise of an existing test that expects durability-gap recovery
WITHOUT raw redelivery.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run: `xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'`
2. Observe failure: "Error: no message available in stream ... confirmation_d_retry: no message found" after ~11-12s (well inside the test's own Timeouts::MEDIUM budget).
3. Confirmed reproducible standalone (no other tests running, no host contention) — not a resource-contention flake.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Either: durability-gap recovery no longer requires the SAME dead consumer instance to survive (fix option 1 or 3 in the design notes), and this test passes without modification.
- [ ] Or: the fatal-crash-on-durability-gap behavior is confirmed as the intended design, and this test is corrected to assert the crash + redelivery-based recovery it was originally written to test (fix option 2), with its name reverted to reflect that.
- [ ] Whichever path is chosen, the decision and rationale get recorded in this bead before closing.
design:
Discovered while implementing sinex-r6d.12 (aggregate-safe raw-message settlement).

The test `jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery`
(crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/events_consumer_integration_test.rs) forces
exactly 3 confirmation-publish failures via `fail_confirmations(3)`, which
exactly matches `CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`
(crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/confirmation.rs). This
exhausts every internal retry attempt inside a SINGLE
`publish_confirmed_event_with_retry` call, so it always returns Err.

That Err becomes a `confirmation_durability_gap` (persist.rs /
prepare.rs), which `run_loop.rs::is_fatal_batch_processing_error` treats as
FATAL: the whole consumer task exits via `return Err(e)`. Nothing in the
test harness (`spawn_consumer_and_wait_ready` — a single bare `tokio::spawn`,
no supervisor/restart loop) restarts the consumer. The raw message is
deliberately left unacked ("left_unacked_for_redelivery" per
`confirmation_durability_gap_error`), but since the consumer task is dead,
nobody pulls it again within the test's `Timeouts::MEDIUM` window — the test
times out waiting for the confirmed-events message ("no message found").

Verified via `git log -p -S` archaeology: this test's core assertion
(`deliveries == 1`, i.e. no raw redelivery needed) was introduced in PR #196
(2026, very early history) as a rename from
`jetstream_consumer_redelivers_when_confirmation_publish_fails`
(which asserted `deliveries >= 2`). The rename's rationale is not documented
in that commit body, and no reconciliation/backfill mechanism that would
let a durability-gapped event's confirmation get retried WITHOUT crashing
the consumer currently exists anywhere in crate/sinexd/src (grepped for
unconfirmed/confirmation_backfill/reconcil — nothing matches). Either the
test's premise stopped being true when some later refactor made durability
gaps fatal, or a repair mechanism that used to exist was since removed.

Verified this is NOT caused by sinex-r6d.12 (envelope settlement
coordinator): for this exact single-event-single-message scenario, old code
(`ack_messages.push` skipped on gap, function still returns
`confirmation_durability_gap_error` at the end) and new code (settle_child
skipped on gap, same Err returned) produce byte-identical outcomes — zero
difference in the diff touches this path's fatal/crash semantics.

Fix options (未 investigated in depth):
1. Make durability gaps non-fatal: keep the raw message unacked, let the
   SAME consumer instance retry via an internal backoff loop or a bounded
   local requeue, rather than crashing and relying on redelivery it may
   never get in the fast path.
2. Restore true crash-and-redeliver semantics and fix this specific test's
   `deliveries == 1` assertion instead (revert to expecting redelivery).
3. Add a genuine unconfirmed-event reconciliation sweep at consumer
   startup/restart that republishes from Postgres for events durably
   persisted but never confirmed — this is closer to the test's original
   intent and would also plug a real operator gap (a crashed consumer today
   has NO automatic way to close this gap outside of raw redelivery, which
   this specific failure mode explicitly avoids).

Verification: run in isolation (no contention):
`xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'`
acceptance_criteria:
Either: durability-gap recovery no longer requires the SAME dead consumer instance to survive
(fix option 1 or 3 in the design notes), and the affected test passes without modification.
Or: the fatal-crash-on-durability-gap behavior is confirmed as the intended design, and that
test is corrected to assert the crash + redelivery-based recovery it was originally written to
test (fix option 2), with its name reverted to reflect that. Whichever path is chosen, the
decision and rationale get recorded in this bead before closing.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run: xtask test -p sinexd --test '*' -E 'test(jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)'
2. Observe failure: "Error: no message available in stream ... confirmation_d_retry: no message found" after ~11-12s (well inside the test's own Timeouts::MEDIUM budget).
3. Confirmed reproducible standalone (no other tests running, no host contention) — not a resource-contention flake.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Either: durability-gap recovery no longer requires the SAME dead consumer instance to survive (fix option 1 or 3 above), and this test passes without modification.
- [ ] Or: the fatal-crash-on-durability-gap behavior is confirmed as the intended design, and this test is corrected to assert the crash + redelivery-based recovery it was originally written to test (fix option 2), with its name reverted to reflect that.
- [ ] Whichever path is chosen, the decision and rationale get recorded in this bead before closing.
close_reason:
Reconciled as a duplicate of sinex-r6d.13, which tracked the same failing test
with a more precise diagnosis. Full investigation and decision recorded on
sinex-r6d.13's closure; summary here:

This bead's premise -- that durability-gap recovery needs a genuine unbuilt
non-redelivery mechanism ("fix option 1 or 3") for the test to pass -- does
NOT hold. Investigation (production code reading + git archaeology) showed:

1. `fail_confirmations(3) == CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS` exhausts every
   in-process retry attempt inside publish_confirmed_event_with_retry
   (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/confirmation.rs), which
   IS a real fatal path (is_fatal_batch_processing_error ->
   JetStreamConsumer::run() returns Err -> the consumer is tracked as a
   "critical task" in event_engine/service.rs and its death fails the whole
   critical-task set). This design tripwire is intentional per CLAUDE.md's
   documented pipeline stage "confirmed publish GATES the ack (durability
   gap = redelivery)": production recovery is via process restart (systemd
   Restart=on-failure) + JetStream redelivering the unacked raw message to a
   fresh consumer instance.

2. But that full-exhaustion/fatal/restart scenario is NOT what this specific
   test (jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)
   is exercising, and never was after 2026-03-27. `git show 2322eb0d2` (PR
   #196) shows the test's assertion was DELIBERATELY changed at that time
   from `deliveries >= 2` (crash + raw redelivery) to `deliveries == 1`
   (in-process retry succeeds, no redelivery needed) when it was renamed
   from jetstream_consumer_redelivers_when_confirmation_publish_fails to
   jetstream_consumer_queues_durable_confirmation_retries_without_raw_redelivery.
   That rename encoded a real, working design: publish_confirmed_event_with_retry's
   in-process backoff-retry loop already recovers from partial failures
   without ever reaching the fatal path. The `fail_confirmations(3)` call-site
   argument was simply never updated to match the new assertion semantics --
   a plain off-by-one leftover from before the rename, not a hint that a
   missing recovery mechanism needs building.

3. This bead's design notes claimed "no reconciliation/backfill mechanism ...
   rationale not documented in commit body" -- true narrowly (the PR #196
   body doesn't explain the rename), but the diff itself makes the intent
   unambiguous once read directly.

Resolution: sinex-r6d.13's mechanical fix (fail_confirmations(2)) is correct
and sufficient -- no production code changes were needed or made. This is a
test-parameter-only fix; it is verified by construction (2 failures then a
successful 3rd attempt is exactly what publish_confirmed_event_with_retry's
existing retry loop and backoff already implement) and confirmed via
repeated isolated test runs (see sinex-r6d.13 closure).

The one genuine gap this bead surfaced -- the fatal crash+restart+redelivery
path itself has NO test coverage anywhere in the suite (the old test that
covered it was repurposed, not duplicated) -- is real and is now tracked
separately as sinex-b0es, since it needs different test infrastructure
(a way to simulate/exercise a consumer restart) than a same-instance
parameter tweak can provide.

title: Transport/DB boundary fault-injection matrix: error-return faults (not crashes) across NATS publish/ack and PG failure modes
description: Verifiability-audit gap (2026-07-08, polylogue-methodology parity): r6d.9 is SIGKILL-only by design; nothing systematically injects ERROR-RETURN faults at the NATS/DB boundary and asserts settlement outcomes. The verified bug corpus is exactly this class: wb1 (DLQ publish failure swallowed before settlement), w4i (mid-record emit failure re-emits persisted siblings), r6d.4 window (b) (failed record skipped by later cursor merge), spool publish-fail paths. Each was found by manual reading; the class has no test generator. Faults to inject: NATS publish error, publish timeout, ack/flush failure, JetStream NAK/redelivery storms, PG connection drop mid-batch, serialization failure under REPEATABLE READ, COPY failure mid-chunk (bisect path), DLQ-publish failure itself.
design: Shape: fault-injection layer at the two boundary traits (NATS client wrapper, DB pool/repositories) — an injectable decorator enabled in test builds, driven by a fault schedule (fail Nth call / fail matching subject / fail with timeout vs error). Assertion vocabulary mirrors r6d.9: after the fault clears, either the operation completed exactly-once-per-occurrence, or durable debt/DLQ evidence exists, or the frontier is provably unadvanced — silent skip and duplicate-without-supersession both fail. Priority scenario families: (1) DLQ-publish failure during material-assembler finalize (wb1 repro); (2) mid-record multi-intent emit failure (w4i repro); (3) failed-record-then-successful-later-record cursor merge (r6d.4 window b); (4) COPY bisect with a poison row + a transport fault in the same batch; (5) spool write-then-publish-fail interleavings. Integrates with the r6d.9 harness runner where process restart is needed, but most scenarios are in-process (faster loop). Red-before/green-after: wb1 and w4i are open — their scenarios must FAIL on current master, becoming their close proofs.
acceptance_criteria: Injectable fault layer exists for NATS + DB boundaries in test builds; the five priority families implemented; wb1 and w4i scenarios fail on pre-fix master (recorded) and their fix PRs cite the passing scenarios; fault schedules deterministic; runs under xtask test --heavy; loss-window matrix (r6d.1) gains a fault-injection column linking each row to its scenario or an explicit not-covered entry.

title: Model-based settlement/frontier state-machine tests: arbitrary interleavings over receipt + commit-frontier invariants
description: Verifiability-audit gap (2026-07-08, polylogue-methodology parity): r6d.9 proves NAMED killpoints (18 fixed scenarios); nothing explores ARBITRARY interleavings of the settlement/checkpoint/catch-up state machines. The Batch-A primitives (r6d.11 DurableEmissionReceipt states, 4as3 CommitFrontier ordering) are exactly the shape model-based/stateful property testing is built for: generate random operation sequences (emit, receipt-complete out of order, checkpoint-due, crash, restart, redeliver, NAK, DLQ, invalidation) against a reference model and assert the invariants hold in every reachable state — the fixed-killpoint harness cannot cover the interleaving space and the bugs this class catches (out-of-order receipt completion racing frontier advance) are precisely the ones manual review missed for months.
design: Shape: proptest-state-machine (or hand-rolled operation-sequence generator, deterministic seed, minimized counterexample on failure) at the UNIT level over the r6d.11 receipt state machine and 4as3 CommitFrontier — no DB/NATS needed: the durable backend is a fake with injectable completion order and crash points. Invariants: (1) frontier never advances past a non-terminal atom; (2) no progress-unlocking state reachable from RawAccepted/mpsc-send alone; (3) crash+restart from any persisted state never loses an atom that lacked a terminal receipt (either unadvanced or receipt-proven); (4) out-of-order receipt completion never reorders the FIFO commit frontier; (5) reflection/best-effort API can never unlock progress. Runs as ordinary xtask test (fast, no --heavy). Complements r6d.9 (integration/crash) — this is the exploration layer under it. Sensitivity proof: seed the generator against the CURRENT (pre-r6d.11) mpsc-only emit model and show it finds the checkpoint-outruns-output violation automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Operation-sequence generator + reference model land beside the r6d.11/4as3 primitives; all five invariant families asserted; failure output = minimized sequence + seed; finds the pre-fix checkpoint-before-output violation automatically (recorded once); runs in default xtask test for the owning crates; r6d.11/4as3 closes cite it.

title: Replay-vs-live derivation equivalence differential: whole-derived-plane agreement, occurrence-keyed
description: Verifiability-audit gap (2026-07-08, polylogue-methodology parity): nothing proves that replaying a corpus yields the SAME derived plane the live pipeline produced. pdq5 invariant 5 covers interval sets only; qky is restore economics, not agreement; r6d.9 proves crash recovery, not derivation determinism. Replay is the load-bearing repair mechanism (fix-forward doctrine: archive cascade + replay), so a silent replay/live divergence — nondeterministic automaton state, ordering-dependent equivalence keys (the ecy class), rule-version skew — corrupts the derived plane exactly when the operator is trying to repair it. Regression-leak likelihood: HIGH once replay is exercised routinely; today it would be discovered only by manual adversarial reading.
design: Shape: e2e differential in tests/e2e (or xtask sandbox scenario). (1) Ingest a fixed synthetic + sampled-real material corpus through the NORMAL pipeline with all default automata; snapshot the derived plane. (2) Fire a full replay cascade over the same materials. (3) Diff the two derived planes keyed by OCCURRENCE identity (source_material_id, anchor_byte) + event_type + semantics_version — interpretation ids and ts_coided are expected to differ (identity model doctrine); payload content, parent occurrence sets, and derived-interval boundaries must not. Divergence report = machine-readable (kind, occurrence key, field-level diff). Known-legitimate divergence classes (rule version bumped between runs) must be declared, not silently allowed. Interacts: ecy (counter keys are a known determinism bug this suite would have caught — use it as the red-before/green-after sensitivity proof), 908 (regime matrix defines what MUST dedup), n9a (supersession changes the diff contract: compare live rows, archived rows both runs). Wire into impact planner so automaton/replay-touching diffs select it.
acceptance_criteria: Differential harness runs under xtask test --heavy; occurrence-keyed diff over ALL derived kinds, not just intervals; proves sensitivity by red-flagging the ecy counter-key defect on pre-fix code and going green after; legitimate-divergence declarations are explicit in the fixture; divergence report is machine-readable and cited by replay-touching bead closes.
notes: 2026-07-11 REFRAMED by fresh-rebuild campaign: original premise 'replay is the load-bearing repair mechanism' is abandoned (campaign wipes+re-imports, not replay-repair). Repurpose as REBUILD-DETERMINISM proof: a fresh re-import from the same /realm/data archives twice must produce an occurrence-keyed-equivalent derived plane. Still valuable (validates the rebuild is deterministic), but no longer a replay-vs-live differential. Not a bake-in blocker.

title: Cross-provider observation fusion: one canonical composite from multiple witnesses of the same occurrence
description: The purpose sleep-merged actually served — and the general mechanism sinex was missing. When two independent providers witness the SAME real-world episode (Samsung Health and Sleep As Android both record tonight's sleep: SaA carries phase structure, Samsung carries HR-during-sleep), downstream consumers need ONE canonical composite observation, not two overlapping fragments to re-reconcile at every query. This is NOT dedup (908 regime-2 suppresses identical occurrences; here the witnesses are complementary) and NOT rollup (k4c.2 aggregates within a domain-day; here we merge witnesses of one episode). The sinex-native shape: a declared fusion derivation (0vx product class canonical_derived_event) consuming both providers' typed events as parents, matching witnesses by episode identity (time-overlap + subject rules declared per fusion kind; ambiguous matches -> regime-3 adjudication per 908), emitting the composite (sleep.night with phases from SaA + HR/physio from Samsung) with: per-field provenance (which witness supplied which field), a declared conflict policy per field (prefer-provider / widest-interval / adjudicate on disagreement beyond tolerance), agreement level reflected in ClaimSupport (two agreeing witnesses raise source_coverage — the vector was built for exactly this), and LATE-WITNESS revision via the y8v/n9a contract: fused output keys on the episode occurrence, so when the second provider's export arrives weeks later the composite SUPERSEDES rather than duplicates or freezes. First instance: sleep.night over rkv.6 events. Same declared shape later serves weight-from-multiple-scales, location-from-multiple-devices, calendar-from-multiple-accounts. Lynchpin's sleep_merged_summary.csv is parity evidence for the sleep instance, never an input.
acceptance_criteria: Fusion derivations are declared data (witness kinds, episode-matching rule, per-field conflict policy, tolerance thresholds) not bespoke automata per pair; sleep.night lands as the first instance with per-field provenance and both parents; single-witness nights emit with honest single-witness ClaimSupport (no fabricated completeness); disagreement beyond tolerance emits an adjudication candidate, never a silent pick; a late second-provider import supersedes the single-witness composite exactly once (n9a fixture); parity vs lynchpin sleep_merged day-slice recorded in the k4c.3 ledger; baselines/rollups consume sleep.night, not raw fragments.

title: Judgment staleness: accepted claims re-open when their evidence is superseded
description: pf54 handles PRE-acceptance proposals; nothing handles POST-acceptance: an operator judgment (accepted claim, entity merge, lane promotion) sits on evidence that supersession (n9a), replay, redaction, or purge (new8) can archive or replace — after which the system keeps presenting the judgment as if its grounds were intact. Knowledge-decay honesty: when the evidence set under an accepted judgment changes materially, the judgment is FLAGGED stale-evidence (never silently reverted — the operator's ruling stands until the operator revisits), the ClaimSupport adjudication axis gains a stale-evidence state rendered by the design-language support scale, dependent surfaces caveat it, and the judgment seat offers a low-priority revisit queue (subject to the pf54 no-nag budget). Mechanically this rides the same cascade: the supersession/replay invalidation walk (68c.4 / n9a) already touches descendants — extend the walk to judgment events whose evidence refs intersect the invalidated set.
acceptance_criteria: Supersession/replay/purge cascades mark judgments whose evidence refs intersect the affected set; stale-evidence is a typed adjudication state, rendered distinctly (never as reduced confidence); affected read surfaces caveat claims resting on stale-evidence judgments; revisit queue in the seat ordered by impact, respecting the pf54 budget; the operator ruling is never auto-reverted; fixture: accept a claim, supersede its evidence via n9a, observe flag + caveat + revisit entry with the original ruling intact.

description: The cheapest highest-leverage capture that does not exist: a global hotkey (Hyprland bind -> tiny client) that mints an operator.mark event in under a second, carrying refs to the current context (active window/attention state, foreground terminal, optional 3-second annotation via a popup or voice-note file anchor). Doctrine: marks are operator-provenance events on the activity lane with material anchors to a tiny capture record; no interpretation at capture time.

title: Prospective memory: context tripwires — intents that resurface when the moment matches
description: The exocortex currently only remembers BACKWARD; an exocortex worth the name also carries the operator's declared future intents and resurfaces them at the contextually right moment — which is exactly what AuDHD working memory drops. Mechanism (all existing planes, no new machinery classes): a tripwire = operator-declared (trigger-pattern, payload-intent, expiry, arm/disarm state) stored as events; a ScopeReconciler-family automaton (the instruction_reconciler shape — desired-state loops already exist for instructions) watches the confirmed stream for pattern matches (attention.span subject matches repo X; source family becomes active; an entity appears; a calendar block starts) and emits a tripwire.fired candidate; delivery respects the o6w notification budget — fired tripwires surface in Today's Resume pane and optionally one push if the operator marked it urgent, never a nag queue. Examples: 'when I next open sinex repo, surface: the y8v veto window'; 'when person P appears in comms, surface: the thing I owe them'; 'if no commit lands in repo Y for 14 days, surface once'. Distinct from 7z0.9 (events trigger AGENT sessions): tripwires trigger OPERATOR resurfacing; 7z0.9 can later consume the same trigger grammar. Distinct from 9cs (predictions): tripwires are intents, not forecasts. Expiry/decay follows the pf54 philosophy: expired tripwires retire to a queryable dormant state with zero noise.

title: Automaton lifecycle consolidation: one prepare/emit/receipt/commit core under capability flags
description: Four wrapper impls bridge Transducer/Windowed/ScopeReconciler(+adapter automata) onto one Automaton trait through ~800 lines of per-wrapper glue (runtime/automaton/traits.rs), and four in-flight campaigns must each thread through every path: the vxu prepare/commit split, r6d.11 receipt awaiting, 5s6 watermark/timer flush, and 0vx.2 DerivedOutput declaration metadata. Without consolidation each campaign is a 4x cross-product patch (the timer_flush_derived default-empty + per-wrapper override pattern shows the drift shape already). Target: ONE core lifecycle — accumulate(input) -> prepare(outputs) -> emit(awaiting receipts per r6d.11) -> commit(frontier per the CommitFrontier primitive) — with model differences expressed as capability flags/policies (windowing, flush_due, scope keying) instead of parallel wrapper code paths. This is COORDINATION architecture: land the core as part of the first campaign that needs it (vxu or r6d.11), then the other campaigns are single-path changes. Explicitly not a big-bang rewrite — the wrappers shrink to adapters over the core incrementally.
design:
DESIGN (2026-07-08, written with the full ratified Batch-A context; receipt backend (A) is FINAL so this can be concrete):

CORE LIFECYCLE — one generic engine, four strict phases:
1. ACCUMULATE: feed inputs to the model; may mutate only the IN-MEMORY working set; watermark evaluation (5s6 two-mode) happens here and may set flush_due. No progress marks, no persisted-state writes.
2. PREPARE: pure. Produces PreparedOutputs (typed events + 0vx.2 DerivedOutput declarations attached here) + a StateDelta (e.g. accumulator reset, window close) + a ProgressAtom description (AutomatonInputBatch or WindowFlush{flush_id}). MUST NOT mutate persisted state — the session.rs:171/analytics.rs:293 mem::take-at-emit bug class is structurally impossible because take moves to COMMIT.
3. EMIT: submit PreparedOutputs via the r6d.11 emit_batch_durable API; await receipt per progress atom. NoOutputSettled is an explicit receipt (benign no-output paths need durable evidence per vxu AC).
4. COMMIT: only on receipt.unlocks_progress(): apply StateDelta to persisted state, mark inputs processed via CommitFrontier (4as3), checkpoint = frontier payload. Crash before commit = inputs unadvanced, replay re-derives; crash after = outputs provably durable. This IS the vxu reorder, implemented once.

CAPABILITY FLAGS (per model, replacing per-wrapper glue): has_accumulator (Windowed), has_timer_flush (mints flush_id in PREPARE; flush StateDelta applies at COMMIT), scope_recompute (ScopeReconciler: invalidation delivery handles retained until settlement — r6d.7 falls out of the core), historical_catchup. manages_own_checkpoints DISAPPEARS: checkpoint payload is always the CommitFrontier state, so the bridge-KV-inert-for-adapters split (vxu headline) is dissolved rather than patched.

MIGRATION ORDER: Transducer first (stateless; prepare = transform — cheapest behavior-identical proof), then Windowed (accumulate + timer flush + shutdown barrier), then ScopeReconciler (invalidation atoms). Shutdown = drain: refuse final state save past unsettled receipts; final checkpoint covers only the committed frontier (replaces adapter/mod.rs:545-574 save-regardless).

INTERLOCKS: vxu + r6d.7 + 5s6 flush + 0vx.2 declarations all become route-through-the-core rather than 4x wrapper patches (that is the point of this bead); 87hu model-based tests exercise the phase machine directly. PITFALL: one wrapper per PR with behavior-identical tests; do not migrate all three at once.
acceptance_criteria: Core lifecycle type exists; at least two of the three wrapper paths route through it with behavior-identical tests; the vxu prepare/commit split and receipt awaiting are implemented ONCE in the core (wrapper-specific emit/state mutation deleted for migrated paths); capability flags documented; remaining wrapper migration tracked with no dual-maintenance of lifecycle logic for migrated models.

title: Schema expectation IR: apply, converge, strict-diff, and docs as interpreters of one typed source of truth
description: The schema engine is three hand-maintained interpretations of the same defs — apply.rs 2,972 + converge.rs 1,401 + strict_diff.rs 996 lines — and they VERIFIABLY drift: strict_diff's comments claim CREATE-OR-REPLACE-every-apply while apply skips on trigger-name existence (the lcj finding); strict DbCheck accepts extra literals that apply rejects (a 2pl finding); diff covers required-index subsets apply repairs silently. Every new invariant is currently written 2-3 times and the copies disagree. The abstraction: a typed Expectation IR generated from defs (TableExpectation, ColumnExpectation{type,generated,default,collation}, ConstraintExpectation{normalized body}, IndexExpectation{def,predicate,opclass}, TriggerExpectation{timing,mask,when,target,enabled}, FunctionExpectation{def hash}, PolicyExpectation{retention,compression,cagg refresh}) — with apply=make-true interpreter, strict-diff=verify-true interpreter, converge=delta subset, docs=render, over the SAME expectations. 2pl and lcj should be implemented AS the verify interpreter over new expectation kinds, not as more hand-enumerated checks — one mechanism, drift class structurally impossible.
acceptance_criteria: Expectation IR types exist with defs generating them; strict-diff runs as the verify interpreter over the IR for at least the surfaces 2pl/lcj require; apply consumes the same expectations for those surfaces (no parallel hand lists remain for migrated surfaces); a deliberate def change flows to apply+strict+docs from one edit; the stale strict_diff comments are gone because the code can no longer diverge from apply for migrated surfaces.
notes: 2026-07-08 verifiability audit rider: the IR bead should include an interpreter-equivalence differential as part of its AC evidence — apply-from-scratch onto an empty DB vs converge-from-an-arbitrarily-drifted DB must yield identical live introspection digests (pg_dump-normalized or catalog-query digest). That differential is what makes apply/converge/strict-diff-as-interpreters falsifiable and kills the lcj class (comments claiming one behavior while code does another) structurally: the digest test cannot lie. sinex-schema is the thinnest suite in the workspace relative to criticality (23 test fns / 12.7k LOC vs sinexd 1968 / 167k, measured 2026-07-08) — the IR interpreters are where that deficit gets repaid.

title: Judgment-queue debt policy: proposals age, evidence supersedes, queues stay honest without nagging
description: The curation plane assumes the operator judges proposals, and the no-nag rule (correctly) forbids pressure — but nothing specifies what happens when proposals sit for weeks: unbounded queue growth, judgments over stale evidence, and a judgment seat that opens onto 400 items (guaranteeing avoidance). Policy to design: (1) EVIDENCE-DRIVEN INVALIDATION — a proposal whose underlying evidence was superseded/archived/replayed is automatically re-validated or withdrawn-with-record (never silently mutated; the withdrawal is itself an event); (2) AGING — proposals carry age and evidence-freshness in the seat's card; ordering favors decision-ready over merely-old; (3) QUEUE BUDGET — a declared soft cap where the system stops GENERATING low-support proposals (generation backpressure, e.g. raising the proposal threshold) rather than nagging the operator to drain (aligns 2k2 cost-fuse philosophy); (4) EXPIRY DECISION — whether never-judged proposals expire to a durable dormant state after a declared horizon (reversible, queryable) or live forever — operator ruling; (5) metrics: queue depth, median age, withdrawal rate visible in the seat header and reflection lane, never as badges elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc + schema/runtime hooks: superseded-evidence proposals auto-withdraw with a recorded cause; seat cards show age + evidence freshness; generation backpressure engages at the declared budget with a caveat, no operator-facing nag anywhere; expiry ruling recorded; queue metrics in seat header + reflection lane; fixture: supersede evidence under a pending proposal and observe withdrawal, not a stale judgment.

title: Interval invariant property suite: simulation-tested semantics for the interval/session stack
description: r6d.9 tests CRASH windows; nothing tests interval SEMANTICS systematically — zs6 (heartbeat chop), uzc (tie drops), and the closure defects were all found by manual adversarial reading. A property/simulation harness generates synthetic evidence streams (transitions, heartbeats with gaps/duplicates/reorderings/ties, start-stop pairs with missing counterparts, suspend fences, replay re-deliveries) and asserts invariants over the emitted interval set: (1) per (state_kind, subject) live intervals are non-overlapping; (2) coverage conservation — total intervalized time never exceeds evidenced wall time per stream and gaps beyond the declared slack are never intervalized; (3) watermark monotonicity — no emission moves an already-closed boundary except via supersession; (4) supersession sanity — at most one live interpretation per occurrence key, superseded readings archived, no orphaned descendants; (5) replay equivalence — replaying the same synthetic stream yields the same interval SET by occurrence key (new interpretation ids allowed); (6) tie/out-of-order inputs never silently vanish (interval, debt, or explicit no-op accounting). Runs as ordinary xtask tests with deterministic seeds (seed printed on failure).

title: Clock-driven closure and suspend/boot fences: interval ends must not require future activity
description: VERIFIED closure-by-next-arrival across the whole stack: analytics Gap fires only when the NEXT event arrives (analytics.rs accumulate gap check); flush_due defaults false and only hourly/daily override it (traits.rs:249, hourly.rs:178, daily.rs:181) so no clock closes an activity window or session; SessionDetector completes only on a Gap-closed window (session.rs:125-143); interval_lift transitions close only on the next transition (interval_lift.rs:664-681). Consequences: the final interval/session of any activity bout is unqueryable until future activity; suspend/shutdown periods are attributed to the last open state (focus 23:59 + next focus 09:00 = 9h focus interval); AFK evidence does not fence focus/workspace kinds (cross-silo). CAUTION: wall-clock flush must be watermark-aware — during historical replay/backfill, input-time watermarks, not wall time, decide gaps, or replay would chop historical continuity. Lens: composability (silos: AFK vs focus) + construct validity (interval end means 'next event arrived', not 'state ended').
design: TWO-MODE WATERMARK (settled design): WatermarkMode::Live — watermark = max(max_input_ts_orig, now - idle_grace); advances with wall clock; flush_due closes an accumulator when watermark - last_evidence >= gap_threshold. WatermarkMode::Catchup — watermark = max input ts_orig ONLY (no wall-clock advance), so historical replay/backfill can never chop continuity by processing delay. Mode source: the consumer catch-up/lag state the bridge already tracks — Live only when lag < declared threshold; any transition Catchup->Live re-evaluates open accumulators against the new watermark. Fences (suspend/resume, boot, AFK-state transitions per the cross-kind fencing table) are INPUT events, valid in both modes, and close at the fence ts_orig — never at processing time.
acceptance_criteria: flush_due (input-time-watermark-aware) closes analytics windows and sessions after gap_threshold of quiet without requiring a next event; live mode uses wall clock as the watermark, replay/catch-up uses max input ts_orig. Suspend/resume and boot fence events close all open desktop interval kinds at the fence (systemd sleep.target/boot as fence inputs). AFK-state transitions fence focus/workspace intervals per a declared cross-kind fencing table. Fixture: activity then silence -> window+session close within one flush period; suspend mid-focus -> focus interval ends at suspend, not next-morning focus.

title: interval_lift heartbeat merge is arithmetically wrong: gap measured from first heartbeat, closes include the idle gap
description: VERIFIED: merged heartbeats never advance the observation timestamp (refresh_metadata_from interval_lift.rs:351-356 touches label/attrs only) while the merge gap is computed against self.ts_orig = the FIRST heartbeat (activitywatch_gap_to:367-369, merge check:703-706). A continuous heartbeat stream therefore chops into fixed ~30-35s intervals (the merge window degenerates into max-interval-length instead of gap-tolerance), inflating interval counts for continuous activity. Separately, when the gap exceeds the window, close_with ends the interval at the NEXT event's ts_orig (371-404 via 711) — the entire idle gap is attributed to the previous subject. For heartbeat-class evidence (absence of heartbeat = absence of evidence) the end must be last-seen (+ bounded slack), not next-seen. Lens: construct validity — the emitted 'interval' measures merge-window arithmetic, not activity.
acceptance_criteria: Merging advances a last_seen timestamp; gap tolerance compares against last_seen; a continuous same-subject heartbeat stream produces ONE interval per activity bout. Over-window closes end at last_seen + declared slack constant, never at the next event's ts_orig. Fixture: 10-minute 5s-heartbeat stream -> one interval of ~10min; heartbeat, 2h silence, heartbeat -> first interval ends within slack of its last heartbeat.
close_reason: Merged via PR #2479. Heartbeat bouts track a last_seen watermark; gap tolerance measured from last_seen; same-subject-gap bout ends at last_seen+slack (not next event); subject switches still close at transition ts. Verify: xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(interval_lift)' -> 23/23 incl interval_lift_continuous_heartbeat_stream_is_one_bout.

title: Schema backfill runner: persist failure state, expose interrupted-vs-active, guard replay/ingest concurrency
description:
schema_backfill_runs has failed/error_message columns but the runner never persists them — errors unwind leaving status='running' with a stale phase/cursor, indistinguishable from an active run (backfill.rs:164-176). Correctness also depends on writer quiescence: replay/ingest can archive rows inside the frozen horizon or add rows after it, producing stale parsed_event_count — the --assume-quiescent flag is load-bearing, not ceremony. Source: new-gpt-pro 08 backfill section.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read backfill.rs:164-176 -- schema_backfill_runs has failed/error_message columns, but the runner never persists them on an unwound error.
2. Trigger a backfill run and force it to error mid-run (e.g. a poison row).
3. Observe the run's status remains 'running' with a stale phase/cursor, indistinguishable from a genuinely still-active run -- no failed state is ever written.
4. Separately, run replay/ingest concurrently with a backfill inside its frozen horizon (without --assume-quiescent) -- rows archived or added inside the horizon produce a stale parsed_event_count, since the flag is load-bearing for correctness, not advisory.
acceptance_criteria: Runner catches errors and persists status=failed + error_message while still releasing the advisory lock. Status output distinguishes active-running / interrupted-running / failed / succeeded / registered. Rerun semantics explicit: resume interrupted by default, reset only on --restart or failed policy. Backfill refuses to run while replay/ingest writers are active or takes a shared writer-quiescence lock. Tests: crash/resume during scan, failure during apply, rerun after failed, concurrent-replay guard.

title: Schema registry integrity: content_hash can go stale against schema_content
description:
Schema sync compares stored content_hash metadata (schema_management.rs:840-895) while runtime validation compiles schema_content from DB (validation.rs:600-685). A manual schema_content edit with stale content_hash false-cleans sync and silently changes validation semantics. Detection today is event rejection behavior, not schema diff. Source: new-gpt-pro 08 finding 8.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read schema_management.rs:840-895 -- schema sync compares stored content_hash metadata to detect drift.
2. Read validation.rs:600-685 -- runtime validation compiles schema_content directly from the DB, independent of content_hash.
3. Manually edit a schema_content row in the DB without updating its content_hash.
4. Run schema sync -- observe it reports clean (false-negative) because it only checks the hash, while runtime validation semantics have silently changed because it reads schema_content directly.
acceptance_criteria: Schema sync or strict diff recomputes content_hash from live schema_content for sinex_schemas.event_payload_schemas; mismatch is reported as drift or repaired from the generated bundle. Test covers manual schema_content mutation with unchanged content_hash.
notes:
[2026-07-11] Attempted fix on branch feature/fix/schema-registry-live-hash (commit 04cb5b668, now deleted; recoverable via git reflog ~30d). APPROACH (sound in principle): load_schema_map now recomputes a LIVE content hash from stored schema_content via calculate_schema_content_hash(source,event_type,schema_version,schema_content) and SchemaRecord.is_unchanged_for() requires is_active && live_content_hash==candidate.content_hash && stored content_hash==candidate.content_hash — so a stale STORED hash no longer masks drifted content. New test sync_schema_bundle_repairs_live_content_with_stale_hash PASSES; sync_schema_bundle family 3/3 green.

REGRESSION (why dropped, not merged): pre-existing test concurrent_schema_bundle_sync_is_idempotent (crate/sinex-db/tests/repositories_schema_management.rs:531) PASSES on master, FAILS on the branch with uk_schema_identity UniqueViolation (23505). Root cause inference: converge_existing_schema is UPDATE-only (no INSERT), so the insert-race must come from concurrent syncs all deciding the row is CHANGED and racing the new-insert path. That means the LIVE recompute formula does NOT match the STORED-hash formula for IDENTICAL content → is_unchanged_for returns false for genuinely-unchanged rows → defeats the unchanged-skip optimization for EVERY sync (not just stale ones) and forces concurrent writes → race. 

FIX DIRECTION for next attempt: make calculate_schema_content_hash's inputs byte-identical to whatever produced the stored content_hash at register time (verify the canonicalization/field-order/encoding match); add a non-concurrent assertion that a freshly-registered unchanged row is detected as unchanged (live==stored==candidate) BEFORE relying on it; only then re-run concurrent_schema_bundle_sync_is_idempotent. Consider whether the new-insert path needs ON CONFLICT hardening regardless.

title: Strict trigger/function drift: enabled state, trigger definition, exact function bodies
description:
VERIFIED on master: ensure_trigger_set_sql skips SQL when the trigger NAME exists (apply.rs:1388-1402); trigger_exists checks only tgrelid/tgname/NOT tgisinternal (apply.rs:1367-1386) — no tgenabled, timing, event mask, WHEN, or target function. strict_diff.rs module comments (lines 18-21, 344) claim trigger functions are installed by CREATE OR REPLACE every apply — FALSE for the guarded set. Blast: ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER or a same-name retargeted trigger silently bypasses payload validation / append-only / archive-before-delete enforcement until data corruption is noticed. Function marker-checks are substring-based and pass body edits preserving markers. Source: new-gpt-pro 08 finding 1 + main correction.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read apply.rs:1388-1402 -- ensure_trigger_set_sql skips SQL entirely when a trigger with the matching NAME already exists.
2. Read apply.rs:1367-1386 -- trigger_exists checks only tgrelid/tgname/NOT tgisinternal, never tgenabled, timing, event mask, WHEN clause, or target function.
3. Run ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER on a payload-validation or append-only-enforcement trigger, or retarget a same-named trigger to a different function.
4. Run schema apply/converge -- observe it reports clean because the trigger NAME still exists, despite the trigger being disabled or retargeted -- payload validation/append-only/archive-before-delete enforcement is silently bypassed until data corruption is noticed downstream.
acceptance_criteria: Strict diff checks tgenabled, timing, event mask, row/statement mode, WHEN clause, and target function for all schema-managed triggers; exact normalized pg_get_functiondef (or source-declared hash) for load-bearing functions, bound to full signatures. The stale CREATE-OR-REPLACE comments in strict_diff.rs are corrected. Tests prove DISABLE TRIGGER and same-name retarget drift are detected.
notes: 2026-07-08 architecture guidance: implement as TriggerExpectation/FunctionExpectation kinds in the schema expectation IR (32p2) interpreted by both apply and strict-diff — the lying comments become structurally impossible when both read the same expectation.

title: xtask impact-mode evidence soundness: completeness tokens, historical-test liveness, risk-class fallbacks
description:
Three balanced-mode false-skip classes (new-gpt-pro 03 P1 x3): (1) hunk 'fully covered' means at least ONE historical evidence row overlaps each hunk (impact.rs:495-517) — not that ALL tests needing the hunk are known; (2) filters emit historical test names with no nextest-list liveness check — renamed/deleted tests become zero-test proofs recorded as success (impact.rs:291-324; runner only fails on stats.failed>0); (3) the syntactic item scanner under-models cross-crate macros, build.rs/env-cfg, generated code, and SQLx/live-DB coupling (impact.rs:647-748; workspace triggers only Cargo/flake/config at 257-264). Owner context: sinex-pke.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read impact.rs:495-517 -- a hunk is marked 'fully covered' when at least ONE historical evidence row overlaps it, not when ALL tests needing the hunk are known -- construct a hunk covered by one weak test among several that should exercise it; observe impact-mode reports full coverage.
2. Read impact.rs:291-324 -- filters emit historical test names with no nextest-list liveness check; rename or delete a test referenced by recorded historical evidence, then run impact mode -- the runner only fails on stats.failed>0, so a zero-test "proof" is recorded as success.
3. Read impact.rs:647-748 and 257-264 -- the syntactic item scanner under-models cross-crate macros, build.rs/env-cfg, generated code, and SQLx/live-DB coupling; workspace-wide triggers fire only on Cargo/flake/config changes. Modify a macro-generated or SQLx-coupled surface without touching those trigger files -- observe impact mode fails to select the tests that would actually catch a regression.
acceptance_criteria: Test-name filtering requires a per-package coverage-completeness token; without it fall back to affected-package or workspace scope. Every history-derived filter is liveness-checked against current nextest discovery; a filter selecting zero current tests invalidates evidence and falls back, never records success. Risk-class fallbacks: proc-macro/macro crates, build.rs, schema/sqlx-bearing files, generated-code roots, and env-cfg surfaces escalate to package-closure or workspace scope unless the proof includes reverse-dependency evidence plus a DB/schema seal.

title: xtask proof substrate seal: fingerprints omit live DB/NATS/env/toolchain and proof reuse skips preflight
description:
Proof fingerprints cover HEAD, scoped dirty content, seven shared config files, and semantic CLI args (coordinator.rs:35-43,883-904,1042-1105; test.rs:849-947) — but NOT live DB schema state, NATS topology, DATABASE_URL, RUSTFLAGS/RUSTC_WRAPPER, or rustc/cargo/nextest versions, even though sqlx compiles against the live DB by doctrine. Worse: exact-impact and package proofs are consumed BEFORE compile/runtime preflight (test.rs:1302-1344,1671-1724 vs preflight at 1812-1835), so a cached proof can report success while the substrate needed for a real run is broken. Fix shape: a substrate seal (env whitelist, rustc -Vv, tool versions, schema digest/strict-diff hash, NATS topology digest, preflight outcome id) folded into the proof key, or a cheap seal validation before proof consumption. Source: new-gpt-pro 03 P1 x2. Related: sinex-6cb, sinex-9wx (whose original pre-queue DDL race IS fixed on master — wrapper flock at flake.nix:1884-1897, launcher-only --bg skips bootstrap, schema apply holds exclusive lock at preflight.rs:977-1011).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read coordinator.rs:35-43,883-904,1042-1105 and test.rs:849-947 -- proof fingerprints cover HEAD, scoped dirty content, seven shared config files, and semantic CLI args, but never live DB schema state, NATS topology, DATABASE_URL, RUSTFLAGS/RUSTC_WRAPPER, or rustc/cargo/nextest versions.
2. Change the live DB schema (or NATS topology, or toolchain version) without changing any file the fingerprint covers.
3. Re-run the previously-proved command -- observe the cached proof is reused (fingerprint unchanged) despite the substrate it was proved against no longer matching reality.
4. Read test.rs:1302-1344,1671-1724 vs the preflight check at 1812-1835 -- confirm exact-impact/package proofs are consumed BEFORE compile/runtime preflight runs, so a cached proof can report success even when the substrate needed for a real run is currently broken.
acceptance_criteria: check/build/test proofs embed a substrate seal: normalized env whitelist, rustc/cargo/nextest versions, devshell/cache identity, live schema digest, NATS topology digest for runtime tests, preflight outcome id. Proof reuse validates the seal (or runs a cheap preflight) before returning success. Detection commands from the audit reproduce the false-pass before, and fail closed after: proof hit + xtask infra stop + rerun same test without --no-reuse must not report success.

title: Material-assembler DLQ publish failure is swallowed before ACK/terminal-failed settlement
description:
route_material_error returns () and only logs DLQ publish failures (finalize.rs:138-202); the pipeline then marks the material failed and ACKs the frame (pipeline.rs:95-118) — no redelivery, no DLQ record. Raw-event DLQ does the stricter thing (ACK only after DLQ publish succeeds, dlq.rs:213-238); material should match. Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-08.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read finalize.rs:138-202 -- route_material_error returns () and only logs on DLQ publish failure, with no propagation.
2. Read pipeline.rs:95-118 -- the pipeline marks the material failed and ACKs the frame regardless of whether the DLQ publish in step 1 actually succeeded.
3. Force the DLQ publish to fail (e.g. DLQ stream full or unreachable) during a material-assembly failure.
4. Observe the material is marked failed and the frame is ACKed off its source stream with no DLQ record and no redelivery -- contrast with the raw-event DLQ path (dlq.rs:213-238), which correctly ACKs only after the DLQ publish itself succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: route_material_error returns a Result. Frame-level DLQ decisions ACK only after DLQ publish confirmation or an equivalent durable failure record. DLQ publish failure causes NAK/retry, never silent terminal settlement. Tests simulate NATS publish failure and assert no ACK/terminal mark without durable failure evidence.
close_reason:
Revalidated against the current master implementation.

## Closure Evidence Manifest

| AC | Evidence kind | Surface | Evidence | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | runtime | material-assembler DLQ settlement | Material DLQ routing persists a PostgreSQL failure witness, confirms JetStream publication before ACK, propagates publish failures, and retains retryable state; the real failure-injection regression proves no silent terminal settlement occurs. | `nix develop --command xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(material_dlq_publish_failure_preserves_retryable_material_state)' --impact-mode=off` | Satisfied |

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
REOPENED 2026-08-10 per audit finding: this bead's own acceptance criterion ('frame-level DLQ decisions ACK only after DLQ publish confirmation') is NOT actually met for materials, despite being closed as done.

The error-HANDLING branches this bead added are genuinely correct: every DLQ-publish failure propagates and callers correctly preserve retry state rather than settling terminal-failed (NAK with delay: pipeline.rs:112-127; phase revert: finalize.rs:219-245; leave-unmarked for next sweep: maintenance.rs:385,462). There is no branch where a failed assembly is dropped without either a DLQ attempt or a retry mechanism owning it.

The defect: the publish those branches gate on is not actually durable. crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/material_assembler/finalize.rs:189-203 publishes via self.nats_client.publish_with_headers(...) where nats_client is async_nats::Client (material_assembler/mod.rs:26,227) -- CORE NATS, no JetStream ack, no store confirmation, no retry loop. The raw-event DLQ path deliberately does the opposite (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/dlq.rs:161-209: js.publish_with_headers(...).await THEN ack.await, 3 attempts with backoff). The assembler already constructs an unused JetStream context at mod.rs:334 -- the fix is likely 'use it'. The DLQ stream is discard='new' (nixos/modules/nats.nix:219), so a full DLQ stream REJECTS the publish invisibly on this fire-and-forget path -- Ok(()) from a core-NATS publish proves nothing about whether the DLQ actually received/stored the frame.

Updated acceptance criteria: material-assembler DLQ publish uses the JetStream client (mod.rs:334's already-constructed context) with ack confirmation, matching the raw-event path's pattern (dlq.rs:161-209) exactly. A test proves: force the DLQ stream to reject a publish (e.g. simulate discard='new' at capacity, or inject a publish error), and confirm the material assembler does NOT settle terminal-Failed/ACK the frame on that failure -- i.e. that the existing correct error-handling branches actually get exercised because the publish now genuinely reports failure when it should.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Confirmed via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{checkpoint,stage_as_you_go,dlq_retry,pacing,backlog,confirmation_handler,durable_emission,durable_emission_backend,durable_emission_registry}.rs (2026-08-11) -- STILL core-NATS on master, and the in-code comments claiming otherwise are false, not just stale.

material_assembler/finalize.rs:188-190 uses self.nats_client.publish_with_headers(...) where nats_client is async_nats::Client, NOT a jetstream::Context. Core publish returns Ok once bytes hit the outbound socket buffer -- no server ack, no stream-acceptance signal. The comments AT THE SITE are unsupported by the code beneath them: finalize.rs:140-143 ("Mirrors the raw-event DLQ discipline... Never swallow a DLQ publish failure here and let a caller treat it as if durable failure evidence exists (sinex-wb1)."), and :206-208 ("only if the DLQ publish actually succeeded").

Specific bite: DLQ stream is discard: New with a max_bytes cap (bootstrap.rs:88,93). A full DLQ REJECTS new messages -- visible error over JetStream, silent drop over core NATS. So material failure evidence is lost EXACTLY when the DLQ is saturated, i.e. when failures are frequent -- the worst-case timing. Caller then settles the material terminal-failed with no record anywhere.

Contrast: dlq.rs:159-190 (the raw-event DLQ path) correctly does js.publish_with_headers + ack.await + 3-attempt backoff -- proving the correct pattern exists in the same codebase, one file over. This bead's fix is a one-line change at the call site (self.nats_client -> self.js, plus awaiting the ack) mirroring dlq.rs's existing pattern.

(core async_nats::Client, no server ack) where the comments at finalize.rs:139-143 and :206-208 both explicitly claim this bead (sinex-wb1) is what guarantees durability here -- the claim is false on current master.

Specific bite confirmed from this audit: the DLQ stream is discard:New with a max_bytes cap (bootstrap.rs:88,93) -- a FULL DLQ REJECTS new messages over JetStream (a visible error) but silently drops over core NATS. So material failure evidence is lost exactly when the DLQ is saturated, i.e. exactly when failures are most frequent -- the worst-case timing for this bug to bite. Fix is one call site: self.nats_client -> self.js (a jetstream::Context), plus awaiting the publish ack, mirroring the already-correct pattern at jetstream_consumer/dlq.rs:166-176.

title: DLQ retry republishes redacted/stubbed preview as if it were original raw payload
description:
DLQ entries store policy-redacted original_payload; parse failures suppress raw bytes (dlq.rs:81-100); oversize entries store a metadata stub (dlq.rs:134-159). dlq_retry serializes that field and republishes it to the original raw subject unless _raw_bytes_base64 exists (dlq_retry.rs:693-728, 436-475), then deletes the DLQ message. Replay can therefore inject mutated/stub events that never existed on the raw stream, or re-emit whole multi-event envelopes. Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-07.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read dlq.rs:81-100 -- DLQ entries store policy-redacted original_payload, suppress raw bytes on parse failure, and store a metadata stub for oversize entries (dlq.rs:134-159).
2. Read dlq_retry.rs:693-728,436-475 -- dlq_retry serializes the stored (possibly redacted/stubbed) payload field and republishes it to the original raw subject unless a separate _raw_bytes_base64 field exists, then deletes the DLQ message.
3. Cause a DLQ entry to be created for an event whose payload triggered redaction, a parse failure (raw bytes suppressed), or an oversize stub.
4. Requeue that DLQ entry via sinexctl ops dlq requeue -- observe the republished raw-stream message carries the redacted/stubbed content rather than the true original payload, and the DLQ copy is deleted, permanently losing the ability to detect the substitution.
acceptance_criteria: DLQ entries carry an explicit replayability flag; suppressed/redacted/stubbed entries are not retried by default. Replayable raw bytes stored separately from operator preview with the durability/access model documented. Retry tests cover redacted payload, oversize stub, parse-failure suppression, and normal replayable payload.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: 2026-08-10 audit correction: the _raw_bytes_base64 branch at crate/sinexd/src/runtime/dlq_retry.rs:709-726's dlq_requeue_target is DEAD CODE. dlq.rs never writes a _raw_bytes_base64 field (only _raw_bytes_suppressed on parse-failure entries, dlq.rs:93-99), so parse-failure DLQ entries are ALWAYS requeued as lossy stubs, never as original bytes -- the base64 fallback this bead's design may have assumed exists as a recovery path never actually fires. Combined with sinex-3kqx's dedupe-window finding: requeuing a stub can delete the only surviving record of the original message. For the oversize-payload case, original bytes were never stored anywhere and the raw message was already ACKed off a WorkQueue stream -- already unrecoverable at DLQ-write time, before any requeue action. Confirmed requeue DOES correctly re-enter the same admission pipeline and preserves event identity/ts_coided (the id comes from the stored payload) -- the divergence this bead tracks is CONTENT (a redacted/stubbed body admitted as if original), not identity or provenance. This correction doesn't change the bead's open status or core scope, just corrects an assumption about the base64 fallback's reachability.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Testable: create a DLQ entry with a redacted/stubbed payload, requeue it, assert republished content is flagged as non-original / DLQ record is not silently deleted. No test yet.

title: Derived batch chunk validation falsely rejects forward parent references across the 2700-row boundary
description: Full-batch cycle check passes (persistence.rs:890-903) but per-chunk liveness validation exempts only the current chunk's ids (persistence.rs:905-939): a child in chunk 0 referencing a parent in chunk 1 of the same acyclic batch queries core.events, finds nothing, and is isolated as a poison row -> DLQ while siblings commit. Triggers on burst replay/import of large derived DAGs (>2700 rows). Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-06.
acceptance_criteria: Parent-liveness validation sees the full batch ID set, or chunks are topologically ordered so parents commit first. Valid acyclic full-batch DAGs never fail on chunk boundaries. Tests cover child-before-parent across the boundary and a genuinely missing parent. Bisection/DLQ still isolates real invalid parents.
notes: Fixed via PR #2524: batch_event_ids computed once over the full derived batch, threaded through every chunk's ensure_source_event_ids_are_live check (replacing the per-chunk-only set). A genuinely missing parent is still correctly rejected (regression test proves it). Adjacent bug also fixed: SYNTHESIS_CHUNK_MAX (2700) was stale against the real 30-binds-per-row (24 base + 6 derivation-control-plane columns from sinex-0vx.4/8cr.2), which meant 2700x30=81000 already exceeded Postgres's 65535 bind-param limit -- corrected to 2000. Both proven via new tests in repositories_events.rs: forward-parent-across-boundary now commits, genuinely-missing-parent still rejected. 16/16 existing persistence tests still pass.
