comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Fix confirmed in production (persistence.rs:1297-1310, comment explicitly cites sinex-wv7: parent-liveness now checked against the full batch id set, not per-chunk). No dedicated regression test found for the cross-chunk forward-parent scenario itself (searched persistence_test.rs for chunk/forward_parent/SYNTHESIS_CHUNK -- no match). Fixed but untested.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2-impl 2026-08-11] Fix reconfirmed correct in production code (persistence.rs:1297-1310). A genuine regression test requires a >2184-row synthetic derived batch to actually trigger the SYNTHESIS_CHUNK_MAX chunk-boundary condition (the bug only manifests across a chunk split) -- not written this pass due to size/runtime cost. Still a real closure-quality gap: the fix is unverified by test, only by source read.

title: payload_schema_id FK strip-retry silently diverges DB row from confirmed stream
description:
On payload_schema_id FK violation, persistence retries with every row's schema id set to NULL (admission.rs:970-1000, matcher 1316-1327) and commits; confirmation still publishes the original event advertising the validated schema id. Schema-cache staleness becomes silent authority drift: DB says no-schema, confirmed stream says schema S. Adjacent to sinex-5ai but not covered by it. Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-05.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read admission.rs:970-1000,1316-1327 -- on a payload_schema_id FK violation, persistence retries the insert with every row's schema id forced to NULL, then commits.
2. Cause a payload_schema_id FK violation during persistence (e.g. a schema-cache entry referencing a not-yet-committed schema row).
3. Observe the DB row is committed with payload_schema_id=NULL while the confirmed NATS stream still publishes the original event advertising the validated schema id S -- the DB and the confirmed stream now silently disagree about which schema governs this event.
acceptance_criteria: FK violation triggers schema reload + revalidation or terminal schema-management failure — never silent schema-id stripping. If a retry lands, DB row and confirmed event agree on payload_schema_id. Metric/audit signal identifies schema-cache races. Tests cover stale schema id, missing schema row, successful reload/revalidate.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] crate/sinexd/tests/event_engine/jetstream_dlq_test.rs:692-867 already tests the DB-row-strip-to-NULL half of this bead; the bead's actual complaint (confirmation stream still publishes the ORIGINAL un-stripped schema id, diverging from the DB row) has no test. Testable via an assertion on the published confirm-stream payload.

title: Reflection-lane admission is lane-blind: dedupe, tombstones, and parent liveness query core.* only
description: Reflection consumer writes reflection.events but equivalence-key dedupe SQL queries only core.events (queries.rs:671-705), tombstone filtering only core.event_tombstones (queries.rs:645-667), and ensure_source_event_ids_are_live only core.events (persistence/validation.rs:85-150). Consequences: replayed deterministic reflection events duplicate in reflection.events; reflection-derived events with reflection parents are falsely rejected as non-live; cross-lane parent semantics are accidental. Related to sinex-x9i (lane separation) but x9i does not cover this admission/persistence parity hole. Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-04.
acceptance_criteria: Repository APIs for equivalence keys, tombstones, and parent liveness accept EventStorageLane. Reflection events dedupe against reflection.events; reflection-derived events can reference same-lane parents; cross-lane parent policy is explicit, tested, and documented. Activity-lane behavior unchanged.
close_reason:
Closure Evidence Manifest: reflection consumer writes to reflection.events, but equivalence-key dedupe, tombstone filtering, and parent-liveness checks were hardcoded to query core.* only -- replayed reflection events never deduped (always resolved Fresh) and reflection-derived events with reflection-lane parents were falsely rejected as non-live.

Fix: threaded EventStorageLane through find_live_by_equivalence_key(s) and ensure_source_event_ids_are_live so both checks run against the correct physical table. Cross-lane parent policy decided and documented: same-lane parents only, matching automaton fan-out subscribing exactly one lane per consumer -- a parent that only exists in the other lane is rejected as non-live, never silently mismatched. Tombstone filtering deliberately left lane-agnostic (core.event_tombstones is keyed by globally-unique event id, not lane; no reflection archive pathway exists yet) -- documented inline rather than silently threading a no-op parameter.

Merged via PR #2600, squash-merged 2026-08-10, commit f66d91ec8.

Verification: xtask check -p sinexd -p sinex-db pass; xtask test -p sinexd -p sinex-db -E 'test(reflection) or test(equivalence) or test(tombstone) or test(dedup) or test(f8v) or test(parent_liveness) or test(source_event_ids)' --no-reuse: 73/73 passed (re-verified independently by me post-rebase onto latest master). New tests prove reflection-lane dedup works against reflection.events not core.events, reflection-derived events with live reflection-lane parents are not falsely rejected, and activity-lane behavior is provably unchanged.

title: Re-run ts_orig plausibility after material timestamp resolution
description:
Material-provenance events may pass admission with ts_orig=None (allowed, admission.rs:529-538); plausibility lower-bound/future-skew checks only run inside 'if let Some(ts_orig)' (admission.rs:546-589). resolve_ready_ts_orig later stamps ts_orig from the material registry/temporal ledger AFTER readiness gating (persist.rs:80-87, prepare.rs:159-176) and row conversion only checks non-null. A registry start_time of 1900 or 2100 persists without ever passing the gates non-material events face. Source: new-gpt-pro 02 EE-03.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read admission.rs:529-538 -- Material-provenance events may pass admission with ts_orig=None (allowed by design).
2. Read admission.rs:546-589 -- plausibility lower-bound/future-skew checks run only inside `if let Some(ts_orig)`, so a None ts_orig skips them entirely.
3. Read persist.rs:80-87 and prepare.rs:159-176 -- resolve_ready_ts_orig stamps ts_orig from the material registry/temporal ledger AFTER readiness gating, and row conversion only checks the value is non-null, not that it's plausible.
4. Register a source material whose registry/temporal-ledger start_time is implausible (e.g. year 1900 or 2100).
5. Observe the resulting event's ts_orig persists with the implausible value, never having passed the same plausibility gates that events with an explicit ts_orig face at admission time.
acceptance_criteria: Resolved material ts_orig values are checked against ts_orig_lower_bound and future_ts_skew before persistence; violations route through validation/DLQ settlement (subject to the aggregate-settlement fix). Tests cover too-old, too-future, and valid resolved material timestamps. Admission-time checks for non-material events unchanged.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
2026-08-10 audit re-verification: CONFIRMED, still open, citations updated for current master (the bead's original line numbers have drifted). Material events with ts_orig=None are exempted from plausibility gates at admission.rs:701-707; both gates run only inside 'if let Some(ts_orig)' at admission.rs:709-753. Resolution happens later at jetstream_consumer/prepare.rs:262-266 (event.ts_orig = Some(ts_orig) straight from derive_ts_orig, zero bounds check), called from persist.rs:85. The only later gate is a non-null check at admission.rs:1503-1509.

Refinement not in the original bead: the FUTURE direction has an accidental backstop the bead didn't cite -- crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/events.rs:348 CHECK (ts_orig <= ts_coided + INTERVAL '1 second'). A resolved 2100 value dies as SQLSTATE 23514, isolatable, bisected to DLQ. Severity HIGH for the past direction (silent, no backstop anywhere) but only MEDIUM (ugly-but-loud) for future (rejected, just late and noisily).

Also relevant: admission's OWN future_ts_skew default (1 hour, admission.rs:495) is 3600x more permissive than the DB's 1-second constraint -- every event in the 1s-1h future window gets admitted then bisected-and-DLQ'd on the DB constraint instead of being cleanly rejected at admission. Worth fixing together with this bead since they're the same skew-check code path.

comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No test found for plausibility re-check after resolve_ready_ts_orig resolves a material event's ts_orig post-admission (admission.rs:546-589 only runs the check pre-resolution). Testable: admit a material event with ts_orig=None that resolves to an implausible timestamp, assert it's still caught.

title: Entity/relation insertion defaults fabricate authority: confidence 1.0, empty source refs, global canonical_name
description:
Verified on master (2026-07-07): entity and relation creation default confidence_score to 1.0 when unset (sinex-db/src/repositories/knowledge_graph.rs:335 entity, :656 relation) and accept empty source_event_ids (unwrap_or_default) — an unreviewed guess becomes maximal authority with zero provenance. Additionally core.entities.canonical_name is globally UNIQUE across ALL entity kinds (sinex-schema/src/defs/entities.rs:100-104), so 'Claude' the person/model/product collide into one identity slot (the partial uk_entities_type_name (type,name) index shows the kind-scoped intent, but canonical_name ignores kind). Adversarial audit section 10 failure mode: relations attach to the wrong node; context packs later cite the relation as fact.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read sinex-db/src/repositories/knowledge_graph.rs:335 (entity) and :656 (relation) -- confidence_score defaults to 1.0 when unset, and source_event_ids accepts empty via unwrap_or_default.
2. Create an entity or relation via the knowledge-graph repository without explicitly setting confidence or source_event_ids.
3. Observe the row persists with confidence_score=1.0 and empty source_event_ids -- an unreviewed guess reads as maximal authority with zero provenance.
4. Read sinex-schema/src/defs/entities.rs:100-104 -- confirm core.entities.canonical_name is a globally UNIQUE constraint across ALL entity kinds, not scoped by kind (the partial uk_entities_type_name (type,name) index shows the kind-scoped intent but canonical_name itself ignores kind).
5. Attempt to create two entities both canonically named "Claude" but of different kinds (person vs. model vs. product) -- observe they collide into one identity slot.
design: Repair direction (audit section 10 + storage/authority doctrine): (a) default confidence for unreviewed candidates = NULL/unknown or explicit low — never 1.0; (b) require non-empty support refs OR an accepted judgment before a relation is surfaced as canonical; (c) entity identity = (entity_kind, namespace, external_id_or_hash); canonical_name becomes display, not identity — drop or kind-scope the global unique; (d) resolution creates entity_identity_candidate rows (basis: exact_email|git_author_email|same_provider_id|lexical|cooccurrence|model_guess), never direct merges. Coordinates with pq5 (consume-or-retire decision) — if pq5 decides retire, this shrinks to just removing the lying defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Audit of all entity/relation insertion paths shows no 1.0-confidence default and no empty-support canonical surfacing; a test proves an unreviewed candidate relation cannot appear as canonical; canonical_name uniqueness is kind-scoped or demoted to display. VERIFY: xtask test -p sinex-db -E 'test(entity)' + grep showing unwrap_or(1.0) gone from knowledge_graph.rs.
notes: Repro: create a relation via pool.knowledge_graph().create_relation_with_executor with confidence_score=None and source_event_ids=None — row lands with confidence 1.0 and empty refs (knowledge_graph.rs:656). Entity same at :335. Cross-kind collision: create entity kind=person name-canonical 'Claude', then kind=model canonical 'Claude' — second insert violates the global unique.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Empirical confirmation 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (Opus): the cross-source entity-linking mechanism this bead's design section proposes (entity identity = (kind, namespace, external_id_or_hash), entity_identity_candidate rows with a basis enum) does not exist yet in ANY form -- confirmed there is currently no live subject for 'cross-source entity linking' to even apply to. Chain of evidence: the entity extractor (crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_extractor.rs:101-103) consumes only 3 event types (document.chunked, command.canonical, command.executed) -- email/browser/media/calendar/git-derived events never enter entity extraction at all, so e.g. an email sender never becomes an entity unless the same address also happens to appear inside a document chunk. find_first_entity (entity_extractor.rs:207-259) returns exactly ONE entity per event by type priority (URL>email>file>tool), not by position -- a chunk containing 200 people's email addresses plus one URL yields the URL and zero people (the multi-output half of this gap is already tracked as sinex-a4w.4). entity_resolver.rs:239-257's identity is UUIDv5(entity_type + canonicalize_name(...)) where the only cross-source join key is EXACT LOWERCASED STRING EQUALITY of the extracted literal -- so alice@example.com from a note and alice@example.com from a shell command DO unify (same literal), but 'Alice Smith' in a chat transcript, alice@example.com as an email sender, and 'Alice Smith <alice@work.example>' as a git author produce three unlinked identities or more commonly zero, since none of those source types is even an input event type and there is no name-shaped extraction pattern at all. core.entities.external_ids is declared and never read or written by any automaton (confirmed, already noted as this bead's item 2). Also confirmed core.entities is written ONLY by PkmService with extraction_method:'manual' -- no automaton writes the entity tables at all; the automaton chain and the graph tables are two fully disconnected worlds using two different canonicalization functions (entity_resolver.rs's lowercase-only vs knowledge_graph.rs's lowercase+underscore-replace) and two different id schemes (deterministic UUIDv5 vs random Id::<Entity>::new()) -- matches this bead's own item stating the disconnect, now independently re-confirmed rather than just designed against.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Confidence=1.0 default and empty-source-refs-allowed are directly testable at the repository layer (assert insertion without evidence is rejected/flagged). None exists yet.

title: Analysis: sinex-corpus extraction — recovered-requirements ledger from 300 design chats
description:
Operator directive (2026-07-06, also rawlog 06-18 22:23 'mass-grabbing every sinex-related chatlog ever... stop feeling like I'm missing something'): systematically mine the ~300 exocortex/sinex sessions in the Polylogue archive (aistudio-drive 98, chatgpt-export 157, claude-ai-export 45) for design intent that never reached the vision docs. First slice done 2026-07-06 (scratch 020 Round-4/5: origin arc, AT-SPI2 provenance, two founding-intent quotes, RecordKeeper era). Remaining: the Vault series (Feb-Apr 2025, 400+msg threads), Sinex_Totality + Sinnix_Exoco (June 2025), and the chatgpt-export set.

## Method (proven this session — route around polylogue-rsad frictions)
(1) facets contains=<term> for origin counts; (2) list_sessions origin+contains, jq '.items|unique_by(.id)' from persisted output; (3) get_messages message_role=user (operator words = intent), extract via jq from persisted files — NEVER read raw MCP output inline; (4) for merged-report sessions, prefer the distilled artifact in sinex-target-vision over 100K-token chat outputs; (5) per session: extract {feature/kind/UX idea, quote, verdict: already-covered | gap->bead | superseded}.

## Acceptance Criteria
A recovered-requirements ledger (scratch/research) covering the Vault series + top-10 chatgpt design sessions: every extracted item has a quote + session ref + verdict; gap verdicts become beads; the ledger cross-referenced from rl4/pi1. Falsifier check per U11 risk 1: note anything contradicting current doctrine rather than silently dropping it.

Falsifier check per U11 risk 1: note anything contradicting current doctrine rather than silently dropping it.

title: Historical archive backfill: the full Polylogue corpus through the staged-import plane
description: Import the full historical Polylogue archive through the shared byte-backed producer only after sinex-4j2.1.1 proves real material/event transport settlement, sinex-4j2.7 proves stable refs, and sinex-4j2.10 installs transcript capability and lifecycle/purge boundaries. Preserve exact provider/attachment materials, immutable normalized segments, manifests, and anchored observations. This is a migration/load proof, not a one-off loader or giant archive material.
design:
Use 4j2.1 protocol, r6d.11 durable receipts, r6d.12 raw-envelope settlement, stable identity/alias ledger, 4j2.10 capability/lifecycle policy, and 2n9 pacing. Segment pathological sessions; preserve refs/anchors across append, re-export, and resegmentation. Checkpoint only after the existing receipt unlocks progress and the raw envelope is aggregate-settled. Record source frontier, counts/digests, coverage/fidelity, PSI/IO/memory, latency, durable debt, and reconciliation against Polylogue physical/logical counts. A one-time migration receipt prevents reverse-loop publication.

Synthetic fixtures and explicitly non-private samples may exercise transport before 4j2.10. Centralizing the full private corpus may not start until the capability matrix, retention/deletion lifecycle, purge inventory, and residual-accounting boundary are installed and verified.
acceptance_criteria: After 4j2.1.1, 4j2.7, and 4j2.10, import the full archive with bounded materials and declared host pressure. Pre-lifecycle runs are restricted to synthetic or explicitly non-private samples and cannot satisfy this bead. Kill/restart at material, partial child, receipt, and producer-ack boundaries resumes without duplicates or unlabelled partial revisions. Mixed multi-event outcomes obey r6d.12. Re-export/resegmentation preserves stable refs; the same revision is idempotent. Reconciliation explains every count/hash/fidelity difference and a missing segment becomes coverage debt. The second run is bounded/no-op except explicit new revisions. Migration receipt and run artifacts are durable, and unauthorized raw access remains denied during and after backfill.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Blocked placeholder for a future Polylogue-archive import phase, gated on 3 unfinished prerequisite beads (4j2.1.1, 4j2.7, 4j2.10). No stable interface exists yet to write a test against.

title: Reverse direction: Polylogue reads Sinex — ambient machine context in session views
description: Expose typed interval/moment evidence for Polylogue session workflows so the product can render commands, focus, browser, filesystem, Git/CI, and source-health context without importing those domains into its conversation ontology. Sinex owns the family-grouped evidence query and coverage caveats; Polylogue owns rendering/context selection and explicit standalone degradation. Cross-repository consumer: polylogue-303r.8.
design: Reuse existing bounded event-window, moment-search, context-pack, ViewEnvelope, public-ref, and source-continuity primitives. Input: stable Polylogue session ref plus host/time interval and optional repo/cwd hints. Output: family-grouped native evidence refs, freshness/frontier, unavailable/stale family caveats, contradictions, and adjacent-outside-window overreach. A readonly capability grants metadata/evidence cards but not arbitrary transcript/blob bytes. Do not create another query engine or expose both full MCP catalogs as the default agent surface.
acceptance_criteria: A gateway/MCP contract returns bounded family-grouped context with resolvable refs, coverage caveats, freshness, and latency evidence for a known session interval; adjacent-outside evidence is marked/excluded as overreach. No-match returns no fabricated moment. Unauthorized raw-content access is denied. Polylogue renders one real/synthetic session with ambient context and exact context-delivery provenance; absent/unreachable/stale Sinex yields typed caveat while standalone transcript reading remains available.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] AC ('gateway/MCP contract returns bounded family-grouped context with resolvable refs, coverage caveats, freshness, latency evidence') is a concrete API-shape assertion, fully testable once the contract exists. Not written yet.

title: Analysis: source registry chain — count the hops from contract to running binding
description:
Streamlining audit 2026-07-06: a source travels register_source_contract! -> register_source_runtime_binding! -> catalog_export.rs -> nixos/modules/source-catalog.generated.json (6,877 lines, checked in) -> lib/source-catalog.nix -> sources.nix glue functions -> generated bindings manifest JSON -> SINEX_SOURCE_BINDINGS_PATH -> sinexd bindings.rs. That is ~8 hops with 2 generated artifacts and 3 hand-maintained mapping layers. Each hop exists for a reason (Rust->Nix boundary, deployment config, dev-vs-prod manifests) — the audit asks which hops still pay rent post-#1727 typed contracts: can the generated JSON drive the Nix side directly without per-family glue functions (mkTerminalGlue/mkDesktopGlue/... each reimplement binding->unit mapping); can dev (.agent/dev/dev-source-bindings.json) and prod manifests share one generator?

## Acceptance Criteria
A hop map with per-hop justification or collapse plan; at least one concrete simplification implemented (e.g. one generic glue replacing N family functions, or dev/prod manifest unification) OR a recorded operator decision that the current chain is the intended shape. title: Lie-audit standing suite: the doctrine falsifiers as CI tests
description:
Blueprint lens L-1 ('how does this lie to me?') — the operationalization of the truth-substrate thesis. Every doctrine names its falsifier (rl4); this bead turns the falsifiers into a standing test suite that catches the system lying about itself. Catalog of lie-vectors to cover: silent zeros (empty read as nothing-happened), stale CAs/projections read as current, dark derivations presenting as knowledge, confidence-without-provenance, coverage gaps rendered as absence, ts_coided read as ts_orig, replayed interpretation read as original, negative-space regressions (content-hashed ids, id-idempotency, auto-pruning creeping back — doctrine 9 / lens L-7).

## Acceptance Criteria
A named test family (xtask-runnable, e.g. -E 'test(lie_audit)') with at least one test per doctrine falsifier; each test FAILS if the falsifier's observation is produced; negative-space greps (ON CONFLICT(id) occurrence-dedup, UUIDv7-from-ts_orig) enforced in forbidden-pattern lint; suite wired into the broad local gate. VERIFY: xtask test run of the family + one deliberately-broken fixture proving a test catches its lie.
design: Depends on rl4 (the doctrine page defines the falsifiers this suite implements — do rl4 first). Split enforcement by level (type-enforcement hierarchy): greppable lies -> xtask check --forbidden patterns; behavioral lies -> sinex_test scenarios; surface lies (bare counts) -> the 42n envelope tests already partially cover. Do not duplicate 42n coverage — extend it.

title: Agent write posture: capable-but-audited (attributability tuple + effect ledger)
description:
Blueprint 018 §2 agent spine + doctrine 8: agents get the FULL MCP mutation surface (annotate, tag, propose, adjudicate, record) — audited, not restricted. Every mutating op carries a stable who-did-this tuple (actor, session, tool, intent) plus operation_id, so the effect ledger is queryable ('show me everything agent session X changed'). Attributability over prohibition.

Current state (2026-07-06): MCP server is read-only by design (crate/sinexctl/docs/mcp_readonly_server.md); mutation exists only via CLI/RPC with token-suffix RBAC; operation_id is honesty-convention (Level 6). The write surface + audit trail is greenfield.

## Acceptance Criteria
MCP exposes the mutation tool set gated per-session (write-scope config); every mutation records the attributability tuple; a query surface answers 'what did session X change' from the ledger; CLAUDE/docs update the agent-posture doctrine; no capability the operator has via CLI is withheld from agents without a recorded attributability reason. VERIFY: MCP write call round-trip on dev runtime + ledger query showing the tuple.
design: DECISION (blueprint, operator-confirmed frame): capable-but-audited, never restricted-by-default. Attributability tuple rides the existing operation_id plumbing (events carry created_by_operation_id; core.operations_log exists) — extend the operations row with actor/session/tool/intent rather than inventing a parallel ledger. MCP write tools should call the SAME RPC handlers as sinexctl (no MCP-only mutation paths). Session identity comes from the MCP transport context. Interacts: 7z0.4 judgment seat (adjudication is a write), k4c.1 recorded-analysis lane (effect ledger generalization), fcb session-bead cross-links.

title: xtask run module should resolve source-binding names
description:
During ActivityWatch replay proof for sinex-60r, `xtask run module desktop.activitywatch --bg` failed with Unknown binary 'desktop.activitywatch' even though `desktop.activitywatch` is a registered source binding. The working command was `xtask run all-sources --service-name source-driver-desktop.activitywatch-1 --bg`. Improve xtask so `run module <source-binding-id>` either resolves source bindings directly or prints the exact all-sources/service-name command for that binding. This is devloop velocity/reliability work: agents should not rediscover binding runner semantics during live source proof.

## Steps to Reproduce
xtask run module desktop.activitywatch --bg -> Unknown binary 'desktop.activitywatch', while xtask run all-sources --service-name source-driver-desktop.activitywatch-1 --bg works (observed 2026-07-05 during sinex-60r replay proof).
design: TARGETS (2026-07-06): xtask/src/commands/run.rs — RuntimeModule subcommand arm :690/:874, binary resolution failure sites :1115 ('Unknown binary … xtask run list') and :1459-:1526 ('Unknown binary: {name}'). The all-sources path already loads the dev bindings manifest (DevSourceBinding; default_source_binding_service_name :80 derives 'source-driver-<id>-1' names; --service-name filter :711-:713,:1213-:1233). Note #2328 already narrowed dev runtime component selection and #2325 narrowed automaton targets — follow that code, not older assumptions.

title: xtask jobs lacks a stop/cancel surface for background runtime jobs
description:
During interval-lift systemd proof on 2026-07-04, xtask run module interval-lift --bg created job 2001574, but xtask jobs stop 2001574 is not a supported command. That forced PID-level cleanup for a normal devloop lifecycle operation. Add a first-class xtask jobs cancel/stop command that terminates the job process tree, records exit/cancel state in history, and is safe for long-running runtime jobs.

## Steps to Reproduce
xtask run module interval-lift --bg (job 2001574, 2026-07-04); then xtask jobs stop 2001574 -> unsupported command; cleanup required manual PID kill.
design: RECONCILED 2026-07-06: the capability ALREADY EXISTS — JobManager::cancel (xtask/src/jobs/mod.rs:760; SIGTERM to the process GROUP with SIGKILL escalation after CANCEL_SIGTERM_GRACE, :758+:23) wired as 'xtask jobs cancel <id>' (commands/jobs.rs:67,118,634) since Jan 2026 (#136/#140). The 2026-07-04 incident used the verb 'stop', got no such command, and concluded the surface was missing. Fix shape = discoverability: visible aliases stop/kill on the Cancel subcommand (implemented 2026-07-06, this session) + verify cancelled state lands in history. Remaining AC beyond the alias: confirm 'cancelled' status + exit code are recorded in job history for a runtime job (xtask run module ... --bg) and that no orphan children survive group-kill.
acceptance_criteria: xtask jobs stop <id> and xtask jobs kill <id> work as aliases of cancel (clap visible_aliases — shows in --help); cancelling a live xtask run module job kills the whole process tree (no orphan sinexd/cargo PIDs) and records cancelled state in jobs history. VERIFY: xtask run module <x> --bg; xtask jobs stop <id>; xtask jobs status <id>; ps for orphans.
close_reason: Reconciled + fixed: JobManager::cancel existed since #136 with full tree-kill semantics (SIGTERM process group -> SIGKILL escalation, jobs/mod.rs:758-794) and cancelled-state recording (finish_invocation_cancelled + finish_background_job Killed). The missing piece was verb discoverability — PR #2395 (merged) adds visible aliases stop/kill on the Cancel subcommand with termination semantics in the help line. VERIFY: xtask jobs stop --help resolves to Cancel help; xtask test -p xtask -E 'test(jobs)' job 2001831 exit 0; xtask check -p xtask job 2001830 exit 0.

title: xtask proof reuse accepted stale interval-lift result after edit
description:
During sinex-8y8 AFK interval-lift work on 2026-07-04, job 2001564 passed before a one-line clamp hardening edit. A subsequent plain xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E 'test(interval_lift)' returned 'Fresh result from invocation 2005414' even though the working tree had changed; I had to force job 2001565 with --no-reuse. Investigate freshness fingerprints for focused test invocations, especially unstaged source changes made shortly after a run completes, and make stale reuse impossible or loudly explain why the tree fingerprint is still valid.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run a focused test (job passes); make a one-line source edit without staging; rerun plain xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E 'test(interval_lift)' -> 'Fresh result from invocation NNN' reused despite the dirty tree (observed 2026-07-04); --no-reuse forces a real run.
design: TARGETS + LIKELY MECHANISM (2026-07-06 code read): the base fingerprint DOES cover dirty content — tree_fingerprint_in (xtask/src/coordinator.rs:887-904) refreshes the git index (rapid same-second edits are the documented motivation) and calls hash_dirty_content. The suspect is the SCOPED path: scoped_tree_fingerprint_in (:1050-:1058) narrows hashing to a package closure via scoped_fingerprint_packages_in when -p is present — if the edited file falls outside the computed closure paths (or the closure/path mapping :910+ misses it), the fingerprint stays stable and reuse false-hits. Repro used '-p sinexd --lib -E test(interval_lift)'. Investigate: does the closure include the edited file's dir? Does the freshness key include the -E filter? Instrument with 'xtask freshness explain test -- -p sinexd --lib -E test(interval_lift)' before+after a 1-line edit; the explanation shows scope inputs (explain_freshness :1116).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and fixed: freshness fingerprint for focused test invocations covers unstaged working-tree edits (dirty-hunk hash or mtime-content probe); regression test proves an edit between run and re-query invalidates reuse; xtask freshness explain shows the invalidating input. Until fixed, --no-reuse workaround documented in command guide.
notes: 2026-07-07: proof-substrate-seal bead extends this — the stale-reuse class is broader than the interval-lift incident (live DB/NATS/env/tool versions all outside the fingerprint; proof consumption precedes preflight).

title: Make pre-push xtask rebuild path observable and cheap
description: Why this exists: pushing PR #2305 rebuilt checkout-local xtask through the pre-push changed-strict hook because this branch touched xtask/src and the hook rejected stale/direnv wrapper candidates. What needs to be done: make the pre-push path explain why each candidate is rejected, expose whether branch changes actually require rebuilding xtask, and prefer a warm checkout-local binary path when safe without bypassing changed-strict. Acceptance: a branch that does not touch xtask build inputs uses an existing current xtask binary without nix develop fallback; a branch that does touch xtask build inputs emits a compact reason and rebuilds once through the intended checkout-local path; tests or shell-level smoke cover both decisions.

title: Avoid cold schema bootstrap rebuilds for narrow proofs
description: Observed while working sinex-9u4 on 2026-07-03: focused xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(raw_stream_reconciliation)' was earlyoom-killed twice at default test-profile codegen-units=256 (rustc RSS 8.2-8.7 GiB; earlyoom threshold 5% RAM). DESIGN (2026-07-08, pq2 ADOPTED and closed — this bead is now pure encoding work, no open semantics):

TARGET: crate/sinexd/docs/automata/derivation_catalog.md, new "Formal core" section. Every composite is expressed as (time | entity | provenance | containment)+ then aggregation then interpretation.

OPERATOR TABLE to encode verbatim from the pq2 ruling:
- time (SEMANTIC, requires interval lifting): key columns = ts_orig ranges + watermark state. CLOSURE RULE: only closed-and-settled intervals are joinable (closed-before-watermark per 5s6 two-mode watermark). A join over the live edge is a category error, not a caveat — document it as a refusal state, not a caveat row.
- entity (SEMANTIC, requires resolution): key = resolved entity_id. Never raw strings; a string-match urge = a missing entity kind (rule 7).
- provenance (STRUCTURAL, free today): key = source_event_ids DAG reachability. Exact.
- containment (STRUCTURAL, free today): key = (source_material_id, anchor_byte, anchor_len) overlap. Exact.

RECLASSIFICATIONS required by the ruling: screen.grounding = containment-join (exact), NOT a fuzzy time-join; provenance_pack = provenance-join. Also classify attention.stream, work.episode, capture.coincidence.

REVISION CLOSURE (encode as a doctrine paragraph): when an input interval is superseded (y8v supersede-by-occurrence, RATIFIED), the join output is a derived descendant of the superseded row and re-derives through the SAME archive-cascade + scope-invalidation path replay uses. There is no join-specific staleness machinery; projections get staleness via 68c.4. This is what makes the algebra closed over its own inputs.

PITFALL: do not restate provenance.md or the y8v/pq2 rulings in prose — cite the closed beads and the doctrine page (rl4). The catalog states the algebra and classifies composites; the semantics live in their owning beads.

title: Decision: adopt the 4-operator join algebra (time, entity, provenance, containment)
description: derivation_catalog.md states two join keys (time-join on ts_orig intervals, entity-join on resolved ids) and 'a third ad-hoc key = a missing entity kind'. That is right for SEMANTIC joins but omits two STRUCTURAL joins intrinsic to the provenance model: provenance-join along the source_event_ids DAG (already the trace/replay substrate) and containment-join on shared source_material_id + overlapping anchor ranges. Both are available TODAY from provenance columns and are the cheapest honest L3 - and several catalog composites filed under time-join (screen.grounding) are actually containment-joins done exactly instead of fuzzily.
design:
PROPOSED RULING (2026-07-08, encoded for operator ratification — doctrine-level, one-way):

ADOPT the 4-operator join algebra. The catalog recognizes exactly four join operators; a fifth ad-hoc key is by definition a missing entity kind or a missing containment declaration.

1. TIME-JOIN (semantic): overlap/containment on ts_orig intervals. CLOSURE RULE (adversarial input 1 answered): time-joins consume only CLOSED-AND-SETTLED intervals — closed-before-watermark per the 5s6 two-mode watermark; the live edge is never joinable. A join product over an open interval is a category error, not a caveat.
2. ENTITY-JOIN (semantic): equality on resolved entity ids (never raw strings; a string match urge = missing entity kind).
3. PROVENANCE-JOIN (structural): reachability along source_event_ids — the trace/replay substrate reused as a query operator. Exact, always available.
4. CONTAINMENT-JOIN (structural): shared source_material_id + anchor-range overlap. Exact; screen.grounding and provenance_pack reclassify here (they were filed as fuzzy time-joins but are exact containment).

REVISION PROPAGATION (adversarial input 2 answered): when an input interval is superseded (y8v supersede-by-occurrence), the join output is a derived descendant of the superseded row — the SAME archive-cascade + scope-invalidation path replay uses re-derives it. No join-specific staleness machinery; projections get staleness via 68c.4. This makes the algebra closed over revision: every operator declares what its outputs do on input supersession = re-derive, uniformly.

KEY COLUMNS TABLE (for dcs to encode in derivation_catalog.md): time -> ts_orig ranges + watermark state; entity -> resolved entity_id; provenance -> source_event_ids DAG; containment -> (source_material_id, anchor_byte, anchor_len).

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED (rejected): keep 2-operator catalog + treat provenance/containment as implementation details — rejected because both are already load-bearing in replay/trace code and hiding them produces exactly the screen.grounding misclassification observed.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision adopting (or amending) the 4-operator algebra; derivation_catalog.md updated by dcs accordingly; each operator names its key columns and its semantic/structural class; screen.grounding and provenance_pack reclassified under the adopted operators. Operator sign-off (doctrine-level).
notes:
2026-07-07 sequencing round: promoted wave:4->3. This is a pure operator decision with zero hard blockers that now gates five beads (k6s, 2xy, a4w.3.2, a4w.3.3, a4w.3.12) after the dcs->pq2 gate swap; landing it before wave:4 work starts unblocks the consumption lane. One-way reversibility noted — take the deliberation, but do not let the decision idle behind implementation waves it gates.
2026-07-07 adversarial hardening — two decision inputs the join-algebra ruling must cover or explicitly defer: (1) interval-end watermark semantics: every interval end in the current stack means 'the next event arrived', not 'the state ended' (closure-by-next-arrival, see 5s6) — a time-join must define which intervals are joinable (closed-before-watermark) or joins over the live edge are nondeterministic; (2) revision propagation: intervals have no revision mechanism today (y8v) — the algebra must say what happens to a join output when an input interval is later superseded/extended (re-derive via scope invalidation? projection-only staleness via 68c.4?). Without both, the algebra is not closed over its actual inputs.
RATIFIED 2026-07-08 (operator, decision-brief batch): 4-operator join algebra ADOPTED as specified in design (closure rule: closed-and-settled inputs only; revision propagation: supersession re-derives via the replay invalidation path). Catalog encoding is owned by dcs (open). Closing this decision bead.
close_reason: Decision FINAL and operator-ratified 2026-07-08: 4-operator join algebra ADOPTED (time/entity/provenance/containment) with the closure rule (joins consume closed-and-settled intervals only) and revision propagation (input supersession re-derives outputs via the replay archive-cascade/invalidation path — no join-specific staleness machinery). Key-columns table in design. Catalog encoding owned by sinex-dcs (open, now unblocked); screen.grounding/provenance_pack reclassify under containment there. Verify: bd show sinex-pq2 (design ruling + ratification note); bd show sinex-dcs (catalog carrier open).

title: Decision: bound the wildcard fan-in (five automata reading *)
description: Five automata read the wildcard event stream (session, analytics, entity_extractor, tag_applier, and the summarizers via activity). This is the automaton-side of the telemetry-lane lesson: x9i separated self-observation for the ENGINE, not for the automaton fan-out. Every new *-reader is a linear cost on the busiest stream.
design:
DECISION FRAME: the *-readers are session-detector (by design: needs everything), analytics, tag-applier (+ summarizers via broad activity types); entity-extractor was narrowed to MaterialOnly earlier (8a589c0be). Reflection-lane separation (x9i) already removes self-observation volume from the activity stream.

PROPOSED RULING (2026-07-08, encoded for operator ratification): per-automaton verdicts, effective with pq5-B: (1) session-detector: KEEP WILDCARD — its contract is everything by design. (2) entity-extractor/resolver/enricher/relation-extractor: MOOT under pq5 ruling (B) — default-disabled removes them from the fan-in entirely; on shadow-lane re-entry they return with explicit filter_subjects allowlists, never wildcard. (3) analytics + tag-applier: DEMAND-GATE — default-disabled until a named consumer exists (same construct-validity logic as pq5; recall p1 consuming analytics would be that evidence). title: xtask preflight/proof substrate seal (original pre-queue DDL race fixed on master)
description:
Concurrent xtask invocations can run checkout-local SQLx/Postgres schema bootstrap before the coordinated job slot is assigned. During recall verification on 2026-07-03, launching test/check commands in parallel emitted duplicate pg_class_relname_nsp_index errors for ix_archived_events_archived_at / ix_archived_events_ts_orig, even though xtask later queued jobs behind the active slot. This is confusing observability and a real reliability smell: the queue boundary should cover schema bootstrap, or schema apply must be idempotent under concurrent bootstrap.

## Steps to Reproduce
On a fresh checkout, launch two xtask test/check invocations simultaneously -> duplicate pg_class_relname_nsp_index errors for ix_archived_events_archived_at / ix_archived_events_ts_orig during concurrent schema bootstrap (observed 2026-07-03).
design: Move checkout-local SQLx schema bootstrap behind the same coordinated slot used by xtask jobs, or add a per-checkout bootstrap lock before apply. Do not paper over this by telling agents never to use --bg; xtask should make queued parallel verification safe and quiet. Evidence jobs: 2001381-2001383, with foreground wrapper output showing duplicate pg_class_relname_nsp_index while jobs were queued/running.
acceptance_criteria: Two xtask test/check invocations launched simultaneously on a fresh checkout produce zero duplicate pg_class/index-exists errors: bootstrap runs exactly once behind the coordinated slot or a per-checkout lock, the second waits. VERIFY: parallel launch repro from description; check journald/xtask output for ix_archived_events_* duplicate errors.
notes: 2026-07-07 audit (new-gpt-pro 03): the originally-described failure (two frontends both run DDL before queueing on a fresh checkout) is FIXED in current source — wrapper SQLx bootstrap serialized under flock (flake.nix:1884-1897), launcher-only --bg skips pre-exec bootstrap (flake.nix:1457-1464), Rust schema apply waits on exclusive lock (preflight.rs:977-1011). Remaining live risk is proof reuse bypassing/under-sealing preflight — now owned by the proof-substrate-seal bead. Keep this bead only for the parallel-smoke regression (two xtask check --bg on a schema-pending checkout, second queues without duplicate pg_class/index errors); close after that test lands.

title: Moment search / evidence windows: seed hits become intervals, intervals gather heterogeneous evidence, output states support and overreach
description: The flagship consumption capability of the substrate claim, and a genuinely new query shape: 'commands I ran while discussing X' is not an event search — it is a MOMENT search. Pipeline: (1) SEED: full-text/semantic hits for X in agent messages (or any content family) produce candidate anchor points; (2) WINDOW: anchors lift to candidate time intervals (session-bounded, gap-merged — interval logic shared with attention.stream, not reinvented); (3) GATHER: within each window, pull heterogeneous evidence across families — shell commands, window focus, browser visits, fs activity, git operations, machine context — via the normal ts_orig window queries; (4) REPORT: for each moment, state SUPPORT (evidence consistent with the seed topic), CAVEATS (families with no coverage in the window — from source-continuity data), CONTRADICTIONS (evidence inconsistent with the claim), and TEMPORAL OVERREACH (the seed discussed X at 14:02-14:15; commands at 14:40 are adjacent, not during — the boundary is stated, not smoothed). This is where Sinex-as-backend pays: heterogeneous evidence without forcing everything into Polylogue's chat schema. Polylogue consumes it for 'what was happening around this session'; the operator consumes it for any 'while' question; agents consume it via MCP.
design: DECISIONS: (1) build as a composition over existing primitives — seed search (docs/semantic search + payload text match), interval lifting (shared L2 helper), window evidence pull (the recall/context substrate) — the new code is the orchestration + the four-verdict report shape, NOT a parallel query engine (algebra rule). (2) Surface: sinexctl moments <query> [--families ...] [--range ...] + an events/context RPC + MCP tool; output = moment cards, each with interval, seed refs, per-family evidence refs, and the four verdict sections; every claim in the report is a resolvable ref. (3) Support/contradiction classification starts MECHANICAL (family presence, term co-occurrence, count thresholds — each a measured quantity per standing rule 1); LLM-graded relevance is a later recorded-effect enrichment (k4c.1 lane), never a hardcoded score. (4) Coverage caveats reuse the source-continuity machinery from recall verbatim. (5) Latency: moment search is explicitly a bounded-work operation (N windows cap, per-family limits) — it inherits the g3k read-model outcome; do not promise interactive full-archive moments before that lands. PITFALL: seeds from agent messages need the observation vocabulary sibling landed first for message-grain anchors; the fallback seed source (documents/browser content) works today — build the pipeline against what exists, add the agent family when the lane flows.
acceptance_criteria: The motivating query works end-to-end: given a topic discussed in a known session, sinexctl moments returns the discussion interval(s) with the shell commands actually run during them, families absent from the window listed as caveats, and adjacent-but-outside evidence marked as overreach rather than included silently; all refs resolve; JSON stable for MCP; a falsifier run (topic never discussed) returns zero moments, not fabricated ones.

title: The adjudication seat: a judgment queue an operator can actually clear
description: The place you JUDGE — the missing workflow for the doctrine's only path to truth. Today proposals (shadow-lane entities/relations/curation diffs) accumulate with no queue, no triage order, no fast accept/reject loop; when the semantic plane activates (sinex-5v6, sinex-2nd), an unworkable judgment UX means L4 silently stops mattering. Build: a proposal queue surface (TUI pane + CLI) ordered by evidence strength x staleness, single-keystroke judge (accept/reject/edit-then-accept/defer), batch judgment over a selection with one recorded judgment covering N proposals (the judgment event carries all proposal parents), and session summaries ('you judged 40 proposals, 3 deferred'). Delegated policy comes AFTER the manual loop proves its shape: a recorded standing judgment ('auto-accept entity-merge proposals with >=N corroborating sources from lane L') is itself an adjudication object with provenance — but do not build delegation before the manual queue has real usage evidence.
design: DECISION: judgments stay typed and recorded exactly per doctrine (§adjudication) — the UX changes throughput, never the authority model; batch = one judgment event, N proposal parents (legal: NonEmptyVec); queue ordering factors are each measured quantities surfaced in the row (standing rule 1); defer is a first-class verdict so the queue can reach zero honestly; queue age/depth are telemetry so the epic's 'judged within days' acceptance is measurable. Surfaces: sinexctl semantic judge (interactive TUI mode + scriptable flags) over the existing curation/proposal read models — check sinexctl semantic + curation_proposals MCP tool for the current read surface before adding any.
acceptance_criteria: Operator clears a real 50-proposal backlog in one sitting without leaving the TUI; every canonical write traces to a judgment event with proposal parents; queue depth/age queryable; deferred items resurface; no auto-promotion path exists.

title: Daily-grain rollup lane + parity: per-domain (domain, local-day) derived events replace Lynchpin daily products
description: Lynchpin's layer-3 (derived daily products: daily_signals.ndjson, spotify/daily.ndjson, web_category_daily, operator_daily) and its DuckDB substrate tables exist to make cross-domain daily correlation cheap. Sinex replacement: a general per-domain daily-rollup lane — windowed/scope-reconciler automata keyed (domain, local-day) emitting typed daily summary events (activity, terminal, web, media, physiological once rkv.6 lands, machine telemetry) — plus query units over them (sinex-lv8 direction) so 'join domains on day' is one query expression, not an NDJSON copy step. The existing hourly/daily summarizers are the seed; this generalizes them from activity-only to per-domain and makes local-day (timezone-honest, cf. sinex-nbi.5) the scope key. Parity target: every field Lynchpin's daily products carried either exists in a Sinex daily event, is derivable by query, or is recorded as deliberately dropped in the ledger.
design: DECISION: one parameterized daily-rollup automaton family (domain -> input filter + reducer), not N bespoke automata; scope = (domain, local_day, tz) with DST-correct day boundaries; emitted kind activity.summary.daily.<domain> or a single kind with domain field (prefer single kind + domain field — parsimony rule); replayable (semantics_version); backfill over history via normal replay, paced (sinex-2n9). Query side: day-grain query units so 'sleep_hours x commits_count by day' is expressible in one expression — this is the acceptance query.
acceptance_criteria: sinexctl query can answer a two-domain day-grain join (e.g. sleep duration vs commit count per day over a month) in one expression against derived daily events; parity table for daily_signals fields recorded in the subsumption ledger; timezone/DST day-boundary test passes.
notes:
2026-07-06 parity source enumeration (from census): the proving domains are lynchpin health_daily + sleep_productivity + personal_signals substrate tables — their DuckDB schemas ARE the parity column lists. Substrate table defs: /realm/project/sinity-lynchpin/lynchpin/substrate/{personal,readers_health}.py.
2026-07-08: this lane is the canonical example of the generality rule — one parameterized family, domains as data. Physiological (rkv.6), web (rkv.16), media (spotify), machine (rkv.17) all land as domain parameters here; any PR adding a per-domain rollup automaton instead is wrong by doctrine.

title: Recorded-analysis lane: generalize the effect ledger from model calls to arbitrary computations
description: Apply the independently landable sinex-k4c.1.1 recorded-effect envelope to one-shot cross-source computations. This bead owns the recorded-analysis command/profile, provenance artifacts, and promotion path; k4c.1.1 owns RequestKey, ResultRecord, EligibilityRecord, ReplayPolicy, encoding, persistence, and the explainer used by this and other runners.
design:
ENVELOPE PREREQUISITE:
sinex-k4c.1.1 lands the reusable typed effect contract and persistence boundary first. This bead consumes that contract and does not redefine identity, result integrity, eligibility, or replay policy.

RECORDED-ANALYSIS PROFILE:
Analysis records add question/title, query-unit specs and as-of watermark, input event/material digest, code hash/ref, semantics tag, artifact refs, and optional derived events as operation-specific fields under k4c.1.1. Re-run creates a new execution/result record under the same or changed RequestKey; it never mutates prior evidence. Large provenance uses a registered analysis artifact/material rather than unbounded parent arrays. A proven recurring analysis can promote to an automaton without changing the envelope contract.

The command resolves inputs at an explicit frontier, records the canonical RequestKey before execution, persists result/eligibility/provenance through k4c.1.1, and explains unchanged reuse versus changed recomputation.
acceptance_criteria: After sinex-k4c.1.1 lands, an agent runs one cross-source analysis in one command. Show resolves its RequestKey, eligibility, code/input hashes, output_hash, artifact, as-of frontier, and provenance through the shared envelope. An unchanged rerun is detectable; changing query/input/code/semantics changes the request; an authorization change can forbid reuse without rewriting history. A large-input case uses a registered artifact rather than unbounded parents, and a promotion fixture proves a recurring analysis can move to an automaton without another effect-key type.

title: Lynchpin subsumption: absorb the higher-order layers properly, retire the stopgap
description: Operator directive (2026-07-03): ~total subsumption of Lynchpin into Sinex — not just sources. Lynchpin is the dormant stopgap; Sinex is the real system. Its four layers map onto the tower, and the higher layers are the hard, valuable part. Layer map: (1) lynchpin.sources.* typed iterators -> Sinex source contracts over RAW provider data (never Lynchpin's processed intermediates); (2) lynchpin.substrate.* DuckDB read models (commit_fact, ai_work_event, machine_metric_sample) -> Sinex query units / consumer-maintained projections; (3) /realm/data/derived/lynchpin daily products (daily_signals, spotify/daily) -> L2 windowed daily-rollup automata, typed + versioned + replayable; (4) lynchpin.analysis.* (~40 modules: burnout_warning, mood_correlations, lifestyle_correlations, sleep_architecture_productivity, substance_kinetics, productivity_predictors, life_phase, operator_rhythm, weather_correlations...) -> split into standing derivations (L3 automata: baselines, anomaly, episode composites) and one-shot investigations (the recorded-analysis lane — the new abstraction this epic forces, see child bead); (5) graph/context packs -> recall/context (already Sinex's). EXCLUDED for now (operator): codebase analytics (dms/, code_index, code_quality, code_history_claims, tool_rules). Existing beads that become this epic's limbs: sinex-44q (source promotion ledger), sinex-rkv.6 (health raw-fidelity), sinex-stm (import glue), sinex-a4w.3.6 (routine.baseline/anomaly), sinex-a4w.3 composites generally.
design: DOCTRINE FOR TRANSLATION (settled): Lynchpin things are not ported line-for-line — each is re-derived from what question it answered. Rule per module: name the question -> classify {standing derivation | one-shot investigation | read model | dead} -> map to {L3 automaton | recorded analysis | query unit/projection | retire}. Raw-data rule: every subsumed source re-lands on ORIGINAL provider data as materials; Lynchpin processed intermediates are never inputs (they are evidence for parity checks only). Parity-then-retire rule: a Lynchpin module turns off only when a named Sinex surface answers its question with an evidence artifact proving parity or superiority; the ledger records question -> lynchpin module -> sinex surface -> parity artifact. Daily-grain rule: cross-domain daily correlation (sleep x productivity, weather x mood) requires the (domain, local-day) rollup lane as query units — the composite plane's daily grain, not ad-hoc NDJSON.
acceptance_criteria: Every non-excluded Lynchpin module has a ledger verdict with evidence; the 'port' rows have child/linked beads; the recorded-analysis abstraction is decided and implemented (child); at least the health+sleep and daily-signals families run natively in Sinex with parity artifacts; Lynchpin runs nothing on a schedule that Sinex now answers.

The subsumption toolkit, by purpose: ingest shape -> stm static-import glue + producer protocol (zi6); occurrence identity & re-import -> 908 dedup regimes (never per-source dedup code); interval/session/episode shapes -> the declarative state-evidence engine (4b86: evidence adapters + closure policies + fence table) — sleep sessions, listening sessions, browse sessions are ADAPTERS + POLICY ROWS there, never new interval logic; multi-witness composites -> 0eam fusion declarations; day-grain aggregation -> the k4c.2 parameterized rollup family (never a per-domain rollup automaton); one-shot investigations -> k4c.1 recorded-analysis lane; read models -> 68c projection registry; operator/agent surfaces -> x5mg pack pipeline. title: Capture-stall alerting: sources must not silently stop capturing (push, not caveat)
description: Today a stalled source surfaces only as a pull-side caveat: the recall-v2 terminal packet itself shipped with browser.history in runtime_binding_stalled, and nobody was notified — the stall was discovered because a demo happened to render caveats. The recall caveat plumbing (source-status gap details, runtime_binding_stalled classification) already computes the right facts; what is missing is the push leg: when a source with an expected cadence stops producing output beyond its family-appropriate threshold, the operator gets an actionable desktop notification (and the fact lands as a reflexive event). This is the capability behind demo sinex-cem.2 (fault injection proves the detector); the demo must not be the only consumer. Distinct from sinex-r6d.3 (honest health = truthful check results) — this is delivery of those results to the operator without being asked.
design: DECISION: reuse existing source-continuity/source-status classification as the single detector (no parallel staleness logic). A small watcher (sinexd-internal tick or systemd timer running sinexctl sources status --format json) evaluates per-source expected-cadence thresholds from the source contract/binding (continuous sources: minutes-hours; scheduled imports: their period + slack); emits notify-send on transition into stalled and on recovery, plus a reflexive event for history. Threshold config lives with the binding, not hardcoded per source. Anti-flap: alert on state transition only.
acceptance_criteria: Killing the browser runtime binding (or the cem.2 fault injection) produces an operator notification within one evaluation period and a queryable stall event; recovery notifies once; no notification storms from a flapping source; thresholds visible in sources status output.

title: Stop devshell xtask launchers rebuilding schema-apply bootstrap repeatedly
description: During repeated xtask test/check/build launches on 2026-07-03, the devshell wrapper rebuilt schema-apply-bootstrap before queueing jobs, even for quick reruns. This adds ~30-60s of serial latency before useful background work starts. Investigate the flake/devshell wrapper path and make schema bootstrap reuse/cache/queue behavior explicit without bypassing SQLx correctness. Evidence jobs around 2001369-2001373 repeatedly printed 'this derivation will be built: ... schema-apply-bootstrap-0.4.2.drv' before job start.
design: DIAGNOSE FIRST (the fix depends on which layer rebuilds): evidence shows 'this derivation will be built: schema-apply-bootstrap-0.4.2.drv' repeatedly — determine whether (a) the drv inputs genuinely change per invocation (e.g. a timestamp/env/store-path leak into the derivation), (b) the wrapper calls nix build without --no-link/reuse so the result is GC'd or not cached, or (c) the wrapper unconditionally rebuilds instead of checking an existing result symlink/profile. FIX SHAPE by branch: (a) pin the leaking input; (b/c) cache the built bootstrap at a stable per-checkout path (.sinex/ or the /var/cache/sinex tree) keyed by the drv hash, and have the wrapper exec the cached result when the hash matches — rebuild only on real input change. HARD CONSTRAINT: never skip SQLx schema correctness — the cache key must cover schema defs; a stale bootstrap running against changed defs is worse than the latency.
acceptance_criteria: Back-to-back xtask check launches show zero 'will be built' schema-bootstrap lines on the second run (cold->warm proven with timestamps); a schema-defs edit DOES trigger rebuild (cache-key correctness); serial pre-job latency for warm launches drops by the measured 30-60s; root cause written in the closing comment (which branch it was).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2286: devshell cargo/xtask wrappers now cache the schema-apply-bootstrap executable path under SINEX_DEV_STATE_DIR, keyed by a source fingerprint over Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, flake.nix, crate/sinex-schema, and crate/sinex-primitives. Warm in-devshell SQLx-needed xtask launch verified at 1.657s with no schema-apply-bootstrap build line; temporary schema definition edit triggered the rebuild path.

title: Replace recall diversity top-up with bounded shared query
description: The sinex-0tj hardening slice made recall finite and observable, but live proof still shows diversity_top_up consuming its full 8s budget and returning recall.diversity_top_up_timeout. Replace the sequential per-source events.cards loop in crate/sinexctl/src/commands/context.rs with either a bounded concurrent implementation or, preferably, a server-side source-diverse event-card query in the shared events/context substrate. Preserve algebraic query composition; do not add a recall-only silo.
design: DECISION: server-side source-diverse event-card query in the shared events/context substrate (option 2 of the 0tj packet — the bounded-concurrent CLI loop is acceptable only as an interim commit if the server query stalls). Shape: one RPC extending events.cards semantics — given a base filter + a diversity spec (source/family list), return base latest cards PLUS latest card per requested source in one disclosure pass; implemented in the composable-query layer (crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events/composable_query.rs) as a lateral/union-per-source plan bounded by the existing indexes (ix_events_source_ts_orig), NOT a recall-only handler. CLI top_up_context_diversity (context.rs:456) collapses to one call. Keep stage timings from the 0tj instrumentation; keep the diversity budget caveat for the degraded path. PITFALL: per-source LIMIT 1 over ts_orig on the hypertable is the exact shape g3k is diagnosing — run EXPLAIN on the generated plan before declaring the latency win; if chunk-exclusion kills it, this bead's RPC consolidation still lands (1 RPC vs N) and the plan evidence hands off to g3k.
acceptance_criteria: Recall issues a bounded number of RPCs independent of missing-source count (target: 1 cards RPC + optional source-status); diversity_top_up stage time drops from 8s-budget-exhaustion to sub-second on the dev store with the EXPLAIN plan recorded; composable-query tests cover the diversity spec; no recall-only query silo (the RPC is usable by any events consumer).

title: Emit bounded multi-entity outputs from entity extractor
description: Dead-lane sweep follow-up from sinex-y7l and fixture prerequisite for sinex-a4w.1. entity_extractor currently returns only find_first_entity from a single-output transducer, hiding co-occurring URL/email/file/tool entities in one input event. Move to bounded multi-output extraction or equivalent shared runtime support.
design: DECISION: extend the extraction to bounded multi-output while keeping the Transducer runtime shape — emit ONE entity.extracted event whose payload carries a bounded entities[] array (deterministic order: by kind priority then first-occurrence offset; cap configurable, default ~8 with an overflow count field), rather than N events per input. Rationale: one input -> one interpretation event preserves 1:1 occurrence mapping and avoids multiplying the already-noisy lane (the 2h demo window showed 503 extractor events — one per input; N-per-input would make it the top volume source); consumers and the golden set (a4w.1) score the array. The single-output DerivedNodeImpl constraint (one event_type per node) is untouched — same type, richer payload. Schema: bump the payload schema + semantics_version so replay re-derives history under the new semantics when invoked. PITFALL: keep find_first_entity's kind-priority logic as the ORDER, not the FILTER.
acceptance_criteria: An input containing multiple supported entity kinds emits all bounded matches with deterministic ordering and volume limits. Existing priority/first-match behavior is replaced by tests that assert URL/email/file/tool co-occurrence. Entity golden-set scoring can evaluate all predicted entities. One entity.extracted event per input (bounded entities[] payload), never N events per input; overflow count present when the cap truncates.

title: Fix entity enricher active-hours timezone semantics
description:
Dead-lane sweep follow-up from sinex-y7l. entity_enricher active_hours currently buckets by raw UTC hour, which is a misleading behavioral surface for operator-local activity. Decide and implement either operator-local timezone with explicit metadata or delete the field.

## Steps to Reproduce
Ingest activity spanning a local-vs-UTC hour boundary; entity_enricher active_hours buckets by raw UTC hour, so evening local activity lands in the wrong day/hours for any operator east of UTC.
design: DECISION (settled now per design-now doctrine): operator-local timezone with explicit metadata — not deletion. Rationale: active-hours is exactly the shape routine.baseline (a4w.3.6) consumes, so the field has a named consumer derivation; raw-UTC bucketing is the bug, not the field. Implementation: bucket by the operator's local tz (from config, one authority — the same local-day source k4c.2 standardizes; do NOT invent a second tz-resolution path), stamp the payload with the tz used (tz_id field) so the value is self-describing, bump semantics_version, and replay re-derives history when invoked. While in the file: grep the automata for other raw-UTC-hour bucketing (this is the template instance of the timezone-class sweep noted on the nbi epic).
acceptance_criteria: active_hours histogram computed in operator-local timezone (config/env-provided, not host guess) with explicit tz metadata on the payload; DST-boundary test; entity_enricher docs/derivation_catalog name routine.baseline (a4w.3.6) as the consumer. VERIFY: xtask test -p sinexd -E 'test(enricher)' incl. a fixed-offset + DST case.

title: Classify source contracts by replayability and loss authority
description: Checkpoint-loss matrix follow-up from sinex-r6d.1. The loss-window matrix needs source rows grouped by whether the source is a live observation, mutable snapshot, append stream, staged export, or external producer, and what authority can replay/catch up after a crash.

Add explicit SourceRecoveryPolicy to SourceRuntimeBinding, not SourceContract, because binding owns deployment/runtime recovery shape: runner_pack, checkpoint_family, runtime_shape, material_lifecycle, and transport_semantics. Make the policy typestate-required in SourceRuntimeBindingBuilder, add a builder method, extend SourceMeta/SourceDefinition attrs, export to source catalog/package completeness/source-status/replay views, and make replay planner/executor reject archive-then-scan replay for non-replayable bindings unless an explicit operator override records degraded recovery. Non-replayable/live bindings either prove zero silent-loss windows or link fix Beads/accepted-loss records. Replay archive/execution refuses non-replayable source replay before archiving live rows unless explicit operator override records degraded/non-replayable recovery. title: Honest health: replace default-true checks and presence-only verify probes
design: PROBLEM (construct-validity inventory): the system's self-assessment conflates liveness with correctness. Health checks default to true (Level 6 convention — a check that measures nothing); ops verify probes assert presence ('automaton emitted something'), not correctness ('output is right'). Both name constructs they do not measure. DESIGN: (1) health checks must compute their verdict from evidence or report unknown — a default-true path becomes a typed Unknown{reason} state rendered distinctly from Healthy (no more free greens); (2) ops verify gains correctness-class probes alongside presence: for each derived family, a cheap invariant check (e.g. session boundaries non-overlapping, daily summary parent-set spans the day, canonical commands parse back) declared next to the automaton; (3) the health aggregator distinguishes liveness / correctness / unknown per component in its report events, so current_health stops laundering unknown into healthy. RULE this operationalizes (doctrine rule 1): every verdict carries evidence-provenance or is absent.
acceptance_criteria: No health path returns a default-true verdict (rg proves; defaults become Unknown); ops verify reports presence and correctness columns per family with at least one real invariant probe per running automaton; current_health view exposes the three-state distinction; a deliberately-broken automaton output flips correctness while liveness stays green (test).
notes:
2026-07-07 audit integration: verified on master — HealthReporter constructs with last_status=Healthy, liveness_ok=true (health_reporter.rs new_with_clock); missing reporter counts as healthy via is_none_or (adapter/mod.rs:494 health_check, :630 exploration view). Fix shape: HealthStatus::Unknown (or HealthVerdict{observed,status}) until first successful probe; missing reporter renders Unknown/Degraded, never green; split liveness/correctness/freshness/probe-ran into separate fields; render Unknown distinctly in TUI/API/CLI.
Accelerant pointer (2026-07-08): execution packet = .agent/scratch/new/sinex_urgent_correctness_systematic_v2.md section 7 (default-healthy -> Unknown/Unproven). Line anchors in the packet are from a drifted snapshot — re-verify against master on claim (021 protocol).
close_reason: Merged sinex/#2418: HealthReporter::calculate_status() reports Unknown until real evidence exists (has_evidence() gate on events_processed>0 or a completed liveness probe), last_status inits to Unknown, and the two is_none_or(missing-reporter-is-healthy) sites in adapter/mod.rs now use is_some_and. Verified: automata/health.rs's aggregator was already correct (excludes never-reported components, computes Unknown overall status) — this fix feeds it sound leaf data rather than requiring aggregator changes. Deliberately did NOT touch heartbeat.rs (investigated the identical-looking pattern, found 3 existing tests encode zero-errors-across-N-ticks=healthy as intentional; a heartbeat's existence is itself liveness evidence unlike HealthReporter's zero-effort error_rate()). Residual/deferred: ops-verify correctness-class probes per automaton family (a separate, larger feature — not started). AC honesty: 'no default-true health path' and 'three-state distinction exposed' are satisfied; 'ops verify gains correctness-class probes... at least one real invariant probe per running automaton' is NOT done. Verify: xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E 'test(health_reporter) | test(heartbeat)' -> 16 passed.

title: Projection mechanism unification: migrate documents off the DB trigger (operator-decided)
design: DECISION (operator, 2026-07-03): documents MIGRATE off the trigger path. The standing rule this establishes: consumer-maintained projections (event-engine post-persist hooks or dedicated consumers on the confirmed stream) are THE read-model mechanism for product surfaces; TimescaleDB CAs remain for telemetry rollups only (and move to the reflection table per the telemetry-lane design); DB triggers are retired as a projection mechanism. TARGET: core.fn_document_projection() + trg_document_projection on core.events (crate/sinex-schema/src/defs/documents.rs:292-345) — an AFTER-INSERT trigger folding document.ingested/document.chunked events into core.documents/core.document_chunks. MIGRATION: (1) implement a document-projection consumer on the confirmed stream (same site/pattern as the recall.timeline hook design in the latency bead — build them on one hook mechanism, that is the point); (2) declare it as a DerivationSpec with rebuild + invalidation (replay/redaction), which the trigger version cannot express; (3) backfill/verify parity against the trigger-maintained tables; (4) DROP the trigger + function and remove their schema-apply emission (also shrinks the gh#2182 boot-lock surface — one fewer unconditional CREATE FUNCTION/TRIGGER at boot). WHY the trigger is the odd one out: it is invisible to the derivation registry (no DerivationSpec, no rebuild operation, no invalidation semantics), runs inside the insert transaction (couples ingest latency to projection cost), and is exactly the class of unconditional DDL the boot-race fix has to guard around.
acceptance_criteria: Document projection maintained by a confirmed-stream consumer with DerivationSpec + rebuild op; parity proven against trigger output on the same input set before cutover; trigger + function dropped from defs and from live DBs via convergence; doc search behavior unchanged (existing document tests green); one projection mechanism documented as the standing rule in the schema design docs.
notes: 2026-07-07 overlap reconciliation: sinex-68c.2 (wave:4) registers the document projection in derivation.projection_registry with readiness caveats; THIS bead (wave:9) changes the maintenance mechanism (DB trigger -> confirmed-stream consumer). Sequencing: 68c.2 may register the trigger-maintained projection as-is (status/fingerprint honest about the mechanism); when nbi.3 lands, the registry row's semantics_version/verification_command update. The operator decision recorded here (consumer-maintained projections are THE read-model mechanism; CAs only for telemetry) is standing doctrine for 68c/0vx.4 schema work — do not design the registry around trigger-maintained projections as the long-term shape. Also note: document_chunks ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING staleness (privacy audit) is another reason the trigger path retires.

title: Golden recall/context fixture with stable occurrence labels (supersedes entity-only golden set)
description: Versioned recall-context fixture: ~40 resumption questions over bounded ts_orig windows producing ~200 gold items with relevance grades (0-3), roles, stable occurrence identities, gap expectations, negative assertions, and salience judgments. The measurement substrate for cem.5 (pgvector decision), cem.7 (resumption duel), uxd (salience), and pq5 (dark-entity verdict). Full protocol + JSON Schema (sinex.recall_golden_set/v1) in .agent/scratch/new-gpt-pro/sessions/06-recall-quality-eval. Reframed 2026-07-07 from the entity-only golden set; the entity-extraction baseline survives as a sub-fixture.
design: QUESTION: what is the measured P/R of the current 4-regex entity baseline — and what fixture will every future lane comparison score against? INSTRUMENT: hand-label ~200 events (entities + relations) sampled across sources, LABELED BEFORE any lane runs (pre-registration); score the current extractor against it. ARTIFACT: the committed golden set + the baseline P/R number. PURPOSE: the prerequisite instrument for the semantic-lane duel demo and all LLM-lane work — without it the A/B harness has nothing valid to measure against. Also becomes the standing monthly drift-check epoch fixture (U9 class 4).
acceptance_criteria: Committed recall_golden_v1 fixture: >=40 resumption questions producing >=200 labeled gold items across strata — 50% high-signal work windows, 25% gap/edge windows, 15% sparse/single-source, 10% negative controls; source families terminal/browser/filesystem/git/desktop/activitywatch + derived attention/interval/session. Fixture uses JSON Schema sinex.recall_golden_set/v1 (full schema in new-gpt-pro sessions/06) recording store epoch, repo commit, source-coverage snapshot, label protocol version, and generator exclusions. Labels committed BEFORE any retrieval/pack/salience/duel runs (git history proves precedence). Every grade-2/3 item has stable identity: source-material occurrence identity when available, else derived equivalence_key + parent refs, else explicit manual key with rationale — never bare event ids (replay mints new ids). Gap expectations labeled against the caveat vocabulary (source.absent, window.partial, coverage.unmeasurable, derivation.lane_not_promoted, recall.session_rows_absent, recall.attention_lineage_timeout). Annotation protocol: 8-12-item or 20-minute batches, first-class defer reasons, 10-15% hidden duplicates, sentinel windows, adjudication flow; consistency report emits weighted kappa, Jaccard, salience-rank correlation, defer rate. The entity-extraction baseline this bead originally described is preserved as a separate sub-fixture (still unblocks lane duels / pq5) and is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence for recall/context quality.

title: Recall salience scoring: every term measured, breakdown in the DTO
description: Recall (sinex-vhm) needs ranking beyond family round-robin, and doctrine forbids unexplained numbers. This implements the honest scoring design from handoff U4. Sequence after the truthfulness slice (sinex-vhm) so scores rank real derived-plane rows, not the degenerate heuristic.
design: DESIGN (settled, from handoff U4): score(card) = w_r*recency + w_x*rarity + w_e*effort + w_a*anchor, with family-diversity as a re-rank pass (not a score term). Every term is a measured quantity: recency = exp-decay on ts_orig with half-life = the MEASURED session-gap median (not a magic number); rarity = -log(frequency of the canonical form in a trailing 30d window) computable from command_frequency_hourly CA + per-family equivalents; effort = dwell/duration evidence (session length share, fs edit churn); anchor = boundary bonus (session start/end, first-seen entity). Weights: fixed documented constants initially; the DTO carries per-term contributions (salience: {recency: .41, rarity: .32, ...}) so the number has provenance — doctrine rule 1. Calibration loop later via the predictions domain (operator marks rows that did/didn't matter).
acceptance_criteria: Recall rows carry a salience breakdown whose terms are each traceable to a measured quantity; removing a term's evidence (e.g. no session data) drops the term, never fabricates it; ranking is stable and explainable in the JSON output; a doc comment names each constant and its provenance. VERIFY: unit tests on the scorer with synthetic distributions; live recall output inspection.
notes: 2026-07-07 eval harness defines the salience acceptance experiment (uxd_salience_ranking_v1): reverse-chronological baseline vs measured-salience arm; primary nDCG@10 with lower 95% CI >= +0.05 AND salience_term_nonfabrication == 1.0 (any fabricated term kills); every displayed salience contribution must trace to measured evidence and removing the evidence must remove/reduce the term.
