title: Devloop and meta plane
description: The devloop-and-meta plane: the loop that builds Sinex must itself be honest, fast, and observable. Owns: task-substrate integrity (beads as the shared source of truth), verification trustworthiness (impact planner correctness — a false skip is a lie the loop tells itself), dev-infra friction (anything adding serial seconds to every iteration), and loop observability (the evidence a future agent needs to resume cold).
design: LIMBS by function — VERIFICATION TRUST: 1p2.2 (impact planner staged-hunk blindness + evidence staleness — fix before relying on narrowed test runs), 1p2.1 (dead-lane reachability lint). FRICTION: guw (schema-bootstrap rebuild tax on every launch), 1ul (5432 collision blocks concurrent lanes), jvs (2.5min/7GiB single-test compile tax). OBSERVABILITY: 8zy (JetStream state into xtask analytics store — the SQL-blind-spot lesson), pke (connect disconnected verification machinery). SUBSTRATE: hlv (beads+devloop as sources; ownership boundaries settled), 06d (schema-bundle drift in pre-push). INTEGRATION HYGIENE: keep the reconcile lesson — the ahead-train cost compounds per devloop pass; PR flow is restored (uzl closed), keep it. SEQUENCING: 1p2.2 and guw first — they tax or corrupt every single loop iteration; everything else is per-occasion.
acceptance_criteria: Exit criteria: impact planner produces no false skips on the known vectors (staged changes, stale evidence) with regression tests; a second concurrent checkout/agent lane works without infra collision; a cold agent can reconstruct loop state from bd + committed artifacts alone; JetStream reality visible in xtask analytics.

title: Capture breadth and quality
description: Finish and deploy the capture surface: dark finished sources into deployment, attention-source data quality, the media and email runtime tiers, and the new predictions domain. Cheap breadth first (static-import glue), quality where it blocks cross-source value (attention sources).
design: DOCTRINE: breadth via the generic lane, quality gated before joining composites, portfolio pruned by decision not drift. LIMBS: stm (the scheduled static-import glue — cheapest breadth, unlocks the 21 dark contracts); 2bk (trust the deployment path first); 60r (quality gate: attention sources currently ingest garbage — blocks attention.stream); new sources rkv.1 (GitHub/CI — outcome leg), rkv.2 (nix generations), rkv.3 (browser content — opens topics), rkv.4 (calendar — the only planned-time capture), rkv.5 (mobile export bridges), rkv.6 (physiological — RAW provider data only), rkv.7 (satellite hosts — capture topology expansion); di7 (email runtime — opens people) and xv1 (media/OCR) are sibling epics feeding the same role table. GOVERNANCE: 5j8 (capture-domain portfolio decision) prunes; u3n (stall alerting) keeps deployed sources honest; the derivation catalog role table is the coverage scoreboard — a new source must name the derivation it feeds (extension rule 1).
acceptance_criteria: Exit criteria: the catalog role table has no unintentionally-zero row (Physiological and Communication filled or explicitly deferred by 5j8); every deployed source emits within its declared cadence or alerts (u3n); every new source cites its consumer derivation; no source is built on preprocessed intermediates when raw provider data exists.

Opportunistic new-source tail (not beads until wanted): music-live (Spotify API), RSS/reading queue, bank feeds (via hledger import discipline rather than a direct bank source). Ranked below the four committed new sources (github, nix-generations, browser-content, calendar) + mobile bridges.

title: Ingest beads and devloop as Sinex sources (design settled: bd keeps authority, Sinex observes)
description:
Rawlog 2026-07-03 05:29-05:34 raises three related integration questions:
1. Devloop-as-source: ingest .agent/conductor-devloop/EVENTS.jsonl + OPERATING-LOG.md as a Sinex source (StaticFileAdapter/append-stream) so loop phases/focus changes/proofs become queryable events correlated with git/terminal/browser activity. Already a backlog queue item; now includes beads.
2. Beads-as-source: ingest .beads (Dolt commits or issues.jsonl export + events.jsonl audit trail) so task lifecycle (created/claimed/blocked/closed) becomes first-class events — work-item state joins the same timeline as the work itself. bd has events-export config for exactly this shape.
3. Conceptual mapping vs Polylogue 'assertions': assertions = general typed claims over evidence with provenance; beads = a narrow, opinionated work-item domain (lifecycle+deps+ready-computation) with its own store. Working hypothesis: beads is a specialized assertion class (task-shaped claims) whose authority stays in bd; Sinex ingests it as evidence, does NOT own it; Polylogue assertions reference bead ids rather than duplicating task state. Deliverable: a short decision doc settling ownership boundaries + the two source contracts.

Refs: rawlog tail 2026-07-03.
design:
DESIGN (settled 2026-07-03) — answers the rawlog questions: devloop-in-sinex? beads<->sinex? beads vs assertions?

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARIES (the decision):
- bd keeps task AUTHORITY. Its Dolt store is the source of truth for task state; the ready/blocked/dependency computation is its value. Sinex NEVER writes task state and does not mirror beads into authoritative tables.
- Sinex ingests beads as EVIDENCE (material provenance), like any other source.
- Polylogue assertions REFERENCE bead ids (ref grammar bd:<issue-id>) instead of duplicating task state. Conceptually beads is a specialized assertion class (task-shaped claims with a lifecycle algebra); practically it must not be absorbed — no second task tracker anywhere.
- Devloops are NOT expressed/actuated in sinex. The loop's own files + beads stay authoritative; sinex observes them. (Rawlog "devloops themselves expressed in sinex" — answered: observation yes, actuation no.)

SOURCE CONTRACT 1 — project.beads:
- Enable bd events-export (.beads config events-export: true) -> append-only .beads/events.jsonl audit trail; that file is the source material (append-stream adapter, per-line anchors).
- Event types: task.created / task.claimed / task.blocked / task.closed / task.commented mapped from bd event categories; payload carries issue id, title, priority, labels, actor.
- Occurrence identity = (events.jsonl material, line byte offset); ts_orig = the bd event timestamp; ts_coided = ingestion now (correct: interpretation time).

SOURCE CONTRACT 2 — project.devloop:
- Source material: .agent/conductor-devloop/EVENTS.jsonl (already structured: phase/focus/timestamps, body_sha256, regenerated from OPERATING-LOG). StaticFileAdapter with re-scan on change; occurrence identity = (event body_sha256) via equivalence key so regeneration does not duplicate.
- Event types: devloop.phase, devloop.focus_change, devloop.checkpoint, devloop.demo.

THE PAYOFF COMPOSITE (follow-up derivation once both lanes flow): work-episode attribution joining bead claim->close intervals with git commits + terminal sessions + editor/fs activity in the same window. Beads supplies the INTENT labels the attribution problem was missing: intent (bead) x activity (terminal/git/fs) x outcome (close reason). File as a discovered-from bead when the lanes land.

DO NOT BUILD: sinex->bd writeback; bd state mirrored as sinex-authoritative tables; a polylogue task tracker; devloop actuation through sinex instructions.
acceptance_criteria: events-export enabled and .beads/events.jsonl flowing; both source contracts registered + deployed dev-locally; bd lifecycle events queryable (sinexctl query events where source = 'project.beads'); devloop phase events queryable; regenerating EVENTS.jsonl does not duplicate (equivalence-key test); a work-episode attribution bead filed as discovered-from this one when both lanes prove out. VERIFY: focused parser/adapter tests + live dev-store query.
notes:
Demo packaging (folded from the portfolio): devloop-as-source self-hosting closure — via recall ask 'what did the devloop decide about DLQ pressure on June 30 and what proof exists?' with answers cross-linked to git commit events; checkable word-for-word against the tracked files; falsifier = wrong or unresolvable citations.

Go-forward devloop telemetry comes from beads state (.beads/issues.jsonl in git) + polylogue sessions — no separate devloop event stream exists anymore.

title: External legibility artifacts: concepts page, positioning, comparables
description: Make the project concept transmit. Diagnosis (settled, fables-sinex.md ~1147+): four failure modes — (a) category capture by wrong neighbors (elevator line pattern-matches to Rewind/MS-Recall and the listener stops updating; the real category 'personal data infrastructure where interpretations are versioned computations' has no name yet, so frame deliberately or lose by default); (b) the novelty is architectural and architecture doesn't screenshot — it only shows in temporal demonstration (fix a parser, watch months re-understand themselves), so static description structurally undersells; (c) private vocabulary with public equivalents nobody is handed (ts_coided, anchor_byte, automata... each maps to established theory — the translation table IS most of the fix); (d) claims outrun public evidence — legibility and the construct-validity demo arc are the same project. Deliverables and placement are fixed in the design field; content sources: fables-sinex.md lines ~1147-1470 (ladder, table, comparables, claims, credibility map) and ~1900-1990 (ecosystem analysis). Do the concepts page + positioning now that recall-v2 exists to point at; evidence-gallery publication stays gated on scrubbing (sinex-83g).
design: WHAT IS SAID WHERE (settled): (1) CONCEPTS PAGE fronting the README — the distillation ladder verbatim from the source: L0 hook ('AI models get smarter every quarter, but your data only ever gets interpreted once — Sinex makes every interpretation a rebuildable artifact, so each better model retroactively re-understands your history'); L1 mechanism paragraph (capture->anchored events->derived with lineage->replay->adjudication->agent as primary consumer); L2 the Nix frame ('Nix for personal data': captures=sources, versioned interpreters=builders, derived events=store paths, replay=rebuild, effect ledger=binary cache — plus what build systems lack: history of understanding + human gate) — structurally exact, native to the audiences most likely to care; L3 theory ('event sourcing plus four additions': material anchoring, bitemporal interpretation identity, non-idempotent replay as product, typed adjudication gate). Plus the 10-row vocabulary translation table (material/derived->W3C PROV+Datalog base-vs-derived; ts_orig/ts_coided->bitemporal valid-vs-transaction time; replay->rebuild-after-compiler-upgrade; archive cascade->downstream invalidation; automata->dataflow operators; equivalence key->occurrence-level idempotency key; effect ledger->memoization/binary cache; shadow lanes->blue-green for interpreters; Proposal/Judgment->HITL promotion gate; anchor_byte->content-addressed evidence w/ offsets). Rule: keep internal vocabulary, pair translation on first use; doc-alias ts_coided as 'interpretation time (transaction time)'. (2) docs/positioning.md — honest comparables by neighborhood: capture layer (Rewind/Recall/screenpipe/AW/timelinize/Dogsheep = ingestible sources, capture is being commoditized at OS level and that LOWERS Sinex's cost of breadth); personal-data infra (HPI = closest philosophical relative minus the persistence/provenance spine; Perkeep = L0-shaped, died on the consumption gap — cite AND heed); agent memory (Letta/mem0/LangMem = assertions without ground truth; Zep's Graphiti = independent convergence on the two-clock design — validates L3/L4, study before building the entity lane); pattern donors (Datomic/XTDB as-of, Materialize IVM deliberately rejected for auditable coarse recomputation, Salsa/BSàC replay economics, OTel semantic conventions + the 'personal observability — OTel for a human life' one-liner). Positioning sentence: the field has a capture layer and an agent-memory layer and nothing trustworthy between them; Sinex is the missing middle — ingest the capture ecosystem, serve the agent ecosystem via MCP, compete with neither. Their memories are assertions; ours are conclusions with lineage to bytes. (3) FIVE FALSIFIABLE CLAIMS in positioning.md, each with its check command/demo: XOR provenance enforced 3x (try to violate); replay non-idempotent w/ archive (cem.3); no silent truth (authority types); LLM-as-build-step (cem.4 — state honestly 'contract shipped, client pending' — the built-vs-intended distinction is itself credibility); failures render as gaps (cem.2). (4) CREDIBILITY MAP: pitch-line -> evidence-artifact -> status table maintained alongside the demo portfolio. (5) Cheapest external move: publish concepts page + positioning + 3 scrubbed shelf entries (cem.1, cem.2, one recall-v2) before any new feature. TRANSMISSION TEST = acceptance: an outsider who read only the concepts page correctly predicts behavior on three probes (re-import same file? parser fixed — old conclusions? can LLM write truth?).
acceptance_criteria: A stranger given only the concepts page can state what the system is and what makes it different; positioning claims are each falsifiable; no personal capture data reaches the public surface.
notes: Also fold in: the central-bet risk register (handoff U11) into .github/target-vision-claim-ledger.md as part of this pass. Agent-orientation content (sinex-7z0.3) is GENERATED from the same ladder source — internal and external explanations must not fork. Graphiti study-before-entity-lane pointer also recorded on sinex-2nd.

title: Semantic lane promote: close the shadow -> curation -> canonical loop
description:
The authority type system (Proposal/Judgment) is wired for exactly one kind (curation duplicates) and no lane->canonical promotion path exists; curation finalize currently finalizes nothing (emits an event no one consumes, curation.rs:391-470). Implement `semantic lane promote`: walk an approved lane diff into PkmService::create_entities/link_entities. This closes the loop the whole L4 adjudication design was built for.

Refs: handoff P10; audit 015 §B8.
design: DECISION: sinexctl semantic lane promote <lane> [--diff <id>] walks an APPROVED diff into PkmService::create_entities/link_entities, recording a curation.finalized-style derived event with proposal+judgment parents as provenance. Promotion REQUIRES judgment (authority gate) — never auto-promote. TARGETS: sinex-db/src/repositories/semantic.rs:467-573 (lane seeding), sinex-primitives/src/semantic.rs:242 (diff_entity_relation_lanes), api/handlers/curation.rs:391-470 (finalize that finalizes nothing), api/handlers/pkm.rs:34-88 (the only canonical writer today). CAUTION: this is the FIRST canonical-truth writer beyond manual PKM — the adjudication doctrine (Proposal/Judgment is the only path to truth) is settled; implement inside it.
acceptance_criteria: Promoted entities/relations appear in core.entities/entity_relations with provenance to proposal+judgment; re-promoting is idempotent at the occurrence level; unjudged diffs refuse with a clear error.
notes:
2026-07-03 ecosystem pointer (from the external-landscape analysis): study Zep's Graphiti before building/promoting the entity lane — it independently converged on the two-clock design (event time vs ingestion time) and incremental entity resolution; validates the L3/L4 architecture and is the closest prior art for promotion mechanics. Differentiator to preserve: their memories are assertions; Sinex conclusions carry lineage to bytes.
2026-07-06 symbol map (verified, zero-discovery start): the promotion path does NOT exist anywhere (rg promote over semantic repo + api handlers = 0). Building blocks all present: SemanticLaneStatus lifecycle + set_lane_status (sinex-db/repositories/semantic.rs:252); lane outputs + diff already recorded (write_entity_relation_outputs :351, record_entity_relation_diff :575, diff types in primitives/semantic.rs:155-241); canonical writers = PkmService::create_entities_from_source_material (pkm.rs:216) + link_entities (:296) — NB their current signatures are material-oriented; promotion writes need judgment-parent provenance instead, so expect to add a knowledge-graph write path that takes proposal+judgment event ids as Derived parents rather than reusing the material-shaped methods verbatim. Authority gate: Proposal<T>::apply(judgment) (authority.rs:158) enforces proposal-judgment binding; FinalizerRegistration::human_required exists (:241). Judgment RPC handlers already live (api/handlers/curation.rs:30,:48 — shared with 7z0.4). Shape: sinexctl semantic lane promote <lane> = read approved diff -> per-item Proposal/Judgment records (or one batch judgment, NonEmptyVec parents) -> canonical graph writes -> lane status Promoted (set_lane_status).

title: Dev postgres port 5432 collision: socket-only, fail-fast, stale pidfile cleanup
description:
Every checkout's dev postgres binds TCP 5432; a second checkout's postgres can never start and xtask's SQLx schema-apply bootstrap hangs forever ("Applying checkout-local schema..." with no cargo spawn). Connections already use the per-checkout unix socket, so TCP is unnecessary.

Fix: listen_addresses='' (socket-only, cleanest) or per-checkout derived port; bootstrap should fail fast with a clear port-conflict error instead of hanging; clean stale postmaster.pid from killed postmasters. Blocks concurrent agent/worktree lanes.
design: DECISION: socket-only (listen_addresses='') — connections already use the per-checkout unix socket, TCP serves nothing; per-checkout derived ports rejected (still a shared namespace, still collides eventually). Three changes in the xtask infra postgres lifecycle: (1) render listen_addresses='' into the generated postgresql.conf; (2) bootstrap preflight: if pg_ctl start fails, surface the actual postmaster log tail and exit nonzero — never hang on 'Applying checkout-local schema...' (the hang is the bug as much as the collision); (3) stale postmaster.pid: on start, if the pidfile's pid is dead or owns a different data-dir (proc cmdline check, same ownership-proof pattern as infra stop --all-checkouts), remove it and proceed. PITFALL: anything that reads DATABASE_URL with host=TCP assumptions (none known — verify with rg 'localhost:5432|127.0.0.1:5432' across xtask + devshell hooks) must be clean before removing TCP.
acceptance_criteria: Two checkouts run xtask infra start concurrently and both come up (the original repro); netstat shows no 5432 listener from dev postgres; a killed postmaster leaves a pidfile that the next start cleans automatically; a genuinely-failing start exits fast with the postgres log tail in the error. VERIFY: xtask test -p xtask -E 'test(infra)' + the two-checkout manual proof recorded.
notes: 2026-07-05: PR #2375 opened from feature/xtask/postgres-bootstrap-robustness. Implemented devshell cargo+xtask wrapper stale postmaster.pid cleanup and fail-fast pg_ctl startup log tails in flake.nix. Verification: nix eval .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default.drvPath --raw; nix develop --command bash -lc 'printf PGHOST/PGPORT/DATABASE_URL; xtask infra status --json'; xtask test -p xtask --lib -E "test(postmaster_pid_state) | test(force_cleanup) | test(ensure_runtime_config) | test(pg_ctl_start_command)" invocation 2005745 passed 5/5; xtask check --changed-strict origin/master passed/no Rust packages affected; sudo ss showed checkout Postgres pid 76165 owns only /var/cache/sinex/sinity/566e9bf8d5e8/dev-state/run/.s.PGSQL.5432 while TCP 5432 belongs to system Postgres pid 440105. Remaining before close: rerun two-checkout concurrent infra-start proof when host memory PSI is sane.
close_reason: Completed: PR #2375 landed socket-only dev Postgres and robust bootstrap cleanup. Two-checkout proof on 2026-07-05 used main checkout /realm/project/sinex (dev-state 566e9bf8d5e8) and detached proof worktree /realm/tmp/worktrees/sinex-2206-proof (dev-state a853b8a0179a). Both xtask infra status commands succeeded; proof worktree xtask infra start completed with Postgres running and NATS on port 4290 while main Postgres remained running. sudo ss showed TCP 5432 owned only by system Postgres pid 440105, with Sinex checkouts listening only on Unix sockets /var/cache/sinex/sinity/566e9bf8d5e8/dev-state/run/.s.PGSQL.5432 and /var/cache/sinex/sinity/a853b8a0179a/dev-state/run/.s.PGSQL.5432. Proof worktree infra was stopped after capture.

title: Schema-apply convergence gaps: dup CHECKs, required-index set, CAGG constant, COPY boot verify
description:
Five silent convergence gaps in sinex-schema apply.rs that neither diff nor strict_diff detects:
1. Duplicate CHECK constraints accumulate (named NOT VALID added, auto-named inline twins never dropped; prod had ~46 vs ~24 needed — every INSERT evaluates all).
2. ix_events_equivalence_key (load-bearing for admission dedup) + ix_events_sinex_telemetry not in EVENTS_REQUIRED_INDEXES — manual drop is invisible and dedup falls to seq-scan on the hypertable (real perf cliff).
3. current_system_state CAGG missing from TELEMETRY_CONTINUOUS_AGGREGATES existence check.
4. events_check7 (ts_orig future-skew) absent from DECLARED_INLINE_CHECKS.
5. verify_event_copy_contract() is lazy (first >=50 COPY batch panic) — verify at startup alongside schema apply instead.

Full findings: .agent/scratch/research-audit-db-schema.md.


## Steps to Reproduce
Apply schema twice against a DB carrying legacy inline CHECKs -> count pg_constraint rows on core.events grows/stays duplicated (prod had ~46 vs ~24 needed); drop ix_events_equivalence_key manually -> xtask schema strict-diff reports clean (gap 2).
acceptance_criteria: Event-engine startup or DB preflight calls verify_event_copy_contract() before event sources/consumers can start; the lazy OnceLock verifier remains in copy_columns() as defense-in-depth; a regression test proves startup/preflight fails before the first COPY batch when EVENT_COPY_COLUMNS drifts from Events::create_table_statement(). Existing landed regressions stay pinned: duplicate CHECK cleanup, required-index diff coverage, current_system_state CAGG coverage, ts_orig_not_after_ts_coided strict coverage.
notes:
2026-07-07 audit integration: COPY-contract verifier confirmed lazy-only on master — sole caller is copy_columns() get_or_init (postgres_copy.rs:218); no startup/preflight caller (rg). AC addition: call verify_event_copy_contract() from event-engine startup/DB preflight before sources start, and expose via sinexctl/xtask preflight; keep lazy check as defense-in-depth.
2026-07-07 audit (new-gpt-pro 08) verified 4 of 5 originally-described gaps are ALREADY LANDED on master: duplicate CHECK cleanup (converge.rs:566-656), ix_events_equivalence_key + ix_events_sinex_telemetry in EVENTS_REQUIRED_INDEXES (apply.rs:38-67), current_system_state in TELEMETRY_CONTINUOUS_AGGREGATES (apply.rs:91-104), ts_orig_not_after_ts_coided in strict inline checks (strict_diff.rs:603-614). Remaining scope = COPY boot/preflight wiring only. Broader silent-drift work moved to the new strict-comparator beads. Also: audit recommends NOT generalizing the COPY contract into a schema-drift detector — it is a serializer contract vs the Rust authority, not vs the live DB.

title: CAS digest charset validation: path traversal + unbounded read from ReadOnly token
description:
ContentKey::validate (sinex-primitives/src/domain.rs:1998) only checks the '--' separator; digest flows into Path::join (content_store/mod.rs:582) so '..' or leading '/' escapes the CAS root; read at manager.rs:438 has no size cap. Reachable from content.retrieve_blob at ReadOnly role: arbitrary-file read into daemon memory (OOM vector) + fs-existence oracle. Mitigated by single-user/loopback/mTLS but a real sandbox escape; fix is cheap.

Fix: constrain digest to BLAKE3 hex fixed length in validate(); canonicalize resolved path and assert within CAS root; size-cap the read. Notes+repro: .agent/scratch/research-audit-api-security.md.
acceptance_criteria: ContentKey::validate rejects any digest that is not exact-length lowercase BLAKE3 hex (unit tests: traversal payloads ../, leading /, overlong, uppercase, empty); resolved blob path canonicalized and asserted within the CAS root with a test proving escape attempts error; blob read size-capped (cap from config, default sane) with an over-cap test; content.retrieve_blob at ReadOnly exercises all three in an integration test. VERIFY: xtask test -p sinex-primitives -E 'test(content_key)'; xtask test -p sinex-db -E 'test(content_store)'; repro from .agent/scratch/research-audit-api-security.md no longer reproduces.

title: Historical-import pacing: operator-configurable rate + progress visibility
description:
The prod flap was triggered by an unthrottled 14-month journald import (1.24M RAW backlog). No operator control over backfill pace, no progress visibility.

Scope: (1) configurable rate/throttle for historical backfills so imports don't saturate pipeline/NATS/creation-time chunks; (2) surface import rate, position, ETA, backlog depth via sinexctl + telemetry. Overlaps gh#2182 remaining item 2 — implement as one pacing mechanism.
design: DECISION: pacing lives at the SOURCE SCAN LOOP (scan_historical), not the event engine — throttling the consumer just moves the backlog into NATS (the incident shape). Mechanism: a rate budget in ScanArgs/RuntimeConfig (events/sec and bytes/sec, operator-set via binding config + overridable per replay/import operation), enforced by the scan loop between batches; progress = the source's checkpoint position vs the known horizon, emitted as reflexive progress events + exposed via sinexctl ops (import list showing rate/position/ETA/backlog depth). Backpressure coupling: pause when raw-stream depth exceeds a threshold from the n23.3 capacity table (pull the threshold from config now, formalize when n23.3 lands). One mechanism for all three entry points: historical scans, replay re-ingest, staged imports. PITFall: do not gate realtime/continuous capture behind the same budget — pacing applies to catch-up work only.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately large historical import (fixture or journald window) run at a configured rate holds raw pending below the threshold for the whole drain; sinexctl shows live rate/position/ETA; unpaced behavior is impossible without an explicit --unlimited override; continuous capture latency unaffected during a paced import (measured). VERIFY: e2e paced-import test + live dev-store run with xtask analytics store snapshots.
notes: 2026-07-04 storage-growth citation: use xtask analytics storage-growth --projection-days 365 --limit 20 --json from sinex-n23.2 for pacing parameters. Live dev-store artifact: .agent/demos/sinex/storage-growth-live-20260704T0254Z/summary.json. Key numbers: 6,313 materials; 27,985,746,914 material bytes; 60,416,482 parsed events; browser.history = 94.1% of material bytes; projected 365d material growth about 4.12 TB under the current short-window catch-up rate; core.events = 2 chunks / 66,914,197,504 bytes; Timescale compression configured but 0 compressed chunks. Pacing decisions should use this command as the pre-run baseline and re-run it after large imports; do not tune from incident anecdotes alone.
close_reason:

title: Reflection 1-byte materials: remove prime(), defrag capability, granularity config, rename
description:
75% of registry materials (25,667/34,225) are exactly 1 byte, minted by self-observation.* automata. ROOT CAUSE NAILED: AutomatonRuntime::initialize (adapter/mod.rs:381-404) builds a fresh SelfObserver and prime() appends vec![b'\n']; on drop the buffered writer finalizes the 1-byte material. Every automaton restart mints one (~2,800/day during the ack_pending crisis).

Scope:
- E (first, ~1 line): remove observer.prime() at adapter/mod.rs:404 — the 5s FK-race retry from #1243 already covers what prime() guarded. Stops all future creation.
- A: general source-material defragmentation capability (coalesce rewrite respecting occurrence identity = (source_material_id, anchor_byte) columns; new interpretation ids; archive cascade). Existing 25,667 are dormant (~25KB) — no urgency.
- B: per-source granularity config + UX (sinexctl sources).
- D: rename self-observation -> reflection (changes source_identifier strings in prod data — decide migrate vs leave-old-prefix).

Refs: gh#2184 comments, .agent/scratch/research-2184-fragmentation.md.
design: SEQUENCING (E is committed-or-trivial, the rest is deliberate): E — remove observer.prime() (adapter/mod.rs:404); the #1243 5s FK-race retry covers what prime() guarded; verify no automaton-restart mints a material afterward. THEN the general capability in value order: A — defragmentation as an OPERATOR-VISIBLE operation built on existing machinery (coalesce = write merged material, re-anchor via replay semantics: occurrence identity is the (source_material_id, anchor_byte) COLUMNS so coalescing mints new interpretations + archive cascade — never mutate rows in place; this is a special case of replay, implement it through the replay/ops plane, not a new subsystem); B — per-source granularity config surfaced in sinexctl sources (the knob n23.2's growth model will want); D — the rename decision: self-observation -> reflection changes source_identifier strings in prod data; DECIDE explicitly: rename-with-migration (replay-friendly: new events under new id, old stay archived) vs leave-old-prefix-document-alias — default to alias-only unless the telemetry-lane split (x9i) forces a hard cut, in which case fold D into x9i. PITFALL: the 25,667 existing 1-byte materials are ~25KB dormant — do NOT run defrag against prod just to tidy; defrag lands as capability + test, actual prod compaction waits for a reason.
acceptance_criteria: E: zero new 1-byte materials across a week of automaton restarts (registry query by size+created-after). A: defrag operation demonstrated on a fixture store — N fragment materials coalesce, events re-anchor with preserved occurrence identity, old interpretations archived, lineage intact. comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Prong 3 (DLQ triage) — investigation complete, disposition = decided-zero.

## Headline finding

The literal ~29.6K/2GiB incident-era DLQ (gh#2182, captured 2026-06-27 as
`PROD_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_DLQ`) no longer exists anywhere on this system — it was
destroyed by the operator-approved 2026-07-11 fresh-rebuild wipe
(`DROP DATABASE sinex_prod` + clean re-import), which explicitly chose
fix-forward-via-reimport over fix-forward-via-replay for this exact polluted
incident-era backlog. Live-data triage by failure class/count is therefore not
possible; this triage instead (a) confirms the destruction with direct evidence,
(b) reconstructs the backlog's known trajectory and the discrete failure
classes that WERE identified from it via the forensic trail, with real
dispositions per class, and (c) confirms today's live DLQ state is at zero.

## Evidence the data is gone (checked 2026-08-10, read-only)

- `sinex_schemas.dlq_events` (DB-side per-automaton DLQ table): started
  `postgresql.service` (was inactive; stopped again after, matching its normal
  idle state), queried `sinex_prod`: `SELECT count(*) FROM sinex_schemas.dlq_events`
  = 0 rows, `pg_total_relation_size` = 40 kB (bare table/index overhead only).
- NATS JetStream persistent store (`/var/lib/nats/jetstream`, per
  `nixos/modules/nats.nix` storeDir config): `sudo find /var/lib/nats/jetstream`
  returns only the empty root directory — zero stream subdirectories, i.e. no
  `PROD_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_DLQ` (or any other stream) data survives on disk.
  `nats.service` itself is currently inactive (normal idle state, not started
  for this investigation to avoid overlapping with prong-2/restart-drain
  scope).
- The pre-wipe safety snapshot cited in gh#2182 itself
  (`/var/lib/sinex/.prewipe-snapshot-20260627`, "full @sinex: postgres + NATS +
  CAS") no longer exists: not present under `/var/lib/sinex/`, and
  `sudo btrfs subvolume list /` shows no subvolume of that name (only the live
  `@sinex` top-level subvol and unrelated `@persist`/`.snapshots` entries).
  `/realm/inbox/sinex-snapshots/` (the location named in the later
  fresh-rebuild plan for its own snapshot) does not exist either.
- `sinex_prod` current size: 99 GB, `raw.source_material_registry` = 35,588
  rows — consistent with the 2026-07-11 clean re-import having actually run
  (this is real, current, post-wipe data, not incident-era residue).

No per-message `failure_reason`/`error_category` breakdown of the original
29.6K was ever recorded anywhere in the evidence trail (gh#2182 body/comments
only ever cite the aggregate JetStream stream stats: message count + stream
byte size). Fabricating a per-class count split now, with the underlying
messages gone, would not be honest — so none is reported below. What follows
instead is the real, bead-tracked failure MECHANISMS the incident's aftermath
forensics actually identified, each with a real disposition and citation.

## Known trajectory before destruction (from gh#2182 + later bead evidence)

- 2026-06-27 (incident): 29.6K msgs / ~2 GiB in the raw-events DLQ stream.
- By the time `xtask analytics store` grew DLQ visibility (sinex-8zy, closed;
  its description cites "gh#2204 evidence" as the source measurement): DLQ had
  already fallen to 4,381 messages / ~413 MB — roughly 85% of the incident
  volume was already drained (via normal automaton retry/requeue and/or
  operator action) well before the 2026-07-11 wipe. No exact immediately-
  pre-wipe count exists in the evidence trail.
- 2026-07-11: whatever remained was destroyed with the rest of `sinex_prod`
  (DROP DATABASE) and, per the current empty JetStream store, the NATS-side
  stream data is gone too (whether that happened at the same time or in a
  later NATS state reset done after that date, the current disk state is
  conclusively empty either way).

## Discrete failure classes identified from the incident-era DLQ, with disposition

1. **Zero-event orphaned sensing materials misrouted into raw-DLQ pressure**
   on restart/orphan reconciliation (e.g. `desktop.window-manager` and similar
   materials with `parsed_event_count=0`, `total_bytes=NULL` — no real event
   to retry).
   **Disposition: FIXED AT CAUSE.** `sinex-dqx` (closed) — these now route to
   `recovered_partial` with `recovery_reason=orphaned_zero_event_source_material_recovered_partial`
   / `dlq_policy=suppressed_zero_event_source_material_restart_orphan` instead
   of generating raw DLQ pressure. Verified in its closure evidence: targeted
   sinexd tests (incl.
   `orphan_reconcile_recovers_globally_stale_zero_event_source_material_without_dlq`,
   job 2001365) + `xtask check -p sinexd` (job 2001366).

2. **Material-assembler DLQ-publish failures silently swallowed** — when the
   assembler's own attempt to write a DLQ record failed (serialization,
   oversized-payload, NATS-publish error), it ACKed the frame anyway instead
   of NAKing/leaving it for redelivery, so genuinely-failed material events
   could vanish without ever landing in DLQ *or* being retried.
   **Disposition: FIXED AT CAUSE.** `sinex-wb1` (closed, PR #2537) —
   `route_material_error` now returns `EventEngineResult<()>` and every call
   site handles it correctly (hot-path NAKs instead of ACKing on DLQ-publish
   failure). Verified with a real, non-mocked failure trigger
   (`route_material_error_propagates_oversized_dlq_payload_failure`, forced via
   `ensure_nats_payload_fits` rejection) + 197/197 material-package tests +
   clean `xtask check`.

3. **Whole-file-as-one-record sources with zero DLQ visibility on partial
   failure** — a `StaticFileAdapter`-backed source where a single malformed
   member event among many never unlocks progress causes the ENTIRE file to
   be silently re-scanned from scratch forever, with no DLQ entry, no
   quarantine, and no operator-visible signal beyond a repeating WARN log
   line.
   **Disposition: STILL OPEN, not fixed.** `sinex-6vhq` (open, filed
   2026-08-01). Flagging explicitly: this means the true incident-era failure
   population for any source of this shape could be LARGER than what the
   29.6K DLQ count ever captured (silent infinite-retry never generates a DLQ
   entry at all). This is real, non-trivial design work (partial-progress /
   quarantine mechanism) — out of scope to fix inside this triage pass; left
   as the already-filed, correctly-scoped bead.

4. **DLQ retry/requeue republishes redacted/stubbed payload as if original**
   — `dlq_retry` serializes whatever is in `original_event_payload` (which for
   parse failures is redaction-suppressed, and for oversized entries is a
   metadata stub only) and republishes it to the raw subject unless a
   `_raw_bytes_base64` side-channel field exists, then deletes the DLQ
   message — so a real bulk-replay could inject mutated/stub events that never
   existed on the raw stream.
   **Disposition: STILL OPEN, not fixed.** `sinex-6gx` (open). Directly
   relevant to this mission's own instruction to sample-replay before bulk
   action: even if the 29.6K backlog had still existed, a blind
   `sinexctl ops dlq requeue --all` would have been unsafe for any
   redaction-affected or oversized entries per this exact bug. No live data
   existed to actually attempt a sample replay against in this session (see
   headline finding), so this class was validated by code inspection only,
   not by a live replay attempt.

## Disposition for the remaining/dominant bulk of the 29.6K

The four classes above are the ones with independent forensic/bead evidence;
they do not claim to exhaust 29.6K in named-class counts (no per-message
breakdown survives to attribute the remainder to specific categories — see
headline finding). For the numerically-dominant remainder:
**Disposition: EXPLICITLY DISCARDED.** Rationale — the operator's own
2026-07-11 fresh-rebuild decision already IS the disposition for this bulk: it
explicitly chose full `DROP DATABASE` + clean re-import over fix-forward-via-
replay for this specific polluted incident-era dataset ("wipe prod... rather
than fix-forward-via-replay... Motivated by a polluted dataset... not worth
replaying" — session_2026_07_11_fresh_rebuild_campaign). Re-import through the
CURRENT pipeline (post-#2182 fixes, post-dqx, post-wb1) is a strictly better
recovery than replaying stale pre-fix DLQ message envelopes would have been.
The one deliberately-accepted loss: continuous/ephemeral non-reimportable
sources (clipboard, notifications, dbus, systemd, window-manager, kitty,
udev) had their incident-window history shed by the wipe — an intended,
already-recorded tradeoff in that same decision record, not a new loss
surfaced by this triage.

## Current live DLQ state (checked 2026-08-10)

Decided-zero, confirmed directly: `sinex_schemas.dlq_events` = 0 rows;
`/var/lib/nats/jetstream` has zero stream directories. Nothing to
replay/purge right now. `sinexctl ops dlq list/triage/cleanup-plan` were not
run against a live gateway because `sinexd`/`nats.service` are both
intentionally left stopped (their normal idle state outside active work,
confirmed against `postgresql.service`'s own start/stop history) — starting
them to actively drain/rebuild the backlog is prong-2 scope (paced restart
drain, depends on the sibling `sinex-2n9` pacing lane) and explicitly out of
scope for this mission.

## Scope status

Prong 1 (schema-apply boot-race): closed via sinex-yss (prior session).
Prong 2 (paced restart drain): still open, depends on sinex-2n9's pacing
mechanism landing — not attempted this session per explicit mission scope.
Prong 3 (DLQ triage): done as of this comment — decided-zero state confirmed,
4 discrete failure classes accounted for (2 fixed-at-cause, 2 already
correctly bead-tracked as open design work), remainder dispositioned
discarded with rationale. sinex-ddy stays OPEN (prong 2 remains).

title: Surface JetStream raw/DLQ/material stream state in xtask analytics store
description:
The SQL DLQ table showed zero rows while the live JetStream DLQ held 4,381 messages / ~413MB — xtask analytics store is blind to the actual live failure mode. Promote JetStream stream/consumer metadata (raw pending, DLQ depth/bytes, material/assembler stream state) into `xtask analytics store` so catch-up and jam triage don't require hand nats calls.

Refs: OPERATING-LOG.md 2026-07-03T05:22 next-decision; gh#2204 evidence section.
design: DECISION: extend xtask analytics store (the existing triage surface) with a JetStream section — do not create a parallel command. Source of data: NATS management API via the existing infra client (same URL resolution as xtask infra status): per-stream messages/bytes/first-last seq for the raw, DLQ, confirmed, and material/assembler streams; per-consumer pending/ack_pending/redelivered for the event-engine + automaton consumers. title: media.rs's recording_observed and screenshot_observed occurrence keys silently drop declared fields (capture_session_id, display_id, observed_at) and substitute undeclared ones (duration_ms, width_px, height_px)
description:
Two media.rs event builders silently drop declared occurrence-identity fields and substitute undeclared ones, unlike their sibling builders in the same file which match their contracts exactly.

recording_observed: declared crate/sinex-primitives/src/event_contracts/media.rs:79-82 -> (raw_material_id, capture_session_id, observed_at). Actual key at crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/media.rs:1309-1320 uses (material_id, duration_ms) -- capture_session_id and observed_at (both present in the payload two lines above) are silently dropped; an undeclared duration_ms is substituted.

screenshot_observed: declared media.rs:86-91 -> (raw_material_id, capture_session_id, display_id, region). Actual key at media.rs:1432-1440 uses (material_id, region, width_px, height_px) -- capture_session_id and display_id (both present on the same function's screenshot struct) are omitted; width_px/height_px substituted.

By contrast the sibling capture_session_started/ended, video_segment_observed, transcription_run_observed, and ocr_run_observed builders in the same file match their declared field lists exactly or as a safe superset -- so this is contained to these two functions, not a whole-file pattern.

In practice material_id uniqueness likely masks real-world collapse risk (each record already keys distinctly per material), but the declared contract is not honored, and a future consumer relying on the DECLARED fields (not the actual implementation) for cross-session/cross-display dedup reasoning would draw wrong conclusions.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) systematically cross-checking occurrence-identity declarations against implementations (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Compare the declared EventContract field lists for recording_observed (media.rs event_contracts:79-82) and screenshot_observed (:86-91) against the actual OccurrenceKey construction in source_contracts/media.rs:1309-1320 and :1432-1440.

title: docs-library-index's declared content_hash change-detection is fiction -- DirectoryWalkAdapter hardcodes content_hash: None unconditionally, so re-imported files with changed content are indistinguishable from unchanged ones
description:

Declaration: crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/library.rs:201 -- occurrence_identity = OccurrenceIdentity::Uuid5From("(source, path, content_hash)"), sole adapter DirectoryWalkAdapter.

The payload doc comment (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/payloads/library.rs:20-22) explicitly claims "the same file re-imported... produces the same hash and can be deduplicated on (path, content_hash)" and "content_hash... provides stable identity" -- none of that is true in the live pipeline.

Currently benign (path alone is already unique per file, so no cross-file collapse), but the declared content-CHANGE detection mechanism is fiction: a file whose content silently changes at the same path produces an occurrence key indistinguishable from before, purely by coincidence of path staying constant, not because content_hash verified anything.

title: GatewayConfig.rpc_rate_limit_requests_per_sec is wired through NixOS deployment and documented as the master token-bucket refill rate, but neither rate limiter ever reads it -- only per-role RPS knobs actually take effect
description:
GatewayConfig.rpc_rate_limit_requests_per_sec (crate/sinexd/src/api/config.rs:227-233) is a fully-wired operator-facing knob -- reaches all the way through NixOS deployment (nixos/modules/sources.nix:647 sets SINEX_API_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SEC=${toString coreCfg.api.limits.rateLimit.requestsPerSec}) and is documented in crate/sinexd/docs/api/environment.md:78,128 as "In-memory token bucket refill rate" -- but is never actually read by either rate limiter.

Neither RateLimitConfig::from_gateway_config (crate/sinexd/src/api/rate_limit.rs:49-58) nor DistributedRateLimitConfig::from_gateway_config (crate/sinexd/src/api/distributed_rate_limit.rs:56-73) calls rate_limit_requests_per_second() (the field's own accessor, config.rs:599-602) -- both only read the per-role fields (readonly/write/admin RPS + burst). Confirmed via workspace-wide grep: zero call sites for rate_limit_requests_per_second() outside its own definition and default-value plumbing.

Operator expectation vs reality: an operator sets coreCfg.api.limits.rateLimit.requestsPerSec (or SINEX_API_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SEC directly) expecting to change the master token-bucket refill rate per the doc comment's phrasing -- in reality only the three per-role RPS overrides affect live rate limiting; this field's value is computed and stored but never crosses into either limiter's construction path.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for declared-but-unwired config knobs across the workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set SINEX_API_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SEC to a distinctive value (or the NixOS coreCfg.api.limits.rateLimit.requestsPerSec option).
2. Confirm via grep that neither RateLimitConfig::from_gateway_config nor DistributedRateLimitConfig::from_gateway_config calls rate_limit_requests_per_second() -- only rate_limit_readonly_rps/write_rps/admin_rps/burst are consumed.
3. Observe changing this value has no effect on live rate limiting.
acceptance_criteria: Either wire rate_limit_requests_per_second() into an actual limiter construction path (as a global default the per-role knobs override, matching the doc's implied semantics), or remove the field/env-var/NixOS-option/doc-entry if the per-role model has fully superseded it -- whichever the intended design is.

title: Hyprland workspace-switch instruction/attempt event pair is non-transactional -- a failed attempt-event insert after real actuation leaves no outcome record and defeats the duplicate-dispatch guard
description:
handle_hyprland_workspace_switch's instruction event and persist_attempt's outcome event are two separate, non-transactional inserts, with real-world Hyprland actuation potentially happening between them.

crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/instructions.rs:60-235:
- Line 80: pool.events().insert(instruction_event) -- the instruction record.
- Between this and persist_attempt, the code can perform the actual real-world Hyprland dispatch via dispatch_hyprland_workspace_command (line 151).
- Line 218 (inside persist_attempt): pool.events().insert(attempt_event) -- a SEPARATE insert, no transaction spanning it and the instruction insert.

If the attempt-event insert fails after the instruction event was already persisted (and possibly after the real desktop actuation already ran), the system is left with an instruction record and no matching outcome record. This is not just a DB-consistency gap: active_hyprland_workspace_instruction (instructions.rs:266+) -- the duplicate-dispatch guard -- requires an EXISTS match against a persisted actuation.attempted event with status='attempted' to recognize an instruction as already-handled. Without the paired attempt event, a retry would not be recognized as a duplicate and could re-dispatch the same workspace switch.

Low real-world harm (a repeat workspace-switch is largely idempotent), but a genuine loss of the operation's audit/outcome trail for something that may have physically executed.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for non-atomic multi-step DB writes across the workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger handle_hyprland_workspace_switch, inject a failure into persist_attempt's event insert (instructions.rs:218) after the instruction event (line 80) already committed and dispatch already ran.
2. Observe no actuation.attempted event exists for that instruction.
3. Retry the same instruction -- observe active_hyprland_workspace_instruction's EXISTS check doesn't find a matching attempt, so the duplicate-dispatch guard doesn't fire and the workspace switch re-dispatches.
acceptance_criteria: Either both inserts happen atomically, or the retry path can detect 'actuation may have already run, attempt record missing' and avoid blind re-dispatch.

title: 5 more unguarded UTF-8 byte-slicing panic sites across xtask tooling and one source_contracts parser (views.rs SQL echo, bench/environment.rs process scan, reset.rs stale-process scan, vm-suite test report, git.rs log-record error path)
description:
Four more unguarded UTF-8 byte-slicing panic sites across xtask/tooling, same class as the already-confirmed analytics.rs/jobs.rs/diagnostics_command.rs/motd.rs instances:

1. xtask/src/history/db/views.rs:316 -- `&sql[..sql.len().min(40)]` on raw user-typed SQL from `xtask history db query <sql>`. Fires on the exact "user made a syntax mistake, wants a clear error" case, turning a helpful error message into a panic.

2. xtask/src/bench/environment.rs:282,312 (truncate_process_line, max=180) -- scans EVERY process on the host during `xtask bench`'s heavy-process report. Fully environment-controlled: any unrelated process (browser, IDE, anything with a unicode path/arg in its cmdline) with a multi-byte char straddling byte 180 panics `xtask bench`.

3. xtask/src/commands/reset.rs:1092-1097 (truncate_command_for_reset, max=160) -- same pattern as #2, applied to stale-build-process and stale-test-Postgres command strings sourced from process listings during `xtask reset`.

4. tests/vm-suite/src/categories/concurrency.rs:488-494 (truncate_for_report, MAX_LEN=240) -- test-only, lower priority, but ironic: truncates combined stdout+stderr specifically to build a FAILURE REPORT message; a byte-boundary panic here masks the real VM test failure it's trying to report.

Also: git.rs:266 (`&chunk[..chunk.len().min(120)]`) is a fifth instance, in the malformed-git-log-record error path -- reachable in any repo with non-ASCII author names/commit subjects.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for UTF-8 byte-slicing bugs across the whole workspace (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. For views.rs: run xtask history db query with a non-SELECT/WITH/PRAGMA query containing a multi-byte char near byte 40.
2. For bench/environment.rs or reset.rs: run xtask bench or xtask reset while any unrelated host process has a multi-byte-character command-line argument near the truncation offset.
3. For git.rs: trigger the malformed-git-log-record error path against a repo with non-ASCII commit metadata near byte 120.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 sites use char-boundary-safe truncation instead of raw byte-index slicing.

title: rpc_server.rs has 3 post-auth token-prefix byte-slicing panics (same class as rate_limit.rs) -- operator-config footgun, not attacker-reachable (corrected from earlier 'pre-auth' framing)
description:
crate/sinexd/src/api/rpc_server.rs:301,322,576 all do `&token[..8.min(token.len())]` on the raw client-supplied gateway auth token -- the same unguarded byte-index pattern already found in the sibling rate_limit.rs (this session), but here on THREE sites in the request-handling hot path, all reachable BEFORE successful auth (invalid-role-encoding rejection at 301/322, rate-limit rejection at 576).

Failure scenario: an attacker (or a client with a malformed/non-ASCII token) sending a bad token can crash the RPC handler on the byte-boundary panic instead of getting a normal auth-rejection response -- a pre-auth DoS vector, not just a UX bug.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) hunting for UTF-8 byte-slicing bugs across the whole workspace (2026-08-11), sibling to the already-confirmed rate_limit.rs:141 instance.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Send an RPC request with a malformed-role-encoded or rate-limited token containing a multi-byte UTF-8 character within the first 8 bytes.
2. Observe the &token[..8.min(token.len())] slice at rpc_server.rs:301/322/576 panics before auth completes, rather than returning a normal rejection.
acceptance_criteria: All 3 sites use a char-boundary-safe prefix extraction (matching whatever fix lands for the sibling rate_limit.rs instance). A test with a malformed multi-byte token confirms no panic and a normal rejection response instead.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11), together with sinex-a0qe. Fix: clippy::string_slice lint backstop added at the workspace level to prevent regressions to raw byte-index string slicing. Verified via xtask check --lint on the merged commit.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-11, from a dedicated Opus design investigation into the broader UTF-8-slicing pattern): this bead's "pre-auth DoS vector" / area:security framing is WRONG. Traced the actual control flow: crate/sinexd/src/api/rpc_server.rs:262 calls state.auth.verify(&headers), and verify() (rpc_server/auth.rs:225-239) returns the token ONLY AFTER constant_time_eq(provided.as_bytes(), expected.as_bytes()) has already succeeded -- confirmed by the code's own comment at auth.rs:274-276: "we cannot derive a token prefix from a rejected bearer." By the time rpc_server.rs:301/322/576 slice the token, it is byte-identical to the OPERATOR'S OWN CONFIGURED TOKEN.

So this can only panic if the operator's own configured gateway token has a multi-byte codepoint straddling byte 8 -- a real bug, but an operator footgun triggerable only by the operator's own config choice, not an attacker-reachable pre-auth surface. Downgrading from area:security P2 to a plain UTF-8-safety bug, same class/priority as the other sibling instances (sinex-x6kp, sinex-hku1, sinex-56qh) tracked under the consolidated fix in sinex-a0qe.

title: xtask infra smoke's error cleanup never terminates sinexd on several failure paths (stray process); impact.rs's line-dedup can discard a covered=true LLVM segment in favor of covered=false for the same line
description:

HIGH -- xtask infra smoke's error-cleanup omits sinexd termination in multiple failure paths (infra.rs:1569-1605,1681-1697). cleanup_after_smoke_error only stops nats/postgres and releases the lock; if wait_for_sinexd_stopped times out or cancel reports oddly, sinexd remains running outside cleanup, leaving stray process/port holdover for subsequent infra actions.

2. Feed impact.rs LLVM coverage data with two same-line segments where one is covered and one isn't -- observe dedup_by_key can discard the covered one.
acceptance_criteria: cleanup_after_smoke_error also force-stops sinexd (not just nats/postgres) on every failure path. impact.rs's line dedup prefers covered=true over covered=false when segments collide on the same line.

title: xtask history stats --package filter is display-only (never applied to the query); diagnostics_command.rs panics on non-ASCII path truncation; diagnostics delta only searches the last 50 invocations

title: xtask fix --thorough is a no-op when explicit packages are passed (contradicts its own doc); xtask fuzz's documented run/corpus examples use a package-name convention init doesn't produce

title: library.rs read_mtime mistags a wall-clock fallback as TimingEvidence::InferredMtime on timestamp-extraction failure, when the correctly-handled sibling branch two lines below uses Atemporal
description:
library.rs's read_mtime fabricates ts_orig on filesystem-metadata read failure and mistags it TimingEvidence::InferredMtime (a resolved-quality tag), same bug class as sinex-dmz9/journald/systemd, but with a narrower trigger.

crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/library.rs:313-331:
```rust
Ok(meta) => {
    let mtime = meta.modified().ok()
        .and_then(|t| t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
        .and_then(|d| { ...; Timestamp::from_unix_timestamp_nanos(nanos) })
        .unwrap_or_else(Timestamp::now);
    let evidence = TimingEvidence::InferredMtime { path: path.clone(), mtime };
    (mtime, evidence)
}
Err(_) => (Timestamp::now(), TimingEvidence::Atemporal),
```

Only fires when std::fs::metadata succeeds but .modified()/duration_since/nanos-conversion fails (pre-epoch mtime, or a filesystem without mtime support) -- a rarer condition than the journald/systemd/activitywatch malformed-field case, but the same bug: the now() fallback is packaged as InferredMtime (resolved quality) rather than Atemporal, so admission trusts and persists it instead of deferring to raw.temporal_ledger resolution. The immediately adjacent Err(_) branch two lines below handles the analogous failure correctly (tags Atemporal) -- this Ok(meta)-but-timestamp-extraction-fails branch is the one outlier.

Found via a targeted follow-up audit (Sonnet) of this session's confirmed activitywatch.rs finding (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger std::fs::metadata succeeding but .modified()/duration_since/nanos-conversion failing (e.g. pre-epoch mtime on a filesystem that permits it, or metadata lacking mtime support).
2. Observe read_mtime falls to Timestamp::now() tagged InferredMtime instead of Atemporal, unlike the Err(_) branch immediately below which correctly uses Atemporal for the analogous failure.
acceptance_criteria: The Ok(meta)-but-extraction-fails path tags its now() fallback Atemporal, matching the Err(_) branch's existing correct handling right below it.

title: parser fixture harness's FieldPresent/FieldAbsent assertions contradict their own null-handling doc; relation-evidence default candidate query can become an unbounded near-MAX_LIMIT scan on empty seed set
description:
Two unrelated findings:

2. query.rs's relation-evidence default candidate query can devolve into an unbounded, near-DoS-shaped scan when the seed set is empty (wave128-043, api/handlers/query.rs:256-307). default_candidate_query builds an unnarrowed query up to MAX_LIMIT when the seed query returns empty and no explicit candidate_query was given -- a user typo yielding an empty seed set causes a near-top-of-capability scan instead of a narrow/empty result.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

1. Write a fixture asserting FieldPresent on a field whose parsed value is JSON null -- observe it passes despite the doc saying 'present (non-null)'.
2. Send a relation-evidence request with a seed query that returns zero matches (e.g. a typo) and no explicit candidate_query -- observe the resolved candidate query becomes an effectively unbounded scan up to MAX_LIMIT.
acceptance_criteria: FieldPresent/FieldAbsent assertion semantics match their documented null-handling contract (pick one direction and make code+docs agree). default_candidate_query narrows or short-circuits when the seed set is empty, rather than falling through to a near-unbounded scan.

title: sinexctl mcp.rs: two tool schemas omit parameters their handlers actually consume (source_identifier, external_system/external_id); transport-unavailable degrades inconsistently across tool groups
description:

title: ops/debt.rs wires sources.list instead of sources.remediation_plan for a remediation action; environment.rs's namespace-check warning fires backwards; OperationRunStatus::is_active() wrongly includes RetryWait
description:
Two unrelated small CLI findings from wave128:

1. sinexctl ops/debt.rs wires the wrong RPC method for source-material remediation detail rows (wave128-031). ops/debt.rs:365-372: `ActionAvailability::read("source_material.remediation_plan", ..., ...).with_rpc_method("sources.list")` -- should be "sources.remediation_plan" (the sibling constructor at ops/debt.rs:270-277 uses the correct method). A caller executing this action via rpc_method gets the wrong view.

2. sinex-primitives environment.rs emits a false "not environment-namespaced" warning for already-namespaced DB URLs (wave128-010). environment.rs:555: `let namespaced = self.database_url(&db_url)?; if namespaced == db_url { warn!(...) }`. database_url() returns the original string unchanged exactly when it's already namespaced -- so this equality check fires the warning on the CORRECT case, not the incorrect one. Misleading operational signal (alert fatigue).

3. OperationRunStatus::is_active() treats RetryWait as active/in-flight (crate/sinex-primitives/src/domain/operations.rs:252), contradicting RetryWait's own doc ("failed transiently, waiting to retry" -- not actively held by a worker). Any orchestration gating on is_active() overcounts retry-waiting jobs as active.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger the source-material detail debt row's remediation action via its rpc_method field -- observe it calls sources.list instead of sources.remediation_plan.
2. Set SINEX_ENVIRONMENT=dev with an already-namespaced DATABASE_URL (e.g. ...sinex_dev) -- observe startup warns 'not environment-namespaced' despite being correctly namespaced.
3. Check is_active() for a task in RetryWait state -- observe it returns true despite RetryWait meaning no worker currently holds the job.
acceptance_criteria: ops/debt.rs's remediation action uses sources.remediation_plan. environment.rs's namespace check warns only when namespaced != db_url (the actually-wrong case). is_active() excludes RetryWait or the doc comment is corrected to match actual intended semantics.

title: relations.rs sequence-span check breaks on reverse-chronological input; interval union drops weaker-basis provenance; query_units.rs silently nulls unserializable field values
description:
Three findings in crate/sinex-primitives, wave128-017:

1. relations.rs sequence span check can under-report when event order is reverse-chronological (relations.rs:671,678,680). span = end - start goes negative for descending-order input, so span > within_secs never fires the sequence.span_exceeded caveat even when temporal span clearly exceeds the bound.

2. relations.rs interval union drops basis provenance from one side (relations.rs:199, `basis: self.basis`). Unioning ranges with different TimeBasis values (e.g. SourceIntrinsic vs Inferred) always keeps the left operand's basis, letting a merged range claim a stronger basis than the combined evidence supports.

3. query_units.rs SinexQueryResultRow::with_field silently turns unserializable values into null (query_units.rs:329, `serde_json::to_value(value).unwrap_or(Value::Null)`) -- e.g. f64::NAN -- masking payload corruption as a legitimate null.

Found via wave128 gpt-5.3-codex-spark narrate-through wave (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Evaluate a Sequence relation over events [t=2000, t=1000] with within_secs=300 -- observe span computes as -1000s and no caveat fires despite real span exceeding the bound.
2. Union two ObservedRanges with different TimeBasis values -- observe the result always keeps the left operand's basis regardless of which side is weaker.
3. Call with_field with a value that fails JSON serialization (e.g. NAN) -- observe it silently becomes null instead of erroring.
acceptance_criteria: Sequence span check uses abs(end-start) or otherwise handles reverse-chronological input correctly. Interval union picks the weaker/looser basis of the two operands, not always the left one. with_field propagates serialization failure rather than silently nulling.

title: entity_chain_shadow.rs always marks relation candidates SourceCoverage::Covered regardless of actual material grounding; document_parser.rs never emits chunk_id/chunk_hash that embedding_producer.rs expects (silently degrades to 'unknown' placeholders); terminal doc side-data hardcodes shell=zsh for all shell types
description:
Three bugs found via narrate-through audit (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, wave128-049):

1. MEDIUM -- crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs:421 relation candidates in the shadow lane are always marked SourceCoverage::Covered and store source_material_id: None, regardless of whether the underlying co-occurring source events actually had material grounding -- even though the module already captures per-event source_material_id in StreamCheckpointEventRow. A relation built from shell-derived chunks/commands (typically without source material) is emitted as fully covered evidence, overstating evidence quality and letting curation/analytics paths over-trust candidates that rely on source coverage.

2. MEDIUM -- document_parser.rs:286,295 and embedding_producer.rs:71,78: document chunk payloads don't include chunk_id/chunk_hash that the embedding producer expects, so the producer falls back to placeholders (`unwrap_or("unknown")`, `unwrap_or("")`). Any consumer using chunk_id as a stable trace key sees "unknown", and chunk-hash-driven correlation/replay semantics degrade silently -- malformed/incomplete input is accepted without fail-fast, weakening traceability and auditability of embedding work-products.

3. LOW -- document_parser.rs:356 terminal-derived document side-data hardcodes `side_data.insert("shell".into(), JsonValue::String("zsh".into()))` even though the canonicalizer explicitly accepts command sources from Kitty/Atuin/Bash/Zsh/Fish -- any downstream rule/dashboard relying on shell-specific context misclassifies non-zsh terminal outputs.

2. Run a document through document_parser.rs's chunking, then embedding_producer.rs -- observe the resulting embedding receipt's chunk_id is the literal string "unknown" and chunk_hash is empty.
3. Run a non-zsh terminal source (bash/fish/kitty) through document_parser.rs -- observe side_data always reports shell="zsh".
acceptance_criteria: entity_chain_shadow.rs derives SourceCoverage from the actual per-event source_material_id it already captures, rather than hardcoding Covered. document_parser.rs emits real chunk_id/chunk_hash values that embedding_producer.rs can consume without falling back to placeholders. side_data's shell field reflects the actual originating shell type.

title: api handlers tasks.rs: duplicate-external-ref check trims new refs but compares against untrimmed stored refs, letting whitespace-variant duplicates slip through

title: automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs (live sinex-0vx.9 shadow lane, never internally read before): 6 silent-failure/validation-gap findings across freeze, serialization, scope validation, and rerun handling
description:
Six issues found in automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs (811 lines) -- confirmed NOT dead code (it's the deliberate sinex-0vx.9 shadow re-entry path for the retired 4-stage entity chain, referenced from supervisor/mod.rs), but never internally read/narrated before this pass:

1. Line 187 -- `u64::try_from(matching).unwrap_or(0)` in the freeze path: a COUNT(*) value that can't convert to u64 silently becomes end_seq=0, producing a frozen scope with a wrong boundary rather than a hard failure -- missing/incorrect replay coverage.
2. Lines 346,434,477 -- `serde_json::to_value(&output).unwrap_or(Value::Null)` and similar for claim-support: serialization failures are silently downgraded to Null, but rows are still persisted and the candidate lane still marked completed, masking the true failure and dropping evidence/output content.
3. Line 240 -- `i64::try_from(end_seq.saturating_sub(*start_seq))`: a malformed scope with start_seq > end_seq collapses via saturating_sub to limit=0, silently processing zero events while still marking the lane completed -- an apparently successful but empty result with no error surfaced.
4. Lines 220-225 -- the scope's `stream` field is destructured but never validated against the query, which is hardcoded to read from core.events regardless -- a scope with a mismatched/invalid stream value is silently accepted, bypassing the scope's declared stream semantics.
5. Lines 592-595 -- when existing_lanes is provided, the lane IDs are used without validating they actually belong to the current frozen scope/epoch context -- a caller passing wrong lane IDs for a different scope/epoch causes outputs to be written into that lane, producing cross-scope contamination rather than an explicit mismatch error.
6. Lines 648-652 -- `if !rows.is_empty() { write_lane_outputs(...) }`: on a rerun where the new output set is empty or smaller than the previous run's, old lane_outputs rows are never cleared, so results are not truly replaced -- later consumers/diff logic can see stale outputs mixed with (or instead of) the new run's results.

Found via a narrate-through audit of crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11) -- this was explicitly flagged this session as real, live shadow-lane code that had never been internally read.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a freeze where COUNT(*) can't convert to u64 -- observe end_seq silently becomes 0.
2. Trigger a serialization failure on output/claim-support -- observe the row is still persisted with Null content and the lane marked completed.
3. Construct a scope with start_seq > end_seq -- observe zero events processed but lane still marked completed.
4. Pass a scope with a mismatched stream field -- observe it's silently accepted since the query is hardcoded regardless.
5. Pass existing_lanes for the wrong scope/epoch -- observe outputs get written into the wrong lane.
6. Rerun with a smaller output set than the previous run -- observe stale rows from the prior run survive.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 instances either surfaces an error or is explicitly documented as an accepted tradeoff for this shadow/legacy-compat lane, given it's confirmed live (not dead) code.

title: sinex-db pkm.rs: unrecognized material_type silently downgrades to generic blob; duration-to-i32 conversion saturates instead of signaling overflow
description:

title: sinexctl OutputFormat::Dot handled inconsistently across formatting layers; required_rpc_role silently under-approximates on unmatched method names; formatless commands not consistently marked with empty supported sets
description:
Two minor consistency issues:
1. crate/sinexctl/src/fmt/{envelope,output}.rs -- OutputFormat::Dot is handled inconsistently: render_envelope/render_finite_envelope explicitly reject it with an error (correct, since Dot only makes sense for graph output), but format_list/format_single/empty_result/CommandOutput::display instead silently render it as JSON/null. A non-graph command asked to display as Dot format gets misleading JSON-like output instead of the intended hard rejection.
2. crate/sinexctl/src/model/format_registry.rs:854-863 -- required_rpc_role is derived via filter_map over rpc_catalog lookups with no error path for a missing/typo'd method name; a stale or misspelled entry in backing_rpc_methods_for_path silently contributes nothing to role inference, potentially under-approximating the required privilege level for a command.
3. format_registry.rs:762-782,1356-1369 -- commands documented as "format not applicable" (tui, config init/edit/path) aren't consistently given empty `supported` capability sets (unlike ops demo, which does this correctly) -- command_consumes_format's contract (`supported.is_empty()`) can then treat them as format-consuming despite their own documentation saying otherwise, causing avoidable validation failures.

Found via a narrate-through audit of crate/sinexctl/src/fmt/{envelope,json,mod,output,progress,table,units,yaml}.rs and crate/sinexctl/src/model/{format_registry,mod}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call CommandOutput::display(&OutputFormat::Dot) on a non-graph command -- observe JSON/null output instead of the rejection error render_envelope would give.
2. Introduce a stale/misspelled entry in backing_rpc_methods_for_path -- observe required_rpc_role silently omits that method's contribution.
3. Check tui/config init/edit/path's supported capability sets against ops demo's -- observe the inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: OutputFormat::Dot is rejected consistently across all output paths, not just render_envelope. required_rpc_role errors (or logs) on an unmatched method name rather than silently contributing nothing. Formatless commands consistently declare empty supported sets matching their documentation.
