title: xtask bench tooling: UTF-8 panic in process-line truncation, git-dirty misses staged changes, heavy-process heuristic misses unspaced binary paths, non-atomic run persistence, second-resolution output-dir collision
description:
Five issues in xtask's benchmark tooling (xtask/src/bench/{environment,history,runner}.rs):
1. environment.rs, truncate_process_line -- slices /proc/<pid>/cmdline text by raw byte index without a UTF-8 boundary check; multi-byte command text can panic environment capture (and thus the whole benchmark run).
2. environment.rs, git_dirty() -- uses `git diff --quiet` only, which reports clean (exit 0) when changes are staged but not yet committed; benchmark metadata under-reports workspace dirtiness, corrupting baseline/history comparisons.
3. environment.rs, is_heavy_command() -- matches heavy-process names via space-padded substring tokens (" cargo ", " rustc ", etc.); a command line beginning with the binary path with no leading space (e.g. /usr/bin/cargo) isn't classified as heavy, so contention/noise context can be silently omitted from benchmark snapshots.
4. history.rs:90-124 -- run persistence inserts a `runs` header row then loops inserting `results` rows without a transaction; if one results insert fails mid-loop, the caller gets a failed save but the DB already has an orphaned run header (and possibly partial scenario rows) polluting future history/trend queries.
5. runner.rs:28-34,185-192 -- the default output directory uses second-resolution timestamps (`bench-nextest-{year}{month}{day}-{hour}{minute}{second}`); two benchmark runs started within the same second collide on the same output directory, clobbering each other's environment.txt/report files.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/bench/{config,environment,modes,mod}.rs and xtask/src/bench/{history,reports,runner,stats}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run a benchmark while a process with non-ASCII cmdline text is active -- observe environment capture can panic.
2. Stage but don't commit a change, then run a benchmark -- observe git_dirty reports false.
3. Start two benchmark runs within the same second -- observe they write to the same output directory.
acceptance_criteria: Process-line truncation clamps to a UTF-8 boundary. git_dirty checks both the working tree and the index (git status --porcelain, or diff --quiet plus diff --cached --quiet). Heavy-process matching handles unspaced binary-path prefixes. Run persistence wraps the runs+results inserts in one transaction. The output-dir timestamp includes sub-second resolution or a collision-avoidance suffix.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] 5 xtask bench issues (UTF-8 panic, git-dirty false-clean, heavy-cmd heuristic, non-atomic persistence, timestamp collision) -- each independently unit-testable. O3.

title: xtask deps command: --all and --compare flags are parsed but silently no-op; all_dependencies() docstring claims transitive coverage it doesn't have; several silent-fallback bugs (parse failures, path-separator, format typos)
description:
Six issues in xtask's deps command family (xtask/src/deps/{mod,analyzer,timing,unused,compile_surface,reports}.rs):

1. mod.rs:24 -- `List { all: bool }` is declared and documented ("Include transitive dependencies") but `run` matches `Self::List { all: _ }` and never reads it -- `xtask deps list --all` has zero effect.
2. mod.rs:63 -- `Timings { compare: ... }` similarly is parsed but discarded (`Self::Timings { compare: _, ... }`) and never passed to TimingAnalyzer::analyze_with_options -- `--compare <baseline>` produces the same report as no-compare.
3. analyzer.rs:174 -- `all_dependencies()`'s docstring says "including transitive" but the implementation iterates only `active_direct_dependencies()` once per package (no recursive traversal) -- callers relying on this for a transitive closure undercount indirect dependencies.
4. timing.rs:130-155,202-217 -- JSON/HTML timing-artifact parse failures are silently ignored (`if ... && let Ok(report) = parse(...) { return Ok(report); }` falls through on Err); a stale/corrupt timing artifact silently downgrades to a fallback report with zeroed durations, claiming success.
5. compile_surface.rs:221-227 -- module-bucket path stripping does `format!("{}/", display_path(source_root))` then `strip_prefix`, which is separator-dependent; on mismatched path forms the strip silently fails and the bucket falls back to the full absolute path, garbling module-bucket reporting.
6. reports.rs:24-27 -- unrecognized format strings silently fall back to Human output (`_ => Self::Human`) rather than erroring, so a typo like `--format=jsn` produces unexpected output instead of a clear error.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/deps/{active,analyzer,mod,compile_surface,reports,timing,unused}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask deps list --all vs without -- observe identical output.
2. Run xtask deps timings --compare <baseline> vs without -- observe identical output.
3. Call all_dependencies() and confirm it only returns direct edges despite the docstring.
acceptance_criteria: --all and --compare are actually wired to their intended behavior, or removed if genuinely out of scope with the CLI help updated accordingly. all_dependencies()'s docstring matches its real (direct-only) behavior, or the implementation is made genuinely transitive. The silent-fallback issues (parse failure, path separator, format typo) at minimum log a warning instead of silently downgrading.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] 6 xtask deps issues, all silent-noop/silent-fallback bugs on parsed-but-ignored flags -- directly assertable. O3.

title: xtask nextest wrapper leaks threads on error paths: stderr-reader thread left unjoined on malformed stdout, system monitor never stopped on reporter error
description:
Two resource/thread-leak issues in xtask's nextest wrapper (xtask/src/nextest/{reporter,runner}.rs):
1. reporter.rs:276-283,424 -- TestReporter::run's stdout-parsing loop uses `?` on line_res, serde_json::from_str, and try_into_message() -- any malformed/partial/unexpected-shape nextest stdout line makes `run` return early, BEFORE the final `stderr_thread.join()` call, leaving the stderr-reading thread running detached past the command's logical lifecycle.
2. runner.rs:309,347-356,365 -- TestRunner::execute starts a TestMonitor before calling reporter.run(); because `stats_result?` short-circuits on a reporter error (including the no-suite-discovered case), `monitor.stop()` (called after) is skipped, leaving the monitoring thread running in the background indefinitely on this error path.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/nextest/{junit,mod,monitor,reporter,runner}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed nextest output with a malformed/unexpected-shape JSON line -- observe TestReporter::run returns early without joining stderr_thread.
2. Trigger a reporter error (e.g. no test suite discovered) -- observe TestRunner::execute returns without calling monitor.stop().
acceptance_criteria: Both cleanup paths (stderr_thread.join(), monitor.stop()) run unconditionally via a guard/defer pattern regardless of which error path is taken, not only on the success path.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] reporter_test.rs has malformed_stdout_json_fails_honestly (error path returns Err correctly) but does NOT assert the stderr-reader thread is actually joined/not leaked on that path -- the specific claim in this bead is untested. runner_test.rs has only 1 unrelated test. Thread-leak assertions are testable (JoinHandle tracking) but absent.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 implementation pass 2026-08-11] Deferred: reporter::run() is genuinely testable (generic over BufRead, already exercised black-box in reporter_test.rs), but proving the specific thread-leak claim needs white-box instrumentation (e.g. an Arc<AtomicUsize> line-counter in a custom BufRead passed as stderr, checked immediately after run() returns via the malformed-stdout error path) to distinguish 'thread not joined' from 'thread finished anyway because the fixture was small' -- not attempted this pass due to time budget. Root cause confirmed real: the for-loop over stdout.lines() at reporter.rs:275 uses bare ?, returning before reaching the stderr_thread.join() call at line 423.

title: xtask graph: unrecognized --render-format silently falls back to ASCII instead of erroring; ASCII forest renderer's shared visited-set drops repeated dependencies from later roots
description:
Two issues in xtask's dependency-graph command (xtask/src/graph/{mod,render,workspace,impact}.rs):
1. mod.rs:61 -- an unrecognized --render-format value (e.g. a typo like "jsom") is silently treated as ASCII output rather than rejected, so automation expecting JSON gets ASCII and fails downstream with a confusing parse error rather than an immediate clear rejection.
2. render.rs:399 -- the ASCII tree renderer's `visited` HashSet is shared across the whole forest render and never removed on recursion unwind, so when rendering ALL packages, a dependency shared by multiple roots (e.g. A->C and D->C) only appears once (under whichever root visits it first) rather than under every root that depends on it -- the printed forest is a traversal-pruned view, not a complete representation of the requested graph.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/graph/{impact,mod,render,workspace}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask graph --render-format=jsom (typo) -- observe silent ASCII output instead of an error.
2. Render the full package forest where two roots share a common dependency -- observe the shared dependency only appears under one root's subtree.
acceptance_criteria: Unrecognized --render-format values produce an explicit error. The ASCII renderer either scopes 'visited' per-root-subtree (allowing a shared dependency to appear under every root that depends on it) or documents the pruned-view behavior explicitly if that's intentional for readability.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (reject unrecognized --render-format; visited-set scoping). O3.

title: xtask run <module> --dry-run still performs full runtime preflight, inconsistent with bundle dry-run's skip-readiness behavior
description:
xtask/src/commands/run.rs:1118-1120 -- `xtask run runtime-module <name> --dry-run` still calls `preflight::ensure_ready(ctx)?;` BEFORE the dry_run check, so single-module dry-run runs still perform full runtime-dependency preflight/readiness validation (which can start/couple to live infra), inconsistent with bundle dry-run behavior (which skips readiness checks) and violating the expectation that --dry-run is non-side-effecting.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{test,run}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask run runtime-module fs-source --dry-run against an environment where preflight::ensure_ready would fail or have side effects.
2. Compare to xtask run bundle ... --dry-run, which skips readiness checks entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Single-module dry-run skips preflight::ensure_ready the same way bundle dry-run does, or the inconsistency is documented as intentional with a stated reason.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (dry-run skips preflight). O3.

title: xtask coverage command: browser-open failure not surfaced past spawn, enforce-stage marked successful before JSON parse can still fail
description:
Two issues in xtask's coverage command (xtask/src/commands/coverage.rs):
1. Lines 157-175 -- open_report_in_browser only checks that xdg-open/open spawned successfully, not that it actually opened the report; the Child handle is dropped without wait(), so a later browser-launch failure (no GUI backend, no HTML handler) is silently unreported and the spawned process may become an unreaped zombie.
2. Lines 254-276 -- execute_enforce calls `ctx.finish_stage(stage, output.success())` BEFORE parsing the coverage JSON; if llvm-cov exits 0 but produces unexpected JSON shape (tool-version drift, partial output), the subsequent parse fails and the command errors out, but stage telemetry already recorded success=true for that stage, making automation/history misread this run as a successful coverage-enforce stage.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{freshness,coverage}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask coverage html --open on a headless system with no browser handler for HTML -- observe the command reports success despite the browser never actually opening.
2. Inject an unexpected JSON shape from llvm-cov --json into execute_enforce -- observe finish_stage already recorded success=true before the parse failure surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: open_report_in_browser waits on the child and surfaces its actual exit status, or documents best-effort semantics explicitly. execute_enforce finishes the stage AFTER successful JSON parsing, not before.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (wait on child exit status; finish_stage after parse). O3.

title: xtask infra/vm commands: partial-start leaves NATS running on later PG failure, smoke-cleanup cancel error discarded, VM staged-checkout Drop-cleanup failure silently ignored
description:
Three issues in xtask's infra/vm command implementations:
1. infra.rs:368-404 -- execute_start spawns NATS then applies Postgres schema; if the PG step fails after NATS already started, there's no cleanup of the already-started NATS process, leaving a "start failed but partially up" state that breaks the expected all-or-nothing start semantics.
2. infra.rs:1595 -- `let _ = manager.cancel(job_id);` in the smoke-test cleanup path; if cancel fails, the failure is silently dropped and the caller can't tell whether the spawned background `sinex run` job is still active, risking an orphaned runtime process.
3. vm.rs:686-691 -- `Drop for VmFlakeInput` does `let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&report.staged_root);`, silently ignoring cleanup failures (permissions, transient FS issue) and leaving stale staged VM-test checkout directories to accumulate.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{infra,vm}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger xtask infra start with both pg+nats and inject a PG-step failure after NATS starts -- observe NATS is left running.
2. Inject a manager.cancel() failure during smoke-test cleanup -- observe the failure is silently dropped.
3. Inject a remove_dir_all failure in VmFlakeInput's Drop -- observe the stale directory persists with no warning.
acceptance_criteria: execute_start cleans up already-started components if a later component fails (all-or-nothing). Smoke-cleanup cancel failures are at minimum logged so orphaned background jobs are discoverable. VM staged-checkout cleanup failures are logged rather than silently swallowed.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No test found for the 3 partial-start/cleanup-cancellation issues in xtask infra/vm commands (infra.rs:368-404 and related). Testable via infra integration tests per scenario, live-infra tier.

title: xtask fuzz command has a naming-contract mismatch between init/list/run (tests/ targets unreachable, package-name suffix confusion); fix.rs discards history-snapshot write errors
description:
Four issues in xtask's fuzz/fix/ra command wrappers:
1. fuzz.rs:546-562,394-405 -- find_crate_dir accepts crate/, tests/, and xtask as valid `fuzz init` targets, but discovery for `fuzz list`/`fuzz run` is hardcoded to only search workspace_root/crate -- an init'd fuzz target under tests/ is unreachable via list/run.
2. fuzz.rs:88-105,420 -- init writes the fuzz manifest package name as "{package}-fuzz" but run/list expect an exact match to that suffixed name while user-facing docs/errors describe the bare crate name, creating a naming-contract mismatch that produces confusing "not found" errors.
3. fuzz.rs:420,251-258 -- target matching does an exact-string package-name lookup with no fuzzy/near-match suggestion, compounding the naming-contract confusion from #2 into repeated user-facing failures.
4. fix.rs:110 -- `let _ = ctx.with_history_db(|db| { db.record_fix_session_snapshot(...) });` discards history-DB write errors; a fix-session snapshot silently fails to record with no visible warning, breaking continuity of fix-session telemetry.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{fix,fuzz,ra}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask fuzz init my_crate under tests/ -- then xtask fuzz list -- observe it's not found.
2. Run xtask fuzz init sinex-db then xtask fuzz run sinex-db::some_target (the intuitive form) -- observe a not-found error requiring the suffixed sinex-db-fuzz::some_target form instead.
3. Inject a history-DB write failure during xtask fix -- observe no warning is surfaced.
acceptance_criteria: fuzz list/run search the same locations fuzz init supports (crate/, tests/, xtask). The package-name contract between init and run/list is either unified (same name in both) or run/list accept both forms with a clear error suggesting the correct one. fix.rs surfaces (at minimum logs) history-DB write failures for fix-session snapshots.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Naming-contract mismatch (fuzz init/list/run) and discarded write-error -- both directly reproducible/assertable per the Steps to Reproduce. O3.

title: xtask impact coverage seeding: unstable dedup can drop covered lines in favor of uncovered duplicates, malformed segment counts silently become 0
description:
Two issues in xtask's coverage-impact command (xtask/src/commands/impact.rs):
1. Line 398 -- `points.sort_unstable_by_key(|(line, _)| *line); points.dedup_by_key(|(line, _)| *line);`: LLVM coverage segments can yield multiple entries for the same source line with mixed covered/uncovered flags; because dedup collapses by line only and sort_unstable is not stable for equal keys, a covered point can be dropped in favor of an uncovered one, silently under-reporting coverage.
2. Line 395 -- `let count = segment.get(2)...unwrap_or_default();`: if the coverage JSON segment shape changes or has unexpected types, a malformed count silently becomes 0 (uncovered) rather than surfacing an error, masking upstream data-format issues.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/commands/{jobs,impact,reap}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed LLVM coverage data with duplicate entries for the same line, mixed covered/uncovered -- observe dedup_by_key can drop the covered entry.
2. Feed a coverage JSON segment with an unexpected shape at index 2 -- observe it silently becomes count=0.
acceptance_criteria: Dedup prefers a covered entry over an uncovered one for the same line (e.g. sort by (line, covered) before dedup, or explicitly merge covered-OR semantics). Malformed segment shapes surface a warning/error rather than silently defaulting to uncovered.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (dedup prefers covered entry; malformed segment surfaces error not silent 0). O3.

title: xtask history seeding + test-result parsing: swallowed secondary-insert failures, future-dated synthetic events, status-alias blind spot in queries, silent malformed-line drops, panic on empty event, non-deterministic ordering
description:
Two clusters of findings in xtask's synthetic-history seeding and test-result parsing:

**seed.rs** (xtask/src/history/seed.rs):
1. Lines 115-118,138-154,168-220,239-246 -- multiple `let _ = db.conn.execute(...)` on secondary inserts (invocation_packages, build_diagnostics, stage_timings, test_results); a real insertion failure is silently dropped and seed_history still returns Ok, marking the DB "synthetic" despite partial corruption.
2. Lines 59-71,83-84 -- timestamp generation (`start_unix = now - days*86400` plus per-step avg_gap+jitter) can push the final synthetic event's timestamp INTO THE FUTURE for low invocation counts, violating the implied "seeded events bounded by the requested past window" invariant of SeedOptions::days.

**tests.rs** (xtask/src/history/tests.rs, 1836 lines, the largest single unswept history file):
3. Status-alias handling is inconsistent: the parser accepts aliases (pass/ok/passed, fail/failed, skip/ignored, flaky at lines 43-48) but downstream SQL filters use canonical-only string literals (status = 'fail'/'pass'/'skip' at lines 325,354+) -- legacy rows stored with an alias spelling become invisible to analysis/count queries, under-reporting failures/skips.
4. Line 122-129 -- the nextest JSON parser silently `continue`s on empty/non-JSON lines and swallows parse errors (`Err(_) => {}`), hiding data-loss in ingestion with no warning.
5. Line 136 -- `assert!(!event.is_empty(), ...)` panics on an empty/corrupted suite-event payload, aborting the whole parse rather than failing soft on that one line.
6. Lines 616-625,646 -- trend-detail grouping uses HashMap iteration order (non-deterministic) as a tie-break when sorting only by test_name, so tests sharing a name across packages can appear in unstable order across runs.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/history/{seed,tracing_layer}.rs and xtask/src/history/tests.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Inject an insert failure into one of seed.rs's secondary inserts -- observe seed_history still reports success.
2. Seed with days=1, invocations=1 -- observe the synthetic timestamp can land in the future.
3. Store a test-result row with status='failed' (alias) then query get_failing_tests (canonical-only filter) -- observe it's missing.
4. Feed a malformed nextest JSON line -- observe silent skip with no warning.
5. Feed a suite event with an empty event field -- observe a panic rather than a handled error.
acceptance_criteria: Secondary-insert failures during seeding propagate or are at minimum logged with the seed marked partial. Synthetic timestamps are clamped to not exceed 'now'. SQL filters use the same alias-normalization the parser applies (or normalize on write). Malformed nextest lines are counted/logged, not silently skipped. The empty-event case returns an error instead of panicking.

title: xtask history DB top-level: metric writes ignore affected-row count, aux-file rename failure on schema-recreate silently ignored, schema-compat logic duplicated across two query builders
description:
Three issues in xtask's top-level history-DB module (xtask/src/history/{db.rs,mod.rs}, db/metrics.rs):
1. metrics.rs:10-19,28-97 -- two metric-write UPDATE statements ignore their affected-row count; if the caller passes a stale/nonexistent invocation_id, the SQL succeeds with 0 rows updated and the caller gets Ok(()) with metrics silently dropped, creating blind spots in analytics.
2. db.rs:424-431 -- on schema-recreate, auxiliary WAL/SHM artifact rename is `let _ = std::fs::rename(...)`; on failure the old aux files are left in place unrenamed while the DB is recreated, risking the new DB reading stale journal/shared metadata state.
3. metrics.rs:130-316 vs 419-605 -- the same schema-compatibility expression logic (which optional metric columns exist) is independently duplicated across two resource-usage query builders rather than centralized -- a future schema change applied to only one risks divergent query shapes between the list-view and single-invocation-view.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/history/{db.rs,mod.rs} and xtask/src/history/db/metrics.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call a metrics-write method with a stale invocation_id -- observe Ok(()) despite 0 rows affected.
2. Trigger a schema-recreate with an aux-file rename failure injected -- observe old WAL/SHM files remain alongside the recreated DB.
3. Compare metrics.rs:130-316 and 419-605's column-compatibility expression-building logic -- confirm it's duplicated rather than shared.
acceptance_criteria: Metric writes check affected row count and surface a warning/error on zero. Aux-file rename failures on schema-recreate are surfaced rather than silently ignored. The schema-compat expression logic is factored into one shared helper both query builders call.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] xtask/src/history/db/metrics.rs has zero test file and zero #[test] fns. All 3 cited issues (ignored affected-row counts, aux-file rename failure) are pure-logic, testable against the existing xtask-history SQLite test harness used by sibling modules. None written.

title: xtask history analysis/query: diagnostic count() is capped by limit not true cardinality, args_json parse failures silently treated as empty, scoring formula doesn't match its own doc comment
description:
Three issues in xtask's history analysis/query layer (xtask/src/history/{analysis,query}.rs):
1. query.rs:587 -- `DiagnosticQuery::count` is implemented as `self.run_diagnostic_query(q)?.len()`, which is capped by whatever limit is set (including the default 200) -- it returns min(true_count, limit), not true cardinality. A package with >200 current diagnostics reports a capped count, understating diagnostic_count/fixable_count in health outputs and workspace severity scoring.
2. analysis.rs:347 -- `serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(json).ok()` then `.unwrap_or_default()` silently swallows JSON parse failures for args_json; malformed/legacy/corrupted invocation args are treated as empty args, collapsing unrelated invocations into the same workload bucket and hiding real velocity trend shifts.
3. analysis.rs:209 vs 307 -- a documented scoring formula ("100 - errors*10 - warnings*1") doesn't match the actual implementation (warnings_count / 5); with 25 warnings and zero errors the real code yields 95 instead of the documented 75, muting urgent warning-heavy runs in dashboards/recommendations.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/history/{analysis,query}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create >200 current diagnostics for one package and call DiagnosticQuery::count -- observe it caps at 200.
2. Corrupt an invocation's args_json -- observe it's silently treated as an empty-args invocation.
3. Compute the health score for 25 warnings/0 errors and compare against the documented formula -- observe 95 vs. the documented 75.
acceptance_criteria: count() computes true cardinality independent of any result-set limit (e.g. a separate COUNT(*) query). args_json parse failures are logged/surfaced distinctly from genuinely-empty args. The scoring implementation matches its documented formula, or the doc comment is corrected to match the real formula with the intentional-choice reasoning stated.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Confirmed DiagnosticQuery::count (query.rs:587, wraps run_diagnostic_query().len()) has no test in query_test.rs or analysis_test.rs asserting count() differs from true cardinality when a limit is set. Testable via a fixture with rows > limit.

title: xtask history db: git-dirty detection can't distinguish 'command failed' from 'repo clean', prediction window multiplication can overflow
description:
Two lower-severity findings in the same small xtask history db helper files as the PID-reuse kill bug (filed separately, sinex-<pid-kill-bead>):

1. xtask/src/history/db/git.rs:24-26 -- dirty-state detection: `.output().ok().is_some_and(|o| !o.stdout.is_empty())` treats a `git status --porcelain` command FAILURE (not a repo, git unavailable, transient IO error) the same as a clean repo (empty stdout) -- both return `false` (clean). This silently corrupts the `git_dirty` provenance metadata recorded on invocation records.
2. xtask/src/history/db/prediction.rs:16 -- `format!("+{} seconds", window_mins * 60)`: if window_mins is large and user-influenced, this can overflow (panic in debug, wrap in release), producing an invalid or wrong prediction window.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/history/db/{audit,background,exercise,git,process,prediction,sandbox_meta}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run xtask outside a git repo or with git unavailable -- observe git_dirty metadata reports false (clean) rather than unknown/error.
2. Pass a large window_mins value to the prediction window calculation -- observe overflow behavior.
acceptance_criteria: git-dirty detection distinguishes a genuine command failure from a real clean-repo result (e.g. returns Option<bool> or propagates the error). The window-minutes-to-seconds multiplication uses checked/saturating arithmetic.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (git-dirty distinguishes failure from clean; checked/saturating arithmetic). O3.

title: xtask history DB: several silent-swallow/non-atomic bugs across diagnostics, views, impact-plan recording, and artifact integrity helpers
description:
Seven issues found across xtask's history-DB diagnostics/views/impact/integrity helpers:

1. xtask/src/history/db/diagnostics.rs:35 -- `.unwrap_or((0, 0, 0))` hides all query_row failures (and nested unwrap_or(0) per column) in get_diagnostic_counts_for_invocation; a corrupted row or read error silently reports zero diagnostics.
2. diagnostics.rs:215-216,220 -- an invalid/non-numeric invocation token is treated as "no invocation found" and silently returns empty diagnostics rather than an error -- a typo like `xtask history diagnostics abc` gets silent empty output.
3. diagnostics.rs:460-470 -- a string-joined identity key (`format!("{}|{}|{}|...")`) can collide when fields themselves contain '|', misclassifying diagnostics as persistent/new/resolved incorrectly in delta comparisons.
4. views.rs:179 -- `ORDER BY started_at ASC LIMIT 2000` for working-session queries reads only the OLDEST 2000 rows then reverses for display; for >2000 invocations, RECENT sessions are dropped entirely rather than the intended "most recent N".
5. impact.rs:91-110 (record_impact_plan) -- the impact_runs insert and each per-decision insert run on the same connection without an explicit transaction; if a later decision insert fails, a run row is committed with an incomplete decision set.
6. impact.rs:143-148 -- `i64::try_from(sample_size).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` silently collapses counter overflow to a sentinel i64::MAX rather than surfacing the bad input.
7. integrity.rs:108-118 -- artifact-preservation rename failures after earlier successful renames return an error with no rollback of the prior moves, leaving a non-atomic partial backup state.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/history/db/{diagnostics,impact,integrity,rows,test_results,types,views}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Corrupt a diagnostic-count row -- observe get_diagnostic_counts_for_invocation reports zeros rather than an error.
2. Run xtask history diagnostics with a typo'd invocation token -- observe silent empty output.
3. Trigger a decision-insert failure mid-impact-plan-recording -- observe an orphaned run row with incomplete decisions.
4. Accumulate >2000 invocations and query working sessions -- observe recent sessions are missing.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 7 instances either propagates its real error or is documented as an intentional best-effort tradeoff. The views.rs query orders/limits to keep the MOST RECENT rows, not the oldest. impact-plan recording wraps its multi-insert sequence in a transaction.

All 7 cited silent-swallow/non-atomic issues are pure-logic and testable against the existing history-DB test harness. None written.

title: xtask sandbox DB cleanup config: hardcoded table exclusion can mask dirty state, protected flag not enforced against Truncate method, synchronous_commit setting is per-connection not pool-wide
description:
Three issues in xtask's sandbox DB cleanup-config/common glue (xtask/src/sandbox/db/{common,mod,permissions,cleanup_config}.rs):
1. common.rs:57,16 -- `get_nonempty_tables` hardcodes an exclusion for "raw.source_material_registry"; if that's the ONLY table with residual rows, verify_clean_state can return Ok(()) despite dirty state, hiding test pollution.
2. cleanup_config.rs:302, common.rs:75 -- `truncatable_tables()` returns any entry with `method == Truncate` without checking its `protected` flag; a table constructed with protected=true but method=Truncate is still truncated, violating the documented "must never be truncated or deleted" contract for protected tables.
3. common.rs:124 -- `SET synchronous_commit TO OFF` is applied to one acquired connection; since this is a per-session Postgres setting, if tests use multiple pool connections the optimization only applies to some of them, making performance/behavior inconsistent across the pool.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/db/{common,mod,permissions,cleanup_config}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Leave rows only in raw.source_material_registry after a test -- observe verify_clean_state still reports clean.
2. Construct a CleanupConfig entry with protected=true and method=Truncate -- observe truncatable_tables() still includes it and the table gets truncated.
3. Run tests against a pool with 2+ connections -- observe synchronous_commit=OFF only applies to whichever connection happened to run the SET.
acceptance_criteria: get_nonempty_tables doesn't hardcode an exclusion that can mask real residual data (or the exclusion is documented as deliberate with a comment explaining why). truncatable_tables() excludes any entry where protected=true regardless of method. The synchronous_commit optimization is applied pool-wide (e.g. via connection-init hook) or documented as best-effort/single-connection.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No test in cleanup_config_test.rs or permissions_test.rs references get_nonempty_tables or the hardcoded raw.source_material_registry exclusion. Testable via a fixture asserting the exclusion doesn't mask a genuinely-dirty table. None written.

title: xtask sandbox workspace/dataset-seed helpers: duplicate [dependencies] table on repeated inject, silent no-op member-add, dropped IDs on seed publish
description:
Three issues in xtask's sandbox workspace/dataset-seed test helpers:
1. xtask/src/sandbox/workspace.rs:187-193 -- inject_unused_dep always appends a new `[dependencies]\n{dep} = "{version}"\n` block; calling it twice for the same crate (or after a [dependencies] table already exists) produces a Cargo.toml with duplicate table headers, an invalid manifest that fails at parse stage rather than producing the intended "unused dependency" test scenario.
2. xtask/src/sandbox/workspace.rs:214-221 -- add_member does an unchecked string `.replace(...)` on the workspace manifest; if the existing content doesn't exactly match the expected pattern (differently formatted, extra members already present), the replace is a silent no-op and add_member still returns Ok(self) with no member actually added.
3. xtask/src/sandbox/dataset_seeds.rs:128-137 -- `if let Some(id) = event.id { ids.push(id.to_uuid()); }` silently drops events with no id rather than erroring, so a caller relying on positional correspondence between seeded events and returned ids can silently lose entries.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/{workspace,dataset_seeds,mod,prelude}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call inject_unused_dep twice for the same crate -- observe the resulting Cargo.toml has duplicate [dependencies] headers and fails to parse.
2. Call add_member against a workspace manifest that doesn't exactly match the expected string pattern -- observe it returns Ok with no member actually added.
3. Seed events where one has no id -- observe the returned ids Vec silently has fewer entries than events seeded, breaking positional correspondence.
acceptance_criteria: inject_unused_dep checks for an existing [dependencies] table and appends to it rather than always creating a new header. add_member verifies the replacement actually happened (e.g. checks the string changed) and errors if not. dataset_seeds surfaces an error (or an explicit None marker) for events missing an id rather than silently shortening the result Vec.

Testable, not written.

title: xtask sandbox chaos helper: sub-millisecond jitter panics on empty range, failure-rate setting not wired into process_event
description:
xtask/src/sandbox/chaos.rs (test chaos-injection helpers):
1. Line 441 -- `Duration::from_millis(fastrand::u64(0..self.latency_jitter.as_millis() as u64))`: a sub-millisecond jitter value (e.g. 500 microseconds) is non-zero but rounds to 0 milliseconds, producing an empty range `0..0` for fastrand::u64, which panics.
2. Line 460 vs the `process_event` pipeline -- `should_fail()` (the failure-rate check) is defined but never called from `ChaosContext::process_event`, only from a different pipeline (`ChaosEventProcessor::process`). A caller using `ChaosTestBuilder::with_failure_rate(...)` + `process_event(...)` never actually gets random failures injected, silently defeating the configured chaos setting.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/{background,chaos,preflight}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call with_latency_jitter(Duration::from_micros(500)) then trigger apply_latency -- observe a panic from fastrand::u64(0..0).
2. Call with_failure_rate(1.0) then process_event(...) repeatedly -- observe no failures are ever injected, since should_fail() is never called from this path.
acceptance_criteria: Jitter below 1ms either rounds up to a minimum non-zero range or is handled without an empty-range panic. process_event calls should_fail() (or the two chaos pipelines are unified) so failure_rate actually takes effect on this path.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] chaos_test.rs has zero mention of latency_jitter or jitter at all -- the sub-millisecond-jitter-panics-on-empty-range bug and the failure-rate-not-wired issue are both untested. Directly testable (deterministic input construction).

title: xtask sandbox coordination+NATS test helpers: validation skipped at count==0, i32 downcast overflow, shared-key TLS-mode collision, swallowed canonicalize failure
description:
Coordination/assertions module (xtask/src/sandbox/coordination/, assertions/):
1. publish_batch/publish_batch_with_timestamps: EventType/EventSource validation (EventType::new, EventSource::new) is skipped entirely when count==0 -- an invalid event type string passed alongside count=0 is silently accepted rather than rejected, an inconsistency in when validation actually runs.
2. xtask/src/sandbox/coordination/scope.rs:390-391,406 -- `duration / (count as i32 - 1)` downcasts a usize count to i32; for count > i32::MAX this wraps/overflows, producing wrong or non-monotonic timestamp spreads.
3. xtask/src/sandbox/coordination/scope.rs:526-533 -- Drop schedules an async stop without awaiting it (best-effort by design), creating a cleanup race with permit release that isn't strictly ordered before permit reuse.

NATS sandbox setup (xtask/src/sandbox/nats/):
4. setup.rs:187 -- the custom shared-key resolution doesn't encode TLS/secure mode, so a plain and a secure() call using the same custom key can collide on one shared NATS instance despite different security profiles.
5. setup.rs:124 -- `fixture_dir.canonicalize().unwrap_or(fixture_dir)` swallows canonicalization failure and continues with the non-canonical (relative) path, which can silently resolve to the wrong location under varying working directories.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/{coordination/{mod,namespace,scope},assertions/{mod,contextual,event},nats/{mod,jetstream,pipeline,setup}}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call publish_batch/publish_batch_with_timestamps with count=0 and an invalid event_type string -- observe no validation error.
2. Call the timestamp-spread helper with a count exceeding i32::MAX -- observe wrapped/incorrect spacing.
3. Use ctx.with_nats().shared().key("x") in one test and ctx.with_nats().shared().secure().key("x") in another -- observe both resolve to the same shared instance.
acceptance_criteria: Validation runs regardless of count. The spread calculation uses a type that doesn't overflow for realistic counts (or explicitly bounds count). The shared-key resolution incorporates the security/TLS mode so differently-configured callers never collide. canonicalize() failures are surfaced rather than silently falling back to the uncanonicalized path.

title: xtask sandbox DB template pool: extension-drift check skipped on fast-reuse path, schema-verification failure swallowed, hardening steps best-effort, orphaned provisioning tasks on partial init failure
description:
Four issues in xtask's DB template-pool core/template management:

1. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/template.rs:494,698,700 -- the fast template-reuse path (`check_template_reuse(..., false)`) can return reuse without ever checking extension-default drift (only checked when check_drift=true), so extension baseline drift (e.g. a TimescaleDB default-version change) goes undetected until another path forces a rebuild.
2. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/template.rs:946-953 -- `query_scalar(...).await.unwrap_or(0)` on the post-rebuild schema-verification sanity query converts any transient failure (permissions, connection issue) into "0 tables", producing a generic "incomplete schema" error that loses the real failure reason.
3. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/template.rs:394-411 -- critical hardening steps (ALTER DATABASE ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false, pg_terminate_backend, pg_advisory_unlock) are all `let _ = ...`'d; harden_template_database still returns Ok(()) even if these fail, so later clone/rebuild operations can run under weaker-than-assumed safety conditions.
4. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/mod.rs:1179-1185,1358-1365 -- eager pool bootstrap spawns provisioning tasks and joins them in a loop; if one task errors, the function exits before awaiting the rest, leaving un-joined provisioning tasks running unsupervised in the background after the caller sees an init failure.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/{mod,template}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger the fast template-reuse path (matching fingerprint+trust) after an extension default changed -- observe drift is not detected.
2. Inject a transient failure into the post-rebuild table-count query -- observe it's silently treated as 0 tables with the real error lost.
3. Inject a failure into one of the harden_template_database steps -- observe the function still returns Ok(()).
4. Inject a failure in one eager-bootstrap provisioning task -- observe other spawned tasks are left running unjoined.
acceptance_criteria: Extension-default drift is checked on the fast-reuse path too, or the docs are corrected to state it's rebuild-only. The schema-verification query's real error is surfaced rather than collapsed to a table count of 0. Hardening step failures propagate rather than being ignored. Eager pool bootstrap either awaits all spawned tasks before returning an error, or explicitly cancels/tracks them.

But this bead's specific claim is EXTENSION-default drift (not CHECK-constraint drift) being skipped on that same path -- that scenario is not covered by the existing test. 3 of 4 sub-issues remain untested.

The bug is real (confirmed via source read: check_template_reuse's fast-reuse path checks schema-object drift via fingerprint but not extension-default drift specifically) but not implemented as a test this pass.

title: xtask sandbox DB pool bookkeeping: advisory-lock leak on reconnect failure, stale in-memory diagnostics after cleanup failure, ignored username-rewrite failure
description:
Three issues in xtask's ephemeral-Postgres test-pool bookkeeping helpers:

1. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/cleanup.rs:154 -- early return on reconnect failure skips `release_advisory_lock`, which is only called after the match; a pooled connection returned with the lock still held can block future lock attempts.
2. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/cleanup.rs:186-190 -- a cleanup SQL failure is persisted to DB metadata but `slot.record_clean_result(...)` is not called, so in-memory diagnostics stay stale from a previous successful cleanup and mask the recent failure.
3. xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/config.rs:211-214 -- `let _ = parsed.set_username(user);` in `force_user`: if setting the username fails, the function silently returns an unchanged URL, and downstream admin connections proceed with wrong credentials.

Found via a narrate-through audit of xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/{cleanup,config,health,health_benches,meta,metrics,slot,stats,test_database}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a reconnect failure inside the cleanup path -- observe release_advisory_lock is skipped.
2. Trigger a cleanup SQL failure -- observe DB metadata records it but slot.record_clean_result is never called, so in-memory diagnostics stay stale.
3. Call force_user with a username that set_username rejects -- observe the URL is silently returned unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The lock-release path runs even on the reconnect-failure branch (guard/RAII pattern). Cleanup failures update slot-local diagnostics too, not just the DB record. force_user surfaces a failure rather than silently returning an unmodified URL.

title: sinexctl SSE frame dispatcher silently drops malformed frame payloads instead of surfacing a stream error
description:
sinexctl's SSE (server-sent events) frame dispatcher silently drops malformed frame payloads rather than surfacing them as stream errors.

crate/sinexctl/src/client/gateway.rs, dispatch_frame, lines 2166, 2179, 2193:
```rust
serde_json::from_str(&self.current_data).ok()?
```
Used at three call sites in frame dispatch. A malformed SSE payload (e.g. a truncated frame, a server-side serialization bug, a proxy that mangles the stream) is silently skipped via .ok()? rather than surfaced as a stream error the caller could act on (retry, warn, disconnect).

Lower severity than the RPC-call error paths in this file (which were checked and found to correctly propagate errors) -- this is specifically the streaming/SSE ingestion path, a narrower surface, but the same "silent swallow" pattern found repeatedly elsewhere in sinexctl this session.

Found via a targeted audit of crate/sinexctl/src/client/gateway.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11), verified against the quoted code.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Feed a malformed/truncated JSON payload through the SSE stream to dispatch_frame.
2. Observe serde_json::from_str(...).ok()? silently returns None and the frame is skipped -- no warning, no surfaced error, no visible signal to the operator that a frame was lost.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed SSE frame payloads at minimum log a warning with enough context to diagnose (frame content or a hash of it), rather than silently vanishing. If frequent malformed frames indicate a real stream-health problem, consider surfacing a counter or triggering a reconnect after N consecutive parse failures.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Explicit AC given (malformed SSE frame logs a warning). O3.

title: xtask history DB migration checks are shallow (table-exists != column-exists) and both the migration and the introspection query silently swallow errors
description:
Three related robustness gaps in xtask's own SQLite history/telemetry DB (xtask-history.db) schema-migration and introspection code, all in crate/xtask/src/history/db/schema.rs:

1. ensure_proof_schema() (schema.rs:632) treats "both tables exist" as fully migrated, without checking whether the newer test_filter column exists on an older test_proof_units table:
```rust
if self.table_exists("proof_evidence")? && self.table_exists("test_proof_units")? {
    return Ok(());
}
```
On an older DB with both tables present but missing test_filter, this exits early and never adds the column -- later reads/writes of test_filter (e.g. get_successful_reusable_test_proof_unit/set_test_proof_filter in invocations.rs) then fail.

2. The migration that adds the column discards its own errors (schema.rs:680-683):
```rust
let _ = self.conn.execute(
    "ALTER TABLE test_proof_units ADD COLUMN test_filter TEXT",
    [],
);
```
If ALTER TABLE fails for a real reason (readonly DB, lock/corruption), startup continues silently with an inconsistent schema.

3. Column-existence introspection silently masks row-conversion errors via flatten() (schema.rs:612-615):
```rust
let exists = stmt
    .query_map([], |row| row.get::<_, String>(1))?
    .flatten()
    .any(|name| name == column);
```
Row-level conversion errors are dropped rather than surfaced, which can mislead ensure_column_exists() into a wrong migration decision.

Lower stakes than production sinex data (this is xtask's own build-tooling telemetry DB, not sinex_prod), but a corrupted xtask-history.db degrades this session's own verification/history tooling silently.

Found via a targeted audit of crate/xtask/src/history/db/{schema,invocations}.rs using gpt-5.3-codex-spark (2026-08-11), verified against the quoted code.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct an xtask-history.db with proof_evidence and test_proof_units tables present but test_proof_units missing the test_filter column (simulating an older DB).
2. Run any xtask command that calls ensure_proof_schema() -- observe it exits early via the table-exists check and never adds the missing column.
3. Trigger a later call to get_successful_reusable_test_proof_unit/set_test_proof_filter -- observe it fails against the missing column.
acceptance_criteria: ensure_proof_schema() checks for the specific columns it depends on, not just table existence. The ALTER TABLE error path propagates rather than being discarded. query_map's row-conversion errors are surfaced (e.g. via a fallible fold or explicit error collection) rather than silently dropped via flatten().

title: events_test.rs's event_select_columns! drift guard compares the macro against a hardcoded list in the same file (not the real DB schema) -- already silently stale, proven by its own comment/constant disagreement -- tautological-test pattern, sibling of sinex-6cra
description:
events_test.rs's drift guard for event_select_columns! macro drift never worked -- it compares the macro against a hardcoded list in the SAME FILE, not against the real database schema or EventRecord, and has already silently gone stale without being caught. Matches this session's already-identified tautological-test pattern (sibling instance: sinex-6cra).

crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/events_test.rs:1-98. Three #[sinex_test] tests (full DB fixture cost) claim to catch event_select_columns! drift. All three compare the macro against a HARDCODED LIST IN THE SAME FILE. None touches sinex::schema::Events, information_schema.columns, or EventRecord. Two proofs it never worked: (1) :5-6 still says "must equal sinex::schema::Events variant count excluding Table (24)" while EXPECTED_COLUMN_COUNT = 33 at :12 -- the comment and the constant already disagree; (2) :44-47 admits "this list had not been updated when these columns landed."

This is exactly the memorialize-the-diff anti-pattern CLAUDE.md's Verification section forbids, and the real invariant (macro <-> live core.events columns <-> EventRecord fields) is unenforced -- despite the macro's own doc warning it "will cause runtime query errors despite successful compilation." These are already DB tests (full fixture cost paid); an information_schema.columns set-comparison would be a real check for the same cost.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read events_test.rs:5-6's comment ('must equal sinex::schema::Events variant count excluding Table (24)') against :12's EXPECTED_COLUMN_COUNT = 33 -- confirm they already disagree, proving the guard has already gone stale without being caught.
2. Read :44-47's own comment admitting the hardcoded list wasn't updated when new columns landed.
acceptance_criteria: The three #[sinex_test] tests are rewritten to compare event_select_columns! against information_schema.columns for core.events (or an equivalent live-schema source), not a hardcoded list -- since these already pay full DB-fixture cost, this is a same-cost fix that makes the guard real.

Fixing this means rewriting the guard to query live schema; that rewritten guard IS the test. Not yet done.

title: 6 bundled lower-severity db-repositories findings: blob unique-index collision on re-insert, negated numeric PathOp filter silently drops matching rows, unbounded diamond-DAG descendant expansion, update_material_state ignores rows_affected, privacy engine fails open with only a warn on a disabled recognizer, document search splices FTS+trigram rankings at the same offset
description:
Six lower-severity, verified findings bundled from the sinex-db/repositories audit:

1. blobs.rs:47-85 blake3 branch arbitrates only on ON CONFLICT (checksum_blake3); uk_blobs_annex_backend_content_hash (defs/blobs.rs:145-149) is a SECOND unique index, unguarded -- re-inserting content first stored without blake3 raises 23505.
2. composable_query.rs:864-868 PayloadFilter::Not + numeric PathOp: NOT (TRUE AND CASE...END = x) is NULL when the field is absent/non-numeric, so negation silently drops rows it should include.
3. composable_query.rs:602-613 fetch_descendants uses UNION ALL with only a depth bound; diamond DAGs multiply exponentially and the result has no LIMIT.
4. source_materials.rs:201-258 update_material_state never checks rows_affected -- finalize_in_flight/mark_as_failed on a nonexistent id return Ok(()) silently.
5. privacy_policy.rs:193-200: a rule whose recognizer backend is disabled/missing is `continue`d with only a warn! -- the privacy engine fails open with a log line, no harder signal.
6. document_search.rs:184-196: on page 2+ an exhausted FTS result set silently falls through to trigram search AT THE SAME OFFSET, splicing two different rankings together. Also DocumentSearchQuery::vector_params (:68) is never read by search() and SearchMode::{Vector,Hybrid} (:97-98) are unreachable -- the only prod caller passes vector_params:None (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/documents.rs:48).

title: start_run's documented dedup (return existing active run instead of creating a duplicate) can never fire since core.runs has no unique constraint beyond its randomly-defaulted PK -- every restart appends to an unbounded, retention-free table
description:
start_run's documented dedup ("if a run is already active for this service, it is returned instead") can never fire, and every restart appends to an unbounded, retention-free table.

state.rs:967-1018 doc claims the dedup behavior, but core.runs has no unique constraint besides the PK, which is defaulted uuidv7() (defs/sinex_schemas.rs:227-283) -- so ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is structurally unreachable (there's nothing for it to conflict ON), and the .ok_or_else arm claiming to return the existing active run is dead code.

Every sinexd restart + source-runner registration (event_engine/service.rs:534, runtime/stream/runner/registration.rs:69) appends a fresh row to core.runs, which has no retention policy -- unbounded growth over the service's lifetime, worse under a reimport with many restarts.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read state.rs:967-1018's doc comment claiming dedup behavior via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
2. Read defs/sinex_schemas.rs:227-283 -- confirm core.runs' only constraint is its PK, defaulted to a fresh uuidv7() per insert, so no insert can ever conflict.
3. Restart sinexd multiple times and observe core.runs grows by one row per restart+source-runner registration, unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: Either add a real uniqueness constraint (e.g. on service_id + a partial WHERE active clause) so the documented dedup behavior actually works, or if runs are genuinely meant to be append-only history, correct the doc comment and add a retention/archival policy for core.runs so it doesn't grow unbounded.

title: schema_management.rs's if let Ok(...) pattern swallows real DB errors (not just not-found) from find_schema_by_hash, turning a transient connection blip into a confusing 23505 duplicate-key error on the fallback INSERT path
description:
Silent error downgrade on a schema write path can turn a transient DB blip into a confusing unexplained duplicate-key error.

schema_management.rs:242: `if let Ok(existing) = self.find_schema_by_hash(&content_hash).await`. find_schema_by_hash uses fetch_one, so ANY error (including a connection failure, not just "not found") falls through to register_new_schema_version, which at :355-361 finds a matching-hash existing row and does NOT return early -- proceeds to INSERT and hits a raw 23505 on uk_schema_identity. A transient blip during schema sync surfaces as an unexplained duplicate-key error instead of a clear "lookup failed, retry" signal.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Induce a transient DB error (e.g. brief connection blip) during find_schema_by_hash's fetch_one call in schema_management.rs:242.
2. Observe the if let Ok(...) pattern treats the error the same as 'not found', falling through to register_new_schema_version.
3. If a matching-hash row already exists, observe register_new_schema_version's :355-361 doesn't re-check for it and proceeds to INSERT, raising a confusing 23505 rather than surfacing the original connection error.
acceptance_criteria: find_schema_by_hash's error is distinguished from genuine not-found (e.g. match on Result explicitly, propagate real errors via ?), so a transient DB blip surfaces as a clear retryable error rather than masquerading as a duplicate-key violation.

title: pool-based cascade methods (prepare_cascade_session and siblings) are cross-connection-unsafe since the TEMP table is connection-local -- currently a loaded gun since every real caller uses the Tx-scoped twin, but a future pool-based caller would silently operate on the wrong/nonexistent temp table
description:
Pool-based cascade methods are cross-connection-unsafe (a loaded gun, not currently a live wound -- every real caller already uses the transaction-scoped twin).

core.prepare_cascade_session creates a TEMP table (apply.rs:2092-2104) = connection-local. EventRepository::{prepare_cascade_session, populate_cascade_roots, expand_cascade, expand_cascade_from, get_cascade_ids, cascade_node_count, cleanup_cascade_session} (persistence.rs:78-211, :1997-2129) each take a fresh pooled connection -- meaning a naive caller using the pool-based sequence would silently operate on a DIFFERENT connection's (and therefore different/nonexistent) temp table for each call.

Every live caller uses EventRepositoryTx instead (verified: cascade_analyzer.rs:341, lifecycle_ttl.rs:344, handlers/lifecycle.rs:119, handlers/sources.rs:1139, replay_control/execution/collect.rs:420, replay/state_machine.rs:721), so this is a loaded gun for a future caller, not a live wound.

Related: pool-side get_cascade_ids (:2120) omits the validate_cascade_table_name check its Tx twin has (:2902) -- a smaller instance of the same "the pool-based sibling is missing a safety check the Tx-based sibling has" pattern.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call EventRepository::prepare_cascade_session on the pool (not a transaction), then call populate_cascade_roots -- observe each call may acquire a different pooled connection, so the TEMP table created by prepare_cascade_session may not exist for the follow-up call.
2. Confirm every current production caller (cascade_analyzer.rs:341, lifecycle_ttl.rs:344, handlers/lifecycle.rs:119, handlers/sources.rs:1139, replay_control/execution/collect.rs:420, replay/state_machine.rs:721) uses EventRepositoryTx, not the pool-based methods.
acceptance_criteria: Either remove the pool-based cascade methods entirely (since nothing production uses them and they're unsafe by construction), or make them take an explicit single connection/transaction parameter so cross-connection misuse is impossible at the type level. Separately, get_cascade_ids's pool-side variant gains the validate_cascade_table_name check its Tx twin already has.

title: merge_entities would abort on any merge involving related entities (CHECK constraint violation) or a second merge into the same target (unique-index violation) -- both bugs currently unreachable since KnowledgeGraphRepository has zero production callers
description:
Two entity-merge bugs would abort the transaction on any real merge involving related entities, or on a second merge into the same target -- but KnowledgeGraphRepository has ZERO production callers (only tests), so core.entities is currently written by nothing else in the workspace. Filed for completion tracking, not as a live incident.

2a. HIGH (feature-breaking if ever wired) -- merge_entities cannot complete for any two RELATED entities. knowledge_graph.rs:1108-1120 (step 1c) and :1167-1179 (step 2c):
      UPDATE core.entity_relations SET from_entity_id = $2 WHERE from_entity_id::uuid = $1
core.entity_relations has CHECK (from_entity_id <> to_entity_id) -- sinex-schema/src/defs/entities.rs:393. If source has a relation source->target (the canonical duplicate case: same_as/alias_of), step 1b's dedup DELETE cannot remove it (would need a target->target row, forbidden by the CHECK), so 1c rewrites it to target->target and the transaction aborts with 23514. Symmetric via 2b/2c for target->source.

2b. HIGH (feature-breaking if ever wired) -- only ONE entity can ever be merged into a given target. sinex-schema/src/defs/entities.rs:211-218 declares ix_entities_merged as a UNIQUE partial index on merged_into_id WHERE is_merged = true. apply_entity_merge (knowledge_graph.rs:1030-1043) sets is_merged=true, merged_into_id=$target; the second duplicate merged into the same canonical entity raises 23505. Almost certainly .unique() was meant to be omitted from the index declaration.

Per CLAUDE.md "unfinished is not obsolete" -- this is completion work, not deletion, but it means the entity graph stays empty in prod until both bugs are fixed AND something actually calls KnowledgeGraphRepository in production.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/ (2026-08-11), covering 100% of the region.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct two entities with a same_as/alias_of relation between them (source->target).
2. Call merge_entities(source, target) -- trace step 1b/1c (knowledge_graph.rs:1108-1120) rewriting the relation to target->target, which violates core.entity_relations' CHECK (from_entity_id <> to_entity_id), aborting the transaction with 23514.
3. Separately, call merge_entities twice with different sources into the same target -- observe the second call violates ix_entities_merged's UNIQUE partial index on merged_into_id, raising 23505.
4. grep -rn 'KnowledgeGraphRepository' crate/sinexd/src -- confirm zero production callers (tests only), so neither bug currently fires.
acceptance_criteria: Both bugs are fixed as part of whatever work wires KnowledgeGraphRepository into production: the CHECK-violating relation-rewrite path handles the source->target/target->source special case (skip rather than rewrite, since it's already implicitly resolved by the merge), and ix_entities_merged's uniqueness is removed (multiple entities merging into one target is the normal case).

title: 3 smaller event_engine findings: #[cfg(test)] duplicate functions already diverged from production (F8), 8 unconstructed AdmissionDecision/AdmissionRejectionKind/RedeliveryErrorKind variants + a triplicated label-mapping (F9), DLQ msg-id dedup collapses distinct per-event failures within one intent (F10)
description:
Three lower-severity findings from the event_engine audit:

F8 -- #[cfg(test)] copies of production functions are what the tests actually exercise, not the real implementations. prepare.rs:11-20 (require_inserted_ids) and prepare.rs:657-692 (resolve_validation_result) are #[cfg(test)]-gated duplicates of the real implementations at admission.rs:1578-1587 and admission.rs:1541-1576. persistence_support.rs:38-42 (is_uuid_v7) duplicates admission.rs:1589-1591. jetstream_consumer_test.rs:38,52,64,79,86,244-246 test ONLY the copies. They have already diverged (`.with_operation("jetstream_consumer.validate_event")` vs `"admission.validate_event"`); a behavioural divergence would be equally invisible.

F9 -- declared-but-never-constructed variants (grepped whole tree, prod + tests): AdmissionDecision::Transformed (admission.rs:185, matched in 4 places, constructed nowhere); AdmissionDecision::QuarantineNeeded (admission.rs:199, handler at prepare.rs:145 unreachable); AdmissionRejectionKind::PrivacyPolicy/QuarantinePolicy (admission.rs:264-265, carried through three separate exhaustive match tables, never constructed); RedeliveryErrorKind::{DuplicateDelivery,ContentInvalid,ConsumerPanic} (classify_processing_error, redelivery_decision.rs:99-172, never yields them -- the module carries an explicit `#[allow(dead_code, reason = "Policy table intentionally names categories the current caller can only classify via tests or future typed assembler outcomes")]`, an in-code admission of the shape). The AdmissionRejectionKind -> label mapping is written out THREE times: outcome_code() (admission.rs:285-306), record_admission_rejection (prepare.rs:352-371), record_admission_suppression (prepare.rs:399-418) -- outcome_code() exists for exactly this purpose and is used by neither.

F10 -- DLQ dedup collapses distinct per-event failures within one intent. dlq.rs:38-56 derives the DLQ Nats-Msg-Id as dlq.{events[0].id} for an envelope. With dupeWindow=1h on SINEX_RAW_EVENTS_DLQ, an intent whose events #2 and #5 fail for different reasons produces two publishes with identical msg-id; the second is silently deduped and its distinct error text lost. Envelope payload preserved either way -- diagnostic loss, not data loss. Related to sinex-3kqx's dedup-window mechanism, different consequence (diagnostic loss vs message loss).

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. F8: compare prepare.rs:11-20/:657-692's #[cfg(test)] copies against admission.rs:1578-1587/:1541-1576's real implementations -- find the already-diverged .with_operation() string as one concrete example.
2. F9: grep each named variant across the workspace -- confirm zero production constructors for AdmissionDecision::{Transformed,QuarantineNeeded}, AdmissionRejectionKind::{PrivacyPolicy,QuarantinePolicy}, RedeliveryErrorKind::{DuplicateDelivery,ContentInvalid,ConsumerPanic}.
3. F10: construct an intent with 2+ events that each fail admission for different reasons -- observe dlq.rs's msg-id derivation from events[0].id causes the second failure's distinct DLQ publish to be deduped within the 1h window, losing its diagnostic text.
acceptance_criteria: F8: tests exercise the real production functions instead of #[cfg(test)] duplicates, or the duplicates are removed. F9: either wire real constructors for the named variants where the capability is wanted, or remove the unreachable variants; consolidate the triplicated AdmissionRejectionKind label mapping to use the existing outcome_code(). F10: DLQ msg-id derivation includes a per-event discriminator (not just the intent's first event id) so distinct per-event failures within one intent don't collide in the dedup window.

title: is_isolatable_batch_persistence_failure exists as two independent copies (admission.rs + jetstream_consumer/persistence_support.rs) that have already drifted; the dead admission.rs copy is stale, and both couple to a sinex-db error message via string-contains prose matching
description:
is_isolatable_batch_persistence_failure exists as two full independent copies of the failure-classification vocabulary, and they've already drifted -- a "same value independently re-resolved in 2+ places" instance where the drift already happened, not just a risk.

Two full copies: admission.rs:46-54 + 1593-1685 (private helpers + public wrappers at :1327,:1336,:1344) and jetstream_consumer/persistence_support.rs:16-104. persistence_support.rs:21 handles SQLSTATE_PROGRAM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CLASS = "54" (too_many_arguments -> bisect); admission.rs:1674-1677 does NOT. AdmissionService::is_isolatable_persistence_failure and is_source_material_fk_violation_for_admitted_batch have ZERO callers anywhere in the tree -- dead code that has already diverged from the live copy.

NON_LIVE_DERIVED_PARENT_ERROR_FRAGMENT is declared identically in both (admission.rs:54, persistence_support.rs:26) with the producing site in a THIRD crate (sinex-db/src/repositories/events/persistence/validation.rs:169) sharing no constant -- the coupling is a to_string().contains() on prose. Reword that error message and isolatable poison rows stop being bisected, NAK-looping the whole batch instead.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Compare admission.rs:1593-1685 against persistence_support.rs:16-104 -- confirm persistence_support.rs handles SQLSTATE class '54' (too_many_arguments) and admission.rs does not.
2. grep -rn 'AdmissionService::is_isolatable_persistence_failure\|is_source_material_fk_violation_for_admitted_batch' crate/ -- confirm zero callers (dead, already-drifted duplicate).
3. grep -rn 'NON_LIVE_DERIVED_PARENT_ERROR_FRAGMENT' crate/ -- confirm the same literal is independently declared in two crates, coupled only via .to_string().contains() on the producing error message in a third file (sinex-db/.../validation.rs:169).
acceptance_criteria: Remove the dead admission.rs copy (zero callers, already-diverged) and keep persistence_support.rs as the single source of truth, OR unify into one shared function if admission.rs's callers actually need it. NON_LIVE_DERIVED_PARENT_ERROR_FRAGMENT's string-matching coupling to the producing error message should get a stronger typed carrier (a distinguishable error variant/code) rather than prose matching, per this project's doctrine against making prose load-bearing for machines.

title: row-level deterministic validation errors (missing ts_orig, claim_support serialization failure) aren't classified isolatable, so one bad event NAK-loops and DLQs its whole batch including healthy siblings
description:
Row-level deterministic validation errors are not classified as isolatable, so one bad event DLQs its WHOLE batch including healthy siblings.

admitted_to_stream_rows can return SinexError::validation for "validated event missing ts_orig" (admission.rs:1504-1509) or "failed to serialize event claim_support" (:1494-1498). Neither carries a sqlstate, and is_isolatable_batch_persistence_failure only treats a Validation error as isolatable when its text contains "non-live source_event_ids" (persistence_support.rs:78-84). So these fall to the generic terminal path (persist.rs:432-578) with NO bisection: every message in the batch NAKs until delivered >= 10, then all of them DLQ -- including healthy siblings.

The missing-ts_orig case is reachable: prepare.rs:207-214 logs "registry row missing after readiness gate" and `continue`s, leaving ts_orig = None rather than failing the event.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger prepare.rs:207-214's 'registry row missing after readiness gate' continue path, leaving ts_orig=None on an event.
2. Let that batch reach admitted_to_stream_rows -- observe the 'validated event missing ts_orig' Validation error (admission.rs:1504-1509) fails is_isolatable_batch_persistence_failure's text-match check (only 'non-live source_event_ids' qualifies), so the whole batch NAKs to delivered>=10 and DLQs together, including unrelated healthy events.
acceptance_criteria: The two named row-level deterministic validation error shapes (missing ts_orig, claim_support serialization failure) are added to the isolatable-failure classification so bisection can isolate just the poison row rather than DLQing the whole batch.

title: CommitFrontier::restore resets next_ticket to 0, risking a stale receipt matching a different in-flight atom -- currently latent since restore() has zero production callers; also TerminalOutcome and EmissionReceiptState are two parallel vocabularies for one concept
description:
CommitFrontier::restore resets the ticket sequence to 0, which can collide with pre-crash tickets and cause a stale/redelivered receipt to be matched against a DIFFERENT still-in-flight atom -- but the affected methods have zero production callers, so this is currently LATENT, not live.

commit_frontier.rs:149-156 restores committed_count but sets next_ticket: 0. Post-restore submit() hands out AtomTicket(0),(1),... colliding with pre-crash tickets. complete() (commit_frontier.rs:182-192) matches purely on ticket equality and documents that an unknown ticket is a silent no-op.

Failure mode (if this code path were ever used): after restore, a late/redelivered receipt carrying pre-crash AtomTicket(0) matches a DIFFERENT still-in-flight atom, marks it terminal with a stale checkpoint payload, advance() folds it in -> frontier commits a checkpoint for work that never completed. A durability hole in the primitive built to close durability holes.

SEVERITY IS LATENT, NOT LIVE: CommitFrontier::restore, .holes(), .is_fully_committed() have ZERO callers outside the module. Both production users construct a FRESH frontier per batch/scan (process.rs:564, crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:1340) and read only .frontier().0 -- restore() is never actually invoked in production.

Related: only TerminalOutcome::PersistedConfirmed is ever constructed; SuppressedWithEvidence/DurableDebt/NoOutputSettled/SpoolAcceptedLossless have zero constructors workspace-wide -- a PARALLEL EmissionReceiptState enum in crate/sinexd/src/runtime/durable_emission.rs carries those states instead. Two vocabularies for one concept.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. grep -rn 'CommitFrontier::restore\|\.restore(' crate/ -- confirm zero production callers (only test usage).
2. Read commit_frontier.rs:149-156 -- confirm next_ticket resets to 0 on restore while committed_count is preserved, and complete() (:182-192) matches purely on ticket equality with no cross-restore epoch/generation marker.
acceptance_criteria: If/when CommitFrontier::restore gains a real production caller, next_ticket must be restored from (or made disjoint from) the pre-crash sequence, e.g. via a monotonic epoch/generation prefix on AtomTicket, before it's trusted for durability. Separately, consider whether TerminalOutcome and durable_emission.rs's EmissionReceiptState should be unified into one vocabulary rather than maintained as two parallel enums for the same concept -- no urgency pre-wipe since restore() is unused, but flag for whoever eventually wires it.

title: the global AdmissionPolicy's five behavior fields (schema_validation/occurrence/malformed_material/resource_pressure/proposal_routing) have zero readers, and the declared malformed_material:Quarantine doesn't even match the real engine's actual DLQ behavior

admission_policy.rs:114-155 inventory::submit!s the one and only AdmissionPolicy declaring schema_validation: AllowPayloadInventoryLookup, occurrence: AllowSourceContractIdentity, malformed_material: Quarantine, resource_pressure: DeferAndSurfaceDebt, proposal_routing: None.

The real engine (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/admission.rs) routes independently -- per CLAUDE.md the actual schema-failure behavior is DLQ, while the declared policy says Quarantine, i.e. the declared policy doesn't even match the real behavior.

Only real consumers of the registry are membership checks (crate/sinexd/src/sources/package_completeness.rs:1230) and tests.

Module docstring claims "They are not a hidden policy engine: suppression, sampling, quarantine, and deferral are explicit outcomes with policy ids" -- they are currently NOT outcomes at all, just unread struct fields.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

2. Compare admission_policy.rs's declared malformed_material: Quarantine against event_engine/admission.rs's actual behavior for a malformed material (DLQ, per CLAUDE.md) -- confirm they diverge.
