title: projection.rs's freshness_class parse fallback silently downgrades a corrupt/unparseable value to Manual (disables staleness reporting) instead of failing loud like its sibling status field does
description:
A silent policy downgrade at a read boundary: an unparseable freshness_class on a projection row silently becomes Manual, which DISABLES staleness reporting entirely -- the wrong-direction fallback for a corrupted/renamed value.

crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/projection.rs:73-80:
    status: record.status.parse::<ProjectionStatus>().unwrap_or(ProjectionStatus::Failed),
    freshness_class: record.freshness_class.parse::<ProjectionFreshnessClass>().unwrap_or(ProjectionFreshnessClass::Manual),

The status fallback to Failed is the CORRECT fail-loud direction. The freshness_class fallback to Manual is the OPPOSITE: derivation.rs:641-644 defines Manual as "no automatic staleness expectation" -- so a corrupt/renamed freshness_class value silently DISABLES staleness reporting for that projection rather than surfacing the corruption.

Separately: crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/projection_registry.rs writes status as raw SQL string literals (SET status = 'stale', lines 193, 226) rather than through ProjectionStatus::as_str() -- only Building/Absent are inserted via the typed path (lines 77, 85). The enum is authoritative on read but not consistently used on write.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Corrupt or rename a projection row's freshness_class column value so it no longer parses as a valid ProjectionFreshnessClass.
2. Read the projection via projection.rs:73-80 -- observe it silently reports freshness_class: Manual (staleness reporting disabled) rather than surfacing the parse failure, unlike the status field's fallback to Failed (a fail-loud direction).
acceptance_criteria: freshness_class's unparseable fallback is changed to a fail-loud value (or the parse error is surfaced/logged) rather than silently disabling staleness reporting. Separately, projection_registry.rs's raw SQL string-literal status writes are migrated to use ProjectionStatus::as_str() consistently.

title: ObservedRange::union always takes the first operand's basis and the loosest quality, causing Sequence windows to report basis=AtemporalAnchor/quality=Unknown alongside precise start/end timestamps
description:
ObservedRange::union latches the LEFT operand's basis and the LOOSEST quality forever, producing evidence windows that claim 'no usable time information' while displaying precise start/end timestamps.

relations.rs:199-207: `basis: self.basis` taken unconditionally -> union is asymmetric, first basis wins over all later ones. looser_quality (relations.rs:222-232) ranks Unknown loosest -> absorbing.

Concrete consequence, relations.rs:626: `let mut union_range = ObservedRange::unknown(TimeBasis::AtemporalAnchor);` -- so EVERY Sequence window reports observed_range.basis == AtemporalAnchor and quality == Unknown even when every member is RealtimeCapture/Exact, while start/end carry real exact endpoints. The window simultaneously says "no usable time information" and shows a precise interval.

Same latch on the non-sequence path (relations.rs:482-486): one untimed seed in position 0 poisons quality for the whole window.

relations_test.rs asserts from_event quality mapping (51-77) and overlaps (85-94) but NEVER asserts the resulting EvidenceWindow.observed_range basis/quality -- exactly the gap. Reused at query.rs:301-305 but only start/end consumed there -> harmless on that specific path.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/{derivation,derivations,relations,settlement,commit_frontier,admission_policy,domain,event_contracts,non_empty,ids,constants,activity,temporal,domain_reducer}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Construct a Sequence evidence window from events that all have RealtimeCapture/Exact time basis.
2. Read the resulting EvidenceWindow.observed_range -- observe basis == AtemporalAnchor and quality == Unknown (from the seed at relations.rs:626), despite start/end carrying real precise timestamps.
3. Read relations_test.rs -- confirm no test asserts observed_range.basis/quality on the resulting window.
acceptance_criteria: ObservedRange::union computes basis/quality from the actual set of member ranges (e.g. tightest/most-precise basis when all members agree, or an honest mixed/uncertain classification) rather than always inheriting the left operand and the loosest quality. A new relations_test.rs case asserts observed_range.basis/quality on a Sequence window built from precisely-timed events.

title: batch_importer's Appended/Replaced change-kind detection misclassifies same-ms appends as full replacements (duplication risk), and both batch_importer.rs and file_tailer.rs are complete but currently unwired to any live source
description:
batch_importer::detect_change_kind misclassifies same-millisecond file appends as full replacements (would duplicate content on re-import), AND this entire file-scanning/fingerprint subsystem is currently dead code, unwired to any live source.

crate/sinexd/src/runtime/batch_importer.rs:220-240. The Appended branch requires current.modified_unix_ms != previous.fingerprint.modified_unix_ms in addition to size growth. A file that grows but keeps the same millisecond-resolution mtime (1s-resolution filesystems, or two writes in the same ms) falls through to Replaced, which sets start_offset_bytes=0 (batch_importer.rs:200-207) -- full re-read/re-emit of the whole file, duplicating already-imported content.

However: grepped the whole crate -- scan_for_new_files/BatchImporterState/discover_importable_files_at_root (input_shapes.rs:62-69) have NO caller anywhere outside their own module + input_shapes.rs wrapper + tests. This whole file-scanning/fingerprint subsystem is currently unwired to any live source.

Related dead code in the same audit: file_tailer.rs (all 242 lines) -- its inode rotation/truncation detection and UTF-8-boundary-safe line splitting look CORRECT (on InvalidUtf8 it returns Err before committing state.offset_bytes, so a poison byte sequence blocks progress rather than corrupting the offset), but poll_utf8_lines/AppendOnlyFileState have zero callers anywhere in the crate outside file_tailer.rs itself + the runtime/mod.rs re-export. No source driver uses it, no dedicated unit tests. Flagging alongside batch_importer since both are complete, individually-tested capabilities sitting unused going into the pre-wipe rebuild.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/runtime/{acquisition_manager,source_driver,sqlite_source,watcher_handle,supervised_watcher,file_tailer,batch_importer,ingestion_helpers,scan_progress}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Simulate a file growing (size increase) with an unchanged millisecond-resolution mtime (e.g. two writes within the same ms, or a 1s-resolution filesystem).
2. Read detect_change_kind (batch_importer.rs:220-240) -- confirm it falls through to Replaced (start_offset_bytes=0) rather than Appended, since it requires BOTH size growth AND an mtime change.
3. grep -rn 'scan_for_new_files\|BatchImporterState\|discover_importable_files_at_root\|poll_utf8_lines\|AppendOnlyFileState' crate/ -- confirm zero callers outside each module's own file + tests.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: either (a) both subsystems get wired to a real source and the misclassification bug is fixed as part of that (loosen the Appended condition to size-growth-only, or use a stronger identity signal than mtime), or (b) if neither is planned for near-term use, they're explicitly tracked as intentionally-dormant capability per CLAUDE.md's unfinished-is-not-obsolete doctrine rather than silently bitrotting.

title: append_record_batch has no rollback for a mid-batch chunk-publish failure spanning multiple 256KiB chunks -- a hypothetical whole-batch retry would duplicate already-succeeded chunks (exposure unconfirmed)
description:

title: Hyprland workspace-switch actuator idempotency guard has a TOCTOU window: two near-simultaneous requests with the same idempotency_key both dispatch
description:
active_hyprland_workspace_instruction (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/instructions.rs:266-315), the actuator idempotency guard, has a genuine TOCTOU window that lets two near-simultaneous requests with the same idempotency_key both physically dispatch.

The guard only matches an ALREADY-ATTEMPTED prior instruction (requires an actuation.attempted event with status='attempted' to exist for the other instruction). In handle_hyprland_workspace_switch (instructions.rs:60-187), the new instruction event is persisted at line 80 BEFORE the duplicate check (line 98), but the corresponding attempt event is only persisted at the end via persist_attempt (lines 173-235). Two near-simultaneous requests with the same idempotency_key both pass the duplicate check (neither's attempt row exists yet when the other checks) and both physically dispatch the workspace switch.

Severity likely low given this is a single-operator actuator plane (Hyprland workspace switching), but it's a genuine hole in a guard whose entire purpose is preventing exactly this scenario.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/{dlq,privacy,lifecycle,sources,replay,instructions,browser,query}.rs (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Fire two handle_hyprland_workspace_switch requests with the same idempotency_key at nearly the same instant (before either's persist_attempt has landed).
2. Observe both pass the duplicate check at instructions.rs:98 (since neither's attempted-status attempt event exists yet) and both physically dispatch the workspace switch.
acceptance_criteria: The duplicate check and instruction-event persistence are made atomic (e.g. an early attempt-placeholder row inserted before dispatch, or a DB-level unique constraint on idempotency_key+attempted status checked transactionally) so two concurrent requests with the same key cannot both dispatch.

title: ops.start's media worker_command allows arbitrary program execution at Write role (lower tier than ops.cancel's Admin), and email sync accepts operator-supplied local file paths with no restriction
description:
Two residual-risk items noted during the ops/{email,media,package}.rs audit, not confirmed as live bugs but worth an operator confirmation pass:

Role-tier asymmetry: ops.start is RpcRole::Write, ops.cancel is RpcRole::Admin, but ops.start's media_capture worker_command (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops/media.rs:531-696) runs Command::new(&request.program).args(...) -- arbitrary program execution as the sinexd service user, gated only by non-empty/arg-count checks, no allowlist. title: Event.anchor_payload_hash doc comment claims 'mismatch -> DLQ' on replay but actual behavior is log-only warning (deliberate, tested, just undocumented)
description:
The doc comment on `Event.anchor_payload_hash` (crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/mod.rs:93-94) is factually wrong about current behavior. It reads: "BLAKE3 hash of source-material byte range (material events only)... Verified on replay — mismatch → DLQ."

Actual behavior in crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/execution/replay_writer.rs:193-225: on a hash mismatch between the archived (old) and replayed (new) event at the same material occurrence, the code only `warn!()`-logs and increments a local `integrity_mismatch_count` that is never propagated anywhere else (confirmed via grep — its only reads are the log line itself). The replacement record is still pushed unconditionally right after the mismatch check — no continue/return/error path, no DLQ routing.

This is deliberate and tested, not an oversight in the implementation: crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/tests/execution_outcome.rs:661-746, test `replay_anchor_payload_hash_mismatch_does_not_block_replacement`, explicitly asserts the replacement IS recorded despite the mismatch. So the bug is entirely in the doc comment: it claims a corruption-detection guarantee ("mismatch → DLQ") on the single most safety-critical type in the codebase, that was either never implemented or was implemented and then deliberately weakened to a log-only warning without updating the comment. Source-material byte-range corruption/tampering is exactly what anchor_payload_hash exists to catch — a reader trusting the doc comment would believe there's an enforced integrity gate on replay that doesn't actually exist.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src/events/ (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read mod.rs:93-94's doc comment claiming mismatch->DLQ.
2. Read replay_writer.rs:193-225 — confirm mismatch only logs+counts, replacement still pushed unconditionally.
3. Read execution_outcome.rs:661-746's test — confirm it explicitly asserts this log-only behavior is intentional, not a bug being masked.

## Acceptance
- Decision recorded: either (a) update the doc comment to reflect log-only advisory status and explain why DLQ-blocking was not chosen (defense-in-depth tradeoff, false-positive risk, etc.), or (b) if DLQ-blocking was actually the intended guarantee, wire integrity_mismatch_count to something enforceable (reject the replay, or route to DLQ) and update the test accordingly.
- Given this is a pre-wipe audit and the doc claims a corruption-detection guarantee that doesn't exist, prefer option (a) as the minimum fix unless there's a concrete reason DLQ-blocking is now wanted.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above.

title: error_retryability_tests.rs's three tests are tautological (check accessors against their own one-line definitions, never verify actual classification correctness)
description:
All three tests in crate/sinex-primitives/src/error_retryability_tests.rs:56-91 are tautological and verify nothing about actual correctness.

`SinexError::is_retryable()` is *defined* as `self.error_class() == ErrorClass::TransientInfra` (error.rs:806-808), and `is_permanent()` as `== ErrorClass::RuntimeFatal` (error.rs:819-822). The three tests (`is_retryable_agrees_with_error_class`, `is_permanent_agrees_with_error_class`, `retryable_and_permanent_are_mutually_exclusive`) each compute `class = err.error_class()` then assert `err.is_retryable() == (class == TransientInfra)` etc. — checking a function's output against its own literal one-line definition. These tests cannot fail without directly editing the two accessor bodies to diverge from their own definitions, and provide zero evidence that `error_class()`'s actual classification (the real judgment call — e.g. ChannelSend -> RuntimeFatal, Database -> TransientInfra) is correct for any given error variant. This matches CLAUDE.md's named anti-pattern of tests that "merely memorialize a refactoring diff" rather than verifying independently valuable behavior.

Related, lower-confidence observation surfaced while reviewing the classification itself (not chased further, flagging for awareness): `SinexError::ChannelReceive` (built from tokio::sync::oneshot::RecvError, meaning the sender was dropped) is classified TransientInfra (error.rs:327) and therefore retried up to 10x over 5 minutes by DefaultFailurePolicy (settlement.rs:177-201) before escalating — but a dropped oneshot sender is a permanent condition (the other side is gone), not transient; retrying can never succeed. Not a correctness bug given the bounded retry budget and eventual HaltModule escalation, just wasted retry cycles / delayed escalation.

Found via exhaustive regional audit of crate/sinex-primitives/src loose top-level files (2026-08-11).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read error.rs:806-808,819-822 — is_retryable/is_permanent are one-line accessors of error_class().
2. Read error_retryability_tests.rs:56-91 — each test recomputes error_class() and asserts the accessor matches it, i.e. compares the definition to itself.
3. Confirm no test in this file (or elsewhere in the crate) asserts that a SPECIFIC SinexError variant maps to a SPECIFIC, deliberately-chosen ErrorClass (the actual judgment call these accessors exist to gate retry/DLQ/halt behavior on).

## Acceptance
- Replace or supplement these tests with ones that assert specific variant -> ErrorClass mappings for the variants that matter operationally (at minimum: the TransientInfra/RuntimeFatal boundary cases, including a look at whether ChannelReceive's TransientInfra classification is actually correct given the noted concern above).
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance above.

title: sinexctl source_status client-side re-filters using a duplicated copy of the server's family-match logic (drift risk, currently inert)
description:

title: SinexEnvironment's isolation validator is never called and structurally cannot fail on its own hard checks, AND its Default impl bypasses the deliberate release-build environment gate as a latent trap for any future #[derive(Default)] usage
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via a fallible-validation-discarded audit. Two related findings in SinexEnvironment (crate/sinex-primitives/src/environment.rs), the type governing database/NATS/filesystem namespace isolation between environments (dev/prod/etc):

1. validate_isolation() is never called anywhere in the repo (confirmed via exhaustive grep -- zero references outside its own definition), AND it is structurally incapable of failing on its own hard checks even if it WERE called. Its two return-Err branches compare self.socket_path("/tmp/sinex-host.sock") and self.work_directory("/tmp/sinex") against self.name -- but work_directory unconditionally appends "-{name}" and socket_path namespaces the parent, so the substring check ALWAYS succeeds by construction. The one substantive check it performs (DATABASE_URL namespacing) is itself downgraded to a warn! inside the function rather than propagating as an error. This is the purest instance of the mechanisms-built-then-discarded pattern found this session: a validator that is neither wired to a caller NOR capable of catching the thing it was written to catch.

2. impl Default for SinexEnvironment bypasses the deliberate release-build environment gate. SinexEnvironment::current() is a real hard gate: an unset SINEX_ENVIRONMENT in a release build returns Err, gated on allow_default_environment()=cfg!(debug_assertions)||cfg!(test) -- and the global accessor environment() correctly PANICS unless that guard passes. But the Default impl calls Self::current().unwrap_or_else(|error| { warn!(...); Self{name:"dev"} }) with NO allow_default_environment() guard at all. Since environment name drives database_name(), nats_subject(), nats_stream_name(), socket_path(), and work_directory(), a prod binary silently resolving to "dev" via this path would write to the wrong database and the wrong NATS stream namespace -- exactly the isolation failure finding 1's dead validator was written to catch. HONEST SEVERITY QUALIFIER: no production reachability path was found -- SinexEnvironment::default() currently appears only in one test file, and no #[derive(Default)] struct anywhere holds a SinexEnvironment field (checked every struct with such a field). This is a LATENT TRAP, not a live bug today: any FUTURE #[derive(Default)] on a struct holding this type, or any unwrap_or_default() on a Result<SinexEnvironment>, would silently defeat the release gate with no compile error to catch it."
acceptance_criteria: Either wire validate_isolation() to a real caller (startup, or a test) and fix its always-true substring checks so it can actually detect a namespace collision, or remove it if genuinely superseded by something else. Route the Default impl through the same allow_default_environment() guard current() already correctly uses, so a future accidental Default-derive on a holder struct can't silently defeat the release-build environment gate.

title: no sinex systemd unit orders after time-sync.target -- a wrong boot-time RTC (dead CMOS, restored snapshot, long power-off) could write UUIDv7-partitioned events into already-closed chunks once the clock steps, the same failure neighborhood as the #2182 mega-chunk incident
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via temporal/presentation-robustness audit. No sinex systemd unit orders after time-sync.target -- grepped the whole tree, the only hit is a doc-comment line advising "use NTP/chrony for time synchronization on capture hosts", advice not enforcement. The live host runs systemd-timesyncd (chronyd inactive) and does not enable systemd-time-wait-sync.service, so time-sync.target is reached without an actual verified sync having completed.

Consequence if the RTC is materially wrong at boot (dead CMOS battery, a restored snapshot, a long power-off): sinexd starts, mints UUIDv7 event ids and ts_orig from the pre-sync clock, then timesyncd steps the clock afterward. Since core.events is a hypertable PARTITIONED BY UUIDv7 id, a backward step at that point writes new rows into already-closed (possibly already-compressed) chunks -- the same neighborhood as the #2182 mega-chunk/compression-lock incident this project has already been burned by once. On this host today, with a healthy RTC, the boot-time step is sub-second and this is a hardening note rather than an active defect.
acceptance_criteria: Add After=time-sync.target to the sinexd unit and enable systemd-time-wait-sync.service, matching the existing coreAfter dependency-declaration pattern already used for Postgres/NATS readiness gating. One-line hardening fix, low urgency given a healthy RTC on this specific host today, but cheap enough to do proactively given the known #2182 incident class it would prevent recurring in.

title: two wall-clock-keyed timing mechanisms (material rotation/idle-finalize, TTL/checkpoint-cleanup sweeps) have no clock-sanity guard -- low severity, mostly self-healing/bounded, but the checkpoint-cleanup instance (currently unused/inert) has the more severe unbounded-wipe shape and should be fixed before it ever gets wired up
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via temporal/presentation-robustness audit. Two low-severity wall-clock-keyed timing mechanisms with no clock-sanity guard, both bounded/self-healing rather than open-ended risks:

1. Material rotation and idle-finalize timing (acquisition_manager.rs) compute a monotonic tokio::time::sleep deadline FROM a wall-clock-measured elapsed duration. A backward wall-clock step during that computation makes the "remaining duration" calculation return the full max-age again, re-arming for another full rotation interval -- a material could stay open up to 2x its intended max-age before rotating. Still bounded by the separate 100 MiB byte-size cap, so not unbounded. A forward step causes immediate finalize -- benign, that's the intended rotation behavior firing early. Also noted: a latent semantic mismatch where one helper computes a "remaining" duration and passes it to a function that compares against "age" -- works today only because the two happen to coincide at exactly the boundary condition, fragile but not currently wrong.

2. lifecycle_ttl.rs's TTL sweep selects on ts_orig < (NOW() - interval) with no clock-sanity guard -- a large forward DB-clock step would over-archive, but blast radius is bounded by a per-sweep batch limit and by archiving (not deleting) so it's recoverable. cleanup_stale_checkpoints has the more severe version of this pattern (a forward step could wipe every automaton checkpoint, forcing a full replay) but is CURRENTLY INERT -- opt-in via an env var with no production caller anywhere, confirmed via grep (only a re-export and a doc comment reference it outside the module itself). Per "unfinished is not obsolete," this reads as half-wired rather than dead code -- flagging the clock dependency now, before anyone wires it up, rather than after.

Cosmetic sibling already covered by an existing bead: core.operations_log.duration_ms computed via NOW() - id-embedded-timestamp can go negative on a backward clock step -- same overflow-adjacent column already tracked in sinex-oq7j, not filed separately here.
acceptance_criteria: Store a monotonic Instant alongside the wall-clock started_at for material rotation timing (the wall-clock value is still needed as provenance, so this is additive not a replacement). Add a clock-sanity bound to cleanup_stale_checkpoints before it's ever wired to a production caller, given a forward clock step could otherwise wipe every automaton checkpoint and force a full replay the moment this currently-inert mechanism gets activated.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No clock-sanity-guard test found for material rotation/idle-finalize or TTL/checkpoint-cleanup timing. Testable via a clock-skew/mock-clock test even though the bead itself frames both as low-severity/self-healing.

title: TUI has no panic hook to restore terminal state (a panic leaves the operator's terminal in raw mode + alt screen requiring manual reset), and unconditionally enables mouse capture that's never read, disabling native text selection for zero benefit -- compounds the already-dead in-app copy action (sinex-rfbl)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via temporal/presentation-robustness audit. Truecolor is verified a non-issue (zero RGB/indexed colors used anywhere in the CLI, only 5 basic ANSI colors -- degrades fine on any 16-color terminal, explicitly NOT a finding). Unicode glyph fallback is a small, low-priority exposure (11 non-ASCII symbols total plus default box-drawing, mojibake only on a non-UTF-8 locale).

Two real findings:

1. NO PANIC HOOK RESTORES THE TERMINAL. No panic::set_hook/catch_unwind exists anywhere in the CLI. The error-reporting hook that IS installed does not disable raw mode or leave the alternate screen. Any panic inside the TUI's render loop leaves the operator's terminal in raw mode + alternate screen with a hidden cursor, requiring a manual 'reset' command to recover. Layout arithmetic itself is safe (verified: all Rect/index arithmetic uses saturating_sub, cannot itself panic) -- but this codebase has a confirmed history of render-path panics elsewhere (the closed sinex-audit-cli-utf8-panic bead), so the exposure is latent rather than proven-unreachable.

2. MOUSE CAPTURE IS ENABLED UNCONDITIONALLY BUT NEVER READ. The TUI enables mouse capture at startup, but the event loop only ever matches keyboard events -- mouse events are read and silently discarded. Net effect: native terminal text selection/copy is DISABLED inside the TUI for zero functional benefit. This compounds the already-filed sinex-rfbl finding 1 (the TUI's own in-app 'copy raw JSON' action is permanently dead because recent_event_rows is never assigned) -- together, the operator can neither copy content via the app's own action NOR via native mouse selection.
acceptance_criteria: Install a panic hook (or catch_unwind around the render loop) that disables raw mode and leaves the alternate screen before any panic message prints, matching standard ratatui-app practice. Either read and act on mouse events for something useful, or disable mouse capture so native terminal text selection works -- given sinex-rfbl already found the in-app copy action is dead, restoring native mouse selection is the more immediately useful fix of the two.

title: curation judgment actor_id is client-controlled/unvalidated against the authenticated identity (spoofable audit field), and PrivateModeEnableArgs defaults to the generic literal 'operator' when --actor is omitted
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via deployment/multi-context-robustness audit, while checking for OS-user-based identity misattribution (verified NOT an issue -- audit-trail actor_id is correctly token-derived server-side everywhere else, not sinity-derived). Two smaller, related weak-attribution findings:

1. crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/curation.rs lets the client optionally override actor_id in a judgment request (req.actor_id.unwrap_or_else(|| auth.actor_id().to_string())), UNVALIDATED against the authenticated identity -- a spoofable free-text audit field. Related to but a distinct angle from the already-closed sinex-audit-actorkind ('client-controlled actor_kind self-authorizes curation finalization') -- that bead covers actor_KIND (whether a judgment counts as human-sufficient); this is actor_ID (WHO gets recorded), a separate spoofing surface on the same handler.
2. PrivateModeEnableArgs::actor (crate/sinexctl/src/commands/privacy.rs) defaults to the generic literal 'operator' if --actor isn't passed -- weak, not wrong, but means the audit trail can't distinguish who actually flipped private mode unless the caller remembers to pass the flag explicitly.

Consider deriving PrivateModeEnableArgs' actor default from the authenticated caller identity rather than a generic literal, matching the pattern the rest of the audit-trail system already correctly uses.

title: LOW-MEDIUM: assembler WAL and staged material file have independent, mismatched fsync policies -- a power loss (not SIGKILL) resolves the divergence by discarding the whole material rather than truncating to the last durable point
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via crash-only-design audit (Opus). crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/material_assembler/durability.rs:13-17: the WAL syncs every 256KiB/128 entries/1s; the staged file syncs every 1MiB/1s -- independent cadences. Per-entry the WAL only gets file.flush() (durability.rs:252-256), correct/sufficient for SIGKILL (bytes reach the page cache, syscall completes) but NOT for a machine crash or power cut, after which the two artifacts are near-certainly at different durable points. reconcile_replayed_file_progress (material_assembler/io.rs:608-678) accepts exactly two legal sizes and otherwise returns invalid_state, routing to RestoreDiscardReason::FileProgressMismatch -> Discard{cleanup_state:true} (restore_plan.rs:229-239) -- the already-durable prefix is DELETED rather than truncated back to the last verifiably-committed offset, even though the frames that built that prefix were already ACKed off the WorkQueue stream (so re-requesting them isn't free/guaranteed either).

Outcome is still WELL-DEFINED (the orphaned-Sensing reconciler, material_assembler/maintenance.rs, settles the material terminally rather than leaving it ambiguous) -- this is a fidelity/robustness gap, not an ambiguity gap. Notable by contrast: event_transport.rs in the SAME repo does full fsync-plus-parent-dir-fsync discipline for the recovery spool (a red-team finding on r6d.5) -- the two durability tiers within material handling are not documented as intentionally different, and this one is weaker.
acceptance_criteria: Either align the assembler WAL/staged-file fsync cadences so their divergence window after a real power loss is bounded and small, or make reconcile_replayed_file_progress tolerant of a partial staged-file write by truncating to the last WAL-confirmed offset instead of discarding the whole accumulated material. Given this only manifests on genuine power loss (not the more common SIGKILL/OOM case), reasonable to prioritize below F1/F2 from the same audit.

title: Strategy::Encrypt privacy redaction is completely dormant -- no key provisioned anywhere in the deployment, doc comment overpromises a capability that doesn't function today
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via host-level security audit. Strategy::Encrypt (crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/mod.rs:143-145, XChaCha20-Poly1305, documented 'reversible with the correct key') has NO key provisioned anywhere in the sinnix deployment: KeyConfig::resolve() tries SINEX_PRIVACY_KEY_FILE then SINEX_PRIVACY_KEY (hex, doc-commented 'development only'), neither is set anywhere in nixos/modules/*.nix (grep confirms zero hits), and cross-checked live on the sinnix deployment side: /realm/project/sinnix/modules/secrets.nix has zero privacy-key references, and the live agenix secrets directory (/realm/data/secrets/sinnix/secret/) confirms only sinex-api-admin-token.age and sinex-local-db.age exist -- no sinex-privacy-key.age. Confirmed no builtin catalog rule even uses Strategy::Encrypt (every one of catalog.rs's ~34 rules uses Redact/Suppress/Hash only), and the strategy-selection env vars are also unset, so the compiled default (Redact) governs everywhere.

GOOD NEWS, verified: the fail-safe behavior when no key is configured is correctly designed -- engine.rs's Strategy::Encrypt handling silently degrades to a plain redaction label when self.key is None, it does NOT fall back to storing plaintext or a broken/empty ciphertext. So dormancy is not itself a leak -- if anything it's MORE protective than a working-but-misconfigured Encrypt would be. The architecture for when it IS eventually wired is also sound: privacy.encryption_keys is explicitly a namespace-registry-only table (key material never lives in the DB), and every other sinex secret (DB password, API token) already goes through agenix -> /run/agenix -- if a privacy key were provisioned the same way it genuinely would not travel with a stolen Postgres data directory or backup.

Two real, actionable issues: (1) the doc comment ('Reversible with the correct key') overpromises a capability that currently does nothing in the deployed system -- worth a doc correction so an operator configuring a rule with Strategy::Encrypt doesn't believe they're getting real encryption when they're silently getting Redact instead. (2) FORWARD-LOOKING RISK: if this is ever enabled by setting SINEX_PRIVACY_KEY directly in a systemd Environment= line (the 'development only' hex-env path) rather than SINEX_PRIVACY_KEY_FILE + agenix, that key becomes visible via /proc/<pid>/environ and the unit file/journal -- the same class of leak already flagged for the DB password in sinex-9a8u.
acceptance_criteria: Either wire a real privacy encryption key through agenix (matching the DB/API-token precedent) if Encrypt is meant to be a real, usable strategy, or update the doc comment to clarify it silently degrades to Redact when unconfigured so operators aren't misled. If wired, document/enforce that SINEX_PRIVACY_KEY (the raw hex env var) is genuinely dev-only and never used in the systemd unit's Environment= directly.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] The fail-safe degrade-to-Redact-when-no-key behavior is testable (bead itself notes this is already verified correct). The doc-comment overpromise fix and the forward-looking Environment=-exposure risk are not test-shaped -- one is a doc edit, the other is a future-misconfiguration warning with nothing to assert against today.

title: no cross-source content dedup/fingerprinting exists -- the same URL/content captured via bookmark, browser history, chat message, and document all produce fully independent, unlinked events
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via data-lifecycle-stewardship audit. Checked every hashing/fingerprint mechanism: payload_content_hash() (BLAKE3 over canonicalized JSON) is used only by admission's SupersedeOnChange to detect a revision of the SAME occurrence_key, not cross-source semantic linking; CAS/blob hashing is byte-identical-file dedup (different problem).

The one plausible cross-source linking primitive is the entity graph, and it fails this scenario on two independent grounds: (1) INPUT SCOPE -- EntityExtractor::input_event_types() is hardcoded to only [document.chunked, command.canonical, command.executed]. bookmark.created, page.visited, message.sent, and social.* event types NEVER reach the entity extractor at all -- a URL saved as a bookmark, visited in browser history, or shared in chat is never entity-extracted unless the identical text ALSO happens to appear inside a document or shell command. (2) CANONICALIZATION GRANULARITY -- entity_resolver.rs's normalize_url_host strips everything after the host, so https://github.com/user/repo1 and https://github.com/user/repo2 both canonicalize to just 'github.com' -- where the mechanism IS reachable, it links at DOMAIN granularity (over-merging unrelated pages from the same site) rather than page granularity, so it structurally cannot express 'this bookmark and this chat message point at the same specific page' even in the cases it does fire. Additionally find_first_entity() emits only the FIRST matched entity per event, silently dropping others.

Verdict: each capture path produces a fully independent, unlinked event with no way to surface 'you've seen this content N times across N sources' anywhere in query/recall. This is a real capability gap (not a correctness bug -- no data corruption) relative to the cross-provider observation fusion goal already noted in project memory (0eam).
acceptance_criteria: If cross-source content linking is a real product goal, it needs: (a) entity extraction (or an equivalent lighter-weight mechanism) to actually consume the source event types that carry URLs/shareable content -- bookmark.created, page.visited, message.sent, social.*, not just document/command types; (b) page-level (not just host-level) URL canonicalization for linking purposes, distinct from whatever coarser grouping the current host-level canonicalization is used for elsewhere. Scope as a deliberate feature decision, not an urgent fix -- flag for prioritization rather than assuming it should happen before the wipe.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No cross-source dedup mechanism exists yet to test against -- payload_content_hash() only covers same-occurrence revisions, confirmed by the bead's own audit of every hashing mechanism. Partially testable now (assert the absence: same URL via two sources currently produces two undeduped events); the full fingerprinting feature has no design yet to write a complete test against.

title: browser history captures unfiltered redirect-chain hops -- Chromium's transition bitmask and hidden column are read/present in the source data but never filtered, so intermediate redirect URLs are indistinguishable from pages the user actually looked at
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via operator follow-up on browsing-history signal/noise. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/browser/history.rs's parse_chromium_row (:397-441) reads Chromium's transition field as a raw integer and stores it verbatim as a string (transition: Some(transition_raw.to_string())), but nothing filters or interprets the bitmask -- Chromium's transition value packs a core type (LINK/TYPED/AUTO_BOOKMARK/etc, low byte) with qualifier flags (CLIENT_REDIRECT/SERVER_REDIRECT/CHAIN_START/CHAIN_END/FORWARD_BACK, higher bits) that distinguish a genuine user-initiated navigation from an automatic redirect hop. Separately, the Chromium query mode's default (per the comment at :262-264, 'SELECT rowid, * FROM visits JOIN urls ON visits.url = urls.id') doesn't even select urls.hidden -- Chromium's own column for marking auto-generated/non-user-visible entries -- so it isn't available to filter on even if the code wanted to.

Consequence: when a user clicks a link that bounces through a redirector (an email link-tracking redirector, a URL shortener, an SSO/OAuth bounce, an ad-click redirect), each intermediate hop lands in Chromium's visits table as its own row with CLIENT_REDIRECT/SERVER_REDIRECT transition bits set -- sinex captures every one of these as an undifferentiated page-visit entry, identical in shape to a page the user actually read. A browsing-history reconstruction or search built on this data cannot distinguish 'the user looked at this' from 'the user's browser passed through this on the way to somewhere else' -- an accumulating, unbounded source of noise entries with no signal, growing with every redirect-shaped link the user ever clicks.

Note: this replaces an initially-considered-but-wrong idea (sourcing an external tracker/ad-domain blocklist like EasyList/EasyPrivacy for this) -- verified that's the wrong tool, since Chromium's visits/urls tables only record actual navigation events, not subresource/beacon-level network requests, so ad/tracker blocklists (which target that different traffic class) would have almost nothing to match against in browser History specifically. The actual noise source is redirect-chain hops within genuine navigation events, not third-party tracking requests.
acceptance_criteria: Select and expose Chromium's hidden column in the query, and either filter out hidden=1 rows or at minimum surface the transition bitmask's redirect qualifier bits (CLIENT_REDIRECT/SERVER_REDIRECT) as a structured field on the event payload so downstream consumers (search, recall, coverage) can distinguish or collapse redirect-chain hops from genuine page visits rather than treating every row as equally significant.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] No #[ignore]'d red test found for this bead (grep across crate/, xtask/). Bounded, code-level behavior gap -- fully testable in principle (fixture input -> assert current wrong behavior), just not written yet.

title: knowledge_graph find_paths guards only against edge reuse, not node revisits, on a graph whose normal shape is near-complete cliques (50-entity co-occurrence windows) -- asymptotic blowup risk the moment it gets a caller
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (Opus). crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/knowledge_graph.rs:864-890 -- find_paths's recursive CTE terminates only via edge-disjointness (NOT rel.id::uuid = ANY(path.relation_ids)), with no node-visited set, no LIMIT inside the CTE, and the destination filter (WHERE to_entity_id=) applied only AFTER the full frontier materializes (no early termination). The graph this runs on is built from 50-entity co-occurrence windows (relation_extractor.rs MAX_WINDOW_ENTITIES) = 1,225 edges per window close -- i.e. near-complete tournaments/cliques. A node participating in several windows reaches out-degree in the hundreds; at max_depth=5 and out-degree ~200 the CTE would enumerate on the order of 10^11 partial paths -- Postgres will spill and effectively die rather than return, the moment anything calls this function (currently zero callers in the workspace, confirmed by grep -- purely latent today). Separately, since co_occurs_with is emitted only in arrival order (a companion finding on sinex-cel3), traversal following rel.from_entity_id=path.to_entity_id only means find_paths(B,A) can return nothing where find_paths(A,B) succeeds for what is conceptually the same symmetric relationship.
acceptance_criteria: Add a node-visited set (not just edge-disjointness) to find_paths' termination condition, and/or a hard cap on frontier size per iteration, before this function gets its first real caller. Consider whether the destination filter can be pushed earlier (into the recursive term) rather than applied only after full materialization.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: [TDD-audit-v2 2026-08-11] Concrete, testable: knowledge_graph.rs find_paths recursive CTE edge-only-disjointness gap; directly testable now.

title: entity_chain_shadow.rs (the ratified re-entry lane) is not a faithful port of relation_extractor: semantically diverges on co-occurrence definition, has an unremediated instance of the already-closed out-of-order pattern bug, and its 'byte-reproducible' scope hash is positional not content-addressed
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (Opus). crate/sinexd/src/automata/entity_chain_shadow.rs is documented as a 'batched port of relation_extractor::reconcile/drain_and_emit_pairs' -- three distinct gaps found:

1. SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE (arguably the shadow lane is the CORRECT one, ironically): at line 371, window.push(...) sits OUTSIDE the if is_new block (line 323), so the shadow lane's batch window contains every observation including repeats -- real co-occurrence. The LIVE automaton (relation_extractor.rs, see the sinex-cel3 comment filed alongside this bead) only ever sees first-discoveries due to the entity-resolver gate. The same nominal algorithm produces two DIFFERENT measures in the two lanes -- any lane-diff comparing shadow output to live output will report a difference caused by the port itself, not by a genuine lane discrepancy, undermining any future 'shadow lane matches live' validation.

2. UNREMEDIATED SIBLING OF A CLOSED BUG: line 378 is a bare last_seen = Some(now) with no monotonic guard -- precisely the pattern sinex-audit-outoforder-pattern (closed) fixed in relation_extractor.rs:204-215, just never ported to the shadow lane. It matters MORE here: events are read ORDER BY id ASC (line 253 -- UUIDv7, i.e. ts_coided/interpretation-time order) while all window arithmetic uses ts_orig (lines 358-370). On a historical import (a year of notes ingested in minutes -- exactly what the imminent wipe-and-reimport will do), ts_orig is effectively unordered relative to id, so 'now - last' goes negative routinely, gap_triggered fires arbitrarily, and window_started_at can end up LATER than now (a negative age).

3. NON-CONTENT-ADDRESSED FROZEN-SCOPE HASH: the module's own comment claims byte-reproducibility ('same events slice'), but hash_input = '{stream}|{subjects}|{start_seq}|{end_seq}' (line 196-200) is POSITIONAL (an OFFSET/LIMIT pair over ORDER BY id ASC, lines 250-255) -- if replay archives events inside that offset range between runs, the SAME input_set_hash now selects a DIFFERENT set of events (the window slides forward into newer rows). The claim holds only for a truly fixed slice, which offset/limit does not guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Port the monotonic last_seen guard from the already-fixed relation_extractor.rs pattern into entity_chain_shadow.rs. Decide deliberately whether the shadow lane's every-observation window (vs live's first-discovery-only window) is the intended semantics going forward -- and if so, prioritize fixing the LIVE automaton's entity-resolver gate (per the sinex-cel3 comment) to match, since the shadow lane already has the more defensible behavior. Replace the offset/limit-based scope hash with one based on actual selected event ids (or pin min_id/max_id) so the reproducibility claim actually holds under interleaved replay.

title: AI session capture: Claude tool-use/tool-result content blocks silently dropped (undocumented, unlike ChatGPT's documented equivalent); ChatGPT thread reconstruction only walks current_node->root, silently drops every regenerated/edited branch
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via per-source bespoke-logic audit. Two distinct completeness gaps in crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/ai_session.rs, both silent (no error, no partial-capture marker):

1. Claude parser (228-241): the content-block filter keeps only block_type=='text' (or empty), discarding tool_use/tool_result/thinking/image blocks entirely with no trace in the payload. The module's own doc comment documents this loss explicitly for ChatGPT ('tool-use and non-text content nodes are skipped') but never mentions it for Claude -- a Claude message consisting only of a tool call produces an emitted ai.message event with text:null, silently losing the actual content with no documentation that this is expected.

2. ChatGPT thread reconstruction (extract_chatgpt_thread, 436-455): iterates conv.mapping only along the single parent-chain from current_node to root. Any node reachable elsewhere in the conversation DAG (regenerated responses, edited-and-resubmitted prompts -- both routine in real ChatGPT exports) is never visited, never emitted, and never even errors -- it's structurally invisible, not just deprioritized. No test fixture exercises a branching/sibling conversation shape.

Both are related to but not named by the already-open sinex-4j2.1.2 (converge direct ai_session parsers onto the Polylogue material protocol, which flags fabricated pseudo-ByteRange anchors as a problem with these parsers) -- worth surfacing explicitly as additional scope for that convergence work. Redaction tagging itself is verified solid for both parsers (consistent ProcessingContext::Document, no bypass).
acceptance_criteria: Document (at minimum) or fix (preferably) the Claude tool-use-block loss to match ChatGPT's documented behavior. For ChatGPT branch loss: either walk and emit every reachable node in conv.mapping (not just the current_node path), or explicitly document that only the currently-selected conversation path is captured and regenerated/edited branches are permanently lost. Fold into sinex-4j2.1.2's scope if that convergence work supersedes fixing these parsers in place.

title: mbox/zip/tar.gz email-archive streaming has no aggregate decompression-ratio guard -- a crafted archive of many small under-cap messages can hang the scan indefinitely
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via untrusted-file-parser-robustness audit. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapters/email_mbox_file.rs streams zip/tar.gz-packaged mbox archives (the real, shipped Google-Takeout-Mail-shaped ingestion path). Per-message size IS capped (max_message_bytes, default 64MiB, stream_mbox_reader lines 398-406) and rejected cleanly. But there is NO cap on the AGGREGATE decompressed volume of an archive, nor on total entry/message count -- a crafted zip/tar.gz with an extreme compression ratio spread across many small From-delimited messages, each individually under the 64MiB per-message cap, causes the adapter to keep streaming/emitting records indefinitely: a CPU/wall-clock hang on one background scan (not a memory-corruption bug, since streaming discards prior message bytes as it goes), given no ratio-limiting wrapper exists around flate2::GzDecoder or the zip crate's deflate reader anywhere in this file. This is the one archive-handling code path in the whole ingestion surface that is real, user-suppliable (a corrupted or maliciously-substituted Takeout export), and the module's own doc comment says it handles 'gigabytes'.

Minor secondary correctness note (not itself a vuln, worth a one-line callout either way): on hitting an oversized message, stream_mbox_reader returns immediately (line 401) rather than skipping just that message and continuing -- one malformed/oversized message aborts parsing of every subsequent message in that file/archive entry, silently dropping later valid messages too.

Verified SOLID in the same file: zip-slip/path-traversal is not reachable (entry names are used only as string keys, archive entries are never extracted to the filesystem); truncated/corrupt zip archives fail cleanly at ZipArchive::new with no panic; symlink entries are implicitly excluded via entry.is_file().
acceptance_criteria: Add an aggregate decompression-ratio or total-bytes-processed ceiling to the zip/tar.gz streaming path in email_mbox_file.rs, distinct from the existing per-message cap, so a crafted or corrupted archive with many small messages can't hang a scan indefinitely. Consider whether the oversized-message abort-vs-skip-and-continue behavior is intentional; if not, prefer skip-and-continue so one bad message doesn't silently drop the rest of a multi-GB mbox.

title: document ingestion trusts filename-extension MIME type with no content verification -- latent trust-boundary gap that activates the moment a real PDF/DOCX parser gets built
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via untrusted-file-parser-robustness audit. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/document/runtime.rs:557-560 and document/staging.rs:136-139 both determine mime_type via MimeGuess::from_path(...).first_raw() -- a pure extension-to-MIME lookup table with zero content inspection. No magic-byte sniffing dependency (e.g. the infer crate) exists anywhere in Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock. This mime_type field is trusted verbatim into DocumentIngestedPayload, MIME-based auto-tagging, and text-encoding detection (which itself only checks mime_type.starts_with('text/') before treating bytes as text).

Scope-defining finding from the same audit: currently there is NO PDF or office-document content parser anywhere in the tree at all -- DocumentParserAutomaton::process_dendron unconditionally calls std::fs::read_to_string() regardless of declared mime_type, which simply fails (non-UTF8) and silently returns an empty result for any real PDF/DOCX. So this MIME-trust gap is presently inert (nothing dangerous consumes the mismatch) -- but it becomes live risk the instant a real PDF/office-format extractor is added on top of this untrusted MIME field without independently verifying content, since a file named report.pdf could actually be an arbitrary binary and would be routed to whatever parser trusts the .pdf-derived mime_type.
acceptance_criteria: When/if a real content parser (PDF/DOCX extraction) is added, it should verify file type via content (magic bytes) rather than trusting the extension-derived mime_type, OR the extension-derived mime_type should be treated as a hint only, with a content check gating which parser actually runs. File this as a pre-condition to any future PDF/office-parser work, not an urgent standalone fix given today's inert reachability.

title: renamed/moved Obsidian vault notes silently fork into a new, unlinked occurrence -- no rename detection, old path's occurrence stays live forever with no supersession signal
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via untrusted-file-parser-robustness audit. crate/sinexd/src/sources/source_contracts/knowledgebase.rs:230: occurrence_identity = Uuid5From('(path, body_text_hash)') -- the occurrence key is derived from the file PATH, not a content-only or stable note-id. DirectoryWalkCursor (directory_walk.rs:82) is likewise keyed by absolute path with no rename-detection heuristic (e.g. matching an appearing path against a disappearing path with an unchanged body_text_hash).

Concrete scenario: renaming/moving Projects/foo.md -> Archive/foo.md in Obsidian, with identical content, produces a NEW note.observed occurrence at the new path -- the old path's occurrence remains live in core.events untouched, with nothing marking it superseded, archived, or 'the same note as X'. Every rename is a silent, permanent fork with no operator-visible signal. No test covers this (grep for rename/moved in knowledgebase_test.rs is empty). Same class of gap as the project's own documented interval-revision doctrine (sinex-y8v) but not previously tracked for this specific source.
acceptance_criteria: Either detect renames (matching a newly-appeared path against a recently-disappeared path with an unchanged body_text_hash, within some scan window) and emit a supersession/link rather than a fresh occurrence, or explicitly document that path-based identity means renames are NOT tracked as the same note (so operators know to expect vault reorganizations to fork history) and consider whether a content-hash-only identity would be less surprising than path-based.

title: ReplayTelemetry: an unstoppable, unreadable, unbounded background poller -- the exact decorative-subsystem shape found elsewhere, but also resource-growing and shutdown-unsafe
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via lifecycle/crash-consistency audit. Same class as the EphemeralRaw media-retention flag (wired, running, resource-consuming, product discarded) but with two additional defects.

crate/sinexd/src/api/replay_control/mod.rs:75: ReplayTelemetry::new(replay.clone()).spawn() -- return value discarded. spawn() (telemetry.rs:57-66) is an infinite loop with NO select! on any shutdown channel, not in the supervisor's reverse-order join -- it keeps querying the DB after 'sinexd stopped' is logged, against pools being torn down. Every poll_interval (default 30s), sample() calls list_operations(None,None,None), which issues SELECT ... FROM core.operations_log WHERE operation_type='replay' ORDER BY id DESC with NO LIMIT, then JSON-decodes every row -- cost grows monotonically with replay history, and the re-import campaign will generate replay operations, so this specifically gets worse right when it matters. Finally, the result is unreachable in production: spawn(self) moves self, latest_snapshot() is #[cfg(test)] only, and grep for ReplayTelemetrySnapshot outside tests finds only its own definition and a re-export -- the module docstring's claim that it 'publishes a snapshot the gateway exposes for operator-facing surfaces' is false. The only observable effect is an info! log line every 30s, forever, including after shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Either wire ReplayTelemetry's snapshot to an actual consumer (matching its docstring's claimed purpose) and add a LIMIT to the underlying query, or delete the subsystem entirely since it currently produces nothing anyone reads. Either way, its spawn must observe shutdown (JoinHandle owned and joined, or select! on the shutdown signal) so it doesn't keep querying torn-down pools.

title: no RPC protocol-version handshake and near-zero deny_unknown_fields coverage -- a renamed/dropped request field is silently ignored rather than rejected on version-skewed calls
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via lifecycle/crash-consistency audit (partial finding, mechanism confirmed, specific exploitable command not yet enumerated). There is no protocol-version handshake anywhere in the gateway -- no version header, no negotiated capability set; SYSTEM_VERSION_METHOD exists but is purely informational and never consulted before dispatch. Only THREE structs in the entire workspace use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (crate/sinexd/src/api/handlers/ops.rs:599,626 and ops/media.rs:63). Consequence: an older sinexctl sending a parameter a newer server renamed or dropped has that parameter SILENTLY IGNORED, and the server applies its own default instead of erroring -- most dangerous on destructive/scoped commands (replay scope, tombstone/purge, blob sweep) where a silently-defaulted scope could be broader or narrower than the caller intended. Response-side skew is verified SOLID (serde_path_to_error gives loud failures on the client). Not yet enumerated: which specific request structs combine #[serde(default)] with a scope/limit field, which would make this concretely exploitable rather than theoretical.
acceptance_criteria: Enumerate request structs on destructive/scoped RPC methods (replay, tombstone, purge, blob sweep) that combine #[serde(default)] with a scope-narrowing field, and add deny_unknown_fields (or an explicit version check) to those specifically, prioritizing over a blanket workspace-wide change.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Concrete, traced exploitability confirmed 2026-08-11 via residual-risk-ledger follow-up. Four request structs on destructive/scoped RPC methods combine #[serde(default)] with a scope-narrowing field, each traced to its widened SQL/NATS behavior:

1. DlqPurgeRequest (crate/sinex-primitives/src/rpc/dlq.rs:323-332) -- start_sequence/end_sequence default to None -- (None,None)=>None at handlers/dlq.rs:588 PURGES THE ENTIRE RAW-INGEST DLQ STREAM instead of the requested sequence range. confirm:bool has no default, so the safety flag survives version skew while the scope narrowing does not -- 'purge sequences 100-200' silently becomes 'purge everything'. SHARPEST instance -- recommend prioritizing this struct's fix.
2. LifecycleArchiveRequest (rpc/lifecycle.rs:67-86) -- before/source/event_ids/dry_run all default -- defaulting before+source gives get_live_event_ids(None,None,limit) -> SELECT id FROM core.events ORDER BY ts_orig,id LIMIT  at persistence.rs:2253-2259 -- the OLDEST 1000 events across the WHOLE DATABASE, no source filter, no time bound. Compounded: dry_run also defaults false, so a skewed dry-run field turns a preview request into a real cascade archive.
3. ReplayExecuteRequest (rpc/replay.rs:344-354) -- dry_run defaults false -- a dry-run execute silently becomes a real execute (archives the cascade, dispatches the source scan).
4. TombstoneCreateRequest (rpc/lifecycle.rs:419-434) -- before/source/event_ids all default to None; limit defaults to 1000 -- same widening shape as archive, on the PERMANENT-deletion tier.

Fails safe, verified, no action needed: TombstoneApproveRequest.yes_i_understand_data_is_gone defaults false and the handler rejects on false (correct fail-closed default); ReplayGateOverrides' four gate bools all default false (more restrictive, correct). Not an RPC surface at all: sinexctl ops blob sweep-orphans connects to the DB directly with no request struct, so it has no version-skew surface -- can be excluded from this bead's scope.

Recommend prioritizing deny_unknown_fields on these 4 specific structs over a blanket workspace-wide change, per the bead's own acceptance criteria.

title: phone_number redaction rule excludes ProcessingContext::Command -- phone numbers embedded in shell commands are never redacted despite Forever retention on terminal capture
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via cross-implementation consistency audit (redaction detector context-coverage sweep). crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/catalog.rs:432-442: phone_number (Hash strategy) is scoped to contexts:[Clipboard, Document, Notification] only -- Command is missing. Every terminal/shell-history source contract (bash_history.rs, zsh_history.rs, fish_history.rs, text_history.rs, atuin_history.rs, kitty_osc.rs, asciinema.rs, weechat.rs) uses ProcessingContext::Command, a high-frequency, RetentionPolicy::Forever capture surface. A phone number embedded in a shell command (a Twilio/SMS CLI invocation, a curl argument, a mysql -e one-liner with a phone literal) is never hashed/redacted, while the identical string would be caught in Document/Clipboard/Notification. Same 'detector exists but isn't wired to every context that needs it' shape already found for generic_secret_assign (which is Command/Journal-only, missing Document/Clipboard -- the opposite direction of this gap). Verified ssn/pesel/nip/regon rules deliberately share a consistent 4-context set including Command -- phone_number is the outlier, not part of a deliberate policy.
acceptance_criteria: phone_number's contexts list includes Command, matching the other structural PII detectors (ssn/pesel/nip/regon) that are already correctly scoped to include it.
close_reason: Closure Evidence Manifest: Merged via PR #2615 (squash-merged 2026-08-11). Fix: Command context added to the privacy cluster's disclosure/redaction path. Verified via xtask check -p sinexd + xtask check -p sinex-primitives on the merged commit.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Adjacent, distinct-mechanism finding 2026-08-11 via arbitrary-hardcoded-limits audit: crate/sinex-primitives/src/privacy/detector.rs:130-143's phone-number plausibility filter applies a NANP (North American) structural rule to any bare 10-digit candidate with no leading '+' -- digits[0]<2 || digits[3]<2 rejects it as implausible. A domestic (no-plus-prefix) 10-digit phone number from a country whose national dialing plan doesn't follow NANP's 'area/exchange code can't start with 0 or 1' rule (e.g. many European domestic numbers with a leading 0) FAILS this plausibility check and passes through UNREDACTED, where the identical number in +-prefixed international form would be caught. This is a failure-to-redact bug via regex/heuristic scope, distinct from this bead's own context-list (ProcessingContext::Command) scoping gap -- both should be fixed together given they affect the same detector.

title: DB password exported into sinexd's own process environment via PGPASSWORD, readable via /proc/pid/environ -- inert only while Postgres trust-auth (sinex-s4lj) stands
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via boundary-enforcement/trust-mapping audit. nixos/modules/lib/database-runtime.nix's mkDatabasePasswordExec generates a wrapper (sinex-sinexd-database-auth, invoked at nixos/modules/sources.nix:678) that does 'export PGPASSWORD="$(tr -d ...)"' then 'exec ${command}' -- so the plaintext DB password persists in sinexd's own environment for its whole lifetime, readable via /proc/<pid>/environ by root or the same uid. sinexdArgs itself (sources.nix:487-490) carries no secrets, so ps aux/cmdline exposure is clean -- only the env-var vector applies. Exploit value today is ~zero because Postgres loopback auth is trust (sinex-s4lj, open) so the password is never actually checked -- but this will matter the moment s4lj is fixed, and is cheap to fix in the same pass (e.g. a .pgpass file instead of an exported env var).
acceptance_criteria: Fix alongside sinex-s4lj: use a .pgpass file or another non-environment credential-passing mechanism instead of exported PGPASSWORD, so fixing the trust-auth hole doesn't simultaneously introduce a live env-var credential-leak vector.

title: raw-stream backpressure loop holds a global mutex across an unbounded wait with no shutdown escape
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via perturbation-robustness audit. crate/sinexd/src/runtime/nats_publisher.rs:549-629 (wait_for_raw_events_stream_capacity) takes self.raw_stream_pressure.lock().await at line 550 and holds it through a loop doing three NATS round-trips (get_stream, consumer_info, stream.info) plus tokio::time::sleep(RAW_STREAM_BACKPRESSURE_POLL_INTERVAL) at line 628. The serialization itself is intentional backpressure design, but two properties are not: (1) no exit condition other than the backlog draining -- if the event engine is wedged (DB down, DLQ jammed), every caller of publish_intent blocks forever with no shutdown-token select and no maximum wait, so shutdown will hang on these tasks; (2) no error budget on the NATS probes -- each retry iteration re-issues three round-trips per 250ms while holding the global lock, so a slow NATS multiplies latency across every publisher in the process. sinex-uz9d (open) is adjacent but scoped to error-return faults, not this unbounded-wait shape.
acceptance_criteria: wait_for_raw_events_stream_capacity's wait loop selects against the shutdown signal (or a maximum wait duration) so a wedged event engine doesn't hang shutdown indefinitely on every publisher task holding this lock.

title: schema strict-diff DECLARED_INLINE_CHECKS only declares expectations for core.events -- reflection.events and audit.archived_events inherit XOR check only by accident of LIKE-based creation
description: Discovered 2026-08-11 via test-coverage risk-mapping audit (Opus), while assessing the schema apply/converge engine (otherwise the best-tested surface in the codebase). title: sinexctl civil-time computations (report today/yesterday/calendar, --since/--until date parsing) use UTC midnight instead of operator-local civil day -- sibling gap to the already-closed sinex-2ged
description:
Discovered 2026-08-11 via numeric/temporal envelope audit. sinex-2ged (closed, PR #2482) fixed hourly/daily bucketing for automata::civil (jiff dep, SINEX_LOCAL_TZ) but its own close_reason explicitly scoped 'baseline/brief/calendar surfaces cite the contract, nbi.5 reconcile' as remaining forward work -- confirmed SINEX_LOCAL_TZ/jiff exist ONLY in crate/sinexd/src/automata/civil.rs (grep across crate/ finds nothing in sinexctl), so this gap is real and unaddressed.

1. crate/sinexctl/src/commands/report.rs: today_range() (:88-92), yesterday_range() (:95-104), midnight_utc() (:106-114) all derive boundaries from OffsetDateTime::now_utc(). collect_calendar_data() (:585-594) and print_calendar() (:697-721) reuse the same midnight_utc() for the calendar view. Concrete scenario: operator (Europe/Warsaw, CEST=UTC+2) runs  at 2026-08-11 01:00 local (=2026-08-10 23:00 UTC) -- the reported 'today' window is local Aug-10 02:00 through Aug-11 01:00, mislabeled 'today' and offset from what the operator means. The same UTC-midnight arithmetic repeats in the Calendar command's per-day loop, shifting every day-bucket by the CET/CEST offset, worst around each local midnight.

2. crate/sinexctl/src/validation.rs:29-37 (parse_time_input_with_now) and crate/sinexctl/src/commands/telemetry.rs:545-553 (resolve_time_arg) both parse a bare YYYY-MM-DD date-only CLI arg (--since/--until) as date.with_hms(0,0,0).assume_utc() -- an operator typing --since 2026-08-10 means local midnight, gets UTC midnight instead, excluding the first 1-2 hours of their intended day.

Not data loss -- results are off by 1-2h at day boundaries only, everything after is fine -- but exactly the operator-visible gap 2ged's own acceptance criteria flagged as remaining. Verified: no chrono::Local/host-local-offset usage exists anywhere in sinexctl or sinexd (uniformly UTC-only, at least predictable rather than machine-dependent). TUI 'Recent Events (1h)' and baseline's 30-day rolling window are verified SOLID -- they use sliding durations, not calendar-day boundaries, so they're inherently timezone-agnostic.
acceptance_criteria: sinexctl's civil-day-shaped commands (report today/yesterday/calendar, --since/--until date-only parsing) use the same SINEX_LOCAL_TZ-aware civil-day computation as automata::civil, rather than UTC midnight, so 'today' actually means the operator's local today.

title: TUI: raw payload copy shows truncated preview data mislabeled as raw JSON, UI blocks up to 4.5min with dead loading indicator, hot reconnect loop with no backoff
description:
Batch of smaller TUI findings from the 2026-08-10 audit sweep:

1. recent_event_rows is declared (line 103), cleared (405,413), but NEVER ASSIGNED anywhere. Consequence: 'event JSON'/'payload JSON' copy actions are permanently disabled with the misleading reason 'raw query event is unavailable' (1978-1986), AND payload_lines always falls back to card.payload_preview (1858-1860) while the UI header literally says 'Payload Raw JSON' (1732-1734) -- but that preview is ALREADY truncated (8 top-level keys / 240 chars per string / 5 array items max, per views/events.rs:768-800) then truncated AGAIN to 12 display lines. An operator reading what's labeled 'raw JSON' is actually reading a doubly-truncated preview.

2. app.loading is set (284) and cleared (301) entirely between terminal.draw and the next loop iteration (457-463) -- so it is ALWAYS false at actual render time. Every 'if app.loading' branch in the codebase is dead code (617,767,1216,1242,1662,1669,1693). Meanwhile refresh() awaits 9 SEQUENTIAL RPCs on the UI thread at a 30s timeout each -- the terminal can show a frozen, unresponsive frame (ignoring even 'q' to quit) for up to ~4.5 minutes with zero visual indication anything is happening.

3. On a refresh failure, last_refresh is never updated (line 302), so should_auto_refresh() (277-281) is true on EVERY subsequent loop iteration -- a connect attempt fires every single frame with no backoff, while the UI simultaneously displays 'Auto-refresh in 0s' as if it were behaving normally.

4. Minor: TimeRange::new(...).ok() (397) silently degrades to NO time filter at all while labels still claim 'last hour'; dlq_peek(Some(5)) (323) means the automaton-DLQ card silently vanishes if the relevant message happens to be 6th-or-later in the queue; source_cockpit_state (1509-1515) paints a source fully red/blocked if ANY single action is disabled, ahead of checking actual readiness/continuity state; state_snapshot_operation_card() (1008-1041) renders 100% hardcoded placeholder prose inline in the live Operations Room list next to real replay/ops rows, with only the literal string 'target' as a phase value distinguishing it as fake.
acceptance_criteria: recent_event_rows gets actually populated so the 'Payload Raw JSON' label is honest, or the label is corrected to say 'preview' when that's genuinely what's shown. app.loading reflects real in-flight state (e.g. set before the async refresh starts, checked during render via a shared flag, not scoped entirely within one synchronous block) so a slow/hung refresh is visible to the operator. Auto-refresh backs off after a failure instead of hot-looping. Items 4 are lower priority cleanup, fold in opportunistically.

title: Embeddings/semantic-lane findings (lane confirmed fully DORMANT, zero live callers -- severity capped accordingly)
description:
Findings from the 2026-08-10 embeddings/semantic-lane audit. VERDICT ON DORMANCY: the embedding lane is fully dead in production -- EmbeddingRepository has zero non-test callers, search_similar/hybrid_search/store_cache/check_cache/count_models have zero callers including tests. Live dev DB confirms core.embedding_models=0 rows, core.event_embeddings=0 rows, zero HNSW indexes exist. This caps severity on everything below -- these are latent bugs in inactive code, worth fixing before activation, not urgent now.

1. MEDIUM-HIGH (latent): every pgvector HNSW index is unusable by every query in the repo. Index built on expression ((embedding::vector(N)) vector_cosine_ops) (apply.rs:2587,2594); every query orders by the RAW column (embeddings.rs:246,281,333; apply.rs:2685-2688) -- Postgres cannot match a length-coercion expression index to a bare column reference. Empirically confirmed via a rolled-back temp-table test: ORDER BY emb <=> '...' produces Seq Scan; ORDER BY emb::vector(N) <=> '...' uses the index. Results are exact, not wrong -- pure performance defect (O(n) scan per search once activated), hnsw.ef_search config is inert theatre.

2. MEDIUM (live): embedding-producer automaton (registry.rs:151) IS registered and fed by the live document-parser -- it computes no actual vector, just emits one document.embedded event per chunk carrying an effect_key/replay_policy pointing at a core.model_effects row that is NEVER WRITTEN anywhere (confirmed zero production callers). On any real document ingestion this is pure ceremony -- one fictional-receipt derived event per document chunk. Claim support is correctly UNKNOWN with zero evidence counts (doctrine-clean on that front).

3. MEDIUM (live but currently inert): semantic.lanes.set_status (handlers/semantic.rs:205-216) lets ANY :write-scoped caller stamp a lane's status to 'promoted' with no transition validation and no auth argument threaded through (registered via pool_typed_rpc not pool_auth_typed_rpc, rpc_registry.rs:805-808) -- planned->promoted or discarded->promoted both succeed. Mitigating: nothing currently reads status='promoted' to make outputs canonical -- the real promotion bridge (promote_entity_related_output, entity_chain_shadow.rs:692) correctly routes through handle_curation_finalize+authorize_finalization. So today this is a STATUS LIE surface (the field can say something false), not a content-auto-promotion vulnerability.

4. LOW-MEDIUM: fabricated 1.0 confidence (DEFAULT 1.0 in entities.rs:126,358, unwrap_or(1.0) in knowledge_graph.rs:335 -- same root cause already filed as sinex-jb7x) flows through into shadow-lane candidates via seed_entity_relation_outputs_from_canonical_graph (derivation.rs:845,861). Only PKM RPC writes the graph today so blast radius is small, but it's the exact doctrine violation this whole sub-sweep has been finding.

5. LOW rot: insert_event_embeddings uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING while store_event_embedding uses DO UPDATE -- divergent staleness semantics if both paths ever get used together. events_without_embeddings only detects 'never embedded', no staleness/re-embed-after-reinterpretation trigger. validate_embedding_values rejects non-finite but not all-zero vectors (NaN cosine distance risk). Dead-code rot: xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/template.rs:1133-1135 drops index names that don't exist in the schema; core.drop_embedding_model_index has zero callers.

NO FINDING (verified clean): the dimension-change rejection fix (sinex-audit-embedding-dim-change) has no bypass -- every vector write path validates against declared model dimensions, the only raw-SQL insert is restore-from-archive of already-validated rows, and real DB-backed tests exist for this specific path.
acceptance_criteria: Item 1 fixed before any activation: index and query expressions must match (either index on the raw column with a CAST at write time, or queries cast consistently to match the expression index) so HNSW is actually used once this lane goes live. Item 2: embedding-producer either actually computes/stores vectors, or is disabled/removed until it does something real rather than emitting fictional receipts. Item 3: semantic.lanes.set_status validates legal state transitions and threads through real auth (pool_auth_typed_rpc), even though nothing currently trusts the status field -- fix before it becomes trusted. Item 4: tracked jointly with sinex-jb7x's fix. Item 5: low priority cleanup, fold into whatever activation work eventually touches this lane.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Sharpened 2026-08-11 via derived-intelligence algorithmic-quality audit (item 5, model-revision case). Concrete mechanism for 'old vectors silently comparable-by-distance-math but semantically incomparable': model identity in crate/sinex-db/src/repositories/embeddings.rs:33-79 is exactly (provider, model_name) -- dimensions is immutable (PR #2591) but NOT part of identity beyond that, and ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET is_active=true, metadata=EXCLUDED.metadata keeps the SAME model_id on re-registration. metadata is not hashed or compared. Concrete scenario: register ('ollama','nomic-embed-text',768), ingest 200k chunk embeddings, then a routine  updates the local model v1->v1.5 (same name, same 768 dims) -- ensure_model returns the IDENTICAL model_id, new vectors land in core.event_embeddings under that same id, in the same partial HNSW index, alongside v1 vectors. search_similar and hybrid_search both filter only on embedding_model_id, so cosine distance ends up computed ACROSS two incompatible embedding spaces with no error, no flag, no staleness column, no revision counter -- events_without_embeddings' NOT EXISTS check means no event is ever re-embedded either. Directly relevant to sinex-5v6's RequestKey design, which already lists 'provider, model AND revision' -- but core.embedding_models has no revision column to carry it yet, and register_model's immutability guard is keyed on dimensions only, not revision. Also confirmed cross-model contamination IS correctly blocked today (every query filters embedding_model_id) -- this is specifically about same-model-id-different-weights, not cross-model mixing.
