title: Adapter-source emit_batch_durable settlement lies: checkpoint reports AdmissionSettled with zero events actually persisted (raindrop-bookmarks repro, 27452 events)
description:
sinex-yslt (dev-stack re-import rehearsal, 2026-08-01) surfaced a serious, reproducible, self-masking data-loss bug on the raindrop-bookmarks source, worse than the documented crash-window loss seam: NOTHING crashed, yet the durable checkpoint ends up permanently wrong.

Repro: an isolated dev-stack rehearsal (fresh empty DB, fresh NATS/JetStream, checkout-local Postgres) ran two real historical-scan sources against real /realm/data archives. git-commit-history (1813 commits) round-tripped perfectly, verified via 4 independent surfaces (core.events row count, DEV_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS stream message count, event-engine-dev JetStream consumer events_processed stat, sinexctl sources status) -- all agreed at exactly 1813.

raindrop-bookmarks (real 34,483-row CSV export at /realm/data/exports/raindrop/processed/bookmarks.csv, genuinely parsed -- fingerprinted header matched the real files 11 columns) did NOT: the source drivers durable checkpoint (NATS KV bucket KV_dev_sinex_checkpoints, key source-driver-raindrop-bookmarks-1...) records total_events_emitted:27452 with every event settled as AdmissionSettled (progress-unlocking, no partial-failure warning), but:
- core.events has ZERO raindrop rows (only the 1813 git rows exist)
- sinex_schemas.dlq_events has 0 rows
- audit.archived_events has 0 rows
- DEV_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS stream: only 155 total messages ever published+consumed across the whole session (git + reflection heartbeats) -- nowhere near 27,452
- event-engine-dev JetStream consumer stats stayed frozen at events_processed=1813 (gits exact count) for 7+ straight minutes after raindrops checkpoint claimed 27,452 settled, with events_failed=0/validation_failures=0/dlq_routed=0 -- the consumer never saw them, successfully or otherwise
- sinexctl sources status independently reports raindrop-bookmarks as missing-material/gapped, runs=0, events=0 -- the operator-facing surface agrees with the DB, not with the source drivers own checkpoint
- The source then got stuck indefinitely (30s poll loop, 5+ repeats observed) logging runtime.checkpoint_kv_behind_total / "Checkpoint KV is ahead of this save; skipping without regressing or crashing" every cycle, never finalizing or retrying

Net effect: the source durably believes a full successful import of the entire 27,452-row archive completed and settled -- while not one single row exists anywhere in the persistence layer. Because the checkpoint is durable, a future re-scan of the same file would likely SKIP re-emitting (cursor already advanced past the whole file), making this data PERMANENTLY UNRECOVERABLE without a manual checkpoint reset.

Code-path confirmation (independently re-verified 2026-08-01, not just trusting the report): crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:1646 genuinely calls emit_batch_durable() (imported at line 126) -- this IS a real caller. But crate/sinexd/src/runtime/durable_emission_backend.rs:24-30s module doc comment still says "it does NOT wire it into any real caller (source cursor, automaton checkpoint, invalidation ack). That caller integration is the next slice (sinex-vxu et al.)" -- that doc is STALE; this rehearsal is likely the first real-volume exercise of an integration that already landed silently, undocumented, and apparently buggy.

This is CLAUDE.mds documented "Known open correctness seam" ("Emission is an in-memory handoff end-to-end until NATS publish: source cursors and automaton checkpoints can durably advance before outputs are durable") manifesting concretely and reproducibly during ORDINARY same-process operation for at least one source/volume profile, not merely under a crash scenario as the doc implies -- and worse than "a loss window on crash" since nothing crashed, nothing retried, and the checkpoint is durably wrong from a clean run.

Discovery: sinex-yslt rehearsal, full evidence + command log on that bead. Should probably land under epic r6d alongside r6d.4/vxu/r6d.7/w4i, or be treated as a hard prerequisite blocking sinex-poma Phase C (a real re-import that hits this exact code path for a large source would silently lose the entire source with a durably-corrupted checkpoint that resists retry).
design: Undecided, needs an r6d-epic-aligned design pass (repo doctrine: do not fix this class ad-hoc in passing, it is sequenced campaign work with a shared primitive -- check r6d state first, this may share a root cause/fix with r6d.4/vxu/r6d.7/w4i). Candidate angle: emit_batch_durable and/or its caller in adapter_source.rs may be marking a batch AdmissionSettled based on local acceptance rather than confirmed downstream persistence -- needs tracing the actual settlement decision point against the real NATS publish/consumer-ack path for a large multi-chunk batch specifically (git, the source that worked, is small -- 1813 events single-digit-chunk; raindrop is 34483 rows, likely multi-chunk -- chunk-boundary handling is a plausible fault line, cf. the already-closed sinex-wv7 >2700-row chunk boundary bug in the same file, possible related regression).
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: the raindrop-bookmarks repro (or an equivalent large multi-chunk CSV/file source) round-trips correctly -- checkpoint total_events_emitted matches actual persisted core.events row count, matches DEV_SINEX_RAW_EVENTS stream message count, matches JetStream consumer events_processed, matches sinexctl sources status.
AC2: a regression test proves this at the unit/integration level using a real multi-chunk batch through the real emit_batch_durable/adapter_source.rs path (not a mock) -- anti-vacuity: reverting the fix makes the test fail by asserting settled-count == persisted-count after a simulated or real chunk-boundary-crossing scan.
AC3: durable_emission_backend.rs module doc comment updated to reflect reality (emit_batch_durable DOES have a real caller now) once this is fixed, not left stale.
AC4: sinex-yslt rehearsal is re-run clean (this exact repro no longer reproduces) before sinex-poma Phase A is scheduled.
notes: Filed via bd sql direct INSERT workaround (bd create broken this session -- events.id has no default, DB schema 1.1.0 vs CLI 1.0.4 mismatch). Code-path claim (emit_batch_durable is a real caller in adapter_source.rs, contradicting the stale module doc) independently re-verified via grep before filing, not just trusted from the discovering agents report. BLOCKS sinex-poma Phase A scheduling per operator campaign doctrine (sinex-yslt exists specifically to catch this class before Phase C) until fixed or explicitly triaged/accepted.
close_reason:
NOT REPRODUCIBLE as originally described -- independently investigated and closed 2026-08-01 by direct live reproduction, not just review.

ROOT OF THE ORIGINAL CONFUSION: the raindrop-bookmarks CSV export note/excerpt columns contain embedded newlines inside quoted fields. Naive line counting (wc -l, or a head -n truncation) over-counts rows, because CSV quoting means one logical row can span multiple physical lines. The bead described the file as "34,483 rows" (a wc -l-derived figure) and framed 27452 settled-vs-0-persisted as a huge gap. The TRUE logical row count, verified via RFC4180-compliant parsing (Python csv.DictReader, independently cross-checked against sinexs own csv-crate-based parser output), is exactly 27452 -- there is no missing 7031-row gap in the file itself.

INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION (2026-08-01, this session, not delegated): ran the UNMODIFIED real file (/realm/data/exports/raindrop/processed/bookmarks.csv) against a from-empty dev stack (fresh Postgres AND fresh NATS JetStream/KV -- discovered along the way that a Postgres-only dev-state wipe leaves NATS KV checkpoints durably stale across wipes; had to explicitly clear both). Result: ALL 27452 real rows persisted correctly in core.events. Verified via exact-match diff of the full ID set (persisted core.events raindrop_id values vs the CSV files own id column, both deduplicated and sorted) -- zero difference, not just a matching count. The emission-receipt checkpoints total_events_emitted:27452 exactly matches reality; it does not lie.

PLAUSIBLE (not independently confirmed) explanation for the original observation: the rehearsal that discovered this ran BEFORE sinex-amg2 (PR #2543, merged today) fixed a severe, 100%-reproducible DB connection-pool starvation bug -- POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS=64 was silently clamping the sandbox pool from its intended 48 slots down to 4. Running raindrop-bookmarks concurrently with git-commit-history under that starvation is a plausible trigger for a genuine (but different, and likely fixed as a side effect of amg2s unrelated pool-sizing fix) persistence failure. This explanation is NOT independently verified by reproducing under the old pool-starved config -- flagging as the leading hypothesis, not a proven cause.

A SEPARATE, REAL, LOWER-SEVERITY finding surfaced during this investigation: when a whole-file-as-one-materialized-record source (StaticFileAdapter) contains a genuinely unparseable/perpetually-failing member (reproduced with a deliberately truncated/malformed test file), the record never fully unlocks progress and the ENTIRE file is re-scanned from scratch every ~30s poll cycle, forever, with no DLQ/quarantine path and no partial-progress mechanism -- burning CPU/NATS/DB resources indefinitely without completing. This is real but far less severe (affects only genuinely malformed input) and is filed separately as sinex-<pending> rather than conflated with this beads original, unsupported claim.

Phase A is UNBLOCKED by this closure -- see sinex-poma.

title: xtask infra start does not detect/apply Postgres max_connections config drift on an already-running instance
description:
PostgresManager::start returns as soon as an already-running server accepts connections; max_connections is a restart-only Postgres setting. On a checkout whose dev Postgres was already running before a POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS constant change lands (e.g. sinex-amg2 PR #2543s 64->500 bump), xtask infra start alone does NOT pick up the new value -- the operator needs an explicit xtask infra stop && xtask infra start to actually apply it. Self-resolves on the next full stop/start cycle (e.g. via xtask doctor or a fresh checkout), but silently leaves a stale-config live instance in the interim with no warning.

Discovery: found by sinex-amg2s agent (2026-08-01) while verifying PR #2543 locally -- confirmed SHOW max_connections stayed at 64 until an explicit stop/start cycle, matching the pool-init log going from "Reducing pool size to 4 (from 48)" to the correct 48-slot init only after that cycle.

Full investigation: https://github.com/Sinity/sinex/pull/2543#issuecomment-5152133763
design: Undecided. Candidate directions: (1) xtask infra start detects live Postgres config drift (compare running SHOW max_connections/other managed settings against the current constants) and auto-restarts when mismatched; (2) at minimum, surface a warning when live config does not match the constants, pointing at the stop/start remediation.
acceptance_criteria: xtask infra start either auto-corrects a live Postgres instance whose managed config (max_connections at minimum) does not match current constants, or prints an explicit warning naming the drifted setting and the remediation command; a test proves the drift is detected (e.g. start with an old constant baked into a fixture config, bump the constant, assert start reports/fixes the mismatch).

title: sandbox test-DB pool: connection-budget mismatch + multi-statement-in-prepared-statement bug under load
description:
Discovered while resurrecting `crate/sinex-db/tests/schema/` into a compiled test target (sinex-xjx8): the checkout-local sandbox test-DB pool wants 48 pool-database slots (`SLOT_MAX_CONNECTIONS`-based default in `xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/config.rs`), each budgeted 8 connections, but the checkout-local Postgres instance's effective connection budget after reserved connections is only ~45 (`xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/provisioning.rs::effective_connection_budget`), even though `POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS` in `xtask/src/infra/services/postgres.rs` is a 64 constant. The pool self-corrects by shrinking to ~4 usable slots ("Pool reduced by 91%"), but under real load (the newly-wired ~68-test `tests/schema/` suite, ~364 tests total for `-p sinex-db` at default parallelism) that 4-slot budget is not enough headroom for nextest's default thread count, and the sandbox's own slot-recreation/cleanup machinery starts failing under contention:

- `error returned from database: cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement` -- the sandbox's own slot-recreation/cleanup path is issuing multi-statement SQL through the extended (prepared-statement) protocol instead of the simple query protocol, which only surfaces once slots are being concurrently recreated under contention.
- `terminating connection due to administrator command` -- connections getting killed, presumably by the sandbox's own contention-timeout/watchdog logic.
- `Test timed out after 120 seconds` with `Could not acquire slot lifecycle lock ... within 10s` -- cascading lock contention.
- `database "sinex_test_pool_N" does not exist` -- a race where a slot gets dropped mid-use by a concurrent recreation attempt.

Verified: running the same `xtask test -p sinex-db --test schema_test` (and the full `-p sinex-db` suite) with `-t 2` or `-t 4` (reduced nextest thread count, i.e. less connection pressure) passes 100% reliably; running at default parallelism intermittently fails ~5-7 tests with the above symptoms, always at the pool/connection layer, never a real assertion failure.

Not fixed as part of sinex-xjx8 (out of scope -- that bead is specifically about wiring/repairing `tests/schema/`, not sandbox pool capacity tuning). Two independent angles worth investigating separately:

1. Raise the effective connection budget (either `POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS` or the reserved-connection subtraction in `effective_connection_budget`) so the pool's desired ~48 slots actually fit, instead of silently degrading to ~4.
2. Fix the "cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement" error in the pool's own recreate/cleanup path -- likely a `sqlx::query()` call somewhere in `xtask/src/sandbox/db/pool/*.rs` that should use the simple-query execution path (`PgConnection::execute` via a raw multi-statement string, matching how `apply()`/`execute_sql` do it) rather than a bind-parameterized/prepared path, for whatever SQL string it constructs during slot recreation.

Acceptance: `xtask test -p sinex-db --all` at default parallelism (no `-t` override) passes reliably across several consecutive runs without pool/connection-layer failures.
acceptance_criteria: xtask test -p sinex-db --all at default parallelism (no -t override) passes reliably across several consecutive runs without pool/connection-layer failures (no 'cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement', no 'terminating connection due to administrator command', no slot-lifecycle-lock timeouts).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2565 (branch feature/fix/xtask-sandbox-multistatement-and-forbidden-lint-blindspots). Closure Evidence Manifest: (1) ensure_default_session_state_conn multi-statement SET-batch bug -- SATISFIED, fixed by looping per-statement, regression test added (ensure_default_session_state_conn_resets_multiple_dirty_settings), xtask test -p xtask passing. (2) ensure_core_events_triggers multi-statement trigger-DDL bug (found during verification, more frequent than #1 since it runs on every cleanup pass, not just on drift) -- SATISFIED, fixed via conn.as_mut().execute(sql: &str), verified with 3 consecutive xtask test -p sinex-db --test schema_test --impact-mode=off runs, 68/68 passed each time, zero cannot-insert-multiple-commands occurrences (first post-fix-1-only run had shown 2/68 failing via this exact site). (3) Full xtask test -p sinex-db --all --impact-mode=off run: zero occurrences of all three AC-listed symptoms (cannot insert multiple commands, terminating connection due to administrator command, Could not acquire slot lifecycle lock) -- but 6 unrelated failures (uk_derivation_product_event_output duplicate-key unique violation in sinex-db::database tests) appeared, a DIFFERENT failure class not part of this bead scope. DEFERRED: bead angle 1 (raise effective Postgres connection budget so the desired ~48 slots fit instead of degrading to ~4) -- not addressed, separate capacity-tuning concern. DEFERRED: the newly-discovered uk_derivation_product_event_output flake -- attempted to file as a follow-up bead but bd create is currently broken (Error 1105, Field id doesnt have a default value, matches known bd write-path incident); documented instead in this comment thread and the PR body Not-in-scope section for manual follow-up bead creation once bd write path is repaired.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Fixed both real bugs in this class, PR #2565 (branch feature/fix/xtask-sandbox-multistatement-and-forbidden-lint-blindspots):

1. ensure_default_session_state_conn (reset.rs): joined dirty SET statements with "; " and ran the batch through sqlx::query(), which uses Postgres's extended (prepared-statement) protocol and rejects multi-statement strings. Fixed by looping and issuing each SET individually. Runs on every pool before_acquire.

2. ensure_core_events_triggers (same file, found during verification when the sinex-db schema_test suite still hit "cannot insert multiple commands" after fix #1): ran the multi-statement trigger-definition SQL (CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ...; DROP TRIGGER ...; CREATE TRIGGER ...;) through sqlx::query() the same way. Fixed via conn.as_mut().execute(sql: &str) (Executor trait on a bare &str -> simple-query protocol, matching sinex-schema::apply.rs's own execute_sql helper). This one runs on EVERY cleanup pass (not just when settings drift), so it was the more frequent contributor to the flake class. sqlx::raw_sql() was tried first and also works protocol-wise, but triggers a rustc "Send is not general enough" HRTB false-positive at unrelated tokio::spawn sites elsewhere in the crate.

Verification: 3 consecutive `xtask test -p sinex-db --test schema_test --impact-mode=off` runs, 68/68 passed each time, zero "cannot insert multiple commands" occurrences (the run right after fix #1 alone still showed 2/68 failures via the trigger-recreation site).

NOT addressed: the bead's angle 1 (raise the effective Postgres connection budget so the pool's desired ~48 slots fit instead of degrading to ~4). That's a separate capacity-tuning concern from the SQL-protocol bug fixed here -- the AC line "xtask test -p sinex-db --all at default parallelism passes reliably across several consecutive runs" is satisfied for the protocol-error failure mode specifically verified above, but I have not run the FULL -p sinex-db --all suite (not just --test schema_test) at default parallelism repeatedly, nor addressed the connection-budget angle. Leaving this bead open is reasonable if the operator wants angle 1 tracked separately, or it can close on the strength of the protocol fix with a follow-up bead for the budget angle -- operator's call.

title: no test coverage for confirmation-durability-gap fatal-crash + JetStream-redelivery-after-restart path
description:
Discovered while resolving sinex-r6d.13 / sinex-5smc (jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery
off-by-one). The consumer's confirmation-publish full-exhaustion path
(all CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS in-process attempts fail ->
confirmation_durability_gap_error -> is_fatal_batch_processing_error -> the
whole JetStreamConsumer task returns Err and terminates) has ZERO test
coverage today. This is deliberate, documented pipeline behavior
("confirmed publish GATES the ack (durability gap = redelivery)" per
CLAUDE.md): the raw message is left unacked, the consumer/critical-task-set
dies, and recovery is expected to happen via a process restart (systemd
Restart=on-failure in prod) that spins up a fresh consumer instance which
then receives the redelivered raw message from JetStream.

A test with this exact shape used to exist
(jetstream_consumer_redelivers_when_confirmation_publish_fails, asserting
deliveries >= 2) but PR #196 (2026-03-27) repurposed the test into
jetstream_consumer_queues_durable_confirmation_retries_without_raw_redelivery
(later renamed again to
jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery),
changing the assertion to deliveries == 1 to test in-process retry-then-
succeed instead. That repurposing was a legitimate, deliberate design
choice (verified via git show 2322eb0d2) -- but it left the full-exhaustion
crash+redeliver-after-restart scenario permanently uncovered, since no
other test in events_consumer_integration_test.rs or jetstream_consumer_test.rs
drives a batch through the fatal confirmation_durability_gap path.

A same-process test cannot drive this scenario end-to-end (there is no
in-test supervisor that restarts a dead JetStreamConsumer), so proper
coverage likely needs either (a) a narrower unit/integration test asserting
that a full-exhaustion confirmation failure returns the fatal error class
and leaves the raw message unacked (without needing an actual second
consumer instance), or (b) a two-consumer-instance integration test: kill
the first consumer after the fatal error, spawn a second against the same
stream/consumer name, and assert it receives the redelivered raw message
and successfully confirms it.
design: Follow-up from sinex-r6d.13 closure. See that bead's close reason for full reconciliation with sinex-5smc.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test (or pair of tests) exercises the confirmation_durability_gap fatal
  path: full exhaustion of CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS returns the fatal
  error class, is_fatal_batch_processing_error classifies it as fatal, and
  the raw message is left unacked (not just that the consumer task ends).
- If practical, a second phase asserts that a freshly spawned consumer
  instance against the same durable consumer name receives the redelivered
  raw message and successfully confirms it (mirroring production's
  restart-based recovery).
- Test naming makes the scenario distinguishable from
  jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery
  (which now covers only the in-process retry-success path).

title: VM test scenario files reference undefined 'sinexd' instead of 'sinex' arg (breaks xtask check --nix)
description:
Pre-existing bug, discovered 2026-07-12 while verifying an unrelated automata.nix change via `xtask check --nix`.

4 files under tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/ have the pattern:
  sinexPackage = if sinex != null then sinex else sinexd;
but the function parameter is `sinex ? null` — there is no `sinexd` in scope, only `sinex`. Affected: failure-recovery.nix:10, runtime-matrix.nix:11, multi-source.nix:10, mtls-enforcement.nix:16. Correct siblings use `if sinex != null then sinex else <valid-fallback>` (check basic-flow.nix / chaos-*.nix for the working pattern before copying).

`nix flake check` evaluates checks.x86_64-linux.sinex-vm-failure-recovery and hits "error: undefined variable 'sinexd'" — this currently BREAKS `xtask check --nix` / `xtask check --full` for everyone, unrelated to whatever else is being changed. Since flake.nix's vmCheckOutputs always passes a non-null `sinex = sinexVmPackage`, the buggy else-branch should never be forced under normal lazy evaluation — but nix flake check's evaluation order (or a stricter check path) reaches it anyway for at least failure-recovery.nix. Root cause not fully diagnosed (why THIS scenario forces the else-branch when its 3 siblings with the identical bug apparently don't get reached first) — needs someone to actually run `nix flake check --show-trace` to completion once fixed to confirm no other lurking issues.

Fix: change `else sinexd` to `else sinex` (self-referential no-op, matches the working pattern in unaffected files) or better, remove the dead fallback entirely if `sinex` is never actually null in the real call sites — check tests/e2e/nixos-vm/default.nix.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/failure-recovery.nix:10 (and runtime-matrix.nix:11, multi-source.nix:10, mtls-enforcement.nix:16) -- each contains `sinexPackage = if sinex != null then sinex else sinexd;` where the file's own lambda parameter list only declares `sinex ? null`, not `sinexd` -- a free-variable reference.
2. Run `nix flake check` (or `xtask check --nix` / `xtask check --full`).
3. Observe evaluation of checks.x86_64-linux.sinex-vm-failure-recovery (and the 3 sibling checks) fails with "error: undefined variable 'sinexd'" -- breaking the nix check for everyone, unrelated to whatever else is being changed in a given session.
4. Compare against a working sibling scenario file (e.g. basic-flow.nix or a chaos-*.nix file) to see the correct `if sinex != null then sinex else <valid-fallback>` pattern before copying it into the 4 broken files.
acceptance_criteria: nix flake check (and xtask check --nix / xtask check --full) succeeds for all 4 previously-broken VM scenario checks (sinex-vm-failure-recovery, runtime-matrix, multi-source, mtls-enforcement). Each file's sinexPackage fallback either declares sinexd in its parameter list or drops the dead fallback branch entirely, matching the working pattern in basic-flow.nix/chaos-*.nix. Fix does not change which package a scenario deploys when sinex is explicitly provided.

title: Boot fence for interval_lift: capture a boot marker event, fence all open intervals at boot
description: sinex-5s6 landed suspend + AFK cross-kind fences in interval_lift (PR #2484), but boot fencing was deferred: no source emits a boot marker event, so interval_lift has no boot input to fence on. A boot ends the previous machine session — every interval open before the boot (including systemd unit subject-states, which suspend does NOT fence) should close at the boot instant. Needs: (1) a boot-marker event payload + a source that emits it (journald _BOOT_ID change is the natural signal, or a systemd boot.target/multi-user.target reached marker); (2) interval_lift Fence::Boot in classify_fence that closes ALL open kinds (focus, workspace, heartbeats, AND active_subject_states) at the boot ts. The MultiOutputTransducer machinery + close_at_fence already exist (5s6), so this is additive.
acceptance_criteria: A boot-marker event payload is defined and emitted by a real source (journald _BOOT_ID change or a systemd boot.target/multi-user.target-reached marker). interval_lift gains Fence::Boot in classify_fence that closes ALL open interval kinds (focus, workspace, heartbeats, and active_subject_states) at the boot timestamp -- including active_subject_states, which the earlier suspend-fence (sinex-5s6, PR #2484) explicitly does not fence. A test verifies an interval open before a simulated boot event closes at the boot instant across all four kinds.

title: 4 VM chaos scenario files reference undefined 'sinexd' variable, fail --validate
description:
Discovered 2026-07-09 while validating a new VM scenario for sinex-r6d.9 (xtask test vm --validate --format human): 4 pre-existing files fail nix-instantiate with "error: undefined variable 'sinexd'", unrelated to that session's changes:

- tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/failure-recovery.nix
- tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/mtls-enforcement.nix
- tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/multi-source.nix
- tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/runtime-matrix.nix

Root cause (confirmed via failure-recovery.nix:10): `sinexPackage = if sinex != null then sinex else sinexd;` references `sinexd` as a fallback, but the file's own lambda parameter list only declares `sinex`, not `sinexd` — a genuine free-variable bug. Fix: either add `sinexd ? null` to each file's parameter list, or (more likely correct) just drop the dead fallback branch entirely (delete `else sinexd`, matching the other working scenario files like chaos-clock-skew.nix which only reference `sinex`).

These are part of the `integration` category in xtask/src/commands/vm.rs's INTEGRATION_TESTS. Given --validate currently exits nonzero whenever ANY scenario file fails, this silently blocks a clean 'xtask test vm --validate' pass for the whole suite until fixed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read tests/e2e/nixos-vm/test-scenarios/failure-recovery.nix:10 -- `sinexPackage = if sinex != null then sinex else sinexd;` references sinexd as a fallback, but the file's lambda parameter list only declares `sinex`, not `sinexd`.
2. Confirm the same pattern in mtls-enforcement.nix, multi-source.nix, runtime-matrix.nix.
3. Run `xtask test vm --validate --format human` -- observe nix-instantiate fails on all 4 files with "error: undefined variable 'sinexd'".
4. Since these are part of the `integration` category in xtask/src/commands/vm.rs's INTEGRATION_TESTS and --validate exits nonzero on ANY scenario failure, confirm this silently blocks a clean `xtask test vm --validate` pass for the whole suite until fixed.

Note: this is the same underlying bug as sinex-ikdi (discovered independently in a separate session, same 4 files, same root cause) -- see that bead for the identical fix-pattern comparison against working scenario files.
acceptance_criteria: xtask test vm --validate reports 0 failed for these 4 files (nix-instantiate succeeds with dummy args); the fix does not change which package each scenario actually deploys when sinex is provided (only removes/repairs the dead undefined-variable fallback path).

title: process_batch's checkpoint-failure halt condition ignores the consecutive-count tolerance for Checkpoint-kind errors
description:
process_batch's checkpoint-failure halt condition short-circuits on error KIND
(Checkpoint/Lifecycle/Configuration/PermissionDenied), which means the "3 consecutive
failures" tolerance the surrounding code/comment/test all describe never actually applies to
Checkpoint-kind errors — the very first failure already halts.

## Steps to Reproduce
xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E 'test(process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures)'
— fails on master (verified via git stash + isolated deterministic rerun, not host contention).
design:
Discovered while verifying sinex-r6d.9's fail-point test didn't cause a regression (it didn't
— confirmed via git stash that this test fails identically on clean master).

process.rs's process_batch checkpoint-save halt condition:
  if self.consecutive_checkpoint_failures >= 3
      || matches!(e, SinexError::Checkpoint(_) | SinexError::Lifecycle(_)
                    | SinexError::Configuration(_) | SinexError::PermissionDenied(_))
  { return Err(...) }

save_state_with_file_fallback's own failure path (state_io.rs) always constructs
SinexError::checkpoint(...) when BOTH the NATS KV save and the file fallback fail — which is
exactly what happens for any automaton whose State fails to serialize (both paths call
serde_json::to_value on the same unserializable state). This means the `matches!` arm always
matches on the FIRST failure, short-circuiting the `||` before consecutive_checkpoint_failures
ever reaches 3 — the "consecutive tolerance" the surrounding code comment and the
process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures test both describe as the
intended contract never actually applies for this error class.

Verification: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/automaton/adapter/tests/processing_replay.rs's
`process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures` test currently fails on
master (verified via git stash + isolated rerun, deterministic, not host-contention-related)
with exactly this symptom: the FIRST checkpoint failure already halts the batch instead of the
second.

## Steps to Reproduce
xtask test -p sinexd --lib -E 'test(process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures)'

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decide the intended semantics: should ANY Checkpoint/Lifecycle/Configuration/
      PermissionDenied-kind error halt immediately (in which case the test's expectation is
      wrong and should be corrected, and the "consecutive" framing in the surrounding comment
      updated to explain which error kinds get the tolerance), or should the consecutive-count
      tolerance apply uniformly regardless of error kind (in which case the `matches!` fast-path
      should be removed or narrowed)?
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, the fix makes process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures
      pass, and the decision + rationale is recorded in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
Decide the intended semantics: should ANY Checkpoint/Lifecycle/Configuration/
PermissionDenied-kind error halt immediately (test's expectation is wrong, correct it and the
comment), or should the consecutive-count tolerance apply uniformly regardless of error kind
(narrow or remove the matches! fast-path)? Whichever is chosen, make
process_batch_halts_after_three_consecutive_checkpoint_save_failures pass and record the
decision + rationale in this bead.

Testable via a targeted unit test on the halt-condition branch.

title: Reconcile bead priority field with wave sequencing order
description:
priority (1-4) is uncorrelated with the wave:N label that actually encodes intended
sequencing (my5 is the standing sequencing instrument that stamps wave:N each round).
Sample from `bd ready` today: wave:6 sinex-2k2/sinex-h2x (embedding preflight, late
horizon) and wave:7/8 sinex-a4w.3/sinex-cem sort ahead of many wave:1 correctness-core
items (r6d.4/.5/.7, vxu, z8p) because nearly every load-bearing bead is stamped P1 —
priority carries almost no discriminating signal, so `bd ready`'s default priority sort
is close to arbitrary among P1 items across waves. Anyone running plain `bd ready`
without reading my5's prose notes gets a misleading order. Same class of bug as
polylogue-8e1b (delivery-gate vs priority reconciliation), confirmed present here too.

Note: bd-graph-lint (.agent/scripts/bd-graph-lint) already catches wave *inversions*
via the dependency graph (blocked-by a higher-wave open bead). It does NOT catch this:
two independent, unblocked P1 beads in different waves still sort arbitrarily relative
to each other, since nothing derives priority from wave.
design:
Re-derive priority from (wave index, blocked-vs-ready, epic-vs-leaf) rather than
hand-set values: earlier waves should dominate later waves at the same nominal
urgency; a blocked item's priority should not compete with a ready item's in an
earlier wave. Candidate mechanical rule: priority = f(wave_index, blocked_flag),
leaving room for genuine P0 (data-loss/security) overrides - see sinex-jdp,
sinex-9u4, sinex-60r class issues. wave:N labels (stamped by sinex-my5 each
sequencing round) are the source of truth for ordering, analogous to polylogue's
.agent/tools/delivery-gate-status.py gate list.

Batch as one mechanical bd update sweep + bd-graph-lint re-run, not per-bead edits.
Consider extending bd-graph-lint itself to flag priority/wave mismatches (P1 in
wave>=N while lower-wave P2s exist) rather than only dependency inversions, so the
check is durable instead of a one-shot sweep that drifts again next round.
acceptance_criteria:
A reconciliation round is complete when: (1) priority is re-derived per bead from
(wave index, blocked-vs-ready, epic-vs-leaf) rather than hand-set, with genuine
P0 (data-loss/security) overrides preserved and noted; (2) `bd ready` sorted by
default priority now surfaces beads in wave order among equal urgency (spot-check:
no wave:N P1 sorts ahead of an unblocked wave:<N P1); (3) bd-graph-lint passes and,
ideally, is extended to catch this class (priority/wave mismatch) going forward so
it does not silently drift again next my5 sequencing round; (4) the sweep is one
batched bd update pass + one graph-lint run, not per-bead edits, and is recorded in
this bead's notes with the date.
notes:
2026-07-08 EXECUTED (mirroring polylogue-8e1b's investigation, then diverging on
the fix): built two durable tools instead of a one-shot bulk rewrite, because a
naive priority=f(wave_index) formula turned out to be UNSOUND for sinex's actual
semantics — verified by inspecting sinex-my5's latest round: wave:6 (LLM plane)
and wave:8 (demo portfolio) carry legitimate P1 items that are genuinely
near-term/parallel-lane work despite high wave numbers, because sinex waves
interleave several genuinely-parallel lanes rather than encoding a strict
delivery-gate sequence the way polylogue's delivery:* labels do (my5: "four
lanes... genuinely parallel"). Blindly demoting high-wave P1s would have wrongly
punished sinex-2k2/h2x/5v6 and possibly sinex-cem.1/.2.

Built:
- .agent/tools/bead-lint.py — ported from polylogue's tool (D1/D2/E1/E2/T1/X1/X2/B1
  checks not already covered by bd-graph-lint's stricter wave/area/AC invariants).
  Caught a real bug in passing: an earlier malformed `bd create` call had silently
  inserted a duplicate row (sinex-a519) before erroring — closed as dup of this bead.
  Currently 0 findings after excluding structural false positives (crate-name/build-
  target/CAS-path/worktree-dirname/markdown-anchor collisions with the id shape).
- .agent/tools/wave-status.py — ported from polylogue's delivery-gate-status.py,
  adapted to discover wave numbers from data (sinex waves are restamped every my5
  round, unlike polylogue's stable named gates) and to print a priority histogram
  per wave as a reminder surface, not a computed pass/fail.

Applied two concrete, textually-grounded corrections found via the board + manual
cross-check against my5's current lane notes and CONVENTIONS.md's own P0-P4 rubric
(not a blind sweep):
- sinex-o6w P1->P3 (pure design/meta/legibility content; not in my5's active lanes)
- sinex-r6d.9 P2->P1 (my5 explicitly frames it as parallel-first with r6d.5, same
  wave:0, same lane A, same data-loss/correctness labels — inconsistent at P2)

Residual: no durable mechanical enforcement of the wave/priority correlation itself
was added (deliberately — see above, it isn't a computable invariant here). Future
rounds should eyeball `python3 .agent/tools/wave-status.py` each time my5 restamps
waves, the same way polylogue treats delivery-gate-status.py as a reminder board.
close_reason: Investigated, built durable tooling (bead-lint.py + wave-status.py, ported from polylogue with stated divergences), applied two evidenced priority corrections (o6w, r6d.9). See notes for why a blind mechanical sweep was rejected as unsound for this repo's wave semantics.

title: xtask progress-keyed stall detection: watchdog on progress signals, not wall-clock output bytes
description: Verifiability-audit gap (2026-07-08, polylogue-methodology parity): the harness protects itself with wall-clock timeouts only (SINEX_CARGO_TIMEOUT default 600s; detached reaper). Two failure shapes result: (1) healthy-but-slow runs (full-workspace clippy under load) hit the timeout and die — the operator remedy is raising a global constant, which then (2) lets genuinely wedged runs (deadlocked test, hung DB connection, target-lock livelock) burn the whole enlarged budget before anyone notices. Both are stall-detection keyed on the wrong signal. cargo and nextest both emit machine-readable progress (compilation unit completions, per-test start/finish events); a stalled run stops PRODUCING PROGRESS long before it stops producing bytes (warning spew) or hits wall-clock.
design: Shape: a progress watchdog inside the xtask job runner — parse the already-captured cargo/nextest event streams; reset the watchdog on progress events (unit compiled, test started/finished, schema step applied), not on raw output bytes; no-progress-for-N (default ~120s, per-phase configurable) => flag STALLED, capture diagnostics (process tree, last progress event, sample of thread stacks via kill -QUIT where applicable), then kill with a distinct exit classification (stalled vs timed-out vs failed — extends the 0mw exit-code honesty work). Wall-clock timeout stays as the outer bound but can be generous once the inner progress watchdog exists. Job records (xtask history) gain last-progress-at + stall verdicts so flake/hang analysis has data. Interacts: 0mw (timeout exit-code split — land the classification vocabulary together), 9es (substrate seal: a stall caused by dead DB should classify as substrate failure, not test failure).
acceptance_criteria: Progress watchdog active for cargo build/clippy and nextest phases under xtask; a deliberately hung test is flagged STALLED within the no-progress budget with diagnostics captured, while a slow-but-progressing full build is NOT killed despite exceeding the old 600s default; stall verdicts recorded in xtask history and visible in xtask jobs output; exit classification distinguishes stalled/timed-out/failed.

title: Substance ledger import: find the primary artifact, ingest it, not the processed CSV
description: Lynchpin sources.substance reads a 'processed substance CSV' — by doctrine we ingest the PRIMARY artifact instead. Step zero is provenance archaeology: determine what the processed CSV was produced FROM (an operator-maintained log? app export? if the CSV itself is the operator's primary hand-maintained ledger, then it IS the raw data and ingesting it as-is is correct — the constraint bans lynchpin PROCESSING, not CSVs). Record the finding; then: primary artifact as material, dose entries as events with provider/operator-intrinsic ts_orig, occurrence identity per row identity, consumer derivation named (substance_kinetics is the k4c.1 recorded-analysis example; correlations flow through syhc). Going forward, new entries should have a first-class capture path (moment-mark k53x compound or a tiny CLI affordance) so the ledger stops being an offline file that rots.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance finding recorded (what the processed CSV derives from, with evidence); the primary artifact ingests as material with row-identity occurrence keys and re-import overlap dedup; if lynchpin processing added value (unit normalization, name canonicalization) that logic is re-derived as Sinex parsing/derivation, never by reading lynchpin output; forward-capture affordance decided (built or explicitly deferred with reason); ledger row updated with parity counts.

title: Evidence-pack export: productize the external-deep-analysis workflow
description: The GPT-Pro handoff rounds proved the pattern: a self-contained evidence package + sharp brief given to a big external model returns high-density analysis. Today that packaging is artisanal (chisel tarballs, hand-written briefs). Productize: sinexctl export evidence-pack --window/--topic/--question builds a self-contained directory — selected events with full provenance chains, material excerpts (anchor-bounded, not whole files), the citation manifest (every included item resolvable back via show refs), coverage/gap statement (jdp), a privacy pass with the residual honesty of the 09 matrix (what classes of content are included; planted-secret scan optional), and rerun/verification instructions for the cold reader. Pairs with a RETURN path: the analysis comes back as annotations/candidate claims citing pack item ids that map back to event refs — external analysis enters the candidate plane like any other interpretation instead of rotting in downloads. This is also the substrate for the polylogue-chisel convergence and any future 'ask a frontier model about my life with receipts' flow.

The doctrine-safe shape: a correlation SCAN is a declared, versioned method (variable pair whitelist from the derivation catalog, lag windows, estimator, multiple-comparison correction, minimum-coverage threshold from jdp) whose outputs are analysis_claim products carrying ClaimSupport with LOW default support, the full method fingerprint, and evidence windows — surfaced only through the candidate plane for operator adjudication, never asserted in briefs or Today until judged. title: Decision: low-blast schema lattice gaps — grants, extension versions, PG enums, collations, extra objects
description:
Per-surface decision: enforce, report-only, or explicit non-goal for excess grants (apply grants but never revokes), extension version drift, future CREATE TYPE AS ENUM (no type inventory exists), collation contracts, extra schemas/tables under managed schemas. Single-operator/pre-release context lowers blast; record the acceptance rationale where non-goal. Source: new-gpt-pro 08 findings 9-10 + category matrix.

## Alternatives Considered
- **Enforce all surfaces (grants, extension versions, PG enums, collations, extra objects) strictly via strict_diff.** Rejected as a blanket default: several of these surfaces (excess grants, extension version drift) have no clear single "correct" value in a single-operator/pre-release deployment, and building strict enforcement for surfaces with no current drift incidents is speculative engineering ahead of need.
- **Ignore all surfaces silently (no per-surface decision, no documentation).** Rejected: leaves genuine schema-lattice gaps completely undetected with no record of whether the gap is a deliberate non-goal or an oversight -- the whole point of this decision bead is to convert "nobody decided" into "each surface has a recorded decision," even where that decision is explicitly non-goal.
- **Chosen approach**: per-surface enforce / report-only / explicit-non-goal, since the surfaces genuinely differ in blast radius and in how meaningful "drift" even is for them (e.g. extra grants vs. a future undeclared enum type are qualitatively different risks).
design:
PROPOSED RULING (2026-07-08, per-surface, encoded for operator ratification; single-operator pre-release context = low blast, so report-only beats enforcement machinery everywhere the failure is visible):

1. EXCESS GRANTS: report-only. strict-diff gains an excess-grant report row (grants present live but not declared); no auto-revoke — a wrong revoke can lock the daemon out, a wrong grant is visible and inert on a single-user host. Falsifier for the non-goal half: a second DB role appears.
2. EXTENSION VERSION DRIFT: pin-minimum + report. Declare minimum versions in defs; strict-diff reports older-than-minimum or major-version-ahead. No auto-upgrade (extension upgrades are deploy-time acts owned by the NixOS module).
3. PG ENUMS (CREATE TYPE AS ENUM): explicit non-goal + tripwire. Zero enums exist by design (domain enums live in Rust newtypes; DB stores text). Enforcement = forbidden-pattern lint (xtask check --forbidden) rejecting CREATE TYPE AS ENUM in schema defs, so the non-goal cannot erode silently. Cheaper than building a type inventory for a set of size zero.
4. COLLATIONS: documented non-goal. Single host, single locale, no collation-sensitive ordering contracts. Falsifier recorded in crate/sinex-schema docs: satellite hosts (rkv.7) or any ORDER BY on user text crossing a consumption contract reopens this.
5. EXTRA SCHEMAS/TABLES UNDER MANAGED SCHEMAS: report as drift. strict-diff lists unmanaged objects inside managed schemas (core/raw/audit/reflection/sinex_schemas/sinex_telemetry) — these are either abandoned experiments or manual surgery; both deserve visibility. Not auto-dropped (state is durable; wipes are design failures).

Implementation rider: all five land as verify-interpreter rows over the 32p2 expectation IR when it exists (2pl guidance applies); if claimed before 32p2, implement as report-only strict-diff additions and note the IR migration on 32p2.
acceptance_criteria: Each surface has a recorded decision. Enforced surfaces gain strict-diff coverage; non-goal surfaces get a documented why in crate/sinex-schema docs.
notes: RATIFIED 2026-07-08 (operator, decision-brief batch): all five per-surface verdicts FINAL. Bead stays open as its own implementation carrier (report rows + forbidden-pattern tripwire + docs), preferably as 32p2 IR interpreter rows.

title: Decision: agent-session content embedding ownership (avoid double-embedding)
description: Define the cross-repository compatibility profile for agent-session embeddings under the independently landable sinex-k4c.1.1 effect envelope and sinex-5v6 embedding operation. This bead owns Polylogue/Sinex field parity and measured reuse, not another envelope or key vocabulary.
design:
K4c.1.1 owns RequestKey/ResultRecord/EligibilityRecord/ReplayPolicy canonical encoding. 5v6 owns embedding execution fields. This compatibility profile requires both systems to encode the same input digest/refs, canonicalization, record/chunk selector, chunking, provider/model/revision, dimensions, task/input type, normalization, tool revision, and schema versions into the k4c.1.1 RequestKey.

output_hash is ResultRecord integrity after lookup/execution. Privacy/access/retention/deletion is EligibilityRecord state. Reuse requires exact RequestKey plus current eligibility. Standalone Polylogue keeps local compute/store; backed mode exchanges k4c.1.1-compatible receipts/results.
acceptance_criteria: Measured cost/storage math is recorded. A checked-in cross-repository fixture yields byte-identical k4c.1.1 RequestKeys and compatible Result/Eligibility records. Computational field changes create a new request; output_hash changes result integrity only; policy changes eligibility only. Unauthorized or deleted inputs cannot reuse. A real 5v6 measurement demonstrates reuse and standalone Polylogue search remains green. No second effect envelope or key type lands.

Generalize into a small experiment-hosting substrate: declared arms, preregistered metrics, paired analysis over the same evidence window — agent-buildable, so future capability claims (retrieval hit@k in cem.5, lane duels in cem.6, blinded resumption in cem.7) reuse one harness instead of bespoke scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria
An experiment descriptor (arms, metric definitions, evidence window) + runner producing a paired-analysis artifact; cem.5 or cem.6 executed THROUGH it as the proving case; 9j9's one-off documented as the precedent it generalizes. VERIFY: one real experiment run end-to-end via the substrate.
acceptance_criteria: Descriptor schema sinex.experiment/v1: experiment_id, claim, preregistered_at, fixtures (store epoch, query set, gold set, coverage snapshot, generator exclusions), declared arms (generator, command, inputs, constraints), metrics (kind: retrieval|pack|ranking|duel|label_quality|latency, primary flag), analysis (unit, paired_by, bootstrap resamples, CI, extra tests), stopping_rule (min_n, max_n, looks_every, keep_if, kill_if), outputs. Runner executes arms over the same fixture, records exact commands/config/store epoch, writes per_item_jsonl, paired_deltas_csv, summary.json, report.md. Supports retrieval (hit@k/MRR/nDCG), structured pack metrics (weighted gold-segment coverage, critical recall, citation resolvability, gap-honesty F1, source-family coverage, support fidelity, self-observation leak rate, finite degraded completion), salience metrics (nDCG@10, precision@5, top3-useful, pairwise preference, term traceability/non-fabrication), duel metrics, label-quality metrics (weighted kappa, Jaccard, rank correlation, defer rate). Paired bootstrap over the declared unit; sign-test/discordance for binary outcomes. Preregistration enforced by hashing descriptor+query set+gold set+coverage snapshot before arm execution. Sequential looks with recorded stopping-rule firing. cem.5 plus at least one pack or salience experiment execute through the substrate before close.
notes: 2026-07-07: five ready-to-run descriptor YAMLs (recall_golden_v1, cem5 hybrid retrieval, recall_pack_quality_v1, uxd_salience_ranking_v1, cem7 duel) committed in new-gpt-pro sessions/06 — lift them verbatim when implementing.

title: Capture-surface threat posture: per-source sensitivity declaration + verification
description:
Blueprint lens L-4: Sinex captures keystrokes, clipboard, window titles, screen frames — live, from a running human. Distinct from the redaction feature (optional by design): this is about the capture INSTRUMENT. Each source declares its maximum sensitivity (privacy_tier exists as Level-6 declaration metadata) but nothing verifies a source cannot exceed its declaration, and the blast-radius stance (what leaks if the store leaks) is documented only in the threat-model doc.

## Acceptance Criteria
Per-source sensitivity declaration becomes verified (Level 4+): a test/lint per capture family asserting emitted payload fields stay within the declared tier (e.g. window-title source cannot emit clipboard content); screen/clipboard secret-class handling stated (field exclusion or suppression path); the at-rest encryption posture doc cross-references the per-source declarations; blast-radius statement per sensitivity tier in the threat model. VERIFY: the verification tests + updated threat-model doc.

Do NOT build redaction features here (privacy is opt-in by doctrine); this is capture-instrument honesty. title: Content axis as one capability: unified material/anchor/extraction contract
description:
Blueprint 018 §2 / 017 Axis A: browser page content, email bodies, screen-OCR, and clipboard content are all 'content capture' — one capability with N adapters, not N independent source designs. Unify under one material/anchor/extraction contract (CAS-backed content material, byte/logical anchors, extraction lane producing document/chunk events) with an up-front volume budget (018 §3.4 decision: transition/point capture + CAS material, tunable cadence, hard volume ceiling before lighting).

## Acceptance Criteria
One documented content-capture contract (material policy, anchor scheme, extraction path, volume budget mechanism); at least two content adapters (e.g. browser page + clipboard) implemented against it sharing the extraction lane; the volume-budget decision recorded with the operator; screen-OCR (a4w.3.7) and email bodies (di7) explicitly declared as later adapters of THIS contract, not parallel designs. VERIFY: two adapters producing through one lane on dev; storage-growth analytics showing budget enforcement.
design: The document layer already exists (document_parser automaton, core.documents, chunking, doc search) — the content axis is adapters INTO that layer, not a new layer. Volume control precedent: xtask analytics storage-growth (#2312) is the measurement instrument. DECISION REQUIRED (operator): the volume budget numbers + whether screen-OCR lights at all before AT-SPI (rkv.8 may obsolete most OCR need — the anti-OCR source). Relates: rkv.3 (browser content = first adapter), rkv.8, a4w.3.7, di7.

title: Design: person entity — identity resolution across email, git-author, handle, messaging
description:

Everything social (comm.thread, relationship.activity, project.attribution people-splits) presumes a PERSON entity resolved across identity facets — email address(es), git author strings, platform handles, messaging contacts — but no entity model, resolution rule set, or adjudication flow exists for persons. title: LLM budget policy automaton: ledger consumer that pauses lanes at threshold
description:
Meta-gap 018 §7.5 + U9 failure class 5: llm.budget.ledger exists as a kind and 5v6 will emit it, but nothing CONSUMES it — no spend policy, no cap, no alert. A budget automaton reads ledger events, aggregates spend per lane/provider/window, and pauses lanes (emit llm.budget.exceeded + lane disable via the control plane) at operator-set ceilings. Without this, activating the LLM plane has an uncapped cost failure mode (U9 #5: cost blowout).

## Acceptance Criteria
Budget automaton consumes llm.budget.ledger; per-lane/window spend aggregation; at threshold emits llm.budget.exceeded AND actually pauses the lane (verifiable via lane status); ceiling configurable at runtime (runtime-config surface once it exists, env until then); fixture test: synthetic ledger events cross threshold -> lane paused. VERIFY: fixture run + lane status flip.

Lane pause mechanism = SemanticLaneStatus via set_lane_status (semantic repo :252) or SINEX_AUTOMATA-level gating — prefer lane status (it is data, resumable, auditable). Failure routes for the whole semantic plane are cataloged in U9 (016/02-uncovered-designs.md:142-155) — implement #5 here, the rest belong to 0vx lane robustness.

title: Temporal-quality propagation: joins inherit the worst input ts_orig quality
description:
Blueprint lens L-3: a time-join between a RealtimeCapture source (ts_orig good to the ms) and an InferredMtime source (good to a day) joins intervals of wildly different precision. The join must carry a confidence derived from the WORSE input quality — and that quality flows into the evidence tier. Today ts_quality exists per-event (temporal ladder) but no derivation propagates it: interval-lift and the composites emit outputs with no quality statement.

## Acceptance Criteria
Derived events produced by time-joins carry a propagated temporal-quality field = min(input rungs); interval-lift stamps it; at least one composite (attention.stream or a4w.3.2) surfaces it; the evidence-tier field (8cr) incorporates temporal quality in its tier derivation for time-join outputs; documented in derivation_catalog. VERIFY: fixture with mixed-quality inputs produces min-rung output; test asserts propagation.
design: Carrier: the same DerivedOutput/synthesized-metadata path as 8cr (do together or immediately after — same files). ts_quality already on Event (events/mod.rs:71) and rungs in TemporalSourceType; propagation is a fold over parents. Interacts: 8cr (tier), interval_lift.rs rules, dcs (catalog formalization).

title: Context-budget arbiter: one budget across recall, context packs, and orientation
description:
Blueprint 018 §2: recall, context_pack, and MCP orientation are three independent renderers deciding what enters an agent's context; nothing arbitrates total budget or priority across them. One arbiter decides allocation (by evidence value, freshness, and caller-declared budget), so an agent asking for 8K tokens of context gets the best 8K across surfaces, not three uncoordinated dumps.

## Acceptance Criteria
A budget parameter flows through recall/context/orient MCP+CLI surfaces; one arbiter module owns allocation with a measured-quantity priority (no invented weights — salience from uxd once it lands); output states what was dropped for budget (honest-gaps rule). VERIFY: same query at two budgets shows principled truncation with drop caveats.

Likely home: the shared context/query substrate in sinexctl (context.rs family) + a budget field in the MCP tool schemas. Relates: uxd, x69, 68c (read-model readiness feeds priority).

title: Partial-record re-emit duplicates: multi-intent record with mid-record emit failure re-emits persisted siblings on retry
description:
Verified seam (grok 2026-07-06): in AdapterBackedSource drain (crate/sinexd/src/runtime/parser/adapter_source.rs:1456-1505), a record can parse into multiple intents; if intent K emits successfully and intent K+1 fails emit, record_processed=false so the cursor does NOT advance (correct, no loss) — but the already-emitted K events proceed through the pipeline and persist. On retry the record re-emits ALL intents, duplicating the first K for any source that does not stamp equivalence_key (only OccurrenceIdentity::Uuid5From sources do; admission.rs:505-525 suppression is keyed on it). Consequence: at-least-once duplicates concentrated exactly at emit-failure boundaries, invisible to sources without occurrence identity.

## Steps to Reproduce
Craft a parser returning 2+ intents for one record; inject emit failure on the second (test hook or NATS payload-cap overflow); drain, restart drain; observe duplicate first-intent rows in core.events with distinct ids, same (source_material_id, anchor_byte).

## Acceptance Criteria
Either (a) per-record emit becomes all-or-nothing (buffer intents, emit after all conversions succeed — emit failures then leave zero persisted siblings), or (b) every multi-intent source stamps occurrence identity so admission suppression covers the retry, or (c) the seam is documented as accepted at-least-once with the r6d.8 classification citing it. A focused test proves the chosen behavior.
design: Option (a) is the cheap local fix: collect converted events for the record into a Vec, then emit sequentially only after all intent_to_event conversions succeeded; a mid-emit transport failure still duplicates (transport is at-least-once by contract) but conversion failures no longer do. Full fix pairs with r6d.4 (durable-emit-before-cursor) — coordinate, do not conflict: both touch the same drain loop. Relates: sinex-r6d.8 (loss/replayability classification), sinex-e5p item 7 (dedup fail-open).
acceptance_criteria: A multi-intent record either commits all sibling outcomes as one durable progress atom, or records durable partial-debt/operation state that prevents silent duplicates on retry. Sequential emit-after-conversion is not sufficient unless the retry path is protected by equivalence-key suppression or another durable occurrence-identity proof (admission dedup only fires when equivalence_key exists — admission.rs:183-188,505-516; sources without it are never suppressed by that path).
notes: 2026-07-31: sinex-r6d.11's reference caller integration merged/in-review as PR #2519 (branch feature/fix/r6d11-durable-emission-receipt). Same API pointer: crate/sinexd/src/runtime/durable_emission.rs + durable_emission_backend.rs. Relevant to this bead's multi-intent partial-emit-failure scenario: emit_batch_durable's receipt is per-event, in submission order (DurableEmissionReceipt::items), so a multi-intent record's siblings can be individually checked via receipt.items slicing (see adapter_source.rs::drain_adapter's per-record span logic) rather than treating the whole record as all-or-nothing — use this to distinguish 'sibling already durably persisted, do not re-emit' from 'sibling never settled, safe to retry' on record retry.

title: context_pack MCP tool: project scoping degraded to a source-prefix guess (#1095 DTO unfinished)
description: The sinex.context_pack MCP tool — an AGENT-FACING surface (the widest way agents consume Sinex) — does not actually scope by project. crate/sinexctl/src/mcp.rs:~2808: project_path is meant to drive a project-scoped query but the real context-pack DTO from #1095 was never finished, so the code falls back to treating the path as a SOURCE-PREFIX hint: 'if the path parses as an EventSource, filter sources to that string'. For any real project path (e.g. /realm/project/sinex) this silently matches nothing or the wrong thing, and the agent receives a context pack that looks scoped but isn't — the exact 'misleading surface' failure mode (standing rule 6: honest gaps). This is distinct from project.attribution (a4w.3.3, the deep entity-join that would make project scoping CORRECT): even before that lands, the tool must not pretend to scope. Options: (a) honest degradation — if project_path can't be properly resolved, return unscoped results WITH an explicit caveat naming the limitation and the blocking work (#1095 / a4w.3.3), rather than a silent wrong filter; (b) wire real project scoping once project.attribution exists. Do (a) now (cheap, honest), (b) when the substrate lands.
design: DECISION: mirror the recall honesty pattern — never silently mis-scope. Immediate fix: when project_path is present, attempt real resolution (project entity if project.attribution is live; else the documented fallback), and whenever the result is not a true project scope, attach a structured caveat to the context-pack output ('project_path scoping unavailable: returning source-hint/unscoped results; blocked on #1095 context-pack DTO / a4w.3.3 project.attribution') so the consuming agent knows the scope is approximate. Real scoping (b) becomes a follow-up wired to a4w.3.3. Check the other MCP tools in the same pass for sibling silent-degradation (nbi.6 covers the inert LLM read surfaces; this is the context-pack instance).
acceptance_criteria: context_pack with a project_path either scopes correctly or returns results carrying an explicit scope-limitation caveat naming the blocking work; no path silently produces a wrong-but-plausible filter; a test asserts the caveat appears when real scoping is unavailable; the #1095 follow-up for true project scoping is linked to a4w.3.3.
close_reason: Implemented context_pack project_path honesty on this branch: project_path now resolves to an explicit scope state; true project scoping is not claimed until #1095 / sinex-a4w.3.3 lands; real filesystem paths return unscoped packs with context_pack.project_scope_unavailable caveat; source-like strings return source-hint filtered packs with the same scope-limitation caveat; no-project_path remains uncaveated unscoped. Verification: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 xtask test -p sinexctl -E 'test(context_pack)' job 2001435 passed; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 xtask check -p sinexctl job 2001436 passed.

title: Application-level semantic hooks: neovim buffer events + kitty deep remote-control (editor/terminal semantics)
description: From the operator's multi-level-capture design conversation: the highest-semantic capture happens INSIDE applications, above the compositor. Two named targets not yet sourced (browser is rkv.3; terminal COMMANDS are shell.atuin already): (1) NEOVIM — a Lua autocmd hook emitting buffer/edit semantics (BufEnter/BufLeave/BufWrite: file path, filetype, mode, cursor, project) — the editor's view of what was being worked on, which fs-watcher (file.modified) cannot see (fs sees the write; nvim sees the intent, the navigation, the time-in-buffer before saving); feeds work.episode/change.episode with editor-grain attention. (2) KITTY deep remote control — beyond command capture: focus events with cwd + foreground processes + scrollback state (kitty's remote protocol exposes these), giving terminal ATTENTION and working-directory context that shell history alone lacks. The operator's framing: 'different levels of abstraction... correlated in all kinds of fun ways later' — each level is deliberately partial; the join is where value emerges. The multi-level-redundancy design principle (capture the same act at compositor + app + system level, eliminate redundancy downstream) is Sinex-native: overlapping interpretations of one occurrence, coalesced/tombstoned via the lifecycle+defrag machinery (lb8) when one level provably subsumes another — record that as doctrine, not a new mechanism.
design: DECISION: each app hook is an EXTERNAL PRODUCER (nvim Lua -> systemd-cat/NATS bridge; kitty python-kitten -> bridge) publishing EventIntent — same external-producer pattern as polylogued/hyprland-plugin, sinexd hosts nothing. Kinds by role: editor.buffer.focused / editor.buffer.written (Activity+Content role, Point; file ref for entity-join to project.attribution and fs events; cursor/mode as payload); terminal.focus.observed (Activity role; cwd + foreground_processes for project entity-join, complementing shell.atuin command events). Occurrence keys from (app session, buffer/window id, timestamp). ts_orig = the in-app event time (RealtimeCapture). REDUNDANCY DOCTRINE (record in the derivation catalog, do not build new machinery): the same real act may be captured at multiple levels (nvim BufWrite + fs file.modified + hyprland focus); these are distinct interpretations of related occurrences, NOT duplicates to suppress at ingest — they carry different information; downstream coalescing/eviction (lb8 defrag, lpz events-are-cache) removes a level only when another provably covers its information, as an explicit operator-visible lifecycle op. START SMALL per the operator's own 'add only what annoys you not having' — nvim buffer hook first (highest editor-semantic value, trivial Lua), kitty deep hook second. PITFALL: do not let app hooks re-capture what a lower level already has well (kitty COMMANDS stay atuin's job — capture terminal ATTENTION/cwd here, not re-log commands).
acceptance_criteria: A neovim editing session produces buffer-focus/write events with file+project refs queryable and joinable to the same window's fs events; a kitty pane's cwd and foreground process are captured as terminal attention distinct from the atuin command log; both run as external producers; the multi-level redundancy doctrine is written into the derivation catalog; no app hook duplicates a lower level's well-covered data (kitty does not re-log commands). VERIFY: nvim + kitty bridges emit to dev NATS; cross-level join query (nvim buffer x fs modified x window focus for one edit) returns coherent multi-level evidence.

title: Compositor-plugin telemetry tier: focus-change reasons, input latency, render/damage perf (Hyprland-internal)
description: From the operator's capture design conversation: a Hyprland PLUGIN can access data available NOWHERE else — the compositor internals. Distinct from the IPC socket2 fix (sinex-60r, which gives clean real-time focus/workspace/window transitions from the socket); this is the deeper tier that requires living inside the compositor. Genuinely-unique signals the operator flagged as most valuable: (1) FOCUS-CHANGE REASONS — not just that focus changed but WHY (mouse click / alt-tab / workspace switch / window close) — turns attention.stream from 'what had focus' into 'how attention moved', which is qualitatively richer for interruption.event (a4w.3.2) and work.episode; (2) input latency (keypress -> window receipt) and compositor render/damage/frame perf — a machine-health signal tied to the actual desktop, feeding machine.context (a4w.3.5) ('that felt laggy' becomes measurable); (3) window geometry/animation/group operations. The operator also settled the storage question in-conversation: single events table with event_type as the virtual-table discriminator + partial indexes handles 144Hz fine — which is exactly Sinex's existing model (one hypertable, typed payloads, event-type routing), so NO separate table is needed; high-frequency perf events are just a declared high-volume class.
design: DECISION: this is an OPTIONAL deep tier layered above sinex-60r, not a replacement — 60r's socket2 driver is the baseline attention source and ships first; the plugin tier is additive and Hyprland-specific (accept the coupling: operator is single-user on Hyprland, extension.md-style external-producer if/when portability matters). Shape: a Hyprland plugin (C++) as an EXTERNAL PRODUCER publishing EventIntent to NATS (same pattern as polylogued) — sinexd does not host it; the plugin writes to a shm/socket bridge that publishes. SPLIT BY VOLUME CLASS + SEMANTIC ROLE into distinct kinds so the high-frequency perf lane never drowns the semantic lane (the telemetry-lane-separation lesson, x9i, applied at capture): desktop.focus.changed (Activity role, Point, carries the REASON enum — the high-value low-volume signal); desktop.render.sampled (Reflexive/machine role, high-volume — declared volume class, its own retention, feeds machine.context, NOT the activity plane); desktop.input.latency (machine role, sampled not per-event). Interval lifting (focus spans) stays L2 (catalog rule 4) — the plugin emits transitions with reasons, not spans. PITFALL: do not emit per-frame at 144Hz into the main event stream — sample/aggregate render perf at the source (e.g. per-second percentiles) or route to the reflection lane; raw per-frame is capture abuse. The operator's single-table conclusion is correct for Sinex and needs no schema change.
acceptance_criteria: Focus changes carry a reason (mouse/alt-tab/workspace/close) distinguishable in queries; a laggy interval is visible as elevated desktop.render latency joinable to what was focused; the perf lane's volume does not appear in activity-plane recall (separated like telemetry); the plugin runs as external producer with sinexd unaware of its process; render sampling is bounded at source (no raw 144Hz in the stream). VERIFY: plugin emits to dev NATS, events queryable; volume-class check that render events route to the reflection lane.

title: AT-SPI2 semantic capture: accessibility widget trees as lossless digital text (the anti-OCR source)
description: From the operator's comprehensive-capture design conversation (2026-07-03 download): the standout insight was that AT-SPI2 accessibility APIs expose complete widget trees — 'so much semantic data', 'why isn't this shit already done'. This is the CONTENT role's answer without OCR: on-screen text as actual digital strings (labels, text fields, document content, menu items) with structural context (widget hierarchy, roles, the owning application), not lossy pixel recognition. It fills exactly the catalog's weakest role (Content = 'weak: documents live, screen-OCR partial'). Complementary to OCR (a4w.3.7), not redundant: AT-SPI2 gives exact text for accessibility-aware toolkits (GTK/Qt apps expose it); OCR remains the fallback for canvas/pixel surfaces (some Electron, games, video). The operator's own framing: hook toolkit accessibility to 'supplant lossy OCR' where digital text already exists; route by surface type downstream (AT-SPI2-capable window -> skip OCR).
design: DECISION: a continuous SourceDriver subscribing to the AT-SPI2 D-Bus registry (org.a11y.atspi) for focus/text-changed/document events, emitting semantic text observations anchored to the active window interval. Kind: ui.text.observed (Content role, StateObservation/Point) carrying text content BY MATERIAL ANCHOR (accessibility snapshots can be large — register the snapshot as material, event references it; never embed bulk, catalog rule 2), widget role, app identity, and the window ref for entity-join to attention.stream. Occurrence key = (window, widget path, content hash) so an unchanged field re-observed does not duplicate (equivalence key). ts_orig = observation time (RealtimeCapture — it is live perception). PRIVACY: this reads on-screen text including passwords fields and private content — declare Sensitive tier; password/secret widgets (role PASSWORD_TEXT) suppressed at source; relies on the central redaction chokepoint for the rest. VOLUME: potentially high on text-heavy focus churn — bounded by change-detection (only on text-changed/focus events, not polling) and volume-classed before joining wildcard fan-in. SURFACE-ROUTING: emit a capability signal (window is AT-SPI2-covered) so the OCR lane (a4w.3.7) can skip covered surfaces — the operator's 'we know we have it here, don't bother with OCR' routing. PITFALL: AT-SPI2 coverage is app-dependent (native GTK/Qt strong, Electron/Wayland-native variable); the source must render coverage honestly (which windows it can and cannot see) rather than implying total capture.
acceptance_criteria: Focused text in a GTK/Qt app (e.g. a document, a form field) is captured as digital text queryable via sinexctl, anchored to the window interval and resolvable to the app; password-role widgets produce no cleartext (test); an AT-SPI2-blind window (canvas/pixel app) renders as an explicit coverage gap, not silent absence; re-observing unchanged text does not duplicate occurrences; a covered window emits the OCR-skip capability signal. VERIFY: driver test against a known-accessible app fixture + live dev capture; privacy suppression test for PASSWORD_TEXT role.
notes: 2026-07-06 intent provenance (chat archaeology): AT-SPI2 semantic capture is ORIGINAL design intent, not late speculation — June-2024-era claude.ai sessions contain the discovery ('AT-SPI2 gives complete widget trees') and the operator reaction ('why isn't this shit already done... it seems genuinely trivial'), predating Sinex itself (RecordKeeper era). It is also the anti-OCR keystone: lossless digital text makes most screen-OCR unnecessary (content-axis bead defers OCR partly on this). Weigh this provenance in the next sequencing round.

title: Phase B: Sinex-primary evidence — Polylogue SQLite demotes to rebuildable read model
description: Prove Sinex-primary evidence without dissolving Polylogue's domain kernel. Cutover is blocked until stable identity, durable assertions/judgments/context delivery, and privacy/lifecycle/deletion are implemented. Sinex holds durable evidence/history; Polylogue keeps ontology, read semantics, UX, and a rebuildable edge projection/replica.
design:
The contract is polylogue rebuild --from-sinex plus shadow cutover, not a generic storage trait or duplicate PostgreSQL transcript query/UI. Rebuild consumes verified manifests, r6d.11 durable receipts, r6d.12 raw settlements, stable identity ledger, user-state judgments, and lifecycle history through existing Polylogue materializers.

FIXED PARITY TAXONOMY:
- exact_match;
- allowlist-eligible: local_ephemeral_excluded, policy_excluded, declared_semantics_version_change, unavailable_optional_effect;
- always-fail: missing_evidence, extra_evidence, corrupt_anchor, stale_frontier, lifecycle_mismatch, judgment_mismatch, unknown_class, defect.
The checked-in allowlist is per difference fingerprint/object with class, reason, evidence ref, owner, and expiry/review condition; no class-wide waiver. New class/fingerprint, expired row, stale frontier, or always-fail class fails. Report counts every class. Mutations that remove/change an allowlist entry, add a novel difference, or suppress a comparison leg must fail.

No dual truth: Polylogue producer -> Sinex; Sinex -> SQLite replica/read model; only an explicit one-time migration importer reverses that direction. Mirror records durable lag. Primary cannot publish local projection before receipt. Shadow parity and rollback precede cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Only after 4j2.7/.9/.10 land, drop local replicas/projections and rebuild with zero unallowlisted differences and zero always-fail classes. Every allowed difference matches one unexpired fingerprinted row. Omitted/corrupt evidence, judgment/lifecycle mismatch, stale frontier, novel class/fingerprint, removed allowlist row, and disabled comparison leg fail. Stable refs, corrections, context deliveries, and deletion visibility survive. Shadow frontiers match before primary cutover; injected failure rolls back without dual authority. Standalone suite remains green.
